FBMCLI.17.1550900.title: Decision of the People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on Amending the Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City (2019)

articles.1:
Decision of the People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on Amending the Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City (2019)

Enacting authority: People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture (including its Standing Committee)
Document number: Announcement No. 2 of the Standing Committee of the 14th People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture
Approving authority: People's Congress of Hunan Province (including its Standing Committee)
Date of approval: 28 March 2019

Status: In force

Subject: Protection of historic and cultural cities

Announcement of the Standing Committee of the 14th People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture
(No. 2)

The Decision of the People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on Amending the Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City was adopted at the Third Session of the 14th People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on 28 February 2019 and approved at the Tenth Session of the Standing Committee of the 13th People's Congress of Hunan Province on 28 March 2019. It is hereby promulgated and shall take effect on the date of promulgation.
Standing Committee of the People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture
8 April 2019

Decision of the Third Session of the 14th People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on Amending the Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City
(Adopted on 28 February 2019 at the Third Session of the 14th People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture; approved on 28 March 2019 at the Tenth Session of the Standing Committee of the 13th People's Congress of Hunan Province)

The Third Session of the 14th People's Congress of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture decides to amend the Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City as follows:

1. The first paragraph of Article 4 is amended to read: “The People's Government of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture (the ‘Prefectural People's Government’) and its relevant departments shall strengthen guidance and supervision of the protection, development, and administration of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City.”
The third paragraph is amended to read: “The authority responsible for the protection and administration of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City shall handle the specific protection and administration work. Relevant departments of the People's Government of Fenghuang County shall carry out related protection and administration work in accordance with their respective responsibilities.”

2. One paragraph is added to Article 12 as its first paragraph: “The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall strengthen ecological and environmental protection in Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City, improve the ecological and environmental protection mechanism, closely monitor environmental carrying capacity and prevent ecological and environmental risks in key areas and watersheds, and formulate specific measures to prevent and control pollution affecting water, light, air, noise, solid waste, soil, and other environmental factors.”

3. Article 13 is amended to read: “The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall establish a waste-sorting system and require waste to be sorted at disposal, collection, transportation, and treatment.”
“The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall reasonably provide public toilets on urban roads and in public places. The entities responsible for managing public toilets shall provide clear signs and carry out routine cleaning and maintenance.”

4. Article 16 is amended to read: “Within the Ancient City of Fenghuang, it is prohibited to set up stalls that occupy roads, leave miscellaneous articles about, write, draw, or post indiscriminately, litter, or solicit customers using audio equipment. Advertisements and signs inconsistent with the historic character of the ancient city are prohibited. The storage or sale of flammable, explosive, toxic, or hazardous substances is prohibited.”

5. One paragraph is added to Article 17 as its second paragraph: “Vehicles traveling within the character-coordination zone or regional control zone shall follow the prescribed routes and park at designated locations.”

6. One item is added to the third paragraph of Article 18 as item 6: “(6) Other conduct that pollutes water bodies or damages aquatic ecosystems.”

7. Article 30 is amended to read: “The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall make reasonable use of the natural and cultural resources of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City, plan tourist areas, attractions, and routes on a scientific basis, and improve public services and tourism infrastructure.”
“The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall strengthen traffic management and take effective measures to closely monitor traffic flows and the carrying capacity of scenic areas. In light of conservation needs, it shall establish green transport and shuttle services, strictly control the entry of private vehicles into the protected area of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City, and ensure safe, orderly, and environmentally sound traffic. The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall formulate and publish specific measures.”

8. The words ‘Article 13’ are deleted from Article 36.

9. The words ‘industry and commerce, maritime affairs, animal husbandry, and other’ are deleted from Article 38.

This Decision shall take effect on the date of promulgation. The Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Fenghuang Historic and Cultural City shall be amended accordingly and repromulgated.

FBMCLI.10.4084953.title: Regulations of Dai County on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City of Dai County

articles.1: To strengthen the protection of the historic and cultural city of Dai County and pass on its outstanding cultural heritage, these Regulations are enacted in light of the circumstances of Dai County and in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages issued by the State Council, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to the planning, protection, restoration, administration, and use of the historic and cultural city of Dai County. The protection of cultural relics shall be governed by the relevant laws and regulations.
articles.3: The protection of the historic and cultural city of Dai County shall follow the principles of coordinated planning, strict administration, giving priority to protection, and scientifically appropriate use. It shall preserve the authenticity and integrity of its historical and cultural heritage and maintain and continue the traditional layout and historic character of the city.
articles.4:
The Municipal People's Government shall strengthen its leadership over the protection of the historic and cultural city of Dai County. The People's Government of Dai County shall be responsible for its planning, protection, restoration, use, and supervision and administration. The relevant departments of the People's Government of Dai County, including those responsible for development and reform, finance, natural resources, housing and urban-rural development, public security, culture and tourism, and ecology and environment, shall perform related protection duties in accordance with their respective responsibilities.
The relevant town and township people's governments and villagers' committees and residents' committees in Dai County shall carry out related protection and administration work in their respective areas.
articles.5: The People's Government of Dai County shall establish an Expert Advisory Committee for the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City of Dai County (the ‘Expert Advisory Committee’). The Committee shall provide advice on the city's planning, protection, restoration, use, supervision, and administration, and participate in studies supporting its protection. The People's Government of Dai County shall separately prescribe the Committee's membership, adjustments to its membership, responsibilities, and rules of procedure.
articles.6: The People's Government of Dai County shall incorporate the protection of the historic and cultural city of Dai County into its plans for national economic and social development and include the required funding in its fiscal budget.
articles.7: Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protecting the historic and cultural city of Dai County by making donations, providing financial support or technical services, or submitting suggestions.
articles.8: All organizations and individuals have a duty to protect the historic and cultural city of Dai County. They are entitled to submit suggestions on the formulation and implementation of conservation plans, dissuade conduct that damages the city, and report such conduct to the relevant departments.
articles.9: The People's Government of Dai County or the relevant administrative departments shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protecting the historic and cultural city of Dai County.
articles.10: The People's Government of Dai County shall prepare a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of Dai County in accordance with the law. Other special-purpose plans shall be coordinated with that conservation plan.
articles.11: The conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of Dai County shall be coordinated with the county's overall territorial spatial plan. It shall protect the integrity of the city's historic layout, reflect its frontier-culture character, strengthen the protection and administration of historic sites, historic districts, and historic buildings, and meet the needs of residents for a modern living and working environment.
articles.12: The conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of Dai County shall designate protected areas. These shall include a core conservation area and a construction-control zone; an environmental-coordination zone may also be designated as appropriate in light of local conditions.
articles.13: When preparing the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of Dai County, the People's Government shall broadly solicit public views and seek the views of the Expert Advisory Committee.
articles.14:
The People's Government of Dai County shall establish a register of protected assets for the historic and cultural city of Dai County.
The register shall include historic districts, cultural relics protection units, historic buildings with conservation value, and other assets.
For each protected asset, the register shall state its name, location, boundaries, date of origin, historical value, and other relevant information, and shall be made public.
The People's Government of Dai County shall install standardized conservation signs. No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a conservation sign without authorization.
articles.15: Construction within a protected area of the historic and cultural city of Dai County shall comply with the conservation plan. Before issuing a construction-project planning permit, the department responsible for issuing the permit shall seek the views of the cultural relics department.
articles.16:
Within the core conservation area, new construction and expansion are prohibited, except where necessary for infrastructure or public-service facilities.
Maintenance and repair of buildings or structures with conservation value in the core conservation area shall preserve their original height, scale, exterior design, and colors, and remain consistent with the area's overall character.
Buildings or structures that currently have a destructive impact on the traditional layout or historic character of the historic and cultural city shall be demolished or relocated in accordance with the law.
articles.17: Within the construction-control zone, new construction, reconstruction, or expansion of buildings or structures shall comply with the construction controls in the conservation plan and be compatible with the historic character in height, scale, and color.
articles.18: The environmental-coordination zone shall focus on protecting the overall layout of the historic and cultural city. New or reconstructed buildings shall reflect local cultural traditions and distinctive building techniques.
articles.20:
The owner of a historic building with conservation value shall perform the duties of administration, maintenance, and repair in accordance with the conservation plan and applicable conservation and repair standards.
If the owner lacks the capacity to administer, maintain, or repair the building, the People's Government of Dai County shall take measures to protect it.
articles.21: Institutions of higher education and research institutions are encouraged to conduct research on the historic and cultural city of Dai County, explore and enrich its cultural heritage, enhance its cultural quality, and present its history and culture.
articles.22: The development of tourism and cultural-industry projects using historic districts, historic-character areas, historic courtyards, historic buildings, and similar assets is encouraged and supported.
articles.23: Where a law, administrative regulation, or local regulation enacted by the People's Congress of this Province or its Standing Committee already prescribes legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, that law or regulation shall apply.
articles.24: Where a state organ or its staff member abuses official authority, neglects duties, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in protecting the historic and cultural city of Dai County, the responsible person shall be disciplined in accordance with the law if the conduct does not constitute a crime; where it constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.25: Where a person installs, moves, alters, or damages a conservation sign without authorization, in violation of the fourth paragraph of Article 14 of these Regulations, the department responsible for urban and rural development under the People's Government of Dai County shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made within that period, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 3,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.26: Where a person constructs a building or structure that damages the traditional layout or historic character, in violation of these Regulations, the planning department of the People's Government of Dai County shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the site to its original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the site or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the planning department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any resulting loss shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.27: The People's Government of Dai County shall formulate implementing rules in accordance with these Regulations.
articles.28:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 May 2021.

FBMCLI.10.8719617.title: Regulations of Chaoyang City on the Protection of Its Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen the protection of the historic and cultural city in this Municipality and to pass on and promote its outstanding history and culture, in light of local circumstances and in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to the planning, protection, use, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city in this Municipality. Where laws and regulations provide separately for the protection and administration of cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, ancient and notable trees, or other matters, those provisions shall prevail.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of scientific planning, giving priority to protection, reasonable use, and continuity and development. It shall preserve and continue the city's traditional layout and historic character, maintain the authenticity and integrity of its historical and cultural heritage, and properly balance economic and social development with heritage protection.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protecting and supervising the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas and shall incorporate such protection into their plans for national economic and social development.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall assist the relevant departments with protection and supervision and administration, and shall conduct routine inspections within their respective areas.
Villagers' committees and residents' committees shall assist township people's governments and subdistrict offices with related protection work.
articles.5:
The housing and urban-rural development departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall, together with the cultural relics departments at the same level, be responsible for protection and supervision and administration of the historic and cultural city in their respective administrative areas and shall organize the implementation of these Regulations.
Departments responsible for development and reform, education, industry and information technology, civil affairs, finance, human resources and social security, public security, natural resources, transport, agriculture and rural affairs, emergency management, forestry and grassland, and comprehensive urban administration and law enforcement, as well as fire and rescue agencies, shall perform their related protection and supervision duties in accordance with their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall include funding for protection of the historic and cultural city in their respective fiscal budgets, in accordance with the principle that financial resources shall correspond to administrative responsibilities.
They shall provide, in accordance with the law, funding to protect assets at imminent risk of loss.
articles.7:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall strengthen public education on protection of the historic and cultural city, disseminate relevant knowledge, and raise public awareness.
Radio, television, newspapers, the internet, and other media shall carry out public-interest publicity on such protection.
articles.8:
Social forces are encouraged to participate lawfully in protecting the historic and cultural city through donations, financial support, investment, technical services, volunteer services, and other means. Organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with relevant national provisions.
All organizations and individuals are entitled to submit views and suggestions on protection work and to dissuade or report conduct that damages the historic and cultural city.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall publish the channels for reporting. Relevant departments shall promptly verify and handle reports and complaints they receive.
articles.10:
Where laws and regulations already prescribe how protected assets are identified or nominated, those provisions shall apply.
To identify a historic area, the housing and urban-rural development department of the relevant county, county-level city, or district shall, together with the cultural relics department at the same level, submit a preliminary proposal. The people's government of that county, county-level city, or district shall organize an assessment and public notice, and submit the proposal to the Municipal People's Government for approval and publication.
articles.11:
The Municipal People's Government shall periodically organize the people's governments of its counties, county-level cities, and districts to survey historic towns and villages, traditional villages, historic districts, historic buildings, cultural relics, and other historical and cultural resources.
Based on the survey, the housing and urban-rural development department of each county, county-level city, or district shall, together with the cultural relics department at the same level, organize expert assessment and, in accordance with applicable identification criteria, propose a preliminary list of assets for protection and make it public.
Any organization or individual may recommend a proposed protected asset to the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located.
articles.12:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish a protection register for the historic and cultural city.
The register shall state each protected asset's name, category, location, protected area, ownership, historical development, historical value, and other relevant information, and shall be made public.
articles.13:
Assets already approved or published by a people's government at or above the county level shall be entered directly in the protection register.
For other proposed assets, the competent industry department shall, together with the housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, and other relevant departments, propose a preliminary register based on the survey of historical and cultural resources, solicit views from interested parties and the public, and submit the proposal to the people's government at the same level for approval after expert assessment and public notice.
If a protected asset is damaged or lost due to force majeure, or its protection grade or category changes, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located shall propose an adjustment to the register and submit it for approval under the original identification procedure.
articles.14:
Where an asset has not yet been entered in the protection register but the people's government of the Municipality, a county, a county-level city, or a district has preliminarily determined that it has conservation value, the government shall designate it for interim protection. Within ten working days from that designation, it shall serve the owner and user with a notice of interim protection and notify them in writing of the measures to be taken.
The interim-protection period is six months, calculated from the date the notice is issued. If the asset is not entered in the protection register before the period expires, the interim-protection measures shall cease to have effect.
If interim protection causes loss to the lawful rights or interests of an organization or individual, the relevant people's government shall provide compensation in accordance with the law.
articles.15:
The people's government of the Municipality, county, or county-level city where it is located shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic and cultural cities and historic districts. The people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic towns and villages, traditional villages, and historic areas.
A conservation plan shall be completed within one year from the date the protected asset is approved and published.
articles.16:
A conservation plan shall be submitted for approval in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
A conservation plan for a historic area shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
articles.17:
Before submitting a draft conservation plan for approval, the authority responsible for its preparation shall broadly solicit views from relevant departments, experts, and the public and may hold a hearing where necessary.
The authority responsible for preparing a conservation plan shall promptly publish the plan once it has been lawfully approved.
A lawfully approved conservation plan may not be amended without authorization. Where an amendment is necessary, the authority responsible for preparing the plan shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and may prepare an amendment only after obtaining its consent. The amended plan shall be submitted for approval under the original approval procedure.
articles.18:
Spatial-control requirements in conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, historic towns and villages, traditional villages, historic districts, historic areas, and other protected assets that concern the natural environment, traditional layout, historic character, or similar matters shall be incorporated into the territorial spatial plan at the same level.
Relevant special-purpose plans for urban transport, municipal infrastructure, landscaping, fire safety, underground-space development, and other matters shall be coordinated with conservation plans.
articles.19:
The conservation plan for a historic and cultural city shall designate protected areas for its protected assets.
For historic towns and villages, historic districts, and historic areas, the protected area shall clearly define a core conservation area and a construction-control zone.
articles.20: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall coordinate and advance implementation of conservation plans, supervise and periodically evaluate their implementation by lower-level governments and relevant departments, and publish the inspection and evaluation results through government websites, news media, and other channels for public oversight. Any problems identified shall be promptly corrected and handled.
articles.24:
This Municipality shall install conservation signs for all categories of protected assets. A conservation sign shall state the asset's subject, name, identification number, date of publication, publishing authority, and other relevant information. Its design and installation shall comply with laws, regulations, and applicable standards.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a conservation sign without authorization.
articles.25:
New buildings and structures in a construction-control zone of a historic district, historic town, or historic village shall comply with the construction controls set out in the conservation plan.
Within the core conservation area of a historic district, historic town, or historic village, new construction and expansion are prohibited except for necessary infrastructure and public-service facilities.
Before issuing a construction-project planning permit or a rural construction planning permit for necessary infrastructure or public-service facilities in such a core conservation area, the relevant department shall seek the views of the cultural relics department at the same level.
Demolition of a building, structure, or other facility other than a historic building in such a core conservation area shall be approved by the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality, county, or county-level city together with the cultural relics department at the same level.
articles.26:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall formulate and publish annual repair plans for historic buildings.
The housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality, county, county-level city, or district shall, together with the cultural relics department at the same level, prepare conservation drawings for historic buildings and implement them after approval by the people's government at the same level.
Based on the annual repair plan, the relevant housing and urban-rural development department shall notify the person responsible for each historic building and supervise and guide repairs in accordance with the conservation drawings and applicable technical standards.
articles.27: Exterior repairs or decoration, the addition of facilities, or changes to the structure or use of a historic building shall be approved by the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality, county, or county-level city together with the cultural relics department at the same level. The relevant procedures shall also be completed in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
articles.28: If a historic building is at risk of damage and the responsible person lacks the capacity to maintain or repair it, the people's government of the Municipality, county, county-level city, or district shall promptly take protective measures. If the responsible person has the capacity but refuses to perform the maintenance or repair duties, the people's government shall take measures to remove the danger, and the responsible person shall bear the costs.
articles.31:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish and improve a routine inspection and administration mechanism for protecting the historic and cultural city and incorporate inspections into community grid-based management.
Departments responsible for protected assets shall monitor them using video surveillance, remote sensing, and other means, and promptly detect, stop, and handle unlawful conduct that damages protected assets or installs, moves, alters, or damages conservation signs without authorization.
When conducting routine inspections, township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall assist the relevant departments with safety and disaster-prevention work. They shall investigate violations of the protection rules in accordance with the law or notify the relevant department to do so. Major incidents shall be promptly reported to the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district.
articles.32:
The protection, continuity, and reasonable use of the historic and cultural city are encouraged, as is the development of tourism and cultural industries, provided that local natural landscapes, cultural landscapes, and historical and cultural resources are not damaged.
The people's government of each county, county-level city, and district shall formulate positive and negative lists for the protection and use of each category of protected asset, periodically evaluate the lists, and adjust them as needed.
articles.34: Use of historic towns and villages, traditional villages, historic districts, historic areas, and historic buildings shall protect the lawful rights and interests of original residents and maintain the continuity of traditional ways of life.
articles.35:
The housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, and other relevant departments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall organize professional training in traditional techniques related to protection of the historic and cultural city.
Departments responsible for education, human resources, and social security shall support and guide universities, vocational schools, and technical schools in offering programs or courses on techniques for protecting historical and cultural heritage and in training practitioners of traditional techniques.
articles.36: Where laws and regulations already prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.37: Where a state organ or its staff member violates these Regulations by abusing approval authority, failing to perform duties, or failing to investigate discovered unlawful conduct, the responsible person in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be disciplined in accordance with the law. Where the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.38:
For the purposes of these Regulations:
(1) ‘historic area’ means an area that authentically reflects the traditional character and ethnic or local features of a particular historical period;
(2) ‘historic district’ means an area designated and published by the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, with an especially rich concentration of cultural relics and historic buildings, that substantially and authentically reflects the traditional layout and historic character and is of a certain scale; and
(3) ‘historic building’ means a building or structure designated and published by the people's government of a city or county for its conservation value and ability to reflect historic character and local features, but not published as a cultural relics protection unit or registered as an immovable cultural relic.
articles.39: These Regulations shall take effect on 15 April 2025.

FBMCLI.17.652269.title: Regulations of Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City of Huili

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to regulate the protection, administration, and use of the historic and cultural city of Huili and to promote cultural and social harmony, in light of local circumstances and in accordance with relevant national laws and regulations.
articles.2: For the purposes of these Regulations, the ‘protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili’ means the buildings and streets within the historic and cultural city of Huili County, as well as cultural relics, historic sites, ancient ruins, and scenic areas within the administrative area of Huili County that represent Huili's history and culture.
articles.3: Protection, administration, and use of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall follow the principles of scientific planning, effective protection, reasonable use, and strict administration. They shall preserve and continue the city's traditional layout and historic character and maintain the authenticity and integrity of its historical and cultural heritage.
articles.4:
The protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili is divided into a key conservation area, an environmental-character coordination zone, and a county-level historical and cultural environment protection zone.
(1) The ‘key conservation area’ means the core conservation area and construction-control zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili.
(2) The ‘environmental-character coordination zone’ means the area designated within 40 metres outside the key conservation area, primarily to protect natural topography and landforms.
(3) The ‘county-level historical and cultural environment protection zone’ means the ‘Two Routes and Nine Areas.’ The ‘Two Routes’ are the ancient Southern Silk Road and the route taken through Huili by the Red Army during the Long March. The ‘Nine Areas’ are Jiaopingdu, the Luchang green-ceramics area, the Lixi copper-mine area, the Ancient City of Huili, the Xiaohuangjing Yi-culture area, the Songpingguan historical and cultural environment area, the provincial-level Longzhoushan Scenic Area, the Taiping karst landscape area, and the Beimu Mountain forest area.
The specific boundaries of the protection zones shall be determined by plans formulated by the People's Government of Huili County.
articles.5:
The People's Government of Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture and its relevant departments shall strengthen their guidance and support for protection of the historic and cultural city of Huili.
The People's Government of Huili County shall be responsible for protecting, administering, and using the historic and cultural city of Huili. Relevant county departments shall carry out specific protection work in accordance with their respective responsibilities.
articles.6: Citizens, legal persons, and other social organizations have a duty to protect the historic and cultural city of Huili and are entitled to report and complain about conduct that damages it.
articles.7: Government funding shall be the primary source of funding for protection of the historic and cultural city of Huili. Social donations and private investment are encouraged.
articles.8: The People's Government of Huili County and its relevant departments shall commend and reward citizens, legal persons, and other social organizations that make outstanding contributions to protecting, administering, or using the historic and cultural city of Huili, in accordance with relevant national provisions.
articles.9: The People's Government of Huili County shall, in accordance with relevant national provisions and in light of conservation needs, prepare or adjust a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of Huili. The plan shall be implemented after approval by the Provincial People's Government and publication to the public.
articles.10: A conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of Huili shall be prepared in accordance with the policy of giving priority to protection while allowing reasonable development and use.
articles.11: The People's Government of Huili County shall prepare construction and repair plans for historic streets and lanes, traditional residences and courtyards, and scenic areas in the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili. The relevant departments shall organize their implementation.
articles.12: The People's Government of Huili County shall supervise and inspect implementation of the plan in accordance with these Regulations.
articles.14: Protection and use of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall strictly comply with earthquake-resistance, fire-safety, and other applicable safety standards.
articles.15: Historic streets and lanes, traditional residences and courtyards, scenic areas, and other protected places in the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall be protected by category through measures such as creating records and installing conservation plaques.
articles.16: All construction, development, and use within the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall comply with relevant national laws and regulations and these Regulations, and conform to the Huili County master urban plan and the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of Huili as approved by the Provincial People's Government.
articles.17:
The People's Government of Huili County shall, in accordance with the law and in a planned manner, relocate residents living in traditional residences and courtyards.
Municipal facilities and public utilities for water, electricity, gas, transport, communications, sanitation, fire safety, and other services in the protection zone shall be progressively improved.
articles.18:
Renovation of historic streets and lanes, and construction or repair of historic buildings, traditional residential courtyards with conservation plaques, historic sites, and scenic areas in the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall follow a repair plan determined by the County People's Government. After expert review, the plan shall be submitted for approval in accordance with applicable laws.
Repairs to other traditional residences and courtyards require approval by the relevant departments.
Construction or repair of religious venues shall comply with urban planning, respect the architectural style of the religious venue, and be submitted for approval under the prescribed procedures.
articles.19: No organization or individual may demolish without authorization a traditional residence or historic building in the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili, or any architectural or decorative component thereof, including doors, windows, plaques, inscribed boards, and beams. No one may alter or decorate a historic building in a manner that affects its historic character or traditional layout.
articles.20: Street advertisements, shop signs, signs, and markers in the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall be compatible with the character of the ancient city.
articles.21: No citizen, legal person, or other social organization may install, move, alter, or damage a conservation sign or marker for the historic and cultural city of Huili without authorization.
articles.22: Ancient and notable trees and old wells in the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall be uniformly documented and protected by conservation plaques. No citizen, legal person, or other social organization may damage, fill in, fell, or relocate them without authorization.
articles.23: Production or storage of flammable or explosive hazardous substances is prohibited in the key conservation area of the historic and cultural city of Huili. Fireworks and firecrackers may not be set off within its core conservation area.
articles.24: Poultry, livestock, and pets may not be allowed to roam freely in streets, lanes, or public places in the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili. Premises for slaughtering pigs, cattle, sheep, or other livestock may not be established in the key conservation area.
articles.25:
No industrial enterprise or building or structure inconsistent with the architectural character of the ancient city may be newly constructed in the key conservation area of the historic and cultural city of Huili.
Buildings, structures, and industrial enterprises inconsistent with the character of the ancient city shall be renovated, demolished, or relocated.
articles.26: Clean energy shall be promoted in the key conservation area of the historic and cultural city of Huili, and the use of raw coal and firewood shall be phased out. It is prohibited to burn asphalt, roofing felt, rubber, plastic, leather, or other substances that produce toxic or hazardous smoke or gases.
articles.27: No enterprise or workshop that pollutes the environment by producing noise, dust, toxic or hazardous gases, or other pollutants may be established in the key conservation area of the historic and cultural city of Huili.
articles.28: Motor vehicle traffic shall be strictly controlled in the key conservation area of the historic and cultural city of Huili.
articles.29: Entertainment venues established in the key conservation area of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall be compatible with the traditional culture of the ancient city.
articles.30:
All buildings in the construction-control zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall be compatible with the architectural character of its core conservation area.
The layout, height, form, colors, and style of groups of buildings in the construction-control zone shall not impair the ancient city's traditional spatial character. Multi-storey or high-rise buildings that obstruct important view corridors, and buildings that damage the historic environment of the core conservation area, shall be systematically reduced in height or demolished.
articles.31: Protection of cultural relics and archaeological excavations in the protection zone of the historic and cultural city of Huili shall comply with the relevant provisions of the Law on the Protection of Cultural Relics.
articles.32: The People's Government of Huili County shall strengthen the protection, exploration, collection, organization, and study of the traditional culture, arts, folk customs, and ethnic traditions of the historic and cultural city.
articles.34: A violation of these Regulations shall be corrected or the original condition restored within a specified period, as ordered by the People's Government of Huili County. In serious cases, the person concerned shall be subject to administrative penalties under national laws and regulations. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law. Where the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.35: Where a violation of these Regulations damages cultural relics, penalties shall be imposed in accordance with national laws and regulations on the protection of cultural relics. Where the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.36: Where a relevant department or its staff member fails to perform supervision and administration duties, fails to investigate unlawful conduct, or otherwise abuses official authority, neglects duties, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in violation of these Regulations, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law if the conduct constitutes a crime; otherwise, the person shall be disciplined in accordance with the law.
articles.37: The People's Government of Huili County shall, in light of the actual protection work and in accordance with these Regulations, formulate specific administration measures.
articles.38:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 August 2012.

FBMCLI.10.5520945.title: Regulations of Henan Province on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities (2010 Amendment)

articles.1:
These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of historic and cultural cities in light of the circumstances of this Province and in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws and regulations.

PKULaw related materials
Laws and regulations · Local regulations (1)
articles.2: These Regulations apply to the protection, planning, construction, and administration of historic and cultural cities within the administrative area of this Province.
articles.3: For the purposes of these Regulations, a ‘historic and cultural city’ means a city designated and published by the State Council that preserves an especially rich collection of cultural relics and has major historical value or revolutionary commemorative significance.
articles.4:
People's governments at all levels shall protect historic and cultural cities within their respective administrative areas, incorporate protection into their plans for national economic and social development, and include protection funding in their fiscal budgets.
All sectors of society are encouraged and supported in participating in protection through donations, financial support, and other means.
articles.5: Protection of historic and cultural cities shall follow the principles of scientific planning, focus on key matters, effective protection, reasonable use, and strengthened administration, and shall properly balance protection and construction.
articles.6: The people's government where a historic and cultural city is located and its relevant departments shall use historic remains and revolutionary sites for education on patriotism and revolutionary traditions, raise public awareness of protecting the city and its cultural and natural resources, and promote civic culture.
articles.7:
The urban planning and cultural relics administrative departments where a historic and cultural city is located shall be responsible, in accordance with their respective duties, for the city's planning, protection, administration, and oversight.
Departments responsible for development and reform, finance, tourism, transport, environmental protection, public security, fire safety, and other relevant matters shall jointly protect the historic and cultural city in accordance with their respective duties.
articles.8:
All organizations and individuals have a duty to protect historic and cultural cities and are entitled to dissuade, stop, or report conduct that damages them.
People's governments at all levels and the relevant departments shall commend or reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection work.
articles.9: The people's government where a historic and cultural city is located shall promptly organize preparation of a conservation plan. After review and approval by the people's congress at the same level or its standing committee, the plan shall be submitted for approval under the prescribed procedure.
articles.10: A conservation plan for a historic and cultural city shall include overall conservation objectives, conservation matters, protected areas, conservation standards, measures to ensure implementation, and other relevant content.
articles.12: A conservation plan for a historic and cultural city shall be supported by scientific assessment, and views shall be broadly solicited from relevant departments, experts and scholars, and the public.
articles.13: For key conservation areas, traditional-character coordination zones, and key protected buildings designated in a conservation plan, the urban planning administrative department shall, together with the cultural relics administrative department, prepare detailed plans, reasonably determine the principal planning controls, and install signs marking the protected areas. Detailed plans for key conservation areas and traditional-character coordination zones shall be approved by the provincial urban planning administrative department after it obtains the consent of the provincial cultural relics administrative department.
articles.14: The people's government where a historic and cultural city is located may make appropriate adjustments to its conservation plan in light of local circumstances and submit the adjusted plan for approval under the original procedure. A major adjustment shall be reviewed and approved by the people's congress at the same level or its standing committee before being submitted for approval.
articles.15: The people's government where a historic and cultural city is located shall promptly publish the approved conservation plan and the detailed plans for key conservation areas and traditional-character coordination zones.
articles.16: Land use and all construction within the urban planning area of a historic and cultural city shall comply with its conservation plan.
articles.17:
Without lawful review and consent by the provincial urban planning administrative department and the provincial cultural relics administrative department, the locality where a historic and cultural city is located may not, without authorization, widen roads within an area covered by its conservation plan or carry out redevelopment of the old city, or arrange construction projects in key conservation areas or traditional-character coordination zones.

PKULaw related materials
Judicial cases · Judicial cases (1)
articles.18: Construction in new urban areas and redevelopment of old urban areas of a historic and cultural city shall comply with its conservation plan and shall not damage the city's traditional character or layout.
articles.19: Where a building or structure designated for protection under a conservation plan for a historic and cultural city needs repair, it shall be repaired in its original form, under the guidance and supervision of the cultural relics administrative department. A construction project in a traditional-character coordination zone shall be compatible with the city's landscape and character in its layout, use, height, scale, form, color, building density, and other respects. Its planning or design proposal shall be submitted to the provincial urban planning administrative department and the provincial cultural relics administrative department for lawful review and approval.
articles.21: The urban planning and cultural relics administrative departments where a historic and cultural city is located shall establish and improve archival systems in accordance with the law, and collect, organize, and preserve records concerning the city's development and history.
articles.22: Where an organization causes serious environmental pollution, endangers the safety of cultural relics, or damages the character or landscape of a historic and cultural city, the local people's government shall, in accordance with the law, order it to remedy the situation within a specified period, close, or relocate.
articles.23: The urban planning administrative department where a historic and cultural city is located shall, together with the cultural relics administrative department, oversee and inspect protection work, promptly correct and handle violations of these Regulations, and report serious violations of the conservation plan to the people's government at the same level and the higher-level competent departments.
articles.24: The people's government where a historic and cultural city is located shall periodically report on its protection work to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level and accept its oversight.
articles.25: Where urban planning, cultural relics protection, or another relevant law or regulation prescribes an administrative penalty for conduct violating these Regulations, that law or regulation shall apply.
articles.26: Where the people's government where a historic and cultural city is located or one of its relevant departments changes or fails to implement the conservation plan without authorization, causing major loss or serious consequences, the persons in charge and persons directly responsible shall be subject to administrative sanctions in accordance with the law. Where the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.27:
For conduct described in item (1) of paragraph 1 of Article 20 that does not involve cultural relics, the urban planning administrative department shall order the person to stop the damage and make corrections within a specified period, and may impose a fine of not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for.
For conduct described in item (2) of paragraph 1 of Article 20, the cultural relics administrative department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct, take remedial measures within a specified period, and impose penalties in accordance with the law.
For conduct described in item (3) of paragraph 1 of Article 20, the urban planning administrative department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and take remedial measures within a specified period, and may impose a fine of not less than RMB 5,000 but not more than RMB 20,000.
For conduct described in items (4), (5), or (6) of paragraph 1 of Article 20, the urban planning administrative department or another relevant administrative department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct, make corrections within a specified period, and impose penalties in accordance with the law.

PKULaw related materials
Laws and regulations · Regulatory documents (1)
articles.28:
Where a staff member of an urban planning, cultural relics, or other relevant department commits any of the following acts in protecting a historic and cultural city, the staff member's employer or a higher-level competent department shall order correction or impose an administrative sanction. Where the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law:
(1) failing to prepare, submit, or review a conservation plan as required;
(2) failing to organize protection in accordance with the conservation plan, thereby damaging historic physical remains or traditional character; or
(3) otherwise abusing official authority, neglecting duties, or engaging in malpractice for personal gain.
articles.29: Protection work for provincial-level historic and cultural cities approved and published by the Provincial People's Government before these Regulations take effect shall be carried out with reference to these Regulations.
articles.30:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 October 2005.

FBMCLI.10.9518646.title: Regulations of Huai'an Municipality on the Protection of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an, carry on the city's historical heritage, and promote outstanding traditional culture, in light of local circumstances and in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages issued by the State Council, the Regulations of Jiangsu Province on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities and Towns, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to protection of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an and related activities.
For the purposes of these Regulations, the ‘National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an’ means Huai'an, which was designated a national historic and cultural city by the State Council in 1986.
articles.4: Protection of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an shall follow the principles of giving priority to protection, scientific planning, living continuity, and shared conservation and benefits. It shall properly balance protection and use, inheritance and development, preserve and continue the traditional layout and historic character, and maintain the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage.
articles.5:
The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protecting the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an, incorporate protection into its plans for national economic and social development, provide policy support, and allocate dedicated funding in its fiscal budget.
The municipal housing and urban-rural development department shall, together with the relevant departments, review and submit conservation plans for approval and supervise their implementation.
The municipal department responsible for natural resources and planning shall administer planning for the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an.
The municipal department responsible for culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism (cultural relics) shall supervise and administer the protection of cultural relics and intangible cultural heritage within the protected area.
articles.7: With the approval of the Municipal People's Government, the People's Government of Huai'an District shall, together with the municipal housing and urban-rural development department and other departments, establish an expert-advisory mechanism. It shall select experts in urban planning, construction, culture, cultural relics, water conservancy, transport, landscaping, fire safety, law, and other relevant fields to form an Expert Advisory Committee for the Protection of the National Historic and Cultural City. The Committee shall participate in assessment and review of major matters and projects concerning conservation plans, the protection register, and construction administration, and provide relevant recommendations.
articles.8: Organizations and individuals are encouraged and guided to participate lawfully in protecting the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an through donations, financial support, investment, establishing nonprofit organizations, providing technical services or volunteer services, and other means.
articles.9: The protection register for the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an shall classify protected assets and state their names, locations, dates of origin, responsible persons, and other relevant information. Protected assets approved and published by the State Council, the Provincial People's Government, or the Municipal People's Government shall be entered directly in the register.
articles.10: Conservation signs for all categories of protected assets shall comply with applicable laws, regulations, and standards and be compatible with the traditional character of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an.
articles.11:
Construction within the protected area of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an shall comply with the conservation plan, respect the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage, and continue the traditional layout, street and lane pattern, local character, and historic appearance in matters such as height, scale, exterior appearance, color, materials, and techniques.
Within the historic urban area, historic districts, and historic areas, the character and quality of those places may be enhanced in connection with urban renewal and residents' needs for a better life. Public open space may be added reasonably, and the provision of municipal infrastructure and public services may be expanded.
articles.15:
A historic area shall focus on protecting its overall character and continuing its historical heritage, while combining protection with reasonable use to sustain its vitality.
Construction within a historic area shall not alter its traditional layout or character.
articles.16:
No organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization.
Repairs or maintenance, the addition of facilities, or changes to the structure or use of a historic building shall not damage its historical or artistic features or its spatial or architectural character.
articles.17:
The owner of a historic building shall maintain and repair it in accordance with the conservation plan. The People's Government of Huai'an District may provide a subsidy as prescribed.
The owner is entitled to receive information and technical guidance on protection, repair, and use from departments responsible for natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, and culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism (cultural relics).
If a historic building is at risk of damage and its owner lacks the capacity to maintain or repair it, the People's Government of Huai'an District shall take measures to protect and urgently repair it.
articles.18: Where a house other than a historic building in the core conservation area of a historic district needs repair, the conservation plan shall be implemented and the traditional character of the house—including its height, scale, exterior appearance, and colors—shall be preserved.
articles.19:
Continuity and use of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an shall follow the principle that appropriate use promotes protection, advance adaptive use, and carry on its history and culture.
The Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Huai'an District shall strengthen the collection, organization, research, and protection of historical and cultural resources such as notable people, works, and food, and support their creative transformation and innovative development.
The cultural meaning of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an is encouraged to be fully explored, and cultural tourism activities are encouraged to make use of the resources of the historic and cultural city.
articles.20:
The People's Government of Huai'an District shall lawfully formulate lists of industries to encourage, control, or prohibit. It shall support modern services such as technological creativity, digital empowerment, cultural tourism, and distinctive commerce, and enhance the city's functions for cultural continuity, tourism and leisure, and development of traditional industries.
Social forces are encouraged to use historical resources reasonably to develop industries that meet conservation requirements and conduct business consistent with the industrial layout.
articles.21: The Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Huai'an District shall establish a compensation system for protection of the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an and compensate organizations and individuals in accordance with the law where protection causes harm to their lawful rights and interests.
articles.22: The People's Government of Huai'an District shall organize routine inspections of the National Historic and Cultural City and promptly address, dissuade, or stop conduct that endangers protected assets.
articles.23: Where laws or regulations already prescribe penalties for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.24: An administrative organ or its staff member who neglects duties, abuses official authority, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in protecting the National Historic and Cultural City of Huai'an shall be disciplined in accordance with the law. Where the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.25: Where the power to grant administrative approvals is relatively centralized in a relevant field or area, comprehensive administrative law enforcement is implemented, or a township people's government or subdistrict office assumes relevant powers, the applicable national and provincial provisions shall apply.
articles.26: The people's governments of other counties and districts in this Municipality shall carry out historical and cultural conservation work in their respective administrative areas with reference to the specific protection duties assigned to the People's Government of Huai'an District by these Regulations.
articles.27:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2026.

Announcement of the Standing Committee of the 9th Yueyang Municipal People's Congress
(No. 5 of 2025)

The Decision of the Standing Committee of the Yueyang Municipal People's Congress on Amending Several Local Regulations was adopted at the 32nd Session of the Standing Committee of the 9th Yueyang Municipal People's Congress on 25 July 2025 and approved at the 18th Session of the Standing Committee of the 14th People's Congress of Hunan Province on 26 September 2025. It is hereby promulgated and shall take effect on the date of promulgation.
Standing Committee of the Yueyang Municipal People's Congress
11 October 2025

Decision of the Standing Committee of the Yueyang Municipal People's Congress on Amending Several Local Regulations
(Adopted on 25 July 2025 at the 32nd Session of the Standing Committee of the 9th Yueyang Municipal People's Congress; approved on 26 September 2025 at the 18th Session of the Standing Committee of the 14th People's Congress of Hunan Province)

At its 32nd Session, the Standing Committee of the 9th Yueyang Municipal People's Congress decides to amend the following local regulations:

I. Amendments to the Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities
(1) The first paragraph of Article 3 is amended to read: “The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protecting and supervising historic and cultural cities, establish and improve a coordination mechanism for their protection, and consider major matters relating to their protection.”
(2) The first and fourth paragraphs of Article 4 are combined and amended to read: “The municipal housing and urban-rural development department shall, together with the competent cultural relics department, handle the specific work of protecting and supervising historic and cultural cities. The municipal and district housing and urban-rural development departments shall supervise and administer repair of historic buildings and their safe use within protected areas of historic and cultural cities.” In the third paragraph, ‘culture department’ is replaced with ‘culture and tourism department.’
(3) Article 5 is deleted.
(4) Article 12 is renumbered as Article 11. In item (2), ‘historic buildings and cultural relics protection units’ is replaced with ‘cultural relics protection units and historic buildings,’ and ‘Lucheng Historic District’ is replaced with ‘Lucheng South and North Main Street Historic District.’
(5) Article 15 is renumbered as Article 14. The words ‘after deliberation and approval by the Municipal Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee’ are deleted, and ‘urban and rural planning department’ is replaced with ‘housing and urban-rural development department.’
(6) Articles 18, 25, 27, and 29 are renumbered as Articles 17, 24, 26, and 28, respectively. In each, ‘urban and rural planning department’ is replaced with ‘housing and urban-rural development department.’
(7) Article 31 is renumbered as Article 30. In its first paragraph, ‘culture department’ is replaced with ‘culture and tourism department.’
(8) Article 35 is renumbered as Article 34. In items (1) and (2), ‘urban and rural planning department’ is replaced with ‘housing and urban-rural development department’; in item (4), ‘culture department’ is replaced with ‘culture and tourism department’; in item (5), ‘housing administration department’ is replaced with ‘housing and urban-rural development department’; and in item (6) and the fifth paragraph of Article 4, ‘the relevant departments of development and reform, finance, housing and urban-rural development, land and resources, urban administration, forestry, and other matters’ is replaced with ‘the relevant departments of development and reform, finance, natural resources and planning, urban administration and comprehensive law enforcement, forestry, industry and information technology, water conservancy, civil affairs, and other matters.’
(9) Article 36 is renumbered as Article 35. ‘Urban administration’ is replaced with ‘urban administration and comprehensive law enforcement.’
(10) Article 37 is renumbered as Article 36 and amended to read: “Within the urban planning area of Yueyang Municipality, the People's Governments of Yueyang County and Linxiang City and the Administrative Committee of Nanhu New Area shall perform the duties assigned to district people's governments under Article 3 of these Regulations.”

II. Amendments to the Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Prevention and Control of Dust Pollution
The words ‘Yueyang Economic and Technological Development Zone and Hunan Chenglingji New Port Area’ are deleted from Article 37.

III. Amendments to the Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Administration of Rural Villagers' Housing Construction
(1) In Article 21, ‘ten working days’ is replaced with ‘five working days.’
(2) The words ‘Yueyang Economic and Technological Development Zone and Hunan Chenglingji New Port Area’ are deleted from the first paragraph of Article 32.

IV. Amendments to the Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Promotion of Civilized Conduct
(1) The first paragraph of Article 4 is amended to read: “A special working mechanism for public morality shall be established at the municipal, county, county-level city, and district levels to coordinate and advance the promotion of civilized conduct within their respective administrative areas.” The words ‘assessment and evaluation’ are deleted from the second paragraph, and ‘every year’ is replaced with ‘as appropriate.’
(2) The following words are added after ‘do not occupy or block safety exits, evacuation routes, fire lanes, or other public facilities or public areas’ in item (4) of Article 11: ‘and do not park electric bicycles or charge them in indoor public areas, fire lanes, or near combustible materials.’
(3) The words ‘the municipal and county (county-level city or district) steering committees for public morality and their working bodies’ are deleted from the first paragraph of Article 18. In the second paragraph, ‘organize activities to create civilized communities, industries, markets, tourist scenic areas, restaurants, and other model entities’ is replaced with ‘carry out initiatives across all sectors of society to cultivate civilized conduct.’
(4) In Article 19, ‘select’ is replaced with ‘identify and promote.’
(5) The words ‘Yueyang Economic and Technological Development Zone and Hunan Chenglingji New Port Area’ are deleted from Article 42.

V. Amendments to the Yueyang Municipality Provisions on the Administration of Road-Transport Stations for Dangerous Goods
(1) The word ‘sampling’ is deleted from item (3) of Article 5, and ‘discharge’ is added before ‘pressure relief.’
(2) The words ‘Yueyang Economic and Technological Development Zone and Hunan Chenglingji New Port Area’ are deleted from Article 9.

Article numbering in the relevant regulations shall also be adjusted accordingly.

This Decision shall take effect on the date of promulgation. The Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities, the Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Prevention and Control of Dust Pollution, the Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Administration of Rural Villagers' Housing Construction, the Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Promotion of Civilized Conduct, and the Yueyang Municipality Provisions on the Administration of Road-Transport Stations for Dangerous Goods shall be amended accordingly and repromulgated.
