FBMCLI.10.7179694.title: Regulations of Chuzhou Municipality on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of historic and cultural cities and carry on and promote China's outstanding traditional culture, in light of local circumstances and in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages issued by the State Council, and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to the planning, research, protection, use, and administration of historic and cultural cities within the administrative area of this Municipality. Where laws or regulations separately prescribe the protection and administration of cultural relics, ancient and notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, or other matters, those provisions shall apply.
articles.3: Protection of historic and cultural cities shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, continuity and development, and reasonable use, and shall properly balance economic and social development with the protection of historical and cultural heritage.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protection of historic and cultural cities in their respective administrative areas, incorporate protection into their plans for national economic and social development, establish and improve protection mechanisms, and allocate protection funding in their fiscal budgets in light of local circumstances.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall carry out specific work within their respective areas, including routine inspections and public outreach concerning protection of historic and cultural cities.
Villagers' committees and residents' committees shall assist township people's governments and subdistrict offices with protection work.
articles.5:
The competent housing and urban-rural development department shall, together with the culture and tourism department, handle specific work concerning designation, preparation and implementation of conservation plans, supervision, and administration of historic and cultural cities.
Departments responsible for development and reform, natural resources and planning, public security, finance, urban administration, transport, agriculture and rural affairs, ecology and environment, forestry, and other matters, as well as fire and rescue agencies, shall protect historic and cultural cities in accordance with their respective duties.
articles.6:
All organizations and individuals are entitled to submit views and suggestions on protection work and to dissuade or report conduct that damages historic and cultural cities.
Enterprises and public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection through donations, financial support, volunteer services, and other means.
articles.7: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection of historic and cultural cities, in accordance with relevant national and provincial provisions.
articles.9:
Under the conservation plan for the Ancient City of Chuzhou, its protected area extends north to the junction of Xijian North Road and the railway, west to Xijian Road, south to Mingguang Road, and east to the Jinpu Railway.
The People's Government of Fengyang County shall, in accordance with the conservation plan for the Ancient City of Fengyang, determine its protected area and protected assets.
articles.10:
A protection-register system shall apply to historic and cultural cities.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall survey historical and cultural resources. Based on the survey, the competent housing and urban-rural development department shall, together with the relevant departments, organize expert assessment and, in accordance with applicable identification criteria, propose a preliminary protection register and make it public for at least 30 days. After the public-notice period, the register shall be submitted to the people's government at the same level for approval and publication. Protected assets approved or designated and published by the State Council or by a provincial, municipal, county, county-level city, or district people's government shall be entered directly in the register.
The register shall state the name, location, historical development, historical value, protection grade, protected area, and other relevant information for each protected asset. It shall be completed within one year after these Regulations take effect.
Any organization or individual may recommend that historical or cultural heritage with conservation value be entered in the register.
articles.11:
The people's government of the Municipality, county, county-level city, or district where a historic and cultural city is located shall prepare a conservation plan in accordance with the law and submit it for approval under the prescribed procedure. The conservation plan shall be incorporated into the territorial spatial plan at the same level. Other special-purpose plans shall be coordinated with it when prepared or amended.
Conservation plans for historic districts, historic towns and villages, and traditional villages shall lawfully designate core conservation areas and construction-control zones.
The protected area of a historic building shall include the building itself and any necessary construction-control zone.
articles.14:
Construction within a protected area of a historic district, historic town, or historic village shall comply with the conservation plan, shall not impair the authenticity or integrity of historical and cultural heritage or damage its traditional layout or historic character, and shall meet the following requirements:
(1) within a core conservation area, new construction and expansion are prohibited except for necessary infrastructure and public-service facilities. Such facilities shall combine conservation with improvements to people's livelihoods; the use of traditional techniques and materials is encouraged to preserve the traditional layout and historic character; and
(2) new construction, reconstruction, and expansion within a construction-control zone shall comply with applicable construction controls, reflect traditional architecture and spatial form, and strictly control the form, height, scale, style, and colors of buildings and structures so that they remain compatible with the traditional layout and historic character of the core conservation area.
articles.15:
Traditional villages shall be protected as a whole, preserving and continuing their traditional layout and historic character and not altering the natural environment and landscape on which they depend.
Construction in a traditional village shall comply with the village plan and conservation plan. Building form, height, scale, style, colors, construction, and decoration shall be compatible with the village's overall traditional character.
articles.16:
Historic buildings shall be protected in accordance with conservation drawings. The municipal or county, county-level city, or district housing and urban-rural development department shall, as required by the drawings, specify each building's conservation category, key features to be protected, conservation requirements, and requirements for reasonable use.
Historic buildings shall be maintained and repaired in accordance with the conservation plan and drawings. Repairs shall not alter their original form, height, scale, style, colors, or other features.
articles.17:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall install conservation signs within three months after publishing the protection register. The signs shall be compatible with the traditional character.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, obscure, or damage a conservation sign without authorization.
articles.21:
Where a historic building is found to be at risk of damage, the person responsible shall promptly perform the duties of maintenance and repair. If the building is certified as a dangerous building, the municipal or county, county-level city, or district housing and urban-rural development department shall require the responsible person to take remedial measures immediately. If the responsible person lacks the capacity to maintain or repair the building, the people's government at the relevant level shall take measures to protect it.
The owner shall bear the costs of maintaining and repairing a historic building. The people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county, county-level city, or district may provide a subsidy. Any separate agreement between the owner and user on those costs shall apply.
articles.22: The protection, continuity, and reasonable use of historic and cultural cities are encouraged and supported. Their cultural meaning should be fully explored so that protection and use are coordinated.
articles.25:
Where laws or regulations already prescribe penalties for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
Matters involving relatively centralized administrative penalty powers or comprehensive law enforcement by townships shall be handled in accordance with relevant national and provincial provisions.
articles.26:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2024.

FBMCLI.10.60978.title: Regulations of Changsha Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of the historic and cultural city of Changsha and carry on and promote its outstanding history and culture, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations and in light of local circumstances.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to the protection, administration, and use of the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
articles.4: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of coordinated planning, effective protection, giving priority to emergency safeguarding, reasonable use, and scientific administration, and shall properly balance protection and construction.
articles.5: The Municipal People's Government shall exercise unified leadership over protection of the historic and cultural city. The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts, counties, and county-level cities shall incorporate protection into their plans for national economic and social development and allocate dedicated funding in their fiscal budgets.
articles.6:
The municipal planning administrative department shall, together with the municipal construction and culture administrative departments, be responsible for protection of the historic and cultural city.
Municipal administrative departments responsible for land, housing, tourism, environmental protection, landscaping, religious affairs, commerce, civil affairs, industry and commerce, press and publishing, radio and television, education, urban administration, and other matters shall protect the historic and cultural city and promote public awareness in accordance with their respective duties.
Relevant departments of the people's governments of districts, counties, and county-level cities shall carry out related protection work within their respective areas.
articles.7:
Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations are encouraged and supported in participating lawfully in protection, development and use, and scientific research concerning the historic and cultural city through investment, donations, and other means.
All organizations and individuals have a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and are entitled to report, complain about, and stop conduct that damages it.
The Municipal People's Government shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection work.
articles.8:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of a special conservation plan for the historic and cultural city in accordance with the urban master plan, and shall publish and implement it after approval.
Based on the special conservation plan, the municipal planning administrative department shall, together with the construction and culture administrative departments, prepare regulatory detailed plans and site-development detailed plans for historic-character conservation areas, historic districts, and historic towns and villages, and publish and implement them after approval by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.9: A special conservation plan for the historic and cultural city shall focus on protecting its character, layout, and environment and create conditions for reasonable use. It shall specify the overall conservation objectives, principles, and matters to be protected; designate protected areas and construction-control zones for historic-character conservation areas, historic districts, historic towns and villages, cultural relics protection units, other immovable cultural relics, and historic buildings; designate underground cultural relics burial areas; and set out control requirements and conservation measures.
articles.10:
No organization or individual may amend, alter, or refuse to implement without authorization an approved special conservation plan for the historic and cultural city or its regulatory or site-development detailed plans. Any adjustment or amendment to a published plan shall be submitted for approval under the original procedure.
When preparing or revising the special conservation plan or its regulatory or site-development detailed plans, the responsible authority shall broadly solicit views from all sectors of society and organize expert review.
articles.11:
The planning, construction, culture, and other administrative departments shall strictly implement the special conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, strengthen review and oversight of construction projects related to protection, and investigate and handle unlawful construction.
Buildings and facilities that do not conform to the special conservation plan or its regulatory or site-development detailed plans shall be progressively renovated or demolished as required by the plan.
articles.12: A ‘historic-character conservation area’ means an urban area where immovable cultural relics, historic buildings, and other historic remains are relatively concentrated and which reflects the historical and cultural character of Changsha during a particular period.
articles.13: The Municipal People's Government shall publish the protected areas and key protected matters for the historic-character conservation areas of Yuelu Mountain, Xiaoximen, Tianxin Pavilion, Chaozong Street, Kaifu Temple, and other areas, in accordance with the approved urban master plan.
articles.14:
Construction within a protected area or construction-control zone of a historic-character conservation area shall preserve, to the extent possible, the original natural environment and distinctive character, and protect immovable cultural relics, historic buildings, and street and lane patterns that reflect the area's history and culture.
The height, scale, form, colors, use, and other features of a new or reconstructed building shall comply with the special conservation plan and its regulatory and site-development detailed plans, as well as ecological and environmental-protection requirements.
articles.15: Outdoor advertisements and similar facilities in a historic-character conservation area shall be compatible with its environment and landscape. Outdoor advertisements are prohibited on landmark features of the area's landscape.
articles.16: Where a town, street, or village within this administrative area preserves an especially rich collection of cultural relics and has major historical value or revolutionary commemorative significance, the Municipal People's Government shall apply in accordance with the law for its designation as a historic district or historic town or village.
articles.17: The area centered on Taiping Street, extending east to Taipingli, Jiangningli, and their northern extensions; south to Jiefang West Road; west to Weiguo Street; and north to Majia Lane and the section on the south side of Wuyi Avenue east of Taiping Street, shall preserve its historic buildings, street and lane pattern, and overall character, with particular emphasis on the period from the Ming and Qing dynasties through the founding of the People's Republic of China.
articles.18: After a historic district is approved in accordance with the law, the Municipal People's Government shall install conservation signs. The relevant administrative departments shall strengthen protection of the district, improve its infrastructure and public utilities, and improve the living environment.
articles.19: A historic district shall preserve its traditional street and lane pattern, distinctive road surfaces, and historic place names; protect its historic buildings; and restore its historic cultural and human landscape.
articles.20:
New construction, reconstruction, repair, and other construction activities in a historic district shall comply with its regulatory and site-development detailed plans. The municipal planning administrative department shall, together with the municipal construction and culture administrative departments, review the design proposal within 20 days and notify the applicant in writing. Construction procedures may be completed only after the proposal passes review.
Cultural and tourism facilities, public utilities, and other facilities in the district shall be compatible with its traditional character.
Demolition or development in violation of the plan is prohibited in the district. Construction or installation of buildings or other facilities that damage the district's traditional character is also prohibited.
articles.21:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize research and documentation on the history and culture of notable towns and villages such as Xinkai Village in Longfu Town, Langli Town, Tongguan Town, and Wenjiashi Town. Where they meet the criteria for historic towns or villages, an application shall be submitted in accordance with the law.
Protection of historic towns and villages shall follow the relevant provisions of these Regulations on protection of historic districts.
articles.22: All categories of cultural relics shall be protected in accordance with the laws and regulations on the protection of cultural relics.
articles.23:
A user of an immovable cultural relic shall enter into a conservation-responsibility agreement with the culture administrative department, be responsible for the safety, upkeep, and repair of the building and its appurtenances, and accept the department's guidance and oversight.
Priority protection and reasonable use shall be provided for immovable cultural relics that especially represent the character of the historic and cultural city, including the Tongguan Kiln Site, Yuelu Academy, the Former Residence of Tan Sitong, the Former Residence of Huang Xing, the former site of the Wenjiashi gathering of forces during the Autumn Harvest Uprising, the Mawangdui Han Tombs, the Former Residence of Jia Yi, the Tomb of Zeng Guofan, Hunan First Normal University, the former site of the Hunan District Committee of the Communist Party of China, Baisha Ancient Well, and the Chu Tomb at Liucheng Bridge.
articles.24: Immovable cultural relics that have not yet been designated and published as cultural relics protection units shall be registered by the culture administrative department of the county-level people's government in accordance with the law, which shall formulate and publish conservation measures. Repair of such relics requires the consent of that department.
articles.25: Where a cultural relics protection unit is opened to visitors, effective conservation measures shall be taken to ensure the relics remain intact and safe.
articles.26:
Before carrying out construction within a published underground cultural relics burial area, the construction entity shall request the municipal culture administrative department to organize an archaeological survey, exploration, or excavation. The construction entity shall include the required expenses in its investment plan.
If cultural relics are discovered during archaeological survey, exploration, or construction, the municipal culture administrative department shall, together with the construction entity and in light of conservation requirements, agree on protective measures and protect the relics in accordance with the law.
articles.27: The Municipal People's Government shall organize surveys and identification of modern-era protected buildings, traditional residences, shops, structures, and similar properties with historical significance, artistic distinction, or scientific research value, publish them as historic buildings, and install conservation signs.
articles.28: Historic buildings shall be protected in their original location and appearance and may not be demolished without authorization. Where relocation is necessary, the municipal planning administrative department shall, together with the municipal construction and culture administrative departments, assess the relocation plan and submit written recommendations to the Municipal People's Government for approval. This work shall be completed within 30 days.
articles.29:
Historic buildings are divided into key protected buildings and generally protected buildings. The original exterior, structural system, floor plan, and distinctive interior decoration of a key protected building may not be altered. The original exterior and structural system of a generally protected building may not be altered.
It is prohibited to damage a historic building or use it in a manner that endangers safety.
articles.30:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize assessments of the safe-use grade of historic buildings, and the relevant departments shall propose corresponding corrective measures.
The owner or user shall be responsible for the safety, upkeep, and repair of a historic building. If the owner or user genuinely lacks the capacity to repair or maintain it, the Municipal People's Government may provide financial assistance as appropriate or lawfully exchange ownership of the historic building.
articles.32:
People's governments at all levels shall, in light of local circumstances, survey, collect, and organize information on the following intangible cultural heritage:
(1) local literature and arts, including Xiang opera, Huagu opera, Changsha storytelling with music, Changsha narrative storytelling, Changsha fishing-drum songs, Changsha folk songs, puppetry, shadow puppetry, and folk stories;
(2) traditional crafts, including Hunan embroidery, Hunan cuisine, stone carving, pottery, and paper-cutting;
(3) time-honored brands and century-old prestigious schools; and
(4) folk customs and traditions.

articles.33:
Administrative departments responsible for culture, commerce, and other matters shall establish a system for bearers of traditional arts and crafts and build specialized museums in light of the characteristics of those arts and crafts, thereby improving their quality.
Rescue measures shall be taken for traditional arts and crafts at risk of being lost. Support measures shall be formulated for distinctive brands such as Hunan cuisine and Hunan embroidery to promote their development.
articles.34: Social forces are encouraged and supported in exploring and documenting folk traditional arts and culture, establishing museums and exhibition halls, and holding exhibitions and performances. Educational and research institutions are supported in training specialists and enabling renowned senior artists to pass on their skills to apprentices.
articles.35: Historic place names that reflect the historical and cultural character of Changsha shall be retained. Where a change or cancellation is necessary, the place-name administration authority shall solicit views from the relevant parties.
articles.36:
Where a state employee violates these Regulations while protecting the historic and cultural city by committing any of the following acts, the higher-level competent authority or the employee's employer shall pursue administrative liability against the responsible person in charge and other persons directly responsible in accordance with the law:
(1) unlawfully adjusting any conservation plan for the historic and cultural city;
(2) unlawfully approving new construction or reconstruction of buildings or demolition of historic buildings; or
(3) otherwise unlawfully granting approval contrary to these Regulations.
articles.37: Where a person lacks a planning permit issued by the planning administrative department or violates the requirements of such a permit, the planning administrative department shall handle the matter in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
articles.38: Where a person unlawfully demolishes or seriously damages a historic building, the construction administrative department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and restore the building to its original condition. The individual shall be fined not less than RMB 2,000 but not more than RMB 20,000, and the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 200,000.
articles.39: Where a person moves, demolishes, or damages without authorization a conservation sign for a historic district or historic town or village, or a commemorative sign for a historic building or site or remains, the construction administrative department shall order restoration to the original condition and may impose a fine of not less than RMB 200 but not more than RMB 500.
articles.40: Other conduct violating these Regulations shall be penalized by the relevant administrative department in accordance with the law.
articles.41: Other protected matters, including scenic areas and ancient and notable trees, shall be protected in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
articles.42:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 November 2004.

FBMCLI.10.343577.title: Regulations of Shenyang Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted in light of local circumstances and in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages issued by the State Council, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to protection of the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
Protection and administration of the Shenyang Imperial Palace, Fuling Tomb, Zhaoling Tomb, other above-ground immovable cultural relics, and underground cultural relics shall be governed by relevant laws and regulations.
articles.3:
The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protecting and supervising the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
The people's governments of districts, counties, and county-level cities shall be responsible for protection and supervision and administration within their respective areas.
The municipal planning administrative department shall administer planning for protection of the historic and cultural city.
The municipal cultural relics administrative department shall protect cultural relics and participate in administering conservation plans for the historic and cultural city.
Administrative departments responsible for housing, construction, public security, finance, tourism, religious affairs, civil affairs, city appearance, landscaping, and other matters shall carry out related protection administration in accordance with their respective duties.
articles.4: Protection of the historic and cultural city of Shenyang shall follow the principles of coordinated planning, scientific administration, giving priority to protection, emergency rescue, and reasonable use. It shall maintain the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage and properly balance protection and development.
articles.5: The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts, counties, and county-level cities shall incorporate protection of the historic and cultural city into their economic and social development plans and include protection funding in their fiscal budgets.
articles.6: Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protecting the historic and cultural city by making donations, providing financial support or technical services, submitting suggestions, and other means.
articles.7: All organizations and individuals have a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and are entitled to dissuade, report, or complain about conduct that damages it.
articles.8: The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts, counties, and county-level cities and their relevant administrative departments shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.9:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city in accordance with the law and incorporate it into the urban master plan.
The people's governments of districts, counties, and county-level cities shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic towns and villages in accordance with the law.
articles.10:
In accordance with the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, the municipal planning administrative department shall, together with the municipal cultural relics administrative department, organize preparation of special conservation plans and regulatory detailed plans and publish them after approval by the Municipal People's Government.
The special conservation plans and regulatory detailed plans shall include the protected areas; conservation principles; buildings, structures, and other facilities to be protected; control indicators for building height, scale, and colors needed to preserve traditional character; land-use functions; population density; improvements to municipal infrastructure; measures to protect and renovate different categories of buildings; specific measures to ensure implementation of the conservation plans; and other matters that should be included.
articles.11:
Before a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city is submitted to the Provincial People's Government for approval, it shall be deliberated by the Standing Committee of the Municipal People's Congress. The Municipal People's Government shall study and handle the Standing Committee members' deliberation comments.
Before a conservation plan for a historic town or village is submitted for approval, it shall be deliberated by the standing committee of the people's congress of the district, county, or county-level city where it is located. The people's government at that level shall study and handle the standing committee members' deliberation comments.
articles.12: After a conservation plan for a historic and cultural city is approved and published, no organization or individual may amend it without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, the procedure in Article 11 of these Regulations shall be followed.
articles.13: The principal protected matters of the historic and cultural city include the historic urban area, historic districts, historic buildings, historic towns and villages, intangible cultural heritage, and other matters.
articles.14:
The ‘historic urban area’ of this Municipality means the urban area that took shape by the early years of the founding of the People's Republic of China. It mainly includes Shengjing City, formed during the Ming and Qing dynasties, and the South Manchuria Railway-affiliated area and commercial port area, formed during the Republic of China period.
The protected area of Shengjing City is the area within the outer city walls (the Eight Gates) of Shenyang during the Qing dynasty, bounded by Huigong Street, Lianhe Road, Dongbiancheng Street, Nanguan Road, and Qingnian Avenue.
The protected area of the South Manchuria Railway-affiliated area is its historic core of development, bounded by Heping Avenue to the east, the Changchun–Dalian Railway to the west, South Wuma Road to the south, and North Qima Road to the north.
The commercial port area is bounded by Harbin Road to the north, Beijing Street and Qingnian Avenue to the east, the South Canal to the south, and Heping Avenue and North Qima Road to the west.
articles.15:
Historic districts include Fangcheng, Cien Temple, Shenyang Station–Zhongshan Road–Zhongshan Square, and Tiexi Workers' Village, among others.
The protected area of Fangcheng Historic District is the area within West Shuncheng Street, North Shuncheng Road, East Shuncheng Street, and South Shuncheng Road.
The protected area of Cien Temple Historic District extends south to Fujiao Lane and Banruo Temple Lane, north to Longfeng Temple Lane, east to Dafosi Lane and Cien Temple East Lane, and west to Danan Street.
The protected area of Shenyang Station–Zhongshan Road–Zhongshan Square Historic District extends from the Changchun–Dalian Railway in the west to Heping Avenue in the east and includes one block on each side of Zhongshan Road and the areas around Shenyang Station and Zhongshan Square.
The protected area of Tiexi Workers' Village Historic District extends east to Zhaogong Street, south to South 11th West Road, west to Zhonggong Street, and north to South 10th West Road.
articles.16:
A ‘historic building’ means a building or structure with a degree of historical significance and conservation value that reflects the historic character and local features of Shenyang, but has not been published as a cultural relics protection unit or registered as an immovable cultural relic.
The Municipal People's Government shall formulate and publish the criteria and procedure for identifying historic buildings.
articles.17: Where buildings, structures, or other cultural landscapes that reflect the distinctive character of the historic and cultural city have not been included in a conservation plan, the municipal planning administrative department shall investigate them together with the municipal cultural relics, housing, and other relevant administrative departments. If they meet conservation requirements, planning controls shall be applied in accordance with the law.
articles.19: New buildings and structures in a construction-control zone of a historic urban area, historic district, or historic village shall comply with the construction controls in the conservation plan. For a construction project that fails to comply with those controls, the development and reform administrative department shall not approve the project, the planning administrative department shall not approve the plan, and the construction administrative department shall not approve commencement of work.
articles.20:
A construction entity shall, in accordance with the conservation plan, progressively renovate, relocate, or demolish buildings, structures, and other facilities lawfully constructed within an area covered by the plan that do not meet its requirements.
For buildings, structures, and other facilities unlawfully constructed in such an area and inconsistent with the conservation plan, the planning administrative department and other relevant departments shall demolish them or order their renovation in accordance with the law.
articles.21: When reviewing a planning application for a construction project within an area covered by a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, the municipal planning administrative department shall assess the project's impact on the city's historic and cultural character. The application shall not be approved without an assessment or if it fails the assessment.
articles.23:
Historic buildings may not be unlawfully demolished, reconstructed, or expanded.
Where a state-owned historic building is lawfully demolished, murals, sculptures, building components, and other items with collection value shall be collected by an institution designated by the cultural relics administrative department.
articles.24:
The owner of a historic building shall maintain and repair it in accordance with the conservation plan and applicable repair standards.
Any separate agreement between the owner and the manager or user on maintenance and repair duties shall apply.
Where the owner, manager, or user genuinely lacks the capacity to maintain or repair a historic building, the people's governments of the Municipality and its districts, counties, or county-level cities shall take measures to protect it.
articles.25: Before maintaining or repairing a historic building, approval shall be obtained from the cultural relics administrative department together with the planning administrative department, and the relevant procedures shall be completed in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
articles.26:
The municipal planning administrative department shall, together with the municipal cultural relics administrative department, install conservation or commemorative signs for historic districts, historic buildings, and important historic sites.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a conservation or commemorative sign without authorization.
articles.27:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts, counties, and county-level cities shall explore and document the history and culture of notable towns and villages and submit applications in accordance with the law where they meet the criteria for historic towns or villages.
Protection of Shifosi Historic Village shall be carried out in accordance with relevant laws and regulations and these Regulations.
articles.28:
Heritage that reflects the industrial history and culture of Shenyang shall be protected.
The people's governments of the Municipality and of Tiexi, Dadong, and other districts, counties, and county-level cities shall strengthen surveys, identification, documentation, and research on industrial heritage in accordance with the law, and protect it by establishing museums, memorial halls, and similar institutions.
articles.29: Historic place names that reflect Shenyang's historical and cultural character shall be retained. Where a change or cancellation is necessary, the place-name administrative department shall seek the views of the cultural relics administrative department.
articles.30:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts, counties, and county-level cities shall protect intangible cultural heritage in light of local circumstances.
They shall organize collection, documentation, research, protection, development, and use of local cultural heritage, including stories and legends, local opera, traditional crafts, folk skills, food culture, local customs, and other matters.
Social forces are encouraged and supported in exploring and documenting folk traditional arts and culture, establishing museums, memorial halls, and exhibition halls, and holding exhibitions and performances. Educational and research institutions are supported in training specialists and enabling renowned senior artists to pass on their skills to apprentices.
articles.32: Where a person maintains or repairs a historic building without approval, in violation of these Regulations, and damages its historic character, the municipal planning administrative department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the municipal planning administrative department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.33: Where a person damages, relocates, or demolishes a historic building without authorization, in violation of these Regulations, the municipal planning administrative department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the municipal planning administrative department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.34: Where a person unlawfully constructs, expands, or reconstructs a building, structure, or other facility in a historic district in violation of the conservation plan, thereby damaging the district's traditional character or local ethnic features, the municipal planning administrative department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the municipal planning administrative department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.35: Where a person installs, moves, alters, or damages any conservation or commemorative sign without authorization, the municipal planning administrative department shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made within that period, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.36: A party that disagrees with an administrative penalty decision may apply for administrative reconsideration or bring an administrative action in accordance with the law. If the party neither applies for administrative reconsideration nor brings an administrative action within the prescribed period and fails to comply with the penalty decision, the administrative organ that made the decision shall apply to a people's court for compulsory enforcement.
articles.37:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 September 2009.
