FBMCLI.10.9191486.title: Regulations of Hengyang Municipality on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen the protection and administration of the historic and cultural city of Hengyang, carry on and promote outstanding history and culture, and coordinate urban and rural development with the protection of historical and cultural heritage, in light of local circumstances and in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to the planning, protection, administration, and use of historic and cultural cities within the administrative area of this Municipality.
Protected assets of a historic and cultural city include historic urban areas, historic districts, historic areas, historic buildings, historic towns and villages, traditional villages, cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, ancient and notable trees, and other assets prescribed by laws and regulations.
articles.3:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protection and supervision and administration of historic and cultural cities in their respective administrative areas, establish and improve a coordination mechanism for protection work, and consider and handle major matters relating to protection.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall carry out specific work in their respective areas, including information collection, routine inspections, and on-site protection.
Villagers' committees and residents' committees shall assist with related protection work.
articles.4:
The competent housing and urban-rural development departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall coordinate protection work for historic and cultural cities and handle the applications, protection, construction, and administration of historic urban areas, historic districts, historic areas, historic buildings, historic towns and villages, and traditional villages.
The competent natural resources departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall administer planning for protection of historic and cultural cities, historic areas, historic districts, historic towns and villages, and traditional villages.
The cultural relics departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall protect and administer cultural relics and intangible cultural heritage.
The forestry and urban landscaping departments shall protect and administer ancient and notable trees in accordance with their respective duties.
Departments responsible for development and reform, education, industry and information technology, ethnic and religious affairs, public security, finance, ecology and environment, transport, water conservancy, agriculture and rural affairs, emergency management, urban administration, and other matters shall carry out related protection and administration in accordance with their respective duties.
articles.5:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall incorporate protection of historic and cultural cities into their plans for national economic and social development and include the necessary funding in their fiscal budgets.
Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection through investment, donations, the provision of services, and other means.
articles.6: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts, their relevant departments, township people's governments, subdistrict offices, villagers' and residents' committees, and news media shall strengthen public education on protection of historic and cultural cities, disseminate conservation knowledge, and raise public awareness.
articles.7:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize the housing and urban-rural development, natural resources and planning, cultural relics, and other relevant departments to prepare a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city in accordance with the overall territorial spatial plan.
The people's governments of the Municipality, its counties and county-level cities, and Nanyue District shall, in accordance with the overall territorial spatial plan and the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, organize preparation of conservation plans for historic districts, historic towns and villages, and traditional villages.
The competent departments designated by the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and Nanyue District shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic areas and historic buildings.
After approval, conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, historic districts, historic areas, historic buildings, historic towns and villages, and traditional villages may not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, consent shall first be obtained from the original approving authority and the amended plan shall then be submitted for approval under the statutory procedure.
articles.8: Historic urban areas, historic districts, historic areas, historic buildings, historic towns and villages, and traditional villages shall be protected as a whole, preserving their traditional layout, historic character, and spatial scale. The natural landscape and historic environmental features on which they depend may not be altered without authorization.
articles.9:
Conservation plans for historic districts, historic areas, historic buildings, historic towns and villages, and traditional villages shall designate protected areas. As needed, a protected area may include a core conservation area and a construction-control zone.
Construction within a protected area shall meet the following requirements:
(1) Within a core conservation area, new construction and expansion are prohibited except for necessary infrastructure and public-service facilities. An old house other than a historic building that has collapsed or is at imminent risk of collapse may, after approval, be reconstructed, rebuilt, or replaced on its original site. The work shall follow the original location, layout, form, and character and comply with the conservation plan.
(2) New buildings or structures in a construction-control zone shall comply with the construction controls set out in the conservation plan.
(3) Effective protective measures shall be taken when repairing roads, underground works, or other municipal infrastructure, so as not to damage protected assets.
articles.10: The housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, and other relevant departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall survey potential resources in their respective administrative areas, including historic districts, historic buildings, historic towns and villages, traditional villages, cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, and ancient and notable trees. They shall give due consideration to views from experts and the public and carry out applications and identification in accordance with the prescribed criteria and procedures.
articles.12: The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection register for historic and cultural cities, and protected assets shall be entered in the register. For each protected asset, the register shall state its name, location, category, grade, ownership, date of origin, historical value, and other relevant information, and shall be promptly made public. The register shall be managed dynamically and adjusted promptly in light of actual circumstances.
articles.13:
Where the housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, or other relevant departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts discover, during a survey of historical and cultural resources or from information supplied by an organization or individual, a resource with conservation value that is not yet in the protection register, they shall solicit views from relevant departments, interested parties, and the public. Following expert review, they may designate it for interim protection. Within ten days, they shall issue an interim-protection notice to the township people's government or subdistrict office where the resource is located and to its owner, manager, or user, and inform them of the protective measures to be taken.
After an asset is designated for interim protection, the relevant people's government shall enter into an agreement with its owner, manager, or user specifying conservation rights, duties, responsibilities, compensation for loss to lawful rights and interests, and other matters.
During the interim-protection period, no organization or individual may damage the asset. The housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, and other relevant departments shall, within one year after designation, submit the asset to the Municipal People's Government for verification and publication under the applicable application criteria and procedure so that it can be entered in the protection register. Interim protection shall cease to have effect if the asset is not entered in the register.
articles.14:
The municipal housing and urban-rural development department shall establish a protection-management system for historic and cultural cities and create conservation records and related databases for protected assets entered in the protection register. The records shall include the asset's history, ownership, survey and mapping data, use, related research findings, and other information, and shall facilitate access to information, sharing of research findings, and protection and use by organizations and individuals.
Relevant departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts, as well as township people's governments and subdistrict offices, shall jointly collect and enter related protection information.
articles.15:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall install conservation signs marking protected areas for published historic districts, historic areas, historic buildings, historic towns and villages, traditional villages, immovable cultural relics, and ancient and notable trees. The Municipal People's Government shall prescribe a uniform design for the signs.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a conservation sign without authorization.
articles.16:
A system of designated conservation responsibility shall apply to historic and cultural cities.
For a historic district, historic area, or historic town, the responsible person shall be the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located. For a historic village or traditional village, the responsible person shall be the township people's government or subdistrict office where it is located.
For a state-owned historic building, its manager shall be responsible; if there is no manager, its user shall be responsible. For a non-state-owned historic building, its owner shall be responsible; if the owner cannot be located or ownership is unclear, its manager shall be responsible; if there is no manager, its user shall be responsible. If the owner, manager, and user of a historic building cannot be identified or located, the competent housing and urban-rural development department of the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall be responsible.
articles.17:
The people's government of the Municipality or the relevant department shall enter into a conservation-responsibility agreement with the responsible person specifying the conservation duties.
The responsible person for a historic district, historic area, historic town or village, or traditional village shall organize implementation of the conservation plan and preserve the integrity of the traditional layout, historic character, spatial scale, and historic environmental features of buildings and structures within the protected area. While maintaining the spatial scale and character of streets, the responsible person shall improve infrastructure, public services, and the living environment and keep the protected area clean and orderly.
The responsible person for a historic building shall use it reasonably, carry out routine conservation and safety precautions, preserve its traditional layout and original character, and perform maintenance and repair duties in accordance with Article 19 of these Regulations.
articles.18:
Historic buildings shall be protected in their original location. They shall receive classified protection in light of their historical, scientific, artistic, and social value and their state of preservation.
Where construction in the public interest makes protection at the original location impossible and relocation or demolition is necessary, the competent natural resources and planning department of the Municipal People's Government shall, together with the housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments, conduct expert review and solicit public views, and then submit the matter for approval by the protection department and cultural relics department designated by the Provincial People's Government.
articles.19:
The person responsible for a historic building shall maintain and repair it and, as conservation needs require, submit a maintenance or repair design proposal. Work may proceed after the proposal is reviewed by the housing and urban-rural development department of the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county, county-level city, or district, together with the natural resources and cultural relics departments.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall allocate maintenance and repair costs for state-owned historic buildings from funds for protection of historic and cultural cities.
The responsible person shall bear maintenance and repair costs for a non-state-owned historic building. If the responsible person genuinely cannot afford those costs, they may apply to the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county, county-level city, or district for a subsidy, or the government may exchange or acquire ownership of the building and arrange its maintenance and repair.
articles.21:
Before allocating or transferring land where underground cultural relics may be buried, the people's governments of the Municipality, its counties and county-level cities, and Nanyue District shall have the cultural relics department organize archaeological surveys and exploration to determine the burial conditions and provide relevant findings.
Any organization or individual that discovers underground cultural relics or a cultural relics site during construction, agricultural production, or other activities shall immediately stop work, take protective measures, and report the discovery to the local people's government or cultural relics department.
articles.22:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall formulate policies to support protection and transmission of intangible cultural heritage and encourage its transmission.
Representative bearers of intangible cultural heritage shall explore, collect, and organize relevant materials and train successors.
articles.24: The Municipal People's Government shall establish a compensation system for protection of historic and cultural cities and compensate organizations and individuals for loss to their lawful rights and interests caused by such protection. The Municipal People's Government shall formulate specific compensation measures.
articles.25:
Any organization or individual may dissuade or stop conduct that damages protected assets of a historic and cultural city, or submit a complaint or report to the relevant department.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts and their relevant departments shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection work in accordance with relevant national provisions.
articles.26: Where a competent administrative department of a people's government of the Municipality or its counties, county-level cities, or districts, or a staff member thereof, neglects duties, abuses official authority, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in protecting a historic and cultural city, the responsible person in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be disciplined in accordance with the law. Where the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.27: Where a law or regulation already prescribes legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, that law or regulation shall apply.
articles.28: These Regulations shall take effect on 1 March 2026.

FBMCLI.10.9191487.title: Regulations of Shaoyang Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City of Wugang

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of the historic and cultural city of Wugang and carry on and promote outstanding history and culture, in light of local circumstances and in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages issued by the State Council, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to protection of the historic and cultural city of Wugang and related activities.
Protected assets include the historic urban area, historic districts, historic buildings, and buildings with traditional character; cultural relics and historic sites; traditional villages; ancient and notable trees, historic waterways, old wharves, wells, bridges, and other historic environmental features; intangible cultural heritage; and other assets prescribed by laws and regulations.
Where laws or regulations separately prescribe protection of cultural relics, traditional villages, ancient and notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, or other matters, those provisions shall apply.
articles.3:
The People's Government of Shaoyang Municipality and its relevant competent departments shall strengthen supervision and guidance for protection of the historic and cultural city of Wugang. The People's Government of Wugang City shall be fully responsible for that protection.
Wugang City shall establish and improve a coordination mechanism for protection, under the leadership of the Communist Party of China committee, coordinated by the government, implemented by departments, and involving public participation, and shall coordinate the resolution of major protection matters. Routine work shall be handled by the Wugang Ancient City Protection and Development Affairs Center (the ‘Ancient City Protection Center’).
The competent housing and urban-rural development department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall, together with the cultural relics department, protect and supervise the historic and cultural city. The competent natural resources department shall administer and supervise conservation planning. Other competent departments, township people's governments, and subdistrict offices shall carry out related protection work in accordance with their respective duties.
Villagers' committees and residents' committees shall assist township people's governments and subdistrict offices in protecting the historic and cultural city within their respective areas. They may guide villagers and residents through village rules, residents' agreements, and other means.
articles.4:
The People's Government of Wugang City shall incorporate protection of the historic and cultural city into its plans for national economic and social development and include the required funding in its fiscal budget. The People's Government of Shaoyang Municipality shall provide funding support as protection needs require.
Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate lawfully in protection through donations, financial support, investment, technical services, volunteer services, leasing buildings or structures, acquiring equity interests, and other means.
The People's Government of Wugang City shall strengthen public education on protection and raise public awareness. All organizations and individuals are entitled to submit views and suggestions on protection work and to dissuade, complain about, or report conduct that damages the historic and cultural city. The relevant departments shall handle and respond to such matters within the prescribed time limits.
articles.5:
Protection of the historic and cultural city of Wugang shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, reasonable use, and coordinated development, and preserve the authenticity of historical and cultural heritage, the integrity of historic character, and the continuity of social life.
The People's Government of Wugang City shall, in accordance with the conservation plan, establish a register of protected assets and digital records, install conservation signs, specify conservation measures and responsible persons, and administer conservation by area, grade, and category.
When reporting on implementation of urban and rural planning to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level, the People's Government of Wugang City, or a township people's government, shall include protection of the historic and cultural city of Wugang as a key matter.
articles.6:
The historic urban area comprises the area within the Wugang City Walls and areas closely related to them. It extends east to the western bank of the Ruan River, south to the northern bank of the Ruan River, west to the Wuqian Road and western city-wall line, and north to the Chenghao Road, Tongbao Road, and Jiefang Road line. The People's Government of Wugang City shall determine and publish its specific boundaries in accordance with the conservation plan.
The People's Government of Wugang City shall protect the landscape and city-wall layout characterized by ‘mountains embracing the city, the Zi River winding around it, canals crossing it, and three cities set side by side’; protect the street and lane pattern; and conserve the remains of landmarks reflecting the city-wall layout, including the Great and Small Forts, Jichuan Gate, Qingqu Gate, Qingcheng Gate, and Ying'en Gate.
New construction, expansion, or reconstruction in the historic urban area shall comply with the conservation plan's controls on building height, scale, style, and colors; preserve the integrity of the traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale, and historic features; and use traditional or traditional-style materials and traditional construction techniques. Such work shall not impair the authenticity or integrity of historical and cultural heritage or destructively affect view corridors, traditional layout, street and lane patterns, or historic character. Before issuing a construction-project planning permit, the competent natural resources department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall seek the views of its housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments and the Ancient City Protection Center.
Awnings, solar panels, air-conditioning equipment, air-source heat pumps, sunrooms, above-ground utility lines, meters, and similar facilities installed in the historic urban area shall be compatible with the overall character of the historic and cultural city of Wugang. The urban administration and comprehensive law-enforcement department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall handle unlawful makeshift construction, installations, wiring, and hanging in accordance with the law.
articles.7:
The five historic districts are Xizhi Street, Muhuo Street, Chuancheng River, Hehe Street, and Taiping Gate. Each has a core conservation area and a construction-control zone. The People's Government of Wugang City shall determine and publish their specific boundaries in accordance with the conservation plan.
The People's Government of Wugang City shall protect the original character, spatial scale, and view corridors of historic districts; control building heights and continuity of street frontages; and strictly prohibit widening or narrowing streets and lanes without authorization. It shall protect historic environmental features, including ancient trees and wells, old courtyard walls, traditional road paving, and vegetation, and preserve traditional street and lane names and place-name heritage.
Within the core conservation area of a historic district, all new construction and expansion are prohibited except for necessary infrastructure and public-service facilities. Before issuing a construction-project planning permit for such necessary facilities, the competent natural resources department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall seek the views of its housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments and the Ancient City Protection Center. Demolition of a building, structure, or other facility other than a historic building requires approval from that natural resources department, which shall first seek the views of those departments and the Center. New construction, reconstruction, or expansion of buildings or structures in a construction-control zone shall comply with the construction controls in the conservation plan.
The People's Government of Wugang City shall lawfully advance development of pedestrian streets such as Xizhi Street, guide compatible business uses, and promote cultural tourism and related industries in historic districts. It may impose traffic controls in accordance with law and actual traffic-management needs. The People's Government of Wugang City shall formulate and publish measures for administration of pedestrian streets.
articles.8:
The People's Government of Wugang City shall dynamically administer the register of historic buildings, make timely adjustments, and publish them. If a listed historic building is lost or damaged due to force majeure, has demonstrably lost its conservation value, or its conservation category changes, the competent housing and urban-rural development department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall, together with the natural resources and cultural relics departments and the Ancient City Protection Center, promptly propose an adjustment, solicit relevant views, and make the adjustment after obtaining approval in accordance with the law.
The owner of a historic building shall maintain and repair it in accordance with the conservation plan. If it has no owner or the owner is unknown, the person actually managing or using it shall maintain and repair it. If a historic building is at risk of damage and its owner, actual manager, or user lacks the capacity to maintain or repair it, the People's Government of Wugang City shall provide necessary financial or technical support or take measures to protect it.
No organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization. Where construction in the public interest makes protection at the original location impossible and relocation or demolition is necessary, the competent natural resources department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall, together with its housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments and the Ancient City Protection Center, submit the matter for approval in accordance with laws and regulations.
Exterior repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or changes to the structure or use of a historic building shall be approved by the competent natural resources department of the People's Government of Wugang City together with its housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments. The Ancient City Protection Center shall also be consulted, and related procedures shall be completed in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
A construction project near a historic building shall not endanger its safety, and its architectural character shall be compatible with the building's overall environment.
articles.9:
The Wugang City Walls are the ancient city walls designated as a Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level, including the walls, gates, and their sites and remains.
The People's Government of Wugang City shall lawfully prepare a conservation plan for the Wugang City Walls, publish their protected area and construction-control zone, establish archival records that include the protected area, signs and descriptions, records, and administration entity, and take lawful measures to protect wall remains, bricks and stones, and other components. Wall sections and appurtenant buildings restored in accordance with the conservation plan shall be integrated into the Wugang City Walls for unified conservation and administration.
No organization or individual may damage, unlawfully possess, or trade bricks, stones, inscriptions, or other cultural relics components from the Wugang City Walls; carve or deface the walls; or erect unauthorized structures or plant crops within their protected area.
articles.10:
The People's Government of Wugang City shall strictly protect the historic alignment and course of the Chuancheng River, ancient bridges such as Panlong Bridge and Hualong Bridge, and waterfront spaces and vegetation along the river, including historic embankments, old wharves, and stone steps.
It shall strengthen protection and improvement of traditional buildings along the river and preserve or restore their traditional character and spatial scale.
articles.11:
Guided by the core socialist values, the People's Government of Wugang City shall lawfully protect modern revolutionary remains, including the former site of the Second Branch of the Whampoa Military Academy (including Zhongshan Hall, the Former Residence of Li Minghao, and Faxiangyan Park), the Xuefeng Mountains Anti-Japanese War sites, the Monument to the Soldiers Killed in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, and the former site of the Caijiatang Peasants' Association. It shall establish bases for patriotic education, promote revolutionary culture, and strengthen a shared sense of community among the Chinese nation.
No organization or individual may damage or make unauthorized rubbings of cliff inscriptions, revolutionary slogans, or similar materials.
articles.12:
The People's Government of Wugang City shall strictly protect and reasonably use historical and cultural heritage and strengthen protection, exploration, collection, documentation, and research concerning traditional culture, arts, folk customs, and ethnic traditions, applying integrated protection across the whole area and all relevant elements.
The competent department of culture, tourism, radio, television, and sports of the People's Government of Wugang City shall protect and conduct archaeological excavations at ancient sites, including Shangtouyuan, the Neolithic site at Siji Rock, the site of the Duliang Marquisate, and the Shenjia ancestral mountain kiln site. It shall support adaptive transmission and use of representative intangible cultural heritage such as Wugang sizian music, Wugang Qiju opera, and Jizi boxing.
The competent commerce department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall, together with market-regulation and culture, tourism, radio, television, and sports departments, survey, explore, and document production techniques for local specialty foods. It shall establish records and databases of the techniques for Wugang braised dishes, Wugang bronze geese, rice noodles, and other foods; encourage and support distinctive experience venues; and promote local food culture.
Organizations and individuals are encouraged and supported in establishing museums, exhibition halls, memorial halls, and venues for trading and exhibiting art and folk collections; filming audiovisual works, creating literature and art, and establishing bases for teaching folk arts; developing distinctive cultural and creative industries; and holding folk activities such as the June 6 New-Grain Tasting Festival and the Shiyang Horse Lantern Festival.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall strengthen protection and administration of historical and cultural heritage and establish a system assigning conservation responsibilities.
articles.13:
Organizations and individuals within the protected area of the historic and cultural city shall implement fire-safety responsibilities, strictly manage the use of fire, electricity, gas, and oil, maintain fire safety and fire-fighting facilities, prevent fires, and report fires.
Public fire-fighting facilities in the historic urban area, including fire-water supply, fire lanes, and fire communications, shall be improved in accordance with current national fire-safety technical standards. Where the standards and codes cannot be met, the fire-safety department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall, together with its natural resources, housing and urban-rural development, and cultural relics departments, the Ancient City Protection Center, and the subdistrict office, formulate a fire-safety assurance plan.
articles.14:
The People's Government of Wugang City shall strengthen housing-safety administration and remediation of dangerous buildings within the historic and cultural city and establish a diversified, community-based mechanism for addressing housing-safety risks.
The owner of a house within the historic and cultural city is responsible for its safe use. If the owner and user are different, they shall allocate responsibility in accordance with their agreement; if there is no agreement or it is unclear, the owner shall be responsible. If the owner cannot be located or ownership is unclear, the manager or user shall be responsible.
Where the foundation, walls, or other load-bearing components of a house show obvious settlement, cracks, deformation, corrosion, or similar conditions; the house is damaged by a natural disaster, fire, explosion, or other incident; a designed, owner-built residence reaches its designed service life; or another evident safety hazard is found in an inspection or routine patrol, and the condition endangers public safety, the person responsible for safe use shall lawfully commission a housing-safety assessment institution to assess the building. If that person refuses to do so, the housing-safety department of the People's Government of Wugang City, a township people's government, or a subdistrict office may commission the assessment on their behalf. If the building is assessed as dangerous, the responsible person shall bear the assessment costs.
The person responsible for safe use of a building assessed as dangerous shall promptly take measures to eliminate the danger in accordance with the applicable dangerous-building repair and handling measures. The People's Government of Wugang City shall formulate specific measures in accordance with the law.
No organization or individual may unlawfully demolish or alter a historic district, cultural relic, historic building, or building with traditional character by falsely claiming that it is a dangerous building.
articles.15:
Where a state organ or its staff member fails to perform protection and administration duties, fails to investigate discovered unlawful conduct, or otherwise neglects duties, abuses official authority, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in protecting the historic and cultural city, the person shall be disciplined in accordance with the law. Where the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Where a person, in violation of the third paragraph of Article 7 or the fourth paragraph of Article 8 of these Regulations, demolishes without approval a building, structure, or other facility other than a historic building; carries out exterior repairs or decoration, adds facilities, or changes the structure or use of a historic building; or otherwise causes a destructive impact on the traditional layout or historic character of the historic and cultural city of Wugang or on a historic building, the competent natural resources department of the People's Government of Wugang City shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
Where laws or regulations already prescribe legal liability for other conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.16:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2026.

FBMCLI.10.9844892.title: Regulations of Zhaoqing Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen the protection and administration of the historic and cultural city of this Municipality, carry on and promote outstanding history and culture, and promote coordinated development of urban and rural construction and historical and cultural heritage protection, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics and the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and in light of local circumstances.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to planning, protection, use, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
Protected assets under these Regulations include historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages; historic districts and areas; traditional villages; immovable cultural relics; historic buildings; intangible cultural heritage; and other protected assets prescribed by laws and regulations.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of giving priority to protection, planning on a scientific basis, administering by category, making rational use, and encouraging public participation. Traditional layouts and historic character shall be protected and carried forward; the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage shall be maintained; the relationship between economic and social development and heritage protection shall be properly managed; and outstanding local history and culture shall be inherited and promoted.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protecting the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas and for supervising and administering that protection, and shall include the relevant work in their plans for national economic and social development. They shall establish and improve a joint-meeting mechanism for protection work, coordinate the resolution of major issues, and strengthen policy and financial support.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall conduct routine inspections of protected assets within their jurisdictions, include them in grid-based administration, carry out public education and guidance and supervision, and guide villagers' committees and residents' committees in assisting with protection.
Villagers' committees and residents' committees shall assist township people's governments and subdistrict offices with related protection work. They are encouraged and supported in guiding villagers and residents to protect the historic and cultural city through village rules and agreements, residents' covenants, and other means.
articles.5:
The housing and urban-rural development departments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts, together with the cultural relics departments at the same level, shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas and shall organize the implementation of these Regulations.
Departments of development and reform, education, industry and information technology, public security, civil affairs, finance, human resources and social security, natural resources, ecology and environment, agriculture and rural affairs, commerce, emergency management, fire and rescue, urban management and comprehensive law enforcement, local chronicles, archives, and other departments shall perform related protection work within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
The Municipal People's Government shall establish a pool of experts on protection of the historic and cultural city. Experts shall participate in professional assessments concerning the designation, adjustment, and removal of protected assets, review of conservation plans, and other related matters, and shall provide advisory opinions to the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts and their relevant departments.
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged and supported in participating in protection through investment, donations, sponsorship, technical services, volunteer activities, and other means.
Radio, television, newspapers, the internet, and other media are encouraged and supported in publicizing and promoting protection of the historic and cultural city and enhancing public awareness and participation.
Any organization or individual has the right to discourage and report conduct that damages the historic and cultural city. The competent departments shall promptly verify and handle reports they receive. For a report made under the reporter's real name, the handling result shall be communicated to the reporter, whose identity shall be kept confidential.
articles.7:
Conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages; historic districts and areas; traditional villages; and historic buildings shall meet historical and cultural protection requirements. They shall focus on carrying forward and developing local Zhaoqing cultures, including Guangfu culture and Duan inkstone culture, as well as revolutionary culture; preserve traditional layouts, historic character, and spatial scale; protect associated cultural landscapes, natural landscapes, and the surrounding setting; strictly control building heights and forms; protect view corridors and the urban skyline; and provide integrated, systematic, and comprehensive protection.
Spatial control requirements in conservation plans concerning natural resources, traditional layouts, historic character, and other matters shall be incorporated into the territorial spatial plan at the same level. Conservation plans shall be coordinated with other special plans.
articles.8:
Conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages; historic districts and areas; and traditional villages shall delineate protected areas. Protected areas shall, in accordance with the law, include core protected areas and construction control areas.
Construction within a protected area shall comply with planning requirements. Its layout, height, bulk, architectural style, color, and other features shall be compatible with the historic character and shall not damage the traditional layout or historic character.
Within a core protected area, no new construction or extension may be undertaken, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
Buildings, structures, and other facilities that do not conform to a conservation plan shall be renovated by the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district. If renovation cannot bring them into conformity with the plan, they shall be relocated or demolished in accordance with the law. Where a building, structure, or other facility that must be relocated or demolished was formed historically or constructed with approval, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall organize implementation in phases and batches and provide resettlement and compensation in accordance with the law. Illegal construction shall be dealt with in accordance with the law.
articles.9:
Outdoor advertisements, signs, awnings, air-conditioning units, covered walkways, sculptures, sanitation facilities, and other exterior facilities installed in a protected area, and any decoration there, shall be compatible with the historic character.
Power, communications, water supply, drainage, gas, and other utility lines in a protected area shall comply with planning requirements and shall, as a priority, be laid underground. Where underground installation is impossible due to site constraints, the lines shall be organized by means such as conduits, bundling, wall-mounted installation, or routing along the building form, and their colors and forms shall be compatible with the historic character.
articles.10:
In accordance with conservation plans, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall organize the formulation of annual protection plans and implement them as part of special plans for urban renewal.
Based on issues identified through monitoring, assessment, and routine inspections, and on the overall objectives set out in conservation plans, annual protection plans shall provide for graded and categorized administration of protected assets. They shall include a list of protected assets and projects, funding arrangements, division of responsibilities, safeguard measures, and other matters.
Experts and villagers and residents shall be consulted in preparing annual protection plans, which shall be made public.
articles.11:
A protection-list system shall be implemented for protected assets of the historic and cultural city. The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall organize the departments responsible for protected assets to conduct surveys and designation of such assets.
Before an asset is added to a protection list, the competent department shall, in accordance with the law, seek opinions from experts, relevant departments, interested parties, and the public.
Where a change in protection level or type, or another circumstance, requires adjustment of a protection list, the list shall be adjusted promptly and dynamically, and the adjustment shall be made public.
Protection lists shall be organized by category, and complete protection archives shall be established. The archives shall identify the owners and boundaries of each category of protected asset and record its name, category, location, area, protected area, ownership, responsible person for protection, history, design or survey materials, and other particulars, together with clear geographic coordinates and corresponding boundary maps.
articles.12:
The person responsible for protection shall be determined as follows:
(1) For a nationally designated historic and cultural city, the responsible person shall be the Municipal People's Government; for a provincially designated historic and cultural city, it shall be the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district.
(2) For a historic town or village or a traditional village, the responsible person shall be the township people's government or subdistrict office where it is located.
(3) For a historic district or historic area, the responsible person shall be the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located. For one spanning county-level administrative areas, the responsible person shall be designated by the Municipal People's Government.
(4) For a state-owned historic building, its management entity shall be the responsible person. For a non-state-owned historic building, its owner shall be the responsible person. If the owner is missing, cannot be contacted, or is unclear, the manager shall be responsible if there is one; otherwise the user shall be responsible. If no responsible person can be determined, the Municipal People's Government or the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where the building is located shall promptly designate one.
Where a people's government of the Municipality or of a county, county-level city, or district is the responsible person, it shall assign dedicated personnel to the protection work.
Relevant departments, including housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts, shall regularly organize training for responsible persons. Training shall cover laws, regulations, and policies concerning historic and cultural cities; routine protection and repair of historic buildings; safety management; emergency response; and adaptive reuse.
articles.16:
Use and development of historic towns and villages, districts, historic areas, traditional villages, and similar places shall primarily proceed through small-scale, incremental renewal, with attention to protecting traditional layouts, historic character, and spatial scale. Large-scale demolition and construction, and imitations falsely presented as historic buildings, are prohibited.
In accordance with plans and in coordination with urban renewal, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall organize the construction and improvement of roads, water supply, drainage, power supply, fire protection, sanitation, and other infrastructure for protected assets and surrounding areas, as well as supporting facilities such as parking lots, visitor service centers, and accessibility facilities, in order to improve the area's functions and quality. Where protection needs make it impossible to follow current technical standards and specifications for construction and administration, the relevant departments shall organize the preparation of a special plan, which may be implemented after expert review.
Before an area proposed for urban renewal is renewed, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall conduct a survey and assessment, review the condition of existing buildings, identify buildings to be retained and protected, and organize expert review. Urban renewal shall not be undertaken in an area where no survey and assessment have been conducted or special work to delineate historic districts and identify historic buildings has not been completed.
articles.17:
Before carrying out exterior repairs or decoration on a historic building, adding facilities, or changing its structure or use, the person responsible for protection shall submit an application and complete approval procedures in accordance with the law.
Before a historic-building repair project is formally completed, the project owner shall organize the design, construction, and supervision entities and historical and cultural protection experts to review and inspect the project. Inspection shall cover both construction quality and compliance with protection requirements. The building may be put to use only after passing inspection.
Where the responsible person repairs a historic building in accordance with the conservation plan and protection guidelines and the work passes inspection, the people's government of the Municipality or its county, county-level city, or district may provide a financial subsidy based on the area, extent, and quality of the maintenance and repair. The Municipal People's Government shall formulate and publish specific measures for such subsidies.
articles.18:
Protection and use of historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages; historic districts and areas; and traditional villages shall give priority to protection, ensure effective inheritance, and make rational use, while safeguarding the lawful rights and interests of original residents and maintaining continuity of traditional ways of life.
Original residents are encouraged to continue living at the original site in accordance with conservation-plan requirements, improve their living and working conditions, and engage in business and other activities in local distinctive industries.
articles.19:
Protection and use of historic buildings shall comply with relevant protection requirements, shall not impair the buildings' architectural value, and shall not contravene core socialist values or public order and good morals.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts may make rational use of non-state-owned historic buildings by acquisition, exchange of property rights, lease, or other means.
articles.22:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall include funding for protection and use of the historic and cultural city in their respective fiscal budgets, coordinate fiscal funds at all levels for the protection and inheritance of the historic and cultural city, and support that work.
Social capital is encouraged to participate in projects for the protection and inheritance of the historic and cultural city, broadening funding channels. The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall facilitate and support such participation through policy measures, publication of project information, and other means.
articles.23:
The culture and tourism departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall survey and identify intangible cultural heritage within their respective administrative areas. Using modern technology, they shall comprehensively and systematically document its types, distribution, living environment, protection status, and other particulars; collect and properly preserve relevant materials and objects; and establish archives and databases for intangible cultural heritage.
For intangible cultural heritage at risk of disappearing, the departments shall promptly document it and collect relevant objects or take other emergency-preservation measures. Where an item requires transmission, effective measures shall be taken to support that transmission.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall coordinate planning for or make rational use of existing public cultural facilities, build comprehensive intangible cultural heritage museums and transmission and experience centers, venues, or sites, and conduct protection and transmission activities such as education, training, research, creation, presentation, performance, sales exhibitions, tourism, experiential activities, and exchanges.
The Municipal People's Government shall formulate support policies for the protection and transmission of intangible cultural heritage. Measures such as industrial guidance, financial subsidies, training, and lectures shall encourage the exploration, collection, organization, and study of traditional culture, art, folk customs, and arts and crafts.
Representative project protection entities, representative inheritors, and representative transmission groups are encouraged and supported in establishing special exhibition venues or transmission and experience centers, venues, or sites that are open to the public.
articles.24:
Persons responsible for protection of historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages; historic districts and areas; traditional villages; historic buildings; and other protected assets shall, in light of the scale and characteristics of the assets, establish mechanisms for disaster prevention and mitigation, safety management, and emergency support, formulate emergency response plans for unexpected incidents, and improve emergency-response capacity.
Fire and rescue agencies, emergency management departments, and competent departments for protected assets of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall, within their respective responsibilities, conduct regular inspections of historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages; historic districts and areas; traditional villages; historic buildings; and other assets within their administrative areas. They shall conduct fire-safety training and drills, promptly identify safety hazards and emergencies, take appropriate measures to eliminate danger, and ensure that fire-prevention, disaster-prevention, and other facilities and equipment remain operational.
Firefighting facilities and access routes within core protected areas of historic towns and villages, historic districts, historic areas, traditional villages, and similar places shall be provided in accordance with applicable fire-safety technical standards and specifications, and a person responsible for fire safety shall be designated. If protection needs make compliance impossible, the fire and rescue agency of the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county, county-level city, or district shall, together with the competent department for protected assets at the same level, formulate a fire-safety assurance plan.
Dedicated fire stations shall be provided in historic districts and historic areas, equipped with small-scale, suitable firefighting facilities and equipment, and a community fire-safety mechanism shall be established.
articles.25:
The competent department for a protected asset shall use video surveillance, remote sensing, and other means to monitor the asset and promptly identify, stop in accordance with the law, and handle unlawful conduct that damages protected assets or unauthorized installation, movement, alteration, or destruction of protection signs.
The housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism, emergency management, fire and rescue, urban management and comprehensive law enforcement, and other departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish and improve coordination mechanisms, including information sharing, regular liaison, and joint law enforcement, and jointly protect the historic and cultural city.
articles.26: Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.27:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 May 2026.

FBMCLI.10.9474334.title: Regulations of Tonghai County, Yuxi Municipality, on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of the historic and cultural city of Tonghai County (the "City"), carry on and promote outstanding history and culture, and, in light of local circumstances, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and the State Council's Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to planning, protection, administration, and use of the City.
Where protection of the City involves cultural relics, nature reserves, scenic areas, ancient and notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, or other matters, the relevant laws and administrative regulations shall apply.
articles.3: Protection of the City shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, inheritance and development, and rational use; preserve and carry forward the City's traditional layout and historic character; maintain the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage; and properly manage the relationship between economic and social development and heritage protection.
articles.4:
The Municipal People's Government shall strengthen its leadership of protection work for the City, coordinate and study major protection matters and issues, and include relevant protection funding in its fiscal budget.
The People's Government of Tonghai County (the "County People's Government") shall be responsible for protection of the City, include that work in its plans for national economic and social development, establish and improve protection mechanisms, and include necessary protection funding in its fiscal budget.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall handle routine protection work for the City within their jurisdictions, establish coordinated protection and administration mechanisms, and strengthen inspections, maintenance, public education, and supervision.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist township people's governments, subdistrict offices, and relevant departments in protecting the City. They are encouraged to guide villagers and residents to participate in protection by adopting village rules, residents' covenants, and other means.
articles.5:
The housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government, together with the culture and tourism and comprehensive administrative law enforcement departments, shall be responsible for protection, administration, and supervision of the City.
Relevant departments, including development and reform, public security, finance, natural resources, ecology and environment, agriculture and rural affairs, forestry and grassland, emergency management, and earthquake prevention and disaster reduction, and fire and rescue agencies shall perform related protection work within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
3 March of each year shall be the City's Protection Publicity Day.
The people's governments of the Municipality and the County and their relevant departments, township people's governments, and subdistrict offices shall organize public education on protection of the City, strengthen the inheritance and presentation of outstanding traditional culture, disseminate protection knowledge, and enhance public awareness.
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and use of the City through donations, sponsorship, volunteer service, and other means.
Any organization or individual has the right to offer opinions and suggestions on protection of the City and to discourage, complain about, or report conduct that damages it.
articles.7:
The County People's Government shall, in accordance with the law, organize the preparation of conservation plans for the City, historic districts, and historic towns ("conservation plans").
In preparing conservation plans, traditional layouts and historic character shall be preserved, and controls on building height and form and on view corridors shall be strengthened. The plans shall conform to the overall territorial spatial plan and be included in the territorial spatial planning system as special plans. Other special plans concerning protection of the City shall be coordinated with the conservation plans.
A conservation plan approved in accordance with the law shall be made public within 15 days after approval and shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, the authority that organized its preparation shall submit a special report to the original approval authority and may prepare an amendment only after consent is obtained. The amended conservation plan shall be submitted for approval in accordance with the original approval procedure.
articles.8: The protected areas of the Ancient City of Tonghai and the historic town of Hexi shall be divided into core protected areas, construction control areas, and environmental coordination areas. The County People's Government shall delineate and publish the specific boundaries in accordance with the conservation plan approved in accordance with the law. It shall install signs at the principal entrances and exits of core protected areas.
articles.10:
A protection-list system shall be implemented for the City. Protected assets approved and published by a people's government at or above the county level shall be included directly in the protection list.
The County People's Government shall organize relevant departments to survey historical and cultural resources. Based on the survey, the housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government, together with the culture and tourism and other relevant departments, shall organize expert assessment and, in accordance with applicable designation standards, propose an initial list of protected assets for approval and publication by the County People's Government.
Any organization or individual that discovers an asset with protection value that has not yet been included in the protection list may propose its inclusion to the County People's Government or a relevant department. A building or structure with protection value that has not yet been designated as a historic building shall be registered for interim protection.
A protection sign shall be installed at the principal entrance or another prominent location of each protected asset on the protection list.
articles.11:
A system of persons responsible for protection shall be implemented for the City. The responsible person shall be determined as follows:
(1) For a historic district, the subdistrict office where it is located shall be responsible.
(2) For a historic town or traditional village, the township people's government where it is located shall be responsible.
(3) For a historic building, its owner, actual user, or manager shall be responsible.
For other protected assets, where laws or regulations specify a responsible person, those provisions shall apply. If no responsible person can be determined, the County People's Government shall designate one.
After publishing the protection list, the County People's Government shall notify the responsible persons in writing of their protection duties.
articles.13:
The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall perform the following duties:
(1) ensure the building's safety and the proper functioning of disaster-prevention and fire-prevention facilities and equipment; promptly take measures to eliminate identified safety hazards or emergencies; and report them to the housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government;
(2) carry out routine maintenance and repair and preserve the traditional character of the original building, including its height, bulk, exterior appearance, colors, and courtyard layout; and
(3) before transferring, leasing, or lending the historic building, enter into a written agreement with the transferee, lessee, or user specifying each party's protection responsibilities.
Repairs to a historic building shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plan. The building's principal structure, main floor layout, or exterior appearance shall not be changed without authorization, and the safety of the principal structure or ancillary facilities shall not be endangered.
Where a historic building is at risk of damage, its responsible person shall promptly maintain and repair it in accordance with the law. If the responsible person lacks the capacity to do so, the County People's Government shall take measures to protect the building.
articles.14:
Protection of the Ancient City of Tonghai, the historic town of Hexi, and traditional villages shall comply with the following requirements:
(1) preserve the historic natural setting and landscape integrating the mountains, the Ancient City of Tonghai, and Qilu Lake; maintain view corridors; and strictly control construction intensity, building height, and form;
(2) preserve the overall layouts and distinctive character of historic districts and historic towns; and
(3) preserve the natural mountain-and-water setting and agricultural ecological landscape associated with traditional villages.
articles.15:
Construction within a protected area of the City shall comply with conservation plans, reflect local architectural characteristics, and, to the extent possible, use traditional techniques and materials. It shall not impair the authenticity or integrity of historical and cultural heritage or destructively affect traditional layouts, street and lane patterns, or traditional character, and shall comply with the following requirements:
(1) No new construction or extension may be undertaken in a core protected area, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
(2) New construction, reconstruction, or extension of buildings or structures in a construction control area shall comply with the construction controls established by the conservation plan. Their form, height, bulk, style, color, and other features shall be compatible with the traditional layout and historic character of the core protected area.
(3) Construction in an environmental coordination area shall be compatible with the character and distinctive features of the construction control area and shall not damage pastoral landscapes, mountain and water forms, other traditional agrarian cultural patterns, or the natural ecological environment.
Buildings, structures, or other facilities in a core protected area that do not conform to the conservation plan and affect the historic layout, street and lane patterns, or historic character shall be gradually renovated or modified in accordance with the plan by the housing and urban-rural development, natural resources, and comprehensive administrative law enforcement departments of the County People's Government, township people's governments, subdistrict offices, or property owners.
articles.16: The bulk of buildings, roofs and skyline, exterior wall materials, and the design and materials of shopfronts, windows, walls, and gates within a protected area of the City shall comply with the conservation plan.
articles.19:
Firefighting facilities and access routes within protected areas of the City shall be provided in accordance with applicable fire-safety technical standards and specifications. If protection needs make compliance impossible, the fire and rescue agency shall, together with the relevant competent departments, formulate a corresponding fire-safety assurance plan.
Organizations and individuals within protected areas of the City shall implement a fire-safety responsibility system, strictly manage the use of fire, electricity, gas, and oil, and perform their duties to maintain fire safety, protect firefighting facilities, prevent fires, and report fires.
The discharge of fireworks and firecrackers shall be strictly restricted or prohibited within protected areas of the City. The County People's Government shall determine the restricted or prohibited times and areas in accordance with the law.
articles.20: The County People's Government shall establish a digital dynamic monitoring system for protection of the City and install relevant facilities and equipment in key protected areas and at key protected assets, thereby improving smart administration of fire safety, security, intelligent inspections, data monitoring, information feedback, public services, and related matters.
articles.21:
The County People's Government shall coordinate implementation of conservation plans, regularly supervise and inspect their implementation, assess the protection status of the City, and promptly correct and handle identified problems.
The housing and urban-rural development, natural resources, culture and tourism, and comprehensive administrative law enforcement departments of the County People's Government, and township people's governments and subdistrict offices, shall strictly implement conservation plans and strengthen routine supervision and inspection of their implementation.
articles.22:
Protection and use of the City shall be compatible with its historical, artistic, scientific, social, and cultural values, so that protection and use are coordinated.
Protection, inheritance, and rational use of the City are encouraged and supported, as is development of tourism and cultural industries, provided that natural landscapes, cultural landscapes, and historical and cultural resources are not damaged.
The people's governments of the Municipality and the County and their relevant departments shall strengthen the collection, organization, study, presentation, and dissemination of the City's cultural resources; protect and carry on folk customs, folk arts, traditional techniques, and other heritage; interpret related historical stories, cultural values, and spiritual significance; promote deeper integration of history and culture with tourism; and bring out the social and educational role of historical and cultural heritage.
The people's governments of the Municipality and the County shall establish online platforms and diversify forms of presentation, using text, audiovisual, digital, and other means to present the influence, cohesion, and appeal of the "Land of Rites and Music" and to showcase historical and cultural resources through digital platforms.
articles.23:
Protection and use of the City shall safeguard the lawful rights and interests of villagers and residents and encourage their active participation in protection. Villagers and residents are encouraged and supported in engaging in traditional handicrafts with local characteristics, producing and marketing distinctive products, and transmitting and making use of intangible cultural heritage, so as to carry forward the City's original form and way of life.
The County People's Government shall improve infrastructure and public service facilities in accordance with conservation plans and enhance the quality of the living environment.
articles.25:
The County People's Government shall protect traditional market-town customs and support folk-cultural activities.
On the condition that relevant protection requirements are met, organizations and individuals are encouraged to make rational use of historic buildings to establish heritage presentation venues such as museums, exhibition halls, art galleries, cultural reading rooms, and village-history museums, and to operate tourism and leisure services such as homestays, inns, distinctive restaurants, and tea houses.
articles.26: Where a state organ or its staff member fails to perform or improperly performs duties in protecting the City, responsibility shall be pursued in accordance with laws and regulations, and the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be disciplined in accordance with the law.
articles.27:
A person committing any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations shall be penalized as follows:
(1) For a violation of subparagraph (7) of Article 17, the relevant competent department of the County People's Government shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the relevant competent department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
(2) For a violation of subparagraphs (1) through (3) of Article 18, the comprehensive administrative law enforcement department of the County People's Government shall order correction within a specified period and restoration of the original condition. If the person fails to comply within that period, the relevant administrative law enforcement department shall demolish the facility in accordance with the law.
articles.28: Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for other conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.29:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2026.
