FBMCLI.10.7056842.title: Regulations of Chengde Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection and administration of Chengde, a historic and cultural city, carry on outstanding history and culture, and promote coordinated development of urban construction and historical and cultural protection, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and in light of local circumstances.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to activities related to the protection, planning, administration, and use of the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of scientific planning, giving priority to protection, rational use, and inheritance and development. The relationship between economic and social development and protection of historical and cultural heritage shall be properly managed; the traditional layout and historic character of the city shall be preserved and carried forward; protection and inheritance of outstanding history and culture shall be strengthened; and high-quality urban and rural development and coordinated economic and social development shall be promoted.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protecting the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas, include such protection in their plans for national economic and social development, arrange protection funding, and include it in their respective fiscal budgets.
The Historic and Cultural City Protection and Administration Committee shall supervise, guide, and coordinate major matters concerning protection of the historic and cultural city.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall, in accordance with these Regulations, handle routine protection and administration of the historic and cultural city within their jurisdictions.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist township people's governments and subdistrict offices in protecting the historic and cultural city.
articles.5:
The housing and urban-rural development departments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city.
The natural resources and planning departments shall be responsible for administration of conservation planning for the historic and cultural city.
The cultural relics departments shall specifically implement applications for World Heritage designation, guide protection and administration of revolutionary cultural relics, and perform other related protection duties prescribed by laws and regulations.
Other relevant departments shall perform related protection and administration work within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6: Social capital is encouraged and guided to participate in protecting the historic and cultural city, and diversified investment and financing mechanisms for such protection shall be established and improved.
articles.7: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts and their relevant departments shall organize cultural tourism publicity, disseminate protection knowledge, and provide more public-interest experiential activities to enhance public awareness of protection.
articles.8:
Any organization or individual has the right to discourage and report conduct that violates conservation plans or damages the historic and cultural city. The relevant departments shall promptly accept reports, organize verification and handling in accordance with the law, and provide feedback.
Organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection of the historic and cultural city shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with relevant State provisions.
Chapter II — Protected Assets
articles.9: The protected area of the historic and cultural city shall be the area specified in the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of Chengde Municipality.
articles.12:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize the preparation of a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of this Municipality and incorporate it into the overall territorial spatial plan. The conservation plan shall include protection principles, overall objectives, the protection system, protected assets, protection priorities, core protected areas, protection requirements, safeguard measures, and other matters.
The people's governments of counties, county-level cities, and districts shall prepare special conservation plans for their respective areas in accordance with the conservation plan.
An approved conservation plan shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, the preparation authority shall submit an amendment justification report. After consent from the original approval authority, the amended plan shall be submitted for approval in accordance with the original procedure.
articles.13: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall coordinate implementation of special conservation plans for the historic and cultural city, strengthen supervision and inspection of implementation, and conduct periodic assessments. Information on inspections and assessments shall be made public through government websites and major local news media and be subject to public supervision. Problems identified shall be promptly corrected and handled.
articles.14:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish a protection-list system for the historic and cultural city.
They shall conduct surveys of historical and cultural resources and, in accordance with prescribed procedures, establish a protection list.
Protected assets approved or published by the people's governments of the State, province, Municipality, or county, county-level city, or district shall be included directly in the protection list.
Any organization or individual may propose that an asset be included in the protection list.
Where an asset already on the list is lost or seriously damaged due to force majeure, or its protection level or type changes so that the list must be amended or the asset removed, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located shall submit an application for approval in accordance with the original procedure.
articles.15:
An asset not yet included in the protection list that is preliminarily determined by the people's government of the Municipality or its county, county-level city, or district to have protection value may be designated for interim protection. Within seven working days after designation, an interim-protection notice shall be sent to the owner and the holder of the right to use, informing them of the protection measures to be taken.
Interim protection shall automatically cease if the asset has not been included in the protection list within one year after delivery of the notice.
During interim protection, no organization or individual may damage the asset. If interim protection causes loss to the lawful rights and interests of an organization or individual, the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county, county-level city, or district shall provide compensation in accordance with the law.
articles.16:
A system of persons responsible for protection shall be implemented for the historic and cultural city. The responsible person shall be determined as follows:
(1) For a nationally designated historic and cultural city, the Municipal People's Government shall be responsible.
(2) For a historic district, historic town, or historic village, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located shall be responsible. If that government establishes a protection and administration organization, that organization shall be responsible.
(3) For a state-owned historic building, its custodian shall be responsible; if there is no custodian, the holder of the right to use shall be responsible. If neither can be identified, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall designate a responsible person.
(4) For a non-state-owned historic building, its owner shall be responsible. If the owner is missing, cannot be contacted, or ownership is unclear, its custodian shall be responsible. If there is no custodian in those circumstances, the holder of the right to use shall be responsible. If the owner, custodian, and user cannot be identified, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall designate a responsible person.
(5) For a protected asset spanning villages or communities, the responsible person shall be designated by the relevant township people's government or subdistrict office; for one spanning townships or subdistricts, by the relevant people's government of the county, county-level city, or district; and for one spanning counties, county-level cities, or districts, by the Municipal People's Government.
The responsible person shall be made public.
articles.18:
Construction within a protected area of the historic and cultural city shall comply with the following requirements:
(1) The Mountain Resort and its Outlying Temples shall be the core of the historic urban area. Important viewpoints, view corridors, and view areas shall be protected through height controls, controls on character by subarea, planning administration, and other means. Buildings shall not obstruct view corridors between the Mountain Resort and surrounding temples and nearby mountains, and the integrity of important view areas shall be preserved.
(2) No new construction or extension may be undertaken in a core protected area, except for necessary public infrastructure and public service facilities. Such necessary construction or extension shall be submitted to the administrative approval department for approval, which shall seek opinions from the competent planning, cultural relics, and other departments before granting approval.
(3) Construction in a construction control area shall comply with building controls established by the conservation plan, maintain traditional layouts, carry forward historic character, and be compatible with that character in height, bulk, color, and other respects.
articles.19: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall install signs at the principal entrances and exits of core protected areas of historic districts, towns, and villages. No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage such signs without authorization.
articles.20:
Where buildings, structures, or other facilities endanger the safety of immovable cultural relics or historic buildings; damage historic layouts, street and lane patterns, traditional character, or spatial environments of historic urban areas, historic districts, towns, villages, or traditional villages; fail to meet conservation-plan requirements on building height, form, view corridors, and other matters; or seriously affect residential safety, the people's government at the county level where they are located or the property-owning entity may, in accordance with the law, organize relocation or renovation through application-based tenancy termination, housing exchange, housing expropriation, or other means.
The people's government at the county level where a historic district, town, village, or traditional village is located shall, in accordance with the principle of intensive land use, coordinate construction land quotas and give priority to land needed for resident and villager housing and public service facilities required to implement conservation plans.
articles.21:
Historic buildings shall be maintained and repaired in accordance with conservation plans and technical standards for repairs. The user shall be responsible for maintaining and repairing a state-owned historic building; the owner shall be responsible for a non-state-owned historic building. The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts may provide financial subsidies. If the owner lacks the capacity to maintain and repair the building, the people's government shall take measures to protect it.
The housing and urban-rural development department shall provide technical guidance and services for repairs to buildings and structures within the scope of historic buildings, excluding cultural relics.
articles.23:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall plan suitable uses for historic urban areas, historic districts, historic towns and villages, traditional villages of China, historic buildings, and other assets; formulate catalogues guiding, restricting, or prohibiting industries in accordance with the law; reasonably control commercial development; and encourage and support local production and business activities with distinctive features, including traditional handicrafts, specialty products, and transmission and use of intangible cultural heritage.
In accordance with conservation plans, historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages may develop diverse distinctive industries and conduct, to an appropriate extent, tourism and business activities compatible with traditional culture, such as processing and making traditional crafts and handicrafts.
articles.24:
Research and documentation of traditional festivals, distinctive folk customs, traditional crafts, and dialects shall be strengthened, and the results shall also be included in local chronicles to explore, cultivate, and establish exemplary traditional cultural brands.
Organizations and individuals are encouraged and supported in organizing, studying, and making use of historical and cultural resources and cultivating regional cultural brands.
articles.25:
Protection and use of revolutionary historical sites shall safeguard the sites themselves and their distinctive historic character.
In connection with major historical events and other occasions, commemorative activities based on revolutionary historical sites are encouraged. Research, organization, publicity, and exhibition of historical materials and the deeds of martyrs shall be emphasized to promote patriotism and the revolutionary tradition.
Revolutionary historical sites are encouraged to be integrated with other protected assets to expand presentation routes and content. Their presentation and use shall avoid excessive commercialization and entertainment and shall not become vulgarized.
articles.27: Where staff members of the people's governments of the Municipality or its counties, county-level cities, or districts or of relevant departments fail to perform supervision and administration duties, fail to investigate unlawful conduct when discovered, or otherwise abuse their authority, neglect their duties, or engage in malpractice for personal gain, they shall be investigated for criminal liability in accordance with the law if their conduct constitutes a crime; otherwise, they shall be disciplined in accordance with the law.
articles.29: Where a person installs, moves, alters, or damages a sign without authorization in violation of Article 19, the urban management and comprehensive law enforcement department shall order correction within a specified period. If the person fails to comply within that period, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.30:
Where a person engages in a prohibited activity within a protected area in violation of subparagraphs (1), (2), or (3) of Article 22, the natural resources and planning department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 500,000 but not more than RMB 1,000,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
Where a person damages, relocates, or demolishes a historic building without authorization in violation of subparagraph (4) of Article 22, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
Where a person carries out exterior repairs or decoration on a historic building, adds facilities, or changes its structure or use in violation of subparagraph (5) of Article 22, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.31: Where a person damages objects or places forming part of intangible cultural heritage in violation of subparagraph (6) of Article 22, the person shall bear civil liability in accordance with the law. Where the conduct violates public security administration, a public security administration penalty shall be imposed in accordance with the law.
articles.32:
Where other conduct violates these Regulations and laws or regulations prescribe penalties for it, those provisions shall apply.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.33:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 September 2023.

FBMCLI.10.7555523.title: Regulations of Xingtai Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of the historic and cultural city of this Municipality, carry on outstanding historical and cultural heritage, continue Xingtai's urban history and cultural lineage, and promote coordinated development of urban construction and historical and cultural protection, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and in light of local circumstances.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to planning, administration, protection, and use of the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
Protection of the historic and cultural city includes protection of historic urban areas, historic districts, historic towns and villages, traditional villages, historic-character areas, protected cultural relic sites, immovable cultural relics, historic buildings, buildings with traditional character, modern and contemporary revolutionary historical sites, ancient and notable trees, traditional place names, intangible cultural heritage, and other assets.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall put protection first and give priority to inheritance, and shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, rational use, and administration by category. The relationships between protection and use, protection and development, and protection and construction shall be properly managed; the traditional layout and historic character of the city shall be preserved and carried forward; the lawful rights and interests of original residents shall be safeguarded; and the authenticity, integrity, and continuity of historical and cultural heritage shall be maintained.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall, in light of local circumstances, include protection of the historic and cultural city in their plans for national economic and social development; establish and improve a protection mechanism involving government departments, experts and scholars, social organizations, and the public; improve working arrangements for policy-making, institution-building, supervision and administration, public education, and related matters; reasonably arrange protection funding; and include it in their respective fiscal budgets.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall assist with specific protection work.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist with related protection work.
articles.5:
The housing and urban-rural development departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall lead protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas.
The culture, radio, television, and tourism departments of those people's governments shall be responsible for protection of cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, and related assets within their respective areas.
The departments of urban management, development and reform, industry and information technology, public security, civil affairs, finance, natural resources and planning, forestry, and other relevant departments shall perform related protection work within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
People's procuratorates at the municipal and county levels are supported in bringing public-interest lawsuits concerning historical and cultural protection in accordance with the law.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall strengthen coordination and cooperation with the people's procuratorates at the same level in procuratorial public-interest litigation, focus on typical unlawful conduct in the field of protection of the historic and cultural city, improve mechanisms for transferring leads, consultation and assessment, information sharing, joint special actions, investigation and evidence collection, professional support, and publication of cases, perform their duties in accordance with the law, and jointly safeguard State and public interests.
articles.7:
Protection of the historic and cultural city is a shared responsibility of society as a whole. Every organization and individual has a duty to protect it and the right to offer opinions and suggestions on protection work and to discourage or report conduct that damages the city.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall establish mechanisms for raising protection funds through multiple channels. By simplifying approval procedures, adopting preferential policies, and other means, they shall stabilize market expectations and encourage and support various business entities in making sustained investments in protection. Enterprises, public institutions, volunteer-service organizations, public-interest social organizations, individuals, and other members of society are encouraged and supported in participating broadly through technical services, donations, sponsorship, and other means.
Chapter II — Protection List
articles.9:
The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection-list system for the historic and cultural city and prepare protection lists by category based on its protected assets. Where needed, a people's government at the county level may establish a protection-list system at its level.
A protection list shall state the name, location, ownership, date of origin, historical value, and other information about each protected asset, and shall be made public.
articles.10:
Protected assets approved and published by the State Council or a people's government of the province, Municipality, or county at the county level shall be included directly in the protection list.
For other proposed protected assets, the relevant sectoral department shall, together with the housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, and other competent departments, seek opinions from interested parties and the public and complete procedures including expert assessment and public notice before submitting the proposal to the people's government at the same level for approval and inclusion in the protection list.
articles.11:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall regularly organize surveys of protected assets of the historic and cultural city.
Any organization or individual may apply to or recommend to the relevant sectoral department that an asset be designated as a protected asset of the historic and cultural city. Upon receiving an application or recommendation, the department shall conduct a preliminary review. If it considers inclusion in the protection list necessary, it shall determine whether to include the asset in accordance with the procedure in the second paragraph of Article 10 of these Regulations.
articles.12: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall comprehensively and systematically organize all types of archives and materials relating to protected assets of the historic and cultural city and establish an information system containing geographic, place-name, historical, cultural, and other information about protected assets. The system shall enable efficient aggregation and sharing of data and facilitate routine supervision and public searches.
articles.13:
Where a protected asset already included in a municipal- or county-level protection list is lost or seriously damaged due to force majeure, or its protection level or type changes, the relevant sectoral department shall propose an adjustment to the protection list and submit it for approval in accordance with the original approval procedure.
Chapter III — Conservation Plans
articles.14:
After a historic and cultural city is approved and published, the Municipal People's Government shall organize the preparation of its conservation plan in accordance with the law.
After a historic town or village is approved and published, the people's government of the county at the county level where it is located shall organize preparation of its conservation plan in accordance with the law.
After a historic district is approved and published, the Municipal People's Government and the people's government of the county at the county level where it is located shall organize preparation of its conservation plan in accordance with the law.
A conservation plan shall be completed within one year after the historic and cultural city, town, village, or district is approved and published.
articles.15: In preparing conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, towns, villages, and districts, the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage shall be maintained; traditional layouts, historic character, and spatial scale shall be preserved; associated cultural landscapes, natural landscapes, and surrounding settings shall be protected; and controls and guidance concerning building height and form, view corridors, and other relevant features shall be strengthened.
articles.16:
Where a conservation plan for a historic and cultural city, town, village, or district concerns spatial layout, the corresponding spatial control requirements shall be incorporated into the territorial spatial plan at the same level.
Special plans concerning urban transport, municipal infrastructure, greening, sanitation, fire safety, underground-space development, and related matters shall be coordinated with conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, towns, villages, and districts.
articles.18:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall regularly organize relevant departments and experts to inspect and assess implementation of conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, towns, villages, and districts. Information on inspections and assessments shall be made public through government websites, news media, and other channels and be subject to public supervision. Problems identified shall be promptly corrected and handled.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.19:
A system of persons responsible for protection shall be implemented for the historic and cultural city of Xingtai. The responsible person shall be determined as follows:
(1) For a historic town, village, or district, the people's government of the county at the county level where it is located shall be responsible.
(2) For a historic building, its owner shall be responsible; if the owner is missing or ownership is unclear, its user shall be responsible.
(3) Where a protected asset has a dedicated protection and administration entity, that entity shall be responsible.
(4) For a protected asset spanning administrative jurisdictions, the people's government at the next higher common level shall designate the responsible person.
For other protected assets, special provisions in laws or regulations shall apply. If laws or regulations do not specify a responsible person, the people's government of the county at the county level where the asset is located shall designate one.
articles.22:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level may provide appropriate subsidies from protection funds for maintenance and repair of historic buildings.
If the person responsible for a non-state-owned historic building cannot bear the costs of its maintenance and repair, that person may apply to the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county at the county level for a subsidy.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall formulate and publish specific measures for subsidies.
articles.23:
The people's government of the county at the county level shall install protection signs for historic districts, historic buildings, ancient and notable trees, immovable cultural relics, and other protected assets of the historic and cultural city. A sign shall state the name, number, location, period of existence, protection category, cultural information, and other particulars of the protected asset.
Except for protection signs whose uniform design has been prescribed by the State or the provincial people's government, the Municipal People's Government shall prescribe a uniform design for other protection signs, and the people's government of the county at the county level shall arrange for their installation within six months after an asset is added to the protection list.
No organization or individual may install, move, remove, damage, alter, or obscure a protection sign without authorization.
articles.24: New construction, extension, or reconstruction in a construction control area of a historic town, village, or district shall comply with construction controls established by the conservation plan. The form, height, bulk, style, color, and other features of buildings and structures shall be strictly controlled and be compatible with the traditional layout and historic character of the core protected area.
articles.25:
No new construction or extension may be undertaken within a core protected area of a historic town, village, or district, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
A construction project for necessary infrastructure or public service facilities within such a core protected area shall obtain a construction project planning permit or a rural construction planning permit in accordance with the law.
The engagement of traditional craftspeople and use of traditional techniques and materials are encouraged to strictly protect historic layouts, street and lane patterns, and traditional character.
articles.26:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall, in accordance with the law, organize the preparation and publication of protection guidelines for historic buildings. Based on each building's historical, artistic, scientific, social, and cultural value, age, state of preservation, and other factors, protection shall be categorized as follows:
(1) A historic building of high historical, artistic, scientific, social, or cultural value and typical representativeness shall receive special protection. Its exterior form, facing materials, colors, principal internal structure, floor layout, and important decoration shall not be changed.
(2) A historic building of relatively high historical, artistic, scientific, social, or cultural value and a degree of representativeness shall receive key protection. Its exterior form, facing materials, colors, and important internal structures shall not be changed.
(3) A historic building with a degree of historical, artistic, scientific, social, or cultural value shall receive general protection. Its exterior form and colors and distinctive internal components shall not be changed.
No organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization. If construction in the public interest makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation or demolition necessary, approval shall be obtained in accordance with relevant provisions.
articles.27:
Organizations and individuals are encouraged and supported, on the condition that relevant protection requirements are met, in making rational use of the characteristics of historic buildings and the functional positioning of surrounding areas to establish museums, exhibition halls, memorial halls, art galleries, libraries, educational study bases, traditional workshops and shops, inns, homestays, and other venues for presenting and using historical and cultural heritage.
In accordance with conservation plans for the historic and cultural city, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall develop designated functional areas for cultural presentation, traditional residences, distinctive commerce, leisure experiences, and other purposes, improve urban functions, and enhance urban vitality.
articles.28:
In accordance with conservation plans, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall use incremental-renewal approaches such as "fine embroidery" and "stitching" and give priority to arranging and organizing relevant departments to construct and improve roads, water supply and drainage, power, sanitation, fire-safety, and other infrastructure and public service facilities within protected areas of historic towns, villages, and districts.
Where protection needs make it impossible to provide infrastructure in a protected area in accordance with current technical standards and specifications, the housing and urban-rural development, urban management, transport, water affairs, fire and rescue, and other competent departments shall, within their respective responsibilities, formulate a corresponding safeguard plan.
articles.29:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties at the county level shall strengthen collection, organization, study, refinement, presentation, and dissemination of Xingtai's historical and cultural resources. Through diverse cultural theme activities, including traditional festivals, commemorations, and cultural years, they shall comprehensively interpret historical stories, cultural values, and spiritual meaning centered on the culture of Shang and Zhou archaeological sites, ancient springs and wetlands, the ancient capital of Xingxiang, notable persons and folk customs, and the city known as "Ox City" for its biomorphic layout. This shall meet the public's cultural needs and support the role of historical and cultural resources in shaping and promoting the city brand "Taihang Spring City, Beautiful Xingtai" and cultivating and carrying forward the city spirit of "Simplicity, Kindness, Beauty, Diligence, and Self-Reliance."
Radio, television, newspapers, the internet, and other media are encouraged and supported in public-interest publicity for protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.30:
The training of traditional craftspeople, transmission of traditional techniques, and production of traditional materials related to protection of the historic and cultural city are encouraged and supported. Relevant intellectual property rights shall be protected in accordance with the law.
Schools and other relevant social organizations are encouraged and supported in offering programs or courses on maintenance and repair of ancient buildings and training professional and technical personnel.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.31:
Where laws, administrative regulations, or local regulations of this Province prescribe other penalties for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
Where an administrative penalty prescribed in these Regulations is within the scope of relatively centralized exercise of administrative penalty powers in urban management approved by the State Council or the provincial people's government, it shall be imposed by the urban management and comprehensive administrative law enforcement department.
articles.33:
Where, without justifiable reason, the person responsible for protection of a historic building fails to perform maintenance and repair duties, causing damage to the building in violation of these Regulations, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.34:
For the purposes of these Regulations, "historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages" means nationally designated historic and cultural cities approved and published by the State Council; historic and cultural cities of Hebei Province approved and published by the provincial people's government; Chinese historic and cultural towns and villages approved and published by the housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments of the State Council; and historic and cultural towns and villages of Hebei Province approved and published by the provincial people's government.
"Historic urban area" means an area of a town that reflects its character during its historical development or during a particular period of development and includes areas commonly called the old city or old urban area. The protected area of Xingtai's historic urban area is the area enclosed by the urban roads specified in the plan, including Tuanjie East Street, Kaiyuan Road, Xinxing East Street, Xinhua North Road, and Xinhua South Road.
"Historic district" means an area designated and published by the relevant State department or the provincial people's government that contains especially rich cultural relics, a concentration of historic buildings, substantially and authentically preserves traditional layout and historic character, and has a certain scale.
"Historic building" means a building or structure designated and published by a people's government of the Municipality or at the county level that has a degree of protection value and reflects historic character and local features, but has not been published as a protected cultural relic site or registered as an immovable cultural relic.
articles.35:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 July 2024.
