FBMCLI.10.8750700.title: Regulations of Taining County, Sanming Municipality, on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of Taining, a historic and cultural city (the "City"), promote and develop China's outstanding traditional and revolutionary cultures, coordinate protection of the City with urban and rural development, and, in light of local circumstances, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and the Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and Traditional Villages.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to protection and use of the City within the administrative area of Taining County (the "County"). The specific protected area shall be determined and published in the conservation plan for the City.
Protected assets of the City include historic urban areas; historic towns and villages and traditional villages; cultural relics; historic buildings and buildings with traditional character; ancient and notable trees; intangible cultural heritage; other historical and cultural resources; and other assets with protection value.
Where laws or regulations provide otherwise for protection of the foregoing assets, those provisions shall apply.
articles.3: Protection of the City shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, territorial responsibility, measures tailored by category, and rational use.
articles.4:
The people's government of the Municipality and its relevant competent departments shall guide and supervise protection of the City and provide related policy support in accordance with the law.
The County People's Government shall take overall responsibility for protection of the City, include it in the County's plans for national economic and social development, and include necessary funding in its fiscal budget.
Competent departments for housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism, development and reform, urban management, education, ethnic and religious affairs, public security, civil affairs, finance, human resources and social security, natural resources, transport, water affairs, emergency management, market regulation, ecology and environment, and related matters shall jointly protect the City within their respective responsibilities.
Relevant township people's governments shall protect the City within their jurisdictions in accordance with their responsibilities.
articles.6: The County People's Government shall establish a compensation system for protection of the City. Where protection needs cause loss to the lawful rights and interests of an organization or individual, fair and reasonable compensation shall be provided in accordance with the law.
articles.7: The people's governments of the Municipality and the County, their relevant competent departments, and the Historic and Cultural City Protection and Administration Agency shall strengthen public education on protection of the City and enhance awareness throughout society.
articles.8: Every organization and individual has a duty to protect the City and the right to discourage and report conduct that damages it. The relevant competent departments shall publish complaint and reporting channels, promptly handle complaints and reports received, and inform the complainant or reporter of the result.
articles.9:
Relevant villagers' or residents' committees may establish community-based protection organizations and adopt village rules to assist with protection of the City.
Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection through donations, investment, volunteer service, and other means.
Chapter II — Protection of the Historic Urban Area
articles.11:
The County People's Government shall coordinate planning and construction of the historic urban area and surrounding areas to carry forward the traditional layout and overall character.
Development and administration of surrounding areas shall support improvements to industries, transport, the environment, and other aspects of the historic urban area.
articles.12: Place names and building names within the historic urban area that embody traditional cultural meaning shall not be changed without authorization. If a change is necessary in special circumstances, before applying for approval in accordance with the law, the civil affairs department of the County People's Government shall seek opinions from the County's Historic and Cultural City Protection and Administration Agency and culture and tourism department.
articles.13:
Construction within the historic urban area shall comply with the conservation plan for the City. Buildings and structures that do not conform to that plan or are incompatible with the traditional layout and overall character shall be gradually renovated or modified in accordance with the law.
The height, style, spatial scale, and color of buildings and structures within the historic urban area shall be controlled. Architectural styles shall reflect the distinctive character of "Shanyang's Ming-era charm." Ground surfaces in squares, pedestrian areas, traditional streets, and lanes shall use materials and forms that reflect the historic character.
articles.14:
In accordance with conservation plans for the City and its historic districts, the housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall organize relevant competent departments to use incremental-renewal approaches to increase public open spaces in historic districts and historic areas and make up for deficiencies in supporting public infrastructure and public service facilities.
Construction and repair of public infrastructure and public service facilities in the historic urban area shall follow the principle of minimum disruption. Water supply and drainage, power and communications, gas, and other utility networks shall be installed underground or handled by other suitable means. If underground installation of existing networks is genuinely difficult, their routing shall be orderly and standardized.
articles.15:
The County's Historic and Cultural City Protection and Administration Agency shall install uniformly designed protection signs at the principal entrances and exits of historic areas and mark their protected boundaries.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection sign for a historic area without authorization.
articles.16: Protection and rational use of historic areas shall be combined, with emphasis on local characteristics. Construction within a historic area shall not change its traditional character.
articles.18: The natural character of mountains within the historic urban area, including Lufeng Mountain, shall be strictly protected. No mountain may be excavated or trees felled without authorization.
articles.19:
Water systems within the historic urban area, including the Beixi and Shanxi streams, shall be strictly protected and their historic layout carried forward. It is prohibited to discharge sewage directly into water, dump refuse, or occupy waterfront space without authorization.
The housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall organize the water affairs, urban management, ecology and environment, and other relevant departments to comprehensively improve the water environment of rivers and ditches in the historic urban area, including through dredging, ecological restoration, and water circulation projects, and improve water quality.
articles.20: The housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall organize the culture and tourism, water affairs, urban management, and other relevant departments to strengthen protection, rehabilitation, and use of ancient wells. In coordination with streets, lanes, and courtyards, they shall organize repair of important damaged ancient wells and gradually restore their landscape or use functions.
articles.21:
Appropriate slow-traffic zones and routes shall be added to the historic urban area to create a street environment suitable for non-motor vehicles and pedestrians. Non-motorized transport and walking shall be the primary modes of travel in historic districts.
Parking facilities meeting residents' needs shall be planned and built to an appropriate extent in the historic urban area. Measures such as time-shared parking, sharing public parking resources, and tiered time-based parking fees shall facilitate parking.
articles.22: Food-service operators in the historic urban area shall install grease separators or other facilities to treat oily wastewater and collect and dispose of such wastewater in accordance with applicable provisions.
articles.23:
The housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall, together with relevant competent departments, strengthen emergency-response capacity in the historic urban area, formulate emergency response plans, and use civil-defense, physical-protection, and technical measures in combination to improve disaster prevention, mitigation, and relief.
Firefighting facilities and access routes shall be provided in the historic urban area in accordance with fire-safety technical standards and specifications, and a person responsible for fire safety shall be designated. If protection needs make compliant installation impossible, the County's Historic and Cultural City Protection and Administration Agency shall formulate a corresponding fire-safety assurance plan together with the fire and rescue agency.
articles.24:
The County's Historic and Cultural City Protection and Administration Agency shall organize routine inspections of urban administration, fire safety, public security, building safety, traffic order, business-use controls, and other matters in the historic urban area, and include such inspections in community grid-based administration.
Chapter III — Protection of Buildings
articles.25: Protection of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character from different periods and of different types within the protected area of the City shall be strengthened, with priority given to protecting exterior features, structures, components, and other elements embodying their core value.
articles.26: The housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall organize the natural resources, culture and tourism, and other departments to survey and assess historic buildings, buildings with traditional character, and other historical and cultural resources within the protected area of the City. It shall propose an initial list of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character and identify the responsible persons for protection. After expert assessment, consultation with interested parties and the public, and public notice, the list shall be submitted to the County People's Government for designation and publication.
articles.27:
The County's Historic and Cultural City Protection and Administration Agency shall install uniformly designed protection signs for historic buildings and buildings with traditional character included in the protection list.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection sign for a historic building or a building with traditional character without authorization.
articles.28:
If construction reveals a building or structure not yet included in the protection list that may have protection value, the project owner shall suspend construction and immediately report it to the housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government. That department shall, together with the Historic and Cultural City Protection and Administration Agency, the culture and tourism department, and other relevant departments, promptly inspect the site and issue a handling opinion within five working days. It shall also notify the owner, user, or manager in writing to take interim protection measures, such as safeguarding the site and installing signs.
For a building or structure under interim protection, the housing and urban-rural development department shall organize expert review within seven working days. If the asset is confirmed to have protection value, it shall be added to the protection list. If it has no protection value, the owner, user, or manager shall be notified in writing within two working days that the interim protection measures are lifted.
articles.29: Historic buildings and buildings with traditional character shall, in principle, be protected in situ. If a construction project in the public interest makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation is necessary, an assessment shall be conducted, opinions shall be widely sought from relevant departments and the public, and approval shall be obtained in accordance with the law.
articles.30:
The housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall, in accordance with the law, organize preparation and publication of protection guidelines for historic buildings and designation and control guidelines for buildings with traditional character, and supervise and guide maintenance and repairs by the persons responsible for protection. Those persons shall strictly carry out maintenance and repairs in accordance with the applicable guidelines. If a responsible person lacks the capacity to do so, the County People's Government shall take measures to protect the building.
An entity undertaking repair work on a historic building or a building with traditional character shall carry on traditional construction techniques and employ craftspeople with repair skills. The housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall, together with the culture and tourism, education, human resources and social security, and other relevant departments, establish and improve training and assessment mechanisms for inheritors of repair techniques and craftspeople.
articles.31:
Where a building is expropriated and demolished in accordance with the law, carved work, murals, building components, and other items retained from it that have value for cultural relic collections shall be collected by a cultural relic collection entity designated by the culture and tourism department of the County People's Government. Items with use value shall be recycled and reused by an entity designated by the County People's Government.
Chapter IV — Inheritance and Use
articles.32: In accordance with the conservation plans for the City and its historic districts and applicable protection requirements, original residents may continue living at the original site and engage in production, business, and other activities in local distinctive industries, thereby carrying forward the City's original social form and way of life.
articles.33:
Business activities in the historic urban area shall comply with the conservation plans for the City and its historic districts. The housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall, together with the market regulation and other competent departments, formulate a catalogue of encouraged businesses and reasonably arrange the distribution of business activities.
Business operators shall comply voluntarily with the business-use layout for the historic urban area, operate lawfully, conduct business in a civilized manner, provide services honestly, and are encouraged to sell local specialty products and establish local brands.
articles.34:
The establishment of designated functional areas for cultural presentation, traditional residences, distinctive commerce, leisure experiences, and other purposes in historic districts and historic areas is encouraged to improve urban functions and enhance urban vitality.
Provided protection requirements are met and original exterior appearances, structures, and components are preserved, qualified organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and use of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character through functional conversion, transfer of operating rights, equity cooperation, and other means, thereby improving the standardization and professionalism of such activities.
articles.36:
The County People's Government shall use sites of important historical events and areas with a concentration of revolutionary cultural relics in the City to establish bases for patriotic education, combine patriotic education with protection of the City, carry on revolutionary culture, and promote patriotism.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.37: Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.38: Where a person installs, moves, alters, or damages a protection sign for a historic area without authorization in violation of Article 15, the housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall order correction within a specified period. If the person fails to comply within that period, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 5,000 but not more than RMB 20,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 5,000.
articles.39: Where a person occupies or damages a pavilion, covered walkway, archway, or its facilities in violation of subparagraph (2) of Article 17, the housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 2,000 but not more than RMB 10,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.40: Where a person keeps a dog in a public place or a common area of a building in violation of subparagraph (5) of Article 17, the urban management department of the County People's Government shall order correction within a specified period. If the person fails to comply within that period, a fine of not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 5,000 shall be imposed.
articles.41:
Where a state organ or its staff member responsible for protection of the City fails to investigate unlawful conduct in accordance with the law when discovered, or otherwise abuses authority, neglects duties, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in violation of these Regulations, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be dealt with by the competent authority in accordance with the law.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.42: For the purposes of these Regulations, "historic area" means an area containing a concentration of buildings with traditional character that substantially and authentically reflects Taining's traditional character and local features during a particular historical period and has a certain scale.
articles.43:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 October 2025.

Regulations cited in this document
Central regulations
Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics (2024 Revision)
Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages (2017 Revision)
Local regulations
Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and Traditional Villages

FBMCLI.10.4783869.title: Regulations of Liaoyang Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: [Legislative purpose] These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection and administration of the historic and cultural city of this Municipality, carry on outstanding history and culture, and, in light of local circumstances, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages.
articles.2: [Scope of application] These Regulations apply to activities concerning protection, planning, and use of the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
articles.3: [Protection principles] Protection of the historic and cultural city shall give priority to protection, coordinate planning, and make rational use; preserve the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage; maintain and carry forward its traditional layout, historic character, and mountain-and-water setting; and properly manage the relationship between economic and social development and protection of historical and cultural heritage.
articles.4:
[Responsibilities of people's governments and departments at all levels] The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas, incorporate conservation plans into overall plans for national economic and social development and territorial spatial plans, and include necessary protection funding in their respective fiscal budgets.
The housing and urban-rural development departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall, together with the cultural relics and natural resources departments at the same level, be responsible for specific implementation of conservation plans and supervision and administration of protection within their respective administrative areas.
Departments of development and reform, industry and information technology, finance, ecology and environment, transport, agriculture and rural affairs, emergency management, forestry and grassland, and other relevant departments shall perform related duties for protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective responsibilities.
articles.5: [Assessment and supervision] The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall organize assessments of protection of the historic and cultural city and report annually to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level on protection work within their respective administrative areas.
articles.6: [Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee] This Municipality shall establish a Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee to provide unified leadership and coordinate protection of the historic and cultural city. The Municipal People's Government shall separately prescribe the Committee's composition and rules of procedure.
articles.7:
[Publicity and guidance] The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts and their relevant departments shall organize cultural tourism publicity, disseminate protection knowledge, and provide more public-interest experiential activities to enhance public awareness of protection. Publicity volunteer teams are encouraged to guide the public's orderly participation in protection work.
Chapter II — Protected Assets and Protection List
articles.9:
[Criteria and procedure for designating historic areas] An area not designated as a historic district that meets either of the following criteria may be designated as a historic area by the Municipal People's Government after expert assessment and review organized by the housing and urban-rural development department together with the cultural relics department at the same level, deliberation by the Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee, and approval by the Municipal People's Government:
(1) an area where traditional streets and lanes are well preserved or buildings reflecting traditional character are concentrated; or
(2) an area with relatively rich surviving remains that can authentically reflect the ethnic or local characteristics of this Municipality in ancient, modern, or other historical periods.
Where laws or regulations prescribe designation criteria, those provisions shall apply.
articles.10:
[Requirements and procedure for the protection list] The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection list for the historic and cultural city.
Protected assets approved or published by the people's governments of the State, province, Municipality, county-level city, or district shall be included directly in the list.
For other protected assets, the people's government of the county-level city or district where the asset is located shall submit an application. The Municipal People's Government's housing and urban-rural development department shall, together with the cultural relics department at the same level, organize expert assessment and review, submit the matter to the Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee for deliberation, and, after approval by the Municipal People's Government, include the asset in the protection list.
Where an asset on the list is lost or seriously damaged due to force majeure, or its protection level or type changes such that amendment or removal is necessary, the people's government of the county-level city or district where the asset is located shall submit an application for approval in accordance with the original procedure.
The list shall state the name, location, ownership, history, value, and other particulars of each protected asset and shall be made public.
articles.11:
[Interim protection system] During historical and cultural resource surveys conducted by the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts, or based on leads provided by organizations or individuals, a historical and cultural resource with a degree of protection value that is not yet included in the protection list shall be assessed and reviewed by experts organized by the people's government of the county-level city or district where it is located and may be designated as an asset for interim protection. Where interim protection measures are needed, the owner, holder of the right to use, or custodian shall be notified in writing.
Within 30 days after an interim-protection decision is made, the people's government of the county-level city or district shall initiate the application procedure for adding the asset to the protection list. During interim protection, the township people's government or subdistrict office where the asset is located shall conduct inspections and supervision. No organization or individual may damage or demolish the asset. The interim-protection decision shall automatically cease if the asset has not been added to the protection list within 12 months after the decision.
If interim protection causes loss to the lawful rights and interests of an organization or individual, the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county-level city or district shall provide compensation.
Chapter III — Conservation Plans
articles.12:
[System for preparing conservation plans] The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of conservation plans for the historic and cultural city and historic districts of this Municipality.
The people's government of a county-level city shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic towns and villages within its administrative area.
The housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic areas, historic buildings, and other protected assets.
Conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, towns, villages, and districts shall be completed within one year after approval and publication.
Conservation plans for historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages shall be incorporated into territorial spatial plans at the corresponding level.
Conservation plans for historic districts, historic areas, historic buildings, and other assets shall be incorporated into detailed control plans at the corresponding level.
Special plans concerning urban transport, municipal infrastructure, greening, sanitation, fire safety, underground-space development, and related matters shall be coordinated with conservation plans.
articles.13:
[Delineation of protected areas] A conservation plan for the historic and cultural city shall delineate protected areas for protected assets.
Protected areas of historic towns, historic villages, historic districts, and historic areas shall include core protected areas and construction control areas.
For a historic building within a historic district, the protected area shall comprise the building itself. For a historic building outside a historic district, the protected area shall comprise the building itself and any necessary construction control area.
Signs shall be installed for the foregoing assets, and their information shall be made public.
articles.14:
[Approval procedure for conservation plans] After deliberation by the Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee, the Municipal People's Government shall submit the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city to the provincial people's government for approval.
After deliberation by the Committee, the people's government of the county-level city where a historic town or village is located shall submit its conservation plan to the provincial people's government for approval.
After deliberation by the Committee, the Municipal People's Government shall submit a conservation plan for a historic district to the relevant provincial department for review and then approve it.
After deliberation by the Committee, a conservation plan for a historic area or historic building shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
Before submission for approval, the authority that organized preparation shall publish the draft plan and solicit public opinions for at least 30 days. A hearing may be held where necessary.
Within 30 days after a conservation plan is approved, the authority that organized its preparation shall make it public.
An approved conservation plan shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, public opinions shall be widely solicited, expert review shall be organized, and the plan shall be amended, submitted for approval, and published in accordance with relevant procedures.
articles.15:
[Implementation of conservation plans] In accordance with conservation plans, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall formulate annual implementation plans, organize relevant departments and experts to inspect and assess implementation, promptly correct and handle identified problems, and make the results public.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.16:
[Designation of persons responsible for protection] A system of persons responsible for protection shall be implemented for the historic and cultural city.
The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protection of the historic urban area.
The people's government of the county-level city or district where a historic town, historic village, historic district, or historic area is located shall be responsible for its protection.
The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall be determined as follows:
(1) For a state-owned building, its custodian shall be responsible; if there is no custodian, the holder of the right to use shall be responsible.
(2) For a non-state-owned building, its owner shall be responsible; if ownership is unclear, the holder of the right to use or custodian shall be responsible.
(3) If the owner, holder of the right to use, and custodian cannot be identified, the people's government of the county-level city or district where the building is located shall designate a responsible person.
For other protected assets not listed above, the people's government of the county-level city or district shall designate a responsible person.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall notify the responsible person in writing. An organization or individual objecting to the designation shall submit the objection within 30 days after delivery of the written notice.
articles.19:
[Permitted activities in protected areas of historic towns, villages, and districts] No new construction or extension may be undertaken in a core protected area of a historic town, historic village, or historic district, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. New buildings and structures in a construction control area shall comply with construction controls established by the conservation plan.
Construction within a protected area shall be compatible with traditional layouts, historic character, and spatial scale and shall not alter associated natural landscapes or settings. Approval procedures for construction shall comply with applicable State and provincial laws and regulations.
Existing buildings and structures within a protected area that are incompatible with traditional layouts or historic character shall be gradually renovated or relocated.
articles.20:
[Prohibited activities within protected areas of historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages] The following activities are prohibited within protected areas of historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages:
(1) quarrying, mining, or other activities that damage traditional layouts or historic character;
(2) constructing factories, warehouses, or other facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances; or
(3) occupying roads, river and lake systems, gardens, green spaces, or other areas designated for retention in a conservation plan.
articles.21:
[Prohibited conduct concerning historic buildings] The following conduct concerning a historic building is prohibited:
(1) carving or defacing the building;
(2) carrying out exterior repairs or decoration, adding facilities, or changing the building's structure or use without approval; or
(3) other conduct that may damage the historic building.
articles.22:
[Installation of protection signs] A protection sign shall be installed for every protected asset included in the protection list within one year after the list is published. The sign shall state protection information such as the asset's name, number, location, date of construction, publishing authority, and a brief historical description.
The Municipal People's Government shall prescribe a uniform design for protection signs, and the people's governments of counties, county-level cities, and districts shall arrange for their installation. No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a sign without authorization.
articles.24:
[Specific measures for repairs] The Municipal People's Government shall formulate and publish an annual repair plan for historic buildings. In accordance with that plan, the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality shall notify the responsible persons and supervise and guide repairs in accordance with conservation plans, protection guidelines, or technical standards for repairs.
Repair of a historic building shall be approved by the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality. Before approval, opinions shall be sought from the cultural relics and natural resources departments at the same level, and relevant procedures shall be completed in accordance with laws and regulations.
If a historic building is at risk of damage and its responsible person lacks the capacity to maintain and repair it, the people's government of the county-level city or district shall take protection measures.
articles.25:
[Protection requirements for historic buildings] A construction site shall avoid historic buildings. If avoidance is impossible due to special circumstances, the building shall be protected in situ.
For in-situ protection, the project owner shall prepare a protection plan and submit it for approval by the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality together with the cultural relics department at the same level.
No organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization. If a construction project in the public interest makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation or demolition necessary, the housing and urban-rural development departments of the Municipality or the relevant county-level city, together with the cultural relics departments at the same level, shall submit the matter to the relevant provincial departments for approval and organize relocation or demolition in accordance with applicable technical standards and administrative provisions.
The project owner shall include the costs of in-situ protection, relocation, or demolition of a historic building in the construction-project budget.
Chapter V — Rational Use
articles.26: [Principles for use] Use of the historic and cultural city shall, alongside protection, take economic development into account. Protection shall take priority; areas suitable for residence may be inhabited and areas suitable for business may be used for business; and use shall proceed incrementally.
articles.27:
[Guidance by people's governments and relevant departments] The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts may use rent reductions, financial subsidies, and other policy measures to guide social capital and individuals in participating in protection and use of protected assets.
People's governments at all levels shall make use of historical resources and natural and cultural landscapes to encourage development of cultural industries with local characteristics and promote tourism, cultural experiences, educational study tours, and other industries.
articles.28:
[Participation by multiple parties in use] Persons responsible for protection are encouraged to make historic buildings that meet public-access requirements available to the public as cultural venues, such as museums and memorial halls, in light of each building's characteristics.
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and use through donations, fund support, technical services, community building, and other means.
Social organizations, university research institutions, and individuals are encouraged to conduct academic research, practical innovation, cultural-product development, cultural publicity, traditional-culture education, talent training, and other work related to protection of the historic and cultural city.
The establishment of presentation and transmission venues for publicizing, presenting, and teaching intangible cultural heritage is encouraged.
Chapter VI — Legal Liability
articles.29: [Prohibited activities in protected areas] Where a person engages in a prohibited activity within a protected area in violation of Article 20, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 500,000 but not more than RMB 1,000,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.30: [Carving or defacing historic buildings] Where a person carves or defaces a historic building in violation of subparagraph (1) of Article 21, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order restoration of the original condition or other remedial measures and impose a fine of RMB 50.
articles.31: [Unauthorized conduct concerning historic buildings] Where a person engages in conduct described in subparagraph (2) of Article 21 without approval from the housing and urban-rural development department together with the cultural relics department at the same level, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.32: [Unauthorized installation, movement, alteration, or damage of protection signs] Where a person installs, moves, alters, or damages a protection sign for a historic town, historic village, or historic district without authorization in violation of Article 22, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order correction within a specified period. If the person fails to comply within that period, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.33: [Damage, unauthorized relocation, or demolition of historic buildings] Where a person damages, relocates, or demolishes a historic building without authorization in violation of Article 25, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.34: [Legal liability of relevant staff] Where staff members of the people's governments of the Municipality or its counties, county-level cities, or districts or of relevant departments fail to perform supervision and administration duties, fail to investigate unlawful conduct when discovered, or otherwise abuse their authority, neglect their duties, or engage in malpractice for personal gain in violation of these Regulations, they shall be disciplined in accordance with the law if their conduct does not constitute a crime; if it constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.36:
[Other legal liability]
Where laws or regulations prescribe penalties for other conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
Where these Regulations do not provide otherwise, relevant laws and regulations shall apply.
Chapter VII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.37:
[Definitions]
"Historic urban area" means an area of a town that reflects its historical development or character during a particular period and includes areas commonly called the old city or old urban area.
"Historic towns and villages" means towns and villages approved and published by the provincial people's government that preserve especially rich cultural relics, have major historical value or commemorative significance, and substantially reflect the traditional character and local ethnic features of certain historical periods.
"Historic district" means a historic area approved and published by the provincial people's government that preserves especially rich cultural relics, has a concentration of historic buildings, substantially and authentically reflects traditional layout and historic character, and has a certain scale.
"Historic area" means an area that authentically reflects the traditional character and ethnic or local features of a particular historical period.
"Protected cultural relic site" means a cultural relic or historic site designated and published for key protection by a people's government at or above the county level.
"Historic building" means a building or structure designated and published by a people's government of a city or county that has a degree of protection value and reflects historic character and local features, but has not been published as a protected cultural relic site or registered as an immovable cultural relic.
"Underground archaeological deposit area" means an area with a concentrated distribution of underground cultural relics designated and published as such by a city people's government or competent administrative department. Underground cultural relics include ancient cultural sites, tombs, and buildings buried beneath the urban ground.
"Historic environmental features" means ancient wells, walls, stone steps, paving, revetments, ancient and notable trees, and other features reflecting historic character.
articles.38:
[Effective date] These Regulations shall take effect on the date of publication.

Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics (2017 Revision)
Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages (2017 Revision)

FBMCLI.10.9476014.title: Regulations of Putian Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection and administration of the historic and cultural city, carry on and promote outstanding history and culture, and promote integrated development of historical and cultural protection and inheritance with urban and rural construction, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and Traditional Villages, and the Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Buildings with Traditional Character, and in light of local circumstances.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to planning, protection, use, and administration of the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
Protected assets include historic urban areas; historic districts, towns, and villages; traditional villages; cultural relics; historic buildings; buildings with traditional character; historic environmental features; traditional place names; and intangible cultural heritage.
Where laws or regulations otherwise provide for the protection and administration of protected assets, those provisions shall apply.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, administration by category, and rational use; preserve the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage and continuity of community life; and promote integration of outstanding history and culture with modern life.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall be responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city, include its protection in their plans for national economic and social development, improve institutions, mechanisms, and policy safeguards, and strengthen coordination among departments and cooperation among regions.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall conduct routine inspections and carry out publicity and other specific protection work within their jurisdictions.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist with related protection work.
articles.5: The Municipal People's Government shall establish a coordination body for protection of the historic and cultural city to coordinate protection work, establish and improve a performance-assessment mechanism, and study major protection matters.
articles.6:
The housing and urban-rural development department, together with the culture and tourism department, shall handle specific protection and administration work for historic and cultural cities, districts, towns, and villages; traditional villages; historic buildings; and buildings with traditional character.
The culture and tourism department shall supervise and administer cultural relic protection and protect and preserve intangible cultural heritage.
Departments of development and reform, ethnic and religious affairs, civil affairs, finance, natural resources, ecology and environment, emergency management, urban management, and other departments, and fire and rescue agencies shall protect the historic and cultural city within their respective responsibilities.
articles.7:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall include funding for protection of the historic and cultural city in their respective fiscal budgets. The funding shall be used for surveys and designation of protected assets; maintenance, repair, emergency protection, and use; related infrastructure; improvement of the living environment; and other work.
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection through donations, investment, volunteer service, and other means.
articles.8:
Every organization and individual has a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and the right to discourage, report, or complain about conduct that damages it. The relevant competent departments shall promptly investigate and handle reports and complaints in accordance with the law.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts and their relevant departments may commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection work in accordance with applicable provisions.
Chapter II — Conservation Plans and Protection List
articles.9:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city of this Municipality.
Conservation plans for historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages shall be prepared in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions.
Once approved in accordance with the law, a conservation plan shall serve as the basis for protection and administration and shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, approval shall be obtained in accordance with statutory procedures.
articles.10:
In preparing conservation plans for the historic and cultural city, districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages, the cultural lineage of the "Seaside Zoulu" and "Land of Literary Renown" shall be carried forward; the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage shall be maintained; traditional layouts, historic character, and spatial scale shall be preserved; associated cultural landscapes, natural landscapes, and surrounding settings shall be protected; and controls and guidance concerning building height and form, view corridors, and other relevant features shall be strengthened.
Protection guidelines for a historic building shall provide for overall protection of associated natural landscapes and the environment.
Special plans concerning urban transport, municipal infrastructure, green spaces, tourism, fire safety, civil defense, and related matters shall be coordinated with the relevant conservation plans for the historic and cultural city.
Spatial control requirements in conservation plans for the historic and cultural city, districts, towns, villages, and other areas shall be incorporated into the territorial spatial plan at the same level and administered uniformly through the territorial spatial basic information platform.
articles.12:
A protection-list system shall be implemented for the historic and cultural city. Within one year after these Regulations take effect, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall establish a protection list and administer protected assets by level and category.
Historic districts, towns, and villages; traditional villages; historic buildings; buildings with traditional character; and other protected assets already approved and published shall be included directly in the protection list.
For other assets proposed for designation by the people's governments of the Municipality or a county or district, the competent department for the asset shall seek opinions from interested parties and the public, organize expert assessment, and conduct public notice. The housing and urban-rural development department shall then submit the proposal to the people's government at the same level for approval and inclusion in the list.
Where a change in protection level or type, or another circumstance, requires adjustment of the list, the competent department may propose an adjustment, which the housing and urban-rural development department shall submit to the people's government at the same level for approval.
articles.13:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall regularly organize surveys of historical and cultural resources. Any organization or individual may apply or make a recommendation to the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality or a county or district to include historical and cultural heritage with protection value in the protection list.
A special survey of historical and cultural resources shall be conducted where urban and rural construction involves renewal and renovation of a large area.
articles.14:
In accordance with conservation plans, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall carry out environmental improvement, repairs, and maintenance in historic urban areas, historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages; improve roads, water supply, drainage, sewage, power, fire-safety, and other infrastructure; and provide supporting facilities such as parking lots and visitor service centers.
Power, communications, water supply, drainage, gas, and other utility lines within protected areas of historic urban areas, historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages shall be relocated or installed underground in accordance with plans and the law.
articles.15:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall establish an information platform for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city, use digital and other new technologies and methods to collect and analyze information on protected assets, enable efficient aggregation and sharing of data, improve intelligent protection and administration, and facilitate public searches.
Chapter III — Controls on Character and Protection Measures
articles.16:
The historic urban area shall receive integrated, systematic, and comprehensive protection in accordance with the conservation plan.
Protected areas of historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages shall include core protected areas and construction control areas. No new construction or extension may be undertaken within a core protected area, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. New buildings and structures in a construction control area shall comply with construction controls established by the conservation plan.
Before area-wide repair or renovation of a historic district, town, village, or traditional village, the people's government of the county or district where it is located shall prepare an implementation plan in accordance with the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city to ensure that the plan is carried out.
The housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality shall organize preparation of technical specifications for protection and repair of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character and strengthen guidance. Exterior repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or changes to the structure or use of a historic building shall be submitted for approval and the relevant procedures completed in accordance with the law.
articles.17:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall install protection signs at the principal entrances and exits of core protected areas of historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages and for historic buildings, buildings with traditional character, and other protected assets. The design and content of signs shall comply with relevant standards and requirements. Smart features such as QR codes shall present information about protected assets to the public, and the information shall be incorporated into the protection and administration platform.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection sign without authorization.
articles.18:
If the historical and cultural value of a protected asset is seriously affected, the competent department for that asset shall, together with the housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism departments, organize expert assessment, and the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county or district shall take emergency protection measures.
For an asset not yet on the protection list that is preliminarily determined by the competent department, together with the housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism departments, to have protection value, interim protection may be provided and the application and designation procedure initiated in accordance with the law. If the asset is confirmed to have protection value, it shall be included in the protection list; otherwise, the relevant organizations and persons shall be promptly notified and interim protection measures lifted. During interim protection, no organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish the asset without authorization, and the township people's government or subdistrict office where it is located shall conduct inspections and supervision.
The Municipal People's Government shall formulate measures for administration of emergency and interim protection.
articles.20:
The persons responsible for protection of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character shall be determined in accordance with relevant provisions and shall perform the following duties:
(1) maintain structural safety and ensure the proper functioning of public fire-prevention, disaster-prevention, and other facilities and equipment; promptly address safety hazards and emergencies and report them to the relevant departments;
(2) carry out maintenance and repairs in accordance with relevant provisions;
(3) promptly stop conduct endangering protected assets and notify the relevant departments; and
(4) perform other protection duties prescribed by laws and regulations.
If a responsible person lacks the capacity to maintain and repair a building, the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county or district shall coordinate a solution as needed.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts may provide financial subsidies for maintenance and repair of non-state-owned historic buildings and buildings with traditional character.
articles.22:
Firefighting facilities and access routes within core protected areas of historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages and within historic buildings and buildings with traditional character shall be provided in accordance with applicable fire-safety technical standards and specifications, and a person responsible for fire safety shall be designated. If objective conditions make compliance impossible, the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality or the relevant county or district shall, together with the fire and rescue agency, formulate a fire-safety assurance plan compatible with protection requirements.
Chapter IV — Rational Use
articles.23:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall plan suitable business uses and guide industries in historic urban areas, historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages. They shall support cultural tourism, protection and transmission of intangible cultural heritage, and related uses.
Subject to protection requirements, the establishment of intangible cultural heritage presentation centers, memorial halls, museums, and other venues to present the historical and cultural meaning of the historic and cultural city is encouraged.
Through policy guidance, financial support, and other means, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall renew Putian's historic and cultural identity and recreate cultural elements or historic scenes such as Xinghua Prefectural Academy and Ninghai Ancient Bridge.
articles.24:
The organization, study, and use of historical and cultural resources are encouraged. Research and documentation concerning Putian and Xianyou opera, Putian and Xianyou dialects, traditional festivals, distinctive folk customs, traditional crafts, former residences of notable persons, place-name culture, and related matters shall be strengthened to carry on and promote outstanding traditional culture.
Protection, transmission, and use of time-honored brands and traditional crafts shall be strengthened, and regional cultural brands cultivated.
articles.25:
Protection and use of historic districts, towns, villages, traditional villages, historic buildings, and buildings with traditional character shall safeguard the lawful rights and interests of original residents and preserve continuity of traditional ways of life.
Original residents are encouraged to continue living at the original site in accordance with conservation-plan requirements, engage in production and business in local distinctive industries, and participate in protection and use by contributing buildings, funds, and other resources in exchange for a reasonable return.
articles.26:
As needed, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts may coordinate resources to establish an operating platform for acquisition of buildings, exchange of property rights, and leasing and maintenance of traditional residences to promote protection and use of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character.
Use of a historic building or a building with traditional character shall meet relevant protection requirements, shall not impair its historical or cultural value, and shall not contravene core socialist values or public order and good morals.
articles.27:
Protection and use of revolutionary historical sites shall safeguard the sites themselves and their distinctive historic character.
In connection with major historical events and other occasions, commemorative activities based on revolutionary historical sites are encouraged. Research, organization, publicity, and exhibition of historical materials and the deeds of martyrs shall be emphasized to promote patriotism and the revolutionary tradition.
articles.28:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties and districts shall strengthen development of professional personnel for protection of the historic and cultural city, organize training for grassroots administrators, inheritors of repair techniques, and craftspeople, and support and guide universities, colleges, and vocational schools in offering related courses and training professional and technical personnel.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.29: Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.30:
Where any of the following circumstances occurs in violation of these Regulations, the housing and urban-rural development department shall order correction within a specified period. If the person fails to comply within that period, the following penalties shall be imposed:
(1) For unauthorized installation, movement, alteration, or damage of a protection sign for a historic district, town, village, traditional village, or historic building, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
(2) For unauthorized installation, movement, alteration, or damage of a protection sign for a building with traditional character, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 5,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 500 but not more than RMB 1,000.
articles.31:
Where a competent department or its staff member abuses authority, neglects duties, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in protecting the historic and cultural city in violation of these Regulations, the person shall be disciplined in accordance with the law; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.32: An agency dispatched by the Municipal People's Government shall, within the scope of its authorization, perform related work for protection of the historic and cultural city in accordance with these Regulations.
articles.33:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2026.
