FBMCLI.10.9277156.title: Regulations of Yueyang Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2025 Amendment)

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection and administration of Yueyang, a historic and cultural city, inherit and promote outstanding history and culture, and promote coordinated development of the economy and social culture, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and in light of local circumstances.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to planning, protection, use, and administration of the historic and cultural city within the urban planning area of Yueyang Municipality.
articles.3:
The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city, establish and improve a coordination mechanism for its protection, and study major protection matters.
The people's governments of districts shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration within their respective jurisdictions. Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall conduct inspections and submit reports concerning protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.4:
The housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality shall, together with the competent cultural relics department, handle specific work for protection and supervision of the historic and cultural city. The housing and urban-rural development departments of the Municipality and its districts shall supervise and administer repair of historic buildings and safety of their use within protected areas.
The cultural relics departments of the Municipality and its districts shall protect immovable cultural relics within protected areas.
The culture and tourism departments of the Municipality and its districts shall protect and transmit intangible cultural heritage and outstanding traditional culture within protected areas.
Relevant departments of development and reform, finance, natural resources and planning, urban management and comprehensive law enforcement, forestry, industry and information technology, water affairs, civil affairs, and other matters shall jointly protect the historic and cultural city within their respective responsibilities.
articles.5: The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall include protection of the historic and cultural city in their plans for national economic and social development and include protection funding in their respective fiscal budgets.
articles.7: Every organization and individual has a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and the right to offer suggestions on preparation and implementation of conservation plans and to report conduct that damages the city.
articles.8:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall organize public education on protection of the historic and cultural city and enhance awareness among residents. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection through investment, sponsorship, donations, and other means.
Organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection work shall be commended and rewarded by the people's governments of the Municipality and its districts and their relevant departments.
articles.9:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall strictly implement conservation plans, strengthen supervision and inspection of implementation by relevant administrative departments, assess the state of protection, and report every two years to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level on protection work for the historic and cultural city.
Chapter II — Protected Assets
articles.10:
Protected assets of the historic and cultural city include historic urban areas, historic districts, historic-character protected areas, protected cultural relic sites, historic buildings, intangible cultural heritage, ancient and notable trees, and other assets prescribed by laws and regulations.
The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection list stating the name, ownership, location, type, protection level, history, historical value, and other particulars of each protected asset and shall make the list public.
articles.11:
The Municipal People's Government shall designate the following as key protected assets:
(1) The historic urban area, comprising approximately 1.98 square kilometers centered on the old Yuezhou Prefecture city and Baling County city, bounded on the north by the northern boundary of the shipyard, on the west by the eastern shore of Dongting Lake, on the south by the railway siding at Sanjiaoxian, and on the east by the western side of the railway siding within Factory 3517. Key features to protect include the ancient city's mountain-and-water setting represented by Dongting Lake, Jiuhua Mountain, Huomiao Mountain, Wenmiao Mountain, and Baihe Mountain; the city-wall forms of Yuezhou Prefecture and Baling County and the traditional urban structure represented by the "two prefecture-and-county crosses"; the ancient city's core landscape features formed by Yueyang Tower, Yueyang Confucian Temple, Cishi Pagoda, and Lüxianting Pavilion; the names, routes, scale, and traditional character of 11 historic streets and lanes, including Yuxiangzi, Chaxiangzi, Youzhailing Lane, Jinjialing Lane, Jiehekou Street, Nanyue Lane, Wanshougong Lane, Hexiangzi, Shangda Lane, Youji Lane, and Shangcishi Lane; and view corridors between the city and lake, important public buildings and natural mountains, and streets and lanes and towers, temples, pagodas, and pavilions.
(2) Historic districts, including the Dongting South Road Historic District and the Lucheng South and North Main Streets Historic District. Key features to protect include important urban axes, city-wall forms, historic streets and lanes, protected cultural relic sites, historic buildings, intangible cultural heritage, important public buildings, view corridors, and historic environmental features. The Dongting South Road Historic District, approximately 15.72 hectares, lies west of Dongting South Road and adjacent to the Dongting Lake scenic area, east of Dongting South Road, north of Yuxiangzi, and south of Yanjiachong Road. The Lucheng South and North Main Streets Historic District, approximately 13.7 hectares, extends along both sides of Lucheng South Main Street and North Main Street, from the Old West Gate in the west to the south side of Lucheng Central Primary School in Yunxi District in the south, and to the western curb line of Provincial Highway 201 in the east.
(3) Historic-character protected areas, including the Dongting North Road, Hanlin Street, and British Experts' Buildings of the Yue-Han Railway protected areas. Key features to protect include historic streets and lanes, historic buildings, view corridors, protected cultural relic sites, ancient and notable trees, and other environmental features. The Dongting North Road area, 21.1 hectares, extends from the northern road boundary of Baling West Road in the south to the western foothills of Jiuhua Mountain in the north, from the western road boundary of Dongting North Road in the east to the shore of Dongting Lake in the west. The Hanlin Street area, 7.4 hectares, extends from Caiyuanpo Road in the east to Dongting North Road in the west, and from Baling West Road in the south to Wenmiao Mountain in the north. The British Experts' Buildings of the Yue-Han Railway area, approximately 2.37 hectares, is centered on those buildings and extends from the road east of the wharf in the south to the western section of Jingang Lane in the north, with the wharf to the west and Changjiang Timber Industry Company to the east.
(4) Protected cultural relic sites, with priority given to Yueyang Tower, Yueyang Confucian Temple, Cishi Pagoda, Yueyang Church School, Yuezhou Customs House, the Tonggushan site, the Dajitou site, and other sites.
(5) Other assets requiring key protection.
articles.12:
The Municipal People's Government may designate an area that has not been designated as a historic district as a historic-character protected area if it meets either of the following conditions:
(1) historic buildings are concentrated in a contiguous area of a certain scale; or
(2) its spatial layout, landscape form, architectural form, and other features substantially reflect the regional culture of a particular historical period in Yueyang.
articles.14:
The housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality shall, together with the competent cultural relics department, organize expert review and propose a plan for designation or adjustment of a historic-character protected area or historic building, make the proposal public and seek public opinions, and solicit opinions from relevant departments and interested parties through symposiums, hearings, and other means before submitting it to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
Chapter III — Protection Measures
articles.15:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of conservation plans for the historic and cultural city, historic districts, and historic-character protected areas of this Municipality. The people's governments of districts shall organize preparation of conservation plans and repair plans for historic buildings.
Urban planning shall meet the requirements for protection of the historic and cultural city, preserve and carry forward traditional urban layouts and historic character, and maintain the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage.
A conservation plan for the historic and cultural city shall be prepared separately and incorporated into the overall urban plan, with a level of detail meeting relevant State requirements.
A conservation plan for a historic district shall be prepared separately based on the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city and shall have the level of detail required for a detailed control plan for the district.
Conservation plans for historic-character protected areas and historic buildings shall be prepared in accordance with relevant State, provincial, and municipal provisions and shall have the level of detail required for a detailed control plan for the relevant land parcel.
Conservation plans for the historic and cultural city, historic districts, historic-character protected areas, and historic buildings shall be submitted for approval in accordance with statutory procedures.
articles.17:
The following activities within protected areas of the historic and cultural city shall be covered by a protection plan, approved by the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality together with the competent cultural relics department, and carried out after completing relevant procedures in accordance with laws and regulations:
(1) activities that change the natural state of gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, or similar features;
(2) filming or holding a large public gathering in a core protected area; or
(3) other activities affecting traditional layouts, historic character, or historic buildings.
articles.18: Protection requirements for the historic and cultural city shall be incorporated into planning conditions for construction projects. Any organization or individual carrying out construction in a historic urban area, historic district, or historic-character protected area shall comply with the conservation plan and obtain approval from the competent planning, housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, and other administrative departments in accordance with the law. Construction shall not commence without such approval.
articles.19: Protection of the historic urban area shall follow the principle of "overall control and key protection." Protected areas shall be delineated in accordance with the conservation plan, and the remains of the ancient city walls shall be marked. Mountain-and-water landscape features around the historic urban area, including Jine Mountain, Ganshan Mountain, Yueshan Mountain, Junshan Mountain, Dongting Lake, and Nanhu Lake, shall be strictly protected, with priority given to the grand landscape of "tower and lake" formed by Yueyang Tower and Dongting Lake. Activities such as soil excavation at Jiuhua Mountain, Huomiao Mountain, Wenmiao Mountain, and Baihe Mountain that damage their character are prohibited. The traditional spatial structure of "one water, four mountains, two prefectural and county cities" and the traditional layout of historic streets and lanes shall be protected. The names, routes, scale, and traditional character of 11 historic streets and lanes, including Youzhailing Lane and Yuxiangzi, shall be preserved. Building height, bulk, form, and color shall be strictly controlled in construction control areas around core landscape features such as Yueyang Tower, Yueyang Confucian Temple, and Cishi Pagoda. Traditional character of historic buildings and view corridors between important nodes shall be protected.
articles.20: Core protected areas and construction control areas shall be delineated for historic districts. No new construction or extension may be undertaken in a core protected area, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. Such infrastructure and facilities shall not exceed two stories or an eaves height of 7 meters. Buildings in a construction control area shall not exceed three stories or an eaves height of 10 meters.
articles.21: New construction or reconstruction within a historic-character protected area shall be compatible with traditional historic character in height, bulk, form, color, and other respects. A new or reconstructed building shall not exceed four stories or an eaves height of 13 meters. Construction or reconstruction of roads shall not damage their original layout or landscape features.
articles.22: The cultural relics departments of the Municipality and its districts shall strengthen surveys, registration, archiving, and administration of protected cultural relic sites and other immovable cultural relics and prepare conservation plans for protected cultural relic sites. Immovable cultural relics with outstanding value that have not been designated as protected cultural relic sites shall gradually be proposed for designation at the relevant levels.
articles.23: Before carrying out construction within the protected area or construction control area of a protected cultural relic site, the project owner shall apply to the competent cultural relics department at the same level according to the site's protection level. Planning and construction approval procedures may be completed only after review and consent in accordance with statutory procedures.
articles.24:
Historic buildings shall be maintained and repaired in accordance with conservation plans. Repairs shall not change their original height, bulk, form, color, or other features. A new building or structure in the construction control area of a historic building shall be compatible with the building itself in bulk, form, color, and other respects, and shall not be higher than the adjacent historic building.
Exterior wall repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or changes to a historic building's structure or use shall be approved by the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality together with the competent cultural relics department, and relevant procedures shall be completed in accordance with laws and regulations.
articles.25:
For a state-owned historic building, its custodian shall be responsible for protection; if there is no custodian, the holder of the right to use shall be responsible.
For a non-state-owned historic building, its owner shall be responsible; if the owner is missing or ownership is unclear, its custodian shall be responsible; if there is no custodian, its user shall be responsible.
If the owner, holder of the right to use, or custodian cannot be identified, the housing administration department shall be responsible for protection.
articles.26:
The owner or user of a historic building shall use it rationally, be responsible for its maintenance and safety precautions, preserve its original character, and accept guidance, inspection, and supervision by the relevant departments.
The owner shall be responsible for maintenance and repair of a historic building. Such work shall follow a protection plan reviewed by the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality together with the competent cultural relics department.
articles.27:
If a historic building is at risk of damage and its owner lacks the capacity to repair it, the people's government of the district where it is located shall take measures to protect it.
No organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization.
articles.28:
A construction site shall avoid historic buildings. If avoidance is impossible due to special circumstances, in-situ protection shall be implemented to the greatest extent possible.
For in-situ protection of a historic building, the project owner shall determine protection measures in advance and submit them for approval by the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality together with the competent cultural relics department.
If a construction project in the public interest makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation or demolition necessary, the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality together with the competent cultural relics department shall submit the matter for approval by the protection department and cultural relics department designated by the provincial people's government.
The project owner shall include the costs of in-situ protection, relocation, or demolition of the historic building in the construction-project budget.
articles.29:
A protection sign shall be installed for every protected asset included in the protection list. The Municipal People's Government shall prescribe a uniform design, and the people's government of the district shall arrange for installation.
No organization or individual may install, move, obscure, alter, or damage a protection sign without authorization.
articles.30:
The culture and tourism departments of the Municipality and its districts shall strengthen surveys, collection, emergency safeguarding, research, dissemination, publicity, and education concerning intangible cultural heritage and outstanding traditional culture, prepare conservation plans, and establish a system of protection lists.
Use or development of representative items of intangible cultural heritage or outstanding traditional culture shall protect the objects and places forming part of those items.
articles.31:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall support organizations that rationally use representative items of intangible cultural heritage.
A representative inheritor of intangible cultural heritage shall explore, collect, and organize valuable materials concerning the heritage, train inheritors, and actively organize and participate in related presentations and performances.
articles.32:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall strengthen protection of ancient and notable trees. The forestry and landscape-gardening departments shall establish and improve archives for such trees and formulate protection measures.
Chapter IV — Legal Liability
articles.35:
Where a citizen, legal person, or other organization violates Articles 16 through 21, Article 24, or Articles 27 through 29 of these Regulations, the urban management and comprehensive law enforcement and other departments shall handle the matter in accordance with the law. The violator shall bear civil liability for damage to another person's civil rights and interests, be subject to a public security administration penalty imposed by the public security organ if the conduct violates public security administration, and face criminal liability if the conduct constitutes a crime.
Chapter V — Supplementary Provisions
articles.36: Within the urban planning area of Yueyang Municipality, the people's governments of Yueyang County and Linxiang City and the Administrative Committee of Nanhu New Area shall perform the duties assigned to district people's governments under Article 3 of these Regulations.
articles.37:
These Regulations were approved by the Standing Committee of the Hunan Provincial People's Congress and shall take effect on 1 May 2017.

FBMCLI.10.7318142.title: Regulations of Yinchuan Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2023 Revision)

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection and administration of Yinchuan, a historic and cultural city, carry on and promote China's outstanding traditional culture, continue the city's historical and cultural lineage, coordinate historical and cultural protection and use with urban and rural development, and, in light of local circumstances, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and the State Council's Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to planning, protection, and use of Yinchuan, a historic and cultural city.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, rational use, and territorial responsibility; preserve and carry forward its traditional layout and historic character; protect associated natural and cultural landscapes; maintain the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage; and properly manage the relationship between economic and social development and heritage protection.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas, include such protection in their plans for national economic and social development, and include protection funding in their respective fiscal budgets.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall assist relevant departments with protection work and conduct routine inspections within their jurisdictions.
articles.5:
The natural resources department shall be responsible for planning administration related to protection of the historic and cultural city, historic districts, and historic buildings.
The housing and urban-rural development department shall supervise and administer structural safety, use, and repair of buildings and structures other than cultural relics within the protected areas of historic buildings, historic urban areas, and historic districts.
The cultural relics department shall perform the related protection duties prescribed by these Regulations.
Departments of development and reform, finance, public security, gardens and landscaping, civil affairs, water affairs, emergency management, municipal administration, comprehensive law enforcement, and other relevant departments shall perform related protection work within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts and their relevant departments shall strengthen public education on protection of the historic and cultural city and enhance public awareness.
Every organization and individual has a duty to protect Yinchuan, a historic and cultural city, and the right to offer opinions and suggestions on protection work and to supervise and report conduct that damages the city.
articles.7:
Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and use of the historic and cultural city through donations, sponsorship, technical services, volunteer service, and other means.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection of Yinchuan, a historic and cultural city, in accordance with relevant State provisions.
Chapter II — Protected Assets
articles.9:
A protection-list system shall be implemented for protected assets of the historic and cultural city.
The natural resources department of the Municipality shall, together with the cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, gardens and landscaping, water affairs, civil affairs, and other relevant departments of the Municipality, propose a list of protected assets based on Article 8 of these Regulations, seek opinions from the people's governments of counties, county-level cities, and districts, interested parties, experts, and the public, and submit it to the Municipal People's Government for approval and publication.
articles.10:
The protection list shall be dynamically administered, and its update and adjustment shall follow the procedure in the second paragraph of Article 9 of these Regulations.
The cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, gardens and landscaping, water affairs, civil affairs, and other relevant departments of the Municipality shall regularly survey historical and cultural resources and promptly recommend to the natural resources department of the Municipality that qualifying assets be added to the protection list.
If an asset on the list has any of the following circumstances, the relevant departments shall promptly recommend an adjustment to the natural resources department of the Municipality:
(1) it no longer exists;
(2) lawful assessment determines, or severe damage followed by emergency protection confirms, that it has no protection value; or
(3) its protection level or type has changed.
articles.11:
Based on the protection list, the natural resources department of the Municipality shall, together with the cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, gardens and landscaping, water affairs, civil affairs, and other relevant competent departments, comprehensively and systematically organize archives and materials concerning the historic and cultural city using text, audio recordings, video recordings, surveys, multimedia, digital technologies, and other means; establish an archival database; administer it digitally; and update it promptly.
Chapter III — Conservation Plans
articles.13:
Based on the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, the natural resources department of the Municipality, together with the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where a historic district or historic building is located, shall prepare conservation plans for historic districts and plans for protection and use of historic buildings and submit them to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
Before a conservation plan for a historic district is approved, it shall be submitted to the relevant competent department of the autonomous region for review and consent in accordance with the law.
articles.14: Before a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, a historic district, or the protection and use of historic buildings is submitted for approval, the authority that organized its preparation shall publish the draft plan on government websites and in major local news media for at least 30 days and broadly solicit opinions from relevant departments, interested parties, experts, and the public through symposiums, review meetings, and other means. A hearing may be held where necessary.
articles.15: Within 30 days after approval, a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic district, or a plan for protection and use of historic buildings, shall be published on government websites and in major local news media.
articles.16:
An approved conservation plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic district, or a plan for protection and use of historic buildings, shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, the following procedures shall apply:
(1) To amend the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, the Municipal People's Government shall submit a special report and, after review and consent by the people's government of the autonomous region in accordance with the law, amend and resubmit the plan for approval and filing in accordance with the original preparation, approval, and filing procedures.
(2) To amend a conservation plan for a historic district, the Municipal People's Government shall submit a special report and, after review and consent by the relevant competent department of the autonomous region in accordance with the law, amend and resubmit the plan for approval in accordance with the original preparation and approval procedures.
(3) To amend a plan for protection and use of a historic building, the natural resources department of the Municipality shall propose an adjustment and, after review and consent by the Municipal People's Government, amend and resubmit the plan for approval in accordance with the original preparation and approval procedures.
articles.17:
Preparation, approval, and implementation of conservation and development plans for traditional villages shall comply with relevant State and autonomous-region provisions.
Based on such plans, the Municipal People's Government shall prepare an overall implementation plan for protection of traditional villages and formulate support measures.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.18: The historic and cultural city shall be protected as a whole. Its traditional layout, historic character, and spatial scale shall be preserved, and associated natural landscapes and settings shall not be altered.
articles.19:
A system of persons responsible for protection shall be implemented for the historic and cultural city.
The person responsible for protection shall be determined as follows:
(1) For a historic urban area or historic district, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located shall be responsible.
(2) For a historic building, its owner shall be responsible. If the owner is missing or ownership is unclear, its manager or user shall be responsible. If no responsible person can be identified, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where the building is located shall be responsible.
The responsible person, protection duties, and protection measures for traditional villages shall be determined in accordance with relevant State and autonomous-region provisions.
articles.22:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall install signs at the principal entrances and exits of core protected areas of historic districts and protection signs for historic buildings. The Municipal People's Government shall prescribe a uniform design for both types of signs.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a sign for a historic district or a protection sign for a historic building without authorization.
articles.23:
No new construction or extension may be undertaken in a core protected area of a historic district, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
Before issuing a construction project planning permit for necessary infrastructure or public service facilities within a core protected area of a historic district, the approval department shall seek opinions from the cultural relics department at the same level.
Demolition of a building, structure, or other facility other than a historic building within a core protected area of a historic district shall be approved by the natural resources department of the Municipality together with the cultural relics department at the same level.
articles.25:
The owner of a historic building shall be responsible for maintaining and repairing it in accordance with conservation plans. The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts may provide subsidies for such work from protection funds.
If a historic building is at risk of damage and its owner lacks the capacity to maintain and repair it, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall take measures to protect it.
The engagement of traditional craftspeople and use of traditional techniques to maintain and repair historic buildings are encouraged.
articles.26:
No organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization. A construction site shall, to the extent possible, avoid historic buildings. If avoidance is impossible due to special circumstances, in-situ protection shall be implemented to the extent possible.
If a construction project in the public interest makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation or demolition necessary, the project owner shall provide materials including a report demonstrating the necessity and feasibility of relocation or demolition, a relocation plan, and remedial measures. After the natural resources, housing and urban-rural development, and cultural relics departments of the Municipality or the relevant county or county-level city assess the plan and remedial measures, hold a hearing, and publish the plan for public comment, approval shall be requested in accordance with relevant State and autonomous-region provisions.
The owner of a historic building shall be consulted before it is relocated or demolished.
Where relocation or demolition of a historic building is approved, the project owner shall organize it in accordance with the approved plan and relevant provisions, under the supervision and administration of the housing and urban-rural development department of the county, county-level city, or district.
articles.27:
New buildings and structures in a construction control area of a historic district, and new, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures in a construction control area of a historic building, shall comply with construction controls established by the conservation plan. Their height, bulk, color, and other features shall be strictly controlled and compatible with the character of the core protected area.
Chapter V — Rational Use
articles.28: Through policy guidance, financial support, and other means, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall promote rational use of protected assets of the historic and cultural city, including historic urban areas, historic districts, historic buildings, and traditional villages. Such use shall comply with relevant protection requirements and shall not damage traditional layouts, historic character, or historical and cultural value.
articles.29:
In accordance with conservation plans, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall promote development of diverse distinctive industries in historic districts and traditional villages and, to an appropriate extent, business activities compatible with traditional culture, such as tourism and processing and making traditional crafts and handicrafts.
Social forces are encouraged to make rational use of historical and cultural resources to develop industries consistent with conservation plans and conduct business consistent with industrial-layout plans.
articles.30:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts may make rational use of state-owned historic buildings by leasing them, entrusting their operation to market entities, or other means in accordance with the law.
Organizations and individuals are encouraged to use historic buildings in diverse ways suited to their characteristics, including as exhibition halls, museums, libraries, and art galleries, and to conduct local cultural research, cultural creativity, tourism, distinctive commerce, and related activities.
Use of a historic building shall comply with relevant protection requirements.
articles.31: Use of a historic building shall be compatible with its historical value and internal structure, shall not change its traditional layout or historic character, and shall not endanger the safety of its principal structure or ancillary facilities.
articles.32:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts and their relevant departments shall strengthen collection, organization, study, presentation, and dissemination of historical and cultural resources; protect and carry on folk customs, folk arts, traditional techniques, and other heritage; interpret related historical stories, cultural values, and spiritual significance; promote deeper integration of history and culture with tourism; and bring out the social and educational role of historical and cultural resources.
Chapter VI — Legal Liability
articles.33: Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.34: Where staff members of the people's governments of the Municipality or its counties, county-level cities, or districts or of their natural resources, housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, and other relevant competent departments fail to perform supervision and administration duties, fail to investigate unlawful conduct when discovered, or otherwise abuse their authority, neglect their duties, or engage in malpractice for personal gain in violation of these Regulations, they shall be disciplined in accordance with the law if their conduct does not constitute a crime; if it constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.36:
Where, without justifiable reason, the person responsible for protection of a historic building refuses to perform protection duties in violation of Article 21, causing the building to be placed on a danger list or otherwise causing destructive effects on it, the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality or the relevant county, county-level city, or district shall order the person to perform the protection duties and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures.
Chapter VII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.37:
For the purposes of these Regulations:
(1) "historic urban area" means an area of a town that reflects its historical development or character during a particular period and includes areas commonly called the old city or old urban area;
(2) "historic district" means an area designated and published by the people's government of the autonomous region that preserves especially rich cultural relics, has a concentration of historic buildings, substantially and authentically reflects traditional layout and historic character, and has a certain scale; and
(3) "historic building" means a building or structure designated and published by a people's government of the Municipality, county, or county-level city that has a degree of protection value and reflects historic character and local features, but has not been published as a protected cultural relic site or registered as an immovable cultural relic.
articles.38:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2024.

FBMCLI.10.1418169.title: Regulations of Bozhou Municipality on the Protection of the National Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of the historic and cultural city, carry on and promote outstanding history and culture, and, in light of local circumstances, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and other relevant laws and administrative regulations.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to planning, protection, use, and administration of Bozhou, a nationally designated historic and cultural city (the "historic and cultural city").
For protection of cultural relics, the laws and regulations on cultural relics protection shall apply.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of government leadership, social participation, giving priority to protection, and rational use, and shall coordinate economic and social development with protection of historical and cultural heritage.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall conduct routine inspections and submit reports concerning protection of the historic and cultural city within their jurisdictions.
articles.5:
The urban and rural planning department of the Municipality shall, together with the competent cultural relics department, handle specific work concerning application for designation of the historic and cultural city, preparation and implementation of conservation plans, supervision, and administration.
The culture and tourism, urban management, housing, housing and urban-rural development, land and resources, environmental protection, development and reform, civil affairs, public security, transport, ethnic and religious affairs, and other relevant competent departments shall protect the historic and cultural city within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6: The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall include protection of the historic and cultural city in their plans for national economic and social development and include special funding for such protection in their respective fiscal budgets.
articles.7:
Any organization or individual has the right to offer opinions and suggestions on protection of the historic and cultural city and to report conduct that damages it. If a street, building, or structure with protection value is discovered, it shall be reported to the competent cultural relics department.
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection through donations, sponsorship, volunteer activities, and other means.
articles.8: The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection of the historic and cultural city in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions.
articles.9:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall organize public education on protection of the historic and cultural city, disseminate protection knowledge, and enhance protection awareness throughout society.
Chapter II — Protected Areas
articles.10:
Protected areas of the historic and cultural city include the Beiguan Historic District, the historic urban area, and historic-character areas. The Beiguan Historic District is a core protected area.
(1) The Beiguan Historic District is the area bounded by Xinhua North Road in the east, Heping Road in the south, Sixi Street and Chaijiagou in the west, and the south bank of the Wo River in the north. Key protected assets include important protected cultural relic sites and surrounding areas such as Huaxilou, Nanjing Lane Money Shop, and Beijing Temple; and areas where old residences and shops are concentrated along streets and lanes such as Baibu Street, Paizi Lane, Maopu Street, Nanjing Lane, Hongji Bridge, Datong Lane, Old Brick Street, Liren Street, and Dayou Street.
(2) The historic urban area is the area bounded by Mengcheng Road in the east, Lixin Road in the south, Guoyang Road in the west, and Heping Road in the north. Key protected assets include important protected cultural relic sites and surrounding areas such as the ancient tunnels, Huazu Temple, Daode Central Temple, and the old city mosque; ancient streets and lanes such as Renmin North Road, Banjielou, Caoxiangkou, Xiahou Lane, Wenli Lane, Lulu Bend, Hongxue Lane Entrance, Xuejia Lane, and Liuhu Street; remains of the ancient city walls; cultural relics and historic sites, historic buildings, old shops and residences, former residences of notable persons, and sites of important historical events.
(3) A historic-character area is an area within the main urban district, other than the Beiguan Historic District and historic urban area, that is based on cultural relics and historic sites and reflects cultural relic landscapes, environmental character, and features of the period in which they are located. Key protected assets include historic scenic areas such as the Cao Clan tomb complex and Tangwang Mausoleum; the settings of the hometowns of notable persons such as Cao Cao, Hua Tuo, Hua Mulan, and Chen Tuan; cultural relic landscapes such as Xuege Pagoda, Jiangning Guild Hall, and Bajiaotai; and cultural landscapes associated with rivers and lakes such as the Wo River landscape corridor.
articles.13:
The Municipal People's Government shall regularly organize surveys of historical and cultural resources. Measures for interim protection shall be taken for a street, building, or structure with protection value that has not yet been included in the protection list.
Chapter III — Protection Measures
articles.14: Conservation plans for the Beiguan Historic District, historic urban area, and historic-character protected areas shall be prepared separately based on the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city and, after approval in accordance with the law, made public.
articles.15: Preparation or amendment of urban and rural plans, overall land-use plans, and other special plans shall be coordinated with the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city.
articles.16: Construction within a protected area of the historic and cultural city shall comply with the conservation plan. No building, structure, or other facility that damages traditional character may be constructed; no building, structure, or other facility designated for protection by the conservation plan may be damaged; and no object or place forming part of intangible cultural heritage may be damaged.
articles.17: Construction within protected areas of the historic and cultural city shall control building height in accordance with urban planning requirements, shall not obstruct view corridors between principal viewpoints and principal landscape features, and shall comply with the zoned building-height controls for protected areas established by the conservation plan.
articles.18:
Activities within protected areas of the historic and cultural city shall comply with the conservation plan and the following requirements:
(1) Sand mining, quarrying, mining, and other activities that damage traditional layouts or historic character are prohibited.
(2) Occupying gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, roads, or other areas designated for retention in a conservation plan is prohibited.
(3) Constructing factories, warehouses, or other facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances is prohibited.
(4) Demolition of a building, structure, or other facility other than a historic building within a core protected area shall be approved by the urban and rural planning department of the Municipality together with the competent cultural relics department of the Municipality.
(5) Reconstruction of roads, water supply, drainage, power, sanitation, fire-safety, or other infrastructure shall be subject to a special plan that carries forward the traditional layout.
(6) Outdoor advertisements shall not damage the exterior character of historic districts or historic buildings.
(7) No new construction or extension of buildings or structures may be undertaken within a core protected area, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
(8) Carving or defacing a historic building is prohibited.
articles.19:
Protection of streets and buildings in the Beiguan Historic District shall comply with the following requirements:
(1) When historic streets and lanes in the area are rebuilt, their original alignments, spatial structure, appearance, stone-paved surfaces, and other distinctive architectural features shall be preserved.
(2) Household address plates, street and lane signs, and signs presenting the history and culture of streets and lanes shall be standardized. Shops shall install plaques in an antique style.
(3) Before residents repair, reconstruct, or rebuild traditional street-facing buildings and structures, old residences, or old shops, approval shall be obtained from the urban and rural planning department of the Municipality. Architectural forms and decoration shall use vernacular features such as gable roofs, pitched roofs, gray tiles, and exposed gray-brick walls. Original appearance shall be preserved during repair. Exterior facades shall not use decorative materials incompatible with traditional styles.
(4) State-owned shops and old residences along streets that are at risk of damage shall be promptly repaired or rebuilt. For non-state-owned shops and old residences, the responsible persons shall be urged to repair them within a specified period.
(5) During repair of buildings or old residences, no pits may be dug or soil taken, walls raised, or courtyards built, and no architectural components embodying the distinctive commercial style of ancient Bozhou may be damaged, including black doors, white shutter boards, brick, stone, or wood carving, painted decoration, roof-end tiles, wooden door latches, column bases, and curved beam ends.
articles.20: Protection of the historic urban area shall reflect its historic character and preserve the original road-network layout, distinctive streets and lanes, and their names.
articles.21:
New construction, reconstruction, or extension in a construction control area within the historic urban area shall comply with the conservation plan, proceed under an approved planning permit, and meet the following requirements:
(1) in height, bulk, facade, color, and other respects, it shall be compatible with traditional layouts and historic character within key protected areas;
(2) it shall not damage historic settings or cultural landscape features; and
(3) it shall not endanger building safety within key protected areas.
articles.22:
Historic-character areas shall preserve the natural landform, overall layout, and spatial form of the places where cultural relics and historic sites are located.
Renovation and construction in historic-character areas shall primarily create green spaces and squares compatible with historic character. Where cultural tourism facilities or management buildings are needed under a conservation plan, their bulk, form, style, and color shall be compatible with the cultural relics and historic sites.
articles.23: The Municipal People's Government shall provide categorized protection for historic buildings based on their historical, cultural, and artistic value, age, state of preservation, and other factors, formulate technical specifications for categorized protection, and publish them.
articles.24:
A system of persons responsible for protection of historic buildings shall be established. The responsible person shall be determined as follows:
(1) For a state-owned historic building, its custodian shall be responsible; if there is no custodian, its user shall be responsible. If neither can be identified, the urban and rural planning department of the Municipality shall, together with the cultural relics and housing departments, designate a responsible person and make the designation public.
(2) For a non-state-owned historic building, its owner shall be responsible. If the owner is missing or ownership is unclear, its custodian shall be responsible; if there is no custodian, its user shall be responsible. If the owner, custodian, and user cannot be identified, the urban and rural planning department of the Municipality shall, together with the cultural relics and housing departments, designate a responsible person and make the designation public.
articles.25:
The owner or holder of the right to use a historic building shall maintain the building, take safety precautions, preserve its original character, and accept guidance, inspection, and supervision by the relevant departments.
The owner shall be responsible for maintenance and repair of the building in accordance with a protection plan reviewed by the urban and rural planning department of the Municipality together with the cultural relics department.
If a historic building is at risk of damage and its owner lacks the capacity to repair it, the people's government of the district shall take measures to protect it.
No organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization.
articles.26: Before carrying out another construction project within the protected area of an ancient tunnel or a discovered but unexcavated site, approval shall be obtained from the competent authority, and relevant procedures shall be completed in accordance with laws and regulations.
articles.27: Remains of the ancient city walls shall be strictly protected. Any road constructed on existing remains shall retain its original location, layout, and existing spatial scale. No excavation or removal of soil may be carried out on the remains, and the city-wall foundations shall not be damaged.
articles.28:
An old residence discovered during a cultural relic survey that still has repair value and has not been designated as a protected cultural relic site shall be repaired and designated as a protected cultural relic site in accordance with the law.
An old residence with the traditional architectural style of Bozhou and a certain age shall be designated and published by the urban and rural planning and cultural relics departments of the Municipality.
articles.29: Traditional place names embodying the history and culture of Bozhou shall be researched and organized. Where a place name must be restored or changed, the prescribed procedures shall be followed.
articles.30:
Protection signs shall be installed for historic buildings, ancient and notable trees, immovable cultural relics, and other protected assets of the historic and cultural city. A sign shall state the name, number, location, period of existence, protection category, cultural information, and other particulars of the protected asset.
The Municipal People's Government shall prescribe a uniform design for signs, and the people's government of the district shall arrange for installation within six months after the asset is added to the protection list.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection sign without authorization.
Chapter IV — Rational Use
articles.32: Rational use of protected assets shall fully explore their cultural meaning and support distinctive business or public-interest activities, including cultural creativity, leisure tourism, cultural research, traditional handicrafts, dissemination of intangible cultural heritage, cultural experiences, and establishment of exhibition venues and museums.
articles.33:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts encourage the organization, exploration, study, and use of historical and cultural resources, the creation of regional brands, and development of cultural and artistic products with local characteristics.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.35: Where a township people's government, subdistrict office, or its staff members fail to conduct routine inspections or provide on-site protection as required by Article 4 of these Regulations, the people's government of the district shall order correction. If the circumstances are serious, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be disciplined in accordance with the law.
articles.36:
Where a person commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations, the urban management department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law:
(1) demolishing, without approval, a building, structure, or other facility other than a historic building in violation of subparagraph (4) of Article 18; or
(2) causing a destructive impact on traditional layouts, historic character, or historic buildings in violation of subparagraphs (5) or (6) of Article 18.
articles.37: Where a person carves or defaces a historic building in violation of subparagraph (8) of Article 18, the urban management department shall order restoration of the original condition or other remedial measures and impose a fine of RMB 50.
articles.38: Where a person violates the third paragraph of Article 30 of these Regulations, the urban management department shall order correction within a specified period. If the person fails to comply within that period, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.39:
Where a person commits any of the following acts within a protected area of the historic and cultural city in violation of these Regulations, the urban management department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 500,000 but not more than RMB 1,000,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law:
(1) quarrying, mining, or other conduct that damages traditional layouts or historic character;
(2) occupying gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, roads, or other areas designated for retention in a conservation plan; or
(3) constructing factories, warehouses, or other facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances.
articles.40:
Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.41:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2018.

FBMCLI.10.1521716.title: Regulations of Huize County, Qujing Municipality, on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection, administration, and use of Huize, a historic and cultural city (the "City"), carry on and promote outstanding history and culture, and promote coordinated development of historical and cultural heritage protection and the economy and society, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and the State Council's Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and in light of local circumstances.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to planning, administration, construction, and use for protection of the City.
articles.3: Protection of the City shall follow the principles of integrated planning, giving priority to protection, scientific administration, rational use, and coordinated development.
articles.4:
The Qujing Municipal People's Government shall strengthen organizational leadership of protection and administration of the City. The People's Government of Huize County shall be responsible for planning, administration, construction, and use for protection of the City. Relevant competent departments of the Municipality and Huize County for planning, housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism, natural resources, transport, finance, development and reform, ecology and environment, health, public security, fire safety, market regulation, ethnic and religious affairs, and other matters shall perform related protection and administration work within their respective responsibilities.
The People's Government of Huize County shall establish a Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee to coordinate relevant departments and promote integrated law enforcement.
Relevant subdistrict offices and villagers' and residents' committees in Huize County shall assist with protection and administration of the City within their jurisdictions.
articles.6:
The Qujing Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Huize County shall include funding for protection of the City in their fiscal budgets and actively seek special funding from higher-level governments for such protection.
Organizations, individuals, and other entities are encouraged to establish funds for protection of the City in accordance with the law.
articles.7: 18 May of each year shall be the Protection Publicity Day for Huize, a historic and cultural city.
articles.8: Every organization and individual has a duty to protect the City and the right to discourage or report conduct that damages it.
articles.9:
The Qujing Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Huize County shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection of the City.
Chapter II — Conservation Plans
articles.10: The People's Government of Huize County shall include protection and administration of the City in its plans for national economic and social development.
articles.11: The People's Government of Huize County shall, in accordance with the law, prepare and amend the conservation plan, detailed conservation plan, and detailed construction plan for core protected areas of the City. Special plans concerning power and telecommunications, roads and transport, earthquake resistance and disaster prevention, public fire safety, tourism development, underground-space development and use, and related matters shall be coordinated with the conservation plan for the City.
articles.12:
The People's Government of Huize County shall strengthen conservation planning and establish a protection-list system for the City. The list shall state the name, location, boundaries, date of origin, historical value, and other particulars of each protected asset and shall be made public.
Chapter III — Protected Areas and Assets
articles.13: Protected areas of the City comprise a core protected area, a construction control area, and an area for coordination of historic character. The People's Government of Huize County shall delineate and publish the specific boundaries in accordance with the conservation plan for the City approved by the State Council.
articles.15:
Key protected areas of the City are as follows: the historic urban area, 2.51 square kilometers, extending from Cuiping Straight Street in the east to the summit of Jinzhong Mountain in the south, from the Niu Family Ancestral Hall at the Great Buddha Temple in the west to Tongbao Road in the north; and Baiwu Historic Village, 0.53 square kilometers, extending from the iron tower at Shabakou in the east to the rural tractor road in Baiwu Village in the south, from Majia Shagou in the west to a point 20 meters north of the rear public road in the north.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.16:
Construction within protected areas of the City shall be approved in accordance with the law.
Maintenance and repair of buildings and structures designated for protection within a core protected area shall preserve their original height, bulk, exterior form, color, and other features and be compatible with the overall character. Renovation of buildings that are incompatible with the character shall meet requirements for the overall character. Buildings that are damaged or at risk of disappearing shall, after the required approvals are obtained in accordance with the law, be repaired in their original character or preserved as archaeological remains. Contemporary buildings with no protection value or that affect the overall character may be gradually demolished.
The type, height, bulk, color, and form of new or reconstructed buildings in a construction control area shall be compatible with the overall character of the core protected area.
An area for coordination of historic character shall focus on protecting the overall layout of the historic urban area. New or reconstructed buildings shall reflect local cultural traditions and distinctive building techniques.
articles.19:
For a state-owned immovable cultural relic, its user shall be responsible for repair and maintenance. For a non-state-owned immovable cultural relic or historic building, its owner shall be responsible for repair and maintenance.
If a non-state-owned immovable cultural relic is at risk of damage and its owner lacks the capacity to repair it, the People's Government of Huize County may negotiate an exchange of property rights with the owner. If the owner has the capacity to repair it but refuses to do so, the County People's Government may carry out emergency repairs, and the owner shall bear the costs. If neither measure can resolve the matter, the County People's Government may expropriate the asset in accordance with the law.
If inadequate protection puts a historic building at risk of damage, the People's Government of Huize County shall order its owner or user to repair it within a specified period.
If force majeure puts a historic building at risk of damage, the People's Government of Huize County shall order its owner or user to promptly take remedial measures.
Repair, relocation, or reconstruction of a protected cultural relic site shall be undertaken by an entity holding the corresponding qualification certificate for cultural relic protection projects.
No organization, individual, or other entity may obstruct or delay maintenance or repair of cultural relics.
articles.20:
The People's Government of Huize County shall formulate guidelines for protection and use of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character.
The Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee shall notify owners, users, and property management entities in writing of protection and use requirements.
articles.21: Where an owner or user repairs a historic building in accordance with the conservation plan and an approved plan, the People's Government of Huize County shall provide an appropriate financial subsidy, and the Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee shall provide technical support. The County People's Government shall formulate specific measures.
articles.22:
Street-facing facades, signs and shop displays, stalls, municipal facilities, steps and ramps, paving, lighting, and other features within a core protected area shall comply with relevant standards and be compatible with the character of the City. Where buildings or structures affect the character of streets and lanes, the relevant competent departments of the People's Government of Huize County shall require their owners or users to make corrections within a specified period.
Safety hazards within a core protected area shall be eliminated in accordance with laws and regulations on safety and fire protection, fire-safety facilities shall be provided, and fire safety shall be ensured. Where buildings or structures present safety hazards, the relevant competent departments of the People's Government of Huize County shall order their owners or users to eliminate the hazards promptly.
articles.23: Based on road and traffic-flow conditions, the traffic-management department of the public security organ of the People's Government of Huize County may take measures such as directing, restricting, or prohibiting the passage of motor vehicles, non-motor vehicles, or pedestrians entering a core protected area.
articles.24: The People's Government of Huize County shall formulate specific measures for administration of business uses within core protected areas in accordance with the principles of rational layout and control of total volume, and encourage, protect, and support businesses featuring traditional culture.
articles.25:
The People's Government of Huize County shall gradually restore historic water landscapes.
Wastewater within protected areas of the City shall be connected to the municipal wastewater network. During municipal infrastructure renovation, stormwater and wastewater shall be separated.
Chapter V — Protection and Use
articles.26:
Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and rational use of the City in accordance with the law through donations, sponsorship, investment, and other means, under the guidance of the Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee.
Social capital is encouraged and supported to invest in protection of the City. Where social capital is used to protect and repair cultural relics or publicly owned buildings, a right to use or operate them for a specified period may be granted, provided ownership is not changed.
articles.27: Organizations, individuals, and other entities are encouraged and supported in acquiring ownership or use rights in historic buildings in accordance with the law and conducting lawful business activities primarily in tourism, copper-trading culture, traditional handicrafts, distinctive commerce, and related sectors.
articles.29: The People's Government of Huize County shall formulate preferential policies to encourage and support social organizations, entities, and individuals in participating in repair and use of historic districts, guild halls, temples, traditional residential courtyards, and other assets. It shall promote integrated use of eligible historic districts and other historic buildings.
articles.30:
The People's Government of Huize County shall strengthen protection of intangible cultural heritage, designate entities responsible for protection, train inheritors, and support representative inheritors in transmission and dissemination through measures such as providing necessary venues and subsidies.
Chapter VI — Legal Liability
articles.32: Where a person violates subparagraph (3) of Article 17, the relevant administrative law enforcement department of Huize County shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. If the person fails to do so within that period, the department may designate a capable entity to perform the restoration or remedial measures, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 500 but not more than RMB 1,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.33: Where a person violates subparagraph (12) of Article 17, the relevant administrative law enforcement department of Huize County shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. If the person fails to do so within that period, the department may designate a capable entity to perform the restoration or remedial measures, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.34: Where a person violates subparagraph (1) or (3) of Article 18, the relevant administrative law enforcement department of Huize County shall order correction within a specified period and restoration of the original condition. If the person fails to comply within that period, the department shall demolish the facility in accordance with the law and impose a fine of not less than RMB 200 but not more than RMB 1,000.
articles.35: Where a person violates subparagraph (2) of Article 18, the relevant administrative law enforcement department of Huize County shall order correction within a specified period and restoration of the original condition. If the person fails to comply within that period, the department shall demolish the facility in accordance with the law and impose a fine of not less than RMB 100 but not more than RMB 200.
articles.36: Where a person violates subparagraph (13) of Article 17 or subparagraph (4) of Article 18, the relevant administrative law enforcement department of Huize County shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 200 but not more than RMB 500.
articles.37:
Other conduct violating these Regulations shall be penalized in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
Chapter VII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.38:
For the purposes of these Regulations:
"Historic building" means a building or structure designated and published by the People's Government of Huize County that has a degree of protection value and reflects historic character and local features, but has not been published as a protected cultural relic site or registered as an immovable cultural relic.
"Traditional residence" means a civilian building constructed during any historical period within the historic urban area of Huize County or Baiwu Village that reflects Huize's traditional character and cultural features such as traditional construction techniques, social ethics, and aesthetic concepts, excluding a protected cultural relic site, an immovable cultural relic not yet designated and published as a protected cultural relic site, or an ancient building.
"Historic street or lane" means an area within the historic urban area of Huize County or Baiwu Village containing numerous cultural relics and historic sites or contiguous traditional residences that authentically reflects the traditional street-and-lane character of Huize and has a certain scale.
articles.39:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 June 2019.
