FBMCLI.10.1685450.title: Regulations of Xi'an Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2021 Revision)

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of Xi'an, a historic and cultural city, inherit and promote outstanding historical and cultural heritage, and promote urban construction and economic development, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and relevant laws and regulations, and in light of local circumstances.
articles.2: The protected area of Xi'an, a historic and cultural city, comprises ancient-site areas, the ancient city wall and the area within it, and historic-character areas that reflect Xi'an's history and culture within the administrative area of Xi'an Municipality.
articles.3: These Regulations shall be observed in planning, construction, protection, administration, and other activities within protected areas of Xi'an, a historic and cultural city.
articles.4: Protection of Xi'an, a historic and cultural city, shall follow the principles of coordinated planning, effective protection, rational use, and scientific administration.
articles.5: The Municipal People's Government shall include protection and administration of the historic and cultural city in its plans for national economic and social development and include funding for protection, administration, and plan preparation in its fiscal budget.
articles.6:
The natural resources and planning department of the Municipality and the cultural relics administrative department of the Municipality shall be responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city.
Departments of housing and urban-rural development, urban management, culture and tourism, ethnic and religious affairs, ecology and environment, and other departments shall cooperate in protection and administration in accordance with laws and regulations and the authority determined by the Municipal People's Government.
The people's governments of counties and districts shall be responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective jurisdictions.
articles.7: The Municipal People's Government shall organize the collection, organization, study, protection, development, and use of cultural heritage including historical events, place-name stories, poetry and literature, local opera, traditional crafts, food culture, folk customs, and other heritage of Xi'an.
articles.8:
Protection of the historic and cultural city is a responsibility of society as a whole. Every organization and individual has a duty to protect it.
The Municipal People's Government shall organize public education on protection of the historic and cultural city and enhance public awareness.
articles.9:
Social sectors, organizations and individuals at home and abroad are encouraged to participate in protection, development, and use of the historic and cultural city through investment, donations, and other means.
The Municipal People's Government shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection work.
Chapter II — Planning for the Historic and Cultural City
articles.10: Based on the overall urban plan, the Municipal People's Government shall prepare a conservation plan for Xi'an, a historic and cultural city, and formulate protection guidelines.
articles.11: Based on the conservation plan for Xi'an, a historic and cultural city, the natural resources and planning department of the Municipality shall prepare detailed control plans and implementation plans for ancient-site areas, the ancient city wall and the area within it, and historic-character areas.
articles.13: In preparing a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, a detailed control plan, or an implementation plan, opinions from all sectors of society shall be widely solicited and expert review shall be organized.
articles.14:
The conservation plan for Xi'an, a historic and cultural city, shall be implemented after approval by the provincial people's government.
Detailed control plans and implementation plans shall be implemented after approval by the Municipal People's Government.
After approval, the conservation plan, detailed control plans, and implementation plans shall be made public.
Partial amendments and adjustments to the conservation plan, detailed control plans, implementation plans, and protection guidelines shall be submitted for approval and published in accordance with the original approval procedure.
articles.15:
Construction projects within protected areas of the historic and cultural city shall comply with the conservation plan. Planning and construction approvals shall not be issued for a project that does not comply with the plan, and the project owner shall not carry out construction.
Before construction near a protected cultural relic site, the project owner shall apply to the cultural relics administrative department of the Municipality. Planning and construction approval procedures may be completed only after review and consent in accordance with prescribed procedures.
No organization or individual may approve a construction project within protected areas of the historic and cultural city beyond its authority.
articles.16: The natural resources and planning department and the urban management and comprehensive law enforcement department shall strictly implement the conservation plan, inspect and supervise construction projects within protected areas of the historic and cultural city, and investigate and handle illegal construction.
articles.17:
Buildings, structures, and other facilities within ancient-site areas, the ancient city wall and the area within it, and historic-character areas that do not comply with the conservation plan, detailed control plan, or implementation plan shall be renovated, relocated, or demolished in accordance with the law.
Where a building, structure, or other facility to be relocated or demolished under the preceding paragraph was formed historically or constructed with approval, the people's government of the county or district where it is located shall organize implementation in phases and batches and provide resettlement and compensation in accordance with applicable provisions. Illegal construction shall be investigated and handled by the urban management and comprehensive law enforcement department.
Chapter III — Protection of Ancient-Site Areas
articles.18: An ancient-site area is a protected area containing the foundations of ancient villages, cities, palace precincts, and other remains designated as protected cultural relic sites. Such areas mainly include the Lantian Man site, Banpo site, the Feng and Hao capitals of the Zhou, the Epang Palace site of the Qin, the Han Chang'an City site, and the Daming Palace and Huaqing Palace sites of the Tang.
articles.19: The historic character and original terrain of an ancient-site area shall be preserved. Sand mining, soil removal, and excavation of ponds are prohibited. Construction unrelated to protection of the site and other activities damaging the site shall not be undertaken.
articles.20: If construction within an ancient-site area is necessary in special circumstances, the project owner shall apply to the cultural relics administrative department of the Municipality. Planning and construction approval procedures may be completed only after review and consent in accordance with prescribed procedures.
articles.21: Construction approved within an ancient-site area shall comply with the planning permit. It shall not damage the historic character of the site, pollute the environment, or endanger the safety of cultural relics.
articles.22:
Development and use of an ancient-site area shall preserve the site's integrity. Based on the conservation plan for Xi'an, a historic and cultural city, and the implementation plan for site protection, and in light of the site's characteristics and geographic setting, trees and grass shall be planted, the environment improved, and site parks or archaeological museums established to enhance the site's tourism and public-education value.
Chapter IV — Protection of the Ancient City Wall and the Area Within It
articles.23:
The ancient city wall and the area within it comprise the area of the Xi'an City Wall, expanded in the Hongwu era of the Ming on the foundation of the imperial city of the Sui and Tang and preserved to the present, and the area enclosed by the wall.
The ancient city-wall area includes the Xi'an City Wall, moat, encircling forest belt, and ring road.
articles.24:
Protection of the area within the ancient city wall shall reflect its historic character and preserve the original road-network layout, distinctive streets and lanes, and their names. Its principal urban functions shall be commerce and tourism, and population density within the ancient city wall shall be gradually reduced.
Construction of premises for State organs, urban residents, and public institutions within the ancient city wall shall be strictly restricted. Enterprises and public institutions whose functions are incompatible with the city's role shall adjust their operations or relocate within a specified period.
articles.25:
The Municipal People's Government shall strengthen protection and administration of the ancient city wall, moat, and encircling forest belt; repair the wall; control pollution; improve water quality in the moat; develop the encircling forest belt; and create an encircling park with the distinctive character of the old city.
Discharging wastewater into the moat, dumping garbage, or scattering waste is prohibited.
articles.26:
Building heights and styles on both sides of the ancient city wall shall be strictly controlled. Construction projects inside and outside the wall shall comply with the following requirements:
(1) Buildings and structures within 20 meters on the inner side of the wall shall be demolished and the area along the wall restored as a horse path or developed as green space. Within 100 meters, building height shall not exceed 9 meters and buildings shall use a traditional style. Beyond 100 meters, height shall transition in tiers; buildings in the transition area shall have blue-gray pitched roofs.
(2) Within a 100-meter radius centered on the inner edge of each eastern, western, southern, and northern gate tower, the area shall be used for squares, green spaces, and roads. Nearby buildings and structures shall be compatible with the architectural style and colors of the gate tower.
(3) Within a 200-meter radius centered on the outer edge of each gate tower, the area shall be used for squares, green spaces, and roads. Beyond 200 meters, building height shall transition by distance bands of 60 meters, rising from below 24 meters to below 36 meters and then below 50 meters.
(4) Between the outside of the ancient city wall and the green belt along the ring road, only garden-style public service facilities no higher than 6 meters may be constructed in accordance with the plan.
(5) The area between the moat and ring road shall be developed as green space. Existing buildings and structures shall be demolished or renovated in accordance with the plan.
(6) Outside the red line on the outer side of the ring road, building height shall transition by distance bands of 60 meters, rising from below 24 meters to below 36 meters and then below 50 meters.
articles.27:
Construction projects within the area enclosed by the ancient city wall shall comply with planning requirements for the relevant protected area. The bulk, form, and color of new, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures shall reflect traditional architectural styles and features.
Building heights shall be controlled by subarea, and the overall controlled height shall not exceed 36 meters. The overall floor-area ratio shall be below 2.5. No additional buildings may be inserted into institutional or residential courtyards.
When traditional buildings and structures, traditional residences, and shops are repaired, reconstructed, or rebuilt, they shall be restored in their original style and appearance.
articles.28:
Beiyuanmen, Sanxue Street, Zhuba Market, Defu Lane, and Xiangzimiao are historic districts within the area enclosed by the ancient city wall.
The Beiyuanmen Historic District is bounded by Shehui Road in the east, Zaozi Lane in the west, Hongfu Street in the north, and West Street in the south. The Sanxue Street Historic District is bounded by Kaitong Lane in the east, South Street in the west, the city wall in the south, and Dongmutoushi in the north. Buildings in these districts shall preserve traditional courtyard layouts and architectural styles.
Street-facing buildings in the Zhuba Market, Defu Lane, and Xiangzimiao historic districts shall preserve or restore traditional architectural styles.
articles.29: Protected cultural relic sites within the area enclosed by the ancient city wall, including the Bell Tower, Drum Tower, Stele Forest, Baoqing Temple Pagoda, City God Temple, Huajue Lane Mosque, the Eighth Route Army Office in Xi'an, and the site of the Xi'an Incident, shall be protected in accordance with laws on cultural relics protection. Building heights and styles in surrounding areas shall be compatible with the protected assets.
articles.30: View corridors for cultural relics and historic sites shall be delineated between the Bell Tower and the eastern, western, southern, and northern gate towers. The corridor between the Bell Tower and the eastern gate tower shall be 50 meters wide; buildings within it shall not exceed 9 meters in height, and buildings within 20 meters outside the corridor shall not exceed 12 meters. The corridor between the Bell Tower and the western gate tower shall be 100 meters wide; buildings within it shall not exceed 9 meters. The corridor between the Bell Tower and the southern gate tower shall be 60 meters wide. The corridor between the Bell Tower and the northern gate tower shall be 50 meters wide.
articles.31: Outdoor advertisements within the area enclosed by the ancient city wall shall comply with the outdoor-advertising plan. No outdoor advertising signs may be installed on buildings inside or around the outer perimeter of the Bell Tower traffic circle or the traffic circles at the eastern, western, southern, and northern gate towers.
articles.32:
The Municipal People's Government shall strengthen protection and administration of gardens, green spaces, ancient and notable trees, and squares within the area enclosed by the ancient city wall; plan construction and expansion of urban pocket gardens, street-side green spaces, and leisure squares; increase street trees; and expand vegetation.
Chapter V — Protection of Historic-Character Areas
articles.33: A historic-character area is an area, other than an ancient-site area or the area of the ancient city wall and within it, that is based on cultural relics and historic sites and reflects cultural relic landscapes, environmental character, and features of the historical period in which they are located. Such protected areas mainly include the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor, Baling, the Big and Small Wild Goose Pagodas, Huaqing Pool, Louguantai, Daxingshan Temple, Xingjiao Temple, Qinglong Temple, Caotang Temple, Baxian Nunnery, and Shuilu Nunnery.
articles.34: Historic-character areas shall preserve the natural environment, overall layout, and spatial form of the places where cultural relics and historic sites are located and protect buildings, structures, roads, rivers, trees, green spaces, and other features reflecting historic character.
articles.35:
Renovation and construction in historic-character areas shall primarily create green spaces and squares. Where a conservation plan requires a limited number of cultural tourism facilities or management premises, the bulk, form, style, and color of those buildings shall be compatible with the cultural relics and historic sites.
Chapter VI — Legal Liability
articles.36:
Where any of the following acts occurs within protected areas of the historic and cultural city, the approval document shall be invalid. The persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be disciplined in accordance with the law. Any loss caused to a party shall be compensated for in accordance with the law:
(1) unlawfully approving a construction project without authority to do so;
(2) approving a construction project beyond the scope of approval authority; or
(3) issuing a construction project planning permit in violation of the approval procedure prescribed by these Regulations.
articles.37: Where construction within protected areas of the historic and cultural city fails to comply with a construction project planning permit in violation of these Regulations, the urban management and comprehensive law enforcement department shall order construction to stop. If the impact on implementation of the plan can be eliminated through corrective measures, the department shall order correction within a specified period and impose a fine of not less than 5% but not more than 10% of the construction-project cost. If the impact cannot be eliminated through corrective measures, the department shall order demolition within a specified period; if demolition is impossible, the physical property or unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated, and a fine of not more than 10% of the construction-project cost may also be imposed.
articles.38: Where a person conducts exploration or construction, or damages cultural relics or protection signs, in violation of laws or regulations on cultural relics protection within protected areas of the historic and cultural city, the cultural relics administrative department shall impose an administrative penalty in accordance with relevant laws and regulations; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.39: Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for other conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.40:
Administrative penalties imposed under these Regulations shall follow the procedures and enforcement measures prescribed by the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China.
Before deciding to impose a fine of RMB 500,000 or more on an organization or RMB 50,000 or more on an individual, the authority shall inform the party of the right to request a hearing.
articles.41:
Where staff members of the natural resources and planning, cultural relics, urban management, or other departments neglect their duties, abuse their authority, engage in malpractice for personal gain, solicit or accept bribes, or delay or refuse to perform statutory duties, causing damage to protected assets of the historic and cultural city, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be disciplined in accordance with the law; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Chapter VII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.42:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 August 2002.

FBMCLI.10.9602547.title: Regulations of Xiamen Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of Xiamen, a historic and cultural city, continue the city's historical and cultural lineage, coordinate protection and inheritance of history and culture with high-quality urban and rural development, and, in light of the Xiamen Special Economic Zone, in accordance with the fundamental principles of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
articles.2: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of systematic planning, strict protection, rational use, and participation by multiple parties.
articles.3:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall coordinate protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas, establish a protection mechanism, incorporate protection into their plans for national economic and social development, and include funding for conservation planning, protection and repair, rewards, subsidies, and related matters in their fiscal budgets.
The people's government of each district shall designate a competent department for protection of the historic and cultural city in that district to handle related protection, supervision, and administration work.
articles.4:
The natural resources and planning department of the Municipality shall be the competent department for protection of the historic and cultural city throughout the Municipality and shall organize, coordinate, guide, supervise, and administer that work.
The culture and tourism department shall protect and supervise immovable cultural relics and intangible cultural heritage.
The housing and urban-rural development department shall supervise and administer construction techniques, quality, fire safety, and safety for construction work related to protection and repair of protected assets and coordinate, guide, and supervise protection of traditional villages.
The urban management administrative law enforcement department shall exercise administrative penalty powers prescribed by laws, regulations, and rules concerning protection and administration of historic districts, towns, and villages; historic areas and buildings; buildings with traditional character; and other protected assets.
Departments of agriculture and rural affairs, emergency management, fire and rescue, and other relevant departments shall assist with protection in accordance with their respective responsibilities.
articles.5: The Municipal People's Government shall establish the Xiamen Historic and Cultural City Protection Expert Committee. The Committee shall participate in designation, adjustment, and removal of protected assets; review of conservation plans; and professional assessment of other related protection matters, and provide advisory opinions for decision-making by the people's governments of the Municipality and its districts and their relevant departments.
articles.6: The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts and their relevant departments shall strengthen public education on protection of the historic and cultural city, promote outstanding traditional culture, and support practical educational activities related to protection.
articles.7:
A public-participation system shall be established for protection of the historic and cultural city, and public opinions shall be heard.
The adoption of cultural relics for protection is encouraged. The public is encouraged to participate through donations, sponsorship, technical services, volunteer service, and other means.
Persons responsible for protection and other organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions or notable achievements in protection of the historic and cultural city shall be commended and rewarded by the people's governments of the Municipality and its districts.
Chapter II — Protected Assets
articles.10:
Designation and adjustment of protected assets shall comply with relevant State, provincial, and municipal provisions. Where no such provisions exist, the competent department for a protected asset shall formulate criteria and procedures for its designation and adjustment, which shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval and then published and implemented.
An area that authentically reflects traditional character and local features of a particular historical period but is not a historic district, town, village, or traditional village may be included in a recommended list of historic areas by the natural resources and planning department of the Municipality together with relevant departments. After review and approval by the Xiamen Historic and Cultural City Protection Expert Committee and the Municipal People's Government, it shall be designated and published as a historic area.
articles.11:
Relevant departments of natural resources and planning, culture and tourism, housing and urban-rural development, and other matters of the Municipality and the people's governments of its districts shall conduct surveys of protected assets as appropriate.
Before urban renewal, project construction, or expropriation of land or buildings, a district people's government shall organize a survey and review of buildings more than 50 years old in the area to be renewed or developed.
Any organization or individual may recommend an asset with protection value to the competent department for protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.12:
A protection-list system shall be established for Xiamen, a historic and cultural city, and protected assets shall be administered by category.
Assets confirmed as protected in accordance with statutory procedures shall be included directly in the protection list for the historic and cultural city of Xiamen. The natural resources and planning department of the Municipality shall compile and publish the list.
articles.13:
In protecting the historic and cultural city, the natural resources and planning department of the Municipality shall, together with other competent departments for protected assets, actively use new technologies and methods, establish a database of protected assets, promote information sharing and digital development, and support protection, repair, administration, rational use, and public searches.
Chapter III — Conservation Plans
articles.14:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of a conservation plan for Xiamen, a historic and cultural city, and submit it to the provincial people's government for approval.
The natural resources and planning department of the Municipality shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic areas, protection guidelines for historic buildings ("protection guidelines"), and protection plans for buildings with traditional character ("protection plans"). They shall be implemented after review and approval by the Xiamen Historic and Cultural City Protection Expert Committee.
The conservation plan, protection guidelines, protection plans, and other conservation plans prepared in accordance with laws and regulations shall serve as the basis for protection and administration.
During preparation of a conservation plan, the draft shall be published for at least 30 days, and opinions from experts and the public shall be sought through review meetings, hearings, or other means.
articles.15: In preparing or amending territorial spatial plans and relevant special plans, the requirements of conservation plans, protection guidelines, and protection plans shall be fully taken into account.
articles.16: The conservation plan for Xiamen, a historic and cultural city, shall delineate the historic urban area, specify protected assets and requirements, and strengthen protection of its spatial layout and overall character.
articles.17: A conservation plan for a historic area shall include protection principles, protected assets, protected areas, protection measures, core protected elements, protection of distinctive character, construction controls, fire-safety requirements, and related matters.
articles.18:
Protection guidelines shall include protection principles, protected assets, protected areas, protection value, core protected elements, protection requirements, rational-use requirements, fire-safety requirements, and related matters.
A protection plan shall include protected areas, protection requirements, rational-use requirements, fire-safety requirements, and related matters.
articles.19:
A conservation plan approved in accordance with the law shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, the authority that prepared the plan shall submit a special report to the original approval authority and may prepare an amendment only after consent is obtained. The amended conservation plan shall be submitted for approval in accordance with the original approval procedure.
A conservation plan for a historic area, protection guidelines, or a protection plan shall not be amended without authorization. Any necessary amendment shall be reviewed and approved by the Xiamen Historic and Cultural City Protection Expert Committee.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.21:
Protected areas of historic districts, towns, and villages and traditional villages shall include core protected areas and construction control areas.
No new construction or extension may be undertaken in a core protected area, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. Approval for necessary infrastructure or public service facilities shall be sought in accordance with relevant provisions.
New, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures within core protected areas or construction control areas shall comply with construction controls established by the conservation plan. Their height, bulk, color, and other features shall be compatible with traditional layouts and historic character in the core protected area and shall not destructively affect the overall spatial form or landscape setting.
articles.22:
Before area-wide repair or renovation of a historic district, town, or village; traditional village; or historic area, the implementing entity shall prepare an implementation plan in accordance with the conservation plan.
In preparing the implementation plan, opinions shall be sought from the natural resources and planning, culture and tourism, housing and urban-rural development, and other relevant departments of the Municipality and from the public. An implementation plan for a historic district or for a historic town, village, or historic area in an important urban area shall be implemented after consent by the Municipal People's Government. Other plans shall be implemented after consent by the people's government of the relevant district and filed with the natural resources and planning department of the Municipality.
articles.23:
The owner of a historic building or building with traditional character shall be the person responsible for its protection. If the owner entrusts another person with management or designates a management entity, the owner and the entrusted person or designated entity shall jointly be responsible. If the owner is unknown, the user shall be responsible. If the owner is unknown and there is no user, the people's government of the district shall designate a responsible person.
The people's government of the district shall notify the responsible person in writing of the protection duties; regularly verify ownership, custody, and use of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character; and promptly update the responsible person if those circumstances change.
articles.24: The person responsible for protection of a historic building or a building with traditional character shall carry out maintenance, repairs, and use in accordance with the applicable protection guidelines or protection plan, ensure structural safety and the proper functioning of fire-prevention, disaster-prevention, and other facilities and equipment, promptly address hazards when discovered, and report them to the township people's government or subdistrict office where the building is located or to a relevant administrative department.
articles.25:
Unauthorized demolition of a historic building or a building with traditional character is prohibited.
No new construction or extension of buildings or structures may be undertaken within the protected area of a historic building without authorization. To meet modern production and living needs, internal reconstruction or extension and the addition of facilities may be carried out, provided the historic character is not damaged and the work complies with protection guidelines; approval shall be sought in accordance with relevant provisions.
Within the protected area of a building with traditional character, exterior repairs, interior decoration, and addition of facilities may be carried out, provided its appearance and beam-frame structure are not changed, safety is ensured, and the work complies with the protection plan; approval shall be sought in accordance with relevant provisions.
articles.26:
A responsible person applying to repair a historic building or a building with traditional character shall prepare a repair plan in accordance with the applicable protection guidelines or protection plan and submit it to the competent department for protection of the historic and cultural city in the relevant district. Where structural renewal is involved, the applicant shall apply for a construction project planning permit (or rural construction planning permit) and a construction work permit in accordance with the law.
The housing and urban-rural development department shall specify technical administration requirements for repairs and strengthen supervision of construction safety.
articles.27:
The people's government of each district shall supervise and administer safety of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character, mark their safety status, dynamically update related information, and share information with the natural resources and planning, culture and tourism, housing and urban-rural development, and other departments of the Municipality.
If a building or structure described in the preceding paragraph is found to be at risk of damage, the district people's government shall promptly notify the responsible person to perform repair duties in accordance with relevant provisions.
articles.28: Historic buildings and buildings with traditional character shall be protected in situ. If a construction project in the public interest makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation necessary, the project owner shall provide materials including a report demonstrating the necessity and feasibility of relocation and a relocation plan, seek opinions from the responsible person and interested parties, obtain review and approval from the Xiamen Historic and Cultural City Protection Expert Committee, publish the relocation plan, and submit the matter for approval in accordance with relevant provisions.
articles.29: Where a person demolishes, relocates, or damages a historic building or a building with traditional character without authorization, or fails to maintain, repair, or use it as required, the competent department for protection of the historic and cultural city in the relevant district shall order correction and urge the responsible person, within a specified period, to restore the original condition or take protection or remedial measures.
articles.30:
Conservation plans for historic towns, villages, and traditional villages shall allocate homestead sites in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. If protection requirements make it impossible to allocate homestead sites within a protected area, the conservation plan shall propose a resettlement plan.
If protection of the historic and cultural city affects original residents' production or daily life or impairs their lawful rights and interests, the people's government of the district shall provide arrangements in accordance with the law, including housing support, exchange of homestead sites, or financial compensation.
articles.31: Firefighting facilities and access routes within core protected areas of historic districts, towns, villages, and traditional villages and within protected areas of historic areas, historic buildings, and buildings with traditional character shall be provided in accordance with applicable fire-safety technical standards and specifications, and a person responsible for fire safety shall be designated. If objective conditions make compliance impossible, the housing and urban-rural development department shall, together with the fire and rescue agency and other relevant departments, formulate a fire-safety assurance plan compatible with protection requirements through expert review and other means. The plan shall be an important basis for related protection, repair, and use activities.
articles.32:
Relevant departments of natural resources and planning, culture and tourism, housing and urban-rural development, and other matters of the Municipality shall provide responsible persons with information and technical guidance on protection, repair, and use.
Where a responsible person repairs a non-state-owned historic building or building with traditional character in accordance with technical specifications, quality standards, and a repair plan, the responsible person may apply for a subsidy to the competent department for protection of the historic and cultural city in the relevant district. The natural resources and planning department of the Municipality shall, together with the finance, housing and urban-rural development, and other relevant departments, formulate specific subsidy measures.
articles.33:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize an annual assessment of the state of protection and use of Xiamen, a historic and cultural city, and conduct a comprehensive assessment every five years of implementation and effectiveness of its conservation plan.
Chapter V — Rational Use
articles.34: The people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall connect protected assets of the historic and cultural city by level and category and develop historical and cultural presentation routes and paths integrated with production and daily life, to present Xiamen's history and culture systematically and comprehensively.
articles.35:
Relevant departments of the people's governments of the Municipality and its districts shall, within their respective responsibilities, explore, study, and interpret the value of Minnan culture, marine culture, overseas Chinese culture, the Jiageng spirit, the Special Economic Zone spirit, and other cultural resources; guide public access to and sharing of historical and cultural heritage; and promote outstanding history and culture.
Cultural exchanges across the Taiwan Strait based at immovable cultural relics, historic buildings, buildings with traditional character, and other sites related to Taiwan are encouraged.
Primary and secondary schools are encouraged to conduct activities concerning protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.36: In light of the needs for protection and inheritance and the requirements of conservation plans, protection guidelines, and protection plans, the natural resources and planning department of the Municipality shall, together with the culture and tourism, housing and urban-rural development, and other relevant departments, formulate guidelines for rational use of protected assets of the historic and cultural city, specifying encouraged, supported, restricted, and prohibited activities.
articles.37:
Residents of historic districts, towns, and villages; traditional villages; and historic areas are supported in continuing to live at the original site in accordance with conservation-plan requirements, improving production and living conditions, developing diverse distinctive industries, and conducting, to an appropriate extent, business activities compatible with traditional culture, including tourism, cultural industries, and traditional handicrafts, so as to carry forward the original way of life.
Social operators are encouraged to establish a resource platform for protection of the historic and cultural city, coordinate investment promotion and operations in accordance with the law, and, through transfer or exchange of property rights, entrusted management, termination of leases, and other means, renovate buildings, structures, or underused land within protected areas of historic districts, towns, and villages; traditional villages; and historic areas in accordance with conservation plans as supporting public service facilities, innovation and entrepreneurship spaces, green spaces, squares, parks, and other public open spaces.
Township people's governments or subdistrict offices and villagers' or residents' committees where such protected areas are located may establish enterprises or organizations in accordance with the law to manage and operate production and business activities in those areas and receive lawful proceeds.
articles.38:
Through policy guidance, financial support, simplified procedures, reductions in rent for state-owned historic buildings, longer lease terms for state-owned historic buildings, and other means, the natural resources and planning department of the Municipality together with the housing and urban-rural development and other relevant departments shall promote rational use of historic buildings and buildings with traditional character.
In light of their characteristics and the functions of surrounding areas, historic buildings and buildings with traditional character are encouraged to accommodate cultural and service uses such as libraries, museums, memorial halls, art galleries, community cultural venues, and intangible cultural heritage exhibition spaces.
Persons responsible for protection may jointly develop and use historic buildings and buildings with traditional character with relevant organizations and individuals through joint ventures, cooperation, entrusted management, and other means.
articles.39: Traditional techniques and materials are encouraged for construction within protected areas of protected assets of the historic and cultural city. For construction involving traditional styles, traditional components with protection value are encouraged to carry on traditional techniques.
articles.40:
Training traditional craftspeople in protection of the historic and cultural city and promoting the spirit of craftsmanship are supported.
The housing and urban-rural development department shall organize professional training and designation and assessment of inheritors of traditional building repair techniques and craftspeople who repair traditional buildings.
Universities, secondary vocational schools, and social forces are encouraged to offer related courses and train professional and technical personnel.
articles.41:
Diversified funding channels shall be expanded. Financial institutions and local financial organizations are encouraged to innovate financial products and services and participate in protection and use projects for the historic and cultural city.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.42: Where laws or regulations already provide for protection and administration of Gulangyu World Cultural Heritage, Gulangyu historic-character buildings, immovable cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, and other assets, those provisions shall apply.
articles.43:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 March 2026. The Regulations of the Xiamen Special Economic Zone on the Protection of Historic Character, adopted at the 31st Session of the 14th Standing Committee of the Xiamen Municipal People's Congress on 24 December 2015, are repealed simultaneously.

FBMCLI.17.1550906.title: Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Fenghuang, a Historic and Cultural City (2019 Revision)

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of Fenghuang, a nationally designated historic and cultural city, in accordance with relevant State laws and regulations.
articles.2: The protected area of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, comprises the Ancient City of Fenghuang, the Ancient City of Huangsiqiao, the Southern Great Wall (also known as the Xiangxi Frontier Wall), and other areas requiring protection, as designated in the Conservation Plan for Fenghuang, a Historic and Cultural City (the "Conservation Plan").
articles.3: Protection of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, shall follow the principles of scientific planning, unified administration, strict protection, and rational use.
articles.4:
The People's Government of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture (the "Prefecture People's Government") and its relevant departments shall strengthen guidance and supervision of protection, construction, and administration of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city.
The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall take overall responsibility for protection, construction, and administration and strictly implement the conservation plan approved by the State.
The protection and administration agency for Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, shall handle specific protection and administration work. Relevant departments of the People's Government of Fenghuang County shall perform related protection and administration duties within their respective responsibilities.
The Fenghuang County Urban Scenic Area Administrative Law Enforcement Bureau (the "Law Enforcement Bureau") shall exercise relatively centralized administrative penalty powers within protected areas of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city.
articles.5:
The Prefecture People's Government and the People's Government of Fenghuang County shall include protection of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, in their plans for national economic and social development and include funding for its protection, repair, and administration in their respective fiscal budgets. They shall also seek appropriations and social support in accordance with State provisions.
Funding for maintenance of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, shall be raised in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions and used exclusively for its protection.
articles.6:
Every organization and individual conducting activities within a protected area has a duty to protect Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, and shall comply with these Regulations. They have the right to report and complain about conduct violating these Regulations.
The Prefecture People's Government and the People's Government of Fenghuang County shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that achieve outstanding results in protection.
Chapter II — Protection of the Ancient City of Fenghuang
articles.7:
The Ancient City of Fenghuang is divided into a core protected area, an area for coordination of historic character, and a regional control area. Specific boundaries shall be established by the conservation plan.
The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall install visible signs for the core protected area, the area for coordination of historic character, and the regional control area. No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a sign without authorization.
articles.8:
No new construction or extension may be undertaken within the core protected area, except for infrastructure and public service facilities approved in accordance with the law.
Repair or rebuilding of buildings and structures in the core protected area designated for protection shall retain the exterior shell, renovate the interior, preserve the original historic character, and maintain the layout and character of the Ming and Qing periods in architectural style, bulk, and colors. Repairs shall restore the original appearance. Building height shall not exceed two stories. Eaves shall not exceed 3 meters for a one-story building or 5.6 meters for a two-story building. Colors shall be limited to black, white, gray, gray-brown, and natural wood.
Where an owner or manager-user repairs or renovates an ancient building in the core protected area, the work shall follow protection and repair plans and requirements. If repair funding is genuinely insufficient, the person may apply to the protection and administration agency for Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, for an appropriate subsidy.
New, reconstructed, or extended buildings in an area for coordination of historic character shall use timber structures or small blue-brick walls and blue-tile pitched roofs. Height shall not exceed two stories, and eaves for a two-story building shall not exceed 6 meters. Colors, bulk, and architectural style shall be compatible with the character of the core protected area.
New, reconstructed, or extended buildings in a regional control area shall be compatible with the character of the Ancient City of Fenghuang, shall not exceed three stories, and shall have eaves no higher than 8.5 meters.
articles.9:
Historic streets and lanes within the core protected area shall retain their original view corridors and spatial scale and shall not be widened or narrowed. Facades along commercial streets shall retain their historic style.
Occupying roads, ancient wells, open spaces along streets or rivers, green spaces, or other public activity areas is prohibited. New doors or windows shall not be opened on street-facing buildings. Modern facilities and materials such as security doors, rolling shutters, aluminum-alloy doors and windows, and cement panels are prohibited.
articles.10: Where buildings, structures, roads, water systems, or other facilities within the Ancient City of Fenghuang require maintenance, repair, renovation, reconstruction, or new construction, an implementation plan shall be proposed by the relevant department according to the protection requirements and level established in the conservation plan. After review by the protection and administration agency for Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, the plan shall be submitted for approval in accordance with State provisions and carried out by a construction entity with the relevant professional qualifications.
articles.11: The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall control excessive commercial development of the Ancient City of Fenghuang, guide and supervise business activities, periodically publish catalogues of encouraged or restricted business activities, prioritize pollution-free industries featuring local ethnic culture, and rationally arrange markets for goods within the ancient city. The protection and administration agency for Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, shall implement these measures.
articles.12:
The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall strengthen ecological and environmental protection of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, improve protection mechanisms, closely monitor environmental capacity and ecological risks in key areas and watersheds, and formulate specific prevention and control measures for water, light, air, noise, solid waste, soil, and other forms of pollution.
Organizations and individuals in the Ancient City of Fenghuang shall actively protect the environment, conserve energy, reduce emissions, and promote low-carbon clean energy.
articles.13:
The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall establish a waste-sorting system for waste disposal, collection, transport, and treatment.
Public toilets shall be reasonably provided on urban roads and in public places. The entity managing a public toilet shall install visible signs and conduct routine cleaning and maintenance.
articles.14: A dedicated fire brigade shall be established within protected areas of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, and equipped with firefighting equipment in accordance with relevant provisions to handle fire protection in the Ancient City of Fenghuang.
articles.15:
The Ancient City of Fenghuang shall improve public fire-safety facilities, including firefighting water supply, fire-engine access routes, and fire communications, in accordance with current State fire-safety technical standards. If the standards and specifications cannot be followed, the fire protection agency of the public security organ of the People's Government of Fenghuang County shall formulate a corresponding fire-safety assurance plan together with the competent urban and rural planning department.
Organizations and individuals at public activity venues and residences shall ensure fire safety. Setting off fireworks and firecrackers is prohibited.
articles.16: Within the Ancient City of Fenghuang, setting up street stalls, placing miscellaneous items in disorder, writing or drawing on surfaces, posting materials, littering, or using sound equipment to solicit business is prohibited. Advertisements and signs incompatible with the historic character of the ancient city are prohibited. Storing or selling flammable, explosive, toxic, or harmful substances is prohibited.
articles.17:
Within the core protected area, passage of all motor vehicles is prohibited except fire engines and ambulances. Non-motor vehicles shall not be parked indiscriminately.
Vehicles in an area for coordination of historic character or a regional control area shall follow designated routes and park in designated places.
articles.19: The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall improve the urban sewer network, collect urban wastewater, build centralized treatment facilities, and ensure their normal operation.
articles.20:
Mountains surrounding the Ancient City of Fenghuang shall be protected. Afforestation and mountain closure for forest regeneration shall be carried out, and forest fire prevention and pest and disease control shall be strengthened.
Within the protected areas of surrounding mountains delineated by the conservation plan, including Nanhua Mountain, Bajiaolou, Xique Slope, Qifeng Temple, and Beiyuan, tomb construction, quarrying, soil removal, logging, and other activities damaging vegetation or landscapes are prohibited. No building or structure may be constructed without approval.
Chapter III — Protection of the Ancient City of Huangsiqiao and the Southern Great Wall
articles.21:
The protected area of the Ancient City of Huangsiqiao is divided into a core protected area, an area for coordination of historic character, and a construction control area. The conservation plan shall establish the specific boundaries.
The protected area of the Southern Great Wall comprises the wall and associated gates, blockhouses, watchtowers, garrisons, and other assets along the wall in Fenghuang County, including Jingbian Pass and Tingzi Pass.
The relevant provisions of Chapter II of these Regulations on protection of the Ancient City of Fenghuang shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to protection of the Ancient City of Huangsiqiao.
articles.22: The township people's government where the Ancient City of Huangsiqiao is located and the township people's governments along the Southern Great Wall shall strengthen protection and administration of those assets and establish a system assigning protection responsibilities.
articles.23: Firing guns or artillery, quarrying, and other activities damaging the wall are strictly prohibited within protected areas of the Ancient City of Huangsiqiao or the Southern Great Wall.
articles.24:
All construction within protected areas of the Ancient City of Huangsiqiao or the Southern Great Wall shall be reviewed and approved by the planning, construction, cultural relics, environmental protection, fire safety, tourism, and other relevant departments.
Chapter IV — Planning and Administration
articles.25:
The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall organize preparation of a special conservation plan for Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city (the "Special Plan"), which shall be published and implemented after approval by the provincial people's government.
Based on the Special Plan, the competent county planning department shall, together with the construction, culture, cultural relics, and other administrative departments, prepare detailed control plans and detailed construction plans for historic districts, historic towns, and historic villages, and publish and implement them after approval by the County People's Government.
articles.26: The Special Plan shall prioritize protection of the historic character, layout, and setting of the historic and cultural city and create conditions for rational use. It shall specify overall protection objectives, principles, and content and delineate protected areas and construction control areas for the historic urban area, historic and cultural protected areas, mountain-and-water protected areas, historic towns and villages, protected cultural relic sites, other immovable cultural relics, and historic buildings.
articles.27:
No organization or individual may amend, change, or refuse to implement an approved Special Plan or its detailed control and detailed construction plans without authorization. An adjustment or amendment to a published plan shall be submitted for approval in accordance with the original approval procedure.
In preparing or revising the Special Plan or its detailed control and detailed construction plans, opinions from all sectors of society shall be widely solicited and expert review shall be organized.
articles.28:
The planning, construction, culture, cultural relics, and other administrative departments shall strictly implement the Special Plan and strengthen review and supervision of construction projects related to protection of the historic and cultural city and investigation of illegal construction.
Buildings and facilities that do not comply with the Special Plan or its detailed control or detailed construction plans shall be gradually renovated or demolished in accordance with the plans.
articles.29:
Canopies, awnings, solar panels, air-conditioning units, air-source units, sunrooms, above-ground utility lines, meters, and other facilities installed within protected areas of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, shall be compatible with its historic character and approved by the protection and administration agency.
Where disorderly construction, wiring, hanging, or drying of items affects historic character and the person refuses to correct it, the Law Enforcement Bureau shall handle the matter in accordance with the law.
articles.30:
The People's Government of Fenghuang County shall make rational use of the natural and cultural resources of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, scientifically plan tourist areas, attractions, and routes, and improve public services and tourism infrastructure.
The County People's Government shall strengthen traffic administration and take effective measures to closely monitor traffic volume and the carrying capacity of scenic areas. In light of protection needs, it shall establish green transport and shuttle services, strictly control entry of social vehicles into protected areas, and ensure traffic safety, smooth flow, and environmental protection. The County People's Government shall formulate and publish specific measures.
articles.31:
Persons who beg or are homeless and show violent or dangerous tendencies within protected areas of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, shall be handled by relevant departments in accordance with the law.
Poultry, livestock, and pets kept loose within protected areas shall be handled by the Law Enforcement Bureau in accordance with the law.
articles.33:
For protected cultural relic sites at all levels within protected areas of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, protected areas and construction control areas shall be delineated, special conservation plans and protection schemes prepared, and protection projects implemented in a planned manner in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics. Historic buildings, other key traditional residences, stilt-house complexes, and ancient and notable trees shall be documented and marked for protection.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.34: Where a person violates Article 8 of these Regulations, the Law Enforcement Bureau shall order construction to stop, correction or demolition within a specified period. If construction is not stopped or demolition is not completed within that period, compulsory demolition shall be applied for in accordance with the law, and a fine of not less than 5% but not more than 10% of the construction-project cost shall be imposed.
articles.35: Where a person violates the second paragraph of Article 9, the Law Enforcement Bureau shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than RMB 500 but not more than RMB 1,000 may also be imposed.
articles.36: Where a person violates Articles 15 or 16 by writing or drawing on surfaces, posting materials, littering, setting up street stalls, or placing miscellaneous items in disorder in the old urban area of Fenghuang, the Law Enforcement Bureau shall order correction and may impose a fine of not less than RMB 5 but not more than RMB 50. For using sound equipment to solicit business or installing advertisements or signs incompatible with the historic character of the ancient city, the Bureau shall order correction and may impose a fine of not less than RMB 50 but not more than RMB 500. For setting off fireworks or firecrackers, the Bureau shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 40 but not more than RMB 1,000. For storing or selling flammable, explosive, toxic, or harmful substances, the public security department of the People's Government of Fenghuang County shall order correction and may impose a fine of not less than RMB 100 but not more than RMB 1,000.
articles.37: Where a person violates Article 17, the Law Enforcement Bureau shall order correction and may impose a fine of not less than RMB 50 but not more than RMB 200.
articles.38: Where a person violates the third paragraph of Article 18, the Law Enforcement Bureau shall, together with the relevant administrative departments, order correction. If the person refuses to comply, an administrative penalty shall be imposed in accordance with the law.
articles.39: Where a person violates the second paragraph of Article 20 or Article 23, the Law Enforcement Bureau shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures, confiscate any unlawful proceeds, and impose a fine of not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.40:
Where an entity with protection and administration duties or its staff member fails to perform duties in accordance with the law, neglects duties, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, the person shall be disciplined in accordance with the law; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.41: Protection of ethnic and folk culture of Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city, shall comply with the Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Ethnic and Folk Cultural Heritage.
articles.42: 17 December of each year shall be the Protection Publicity Day for Fenghuang, a historic and cultural city.
articles.43:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2012. The Regulations of Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Fenghuang, a Historic and Cultural City, which took effect on 1 July 2004, are repealed simultaneously.
