FBMCLI.10.4621790.title: Regulations of Quanzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of the historic and cultural city, carry on and promote outstanding traditional culture, improve the living environment, coordinate protection and use of history and culture with urban and rural development, and, in light of local circumstances, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the State Council's Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and the Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and Traditional Villages.
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to planning, protection, administration, and use of Quanzhou, a historic and cultural city.
Protected assets include historic urban areas; historic districts, towns, and villages; traditional villages; World Cultural Heritage; immovable cultural relics; historic buildings; buildings with traditional character; and intangible cultural heritage. The historic urban areas are the Ancient City of Quanzhou and the Ancient City of Fengzhou.
Where laws or regulations provide otherwise for protection of historic towns, villages, and traditional villages; World Cultural Heritage; immovable cultural relics; buildings with traditional character; intangible cultural heritage; or other assets within the historic and cultural city, those provisions shall apply.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, living inheritance, rational use, and joint governance and sharing; preserve the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage and continuity of community life; preserve and carry forward the traditional layout and historic character; and promote integration of outstanding history and culture with modern life.
articles.4:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city, include protection in their plans for national economic and social development, strengthen protection of the World Cultural Heritage "Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song-Yuan China" and implement the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, establish working mechanisms and protection policies, improve the protection system, and strengthen supervision and inspection.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall conduct inspections. When they discover conduct violating protection requirements, they shall promptly stop it and report it to the competent department.
Villagers' and residents' committees may adopt village or community rules, establish community-based protection organizations, conduct community-building activities, and assist with protection work.
articles.5:
The housing and urban-rural development department, together with the culture and tourism department, shall handle specific protection and administration work for the historic and cultural city.
The natural resources and planning department shall administer construction planning for protection of the historic and cultural city.
The culture and tourism department shall supervise and administer protection of World Cultural Heritage, immovable cultural relics, and intangible cultural heritage.
Departments of development and reform, finance, urban management, ecology and environment, civil affairs, education, ethnic and religious affairs, emergency management, and other matters, and fire and rescue agencies shall cooperate in protection and administration within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish funding safeguards for protection of the historic and cultural city, raise protection funding through multiple channels, and use it for surveys and designation of protected assets; maintenance, repair, emergency protection, and use; infrastructure; improvement of the living environment; and related work.
articles.7:
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection of the historic and cultural city through donations, contributions, volunteer service, and other means.
Every organization and individual has a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and the right to discourage, report, or complain about conduct violating these Regulations.
articles.8:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts and their relevant departments shall strengthen public education, disseminate protection knowledge, and enhance awareness throughout society of protection of the historic and cultural city.
Schools are encouraged and supported in conducting practical educational activities related to protection.
Chapter II — Conservation Plans and Protection List
articles.9:
The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of conservation plans for the historic and cultural city and historic districts within its administrative area. People's governments at the county level shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic districts outside the urban districts of the Municipality.
In preparing conservation plans for the historic and cultural city and historic districts, special requirements in conservation plans for World Cultural Heritage shall be fully taken into account.
A conservation plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic district, once approved in accordance with the law, shall be the basis for its protection and administration and shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, approval shall be obtained from the original approval authority.
articles.10:
The natural resources and planning and housing and urban-rural development departments shall, within their respective authority, delineate:
(1) protected areas of historic urban areas;
(2) core protected areas and construction control areas of historic districts; and
(3) protected areas of historic buildings.
articles.11:
Where a conservation plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic district includes spatial control requirements, they shall be incorporated into the territorial spatial plan at the same level and administered uniformly through the territorial spatial basic information platform.
Special plans concerning urban transport, municipal infrastructure, green spaces, tourism, fire safety, civil defense, and related matters shall be coordinated with conservation plans.
articles.12: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall strengthen supervision and inspection of implementation of conservation plans and establish an assessment mechanism for protection of the historic and cultural city. Protection shall be assessed every five years, and the results shall be reported to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level.
articles.13:
The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection-list system for historic urban areas, historic districts, and historic buildings and administer them by level and category. Historic urban areas and approved historic districts and historic buildings shall be included in the protection list.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall regularly conduct surveys. Where a district, building, or structure not yet designated as a historic district or historic building is preliminarily determined by the housing and urban-rural development department together with the culture and tourism department to have protection value, interim protection may be provided by reference to these Regulations and the application and designation procedure initiated in accordance with the law.
Any organization or individual may recommend to the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located that a historic district or historic building be designated.
The housing and urban-rural development departments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish protection archives for historic districts and historic buildings included in the protection list.
articles.14:
Where a change in protection level or type, or another circumstance, requires adjustment of the protection list, the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality shall, together with the culture and tourism and other relevant departments, propose an adjustment and submit it to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
Chapter III — Protection Measures
articles.15:
The people's governments of counties, county-level cities, and districts shall install protection signs at the principal entrances and exits of historic urban areas and core protected areas of historic districts and at prominent exterior locations of historic buildings. The Municipal People's Government shall prescribe a uniform design for the signs, which shall be compatible with the surrounding traditional character.
No organization or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection sign without authorization.
articles.16:
A system of persons responsible for protection shall be implemented for historic urban areas, historic districts, and historic buildings.
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall respectively be responsible for the historic urban areas and historic districts within their authority.
articles.19: In accordance with the conservation plan for the historic and cultural city, the people's governments of Quanzhou Municipality, Licheng District, and Nan'an Municipality shall protect the spatial layout and natural landform of historic urban areas; control the height, bulk, color, and facade style of buildings and structures; and gradually renovate buildings and structures incompatible with traditional character.
articles.20:
No new construction or extension may be undertaken in a core protected area of a historic district, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
New buildings and structures in a construction control area shall comply with construction controls established by the conservation plan.
articles.21: Firefighting facilities and access routes within core protected areas of historic districts shall be provided in accordance with applicable fire-safety technical standards and specifications, and a person responsible for fire safety shall be designated. If site constraints make compliance impossible, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall organize the emergency management, natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, and other competent departments and fire and rescue agencies to formulate a fire-safety assurance plan.
articles.22:
For a state-owned historic building, its manager shall be responsible for protection; if the manager cannot be identified, its user shall be responsible; if neither can be identified, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall designate a responsible person.
For a non-state-owned historic building, its owner shall be responsible. If the owner is missing or ownership is unclear, its manager or user shall be responsible. If the owner and manager or user have made a different agreement, that agreement shall apply. If the owner, manager, and user cannot be identified or are missing, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall designate a responsible person and make the designation public.
Where an organization or individual objects to the designation of a responsible person for a historic building, the people's government of the county, county-level city, or district shall decide within 30 days after receiving the objection whether to adjust the designation and notify the applicant and responsible person in writing. If the designation is adjusted, it shall be published again.
articles.24:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall organize relevant departments to prepare protection guidelines for historic buildings in accordance with conservation plans. The guidelines shall serve as the basis for maintenance, repair, and use.
The people's government where a historic building is located shall notify the responsible person in writing of the protection requirements and duties. The housing and urban-rural development department shall supervise and guide its maintenance and repair.
articles.25:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts may provide financial subsidies for maintenance and repair of non-state-owned historic buildings.
If a non-state-owned historic building is at risk of damage and its responsible person genuinely lacks the financial capacity to perform emergency protection duties, the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county, county-level city, or district shall take protection measures, including financial subsidies. If the responsible person has the capacity but fails to perform protection duties, the government shall first carry out emergency protection, and the responsible person shall bear the cost.
No organization or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization.
articles.26:
If a qualified assessment entity determines that a historic building is dangerous and cannot be saved through reinforcement or other emergency measures, or that repair is necessary due to partial collapse or damage, the owner or another responsible person shall prepare a repair design plan in accordance with protection requirements and submit it to the natural resources and planning department of the Municipality. After approval in accordance with prescribed procedures, the building shall be repaired in accordance with its original architectural character and spatial layout.
The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation and publication of specific measures for repair, reinforcement, and restoration of historic buildings.
articles.27:
A construction site shall avoid historic buildings. If avoidance is impossible due to special circumstances, the project owner shall protect the building in situ, determine protection measures in advance, and submit them to the natural resources and planning department of the Municipality together with the culture and tourism department for approval.
If a construction project in the public interest makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation necessary, the housing and urban-rural development department of the Municipality shall, together with the culture and tourism department, submit an opinion for consent by the Municipal People's Government and then seek approval from the relevant provincial departments in accordance with prescribed procedures.
The project owner shall include the costs of in-situ protection or relocation of a historic building in the construction-project budget.
articles.28:
Within protected areas of historic urban areas, a dangerous building that is not World Cultural Heritage, an immovable cultural relic, a historic building, or a building with traditional character, and that has an independent parcel and a real-property title certificate or other proof of housing ownership, may apply for renovation in accordance with prescribed procedures after being assessed as dangerous. Such renovation shall comply with the conservation plan and relevant provisions on renovation of dangerous buildings.
The people's governments of Quanzhou Municipality and Nan'an Municipality shall separately formulate and publish specific measures for renovation of dangerous buildings in the Ancient Cities of Quanzhou and Fengzhou.
articles.29: Before lawfully expropriating buildings within protected areas of historic urban areas, historic districts, or historic buildings, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall conduct surveys of historical and cultural heritage and related work.
articles.30: The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish a protection compensation system and provide appropriate compensation through financial subsidies or other policy measures for losses suffered by organizations or individuals because of protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.31: Traditional place names embodying the history and culture of Quanzhou shall be preserved. No organization or individual may change or cancel them without authorization. Where change or cancellation is necessary, opinions shall be sought from the civil affairs department of the Municipality or relevant county, county-level city, or district, and approval shall be obtained in accordance with the law.
articles.32:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish a joint law-enforcement mechanism, strengthen supervision and inspection of protection and use of the historic and cultural city, promptly stop unlawful conduct, and investigate and handle it in accordance with the law.
Chapter IV — Rational Use
articles.33:
Rational use of the historic and cultural city is encouraged and guided. Subject to protection requirements, exhibition and transmission venues such as intangible cultural heritage presentation centers, memorial halls, and museums may be established, and technology may be used to present the historical and cultural significance of the city and enhance its presentation.
The development of cultural tourism, cultural creativity, traditional production techniques, and other industries compatible with traditional culture is supported.
articles.34:
Through financial support, exchange of property rights, repair in lieu of rent, and other support measures, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall promote protection and use of historic buildings.
Use of a historic building shall comply with protection guidelines and requirements for fire safety and other professional administration, be compatible with its historical value and internal structure, and shall not change its principal structure, main floor layout, or exterior appearance without authorization or endanger the building or its ancillary facilities.
articles.35:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall develop and recruit professional personnel in conservation planning, ancient-building restoration, traditional crafts, and related fields; encourage establishment of specialized research institutions; and increase investment in professional training.
Training traditional-building craftspeople, transmitting their techniques, selecting master craftspeople, and related activities are supported, and a roster of traditional-building craftspeople shall be established and improved.
articles.36:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall strengthen living protection of the historic and cultural city, respect the ways of life and traditional customs of original residents, and promote continuity and inheritance of original production and living practices.
Original residents are encouraged to participate in protection and use through buildings, funds, skills, labor, and other contributions, and their active participation shall be encouraged.
articles.37:
As needed, the Municipal People's Government may coordinate resources and establish an operating platform for acquisition of buildings and exchange of property rights, and encourage and guide owners of buildings in historic urban areas to improve living conditions through exchange of property rights and other means.
In accordance with conservation plans, the people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall gradually improve roads, water supply, drainage, sewage, power, fire-safety, and other infrastructure in the historic and cultural city and provide supporting facilities such as nearby parking lots and visitor service centers.
articles.38:
The people's governments of the Municipality and its counties, county-level cities, and districts shall encourage and support organization, study, and use of historical and cultural resources; strengthen research and documentation of traditional festivals, distinctive folk customs, traditional crafts, and related matters; guide establishment of research bases for intangible cultural heritage transmission, cultural and creative industries, local culture, and related fields; rationally arrange spaces for transmission of intangible cultural heritage; and promote its dissemination and development.
The education and culture and tourism departments shall organize schools to conduct campus activities on Minnan culture, focusing on Nanyin music, Nanxi opera, Nanquan martial arts, southern Fujian architecture, and southern Fujian crafts. Primary and secondary schools and kindergartens are encouraged to offer after-school Minnan-language education.
Protection, transmission, and use of time-honored brands, traditional crafts, traditional opera, and other heritage shall be strengthened to establish exemplary traditional cultural brands. Protection of time-honored brands at their original sites and in their original appearance is encouraged.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.39: Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.41: Where a person damages, relocates, or demolishes a historic building without authorization in violation of the third paragraph of Article 25, the urban management department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.42:
Where a state organ or its staff member commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations, the people's government of the Municipality or the relevant county, county-level city, or district, or the relevant competent department, shall order correction and issue a public criticism. The persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be disciplined in accordance with the law; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law:
(1) due to inadequate protection or a decision-making error, causing the historic and cultural city, a historic urban area, historic district, or historic building to be placed on a danger list or lose its designation;
(2) failing to designate a responsible person for protection of a historic building as required by these Regulations; or
(3) other dereliction of duty, abuse of authority, or malpractice for personal gain.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.43:
For the purposes of these Regulations, "historic district" means an area approved and published by the provincial people's government or a State ministry or commission that preserves especially rich cultural relics, has a concentration of historic buildings, substantially and authentically reflects traditional layouts and historic character, and has a certain scale.
"Historic building" means a building or structure within an urban district designated and published by the Municipal People's Government that has a degree of protection value and reflects historic character and local features, but has not been published as a protected cultural relic site or registered as an immovable cultural relic.
articles.44:
These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2022.

FBMCLI.17.5049775.title: Regulations of Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, on the Protection of Dali, a Historic and Cultural City (2022 Revision)

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection of Dali, a historic and cultural city, carry on outstanding historical and cultural heritage, and promote integrated development of historical and cultural protection and inheritance with urban and rural construction, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and the State Council's Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and in light of local circumstances of Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture (the "Autonomous Prefecture").
articles.2:
These Regulations apply to planning, protection, administration, and use of Dali, a historic and cultural city (the "City").
Where protection of the City involves cultural relics, the laws and regulations on cultural relics protection shall apply. Where it involves scenic areas, nature reserves, Cangshan Mountain, Erhai Lake, the western shore of Erhai Lake, intangible cultural heritage, or related matters, the relevant laws and regulations shall also apply.
articles.4: Protection of the City shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, rational use, public participation, and social supervision; preserve and carry forward its traditional layout and historic character; maintain the authenticity and integrity of historical and cultural heritage; and preserve the public's emotional memories of the City.
articles.5:
The People's Government of the Autonomous Prefecture shall strengthen leadership of protection work for the City, establish a joint-meeting system, and study major protection matters.
The People's Government of the City Municipality shall be responsible for protection and administration of the City, include protection in its plans for national economic and social development, include necessary funding in its fiscal budget, and establish a protection and administration committee to coordinate protection work.
Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall handle routine protection and administration within their jurisdictions.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist township people's governments and subdistrict offices with related protection work.
articles.6:
The housing and urban-rural development administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall, together with the culture and tourism administrative department, supervise and administer protection of the City.
The natural resources administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall administer planning matters related to protection.
Relevant departments of development and reform, finance, emergency management, public security, health, urban management, agriculture and rural affairs, ecology and environment, forestry and grassland, Cangshan administration, Erhai administration, transport, water affairs, commerce, market regulation, ethnic and religious affairs, civil affairs, and other matters of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall perform related protection work within their respective responsibilities.
articles.8:
Every organization and individual has a duty to protect the City and the right to offer opinions and suggestions on protection work and to discourage, report, or complain about conduct that damages the City.
The people's governments of the Autonomous Prefecture and the City Municipality shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection of the City in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions.
articles.9:
The people's governments of the Autonomous Prefecture, the City Municipality, and townships shall strengthen public education on protection of the City, disseminate protection knowledge, and enhance public awareness.
Radio, television, newspapers, the internet, and other media shall actively conduct public-interest publicity for protection of the City.
Chapter II — Conservation Plans
articles.10:
The People's Government of the City Municipality shall organize preparation of a conservation plan for the City, which shall be reviewed by the People's Government of the Autonomous Prefecture and submitted to the provincial people's government for approval.
The conservation plan shall comply with the territorial spatial plan of the City Municipality. Special plans concerning protection of the City shall be coordinated with its conservation plan.
articles.11: In accordance with the conservation plan for the City approved in accordance with the law, the People's Government of the City Municipality shall organize preparation of conservation plans for historic districts, towns, and villages. The plans shall be reviewed by the People's Government of the Autonomous Prefecture and submitted to the provincial people's government for approval.
articles.12:
Before submitting a conservation plan for the City or for a historic district, town, or village for approval, the People's Government of the City Municipality shall publish it and seek opinions from relevant departments, experts, and the public for at least 30 days.
Within 15 days after approval, a conservation plan for the City or for a historic district, town, or village shall be made public.
A conservation plan approved in accordance with the law shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, it shall be submitted for approval in accordance with the original approval procedure.
articles.13: In accordance with the conservation plan for the City approved in accordance with the law, the People's Government of the City Municipality shall delineate core protected areas and construction control areas and install signs at principal entrances and exits of core protected areas.
articles.15:
A protection-list system shall be implemented for the City. The housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism administrative departments of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall, together with relevant departments, organize expert review in accordance with applicable designation standards, propose an initial protection list, publish it for at least 30 days, and submit it to the People's Government of the City Municipality for review and approval.
Protected assets approved and published by the people's governments of the State, province, Autonomous Prefecture, or City Municipality shall be included directly in the protection list.
The protection list shall be made public. A protection sign shall be installed at the principal entrance or exit of each asset on the list.
articles.16: The housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism administrative departments of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall, together with relevant departments, establish archives for protected assets included in the protection list.
articles.17:
The People's Government of the City Municipality shall administer the protection list dynamically, update and adjust it promptly, and make changes public.
If an asset on the list is seriously damaged or lost, or its protection level or type changes, the housing and urban-rural development administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall, together with the culture and tourism administrative department, promptly propose an adjustment and submit it to the People's Government of the City Municipality for approval.
articles.18:
The housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism administrative departments of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall regularly survey historical and cultural resources. For a building or structure meeting the criteria for a historic building, they shall recommend designation to the People's Government of the City Municipality for approval. A building or structure with protection value that has not yet been designated as a historic building shall receive interim protection.
Chapter III — Protection Measures
articles.19: Construction within protected areas of the City shall comply with the conservation plan, reflect local architectural characteristics, and, to the extent possible, use traditional techniques and materials. It shall not impair the authenticity or integrity of historical and cultural heritage or destructively affect traditional layouts, street and lane patterns, or traditional character.
articles.20:
No new construction or extension may be undertaken in a core protected area of the City, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
Buildings and structures in a core protected area that do not conform to the conservation plan and affect historic layouts, street and lane patterns, or traditional character shall be gradually renovated or demolished. Where statutory compensation conditions are met, the People's Government of the City Municipality shall provide compensation in accordance with the law.
articles.21: New, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures in a construction control area of the City shall comply with construction controls established by the conservation plan. Their form, height, bulk, color, and other features shall be compatible with the character of the core protected area. Street- and lane-facing walls, doors, and windows shall use traditional building materials.
articles.22: The remains of the walls of the Ancient City of Dali shall be protected and repaired. New construction, reconstruction, or extension of buildings or structures is prohibited within 13.5 meters of the inner side and 20 meters of the outer side of the remains. Existing buildings and structures shall be gradually demolished. Where statutory compensation conditions are met, the People's Government of the City Municipality shall provide compensation in accordance with the law.
articles.23: Within core protected areas of the City and the four-boundary area around the remains of the walls of the Ancient City of Dali, installation of outdoor advertisements; installation or construction of solar panels, water tanks, water towers, exhaust pipes, communications equipment, security facilities, or other equipment; street excavation for construction; and establishment of temporary stalls shall comply with controls on the character of the City and public-safety requirements. Where approval is required by law, the relevant administrative department shall seek opinions from the protection and administration agency for the City or the township people's government or subdistrict office where the historic district, town, or village is located before granting approval.
articles.24: The principal functions of core protected areas of the City and the four-boundary area around the remains of the walls of the Ancient City of Dali shall be residence, culture, tourism, education, health, and commerce. Activities incompatible with those functions shall be gradually relocated.
articles.25: In accordance with the conservation plan for the City, the People's Government of the City Municipality shall improve infrastructure, public service facilities, and the living environment.
articles.26:
The People's Government of the City Municipality shall strengthen emergency-response capacity, formulate emergency response plans, and improve disaster prevention, mitigation, and relief for the City.
Firefighting facilities and access routes within protected areas shall be provided in accordance with applicable fire-safety technical standards and specifications. If protection needs make compliance impossible, the fire and rescue agency shall, together with relevant administrative departments, formulate a fire-safety assurance plan.
Organizations and individuals within protected areas shall implement a fire-safety responsibility system and perform their duties to maintain fire safety, protect firefighting facilities, prevent fires, and report fires.
Setting off fireworks and firecrackers shall be strictly restricted or prohibited within protected areas. The People's Government of the City Municipality shall determine restricted or prohibited times and areas in accordance with the law.
articles.27: The People's Government of the City Municipality shall establish a digital protection system for the City and install intelligent monitoring systems in key protected areas and at key protected assets.
articles.28:
A system of persons responsible for protection of historic buildings shall be implemented. The owner shall be responsible; if the owner is missing or ownership is unclear, the user shall be responsible; if neither the owner nor user can be identified, the housing and urban-rural development administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall be responsible.
The responsible person shall perform the following duties:
(1) ensure the building's safety and the proper functioning of disaster-prevention and fire-prevention facilities and equipment; promptly address identified safety hazards or emergencies and report them to the relevant departments;
(2) use the historic building rationally and maintain and repair it in accordance with a protection plan reviewed by the housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism administrative departments of the People's Government of the City Municipality, preserving original architectural character and distinctive courtyard features; and
(3) before transferring, leasing, or lending the historic building, enter into a written agreement with the transferee, lessee, or user specifying each party's protection responsibilities.
If a historic building is at risk of damage and its responsible person lacks the capacity to protect or repair it, the People's Government of the City Municipality may take protection measures, including financial subsidies.
articles.29:
The following activities within protected areas of the City shall preserve traditional layouts, historic character, and historic buildings, be covered by a protection plan, and be carried out after completing relevant procedures in accordance with laws and regulations:
(1) activities that change the natural state of gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, or similar features;
(2) filming or holding a large public gathering in a core protected area; or
(3) other activities affecting traditional layouts, historic character, or historic buildings.
articles.31:
The People's Government of the City Municipality shall establish a protection-assessment mechanism, regularly supervise and inspect implementation of conservation plans, assess the state of protection, and promptly correct and handle identified problems.
Chapter IV — Protection and Use
articles.32:
Protection and use of the City shall be compatible with its historical, artistic, scientific, social, and cultural values, so that protection and use are coordinated.
Rational use of protected assets, including the ancient city, historic districts, towns and villages, and historic buildings, is encouraged and supported, provided that natural landscapes, cultural landscapes, and historical and cultural resources are not damaged.
articles.33: Protection and use of the City shall safeguard the lawful rights and interests of local residents and villagers and encourage their active participation in protection. Residents and villagers are encouraged to engage in production and business in local distinctive industries and other related activities, carrying forward the City's original form and way of life.
articles.34: Through policy support, financial assistance, and other means, the People's Government of the City Municipality shall enhance the cultural content and quality of attractions such as the Ancient City of Dali and the Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple. Organizations and individuals are supported in conducting business compatible with traditional culture, including processing and making traditional crafts, cultural creativity, and related activities, promoting adaptive reuse and developing new forms integrating culture and tourism.
articles.35: Organizations and individuals are encouraged to establish museums, exhibition halls, memorial halls, intangible cultural heritage transmission centers, and other venues through contributions, donations, or establishment of funds; conduct folk-cultural activities; present traditional local ways of production and life; and explore historical stories, cultural values, and spiritual significance of the City.
articles.36:
Market entities are encouraged and supported in acquiring and making use of old, unused buildings in the City through exchange of property rights, negotiated acquisition, and other lawful means to develop cultural tourism.
Local residents, villagers, and owners or users of buildings are encouraged to participate in protection and use through funds, traditional skills as equity, and exchange, transfer, or lease of buildings, among other means.
articles.37:
Organizations and individuals are encouraged and supported, on the condition that relevant protection requirements are met, in making rational use of historic buildings to present cultural heritage and operate distinctive commerce, leisure experiences, homestays, and other businesses.
Use of a historic building shall be compatible with its historical value and internal structure, shall not change its principal structure, main floor layout, or exterior appearance without authorization, and shall not endanger the building or its ancillary facilities.
articles.38:
The People's Government of the City Municipality and its relevant departments and persons responsible for protection of historic buildings shall support education departments and schools in organizing regular student visits to museums, exhibition halls, art galleries, and other venues and in conducting practical activities to learn and carry on outstanding traditional culture.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.39: Where a state organ or its staff member fails to perform supervision and administration duties, fails to investigate unlawful conduct when discovered, or otherwise neglects duties, abuses authority, or engages in malpractice for personal gain in protecting the City, the person shall be disciplined in accordance with the law if the conduct does not constitute a crime; if it constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.40:
Where a person commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations, the relevant administrative department shall impose a penalty as follows; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law:
(1) Where a person sets off fireworks or firecrackers at a time or place where they are prohibited in violation of the fourth paragraph of Article 26, the public security organ shall order the person to stop and impose a fine of not less than RMB 100 but not more than RMB 500. Where the conduct violates public security administration, a public security administration penalty shall be imposed in accordance with the law.
(2) Where a person violates any of subparagraphs (1) through (3) of Article 30, the natural resources administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 500,000 but not more than RMB 1,000,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
(3) Where a person violates subparagraph (4) of Article 30, the housing and urban-rural development administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
(4) Where a person violates subparagraph (5) of Article 30, the housing and urban-rural development administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality or the Ancient City of Dali Protection and Administration Agency shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000.
(5) Where a person violates subparagraph (6) of Article 30, the housing and urban-rural development administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality or the Ancient City of Dali Protection and Administration Agency shall order restoration of the original condition or other remedial measures and impose a fine of RMB 50.
(6) Where a person violates subparagraph (7) of Article 30, the housing and urban-rural development administrative department of the People's Government of the City Municipality or the Ancient City of Dali Protection and Administration Agency shall order correction within a specified period. If the person fails to comply within that period, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.41:
Where these Regulations do not prescribe a penalty for conduct violating them, the relevant laws and regulations shall apply.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.42:
The Ancient City of Dali is the historic urban area of the City, and its boundaries are the same as those of the Ancient City of Dali Historic District. Xizhou Ancient Town includes the Xizhou Historic District.
The four-boundary area around the remains of the walls of the Ancient City of Dali is centered on the ancient city and extends to Zhonghe Road in the north, Yita Road in the south, Dafeng Road in the west, and Hongwu Road in the east.
"Historic building" means a building or structure designated and published by the People's Government of the City Municipality that has a degree of protection value and reflects historic character and local features, but has not been published as a protected cultural relic site or registered as an immovable cultural relic.
articles.43:
These Regulations were adopted by the People's Congress of the Autonomous Prefecture, submitted to the Standing Committee of the Yunnan Provincial People's Congress for approval, and shall be published and implemented by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the Autonomous Prefecture.
The People's Government of the Autonomous Prefecture shall formulate implementing measures in accordance with these Regulations.
articles.44:
The Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the Autonomous Prefecture shall be responsible for interpreting these Regulations.

FBMCLI.17.7307208.title: Regulations of Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture on the Protection of Zhenyuan, a Historic and Cultural City (2023 Revision)

articles.1: These Regulations are enacted to strengthen protection and administration of Zhenyuan, a historic and cultural city (the "City"), scientifically and rationally use its historical and cultural resources, carry on and develop outstanding traditional culture, and, in light of local circumstances, in accordance with laws and regulations including the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages.
articles.2: These Regulations shall be observed in planning, protection, administration, and use of the City and in production, business, construction, tourism, and other activities within its protected areas.
articles.3:
Protected assets of the City include the traditional layout, overall character, and spatial scale of the historic urban area and related cultural relics, historic buildings, buildings with traditional character, scenic areas, traditional villages, ancient and notable trees, the ecological environment, intangible cultural heritage, and other assets. Protection of cultural relics, scenic areas, traditional villages, ancient and notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, and related matters shall comply with relevant laws and regulations.
For the purposes of the preceding paragraph, "building with traditional character" means a building or structure, other than a protected cultural relic site or historic building, with a certain age that has value and significance in shaping the overall character of the historic urban area.
articles.4: Protection and administration of the City shall follow the principles of scientific planning, strict protection, rational use, and coordinated development. The relationship between high-quality economic and social development and protection, inheritance, and use of history and culture shall be properly managed, preserving the authenticity and integrity of the City's history and culture.
articles.5:
The People's Government of Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture shall guide and supervise protection and administration of the City. The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall be responsible for protection and administration.
The Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee of the People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall coordinate protection and administration, establish and improve coordination and performance-assessment mechanisms, and study major matters. Its routine work shall be handled by the housing and urban-rural development department of the County People's Government.
Relevant departments of the People's Government of Zhenyuan County, township people's governments, and subdistrict offices shall cooperate in protection and administration within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall include protection and administration of the City in its plans for national economic and social development and include necessary funding in its fiscal budget. The People's Government of the Autonomous Prefecture shall provide financial support in light of actual protection needs.
Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection of the City through donations, sponsorship, volunteer service, and other means.
articles.7:
The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall, in accordance with the law, prepare conservation plans for the City and special conservation plans for historic districts, areas with traditional character, historic buildings, and other assets, and implement them after approval.
Approved conservation plans for the City and other special plans shall be strictly implemented and shall not be amended without authorization. Any necessary amendment shall follow the original approval procedure.
articles.8: In accordance with conservation plans for the City and these Regulations and in light of actual protection needs, the People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall establish a list of protected assets and digital archives, install protection signs, specify protection and administration measures and responsible persons, and administer protection by area, level, and category.
articles.9:
8 December of each year shall be the City's Protection Day.
The people's governments of the Autonomous Prefecture and Zhenyuan County shall strengthen public education and enhance public awareness of protection of the City.
Every organization and individual has a duty to protect the City and the right to discourage, report, or complain about unlawful conduct damaging it.
Organizations and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection and administration shall be commended or rewarded in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions.
Chapter II — Protection of the Historic Urban Area
articles.10:
The historic urban area is a key protected asset of the City. It includes the historic landscape corridor along the Wuyang River section within the urban area, the Fucheng Historic District, the Weicheng Historic District, the Tiexi area with traditional character, the Lianhe Street–Zhou Street area with traditional character, the Xinzong Street–Gonghe Street area with traditional character, and other areas. The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall delineate the specific boundaries in accordance with the conservation plan for the City.
Historic districts shall be divided into core protected areas and construction control areas.
articles.12:
Construction within the historic urban area shall control the height, bulk, style, and color of buildings and structures in accordance with conservation plans; preserve the integrity of traditional layouts, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale, and historic features; use traditional or traditional-style materials and continue traditional construction techniques; shall not impair the authenticity or integrity of historical and cultural heritage; and shall not destructively affect view corridors, traditional layouts, street and lane patterns, or historic character.
Fire performance of building components, construction materials, and interior finishing and decoration materials used in new, reconstructed, or extended commercial buildings shall comply with State standards or, where no State standard exists, industry standards. Interior finishing and decoration in crowded places shall use noncombustible or flame-retardant materials in accordance with fire-safety technical standards.
articles.13:
Roofs in the historic urban area shall preserve the character of small blue tiles, pitched roofs, fire walls, and blue-gray or whitewashed walls. Doors and windows shall retain red-brown or natural-wood colors. Provided fire-safety technical standards are met, building facades shall use decorative materials compatible with traditional character.
Outdoor advertisements, shop signs, display signs, light boxes, and other facilities installed within the historic urban area shall comply with conservation plans and be compatible with historic character.
articles.14:
Buildings and structures within the historic urban area that do not comply with conservation plans or are incompatible with traditional layouts and historic character shall be gradually renovated or modified.
No organization or individual may damage the principal exterior character or distinctive components of a building with traditional character. Reconstruction, renovation, or demolition of a building with traditional character for a construction project in the public interest shall comply with the conservation plan.
articles.16:
In addition to the prohibitions in Article 15, the following activities are prohibited within an area with traditional character:
(1) large-scale new construction or extension;
(2) area-wide demolition, relocation, or commercial development of land; or
(3) establishing new industrial enterprises that affect or damage traditional character.
articles.18:
Before issuing a construction project planning permit for necessary infrastructure or public service facilities in a core protected area of a historic district, the department of the People's Government of Zhenyuan County responsible for planning shall seek opinions from the county cultural relics department.
Demolition of a building, structure, or other facility other than a historic building within a core protected area of a historic district shall be approved by the planning department together with the county cultural relics department.
articles.19: The height, bulk, color, texture, and other features of new, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures in a construction control area of a historic district shall be compatible with the historic character of its core protected area.
articles.20:
Demolition, damage, or occupation of the site of an ancient wharf, and construction of an illegal building or structure within its protected area, are prohibited. An illegal building or structure already occupying or constructed on the site shall be demolished within a specified period and the original appearance restored.
Chapter III — Protection of Historic Buildings
articles.21:
Historic buildings shall, in principle, be protected in situ. If a construction project in the public interest makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation or demolition necessary, the department of the People's Government of Zhenyuan County responsible for planning shall, together with the county cultural relics department, submit the matter for approval in accordance with laws and regulations.
Exterior repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or changes to the structure or use of a historic building shall be approved by the planning department together with the county cultural relics department, and relevant procedures shall be completed in accordance with laws and regulations.
articles.22:
The housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism departments of the People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall regularly organize surveys of historic buildings and publish a protection list. For a building or structure meeting the criteria for a historic building, they shall recommend designation to the County People's Government for approval.
An interim protection system shall be implemented for potential historic buildings. During interim protection, the building or structure shall not be damaged or demolished. Interim protection shall last 12 months from the date the department responsible for planning or the county cultural relics department of the People's Government of Zhenyuan County issues an interim-protection notice.
articles.23:
The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall, in accordance with the law, delineate protected areas for historic buildings and, for historic buildings outside a historic district, any necessary construction control area.
No new building or structure may be constructed within a protected area of a historic building. If an ancillary facility is necessary for protection, it shall be approved by the planning department together with the cultural relics department.
New, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures, roads, underground works, and other municipal facilities in a construction control area of a historic building shall be subject to effective protection measures and shall not damage the building's environmental character. New, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures shall be compatible with the historic building in height, bulk, facade, materials, colors, and other respects.
articles.24:
Reconstruction, extension, and addition of facilities to a historic building shall be compatible with its traditional form, colors, materials, and other features.
A historic building within the core protected area of a historic district shall preserve its original height, bulk, exterior appearance, and colors.
articles.25:
The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall be determined in the following order:
(1) If there is an owner, the owner shall be responsible, unless the owner and user have agreed otherwise.
(2) If there is no owner or the owner is unknown, the actual manager or user shall be responsible.
(3) If there is no owner, actual manager, or user, the township people's government or subdistrict office where the building is located shall be responsible.
A written contract shall be entered into when a historic building is leased or lent, specifying its use and protection responsibilities.
articles.27: If a historic building is at risk of damage and its responsible person lacks the capacity to maintain and repair it, the People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall provide necessary financial or technical support or take effective measures to protect it.
articles.29: The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall strengthen ecological and environmental protection in the historic urban area, develop high-quality ecological civilization, and promote effective integration of historical and cultural protection with ecological development.
articles.30:
The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall strengthen development and administration of river networks and shorelines within protected areas, rationally arrange green spaces, cultural landscapes, leisure facilities, and other features in accordance with the law, improve wastewater collection and treatment systems, reinforce and maintain river embankments, remove silt, dredge channels, and keep rivers clean.
Water tourism, water sports, and other activities within protected areas shall comply with river and water-area conservation plans and shall not pollute river water.
articles.31: The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall strengthen prevention and control of solid waste, air, noise, and other pollution within protected areas of the City in accordance with the law.
articles.32: Food-service operators in the historic urban area shall install grease separators or other facilities to treat oily wastewater and collect and dispose of such wastewater in accordance with applicable provisions.
articles.33: In accordance with the conservation plan, the People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall delineate an environmental coordination area around the historic urban area and promptly make its boundaries public.
articles.34: The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall strengthen landscaping and greening, mountain protection, scenic forest protection, and water purification within the environmental coordination area; strengthen afforestation and mountain closure for forest regeneration; and install signs to protect ancient and notable trees and large trees.
articles.36:
Factories, garbage dumps, and construction projects that pollute the environment or damage ecosystems and are already built within the environmental coordination area shall be remediated or relocated within a specified period. If they are not remediated or relocated by that deadline, they shall be demolished in accordance with the law.
Chapter V — Inheritance and Use
articles.37:
The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall coordinate planning and rational use of the City's historical and cultural heritage, optimize its cultural, leisure, and tourism functions, and promote tourism through improvements to the living environment, adjustment of business uses, and construction of related supporting facilities.
Subject to conservation plans, rational use and orderly public access to all categories of protected assets are encouraged and supported, provided natural landscapes, cultural landscapes, and historical and cultural resources are not damaged.
articles.38:
The People's Government of Zhenyuan County shall use relocation, vacancy, incremental renewal, and other means to increase public open space in the historic urban area, make up for deficiencies in supporting infrastructure and public services, and improve the living environment.
Land and buildings vacated by State organs, enterprises, and public institutions due to relocation or industrial adjustment in the historic urban area shall be prioritized for cultural tourism, education, health services, and related infrastructure.
articles.39:
Subject to conservation-plan requirements, the internal functions of buildings with traditional character and historic buildings in the historic urban area may be improved and updated to improve residential and use conditions and meet modern living needs.
Use of buildings with traditional character and historic buildings for lawful business activities compatible with protection of the City is encouraged to present traditional ways of life and folk culture of City residents.
articles.40: Organizations and individuals are encouraged and supported in rationally using intangible cultural heritage to develop cultural products with local and ethnic characteristics and market potential and conduct cultural services and related activities.
articles.43: Where a person violates subparagraphs (1), (2), or (3) of Article 15, the department of the People's Government of Zhenyuan County responsible for planning shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and, within a specified period, restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. Any unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within the specified period, the department may designate a capable entity to do so, and the violator shall bear the cost. If the conduct causes serious consequences, the organization shall also be fined not less than RMB 500,000 but not more than RMB 1,000,000, and the individual shall also be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000. Any loss caused shall be compensated for in accordance with the law.
articles.44: Where a person installs, moves, alters, or damages a sign for a historic district, area with traditional character, or historic building without authorization in violation of these Regulations, the department of the People's Government of Zhenyuan County responsible for planning shall order correction within a specified period. If the person fails to comply within that period, the organization shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and the individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.45: Where conduct damages the City's cultural heritage, historic character, or ecological environment and harms State or public interests, the relevant authorities and organizations may bring a public-interest lawsuit in accordance with the law.
articles.46:
Where laws or regulations prescribe penalties for other conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
Chapter VII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.47:
These Regulations shall take effect on 31 December 2023.
