FBMCLI.10.4789838.title: Regulations of Fuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2021 Amendment)

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to strengthen the protection and administration of Fuzhou as a historic and cultural city, preserve and carry forward its outstanding history and culture, and promote coordinated economic and social development, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and Traditional Villages, and other applicable laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to the planning, protection, use, and administration of Fuzhou as a historic and cultural city.
Where laws or regulations separately provide for the protection and administration of cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, or other matters, those provisions shall prevail.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, strict protection, and administration at the appropriate territorial level. It shall preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage and properly balance its protection and transmission with its development and use.
articles.4: Article 4 The Municipal and District People's Governments shall be responsible for protecting and administering the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas, incorporate such work into economic and social development plans and annual work plans, and include dedicated funds for protection in their respective budgets.
articles.5:
Article 5 The municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city shall be the competent authority for such protection and administration in this Municipality and shall be responsible for its overall administration.
The municipal natural resources and planning department shall, according to its responsibilities, review and approve, supervise, and administer planning for construction projects in the historic and cultural city.
The municipal housing and urban-rural development department shall, according to its responsibilities, review and approve, supervise, and administer construction projects in the historic and cultural city.
The municipal departments responsible for cultural relics; culture and tourism; development and reform; finance; housing security and real estate administration; urban administration; ecology and environment; education; civil affairs; and ethnic and religious affairs, together with landscaping departments and fire and rescue agencies, shall implement these Regulations in coordination and in accordance with their respective responsibilities.
articles.6: Article 6 Relevant protection and administration bodies established by the Municipal and District People's Governments shall be responsible for the day-to-day protection and administration of historic and cultural districts, historic character areas, and groups of historic buildings.
articles.7: Article 7 The Municipal People's Government shall establish an expert advisory committee for protection of the historic and cultural city. The committee shall be consulted on the preparation of relevant protection plans and protection lists, as well as on major matters concerning development and construction.
articles.8:
Article 8 The Municipal People's Government shall advance applications for World Cultural Heritage status and build an international profile for Mindu culture.
The Municipal and District People's Governments shall strengthen the collection, organization, research, display, and dissemination of Mindu cultural resources, establish a system for their protection and transmission, and promote innovation and development in Mindu culture.
articles.9:
Article 9 The Municipal and District People's Governments and relevant departments shall strengthen public education on protection of the historic and cultural city, raise public awareness, and commend and reward entities and individuals that make outstanding contributions to such protection.
All entities and individuals have a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and may dissuade, report, or lodge complaints against conduct that damages it.
Chapter II — Protected Matters
articles.11: Article 11 Fuzhou shall maintain a protection list for the historic and cultural city. The list shall include protected items approved and announced by the State Council and the People's Government of Fujian Province, as well as items falling within the categories set out in Article 10 of these Regulations.
articles.12:
Article 12 The municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city shall organize the preparation and revision of the protection list.
It shall, together with the departments responsible for natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism, and cultural relics, and landscaping departments, survey the Municipality's historic and cultural resources. Where a resource has protection value, it shall promptly propose that the resource be added to the list.
Except for protected items approved and announced by the State Council or the People's Government of Fujian Province, a proposed item shall be subject to expert review organized jointly with relevant departments and public notice. It shall be announced after approval by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.13:
Article 13 Any entity or individual that discovers a building or structure with potential protection value during urban construction may report it to the housing and urban-rural development department in the locality. That department shall promptly inspect it together with the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city and relevant cultural relics departments, and issue a handling opinion within five working days. If the building or structure is determined to require interim protection, measures such as protecting the site and placing signs shall be taken, and the owner, user, or manager shall be notified in writing.
Within seven working days after interim protection measures are taken, the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city shall organize an expert assessment. If the building or structure is found to have protection value, it shall be added to the protection list. If it is not, the owner, user, or manager shall be notified in writing within two working days that the interim protection measures are lifted.
articles.14:
Article 14 Based on the protection list, the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city shall, together with the departments responsible for natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism, and cultural relics, and landscaping departments, systematically compile archival materials concerning the historic and cultural city using text, audio, video, surveying, digital multimedia, and other means. It shall establish a digital archive database, administer it digitally, and update it promptly.
Chapter III — Protection Planning
articles.15: Article 15 The Municipal People's Government shall organize the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city, the departments responsible for natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, and cultural relics, and other relevant entities to prepare a protection plan for Fuzhou as a historic and cultural city. After approval in accordance with the law, the plan shall be made public and incorporated into territorial spatial planning.
articles.16: Article 16 Based on the protection plan for the historic and cultural city, the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration shall, together with the relevant departments responsible for natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, and cultural relics, prepare special protection plans for historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, historic character areas, groups of historic buildings, and other protected areas. Each special plan shall be made public after approval in accordance with the law.
articles.17:
Article 17 Protection plans shall be prepared on the basis of scientific assessment and after broad consultation with relevant departments, experts, and the public.
A protection plan approved in accordance with the law shall not be amended without authorization. Where an amendment is necessary, opinions shall be solicited from relevant departments, experts, and the public, and the amendment shall be approved and made public in accordance with statutory procedures.
articles.18: Article 18 The protected areas of historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, historic character areas, traditional villages, and groups of historic buildings shall include core protected areas and construction control areas. Where necessary, an environmental coordination area may also be delineated outside a construction control area. Its specific boundaries shall be determined by the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city together with the relevant departments responsible for natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, and cultural relics; included in the protection plan; and made public after approval in accordance with the law.
articles.19:
Article 19 The Municipal and District People's Governments shall strictly implement the protection plan for the historic and cultural city, supervise and inspect its implementation by relevant departments, regularly monitor and assess protection conditions and issue evaluations, and report promptly to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.20: Article 20 In accordance with the protection plan, the Municipal and District People's Governments shall strictly protect the historic city's landscape pattern of ‘three hills, two pagodas, and one river,’ its natural landforms, and its surrounding landscape environment. They shall control the overall scale of development, population, and spatial dimensions of the historic urban area, as well as building height, bulk, color, and facade style.
articles.21: Article 21 The Municipal and District People's Governments shall strictly protect the spatial sequence along the central axis of the historic urban area. The height, bulk, colors, and other features of new buildings along the axis shall comply with the protection plan.
articles.22:
Article 22 The visual corridor between Yushan, Wushan, and Pingshan shall be 100 meters wide. Buildings within the corridor shall not exceed 24 meters in height. Buildings in other areas within the enclosed zone and buildings along the Baima River in the historic urban area shall not exceed 48 meters. Buildings in the area around Youth Association Square on the north bank of the Min River near Jiefang Bridge shall not exceed 18 meters. The profile of Yantai Hill shall remain prominent on the south bank of the Min River.
Buildings exceeding the foregoing height limits, and existing buildings that seriously impair the landscape character of Yushan, Wushan, or Pingshan, shall be rectified in accordance with the protection plan and the law.
articles.23: Article 23 The Municipal and District People's Governments shall protect the overall character and spatial form of historic and cultural districts; protect and restore the lane-and-block pattern of Sanfang Qixiang; preserve the integrated river-and-lane spatial pattern of Zhuzifang; and preserve the historic character of traditional commercial streets, buildings, and guild halls in Shangxiahang.
articles.24: Article 24 The layout of commercial activities within historic and cultural districts, historic character areas, and groups of historic buildings shall comply with the applicable special protection plan, suit the local environment and functions, and give due attention to promoting and presenting Mindu culture internationally.
articles.25: Article 25 The department responsible for cultural relics shall identify and protect cultural relics associated with Taiwan and overseas Chinese, and place them under signposted protection. Where such relics have important cultural value relating to Taiwan or overseas Chinese, they shall be assessed promptly and, in accordance with the law, designated and announced as protected cultural relics.
articles.26: Article 26 The Municipal and District People's Governments shall prioritize the protection of revolutionary cultural relics, integrate sites of important historical events and areas concentrated with revolutionary cultural relics into the urban and landscape settings, and establish bases for patriotic education.
articles.27:
Article 27 The Municipal People's Government shall place conspicuous protection signs indicating the protected boundaries of announced historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, historic character areas, traditional villages, groups of historic buildings, historic buildings, and buildings of traditional character.
No entity or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection sign without authorization.
articles.28:
Article 28 Within the core protected area of a historic character area or group of historic buildings, no new construction or expansion may take place, except for necessary public infrastructure, public service facilities, and other construction activities specified in the protection plan.
Construction within such a core protected area shall be approved by the municipal natural resources and planning department. Before granting approval, that department shall seek the opinions of the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city and the department responsible for cultural relics.
articles.29: Article 29 Construction within a construction control area of a historic and cultural district, famous town or village, historic character area, traditional village, or group of historic buildings shall preserve the traditional layout and continue the historic character. New or reconstructed buildings and structures shall be compatible with that character in height, bulk, color, and other respects. New or reconstructed roads shall not alter the original road layout or landscape features.
articles.30: Article 30 Construction within an environmental coordination area of a historic and cultural district, famous town or village, historic character area, traditional village, or group of historic buildings shall protect the natural and cultural environment on which it depends. New or reconstructed buildings and structures shall be compatible with cultural relics and historic sites and with the character of the surrounding environment.
articles.31: Article 31 For major development or construction in historic and cultural districts or historic character areas, the Municipal People's Government shall solicit public opinions, organize expert review, prepare a construction plan, and submit it to the Municipal People's Congress or its Standing Committee for decision.
articles.32:
Article 32 The owner or user of a historic building shall use it reasonably, maintain it and take safety precautions, preserve its original character, and accept guidance, inspection, and supervision.
The owner shall be responsible for maintaining and repairing a historic building. For a directly managed public housing property, a property managed by the government, or a historic building whose owner cannot be located or whose title is unclear, the manager or user shall be responsible. Maintenance and repairs shall follow the protection drawings, technical repair specifications, and protection plan prepared by the Municipal or District People's Government.
If a historic building is at risk of damage and its owner or user genuinely lacks the capacity to maintain or repair it, the Municipal or District People's Government shall protect it as appropriate by providing a subsidy, carrying out repairs, arranging an exchange, or taking other measures.
articles.33: Article 33 Murals, carvings, building components, and other items retained from buildings lawfully expropriated and demolished shall be collected by a cultural relics collection institution designated by the municipal cultural relics department if they have collection value. If they have reuse value, an entity designated by the Municipal or District People's Government shall be responsible for recovering and reusing them.
articles.34:
Article 34 For immovable cultural relics not yet designated and announced as protected cultural relics, the district cultural relics department shall register and announce them and delineate their protected areas.
Based on historical records and archaeological surveys, the municipal cultural relics department may delineate underground archaeological zones and underwater cultural relic protection areas and submit them to the Municipal People's Government for approval and announcement.
Before a construction project proceeds in an underground archaeological zone, archaeological investigation, exploration, or excavation shall be organized in accordance with statutory procedures. The project developer shall include the necessary costs in the project budget.
articles.35:
Article 35 Ancient river and lake systems shall be restored in accordance with the comprehensive improvement plan formulated by the Municipal People's Government so as to recover their landscape character.
It is prohibited to fill in or occupy an ancient river channel designated for preservation in the protection plan, or to alter its width or course.
articles.36: Article 36 Names of streets, areas, and buildings within the historic urban area that embody Fuzhou's historical and cultural identity shall not be changed without authorization. Where a change is genuinely necessary in special circumstances, before approval is sought in accordance with the law, the municipal civil affairs department shall consult the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city and the department responsible for cultural relics.
articles.37:
Article 37 Institutions of higher education and secondary vocational schools within this Municipality are encouraged and supported to offer courses related to protection of the historic and cultural city and to train professional and technical personnel in the protection and use of historic and cultural resources.
Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations are encouraged to participate in protection and use by donating, providing funding, adopting a protected site, providing technical services, or making suggestions.
Social capital is encouraged to invest in such protection and use through policy guidance, financial support, and other means.
articles.38:
Article 38 Subject to protection taking priority, the activation and adaptive use of the various resources and features of the historic and cultural city are encouraged, including the establishment of museums and cultural institutions and the development of heritage tourism and cultural and creative industries.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.39: Article 39 Where laws or regulations already prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.40:
Article 40 Where any of the following circumstances violates the second paragraph of Article 27 of these Regulations, the authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, a fine shall be imposed as follows:
(1) For unauthorized installation, movement, alteration, or damage of a protection sign for a historic and cultural district, famous town or village, historic character area, traditional village, group of historic buildings, or historic building, an entity shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and an individual shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
(2) For unauthorized installation, movement, alteration, or damage of a protection sign for a building of traditional character, an entity shall be fined not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 5,000, and an individual shall be fined not less than RMB 500 but not more than RMB 1,000.
articles.41: Article 41 Where the approval procedures are not followed in violation of the second paragraph of Article 28 of these Regulations, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel.
articles.42: Article 42 Where maintenance or repair of a historic building is not carried out in accordance with its protection drawings, technical repair specifications, and protection plan, in violation of the second paragraph of Article 32 of these Regulations, the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city shall order correction and impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000 on an entity, or not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000 on an individual.
articles.43:
Article 43 A staff member of the Municipal or District People's Government or a relevant competent department who abuses official powers, neglects duties, or engages in favoritism or malpractice in the protection of the historic and cultural city shall be sanctioned in accordance with the law. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.44:
Article 44 For purposes of these Regulations:
(1) ‘Three hills and two pagodas’ refers to Yushan, Wushan, Pingshan, Wuta Pagoda, and Baita Pagoda.
(2) ‘Sanfang Qixiang’ refers to Yijinfang, Wenrufang, Guanglufang, Yangqiao Lane, Langguan Lane, Taxiang Lane, Huang Lane, Anmin Lane, Gong Lane, and Jibi Lane.
(3) ‘Historic urban area’ refers to the area centered on the Three Hills and Two Pagodas, extending east to Wuyi Road and Wusi Road, west to Baima River (including West Lake), north to the northern foothills of Pingshan, and south to the Dongxi River, together with the riverside areas outside the old city walls, including Taijiang and Cangqian.
(4) ‘Central axis of the historic urban area’ refers to the section running from Pingshan in the north, along Guping Road and 817 Road, across Jiefang Bridge, to Yantai Hill.
articles.45: Article 45 Relevant counties and county-level cities may apply these Regulations by reference when protecting and administering related matters concerning historic and cultural cities.
articles.46: Article 46 The Municipal People's Government shall formulate implementing rules in accordance with these Regulations.
articles.47: Article 47 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 October 2013. The Regulations of Fuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City, adopted at the 19th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 10th Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress on 27 October 1995, shall be repealed at the same time.

FBMCLI.10.4789839.title: Decision of the Standing Committee of the Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress on Amending the Regulations of Fuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2021)

articles.1:
Decision of the Standing Committee of the Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress on Amending the Regulations of Fuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2021)

Issuing authority: Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress (including its Standing Committee)
Document number: Announcement No. 41 [15th Standing Committee] of the Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress
Approving authority: Standing Committee of the People's Congress of Fujian Province
Approval date: 15 December 2021
Date of promulgation: 22 December 2021
Effective date: 22 December 2021
Status: In force
Level: Municipal local regulation
Category: Review and cleanup of laws and regulations

Announcement of the Standing Committee of the Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress
(No. 41 [15th Standing Committee])
The Decision of the Standing Committee of the Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress on Amending the Regulations of Fuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City was adopted at the 40th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 15th Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress on 28 October 2021 and approved at the 30th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 13th People's Congress of Fujian Province on 15 December 2021. It is hereby promulgated and shall take effect on the date of promulgation.
Standing Committee of the Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress
22 December 2021

Decision of the Standing Committee of the Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress on Amending the Regulations of Fuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City
(Adopted at the 40th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 15th Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress on 28 October 2021; approved at the 30th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 13th People's Congress of Fujian Province on 15 December 2021)

The 40th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 15th Fuzhou Municipal People's Congress decides to amend the Regulations of Fuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City as follows:

1. Article 1 is amended to read: ‘These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to strengthen the protection and administration of Fuzhou as a historic and cultural city, preserve and carry forward its outstanding history and culture, and promote coordinated economic and social development, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and Traditional Villages, and other applicable laws and regulations.’
2. Article 3 is amended to read: ‘Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, strict protection, and administration at the appropriate territorial level. It shall preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage and properly balance its protection and transmission with its development and use.’
3. Article 4 is amended to read: ‘The Municipal and District People's Governments shall be responsible for protecting and administering the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas, incorporate such work into economic and social development plans and annual work plans, and include dedicated funds for protection in their respective budgets.’
4. Article 5 is amended to provide that the municipal authority responsible for protection and administration of the historic and cultural city is the competent authority for its overall administration; the municipal natural resources and planning department reviews, approves, supervises, and administers planning for construction projects; the municipal housing and urban-rural development department reviews, approves, supervises, and administers construction projects; and the municipal departments responsible for cultural relics, culture and tourism, development and reform, finance, housing security and real estate administration, urban administration, ecology and environment, education, civil affairs, and ethnic and religious affairs, together with landscaping departments and fire and rescue agencies, implement the Regulations in coordination according to their respective responsibilities.
5. Article 6 is amended to provide that relevant protection and administration bodies established by the Municipal and District People's Governments are responsible for day-to-day protection and administration of historic and cultural districts, historic character areas, and groups of historic buildings.
6. Article 7 is amended to provide that the Municipal People's Government shall establish an expert advisory committee for protection of the historic and cultural city, and seek its opinions on relevant protection plans and protection lists and on major matters concerning development and construction.
7. A new Article 8 is added: ‘The Municipal People's Government shall advance applications for World Cultural Heritage status and build an international profile for Mindu culture. The Municipal and District People's Governments shall strengthen the collection, organization, research, display, and dissemination of Mindu cultural resources, establish a system for their protection and transmission, and promote innovation and development in Mindu culture.’
8. Former Article 8 is renumbered Article 9 and amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments and relevant departments to strengthen public education on protection of the historic and cultural city, raise public awareness, and commend and reward outstanding contributors; all entities and individuals have a duty to protect the city and may dissuade, report, or lodge complaints against conduct damaging it.
9. Former Article 9 is renumbered Article 10 and amended to list the protected matters: the traditional layout and historic character of the historic urban area; historic and cultural districts including Sanfang Qixiang, Zhuzifang, and Shangxiahang; historic character areas including Yantai Hill, Yeshan Hill, and the Fujian Shipbuilding Administration; groups of historic buildings including Guling and the former site of Fujian Union University; historic and cultural towns and villages including Luozhou and Min'an and traditional villages; outstanding traditional streets and lanes; immovable cultural relics, historic buildings, and buildings of traditional character; intangible cultural heritage and other outstanding Mindu culture; ancient river and lake systems, hot springs, ancient banyan trees and other ancient or notable trees, and other historic environmental features; and other matters protected by laws and regulations.
10. Former Article 11 is renumbered Article 12 and amended to provide that the municipal protection authority shall organize preparation and revision of the protection list, survey historic and cultural resources together with the relevant departments, promptly propose listing resources with protection value, and, for proposed items other than those approved and announced by the State Council or Fujian Provincial People's Government, organize expert review and public notice and announce them after Municipal People's Government approval.
11. A new Article 13 is added: Any entity or individual discovering a building or structure with potential protection value during urban construction may report it to the local housing and urban-rural development department. That department shall inspect it promptly with the municipal protection authority and cultural relics departments and issue an opinion within five working days. If interim protection is warranted, it shall protect the site, place signs, and notify the owner, user, or manager in writing. Within seven working days after interim measures are taken, the municipal protection authority shall arrange expert review. An item found to have protection value shall be listed; otherwise, the owner, user, or manager shall be notified in writing within two working days that interim measures are lifted.
12. Former Article 12 is renumbered Article 14 and amended to require the municipal protection authority, based on the protection list and together with the relevant departments, to compile archival materials systematically using text, audio, video, surveying, digital multimedia, and other means; establish a digital archive database; administer it digitally; and update it promptly.
13. Former Article 13 is renumbered Article 15 and amended to require the Municipal People's Government to organize the relevant municipal bodies and departments to prepare a protection plan for Fuzhou as a historic and cultural city, submit it for approval in accordance with the law, make it public, and incorporate it into territorial spatial planning.
14. Former Article 14 is renumbered Article 16 and amended to require the municipal protection authority, based on the city protection plan and together with relevant departments, to prepare special protection plans for historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, historic character areas, groups of historic buildings, and other areas, and make each plan public after lawful approval.
15. Former Article 16 is renumbered Article 18 and amended to provide that protected areas for historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, historic character areas, traditional villages, and groups of historic buildings include core protected areas and construction control areas. Where necessary, an environmental coordination area may be delineated outside a construction control area; its boundaries shall be determined by the municipal protection authority and relevant departments, included in the protection plan, and made public after lawful approval.
16. Former Article 17 is renumbered Article 19 and amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments to strictly implement the protection plan, supervise and inspect relevant departments, regularly monitor and assess protection conditions, and promptly report to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level.
17. Former Article 18 is renumbered Article 20 and amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments to strictly protect the city's ‘three hills, two pagodas, and one river’ landscape pattern, natural landforms, and surrounding landscape, and control development scale, population, spatial dimensions, and building height, bulk, colors, and facade style in the historic urban area.
18. Former Article 19 is renumbered Article 21 and amended to require strict protection of the spatial sequence along the central axis of the historic urban area; new buildings along the axis shall comply with the protection plan as to height, bulk, color, and other features.
19. Former Article 21 is renumbered Article 23 and amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments to protect the overall character and spatial form of historic and cultural districts; protect and restore the lane-and-block pattern of Sanfang Qixiang; preserve the integrated river-and-lane spatial pattern of Zhuzifang; and preserve the historic character of traditional commercial streets, buildings, and guild halls in Shangxiahang.
20. Former Article 22 is renumbered Article 24 and amended to require commercial activity layouts within historic and cultural districts, historic character areas, and groups of historic buildings to comply with the special protection plan, suit the local environment and functions, and promote and present Mindu culture internationally.
21. A new Article 25 is added: ‘The department responsible for cultural relics shall identify and protect cultural relics associated with Taiwan and overseas Chinese, and place them under signposted protection. Such relics with important cultural value shall be assessed promptly and designated and announced as protected cultural relics in accordance with the law.’
22. A new Article 26 is added: ‘The Municipal and District People's Governments shall prioritize protection of revolutionary cultural relics, integrate sites of important historical events and areas concentrated with revolutionary cultural relics into the urban and landscape settings, and establish bases for patriotic education.’
23. Former Article 23 is renumbered Article 27 and amended to require the Municipal People's Government to place conspicuous signs showing protected boundaries for announced historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, historic character areas, traditional villages, groups of historic buildings, historic buildings, and buildings of traditional character. No entity or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a sign without authorization.
24. Former Article 24 is renumbered Article 28 and amended to prohibit new construction or expansion within the core protected area of a historic character area or group of historic buildings, except necessary public infrastructure, public service facilities, or other activities specified in the protection plan. Construction there requires approval from the municipal natural resources and planning department, which shall first consult the municipal protection authority and cultural relics department.
25. Former Article 25 is renumbered Article 29 and amended to require construction in relevant construction control areas to preserve the traditional layout and historic character; new or reconstructed buildings and structures shall be compatible in height, bulk, color, and other respects, and new or reconstructed roads shall not alter the original road layout or landscape features.
26. Former Article 26 is renumbered Article 30 and amended to require construction in relevant environmental coordination areas to protect the natural and cultural environment on which the area depends, and to ensure that new or reconstructed buildings and structures are compatible with cultural relics, historic sites, and the surrounding environment.
27. Former Article 27 is deleted.
28. Former Article 28 is renumbered Article 31 and amended to require the Municipal People's Government, for major development or construction in a historic and cultural district or historic character area, to solicit public opinions, organize expert review, prepare a construction plan, and submit it to the Municipal People's Congress or its Standing Committee for decision.
29. Former Article 29 is renumbered Article 32 and amended to require the owner or user of a historic building to use it reasonably, maintain it, take safety precautions, preserve its original character, and accept guidance and supervision. The owner is responsible for maintenance and repairs, except that the manager or user is responsible for directly managed public housing, government-managed property, or buildings whose owner cannot be located or whose title is unclear. Work shall follow protection drawings, technical repair specifications, and the protection plan prepared by the Municipal or District People's Government. Where a building is at risk and the owner or user genuinely lacks capacity, the government shall protect it as appropriate by subsidy, repairs, exchange, or other measures.
30. Former Article 30 is renumbered Article 33 and amended to provide that retained murals, carvings, and building components with collection value from lawfully expropriated and demolished buildings shall be collected by an institution designated by the municipal cultural relics department; items with reuse value shall be recovered and reused by an entity designated by the Municipal or District People's Government.
31. Former Article 31 is renumbered Article 34 and amended to require the district cultural relics department to register, announce, and delineate protected areas for immovable cultural relics not yet designated and announced as protected cultural relics. The municipal cultural relics department may delineate underground archaeological zones and underwater cultural relic protection areas based on historical records and archaeological surveys and submit them to the Municipal People's Government for approval and announcement. Construction in an underground archaeological zone requires archaeological investigation, exploration, or excavation organized under statutory procedures, with costs included in the project budget by the developer.
32. Former Articles 32 and 33 are deleted.
33. Former Article 34 is renumbered Article 35 and amended to require ancient river and lake systems to be improved under a comprehensive plan of the Municipal People's Government to restore their landscape character, and to prohibit filling in or occupying ancient river channels designated for preservation or changing their width or course.
34. Former Article 35 is renumbered Article 36 and amended to prohibit unauthorized changes to names of streets, areas, and buildings within the historic urban area that embody Fuzhou's historical and cultural identity. Before a necessary change is submitted for approval, the municipal civil affairs department shall consult the municipal protection authority and cultural relics department.
35. A new Article 37 is added to encourage local higher education institutions and secondary vocational schools to offer relevant courses and train professionals in protection and use of historic and cultural resources; encourage citizens, legal persons, and other organizations to participate through donations, funding, adoption, technical services, or suggestions; and attract social investment through policy guidance and financial support.
36. A new Article 38 is added to encourage, subject to protection taking priority, adaptive use of historic and cultural resources, including museums and cultural institutions, heritage tourism, and cultural and creative industries.
37. A new Article 39 is added: ‘Where laws or regulations already prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.’
38. Former Article 36 is renumbered Article 40 and amended to provide that unauthorized installation, movement, alteration, or damage of protection signs in violation of Article 27(2) shall be corrected by order of the municipal protection authority. If not corrected by the deadline, a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 shall be imposed on an entity, or RMB 1,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual, for signs for historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, historic character areas, traditional villages, groups of historic buildings, or historic buildings; for signs for buildings of traditional character, the fine is RMB 1,000 to RMB 5,000 for an entity or RMB 500 to RMB 1,000 for an individual.
39. Former Article 37 is renumbered Article 41 and amended to provide that failure to follow the approval procedures required by Article 28(2) shall result in sanctions under the law for the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel.
40. Former Articles 38, 39, and 40 are deleted.
41. A new Article 42 is added: ‘Where maintenance or repair of a historic building is not carried out in accordance with its protection drawings, technical repair specifications, and protection plan, in violation of Article 32(2), the municipal protection authority shall order correction and impose a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 on an entity, or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual.’
42. Former Article 43 is renumbered Article 45 and amended to provide that relevant counties and county-level cities may apply the Regulations by reference when protecting and administering related matters concerning historic and cultural cities.

The wording of certain provisions is also amended accordingly, and the numbering of provisions is adjusted.
This Decision shall take effect on the date of promulgation. The Regulations of Fuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City, as revised in accordance with this Decision, are hereby republished.

FBMCLI.10.7706123.title: Decision of the Standing Committee of the Haikou Municipal People's Congress on Amending the Regulations of Haikou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2024)

articles.1:
Decision of the Standing Committee of the Haikou Municipal People's Congress on Amending the Regulations of Haikou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2024)

Issuing authority: Haikou Municipal People's Congress (including its Standing Committee)
Document number: Announcement No. 33 of the Standing Committee of the Haikou Municipal People's Congress
Approving authority: Standing Committee of the People's Congress of Hainan Province
Approval date: 31 July 2024
Promulgation date: 12 August 2024
Effective date: 12 August 2024
Status: In force
Level: Municipal local regulation
Category: Protection of historic and cultural cities

Announcement of the Standing Committee of the Haikou Municipal People's Congress
(No. 33)
The Decision of the Standing Committee of the Haikou Municipal People's Congress on Amending the Regulations of Haikou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City, adopted at the 16th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 17th Haikou Municipal People's Congress, was approved by the 12th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 7th People's Congress of Hainan Province on 31 July 2024. It is hereby promulgated and shall take effect on the date of promulgation.
Standing Committee of the Haikou Municipal People's Congress
12 August 2024

Decision of the Standing Committee of the Haikou Municipal People's Congress on Amending the Regulations of Haikou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City
(Adopted at the 16th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 17th Haikou Municipal People's Congress on 13 December 2023; approved at the 12th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 7th People's Congress of Hainan Province on 31 July 2024)

The 16th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 17th Haikou Municipal People's Congress decides to amend the Regulations of Haikou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City as follows:

1. Article 3 is amended to provide that protection of Haikou as a historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, differentiated administration, strict protection, and appropriate use; preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage; and properly balance its inheritance, protection, and use with urban and rural development and coordinated economic and social development.
2. Paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 4 are amended to provide that the municipal housing and urban-rural development department, together with the municipal culture and tourism department, handles the specific work of protecting, supervising, and administering the historic and cultural city; the municipal natural resources and planning department handles related planning administration; and the departments responsible for development and reform, finance, public security, commerce, education, and comprehensive administrative law enforcement, together with fire and rescue agencies, coordinate within their respective authority.
3. Article 5 is amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments to include protection and administration of the historic and cultural city in economic and social development plans, allocate protection funds in their budgets, and increase fiscal investment. Entities and individuals are encouraged to participate through donations, funding, technical services, or suggestions. Investors are encouraged to protectively develop and use the city's resources in accordance with the law and to develop tourism and related industries.
4. Article 14 is amended to require the municipal natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, and comprehensive administrative law-enforcement departments, together with the local government or property owner, to rectify or demolish buildings and facilities that do not comply with the protection plan or the special protection plan for a historic and cultural district, in accordance with the plan and the law.
5. Article 15 is amended to prohibit unauthorized amendment of an approved protection plan or special protection plan for a historic and cultural district. Where amendment is necessary, the planning authority shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and may prepare an amendment only after consent. Public views shall be broadly solicited and experts consulted. The revised plans shall be submitted for approval and published under the original procedures.
6. Former Article 18 is renumbered Article 17 and amended to provide that the protected area of a historic and cultural district consists of a core protected area and a construction control area. The municipal natural resources and planning department, together with the municipal housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism departments, shall propose their boundaries and include them in the protection plan and special district plan. The Municipal People's Government shall place protection signs at the main entrances to core protected areas. No entity or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a sign without authorization.
7. Former Article 20 is renumbered Article 19. Its first paragraph is amended to strictly control building heights on both sides of distinctive streets within the core protected area: the total height of buildings and structures lawfully constructed, extended, or reconstructed shall be less than 15 meters, maintaining a varied streetscape; in the construction control area, the total height shall be less than 20 meters. Heights shall also comply with the construction controls in the protection plan and other applicable plans.
8. Former Article 21 is renumbered Article 20 and amended to prohibit in a protected area: (1) hill cutting, quarrying, mining, or other acts damaging the traditional layout or historic character; (2) occupation of gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, roads, or other areas designated for preservation; (3) construction of factories or warehouses for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances; (4) unlawful demolition or construction; (5) changes to land-use functions specified in the protection plan; (6) construction exceeding controls on building height or floor-area ratio or violating controls on bulk, color, or other features; and (7) other activities prohibited by laws and regulations.
9. Former Article 23 is renumbered Article 22 and amended to provide that a building in a protected area that has been identified as dangerous and has lawful, clear title may be repaired or renovated in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law and other laws and regulations, while preserving its traditional layout and historic character. The Municipal People's Government shall separately formulate detailed measures. Municipal and District People's Governments shall make good use of urban cultural resources and guide and encourage owners of houses in protected areas to improve living conditions voluntarily, including through property exchange.
10. Former Article 24 is renumbered Article 23 and amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments to give priority to building and improving infrastructure and public services in accordance with the protection plan and special district plan, and to improve living conditions. Firefighting facilities and access routes in core protected areas shall meet applicable technical standards and codes. If protection needs make compliance impossible, the municipal fire and rescue agency and housing and urban-rural development department shall formulate corresponding fire-safety safeguards.
11. Former Article 25 is renumbered Article 24 and amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments to adopt supportive policies, optimize the mix of activities in historic and cultural districts, encourage locally distinctive businesses, guide time-honored brands to establish themselves there, and promote integration of district protection with culture and tourism.
12. Former Article 27 is renumbered Article 25 and amended to provide that modern buildings, traditional residences, shops, and structures with historical, artistic, or scientific value shall be surveyed by the municipal housing and urban-rural development department together with the culture and tourism department. After relevant opinions are solicited and expert review is completed, items approved by the Municipal People's Government shall be announced as historic buildings, marked with protection signs, and entered into historic-building archives.
13. Former Article 28 is renumbered Article 26 and amended to require the Municipal People's Government to establish classification standards and a protection list for historic buildings and publish the list promptly. Class I historic buildings shall retain their original facade design, surface materials, color scheme, structural system, floor plan, and distinctive interior decoration. Class II buildings shall retain their original facade design, surface materials, color scheme, and principal floor plan. Class III buildings shall retain their original facade design, surface materials, and color scheme.
14. A new Article 27 is added to require dynamic administration of the historic-building protection list, with timely revisions and public notice. If a listed building is lost or damaged due to force majeure and has genuinely lost its protection significance, or its protection category changes, the municipal housing and urban-rural development department and culture and tourism department shall promptly propose an adjustment, solicit relevant opinions, complete expert review, and submit it to the Municipal People's Government for approval. A historic building shall be removed from the list from the date it is lawfully announced as a protected cultural relic or immovable cultural relic.
15. Former Article 29 is renumbered Article 28 and amended to provide that the owner of a historic building is responsible for its protection. If the owner cannot be located or contacted, or title is unclear, the user or manager is responsible; if the owner, user, and manager cannot be identified, the district people's government shall designate a responsible person in accordance with the law. The responsible person shall maintain and repair the building in accordance with the protection plan and maintenance standards, which shall be formulated by the municipal housing and urban-rural development department together with the culture and tourism department. If the building is at risk and the responsible person lacks capacity, the Municipal or District People's Government shall take protective measures. The governments shall adopt policies encouraging owners to sell or donate historic buildings to the State.
16. A new Article 33 is added to encourage reasonable use of historic buildings. Subject to protection requirements, they may house museums, exhibition halls, and intangible cultural heritage centers, host cultural and creative activities, cultural experiences and research, or hold related exhibitions to display and disseminate history and culture.
17. Former Article 36 is renumbered Article 35. Its second paragraph is amended to require the culture and tourism department to formulate specific measures according to the protection needs of different cultural relics, report them to the people's government at the same level, and publicly announce and implement them.
18. Former Article 37 is renumbered Article 36 and amended to require use of immovable cultural relics to follow the principles of preserving their original state and minimal intervention, protect the safety of the relic and its associated objects, and prohibit damaging, reconstructing, adding to, or demolishing an immovable cultural relic.
19. Former Article 38 is renumbered Article 37 and amended to provide that where a citizen or a non-cultural-relic entity uses a State-owned protected cultural relic or representative memorial building, the user shall enter into a protection-and-use responsibility agreement with the culture and tourism department, manage, maintain, and repair the building, and accept inspection, supervision, and guidance.
20. Former Article 44 is renumbered Article 41 and amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments to establish representative intangible cultural heritage project lists at their respective levels. The culture and tourism department shall organize expert review and public notice for municipal- and district-level projects and publish them after approval by the people's government at the same level. Applications for and designation of national- and provincial-level projects shall follow State and provincial rules.
21. Former Article 45 is renumbered Article 42 and amended to require the culture and tourism department to survey, collect, organize, archive, and research intangible cultural heritage, including traditional arts such as Hainan coconut-shell carving and Longtang carving; traditional opera such as Qiong Opera, Hainan puppet theatre, and Hainan Zhai Opera; traditional music such as Hainan bayin; traditional techniques such as Hainan rosewood furniture making, traditional sugar production, and Hainan rice-noodle preparation; traditional dances such as Hainan Qilin, lion, and tiger dances and Haikou dragon dance; customs such as Madam Xian worship (Junpo Festival) and the Fucheng Lantern Festival flower exchange; folk literature such as legends, stories, and ballads; and other intangible cultural heritage.
22. Former Article 46 is renumbered Article 43 and amended to require the Municipal and District People's Governments to delineate and mark protected areas around cultural spaces on which representative intangible cultural heritage projects depend, and to protect them as a whole. Effective measures shall be taken in urban and rural planning and construction to protect related buildings, sites, and remains. No entity or individual may occupy or damage project records, objects, or related buildings, sites, or remains.
23. Former Article 47 is renumbered Article 44 and amended to require the culture and tourism department, under State and provincial rules, to designate and announce representative transmitters and groups for local intangible cultural heritage projects; systematically record their knowledge and skills; and support them through necessary premises, protection subsidies, participation in public-interest activities, and assistance with professional titles and talent recognition.
24. Former Article 48 is renumbered Article 45 and amended to require representative transmitters and groups to: (1) carry out transmission activities and train successors; (2) properly preserve relevant objects and records; (3) cooperate with the culture and tourism department and other authorities in intangible cultural heritage surveys; (4) participate in public-interest promotion; and (5) perform other duties prescribed by the State and province.
25. Former Article 52 is renumbered Article 49 and amended to provide that a State organ or staff member legally responsible for protecting Haikou as a historic and cultural city who fails to perform duties, including by failing to prepare or amend protection plans, failing to establish or adjust the historic-building list, unlawfully adjusting the boundaries of a historic and cultural district, or otherwise failing to perform oversight duties, shall be subject to sanctions under the law; where a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued.
26. Former Article 58 is renumbered Article 55 and amended to provide that a person who damages or destroys an immovable cultural relic in violation of Article 36 shall bear legal liability under the law and, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability. Unauthorized relocation or demolition of an immovable cultural relic shall be penalized by the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department if it does not constitute a crime.
27. Former Article 60 is renumbered Article 58 and amended to provide that where these Regulations do not prescribe a penalty for a violation but other laws or regulations do, those provisions shall apply.
28. The following terminology and cross-references are revised: (1) in Article 9, ‘master urban plan’ is replaced with ‘territorial spatial master plan,’ and ‘State Council department in charge of construction’ with ‘State Council department in charge of housing and urban-rural development’; (2) in Article 12, the municipal planning authority is replaced by the municipal natural resources and planning department acting with the housing and urban-rural development and culture and tourism departments; (3) in Article 13, the listed authorities are updated to include natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism, and comprehensive administrative law enforcement; (4) Article 22(2) and Article 55(2) are revised to cover film and television production and large public events such as exhibitions, performances, and recreational events in a core protected area; (5) relevant provisions update responsible authorities for building repairs, provincial review, tourism and culture, commerce, education, penalties, and designation of enforcement bodies; (6) in Article 39, ‘manager and user’ is replaced with ‘owner, user, and manager,’ and the cultural relics authority is replaced with the culture and tourism authority; (7) in Article 51, ‘intangible cultural heritage projects’ is replaced with ‘intangible cultural heritage’; (8) cross-references in Articles 54, 56, and 57 are updated from Article 30 to Article 29, and in Article 56 from Article 32 to Article 31; and (9) in Article 61, ‘protection sign’ is replaced with ‘protection signboard or protection sign.’
29. Articles 16, 26, 34, the second paragraph of Article 35, Articles 41, 42, 59, 63, and 66 are deleted.

This Decision shall take effect on the date of promulgation. The Regulations of Haikou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City are revised accordingly, renumbered, and republished.

Regulations cited in this document

Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China (2019 Revision)

FBMCLI.10.1429484.title: Regulations of Nanchang Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to strengthen protection of the historic and cultural city, preserve outstanding historic and cultural heritage, and promote coordinated economic and social development, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages promulgated by the State Council, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to the planning, protection, use, and administration of the historic and cultural city within this Municipality's administrative area.
Protected matters under these Regulations include the historic urban area; historic and cultural districts, towns, and villages; areas with historic character; historic buildings; traditional villages; protected cultural relics; immovable cultural relics; ancient or notable trees; historic place names; intangible cultural heritage; and other related matters.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, differentiated administration, strict protection, and appropriate use; preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage; and maintain the traditional layout and historic character.
articles.4: Article 4 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall be responsible for protecting and administering the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas and incorporate such work into their economic and social development plans.
articles.5:
Article 5 The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection committee for the historic and cultural city to study major protection matters and guide and coordinate protection work.
The committee shall establish an expert committee for protection of the historic and cultural city. Its experts in planning, culture and cultural relics, real estate, architecture, landscaping, tourism, religion, history, place names, folk customs, law, and traditional crafts shall review and assess the protection list, protection plans, protection measures, and other matters.
articles.6:
Article 6 The municipal urban and rural planning department, together with the municipal culture and cultural relics department, shall handle the specific work of protecting and administering the historic and cultural city throughout the Municipality. The municipal administration body for the historic and cultural city shall be responsible for day-to-day work.
The urban and rural planning department of each county, together with the corresponding culture and cultural relics department, shall handle the specific protection and administration of famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, and historic buildings in its jurisdiction.
The departments responsible for real estate, development and reform, construction, urban administration, land and natural resources (including real-property registration), finance, public security, tourism, landscaping and forestry, civil affairs, agriculture, water affairs, environmental protection, transport, education, and religious affairs shall perform related protection and administration work within their respective responsibilities.
articles.7: Article 7 Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall carry out related protection work for the historic and cultural city.
articles.8:
Article 8 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall include protection funding for the historic and cultural city in their respective budgets and ensure that it is used for its designated purposes.
Such funding may be used for surveys, mapping, applications and designation, academic research, professional training, preparation of plans, development and maintenance of information systems, protection facilities and environmental improvement, repair subsidies, public education, and awards for protection.
Individuals and entities are encouraged to participate through donations, investment, establishment of public-benefit organizations, technical services, volunteer services, and other means.
articles.9:
Article 9 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments and relevant departments responsible for urban and rural planning, culture and cultural relics, justice, and education shall strengthen public education on protection of the historic and cultural city, disseminate relevant knowledge, and raise public awareness.
Chapter II — Protection List
articles.11:
Article 11 The Municipal People's Government shall publish the protection list. Protected matters already approved and announced by the State, provincial, or Municipal People's Government shall be included directly. A protected matter approved by a county people's government shall be reported promptly to the Municipal People's Government for inclusion in the list.
Areas with historic character, historic buildings, and other protected matters shall be proposed by the urban and rural planning department together with the culture and cultural relics, real estate, and other departments after consultation with interested parties, the public, and experts, and shall be submitted to the people's government at the corresponding level for approval.
Any individual or entity may propose to the municipal administration body that a matter with protection value be included in the list.
articles.12:
Article 12 An area that has not been designated and announced as a historic and cultural district and that is at least one hectare in size may be designated and announced by the Municipal or County People's Government as an area with historic character if it meets any of the following criteria:
(1) it retains a relatively complete traditional layout and historic character;
(2) it is distinctive and representative of local characteristics during a particular historical period; or
(3) it contains abundant historic and cultural remains.
articles.14:
Article 14 The urban and rural planning department shall, together with the culture and cultural relics, real estate, and other departments at the same level, regularly organize lower-level people's governments and relevant departments to survey historic and cultural resources. Resources with protection value shall be promptly recommended to the municipal administration body for inclusion in the protection list.
The culture and cultural relics department shall promptly collect and organize historical materials concerning protected cultural relics, immovable cultural relics, and intangible cultural heritage.
The real estate and real-property registration departments shall provide information on the use, changes of ownership, maintenance, and repair of historic buildings.
Other relevant departments, township and town people's governments, and subdistrict offices shall assist in collecting information on the history, historic and artistic features, construction techniques, and dates of the protected matters.
articles.15:
Article 15 Where a material change to a protected matter included in the protection list requires adjustment, the relevant department shall make the adjustment under the original approval procedure and notify the municipal administration body.
Where a material change to a protected matter requires adjustment of the list, the Municipal People's Government shall promptly revise and republish it.
articles.16:
Article 16 The municipal administration body shall establish archives for the protection list and an information system for protection of the historic and cultural city.
The departments responsible for culture and cultural relics, real estate, construction, urban administration, civil affairs, landscaping and forestry, water affairs, agriculture, and tourism shall collect and organize relevant information according to their responsibilities, enter it into the information system, and share the information.
Chapter III — Protection Planning
articles.17:
Article 17 Protection plans for the historic and cultural city shall emphasize integrated protection and preserve and continue the traditional layout, historic character, and spatial scale. They shall protect related physical features and environmental elements, including buildings and structures, streets and lanes, mountains, rivers and waterways, and green spaces, and fully present historic and cultural traditions.
Other specialized plans concerning transport, municipal utilities, landscaping, fire safety, civil air defense, and related matters shall be coordinated with the protection plans.
articles.18:
Article 18 The contents of protection plans for the historic and cultural city, historic and cultural districts, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, and the procedures for organizing, approving, and amending such plans shall comply with relevant State and provincial provisions.
The core contents of the protection plan for the historic and cultural city shall be incorporated into the overall urban plan, and its requirements shall be implemented when preparing detailed regulatory plans.
The core contents of a protection plan for a famous historic and cultural town shall be incorporated into the town's overall plan. A protection plan for a historic and cultural district or famous village that meets the technical standards for a detailed regulatory plan may serve as the detailed regulatory plan for that area; one meeting village-planning requirements may serve as the village plan. Any separately prepared detailed regulatory plan or village plan shall be coordinated with the protection plan and include a dedicated section on historic and cultural protection.
articles.19: Article 19 The urban and rural planning department of the Municipality or county shall, together with the corresponding culture and cultural relics department and according to their respective jurisdictions, organize preparation of protection plans for areas with historic character and historic buildings and submit them to the people's government at the same level for approval. Any amendment shall be submitted for approval under the original procedure.
articles.20: Article 20 A protection plan for an area with historic character shall include: an assessment of its distinctive character and historic value, with proposed controls and protection requirements; the protected boundaries, including the core protected area and construction control area; classification-based protection and control measures for buildings; and protection controls for streets, lanes, and historic environmental features.
articles.21: Article 21 A protection plan for a historic building shall include: (1) its distinctive character and related environmental features; (2) its protected area, comprising the building itself and any necessary character-coordination area; and (3) protection measures and requirements for its use.
articles.22:
Article 22 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall strictly implement protection plans, coordinate implementation, supervise and inspect relevant departments, and conduct regular assessments.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.23:
Article 23 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall, in accordance with the protection plans, identify the implementing entities and specific protection measures and organize their implementation.
They may arrange day-to-day protection and administration of historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, and historic buildings through service procurement, establishment of area-based protection organizations, or other means.
articles.24:
Article 24 In accordance with the protection plans, the Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall organize relevant departments to improve roads, water supply and drainage, electricity, sanitation, fire safety, landscaping, lightning protection, other infrastructure and public services, and the living environment in historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, famous towns, and famous villages.
Where protection needs make it impossible to construct or administer facilities in a core protected area under current technical standards and codes, the relevant departments responsible for urban and rural planning, culture and cultural relics, fire safety, real estate, urban administration, and environmental protection shall formulate safeguards suited to those protection needs.
articles.25:
Article 25 The Municipal and County People's Governments shall place signs at the main entrances to core protected areas of historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, famous towns, and famous villages.
The Municipal People's Government shall establish uniform protection signs for historic buildings. The municipal or county urban and rural planning department shall place a protection sign in a conspicuous location on each historic building.
No individual or entity may install, move, cover, alter, or damage a sign or protection sign without authorization.
articles.26:
Article 26 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall designate and publicly announce the responsible persons for protection of historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, famous towns, and famous villages as follows: (1) the subdistrict office where a historic and cultural district or area with historic character is located; (2) the township or town people's government where a famous historic and cultural town is located; and (3) the villagers' committee where a famous village is located. Where a protection organization has been established by the relevant government, that organization shall be responsible.
For a protected matter spanning villages, the responsible person shall be designated by the relevant subdistrict office or township or town people's government; for one spanning subdistricts or townships or towns, by the relevant County (District) People's Government; and for one spanning counties or districts, by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.27: Article 27 The persons responsible for protection of historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, famous towns, and famous villages shall discharge their duties in accordance with the protection plans and shall: (1) preserve the integrity of the traditional layout, historic character, spatial scale, and historic environmental features; (2) promptly stop conduct endangering historic and cultural resources and report it to the competent department with jurisdiction and the municipal administration body; (3) assist relevant departments in ensuring the proper operation of public fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; (4) keep protected areas clean and orderly; and (5) meet other requirements established by the Municipal or County (District) People's Government.
articles.28: Article 28 The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall be determined as follows: (1) for a State-owned historic building, the entrusted manager shall be responsible; if there is none, the holder of the right to use it shall be responsible; (2) for a non-State-owned historic building, the owner shall be responsible; if the owner cannot be located or contacted or title is unclear, the entrusted manager shall be responsible, or, if there is none, the user of the building shall be responsible.
articles.29:
Article 29 The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall: (1) preserve its original height, bulk, exterior appearance, and colors; (2) preserve the integrity of its traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, and historic environmental features; (3) ensure structural safety, take immediate measures to eliminate hazards, and report them to relevant departments; (4) carry out repairs as required; (5) prevent water ingress, damp, and insect damage; (6) ensure proper operation of fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; (7) use the building lawfully and reasonably in accordance with the protection plan; (8) keep it clean and orderly; and (9) meet other requirements under laws and regulations.
When transferring or leasing a historic building, the parties shall specify protection and repair duties in the contract. The transferor or lessor shall notify the transferee or lessee of protection and repair requirements in the manner agreed in the contract.
articles.30:
Article 30 Construction within a protected area of a historic and cultural district, area with historic character, famous town, or famous village shall comply with the protection plan and the following requirements: (1) in a core protected area, no new construction or expansion is permitted except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
