Where dangerous buildings are concentrated or infrastructure is inadequate and implementation of the protection plan requires reconstruction of buildings or structures other than protected matters, the developer shall prepare a construction plan consistent with the historic character. Before granting planning permission, the urban and rural planning department shall consult the culture and cultural relics department at the same level and, where necessary, organize expert review and solicit public opinions; (2) new construction, expansion, or reconstruction in a construction control area shall meet the construction controls in the protection plan or protection measures, be compatible with the historic character in height, bulk, color, and other respects, and not damage the traditional layout or historic character. The applicant shall submit a specific plan addressing historic and cultural protection when applying for planning permission; (3) roads, underground works, and other municipal facilities shall be built with effective protective measures and shall not damage protected matters. Outdoor advertisements, signs, and other external facilities shall comply with the protection plan; and (4) the County (District) People's Government shall require existing facilities and enterprises within a protected area that pollute the environment to relocate or remedy the pollution within a specified period.
No new building or structure may be constructed within a historic building's protected area, except for an ancillary facility necessary for its protection.
articles.31: Article 31 Historic buildings shall receive classified protection according to their historical, artistic, scientific, social, and cultural value and their date of construction. The protection category shall be shown on the protection sign: (1) a historic building of high value and typical representativeness shall receive special protection; its structural system, facade, floor plan, and distinctive interior decoration shall not be changed; (2) a historic building of relatively high value and some representativeness shall receive key protection; its structural system and facade shall not be changed; and (3) a historic building with a degree of historical, artistic, scientific, social, or cultural value shall receive general protection; its structural system and principal facade shall not be changed.
articles.32:
Article 32 The municipal and County (District) real estate departments shall establish an annual structural-safety inspection system for historic buildings.
After hearing the views of the person responsible for protection, the county or district real estate department shall prepare an annual repair plan for a historic building at risk of damage or identified as dangerous and implement it after approval by the people's government at the same level.
The department shall notify the responsible person to repair the building under the annual plan. The responsible person shall carry out the repairs as required and bear the costs, but may apply for a subsidy if eligible. The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall formulate detailed subsidy measures.
If a historic building is at risk and the responsible person lacks the capacity to maintain and repair it, the Municipal or County (District) People's Government shall take protective measures.
articles.33:
Article 33 Repairs to a historic building shall comply with applicable technical specifications, quality standards, and protection-and-repair drawings. Owners and users of adjoining buildings and structures shall cooperate and provide necessary assistance. The municipal or county urban and rural planning department shall prepare the protection-and-repair drawings together with the real estate department at the same level.
Where repairs involve changes to the exterior facade or building structure, the responsible person shall apply for planning permission in accordance with the law. Before granting permission, the urban and rural planning department shall consult the culture and cultural relics department according to the nature of the project.
articles.34:
Article 34 A historic building shall be protected at its original site. No entity or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish it without authorization.
Where construction in the public interest makes protection at the original site impossible and relocation or demolition is necessary, the urban and rural planning department and culture and cultural relics department shall assess the relocation plan and remedial measures, issue an opinion on whether relocation or demolition is appropriate, and submit the matter for approval in accordance with the law.
articles.35:
Article 35 When the department responsible for housing expropriation surveys and registers title, use, floor area, and other details of properties within an expropriation area, it shall consult the urban and rural planning department on whether historic buildings are affected.
Where implementation of a protection plan so requires, the Municipal or County (District) People's Government may lawfully expropriate or exchange a historic building at risk of loss or damage, or another building or structure within the protected area of a historic and cultural district, area with historic character, famous town, or famous village, and shall compensate the owner in accordance with the law.
articles.36:
Article 36 The County (District) People's Government where a famous historic and cultural town or village is located shall allocate construction land quotas in a coordinated manner under the principle of intensive land use and give priority to rural housing needed to implement the protection plan.
Where protection needs require a new residential area for villagers at another location within the protected area, its construction plan shall comply with the protection plan.
articles.37:
Article 37 Subject to protection taking priority, a village collective economic organization where a famous historic and cultural town or village is located may establish relevant market entities and participate in protection and use.
A historic building on collectively owned land may be transferred while retaining the collective ownership status of the land.
articles.38:
Article 38 Individuals and entities are encouraged and supported to acquire ownership or use rights in historic buildings in accordance with the law and to use them protectively, with operating income retained as permitted by law, provided that structural, fire-safety, other professional requirements, and the protection plan are met.
Persons responsible for protection are encouraged to conduct revenue-generating activities centered on tourism, cultural industries, and traditional handicrafts, and to open historic buildings to the public where appropriate.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.39: Article 39 Where laws or regulations prescribe penalties for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.40:
Article 40 Where, in violation of Article 25(3), a protection sign for a historic and cultural district, area with historic character, famous town, or famous village is installed, moved, altered, or damaged without authorization, the urban administration law-enforcement department shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 1,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual.
Where a protection sign for a historic building is installed, moved, altered, or damaged without authorization, the department shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 5,000 to RMB 10,000 on an entity or a fine of up to RMB 1,000 on an individual.
articles.41: Article 41 Where outdoor advertisements, signs, or other external facilities are installed in violation of Article 30(1)(3) and do not comply with the protection plan, the urban administration law-enforcement department shall order correction within a specified period or restoration of the original condition. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 30,000 on an entity or up to RMB 5,000 on an individual.
articles.42: Article 42 Where a township or town people's government, subdistrict office, or its staff fails to discharge protection duties under Article 27, the County (District) People's Government shall order correction and impose sanctions in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel.
articles.43: Article 43 Where the Municipal or County (District) People's Government, a relevant department, or its staff commits any of the following acts, it shall be ordered to make correction and the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel shall be sanctioned in accordance with the law; where a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued: (1) failing to organize preparation, amendment, or publication of a protection plan for an area with historic character or a historic building under the statutory procedure; (2) failing to designate or adjust the protection list as required; (3) failing to grant administrative permission or impose administrative penalties as required; or (4) other dereliction of duty, abuse of powers, or favoritism or malpractice.
articles.44:
Article 44 Protection and administration of traditional villages, protected cultural relics, immovable cultural relics, modern industrial heritage, ancient sites, historic environmental features, intangible cultural heritage, and old place names with historic and cultural value or commemorative significance shall be governed by the relevant laws and regulations.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.45: Article 45 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 June 2018.

FBMCLI.10.1591538.title: Regulations of Kunming Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2020)

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to strengthen protection and administration of the historic and cultural city and preserve its outstanding historic and cultural heritage, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Yunnan Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns, Villages, and Streets, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2: Article 2 These Regulations apply to the planning, protection, administration, and use of Kunming as a historic and cultural city.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of integrated planning, science-based administration, protection first, appropriate use, strengthened transmission, and culture-led development. It shall preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage, protect the natural and cultural landscapes connected with it, and preserve and continue the traditional layout and character of the historic and cultural city.
articles.4:
Article 4 Protected matters in Kunming as a historic and cultural city include the historic urban area; famous historic and cultural towns and villages; historic villages and towns; historic and cultural districts; historic areas; historic buildings; buildings of traditional character; the landscape environment and cultural routes that embody the city's identity; historic environmental features; and other matters designated under relevant laws and regulations.
Immovable and underground cultural relics, former residences of notable persons, traditional place names, ancient or notable trees, industrial heritage, intangible cultural heritage, World Cultural Heritage, World Natural Heritage, scenic areas, and other matters shall be governed by relevant laws and regulations.
articles.5:
Article 5 The Municipal People's Government shall exercise unified leadership over protection and use of the historic and cultural city and its supervision and administration.
The People's Governments of counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protection and use and for supervision and administration within their respective administrative areas.
The competent departments for natural resources and planning and for cultural relics shall be specifically responsible for protection and administration.
The competent housing and urban-rural development department shall assist with construction administration relating to protection.
Other relevant administrative departments shall perform related protection, supervision, and administration duties according to their respective responsibilities.
articles.6: Article 6 The protection committee for the historic and cultural city established by the Municipal People's Government shall guide and coordinate major matters relating to protection. The expert committee for protection of the historic and cultural city shall provide advisory opinions to the Municipal People's Government and the protection committee for their decisions.
articles.7:
Article 7 The Municipal and County, County-level City, and District People's Governments shall incorporate protection of the historic and cultural city into their economic and social development plans. The Municipality and the relevant county-level governments shall include the necessary funding in their respective annual budgets.
Such funding shall be used for surveys, measurement, designation, emergency rescue, collection and administration of archival materials, academic research, plan preparation, repair subsidies, public education, grants, and awards.
articles.8: Article 8 The Municipal and County, County-level City, and District People's Governments may arrange day-to-day protection and administration of famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, historic areas, historic buildings, and buildings of traditional character through service procurement and other channels and means.
articles.9:
Article 9 Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection, transmission, and use of the historic and cultural city through donations, contributions, investment, provision of protection leads, services, and other means.
Enterprises, public institutions, research bodies, industry associations, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to conduct basic research and professional training relating to protection, transmission, and use in accordance with the law.
In accordance with relevant State provisions, the Municipal and County, County-level City, and District People's Governments shall commend and reward entities and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.10:
Article 10 The Municipal and County, County-level City, and District People's Governments and relevant departments shall organize public education on protection of the historic and cultural city and raise public awareness of protection and transmission.
Any entity or individual may dissuade or report conduct that damages or harms the historic and cultural city.
Chapter II — Protection List
articles.11: Article 11 Kunming shall maintain a protection list for the historic and cultural city. Protected matters approved and announced by people's governments at or above the county level shall be included in the list.
articles.12: Article 12 A matter meeting any of the following criteria may, after approval under the prescribed procedure, be designated and announced as a municipal-level protected matter: (1) an urban area that reflects a historical development process or the character of a particular development period; (2) a town or village with a relatively complete state of preservation, rich cultural content, distinctive characteristics, and features reflecting local ethnic traditions; (3) an area with abundant surviving remains that reflects the traditional character or ethnic or local characteristics of a historical period and is of a certain scale; (4) a building or structure reflecting historic character and local features, not announced as a protected cultural relic or registered as an immovable cultural relic, but having protection value; (5) a landscape environment that reflects the local natural landscape pattern and embodies the identity of the historic and cultural city; (6) a route closely connected with historic settlements or long used for settlement life, principal trade, or transport, and important to the formation and development of their layout; (7) environmental features such as ancient wells, walls, stone steps, and paving that reflect historic character and local features; or (8) another matter warranting designation as protected.
articles.13:
Article 13 The People's Government of the county, county-level city, or district where a proposed municipal-level protected matter is located shall organize its nomination. After expert review organized by the municipal natural resources and planning department and the municipal cultural relics department and public notice for no fewer than 10 working days, the Municipal People's Government shall approve and announce the designation.
Criteria for designation and nomination materials shall follow relevant State and provincial provisions by reference.
articles.14:
Article 14 Where a matter meets Article 12 but has not been nominated as a municipal-level protected matter, the municipal natural resources and planning department and cultural relics department shall require the local County, County-level City, or District People's Government to nominate it. If it still fails to do so, the departments may directly recommend to the Municipal People's Government that the matter be designated as a municipal-level protected matter.
A protected matter that has been nominated but not yet approved and announced shall not be demolished while the nomination is pending.
articles.15: Article 15 After a protected matter is announced, the People's Government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located shall conduct regular inspections and assessments, formulate protection measures based on the results, file them with the Municipal People's Government, and make them public.
articles.16: Article 16 Where the protection level or category of a protected matter changes, or it is seriously damaged or lost and has genuinely lost its protection significance, the People's Government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located shall submit any necessary adjustment or revocation for approval under the original approval procedure.
articles.17:
Article 17 The People's Governments of counties, county-level cities, and districts shall establish a dynamic monitoring mechanism for protected matters and regularly survey them within their jurisdictions.
A County, County-level City, or District People's Government shall place a matter meeting Article 12 under interim protection and notify the parties in writing. If it is not included as a municipal-level protected matter within 12 months after a party receives the notice, the interim-protection decision shall expire automatically.
During interim protection, no entity or individual may damage or demolish the matter. If interim protection causes loss to the lawful rights or interests of an entity or individual, the relevant government shall provide compensation.
articles.18:
Article 18 A County, County-level City, or District People's Government shall establish a geographic information system and protection-list archives for protection of the historic and cultural city within its jurisdiction, and file the archives with the municipal natural resources and planning department within 12 months after a matter is included in the list.
The archives shall include: (1) survey materials and basic information on the protected matter; (2) its cultural and artistic features, historic characteristics, historical development, historical events, anecdotes about notable persons, technical materials, and other information; (3) changes in title, current use, and approvals for construction within the protected area; (4) protection plans; (5) design and surveying materials; (6) written records, drawings, photographs, and video materials produced during repair, maintenance, relocation, or demolition; and (7) other materials requiring preservation.
Chapter III — Protection Planning
articles.19:
Article 19 The People's Government of the county, county-level city, or district where an approved and announced protected matter is located shall organize preparation of a protection plan or protection guidelines.
A protection plan for the historic and cultural city shall delineate the historic urban area. Separate protection plans shall be prepared for famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, and historic areas, and shall delineate their protected boundaries. An environmental coordination area may be delineated outside the historic urban area and protected boundaries as needed.
Protection plans shall meet applicable State requirements for planning. Where they concern landscape environments, cultural routes, or historic environmental features, they shall specify protection measures and controls.
Protection guidelines shall be prepared for historic buildings and include basic information, historical development, historic value, character, protected boundaries, measured drawings, protection measures, maintenance and repair requirements, use requirements, and requirements for protecting the historic environment.
articles.20:
Article 20 A protection plan for a municipal-level or county-level protected matter shall be approved and announced by the people's government at the corresponding level. Within 20 working days after approval, it shall be published on the government website and in major news media.
An approved protection plan shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, the authority organizing preparation shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and may prepare an amendment only after consent. The amended plan shall be submitted for approval under the original procedure.
articles.21:
Article 21 Before submitting a protection plan for approval, the authority organizing its preparation shall broadly solicit opinions from relevant departments, experts, and the public and may hold a hearing where necessary.
The materials submitted for approval shall include an account of opinions adopted and the reasons for not adopting others. Where a hearing was held, the hearing record shall also be included.
articles.22:
Article 22 Other specialized plans shall be coordinated with the approved protection plan for the historic and cultural city.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.23: Article 23 The protected areas of famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, and historic areas shall include core protected areas and construction control areas. The protected area of a historic building shall include the building itself and any necessary construction control area.
articles.24:
Article 24 The Municipal and County, County-level City, and District People's Governments shall provide integrated protection for the historic urban area, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, and historic areas.
Based on the protection plan, the County, County-level City, or District People's Government shall provide classified protection for buildings and structures within a protected area.
articles.25:
Article 25 The County, County-level City, or District People's Government shall promptly carry out emergency repairs to endangered buildings and structures on the protection list.
It shall scientifically assess the historic, scientific, and artistic value and state of preservation of historic buildings and specify repair and maintenance requirements without damaging their historic or artistic features, spatial organization, or distinctive character.
Protection of buildings of traditional character at their original sites is encouraged. Repairs and improvements shall not alter their original character category or significant character-defining elements.
articles.26: Article 26 The following activities are prohibited within a protected area: (1) hill cutting, quarrying, mining, or other activities damaging the traditional layout or historic character; (2) occupying gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, roads, or other areas designated for preservation in a protection plan; (3) constructing factories, warehouses, or similar facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances; (4) damaging, relocating, or demolishing a historic building without authorization; (5) carrying out blasting, earth removal, sand excavation, or water reclamation without authorization; (6) constructing buildings, structures, or other facilities that damage the traditional layout or historic character; (7) carving, posting on, or defacing a historic building; or (8) other activities that damage the original architectural style, landscape, view corridors, or environmental integrity.
articles.27: Article 27 An environmental coordination area shall protect the natural and cultural environment on which it depends. New or reconstructed buildings and structures shall be compatible with the character of that environment.
articles.28:
Article 28 New construction, expansion, or reconstruction of buildings and structures in a construction control area shall be compatible with the historic character in height, bulk, form, colors, and other respects.
New or reconstructed roads in such an area shall not damage the traditional layout or historic character. No new industrial enterprise that pollutes the environment may be established there; existing polluting industrial enterprises shall be closed or relocated in an orderly manner.
articles.29: Article 29 Within a core protected area, no new construction or expansion is permitted except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. Reconstruction of existing roads, buildings, and structures shall preserve or restore their original layout and historic character.
articles.30: Article 30 Before the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government approves necessary new construction or expansion of infrastructure or public service facilities within a core protected area, or demolition of buildings, structures, or other facilities other than historic buildings, it shall solicit opinions from the municipal natural resources and planning department, the municipal cultural relics department, the public, experts, and interested parties.
articles.31: Article 31 Outdoor advertisements are prohibited within core protected areas and on historic buildings.
articles.32: Article 32 Where public infrastructure in a protected area cannot meet current standards and codes, the competent housing and urban-rural development department shall determine a construction plan for the infrastructure. Where fire-safety facilities and access routes cannot meet current standards and codes, the fire and rescue agency of the Municipal, County, County-level City, or District People's Government shall formulate fire-safety safeguards together with the housing and urban-rural development department at the same level.
articles.33:
Article 33 A construction project shall, where possible, be sited away from historic buildings. If special circumstances make this impossible, protection at the original site shall be implemented to the greatest extent possible.
Before protecting a historic building at its original site, the developer shall determine protection measures and obtain approval from the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where the building is located. Before approval, opinions shall be solicited from the public, experts, and interested parties.
articles.34:
Article 34 The owner of a historic building shall maintain and repair it in accordance with the protection plan.
The Municipal and County, County-level City, and District People's Governments shall subsidize maintenance and repairs; the Municipal People's Government shall formulate detailed measures.
If a historic building is at risk of damage and its owner lacks the capacity to maintain and repair it, the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where it is located shall take protective measures. A damaged or lost historic building shall be restored where feasible.
articles.35: Article 35 External repair or decoration of a historic building, addition of facilities, or alteration of its structure or use shall be approved by the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where it is located. Before approval, opinions shall be solicited from the public, experts, and interested parties, and relevant procedures under laws and regulations shall be completed.
articles.36:
Article 36 The names of famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, historic areas, and historic buildings shall not be changed without approval.
The Municipal and County, County-level City, and District People's Governments shall place protection signs or markers on protected matters. No entity or individual may install, move, alter, or damage such signs or markers without authorization.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.37: Article 37 A State organ staff member who abuses official powers, neglects duties, or engages in favoritism or malpractice in protection of the historic and cultural city shall be sanctioned in accordance with the law. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.38: Article 38 Where a person violates Article 26(1) through (4), the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where the conduct occurs shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period. Any unlawful income shall be confiscated by the urban administration department. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take remedial measures by the deadline, the local government shall designate a capable entity to do so at the violator's expense. The violator shall compensate for any losses. If serious consequences result, the urban administration department shall impose: (1) for a violation of Article 26(1) through (3), a fine of RMB 500,000 to RMB 1,000,000 on an entity or RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 on an individual; or (2) for a violation of Article 26(4), a fine of RMB 200,000 to RMB 500,000 on an entity or RMB 100,000 to RMB 200,000 on an individual.
articles.39: Article 39 Where a person violates Article 26(5) or (8), the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where the conduct occurs shall order the person to stop and repair the damage within a specified period. If the person fails to do so by the deadline, the local government shall arrange the repairs at the violator's expense, and the urban administration department shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000.
articles.40: Article 40 Where a person violates Article 26(6), the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where the conduct occurs shall order correction and restoration of the original condition within a specified period. If the person fails to comply by the deadline, the local government shall demolish the construction in accordance with the law, and the urban administration department shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000.
articles.41: Article 41 Where a person violates Article 26(7), the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where the conduct occurs shall order restoration of the original condition or other remedial measures, and the urban administration department shall impose a fine of RMB 50.
articles.42: Article 42 Where a person violates Article 31, the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where the conduct occurs shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, the urban administration department shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 20,000 on an entity or RMB 500 to RMB 2,000 on an individual.
articles.43: Article 43 Where a person violates Article 36 by installing, moving, altering, or damaging a protection sign or marker without authorization, the relevant administrative department of the County, County-level City, or District People's Government where the conduct occurs shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, the urban administration department shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 1,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual.
articles.44:
Article 44 Violations of other provisions of these Regulations shall be penalized in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.45: Article 45 For purposes of these Regulations: (1) ‘building of traditional character’ means a building or structure within the historic urban area, a famous historic and cultural town or village, a historic town or village, a historic and cultural district, or a historic area, other than a protected cultural relic or historic building, that has existed for a certain period and has value or significance to the area's overall character; and (2) ‘historic town or village’ means a town or village not designated as a famous historic and cultural town or village by the State or Yunnan Province but approved and announced by the Municipal People's Government as a municipal-level protected matter.
articles.46: Article 46 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 May 2020. The Regulations of Kunming Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City, adopted at the sixth meeting of the Standing Committee of the 13th Kunming Municipal People's Congress on 28 October 2011 and approved at the 27th meeting of the Standing Committee of the 11th People's Congress of Yunnan Province on 22 November 2011, shall be repealed at the same time.

FBMCLI.10.9191449.title: Regulations of Nanping Municipality on the Protection of Jian'ou as a Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to protect Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city, preserve and carry forward outstanding history and culture, and coordinate protection and use of historic and cultural heritage with urban and rural development, in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the State Council Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and Traditional Villages, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to planning, protection, administration, and use of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city in Nanping Municipality.
The primary focus of protection is Jian'ou's historic urban area. Protected matters include its overall layout and character; historic and cultural districts and areas; historic buildings and buildings of traditional character; immovable cultural relics; intangible cultural heritage; and other matters protected under laws and regulations. The specific protected boundaries shall be determined and announced in the protection plan for Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city.
Where laws and regulations separately provide for protection of any of the foregoing matters, those provisions shall prevail.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, strict protection, appropriate use, coordinated development, and administration at the appropriate territorial level. It shall continue the city's historic continuity, preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage, and properly balance protection with development.
articles.4:
Article 4 The Nanping Municipal People's Government and its relevant competent departments shall strengthen guidance and supervision of protection of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city and provide policy support in accordance with the law.
The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall lead protection work, incorporate it into economic and social development plans, and include necessary funding in its budget.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall assist with routine inspections and reporting on protection of historic and cultural heritage within their jurisdictions.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist and guide the public in protecting historic and cultural heritage.
articles.5: Article 5 The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall establish a coordination body for protection of the historic and cultural city to coordinate, oversee, and advance protection work and address major related issues. Its day-to-day work shall be handled by the Jian'ou municipal housing and urban-rural development department.
articles.6:
Article 6 The Jian'ou municipal housing and urban-rural development department, together with the culture and cultural relics department at the same level, shall be the competent authority for protection of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city and shall be responsible for its protection and administration.
The departments responsible for development and reform, natural resources, ecology and environment, transport, urban administration, emergency management, market regulation, and fire and rescue shall perform related protection and administration duties according to their respective responsibilities.
articles.7:
Article 7 All entities and individuals have a duty to protect the historic and cultural city in accordance with the law and may dissuade or report conduct violating these Regulations. Relevant departments shall promptly handle reports and provide feedback.
Entities and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection through donations, funding, investment, technical services, volunteer services, and other means.
Chapter II — Planning and Protection List
articles.8:
Article 8 The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of a protection plan for Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city in accordance with the law and incorporate it into territorial spatial planning.
The Jian'ou municipal urban and rural planning department shall prepare detailed plans based on the protection plan.
Planning shall scientifically assess Jian'ou's historic and cultural value, establish protection objectives and principles, identify protected matters and priorities, and specify protection strategies and requirements.
articles.9: Article 9 The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall supervise and inspect implementation of the protection plan, establish a special assessment mechanism, assess protection conditions annually, and report on protection work to the Standing Committee of the people's congress at the same level every five years.
articles.10: Article 10 Jian'ou shall maintain a protection list for the historic and cultural city. The list shall specify each protected matter's name, category, location, historic and cultural value, protection level, protected boundaries, responsible entity, and other relevant particulars.
articles.11:
Article 11 Based on surveys of historic and cultural resources or applications from entities and individuals, the Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall determine the protection list in accordance with applicable designation criteria and procedures and make it public.
The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall formulate and publish criteria and procedures for inclusion on the protection list.
articles.12:
Article 12 Within three months after a protected matter is placed on the protection list, the Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall install an appropriate protection sign in a conspicuous location, indicating the protected boundaries and requirements.
No entity or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection sign without authorization.
articles.13: Article 13 The competent authority for protection of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city shall, together with the urban and rural planning department at the same level, collect digital information and survey and document protected matters on the protection list, establish a protection database, and improve monitoring and administration.
articles.14:
Article 14 A matter not yet included in the protection list but preliminarily determined by the Jian'ou Municipal People's Government to have protection value may be designated for interim protection. Within seven working days after designation, the owner and user shall receive an interim-protection notice specifying required protective measures.
If the matter is not included in the protection list within one year after service of the notice, interim protection shall expire automatically.
During interim protection, no entity or individual may damage the matter. If interim protection causes loss to the lawful rights or interests of an entity or individual, the Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall provide compensation in accordance with the law.
Chapter III — Protection and Administration
Section 1 — Protection and Administration of the Historic Urban Area
articles.15: Article 15 The historic urban area shall preserve the urban spatial pattern of ‘inner and outer double walls,’ the checkerboard pattern of ‘36 streets and 72 lanes,’ and the historic landscape layout of ‘three hills, six waters, seven bridges, and nine city gates.’ Urban construction shall not damage the traditional layout of the historic urban area.
articles.16:
Article 16 The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall strengthen repair and reinforcement of the towers above the ancient city gates, establish an intelligent monitoring system, and maintain their safety and integrity.
Within the protected areas of the ancient city-gate towers, it is prohibited to install facilities or equipment unrelated to protection, carry out construction, blasting, drilling, or excavation without authorization, or use the towers for commercial or production activities without authorization.
articles.17:
Article 17 The city's historic axes shall retain their existing scale, alignment, and cross-sectional form. The height, bulk, style, colors, and other features of new buildings on both sides of an axis road shall be compatible with its traditional character.
New buildings in the historic urban area shall not damage the alignment or visual corridors of the intersecting axes centered on the Drum Tower.
articles.18:
Article 18 Historic and cultural districts and historic areas shall preserve their traditional spatial layout and structural form and continue the historic information associated with their traditional character.
Within their protected areas, no new construction or expansion is permitted except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. Highways, railways, high-voltage power lines, oil pipelines, and main gas pipelines shall not pass through such protected areas; existing facilities shall be relocated gradually in accordance with plans.
articles.19:
Article 19 Historic streets and lanes shall retain their original urban fabric and layout and receive graded protection.
It is prohibited to damage the alignment, scale, or traditional frontage characteristics of historic streets and lanes specified in the protection plan.
The names of historic streets and lanes shall not be changed without authorization.
articles.20:
Article 20 The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall restore historic river and lake systems, recover their traditional layout, strengthen water-pollution control, and improve water quality.
No person may fill in or occupy their channels or water bodies, or alter their original form, without authorization.
articles.21:
Article 21 The historic urban area shall be divided into character-protection areas, character-control areas, and character-coordination areas, with controls applied in each area according to protection requirements.
Buildings in the historic urban area shall use or draw upon traditional colors, materials, and forms and preserve the traditional character.
articles.22:
Article 22 The height of new buildings in the historic urban area shall be strictly controlled and regulated by area in accordance with the protection plan.
A new building adjacent to a protected building—including a protected cultural relic at any level, an ungraded immovable cultural relic, a historic building, or a building of traditional character—shall not exceed the height of that protected building.
articles.23:
Article 23 The historic urban area shall establish urban view corridors on a scientific basis and specify controls to improve the urban spatial form.
Construction within a view corridor shall be strictly controlled. A landscape-impact analysis shall be prepared before a new building is constructed within a view corridor.
articles.24: Article 24 The landscape pattern of mountains and waters forming the setting of the historic urban area shall be strictly protected. Within the protected area of that setting, no person may excavate hills, fell trees, damage vegetation, or fill in water bodies without authorization.
articles.25:
Article 25 Underground archaeological zones shall preserve the historic character and original topography of archaeological sites.
Within their protected areas, engineering construction unrelated to site protection and other activities damaging the sites are prohibited.
articles.26:
Article 26 In accordance with the protection plan, the Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall improve infrastructure and public services in the historic urban area and increase publicly accessible open spaces.
Priority shall be given to public transport, walking, and cycling. New major through-roads, transport interchanges, and large parking facilities shall be located outside the historic urban area.
Infrastructure in historic and cultural districts shall use quiet, small-scale, and concealed designs. Electricity, water supply and drainage, communications, and other utility lines shall be installed underground or otherwise concealed.
articles.27:
Article 27 The historic urban area shall establish disaster-prevention and mitigation, safety-management, and emergency-response mechanisms; prepare emergency plans for sudden incidents; and strengthen response capacity.
Historic and cultural districts shall have dedicated fire stations equipped with small, appropriate firefighting facilities and equipment and shall establish community fire-safety systems.
articles.28:
Article 28 The following conduct is prohibited within the protection area of the historic and cultural city: (1) hill cutting, quarrying, sand excavation, mining, forest clearing, or other activities damaging the traditional layout or historic character; (2) occupying gardens, green spaces, ancient or notable trees, river and lake systems, roads, or other areas designated for preservation; (3) constructing factories, warehouses, docks, or similar facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances; (4) constructing buildings, structures, or other facilities that damage the traditional layout or historic character; (5) installing advertisements, signs, or posters that damage or impair the area's character; (6) dumping garbage or discharging wastewater, cooking fumes, or other pollutants in public places; (7) damaging objects or places that form part of intangible cultural heritage; or (8) other conduct prohibited by laws and regulations.
Section 2 — Protection and Administration of Historic Buildings
articles.29: Article 29 The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of protection guidelines and technical repair specifications for historic buildings, publish them, notify owners, users, and property-management entities in writing of protection and use requirements, and regularly provide technical guidance and training.
articles.30:
Article 30 The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall maintain, repair, and use it in accordance with the protection guidelines and technical repair specifications.
The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government may provide subsidies from protection funds for maintenance and repairs.
If a historic building is at risk of damage and the responsible person lacks the capacity to maintain and repair it, the Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall take protective measures.
For a State-owned historic building, the manager or user shall be responsible for protection. For a non-State-owned historic building, the owner, user, or manager shall be responsible, subject to any other agreement on responsibility. If the responsible person cannot be identified or located, the Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall designate one.
articles.31:
Article 31 A construction project shall, where possible, be sited away from historic buildings. If special circumstances make this impossible, the developer shall obtain approval from the Jian'ou municipal urban and rural planning department acting together with the competent authority for protection of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city, and shall protect the building at its original site.
If protection at the original site is impossible because of public-interest needs or natural causes such as geological disasters and relocation or demolition is necessary, approval shall be obtained from the relevant authorities in accordance with the law.
Where demolition of a historic building is approved, the developer shall mark and document it and preserve relevant materials, and reconstruct it when conditions permit.
The developer shall include costs for original-site protection, relocation, or demolition under this Article in the construction project budget.
articles.32:
Article 32 A proposal for external repair or decoration of a historic building, addition of facilities, or alteration of its structure or use shall be submitted to the competent authority for protection of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city for approval, and related procedures shall be completed in accordance with the law.
An entity undertaking repair work on a historic building shall employ technical workers skilled in such repairs.
articles.33:
Article 33 Repairs and reconstruction of historic buildings shall, where possible, use original building components and materials and traditional construction methods, techniques, materials, and motifs, so as to continue the area's traditional architectural character.
The competent authority for protection of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city shall strengthen supervision and administration of the recovery, storage, protection, and reuse of historic building components.
The person responsible for protection shall properly preserve components removed or replaced during repairs. If proper storage is not possible, the competent authority may designate a State-owned cultural relics collection institution or cultural relics protection agency to keep them in custody.
articles.34: Article 34 Use of a historic building shall be compatible with its historic value and internal structure. No person may change its principal structure, principal floor plan, or exterior appearance without authorization, endanger the safety of the building or its ancillary facilities, or damage its original character.
articles.35: Article 35 Before carrying out urban renewal or renovation, organizing project construction, or conducting land acquisition and demolition, the Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall survey and assess buildings over 50 years old in the area concerned. A building meeting the criteria for a historic building shall be announced and protected as such. No decision to expropriate a house may be made before the survey and assessment have been completed.
articles.36:
Article 36 No entity or individual may: (1) carve or deface a historic building; (2) store flammable, explosive, or corrosive substances inside it; (3) dismantle or transfer its components without authorization; (4) carry out external repairs or decoration, add facilities, or alter its structure or use without authorization; (5) alter its original height, bulk, exterior appearance, or colors without authorization; (6) relocate or demolish it without authorization; or (7) otherwise damage it.
Chapter IV — Transmission and Use
articles.37: Article 37 Reasonable use and orderly public access to various forms of historic and cultural heritage are encouraged and supported. The Jian'ou Municipal People's Government shall establish a positive or negative list for projects involving the transmission and use of such heritage, specifying projects that are encouraged or supported and those that are restricted or prohibited.
articles.38:
Article 38 Display of local culture and development of distinctive industries—including traditional residence, specialty commerce, leisure experiences, and cultural tourism—are encouraged in the historic urban area, historic and cultural districts, and historic areas.
Use of historic buildings for compatible activities such as museums, exhibition halls, memorial halls, traditional workshops, and distinctive homestays is encouraged.
articles.39:
Article 39 Training traditional craftspeople, transmitting traditional crafts, and producing traditional materials related to protection of the historic and cultural city are supported.
The competent authority for protection of Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city shall, together with the human resources and social security department at the same level, organize professional training and skills certification for traditional craftspeople and establish a grading system for them.
articles.40:
Article 40 Long-term residents are encouraged to continue living at their original locations in accordance with protection requirements. They are supported in operating local specialty handicraft businesses and other activities that help preserve and transmit the historic city's original form and way of life.
Protection of time-honored brands at their original sites and in their original form is encouraged.
articles.41:
Article 41 Entities and individuals are encouraged to research, document, and organize traditional culture, including Jian'ou place-name culture, dialects, notable figures, food, tea, liquor, bamboo, and distinctive folk customs.
Representative transmitters of representative intangible cultural heritage projects are encouraged and supported to teach apprentices and transmit their skills, and training for intangible cultural heritage transmitters shall be strengthened.
articles.42:
Article 42 Entities and individuals are encouraged to open protected matters to the public free of charge where conditions permit.
The use of modern science and technology to present and administer protected matters is encouraged.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.43: Article 43 Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.44: Article 44 Where a person violates Article 12 by installing, moving, altering, or damaging a protection sign for a protected matter without authorization, the Jian'ou urban administration department shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 1,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual.
articles.45: Article 45 Where a person violates Article 19(2) by damaging the alignment, scale, or traditional frontage characteristics of historic streets and lanes designated in the protection plan, the Jian'ou urban administration department shall order restoration of the original condition within a specified period. If serious consequences result, it shall impose a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual.
articles.46: Article 46 Where the person responsible for protection of a historic building fails to maintain, repair, or use it in accordance with its protection guidelines and technical repair specifications, in violation of Article 30(1), the Jian'ou urban administration department shall order the person to stop the unlawful conduct and restore the original condition within a specified period. If serious consequences result, it shall impose a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual.
articles.47:
Article 47 Where a State organ or its staff fails to perform oversight and administration duties in protecting Jian'ou as a historic and cultural city, fails to investigate unlawful conduct after discovering it, or otherwise abuses official powers, neglects duties, or engages in favoritism or malpractice, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the law. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.48: Article 48 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2026.

FBMCLI.10.1424720.title: Regulations of Chaozhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to strengthen protection and administration of the historic and cultural city, preserve and protect outstanding historic and cultural heritage, and promote coordinated urban and rural development and social and cultural development, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to the planning, protection, administration, and use of the historic and cultural city within this Municipality's administrative area.
The protected area includes the ancient urban area of Chaozhou; famous historic and cultural towns and villages; historic and cultural districts; traditional towns, streets, and villages; traditional places; historic buildings; cultural relics; traditional place names; intangible cultural heritage; and other matters.
Protection of cultural relics, traditional place names, intangible cultural heritage, and other matters within the protected area shall be governed by relevant laws and regulations.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, strict protection, differentiated administration, and appropriate use; preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage and the natural and cultural landscapes connected with it; and properly balance economic and social development with heritage protection.
articles.4:
Article 4 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration within their jurisdictions.
Grassroots self-governing organizations shall assist the people's governments in protecting the historic and cultural city.
articles.5:
Article 5 The urban and rural planning department shall organize preparation of protection plans and surveys of historic and cultural districts and historic buildings, arrange their maintenance and repairs, and implement these Regulations together with the cultural relics department.
The cultural relics department shall protect, supervise, and administer matters relating to the historic and cultural city as provided by laws and regulations and these Regulations.
The urban administration and comprehensive law-enforcement department shall inspect and supervise unlawful planning and construction conduct relating to protection and exercise administrative penalty powers under laws and regulations and these Regulations.
The departments responsible for development and reform, housing and urban-rural development, education, ethnic and religious affairs, public security, fire safety, civil affairs, finance, land and natural resources, tourism, public utilities, landscaping, real estate, archives, and other relevant matters shall perform specific supervision and administration duties within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
Article 6 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall incorporate protection and supervision of the historic and cultural city into economic and social development plans and include protection funding in their respective budgets.
They shall establish special funds for protection, to be used for surveys of protected matters, preparation of protection lists and plans, maintenance and repair subsidies, commendations and awards, academic research, and public education.
articles.7: Article 7 The Municipal Committee for Protection and Construction of the Historic and Cultural City shall review, coordinate, and guide the following major protection matters: (1) protection plans and major policies and measures; (2) the contents of the protection list and proposed adjustments; (3) coordination and guidance in addressing major emergencies and review of solutions to major protection issues; and (4) other major matters relating to protection.
articles.8: Article 8 The Municipal People's Government shall establish an expert roster for protection of the historic and cultural city. Experts in planning, architecture, culture, cultural relics, history, land, society, economics, law, and other fields shall assess or review major protection matters and policies and provide advisory opinions.
articles.9:
Article 9 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall strengthen research, publicity, and education on protection of the historic and cultural city. Through traditional-culture research, publications, training, exhibitions, media publicity, and other means, they shall promote outstanding local culture and raise public awareness.
The education department shall include local history and culture in extracurricular education for primary and secondary school students and promote transmission of outstanding local culture.
articles.10:
Article 10 Each year, the Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall inspect and assess protection work and report on it to the Standing Committee of the people's congress at the same level.
The standing committees of the people's congresses at the municipal and county (district) levels shall supervise the corresponding people's governments through law-enforcement inspections, hearing and deliberating special work reports, and other means.
articles.11:
Article 11 Any entity or individual may submit opinions and suggestions on protection of the historic and cultural city and report conduct damaging it.
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate through social funds, donations, volunteer activities, and other means.
Entities and individuals are encouraged to collect and organize traditional place names, historical documents, historic images, and other materials and to provide related information or physical materials to archives departments.
The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall commend and reward entities and individuals that make outstanding contributions to protection.
Chapter II — Protection Plans and Protection List
articles.12:
Article 12 Preparation and approval of protection plans for the historic and cultural city, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, and historic and cultural districts shall follow relevant laws and regulations.
The County (District) People's Government where a traditional town or street, traditional village, traditional place, or historic building is located shall organize preparation of its protection plan and submit it to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall supervise and inspect implementation of all protection plans and assess the state of protected matters.
articles.13:
Article 13 Protection plans for the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, traditional towns and streets, traditional villages and places, and historic buildings shall include: (1) protection principles, protected matters, and boundaries; (2) protection measures, development intensity, and construction controls; (3) requirements for preserving the traditional layout and historic character; and (4) phased implementation plans.
Protection plans for famous towns and villages and historic and cultural districts shall delineate core protected areas and construction control areas. Areas with a relatively complete traditional layout and historic character and a concentration of historic buildings or buildings of traditional character shall be designated as core protected areas, with construction control areas outside them.
Protection plans for historic buildings shall delineate core protected areas, including the building itself, its enclosed courtyard, and necessary fire-access routes. A necessary construction control area may be designated in a zone coordinating the historic building with its surroundings.
articles.14: Article 14 To protect the traditional layout of Chaozhou's ancient urban area, the protection plan for the historic and cultural city shall: (1) designate as a Han River natural-landscape character area the riverfront along both banks of the Han River, from the Egret Crossing in Autumn Wind ferry in the north to the north end of Fenghuang Islet and Fenghuang Pagoda in the south, including a 20-to-50-meter-wide area along both banks; (2) administer the natural-landscape character areas of Hulu Mountain, Jinshan Mountain, and Bijia Mountain as part of West Lake Scenic Area; (3) designate the West Lake section of Huancheng West Road, Huancheng North Road, Huancheng East Road, Wenxing Road, Zhongshan Road, and Jiuxian Lane as tree-lined-road character areas; (4) designate Taiping Road, Xima Road, Yi'an Road, Shangdongping Road, Weixing 1st Road, Taichang Road, Tangping Road, Dongmen Street, and other streets and lanes as traditional arcade-house character areas; and (5) designate lanes with the characteristic form of traditional urban blocks and lanes as traditional-residence historic character areas, with boundaries determined by the municipal urban and rural planning department in accordance with the protection plan.
articles.15: Article 15 The protection plan shall highlight Chaozhou's historic and cultural significance and character, express the distinctive features of the historic and cultural city, and follow the themes of the ancient urban area's protection framework: (1) ‘Renowned Region by the Lingnan Sea’ centers on protecting the ‘three mountains, one river, one city, and eight scenic views’ landscape pattern and presenting the ancient city's traditional layout and natural landscape; (2) ‘Ancient Prefecture of the South’ centers on protecting protected cultural relics at all levels, developing and using Tang- and Song-era remains, and highlighting the historic character of the prefectural city; (3) ‘Zou and Lu of the Seaside’ centers on protecting historic and cultural districts, expressing folk life, and promoting traditional Chaozhou culture and customs; and (4) ‘Trading Port and Overseas-Chinese Homeland’ centers on protecting representative modern buildings and revolutionary historic sites, promoting the patriotism and attachment to their hometown of Chaozhou people overseas, and reflecting Chaozhou's history as a trading port open to the outside world.
articles.16:
Article 16 Based on the overall urban plan and the protection plan for the historic and cultural city, and in light of actual conditions, the Municipal People's Government shall formulate an annual implementation plan for protection of Chaozhou's ancient urban area.
The annual plan shall specify objectives, projects, and funding sources for renewal of key areas, cultural tourism development, improvement of public facilities, and renovation of old or dangerous buildings.
articles.17: Article 17 A town, subdistrict, village, or district within this Municipality that has not been announced as a famous historic and cultural town or village or a historic and cultural district may be designated by the Municipal People's Government as a traditional town or street, traditional village, or traditional place if it meets any of the following criteria: (1) it is an area of a certain scale with a relatively complete traditional layout and historic character; (2) it is distinctive and representative of ethnic or local characteristics during a particular historical period; or (3) it contains historic and cultural remains and is of a certain scale.
articles.18:
Article 18 A building or structure that has existed for at least 40 years and has not been announced as a protected cultural relic or registered as an immovable cultural relic may be designated as a historic building by the Municipal or County (District) People's Government if it meets any of the following criteria: (1) its architectural style, construction methods, or engineering techniques have artistic features or research value and its structure and layout are substantially intact; (2) it clearly reflects Chaozhou's local architectural features or distinctive features from another region; (3) it is associated with a major historical event or is representative of the history of Chaozhou's urban development or an industry and reflects its period, with its structure and layout substantially intact; (4) it is representative industrial or commercial architecture or a site of religious or clan worship; (5) it is near a protected cultural relic and forms part of its setting, or forms a continuous group with traditional architecture; or (6) it is directly related to the protection and transmission of intangible cultural heritage.
A building or structure that has existed for at least 30 but fewer than 40 years and meets one of the foregoing criteria may also be designated if it has special historic, cultural, commemorative, or educational significance. Before designation, the urban and rural planning department shall consult the cultural relics department at the same level, the public, and the owner, user, or entrusted manager and organize expert review.
articles.19:
Article 19 The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection list for the historic and cultural city, including: (1) Chaozhou's ancient urban area; (2) famous historic and cultural towns and villages and historic and cultural districts; (3) traditional towns and streets, traditional villages, and traditional places; and (4) historic buildings.
The list shall identify each protected matter and its boundaries and state its name, location, area, date of construction, historic value, and other particulars, with geographic coordinates and a corresponding boundary map.
A County (District) People's Government may establish its own protection list and administrative system as needed.
The protection list shall be made public.
articles.20:
Article 20 Protected matters designated by the State, provincial, or Municipal People's Government shall be included directly in the protection list.
For towns, villages, districts, buildings, and structures with protection value found during surveys but not yet listed, the municipal or county (district) urban and rural planning department shall consult the cultural relics department at the same level and the owner, user, or entrusted manager; organize an inspection and expert review; and, if protection value is confirmed, initiate the procedure for designation as a famous historic and cultural town or village, historic and cultural district, traditional town or street, traditional village, traditional place, or historic building, as applicable.
Any entity or individual discovering a town, village, district, building, or structure with protection value may report it to the municipal or county (district) urban and rural planning department. Within 10 working days after receiving the report, that department shall initiate the designation procedure under the preceding paragraph.
A protected matter shall be included in the protection list after designation by the State, provincial, or Municipal People's Government.
articles.21: Article 21 Where a protected matter is lost or damaged due to force majeure, or a statutory reason requires adjustment of the protection list, the municipal urban and rural planning department and cultural relics department shall propose an adjustment. After expert review, public notice, and other procedures, the adjustment shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
articles.22:
Article 22 The municipal urban and rural planning department shall establish archives for protected matters on the protection list, and relevant entities and individuals shall cooperate. The archives shall include: (1) information obtained through surveys; (2) cultural, artistic, and historic features, historical development, events, anecdotes about notable persons, technical materials, and other information; (3) current use and changes in title; (4) protection plans; (5) design and surveying materials; (6) written records, drawings, photographs, and video materials produced during repairs, relocation, or demolition; and (7) other materials requiring preservation.
Chapter III — Protection Responsibilities and Measures
articles.23:
Article 23 A system of persons responsible for protection shall apply to the historic and cultural city.
The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protection of Chaozhou's ancient urban area.
The County (District) People's Government where a famous historic and cultural town, village, or district is located shall be responsible; if it spans counties or districts, the Municipal People's Government shall designate the responsible government.
The township or town people's government or subdistrict office where a traditional town or street, traditional village, or traditional place is located shall be responsible. If it spans townships, towns, or subdistricts, the relevant County (District) People's Government shall designate the responsible person; if it spans counties or districts, the Municipal People's Government shall do so.
articles.24:
Article 24 After a historic building is included in the protection list, the County (District) People's Government shall designate the person responsible for its protection and notify that person in writing of the applicable management requirements. If an entity or individual objects to the designation, the County (District) People's Government shall decide whether to adjust it in light of actual conditions.
The responsible person shall be determined as follows: (1) for a State-owned historic building, the entrusted manager shall be responsible; if there is none, the user shall be responsible; if neither can be identified, the housing department shall be responsible; (2) for a non-State-owned historic building, the owner shall be responsible; if the owner cannot be located or contacted or title is unclear, the entrusted manager shall be responsible; if there is no such manager, the user shall be responsible; and if none of the owner, manager, or user can be identified, the housing department shall be responsible.
articles.25: Article 25 The Municipal People's Government, as the person responsible for protection of Chaozhou's ancient urban area, shall: (1) formulate relevant policies and normative documents for its protection and appropriate use; (2) prepare annual implementation plans, secure funding, and advance protection, improvement, and use in an orderly manner; (3) coordinate development of public services and municipal utilities within the ancient urban area; (4) encourage and support collection, organization, and research concerning traditional Chaozhou culture; (5) regulate traditional folk activities and create a favorable historic and cultural atmosphere; and (6) perform other duties prescribed by laws and regulations.
articles.26: Article 26 The person responsible for protection of a famous historic and cultural town or village or historic and cultural district shall: (1) implement the protection plan and preserve the traditional layout, historic character, spatial scale, and related natural landscape and environment; (2) improve infrastructure, public services, and living conditions while preserving the scale and character of streets; (3) conduct routine inspections, promptly stop conduct endangering heritage, and notify the relevant administrative department; (4) organize festivals and folk activities and promote outstanding traditional culture; and (5) perform other duties specified by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.27: Article 27 The person responsible for protection of a traditional town or street, traditional village, or traditional place shall: (1) inform the public about protected matters and requirements and implement the protection plan; (2) conduct routine inspections, promptly stop conduct endangering heritage, and notify the relevant administrative department; (3) keep the protected area clean and orderly and assist relevant departments in ensuring proper operation of public fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; (4) establish a community service station to assist local residents, provide information and consultation, and collect their opinions and suggestions; and (5) perform other duties specified by the Municipal or County (District) People's Government.
