articles.28: Article 28 The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall: (1) preserve its original height, bulk, exterior appearance, and colors; (2) preserve the integrity of its traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, and historic environmental features; (3) ensure structural safety, promptly take measures to eliminate hazards, and report them to the relevant administrative department; (4) ensure proper operation of fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; (5) use the building lawfully and reasonably in accordance with the protection plan; and (6) comply with other requirements under laws and regulations. Repairs shall comply with these protection duties. When transferring or leasing a historic building, the transferor or lessor shall notify the transferee or lessee of the protection and repair requirements.
articles.29: Article 29 The Municipal or County (District) People's Government may procure services from social organizations qualified in tourism development, community services, or property management and entrust them with relevant duties of the person responsible for protection of a State-owned historic building.
articles.30:
Article 30 No entity or individual may demolish a historic building included in the protection list without authorization. A construction project shall, where possible, be sited away from a historic building; if special circumstances make this impossible, protection at the original site shall be implemented to the greatest extent possible. The developer shall determine protection measures in advance and obtain approval from the municipal or county (district) urban and rural planning department.
If a building is so seriously damaged that repair is impracticable, or demolition is genuinely necessary for the public interest, the developer shall arrange expert review and prepare detailed measured drawings, records, and archival materials. After expert review and preparation of remedial measures organized by the municipal or county (district) urban and rural planning department together with the cultural relics department, the municipal urban and rural planning department shall submit the matter to the provincial urban and rural planning department and cultural relics department for approval in accordance with the law.
Within 30 working days after demolition is approved, the developer shall prepare records including measured drawings and images of the historic building and submit them to the municipal or county (district) urban and rural planning department.
The developer shall include costs for protection at the original site, relocation, or demolition in the construction project budget.
articles.31: Article 31 Based on the protection plan for a historic building, the urban and rural planning department shall prepare protection guidelines and notify the responsible person in writing. The guidelines shall include: (1) basic information, protection category, distinctive character, and related environmental features; (2) controls for core protected and construction control areas; (3) protection, maintenance, and repair requirements; (4) guidance on appropriate use; and (5) other requirements of the protection plan.
articles.32:
Article 32 The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall maintain and repair it in accordance with the protection plan and protection guidelines. The urban and rural planning department shall provide information and technical guidance as needed.
If a building is at risk and the responsible person fails to carry out required maintenance or repairs, the township or town people's government or subdistrict office shall notify that person to perform the duty. If the responsible person has the capacity but fails to act, the urban and rural planning department may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at that person's expense. If the responsible person lacks the capacity, the Municipal or County (District) People's Government shall take protective measures.
A responsible person that performs maintenance and repairs in accordance with the protection plan and guidelines may receive a subsidy from the Municipal or County (District) People's Government based on the area, extent, and quality of the work.
The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall formulate detailed subsidy measures.
articles.33:
Article 33 Within a core protected area of a famous historic and cultural town or village or historic and cultural district, no construction unrelated to protection is permitted except for necessary infrastructure and public-benefit public service facilities.
New construction, expansion, or reconstruction in a construction control area shall comply with the protection plan or protection measures and shall not damage the traditional layout or historic character.
An entity or individual undertaking such work in a core protected or construction control area shall apply to the municipal urban and rural planning department and submit a specific plan addressing historic and cultural protection. Before granting planning permission, that department shall seek written opinions from the municipal cultural relics department and, where necessary, organize expert review and solicit public opinions.
articles.34: Article 34 The following activities are prohibited within the protected areas of the historic and cultural city, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, and historic buildings: (1) hill cutting, quarrying, or mining; (2) occupying gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, roads, or other areas designated for preservation in the protection plan; (3) constructing factories, warehouses, or similar facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances; (4) carving or defacing historic buildings; or (5) damaging the traditional layout or historic character of protected matters or engaging in other activities likely to damage them.
articles.35:
Article 35 Protection signs shall be placed on the protected areas of the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, traditional towns and streets, traditional villages and places, historic buildings, immovable cultural relics, and other protected matters. A sign shall state the name, number, location, period of existence, protection category, cultural information, and other particulars of the protected matter.
The Municipal People's Government shall establish a uniform sign design. The County (District) People's Government shall arrange installation within 30 working days after the matter is included in the protection list. No entity or individual may install, move, cover, alter, or damage a sign without authorization.
Where the State or province provides otherwise, those provisions shall prevail.
articles.36:
Article 36 A protection plan shall be prepared for the following activities within the protected areas of the historic and cultural city, famous historic and cultural towns, or famous villages, so as to protect the traditional layout, historic character, and historic buildings: (1) changing the natural state of gardens, green spaces, river or lake systems, and similar features; (2) filming or holding a large public event in a core protected area; or (3) other activities affecting the traditional layout, historic character, or historic buildings.
The municipal or county (district) urban and rural planning department, together with the cultural relics department at the same level, shall approve the protection plan and the applicant shall complete related procedures under applicable laws and regulations.
Chapter IV — Appropriate Use
articles.37: Article 37 Use of the historic and cultural city shall be compatible with its historic, artistic, scientific, social, and cultural values, take economic benefits into account, and coordinate protection, use, and transmission.
articles.38: Article 38 The Municipal People's Government shall establish an information management system for the historic and cultural city and publish information and guidance on appropriate use of the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, traditional towns and streets, traditional villages and places, and historic buildings, providing a platform for enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals to undertake or participate in appropriate use.
articles.39: Article 39 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments may promote appropriate use of the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, traditional towns and streets, traditional villages and places, and State-owned historic buildings by: (1) supporting appropriate-use activities through funding, simplified procedures, fee reductions, and incentives for development rights; (2) selecting entities and individuals that meet protection and use requirements through public tender or other means; (3) establishing management and operating companies or organizations in accordance with the law; and (4) acquiring use rights in non-State-owned immovable cultural relics or State-owned historic buildings through leasing, entrusted management, or other means.
articles.40:
Article 40 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall encourage organization, research, and use of historic and cultural resources, identification of regional cultural characteristics, development of regional brands, and creation of cultural and artistic products with distinctive local features.
Subject to the protection plan and requirements for building structure, fire safety, and other administration, persons responsible for protection may make appropriate use of historic buildings. They shall strictly protect the historic features and intangible cultural content of those buildings.
articles.41:
Article 41 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall encourage and support entities and individuals in appropriate use of protected matters, including: (1) establishing museums, exhibition halls, and memorial halls in historic and cultural cities, towns, villages, and districts; (2) establishing intangible cultural heritage master studios, cultural and creative venues, and craft display and exchange centers; (3) establishing educational and experiential bases for primary and secondary school students; (4) opening cultural inns in historic areas, traditional towns and streets, or traditional villages; (5) conducting research on local traditional culture and folk-art performances; (6) making, displaying, or selling traditional arts and crafts in protected areas and traditional places; and (7) other forms of protective use.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.42: Article 42 Where a State organ commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations, the Municipal or County (District) People's Government or the relevant competent department shall order correction and impose administrative sanctions in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel. If a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued: (1) failing to organize preparation or amendment of a protection plan or designation or adjustment of the protection list under statutory procedures; (2) failing to perform approval duties under statutory procedures or the protection plan; (3) failing to supervise and inspect the condition of protected matters or inadequately supervise approved renovation or use; (4) failing to accept reports or complaints or investigate violations in accordance with the law; (5) abusing official powers, neglecting duties, or engaging in favoritism or malpractice; or (6) other violations prescribed by laws and regulations.
articles.43: Article 43 Where a person demolishes a historic building on the protection list without authorization, in violation of Article 30, the municipal or county (district) urban administration and comprehensive law-enforcement department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period. If the person fails to do so by the deadline, the department may designate a capable entity to do so at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, the department shall impose a fine of RMB 200,000 to RMB 500,000 on an entity or RMB 100,000 to RMB 200,000 on an individual. The violator shall compensate for any losses in accordance with the law.
articles.44:
Article 44 Where a person violates Article 34(1), (2), or (3), the municipal or county (district) urban administration and comprehensive law-enforcement department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 500,000 to RMB 1,000,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 on an individual. The violator shall compensate for any losses.
Where a person violates Article 34(4), the department shall order restoration of the original condition or other remedial measures and impose a fine of RMB 50.
articles.45: Article 45 Where a person violates Article 35 by installing, moving, altering, or damaging a protection sign without authorization, the municipal or county (district) urban administration and comprehensive law-enforcement department shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 1,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual.
articles.46:
Article 46 Where a person undertakes any of the following activities without approval by the municipal or county (district) urban and rural planning department together with the cultural relics department at the same level, in violation of Article 36, the urban administration and comprehensive law-enforcement department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual. The violator shall compensate for any losses: (1) changing the natural state of gardens, green spaces, or river and lake systems; (2) filming or holding a large public event; (3) demolishing a building, structure, or facility other than a historic building; (4) externally repairing or decorating a historic building, adding facilities, or changing its structure or use; or (5) other activities affecting the traditional layout, historic character, or historic buildings.
The same penalties shall apply where an entity or individual obtains approval for such an activity but damages the traditional layout, historic character, or a historic building while carrying it out.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.47:
Article 47 These Regulations shall take effect on 15 November 2017.

Regulations cited in this document
Central regulations
Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages (2017 Revision)
Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China (2015 Revision)

FBMCLI.10.1681552.title: Regulations of Luoyang Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to strengthen protection and administration of Luoyang as a historic and cultural city and preserve and promote fine traditional Chinese culture, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to planning, protection, administration, and use of the historic and cultural city within this Municipality's administrative area.
Matters not provided for in these Regulations shall be governed by relevant laws and regulations.
articles.3:
Article 3 Matters protected as part of the historic and cultural city include the historic urban area; famous historic and cultural towns, villages, and districts; areas with traditional character; historic buildings; cultural relics; ancient or notable trees; intangible cultural heritage; and other matters.
Protection of cultural relics, ancient or notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, and other matters within the protected area shall be governed by relevant laws and regulations.
articles.4: Article 4 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, strict protection, administration in accordance with the law, and appropriate use. It shall properly balance protection with economic and social development, protect the overall geographic environment and the landscape features of mountains and rivers that depend on it, preserve and continue the traditional layout and historic character, preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage, and sustain continuity in residents' lives.
articles.5:
Article 5 The Municipal People's Government shall exercise unified leadership over protection of the historic and cultural city and coordinate, guide, and supervise protection work throughout the Municipality.
The People's Governments of counties, county-level cities, and districts shall be responsible for protection within their respective administrative areas.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall be responsible for specific day-to-day work, including inspections within their jurisdictions.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist with protection work in their local areas.
articles.6:
Article 6 The competent natural resources and planning department shall administer protection planning and implement these Regulations.
The competent cultural relics department shall protect and administer cultural relics involved in protection of the historic and cultural city.
The competent housing and urban-rural development department shall administer construction matters involved in such protection.
Other relevant departments shall carry out protection, supervision, and administration duties according to their respective responsibilities.
articles.7:
Article 7 The people's governments of the Municipality, counties, county-level cities, and districts, and township and town people's governments shall incorporate protection of the historic and cultural city into their economic and social development plans and include necessary funds in their respective budgets.
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged and supported to participate through donations, investment, establishment of funds, service provision, and other means.
articles.8:
Article 8 Any entity or individual may dissuade, complain about, or report conduct damaging the historic and cultural city.
The people's governments of the Municipality, counties, county-level cities, and districts, township and town people's governments, subdistrict offices, and competent natural resources and planning, cultural relics, and housing and urban-rural development departments shall publish reporting channels, accept complaints and reports, and promptly verify and handle them.
The people's governments of the Municipality, counties, county-level cities, and districts and relevant departments shall commend and reward outstanding contributors in accordance with applicable provisions.
articles.9:
Article 9 The people's governments of the Municipality, counties, county-level cities, and districts, township and town people's governments, and subdistrict offices shall strengthen public education, disseminate knowledge, and raise public awareness of protection.
Radio, television, newspapers, the Internet, and other media shall carry out public-interest publicity on protection of the historic and cultural city.
Chapter II — Protection List
articles.10: Article 10 A protection-list system shall apply to the historic and cultural city, and the Municipal People's Government shall publish the list. Protected matters approved and announced by the State, provincial, or Municipal People's Government shall be included directly. Matters approved by a County (District) People's Government shall be reported promptly to the Municipal People's Government for inclusion in the list.
articles.11:
Article 11 Within three months after the protection list is published, the Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall place protection signs on protected matters. Signs recording relevant historical information shall also be placed at the original site or nearby for important water systems, buildings, ruins, and other features with historic and cultural value that have disappeared. Signs shall follow uniform standards and be compatible with the traditional character.
No entity or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection sign without authorization.
articles.12: Article 12 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall organize relevant departments to collect, investigate, and organize historical information on protected matters, establish archives, and continuously supplement and improve them. Information on protection of the historic and cultural city shall be incorporated into the Municipality's big-data management system and shared.
articles.13:
Article 13 The natural resources and planning department shall regularly survey historic and cultural resources together with the cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, and other relevant departments. Where a matter with protection value is discovered, it shall promptly initiate its nomination.
An entity or individual discovering a matter with protection value may recommend its protection to the local natural resources and planning department.
articles.14:
Article 14 A township or town people's government or subdistrict office where an area with traditional character or historic building is located may apply to the municipal or county-level natural resources and planning department for its designation, for approval and publication by the people's government at the same level.
The natural resources and planning department shall organize expert review and consultation with relevant departments together with the cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, and other relevant departments, publicly announce the proposed matter, and solicit public opinions for no fewer than 30 days.
Applications for famous historic and cultural towns, villages, districts, and other matters shall follow relevant laws, regulations, and State provisions.
articles.15: Article 15 An area that has not been designated as a historic and cultural district may be nominated as an area with traditional character if it meets the following criteria: (1) buildings displaying traditional character are concentrated in a contiguous area, or traditional streets and lanes are relatively well preserved; and (2) its spatial layout, landscape form, and architectural styles substantially reflect the regional cultural features of a particular historical period.
articles.16:
Article 16 A building or structure with protection value that has not been announced as a protected cultural relic or registered as an immovable cultural relic may be nominated as a historic building if it meets any of the following criteria: (1) it reflects Luoyang's history, culture, or folk traditions and has characteristics of a particular period and locality; (2) its architectural style, structure, materials, or construction methods reflect regional culture or artistic characteristics or have scientific research value; (3) it is associated with an important political, economic, cultural, or military event or a famous historical figure; (4) it is a significant modern historic site or representative building that witnesses Luoyang's development and has local character; or (5) it has other historic or cultural significance.
Chapter III — Protection Planning
articles.17:
Article 17 The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of the protection plan for the historic and cultural city.
The People's Government of a county or county-level city shall organize preparation of protection plans for famous historic and cultural towns and villages.
Based on the protection plan for the historic and cultural city, the Municipal or County People's Government shall designate a relevant department to prepare protection plans for the historic urban area, historic and cultural districts, areas with traditional character, and historic buildings.
articles.18:
Article 18 A protection plan shall delineate the protected boundaries of protected matters.
Plans for the historic urban area, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, and areas with traditional character shall delineate core protected areas and construction control areas, mark their boundaries, and make them public.
articles.19:
Article 19 Before a protection plan is prepared, it shall undergo expert review and be publicly announced to solicit public opinions for no fewer than 30 days. A hearing may be held where necessary.
The department preparing the plan shall submit with the approval materials an account of the opinions adopted and the reasons for not adopting others. If a hearing was held, the hearing record shall also be submitted.
articles.20: Article 20 After approval in accordance with laws, regulations, and relevant provisions, a protection plan shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, the department preparing the plan shall revise and resubmit it for approval within its statutory authority and under statutory procedures and make the amended plan public.
articles.21:
Article 21 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall regularly organize relevant departments and experts to inspect and assess implementation of protection plans and promptly correct or address any problems found.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.22: Article 22 Construction within a protected area shall not impair the traditional character or layout of the historic urban area, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, or their historic environmental features; damage the integrity of historic and cultural districts or areas with traditional character; or damage the structure or original character of a historic building.
articles.23: Article 23 The following activities are prohibited within a protected area: (1) hill cutting, quarrying, mining, earth removal, blasting, logging, groundwater extraction, or other activities damaging the traditional layout or historic character; (2) constructing factories, warehouses, or similar facilities for producing, operating, storing, or using flammable or explosive substances or substances that are radioactive, toxic, or corrosive; (3) occupying roads, river and lake systems, gardens, green spaces, or other areas designated for preservation in the protection plan; or (4) other activities damaging protected matters.
articles.24:
Article 24 Unlawful buildings, structures, and other facilities within a protected area shall be demolished in accordance with the law. Buildings, structures, and other facilities that do not comply with the protection plan shall be renovated or relocated gradually.
An application shall be submitted to the local natural resources and planning department before demolishing a building, structure, or other facility within a protected area, other than an immovable cultural relic or historic building. Upon receiving the application, the department shall review and approve it together with the cultural relics department at the same level.
articles.25: Article 25 Within a core protected area of the historic urban area, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, or areas with traditional character, no new construction or expansion is permitted except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
articles.26: Article 26 The following activities concerning a historic building are prohibited: (1) carving or defacing it; (2) storing flammable, explosive, or corrosive substances inside it; (3) constructing a building or structure on its roof or terrace or using its exterior wall for that purpose; (4) carrying out unauthorized construction; (5) dismantling courtyard walls or altering its interior or exterior structure, form, or style without authorization; (6) damaging its principal load-bearing structure or otherwise endangering its safety; or (7) other conduct affecting its protection.
articles.27: Article 27 New, reconstructed, or extended buildings, structures, and other facilities in a construction control area of a famous historic and cultural town, village, or district or an area with traditional character shall be consistent with the traditional layout and historic character in height, bulk, form, style, colors, and other respects and comply with the protection plan.
articles.28: Article 28 A system of persons responsible for protection shall apply. The responsible person for a protected matter shall be determined as follows: (1) for a famous historic and cultural town, village, or district or an area with traditional character, the People's Government of the county, county-level city, or district where it is located; where that government has established a protection body, the body shall assume responsibility within its approved duties; (2) for a historic building, its owner; if the owner is unknown but there is a user, the user; if both are unknown, the County (District) People's Government shall designate a responsible person.
articles.29: Article 29 The person responsible for protection of a famous historic and cultural town, village, or district or an area with traditional character shall comply with the protection plan and: (1) preserve the integrity of the traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale, and historic environmental features of buildings and structures within the protected area; (2) conduct routine inspections and promptly stop conduct endangering the protected area; (3) keep the area clean and orderly; (4) ensure proper operation of public fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; and (5) meet other requirements under laws and regulations.
articles.30:
Article 30 The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall: (1) maintain and repair it regularly and preserve its original exterior form and character; (2) ensure structural safety, assist relevant departments in ensuring proper operation of fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment, promptly take measures to eliminate hazards, and report them to the local township or town people's government or subdistrict office; and (3) inform a transferee, lessee, or user of the protection duties when transferring, leasing, or lending the building.
Any special requirements for the responsible person's duties under laws, regulations, or the protection plan shall apply.
articles.31:
Article 31 The owner of a historic building shall bear the costs of its maintenance and repairs.
If the owner genuinely cannot bear those costs, the owner may apply to the County (District) People's Government for financial assistance and design support, or the government may carry out maintenance and repairs through an exchange or acquisition of title.
The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall formulate procedures and standards for repair subsidies.
articles.32: Article 32 An entity or individual suffering economic loss as a result of protection measures for the historic and cultural city shall receive reasonable compensation. The Municipal People's Government shall formulate detailed compensation measures.
articles.33:
Article 33 The municipal natural resources and planning department shall, together with the cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, and other relevant departments, prepare technical specifications for repair of historic buildings and regularly provide technical guidance and training.
External repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or changes to the structure or use of a historic building shall be approved by the natural resources and planning department together with the cultural relics department at the same level, and related procedures under laws and regulations shall be completed.
Repairs to a historic building within a protected area shall follow the technical specifications and use traditional techniques and materials without damaging the building, structures, or other facilities.
articles.34:
Article 34 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall, in accordance with the protection plan, organize construction and improvement of roads, water supply and drainage, electricity, sanitation, fire-safety, and other infrastructure.
If protection needs make it impossible to construct or administer such infrastructure under current technical standards and codes, the relevant department shall organize preparation of special measures, which shall be published and implemented after expert review.
Fire-safety facilities and access routes in core protected areas of famous towns, villages, and districts shall comply with applicable technical standards and codes. If protection needs make compliance impossible, the fire-safety department shall formulate appropriate fire-safety safeguards together with relevant departments.
articles.35:
Article 35 If the value of the historic and cultural city is seriously impaired, the natural resources and planning department shall assess the matter together with the cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, and other relevant departments. The people's government at the same level shall then direct relevant departments to take remedial measures and order correction within a specified period. If a matter no longer has protection value, it shall be removed from the protection list in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
Chapter V — Appropriate Use
articles.36:
Article 36 Use of the historic and cultural city shall be compatible with its historic, artistic, scientific, social, and cultural values and coordinate protection with use.
Protection, transmission, and appropriate use are encouraged and supported, as is the development of tourism and cultural industries, provided that natural landscapes, cultural landscapes, and historic and cultural resources are not damaged.
articles.37: Article 37 The Municipal and County (District) People's Governments shall use an information management system to publish information and guidance on appropriate use of protected matters, providing a platform for enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals to undertake or participate in such use.
articles.38: Article 38 Based on protection plans and actual conditions, the Municipal and County (District) People's Governments may adjust the population size and structure of famous historic and cultural towns, villages, and districts and areas with traditional character to align them with protection and use requirements.
articles.39: Article 39 State organs, social organizations, enterprises, and public institutions are encouraged to open historic buildings to the public as public places where conditions permit.
articles.40:
Article 40 Commercial activities in a historic and cultural district shall comply with the business-use layout in its protection plan.
Organization, research, and use of historic and cultural resources and development of cultural and artistic products with distinctive local traditions are encouraged. Cultural and creative activities, cultural research and experiences, leisure tourism, exhibitions, handicrafts, and other traditional businesses consistent with the protection plan are supported in famous historic and cultural towns, villages, and districts and areas with traditional character.
articles.41:
Article 41 Subject to protection taking priority, the Municipal and County (District) People's Governments and village collective economic organizations in famous historic and cultural villages may establish relevant market entities and participate in protection and use.
Chapter VI — Legal Liability
articles.42: Article 42 Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.43: Article 43 Where a person violates Article 23(1) through (3), the natural resources and planning department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the responsible person's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 500,000 to RMB 1,000,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 on an individual. The responsible person shall compensate for any losses.
articles.44: Article 44 Where a person violates Article 26(3), (4), or (5), the natural resources and planning department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the responsible person's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual. The responsible person shall compensate for any losses.
articles.45: Article 45 Where a person violates Article 26(6), the natural resources and planning department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the responsible person's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 200,000 to RMB 500,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 100,000 to RMB 200,000 on an individual. The responsible person shall compensate for any losses.
articles.46: Article 46 Where the person responsible for a historic building fails to perform protection duties under Article 30, the local people's government shall order performance within a specified period. If the person fails to do so by the deadline, the government may entrust a qualified organization or individual to perform the duties at the responsible person's expense. If serious consequences result, the local people's government shall direct the relevant department to impose penalties in accordance with the law.
articles.47:
Article 47 Where a relevant department of the Municipal or County (District) People's Government fails to perform its protection duties under these Regulations and serious consequences result, the people's government at the same level or the supervisory authority shall pursue accountability of the principal person in charge.
A staff member who neglects duties, abuses official powers, or engages in favoritism or malpractice in protection work shall be sanctioned by the employing entity, its superior authority, or the supervisory authority. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.48: Article 48 Where an administrative penalty under these Regulations is required by comprehensive urban administration law-enforcement rules to be imposed by another law-enforcement body, the relevant provisions shall apply.
articles.49: Article 49 For purposes of these Regulations: (1) ‘historic urban area’ means an area within a town or city that reflects its historical development or the character of a particular period, generally including areas commonly called an old town or old urban area; for purposes of these Regulations, it specifically means an area with clearly defined historic boundaries, a relatively well-preserved layout and character, and a need for protection; (2) ‘famous historic and cultural town or village’ means a town or village approved and announced by the provincial people's government that has exceptionally rich cultural relics and major historic or commemorative significance and substantially preserves the traditional character and local or ethnic features of one or more historical periods; (3) ‘historic and cultural district’ means a historic area approved and announced by the provincial people's government that has exceptionally rich cultural relics, a concentration of historic buildings, substantially and authentically reflects the traditional layout and historic character, and is of a certain scale; (4) ‘area with traditional character’ means an area approved and announced by the Municipal People's Government where historic buildings are concentrated and the architectural styles, spatial structure, and streetscape substantially reflect the regional cultural features of a particular historical period, but cultural relics and historic-building land occupy less than 60 percent and the area does not yet qualify, or has not yet been designated, as a historic and cultural district; and (5) ‘historic building’ means a building or structure designated and announced by the Municipal or County People's Government that has protection value and reflects historic character and local features.
articles.50: Article 50 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 March 2021.

FBMCLI.10.1552061.title: Regulations of Zhenjiang Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to protect the historic and cultural city, preserve outstanding historic and cultural heritage, and promote urban development and economic and social development, in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the State Council Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Jiangsu Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities and Towns, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to the planning, protection, use, and administration of the historic and cultural city within this Municipality's administrative area.
Protection includes historic urban areas, historic and cultural districts and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages, historic buildings, buildings of traditional character, immovable cultural relics, underground archaeological zones, historic environmental features, and other matters.
articles.3:
Article 3 The Municipal People's Government shall exercise unified leadership over protection of the historic and cultural city and organize its implementation.
The People's Governments of county-level cities and districts shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration in their respective areas and report regularly to the Municipal People's Government.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall carry out specific day-to-day administration and maintenance within their jurisdictions.
articles.4:
Article 4 The urban and rural planning department shall administer protection planning for the historic and cultural city.
The cultural relics department shall protect and administer cultural relics.
The departments responsible for housing and urban-rural development, culture, tourism, urban administration, water affairs, finance, transport, civil affairs, public security, education, and religious affairs shall perform corresponding protection duties according to their respective responsibilities.
articles.5: Article 5 The Municipal and County-level City (District) People's Governments shall incorporate protection of the historic and cultural city into economic and social development plans, arrange dedicated protection funds, and include them in the budgets at the same level.
articles.6: Article 6 The Municipal and County-level City (District) People's Governments and their relevant departments shall encourage and support entities and individuals to participate in protection through donations, funding, technical services, and other means, and reward outstanding contributors.
articles.7:
Article 7 The Municipal and County-level City (District) People's Governments and relevant departments shall strengthen public education, disseminate knowledge, and raise public awareness of protection.
Radio, television, newspapers, and online media shall carry out public-interest publicity on protection of the historic and cultural city.
Chapter II — Protection Planning
articles.8:
Article 8 The Municipal and county-level city people's governments shall organize preparation of protection plans for the historic and cultural city.
The urban and rural planning department shall prepare protection plans for the historic urban area, historic and cultural districts and areas, and historic buildings within its administrative area.
The People's Government of a county-level city or district shall organize preparation of protection plans for famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages.
articles.9:
Article 9 A protection plan shall delineate the protected boundaries of each protected matter.
Protection plans for historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, traditional villages, historic areas, historic buildings, and buildings of traditional character shall delineate core protected areas and construction control areas, mark the boundaries, and make them public.
articles.10: Article 10 The authority preparing a protection plan shall publish the draft in accordance with the law and solicit opinions from relevant departments, experts, interested parties, and the public through review meetings, hearings, or other means. The draft shall be publicly available for no fewer than 30 days.
articles.11:
Article 11 A protection plan shall be submitted for approval in accordance with laws, regulations, and relevant provisions.
Within 30 days after approval, the plan shall be published on the government website and in major news media.
An approved protection plan shall not be amended except under statutory procedures.
articles.12:
Article 12 The core contents of protection plans for the historic and cultural city and famous historic and cultural towns and villages shall be incorporated into territorial spatial plans at the relevant levels.
Other specialized plans concerning urban transport, water affairs, municipal services, landscaping, fire safety, and civil air defense shall be coordinated with the protection plans.
Chapter III — Protection List
articles.13: Article 13 The Municipal and county-level city people's governments shall establish a protection-list system for the historic and cultural city. The list shall specify the name, location, category, grade, ownership, historical development, historic value, and other particulars of protected matters and shall be published on the government website and in news media.
articles.14:
Article 14 Protected matters approved and announced by the State or provincial people's government or already approved and announced by the Municipal People's Government shall be included directly in the protection list.
Other matters meeting any of the following criteria shall be included: (1) a historic urban area reflecting a historical development process or the character of a particular period; (2) a historic area reflecting the traditional character or ethnic or local characteristics of a historical period; (3) a building of traditional character, other than a protected cultural relic or historic building, with a certain history and value or significance to the overall character of a historic area; (4) an underground archaeological zone; (5) historic environmental features reflecting historic character, such as ancient wells, walls, stone steps, paving, embankments, and ancient or notable trees; or (6) another matter requiring inclusion in the list.
articles.15:
Article 15 The urban and rural planning department shall regularly survey historic and cultural resources together with the housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, and other relevant departments.
An entity or individual discovering a matter with protection value may recommend its inclusion in the list to the urban and rural planning department. For a matter with such value, the department shall solicit opinions from relevant departments, interested parties, and the public, organize expert review, and submit it to the Municipal or county-level city people's government for approval and inclusion in the list.
articles.16:
Article 16 If inadequate protection seriously impairs the historic and cultural value of a matter on the protection list, the urban and rural planning department, together with the cultural relics and housing and urban-rural development departments, shall assess the matter and may petition the Municipal or county-level city people's government to place it on a list of endangered protected matters and make that list public. The relevant people's government of the Municipality, county-level city, or district shall direct the relevant departments to take remedial measures and order correction within a specified period.
After the correction period expires, the urban and rural planning department, together with the cultural relics and housing and urban-rural development departments, shall organize expert review. A matter passing review shall be removed from the endangered list. A matter that fails review and no longer has protection value shall be removed from the protection list.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.17: Article 17 Urban renewal and new-area construction shall not impair the traditional character or layout of historic urban areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages, or historic environmental features, or damage the integrity of historic and cultural districts or areas with traditional street character.
articles.18: Article 18 The following conduct is prohibited within a protected area: (1) hill cutting, quarrying or mining, earth removal, blasting, or other activities damaging the traditional layout or historic character; (2) constructing factories, warehouses, or similar facilities for producing, operating, storing, or using explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances; (3) occupying roads, river and lake systems, gardens, or green spaces designated for preservation in the protection plan; (4) damaging, destroying, carving, or defacing a protected matter; or (5) other activities damaging protected matters.
articles.19: Article 19 Within a core protected area of a historic and cultural district or a famous historic and cultural town or village, no new construction, reconstruction, or expansion is permitted except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities.
articles.20: Article 20 New, reconstructed, or extended buildings, structures, or other facilities in a construction control area of a historic and cultural district, famous town or village, traditional village, historic area, historic building, or building of traditional character shall be compatible with the traditional layout and historic character in height, bulk, form, style, color, and other respects.
articles.21: Article 21 Construction within the protected area of a historic urban area shall meet the following requirements: (1) no new overhead utility lines may be installed, and existing overhead lines shall be buried gradually; (2) new construction projects shall separate stormwater and sewage systems; and (3) plazas, sidewalks, and traditional streets and lanes shall use paving materials consistent with the traditional character.
articles.22:
Article 22 Internal waterways shall be connected with one another and with external water systems. The principal water system of the historic urban area shall be protected, important historic waterways shall be restored as appropriate, and water bodies and surfaces shall not be occupied, enclosed, filled, or blocked.
Waterways shall be cleaned routinely and dredged regularly to maintain flowing water and improve water quality.
articles.23: Article 23 The landscape environment around a historic and cultural district shall be controlled to preserve the district's original spatial layout and scale. Its historic street and lane fabric shall not be altered.
articles.24: Article 24 The overall character of a historic area shall receive focused protection. Its historic continuity shall be maintained and its economic and social vitality strengthened.
articles.25:
Article 25 Before land within any of the following areas is transferred, the transferor shall request the cultural relics department to conduct an investigation and archaeological work: (1) an underground archaeological zone; (2) a construction project covering more than 50,000 square meters outside such a zone; or (3) another area that may contain underground cultural relics.
Any entity or individual discovering historic remains, cultural relics, or archaeological sites during construction shall immediately report them to the local cultural relics department. That department shall arrive at the site within 24 hours after receiving the report and issue a handling opinion within seven days. The developer and contractor shall immediately stop work and protect the site.
articles.26:
Article 26 The People's Government of a county-level city or district shall, in accordance with the protection plan, organize construction and improvement of roads, water supply and drainage, electricity, sanitation, fire-safety, and other infrastructure.
If protection needs make it impossible to construct or administer such infrastructure under current technical standards and codes, the relevant department shall organize special measures, which shall be published and implemented after expert review.
articles.27:
Article 27 The municipal urban and rural planning department shall prepare technical specifications for repair of historic buildings and buildings of traditional character together with the cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, and other relevant departments.
External repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or alteration of the structure or use of a historic building or building of traditional character shall be approved by the urban and rural planning department together with the cultural relics department at the same level, and procedures under relevant laws and regulations shall be completed.
Repairs to such buildings within a protected area shall follow the technical specifications and use traditional techniques and materials without damaging buildings, structures, or other facilities that form part of the traditional character.
articles.28:
Article 28 Unlawful buildings, structures, and other facilities within a protected area shall be demolished in accordance with the law. Those that do not comply with the protection plan shall be renovated or relocated gradually.
An application shall be submitted to the urban and rural planning department before demolishing a building, structure, or other facility within a protected area, other than a protected cultural relic, immovable cultural relic, or historic building. Upon receiving the application, the department shall review it together with the cultural relics department at the same level and decide whether to approve demolition.
articles.29:
Article 29 Within three months after publication of the protection list, the Municipal and county-level city people's governments shall place protection signs on protected matters. Signs recording relevant historical information shall be placed at the original site or nearby for important water systems, buildings, ruins, and other features with historic and cultural value that have disappeared.
Signs and markers shall follow uniform standards and be compatible with the traditional character.
articles.30: Article 30 No entity or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a boundary marker, protection sign, or other marker without authorization.
articles.31:
Article 31 The Municipal and county-level city people's governments shall organize relevant departments to collect, investigate, and organize historical information about matters on the protection list, establish and continuously improve archives, incorporate protection information into the Municipality's big-data management system, and share that information.
Chapter V — Appropriate Use
articles.32: Article 32 Use of the historic and cultural city shall be compatible with its historic, artistic, scientific, social, and cultural values, take economic benefits into account, and coordinate protection with use.
articles.33: Article 33 The Municipal and County-level City (District) People's Governments shall use an information management system to publish information and guidance on appropriate use of protected matters, providing a platform for enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals to undertake or participate in such use.
articles.34: Article 34 Protection, transmission, and appropriate use of the historic and cultural city are encouraged and supported, as is the development of tourism and cultural industries, provided that natural landscapes, cultural landscapes, and historic and cultural resources are not damaged.
articles.35: Article 35 Appropriate use of historic buildings and buildings of traditional character is encouraged through policy guidance, financial support, simplified procedures, and other means.
articles.36: Article 36 Government agencies, organizations, enterprises, and public institutions are encouraged to open eligible historic buildings and buildings of traditional character to the public as public places.
articles.37: Article 37 Organization, research, and use of historic and cultural resources and development of cultural and artistic products with distinctive local traditions are encouraged. Cultural and creative activities, cultural research and experiences, leisure tourism, exhibitions, handicrafts, and other traditional businesses consistent with the protection plan are supported in historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages, and other protected areas.
articles.38: Article 38 Subject to protection taking priority, the Municipal and County-level City (District) People's Governments and village collective economic organizations where famous historic and cultural villages or traditional villages are located may establish relevant market entities and participate in protection and use.
articles.39:
Article 39 The Municipal and County-level City (District) People's Governments shall organize historical and cultural research, lectures by experts, public classes for residents, publication of books, media publicity, exhibitions, and other activities to disseminate knowledge about protection of the historic and cultural city.
Education departments and schools shall include local historic and cultural knowledge in students' extracurricular education and organize public lectures, student field activities, and other educational activities relating to protection, use, and transmission.
Chapter VI — Supervision and Administration
articles.40:
Article 40 The Municipal and County-level City (District) People's Governments shall regularly organize relevant departments and experts to inspect and assess protected matters within their respective administrative areas and report the results to the Standing Committee of the people's congress at the same level.
By 31 December each year, the urban and rural planning department, together with relevant departments and based on the condition of protected matters, shall prepare a maintenance and repair plan for the following year and implement it after approval by the people's government at the same level. The annual plan shall be published on the government website and in local major news media.
articles.41: Article 41 The township or town people's government or subdistrict office where a protected matter is located shall: (1) conduct routine inspections and promptly discover and stop conduct endangering or damaging the historic and cultural city; (2) promptly report damaged matters or matters requiring repair to the higher-level people's government; (3) keep the protected area's environment clean and orderly; and (4) perform other protection duties specified by the Municipal or County-level City (District) People's Government.
articles.42:
Article 42 The person responsible for protection of a historic building or building of traditional character shall be determined as follows: (1) for property owned by the State or a collective, its manager; (2) for property owned by an entity or individual, its owner; (3) if the owner cannot be located or title is unclear, the actual user or manager; and (4) if the owner, user, and manager cannot be identified, the township or town people's government or subdistrict office where it is located.
An owner or manager may agree with a user on protection duties, but the agreement shall not exempt any party from protection duties under these Regulations.
Where laws or regulations provide otherwise concerning the person responsible for protecting a category of protected matter or that person's duties, those provisions shall prevail.
articles.43: Article 43 The person responsible for protection shall: (1) maintain and care for the protected matter on a day-to-day basis; (2) promptly repair a protected matter at risk of damage; (3) accept inspection and guidance from the local township or town people's government or subdistrict office and the cultural relics, emergency management, and other departments; and (4) perform other protection duties.
articles.44: Article 44 A township or town people's government or subdistrict office shall enter into a protection-responsibility agreement with the person responsible for a protected matter within its jurisdiction, specifying the protection duties.
articles.45: Article 45 If a historic building is at risk of damage and the person responsible for protection lacks the capacity to repair it, the township or town people's government or subdistrict office where it is located shall organize maintenance and repairs.
articles.46:
Article 46 An entity or individual suffering loss as a result of protection of the historic and cultural city shall receive fair and reasonable compensation. The Municipal People's Government shall formulate detailed compensation measures.
A subsidy shall be provided where the responsible person repairs a historic building within a protected area in accordance with the protection plan and technical specifications, or where an owner and user of public housing cooperate with expropriation or relocation by agreement.
Chapter VII — Legal Liability
articles.47: Article 47 Where a person violates Article 18(1), (2), or (3), the urban and rural planning department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 500,000 to RMB 1,000,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 on an individual. The violator shall compensate for any losses.
articles.48: Article 48 Where a person violates Article 18(4) by damaging or destroying a building, structure, or other facility that is a protected matter other than a protected cultural relic or historic building, the urban and rural planning department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual. The violator shall compensate for any losses.
articles.49: Article 49 A person conducting new construction, reconstruction, or expansion in violation of Article 19 shall be penalized in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
articles.50: Article 50 Where a person continues construction or fails to protect the site after discovering historic remains, cultural relics, or archaeological sites during construction, in violation of Article 25(2), the cultural relics department shall stop the conduct, order the person to cease damaging the site, and require remedial measures within a specified period. It may impose a fine of RMB 5,000 to RMB 50,000. Damage caused shall be penalized under relevant State laws and regulations.
articles.51: Article 51 Where a person demolishes a building, structure, or other facility within a protected area without approval from the urban and rural planning department together with the cultural relics department at the same level, in violation of Article 28(2), the urban and rural planning department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual. The violator shall compensate for any losses.
articles.52: Article 52 Where a person violates Article 30 by installing, moving, altering, or damaging a boundary marker, protection sign, or other marker without authorization, the urban and rural planning department shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 1,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual.
articles.53:
Article 53 Where a relevant municipal department, County-level City (District) People's Government or its department, township or town people's government, subdistrict office, or staff member responsible for protection fails to perform or improperly performs its supervision and administration duties, the superior competent department shall order correction. Where serious adverse effects or consequences result, sanctions shall be imposed on the responsible person in charge and directly responsible personnel. If a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Chapter VIII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.54:
Article 54 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 March 2020.
