FBMCLI.10.1640280.title: Regulations of Longyan Municipality on the Protection of Changting as a Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to protect Changting as a historic and cultural city and preserve and carry forward outstanding history and culture, in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the State Council Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and Traditional Villages, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to planning, protection, administration, and use of Changting as a historic and cultural city.
The primary focus of protection is the historic urban area, including the original Tingzhou ancient city enclosed by the surviving ancient city wall and its ruins and the Shuodong Street Historic and Cultural District on the east bank of the Ting River, with appropriate outward expansion. The specific boundaries shall be determined and announced in the protection plan.
Protected matters include the urban-site setting formed by three mountains (Wolong, Baixiang, and Nanping), two rivers (the Ting River and Xihe River), one axis (the urban central axis), and three rings (the city-wall ring, the southern basin of Wolong Mountain, and the ring formed by surrounding mountains); the settlement pattern of a city among mountains and encircled by mountains and water; the overall layout and historic character of the historic urban area, including historic and cultural districts formed by Dongdajie, Shuodong Street, Diantou Street, and Nandajie, and the Tingzhou Examination Hall historic character area; immovable cultural relics, historic buildings, buildings of traditional character, ancient or notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, and other matters with protection value.
Protection of cultural relics, historic buildings, ancient or notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, and other matters within the protected area shall be governed by other applicable laws and regulations.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of Changting as a historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, strict protection, appropriate use, and coordinated development. It shall properly balance economic and social development with historic and cultural protection, preserve and continue the traditional layout and historic character, protect the natural and cultural landscapes connected with it, preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage, and build a historic and cultural city that continues traditional culture while meeting modern urban functions and contemporary living needs.
articles.4:
Article 4 The Longyan Municipal People's Government and its relevant competent departments shall supervise and guide protection and administration of Changting as a historic and cultural city and provide policy support in accordance with the law and actual conditions.
The Changting County People's Government (the ‘County People's Government’) shall be responsible for planning, protection, administration, and use of the historic and cultural city, incorporate this work into the County's economic and social development plan, and include necessary funding in its budget.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall protect and administer the historic and cultural city within their jurisdictions.
articles.5:
Article 5 The county natural resources department shall organize preparation and implementation supervision of territorial spatial plans relating to protection and use of Changting as a historic and cultural city.
The county culture and tourism (cultural relics) department shall supervise and administer protection of cultural relics and intangible cultural heritage.
The county housing and urban-rural development department shall handle surveys, applications, designation, and list administration for historic and cultural districts and historic buildings.
The departments responsible for urban administration, market regulation, public security, development and reform, finance, water affairs, civil affairs, forestry, and transport, together with fire and rescue agencies and the municipal ecology and environment field office, shall perform related duties according to their respective responsibilities.
Villagers' and residents' committees in the area shall assist the local people's government with protection work.
articles.6: Article 6 The County People's Government's administration body for protection of Changting as a historic and cultural city (the ‘protection administration body’) shall be specifically responsible for protection, use, and day-to-day administration and shall: (1) publicize and implement laws, regulations, rules, and policies on protection; (2) lead preparation and nomination of special plans for protection and use and formulate implementation measures; (3) work with relevant departments to prepare and apply for special protection funds and supervise their use; (4) organize review of business-use plans, street and shop-front designs, and construction plans, and supervise implementation; (5) coordinate and assist relevant departments in investigating violations; (6) participate in tourism planning based on local resources, develop cultural brands, conduct publicity, exchanges, and research, and collect, organize, and compile relevant historical materials; (7) prepare and revise the protection list and maintain its database; (8) guide development and assessment of industry professionals and provide training; and (9) perform other duties assigned by the County People's Government.
articles.7: Article 7 The protection administration body shall establish an expert committee for protection of the historic and cultural city. Experts in planning, housing, architecture, landscaping, culture and cultural relics, tourism, religion, history, place names, folk customs, law, traditional crafts, and other fields shall review protection lists, plans, measures, construction administration, and related matters and provide recommendations.
articles.8: Article 8 The County People's Government shall establish a hearing system for major matters concerning protection of Changting as a historic and cultural city. Experts and public representatives shall be invited to hearings on major matters concerning protection plans and designation of historic areas or buildings of traditional character. Hearing results shall be an important reference for decision-making.
articles.9: Article 9 All sectors of society, organizations at all levels, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and use of the historic and cultural city through investment, donations, volunteer services, and other means.
articles.10:
Article 10 All entities and individuals have a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and may dissuade, report, or lodge complaints against violations damaging its protection.
The County People's Government, relevant departments, and the protection administration body shall strengthen public education, disseminate knowledge, and raise awareness. They shall encourage public participation through public-benefit protection organizations, volunteer activities, and other means.
articles.11:
Article 11 28 November of each year shall be Changting Historic and Cultural City Protection Day.
Chapter II — Protection Planning
articles.12:
Article 12 The County People's Government shall organize preparation of a protection plan for the historic and cultural city and submit it for approval and filing in accordance with the law.
Based on the protection plan, it shall organize preparation of plans for protection of historic and cultural districts and other matters and submit them for approval as required.
articles.13:
Article 13 The authority organizing preparation shall publish drafts of protection plans for the historic and cultural city and historic and cultural districts on the government website or in the County's principal news media and solicit opinions from experts and the public through review meetings, hearings, or other means.
A draft shall be publicly available for no fewer than 30 days.
articles.14: Article 14 Before a protection plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic and cultural district is submitted for approval in accordance with the rules, it shall be deliberated by the Standing Committee of the Changting County People's Congress. The County People's Government shall study and address the deliberation opinions.
articles.15: Article 15 Within 30 days after approval, a protection plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic and cultural district shall be published on the government website or in the County's principal news media.
articles.16: Article 16 An approved protection plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic and cultural district shall not be amended without authorization. Any necessary amendment shall follow statutory procedures.
articles.17:
Article 17 Based on the protection plan, the county housing and urban-rural development department shall organize preparation of urban designs for the historic urban area and other key areas and submit them to the County People's Government for approval.
The contents of an urban design for a key area shall be incorporated into the detailed territorial spatial plan and implemented in its relevant indicators.
articles.18:
Article 18 Planning and construction of the historic urban area and surrounding areas shall be coordinated to continue the traditional character and highlight the city's distinctive features.
Areas outside the historic urban area shall support optimization and upgrading of industry, transport, the environment, and other aspects within it.
Chapter III — Protection Requirements
articles.19: Article 19 The historic urban area shall be protected and controlled in accordance with the protection plan, with particular protection and control of: (1) the authentic and intact urban-site setting, settlement pattern, and layout of Tingzhou's ancient city wall; (2) the integrity of the traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale, and historic environmental features of buildings and structures within the protected area; and (3) other matters prescribed by these Regulations or determined by the Municipal or County People's Government.
articles.20: Article 20 Construction in the historic urban area shall comply with the protection plan and: (1) shall not add land for industrial or storage use; (2) shall not install new overhead utility lines, and utility lines of the same kind that can be combined underground shall be combined and buried; (3) new and reconstructed projects shall separate stormwater and sewage and connect sewage pipes to the urban sewage collection system. If street-space limitations make separation impossible, combined wastewater shall be discharged into the urban sewage collection system and not directly into a river; (4) building and structure colors shall primarily be ochre, gray, white, or black and reflect Changting's distinctive character; (5) plazas, sidewalks, and traditional streets and lanes shall use paving materials and forms reflecting traditional character; and (6) buildings and structures shall not be newly constructed, reconstructed, or extended in violation of the plan. Those inconsistent with the protection plan shall be renovated or demolished gradually.
articles.21: Article 21 A historic and cultural district shall delineate core protected and construction control areas in accordance with its protection plan and: (1) control the surrounding landscape environment, preserve the original spatial layout and scale, and not alter the street and lane fabric; (2) permit no new construction or expansion in the core protected area except necessary infrastructure and public services; (3) require new, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures in the construction control area to meet requirements for preservation of the district's character and visual landscape and to be compatible in height, form, bulk, colors, and style; and (4) relocate gradually factories and warehouses that do not comply with the protection plan or impair the traditional character.
articles.22: Article 22 The overall character of a historic area shall receive focused protection and its historic continuity shall be preserved. Protection shall be combined with appropriate use to strengthen the area's economic and social vitality. Construction within the protected area shall not alter the traditional layout or character.
articles.23: Article 23 The natural character of the mountains in Changting shall be strictly protected. No person may excavate mountains or fell trees without authorization.
articles.24:
Article 24 Internal waterways shall be connected with one another and with external water systems. The Ting River and Xihe River, the two principal water systems of the historic urban area, shall be protected, important historic waterways restored as appropriate, and existing waterways shall not be filled in or occupied.
The bulk, eave height, and colors of new riverside buildings along the Ting River and Xihe River shall be controlled so as not to damage the traditional character of riverside buildings.
Repairs to traditional embankments, landing stages, and bridges shall use traditional techniques and materials and continue the traditional character. Any necessary new embankment, landing stage, wharf, or bridge shall comply with construction controls in the protection plan and reflect traditional features.
Waterways shall be cleaned routinely and dredged regularly to maintain flowing water and improve water quality.
Ancient wells shall be protected, maintained, and used appropriately. Important damaged wells shall be repaired in conjunction with street, lane, or courtyard spaces and their functions restored gradually.
articles.25:
Article 25 The existing layout of the ancient city wall of Changting shall be protected. A character-protection buffer shall be established around the wall. Buildings within the protected area shall not exceed the height of the wall and shall be compatible with it in bulk and use.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.26:
Article 26 The County People's Government shall maintain a classified protection list for the historic and cultural city. Protected matters approved and announced by the State, provincial, municipal, or County People's Government shall be included directly.
The protection administration body shall organize the housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism (cultural relics), and other relevant departments to regularly survey protected matters. The first survey shall be completed within one year after these Regulations take effect.
The protection administration body shall organize relevant departments to prepare and revise the protection list, which, after expert review and public notice, shall be submitted to the County People's Government for approval and publication.
Any entity or individual may recommend inclusion of a matter in the protection list to the County People's Government.
articles.27:
Article 27 The County People's Government shall place protection signs on protected matters. Signs shall comply with relevant laws and regulations and the requirements of relevant international organizations and be compatible with Changting's traditional character.
The County People's Government shall maintain archives for the protection list.
articles.28:
Article 28 Where laws or regulations provide for the responsible persons and protection duties concerning cultural relics, historic buildings, ancient or notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, and other protected matters, those provisions shall apply.
For a State-owned building of traditional character, its user shall be responsible for protection. For a non-State-owned building of traditional character, its owner shall be responsible; if the owner cannot be located or title is unclear, the actual user or manager shall be responsible. The owner may agree with the actual user or manager on protection duties, but may not use the agreement to avoid the owner's own duties.
The actual user of a building of traditional character shall use it lawfully and safely and cooperate with the owner in safety inspections and repairs.
articles.29:
Article 29 The County People's Government shall organize the housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism (cultural relics), natural resources, and other relevant departments and the protection administration body to prepare protection guidelines for buildings of traditional character. The guidelines shall specify requirements concerning layout, height, bulk, exterior appearance, colors, materials, details, and construction techniques, be made public, and be provided in writing to owners, users, and property-management entities.
A responsible person carrying out routine maintenance or repairs shall preserve the building's traditional layout, height, bulk, exterior appearance, and colors in accordance with the guidelines.
No entity or individual may damage or destroy a building of traditional character. If it is at risk of damage, the responsible person shall promptly maintain and repair it. If that person lacks the capacity to do so, the County People's Government shall take protective measures.
articles.30:
Article 30 The County People's Government shall establish a compensation system for protection of the historic urban area. Where government protection measures damage the lawful rights and interests of an entity or individual and cause property loss, fair and reasonable compensation shall be provided in accordance with the law.
The County People's Government shall provide subsidies where a responsible person repairs or maintains a building of traditional character in accordance with the protection plan and technical standards, or where a housing owner and public-housing user actively cooperate with government expropriation or relocation by agreement.
Compensation and subsidies under the preceding paragraphs shall be covered through the special protection fund for Changting as a historic and cultural city.
articles.31: Article 31 The following activities are prohibited within the protected area of Changting as a historic and cultural city: (1) occupying gardens, green spaces, rivers and waterways, traditional streets and lanes, roads, or other areas designated for preservation in the protection plan; (2) installing outdoor advertisements without authorization; (3) installing, moving, altering, or damaging a protection sign without authorization; (4) relocating or demolishing a building of traditional character, historic building, or protected cultural relic without authorization; (5) externally repairing or decorating a historic building, adding facilities, or changing its structure or use without authorization; (6) removing bricks, wood carvings, stone carvings, or other building components with historic, artistic, or scientific value from a historic building without authorization; (7) altering the original height, bulk, exterior appearance, or colors of a building of traditional character or historic building without authorization; (8) carving or defacing a historic building, ancient or notable tree, or other protected matter; (9) storing flammable, explosive, or corrosive substances inside buildings in the historic urban area; (10) conducting outdoor food barbecues or unlawfully discharging cooking fumes in the historic urban area; (11) placing or hanging items that impair the appearance of the city on balconies or outside windows of street-facing buildings; (12) hanging or posting promotional materials on building facades or trees; (13) conducting dust-polluting activities in workshops in the historic urban area; (14) operating vehicle repair or washing businesses in the historic urban area; or (15) other activities prohibited by laws and regulations.
articles.32: Article 32 Before repairing, reconstructing, or constructing a building, structure, road, utility line, lighting system, or other facility in the historic urban area, the developer or individual shall, based on the protection plan, submit an implementation plan to the county natural resources department. That department shall organize a joint review with the protection administration body, housing and urban-rural development, culture and tourism (cultural relics), urban administration, and other relevant departments and the township or town people's government concerned.
articles.33:
Article 33 The County People's Government shall promote appropriate use of protected matters through policy guidance, financial assistance, and other means.
Social organizations and other parties are encouraged to use historic resources appropriately to develop industries consistent with the protection plan and conduct business consistent with industry-layout plans.
Appropriate use shall draw fully on cultural significance and may include cultural and creative activities, leisure tourism, cultural research, traditional handicrafts, transmission of intangible cultural heritage, cultural experiences, exhibitions, museums, homestays, inns, bars, teahouses, coffee shops, and other distinctive commercial or public-benefit activities.
Development and use shall follow the principles of necessity and moderation, preserve overall character, and strictly control the area used for commercial development.
articles.34: Article 34 The County People's Government shall organize the protection administration body and relevant departments to explore, collect, organize, research, and use local historic and cultural resources and promote outstanding local culture through traditional-culture research, publications, training, exhibitions, media publicity, and other means.
articles.35:
Article 35 The County People's Government shall adopt support policies for protection and transmission of intangible cultural heritage and encourage transmission through subsidies from the special protection fund and free training.
Use of buildings of traditional character to display Changting's traditional way of life and folk customs to the public is encouraged.
Establishment of bases for intangible cultural heritage research and transmission, film and television production, cultural and creative industries, local cultural research, and other activities is encouraged.
articles.36:
Article 36 The mix of activities in the historic urban area shall comply with the protection plan.
The County People's Government shall formulate lawful catalogues of industries to guide, control, or prohibit and support technology and creative industries, cultural tourism, specialty commerce, headquarters-based economic activity, and other modern services, improving cultural transmission, tourism and leisure, and traditional industries.
Education, science, culture, health, sports, and other public services shall be retained reasonably and improved to meet residents' needs.
articles.37:
Article 37 Road connections between the historic urban area and surrounding areas shall be improved and the road network laid out rationally.
Parking and transport interchange facilities shall be expanded outside the historic urban area to reduce motor vehicles entering or passing through it.
Slow traffic shall be encouraged in the historic urban area, with right of way protected and pedestrian and cycling areas and routes increased as appropriate. Streets and lanes shall be adapted for cyclists and pedestrians. Parking facilities meeting residents' needs shall be planned and constructed in moderation, and measures such as staggered parking, sharing public parking resources, and tiered time-based parking charges shall be used to ease parking difficulties.
Non-motorized transport and walking shall be the principal modes in historic and cultural districts.
articles.38:
Article 38 The historic urban area shall apply total traffic-volume controls and zoned traffic administration, reasonably increase road-use costs for motor-vehicle drivers, and gradually expand areas where motor vehicles are prohibited, restricted, or subject to one-way traffic.
Priority shall be given to public transport, with motorized travel organized primarily around public transit. Bus-only lanes, transit-priority signals, interchange hubs, bus bays, optimized routes, and an integrated transit system shall be developed scientifically.
Water transport shall be laid out rationally and developed in moderation, including distinctive sightseeing routes.
Environmentally friendly public buses and sightseeing boats shall be used in the historic urban area and their use promoted.
articles.39: Article 39 The County People's Government shall recruit and train professionals in planning, repair of historic buildings, traditional handicrafts, restoration of ancient or notable trees, and other fields related to protection of Changting as a historic and cultural city; establish or attract specialized research institutions; and increase investment in training and use of professionals.
articles.40: Article 40 In accordance with the protection plan, population density in the historic urban area shall be controlled and the population structure optimized through housing-leasing administration, industry adjustment, and other measures.
articles.41:
Article 41 The County People's Government shall establish an information management system covering geographic, historic and cultural, planning, place-name, and other information to improve intelligent administration of protection work.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.42: Article 42 Where laws or regulations prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
articles.43:
Article 43 Where any of the following circumstances violates Article 29, the county urban administration department or another supervisory department designated by the County People's Government shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual. Unlawful income shall be confiscated, and losses shall be compensated in accordance with the law: (1) the responsible person for a non-State-owned building of traditional character fails to maintain or repair it according to the protection guidelines and damages its traditional layout, height, bulk, exterior appearance, or colors; (2) a person intentionally damages or destroys a building of traditional character; or (3) a responsible person for a non-State-owned building of traditional character who has the capacity to maintain and repair it fails to perform protection duties, causing damage or collapse.
Where a responsible person for a State-owned building of traditional character commits any act in the preceding paragraph, the person's employer or superior authority shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures. If the person fails to correct the conduct and serious consequences result, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel.
articles.44: Article 44 Where a person violates Article 31(3) by installing, moving, altering, or damaging a protection sign without authorization, the county urban administration department or another supervisory department designated by the County People's Government shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 1,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual.
articles.45: Article 45 Where a person violates Article 31(13) by conducting dust-polluting activities in a workshop in the historic urban area, the supervisory department designated by the County People's Government shall order correction. If the person refuses to comply, it shall order suspension of production or business and impose a fine of RMB 20,000 to RMB 100,000. Unlawful income shall be confiscated, and losses shall be compensated in accordance with the law.
articles.46:
Article 46 Where the County People's Government, a relevant competent department, or its staff fails to perform supervision and administration duties, fails to investigate a violation after discovering it, or otherwise neglects duties, abuses official powers, or engages in favoritism or malpractice, the employer, superior authority, or supervisory authority shall order correction and circulate a notice of criticism. Where circumstances are serious, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.47: Article 47 For purposes of these Regulations: (1) ‘historic area’ includes a historic and cultural district and an area with historic character and means an area within the historic urban area containing numerous cultural relics or a concentration of buildings of traditional character that substantially and authentically reflects Changting's traditional street and lane character and is of a certain scale; (2) ‘historic and cultural district’ means an area within the historic urban area with exceptionally rich cultural relics and a concentration of historic buildings and buildings of traditional character that substantially and authentically reflects the traditional layout and historic character and is of a certain scale; (3) ‘area with historic character’ means an area within the historic urban area whose spatial layout, landscape character, and architectural styles substantially reflect the cultural features of a particular period in Changting's history and is of a certain scale, but does not meet the land-area standard for buildings and structures in a historic and cultural district; and (4) ‘building of traditional character’ means a residence, shop, temple, or other building constructed in any historical period in the historic urban area that reflects Changting's traditional character and traditional construction techniques, social ethics, aesthetic views, or other cultural elements, excluding an immovable cultural relic or historic building.
articles.48:
Article 48 These Regulations shall take effect on 28 November 2020.

Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages (2017 Revision)

FBMCLI.10.452415.title: Regulations of Nanjing Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to protect the historic and cultural city, preserve and carry forward fine traditional culture, and promote coordinated economic and social development, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the State Council Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Jiangsu Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities and Towns, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to planning, protection, use, and administration of the historic and cultural city within this Municipality's administrative area.
Protected matters include the old city's layout and urban character; famous historic and cultural towns and villages; historic and cultural districts; historic character areas; historic streets and lanes; historic buildings; ancient towns and villages; key underground archaeological protection areas; intangible cultural heritage; and other matters.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of government leadership, integrated planning, holistic protection, and appropriate use. It shall properly balance economic and social development with protection of historic and cultural heritage, preserve the authenticity and integrity of heritage, and preserve and continue the city's traditional layout and character.
articles.4: Article 4 The Municipal, District, and County People's Governments shall strengthen leadership over protection of the historic and cultural city, incorporate protection into economic and social development plans, establish protection mechanisms, and ensure funding.
articles.5:
Article 5 The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection committee for the historic and cultural city to plan, coordinate, review, and guide major protection matters.
The municipal urban and rural planning department shall implement these Regulations together with the cultural relics department.
The departments responsible for construction, real estate, land, finance, culture, tourism, urban administration, public security, and other matters shall perform protection duties according to their respective responsibilities.
The District and County People's Governments shall organize specific protection work within their jurisdictions.
articles.6: Article 6 Nanjing shall establish an expert committee for the historic and cultural city. Its experts in planning, cultural relics, culture, architecture, landscaping, tourism, religion, history, folk customs, law, and other fields shall review and assess protection plans, protection lists, and related matters.
articles.7:
Article 7 All entities and individuals have a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and may dissuade, report, or lodge complaints against conduct damaging it.
The Municipal, District, and County People's Governments shall commend and reward outstanding contributors to protection.
articles.8:
Article 8 The Municipal, District, and County People's Governments shall include protection funds in their respective budgets.
Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection through donations and other means.
Protection funds and donations shall be used exclusively for protection and shall not be diverted to other purposes.
articles.9:
Article 9 Subject to protecting historic and cultural heritage and historic character, appropriate cultural and tourism activities in historic and cultural districts and areas with historic character are encouraged and guided.
Chapter II — Protection Plans and Protection List
articles.10:
Article 10 The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of the protection plan for Nanjing as a historic and cultural city.
Based on that plan, plans for specific protected matters shall be prepared. In the municipal districts, the municipal urban and rural planning department shall prepare them together with relevant municipal and district departments. In Gaochun and Lishui, the County People's Government shall organize their preparation.
articles.11:
Article 11 A protection plan shall include: (1) basic information; (2) an assessment of historic and cultural value and current conditions; (3) requirements for protecting the traditional layout and historic character; (4) core protected and construction control areas for historic and cultural districts, towns, and villages; (5) protection principles, matters, boundaries, requirements, and measures; and (6) development intensity, use, and implementation plans.
A plan for a specific protected matter shall include the protection text, drawings, and relevant appendices.
articles.12: Article 12 Before a protection plan is prepared, the expert committee shall review it and opinions shall be solicited from relevant departments and the public. A hearing shall be held if a matter involves a major public interest.
articles.13: Article 13 After deliberation by the Standing Committee of the Nanjing Municipal People's Congress, the protection plan for the historic and cultural city shall be submitted for approval in accordance with the law. Unless laws or regulations require approval by a provincial-level or higher people's government or department, a protection plan shall be approved by the Municipal People's Government. No entity or individual may violate an approved plan. Any amendment shall be submitted for approval under the original procedure.
articles.14: Article 14 Construction within a protected area shall comply with the protection plan and shall not: (1) damage or demolish without authorization a building or structure with protection value; (2) damage the natural environment, traditional character, architectural or street layout, or spatial scale; (3) exceed controls on building height or bulk or violate requirements for architectural style, exterior appearance, or colors; (4) impair the authenticity or integrity of historic and cultural heritage; or (5) otherwise violate the protection plan.
articles.15:
Article 15 Before issuing a site-selection opinion for a construction project in a protected area or approving a construction design, the urban and rural planning department shall arrange expert review and public notice.
Design and construction entities for major historic and cultural protection projects shall hold the qualification grade required by the State.
articles.16: Article 16 For new, reconstructed, or extended buildings, structures, and infrastructure within a protected area, setbacks, spacing, sunlight, energy efficiency, earthquake resistance, road widths, and other matters shall meet current standards and codes. If existing conditions make compliance impossible, a design meeting protection requirements shall be prepared and implemented after approval. If municipal infrastructure cannot meet current standards, the construction department and urban and rural planning department shall determine a construction plan together. If fire-safety facilities or access routes cannot meet current standards, the public security fire agency and urban and rural planning department shall determine fire-safety safeguards together.
articles.17:
Article 17 Nanjing shall maintain a protection list, including matters approved and announced by the State Council or provincial people's government and matters already designated by the Municipal People's Government.
For another matter meeting the following criteria, the municipal urban and rural planning department and cultural relics department shall organize expert review and public notice. After deliberation by the protection committee, the Municipal People's Government shall approve and announce it for inclusion in the list: (1) an area with distinctive historic character, a certain scale, and relatively abundant cultural relics, reflecting the traditional character or local features of a historical period; (2) an ancient town or village with the traditional character of a particular historical period; (3) a relatively well-preserved historic street or lane with rich cultural content, distinctive features, and characteristics of the historic and cultural city; (4) a historic building reflecting historic character and local features that has protection value but has not been announced as a protected cultural relic or registered as an immovable cultural relic; (5) a key underground archaeological protection area; or (6) another matter requiring protection.
An adjustment to the protection list shall be submitted for approval and publication under the original procedure.
articles.18:
Article 18 The urban and rural planning, cultural relics, real estate, and other departments shall regularly survey the Municipality's historic and cultural resources and promptly recommend matters with protection value for inclusion in the protection list.
The cultural relics department shall collect and organize historical information on protected matters and investigate and assess their historic value.
The urban and rural planning department shall establish and maintain a geographic information system for protected matters.
articles.19:
Article 19 Any entity or individual may recommend to the municipal urban and rural planning department that a matter with protection value be included in the protection list.
Chapter III — Protection of the Old City's Layout and Urban Character
articles.20:
Article 20 The Municipal People's Government shall formulate a protection plan for the old city to strictly protect its historic character, overall layout, and natural environment; control the total scale of development, building bulk, and spatial dimensions; and ease population pressure.
The system of historic streets and lanes, cultural relics and historic sites, ancient or notable trees, traditional architectural character, intangible cultural heritage, historic urban fabric, and cultural continuity shall be protected.
The Municipal People's Government shall protect, use, renovate, and revitalize historic and cultural resources in the old city and improve its overall urban quality and cultural identity.
articles.21:
Article 21 The height of new buildings in the old city shall comply with the height controls by area in the protection plan. (1) South of Jiqing Road and Changle Road, new buildings shall not exceed 12 meters; between those roads and Jiankang Road and Shengzhou Road to the north, they shall not exceed 18 meters. (2) In historic and cultural districts and areas with historic character north of Jiankang Road and Shengzhou Road, new buildings shall comply with the controls in the protection plan. For new buildings around those areas, height and bulk shall be determined through viewshed analysis.
New high-rise buildings in the old city shall be strictly controlled in accordance with the protection plan.
articles.22:
Article 22 The three historic urban areas of Chengnan, Ming Palace, and the corridor from Gulou to Qingliang Mountain shall be strictly protected.
No elevated road or other high-volume motor-vehicle route may be newly built in a historic urban area, and no large municipal infrastructure impairing the cityscape may be constructed. Municipal, power, and communications lines shall be installed underground.
New buildings and structures in Chengnan shall be compatible with the historic character; existing buildings and structures that are incompatible shall be renovated gradually.
The layout of the imperial city and palace city, the moat system, and the remains of altars, temples, government offices, and other features in the Ming Palace historic urban area shall be protected. No new construction may take place within the Ming Palace City archaeological site or within 100 meters of it.
The original mountain-and-water environment and spatial pattern dominated by a high proportion of green space shall be maintained in the Gulou–Qingliang Mountain historic urban area.
articles.23:
Article 23 The Southern Tang axis along Zhonghua Road, the Ming dynasty axis along Yudao Street, and the Republican-era axis along Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan Road, and Zhongshan East Road shall be strictly protected. Their existing scale, alignment, and cross-sectional form shall be preserved. New buildings and structures on both sides shall be compatible with the axis's traditional architectural character in height, bulk, style, colors, and other respects.
The traditional character and existing street scale of Zhonghua Road between Jiankang Road and Zhonghuamen shall be preserved; the streetscape between Jiankang Road and Neiqiao shall be improved gradually to continue the southern section's character.
A 10-meter green belt shall be retained on each side of Yudao Street. No new construction may take place between Wuchaomen and Waiwulong Bridge. Between Waiwulong Bridge and Guanghua Gate, new buildings shall be set back at least 10 meters from the green line.
The three-lane, four-green-strip cross section and the characteristic plane trees along Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan Road, and Zhongshan East Road shall be preserved. Public buildings shall predominate along these roads.
articles.24:
Article 24 The remains and archaeological sites of Jiankang City of the Six Dynasties, the Southern Tang Jinling Palace City, the Ming Nanjing Palace City, and the Republican-era Nanjing City shall be strictly protected. No entity or individual may damage remains or sites within protected areas. Important remains discovered during archaeology or construction shall be protected at their original locations and displayed to the public as urban open space.
The Southern Tang and Ming capital city walls and moats shall be strictly protected. No entity or individual may damage surviving sections or the overall alignment of the Ming Outer City wall. Public green space 30 to 50 meters wide shall be delineated on each side of the wall foundations. Buildings and structures on Ming capital city-wall ruins designated by the cultural relics department shall be demolished.
No new building may be constructed within 30 meters of the Ming capital city wall or its remains. Within 30 to 50 meters, new buildings shall not exceed 12 meters in height.
articles.25: Article 25 In important view corridors from Gulou to Beijige and Jiuhua Mountain; from the south of Shizishan to the Stone City and, in the north, to the Yangtze River Bridge; from Zhonghuamen south to Yuhuatai and north to Neiqiao; from Wuchaomen south to Guanghua Gate and north to Fugui Mountain; from Shence Gate south to Beijige and east to Xiaohong Mountain; and from Xuanwu Lake to Zijin Mountain, the height and bulk of new buildings shall be controlled in accordance with the protection plan.
articles.26:
Article 26 The natural mountain-and-water landscape of Nanjing shall be strictly protected. The three branches of the Ningzhen Mountains shall be protected: the northern branch, including Qixia, Wulong, Mufu, and Shizi Mountains; the central branch, including Zhong, Fugui, Jiuhua, Jilong, Gulougang, Wutai, and Qingliang Mountains; and the southern branch, including Qinglong, Huanglong, Niushou, and Zutang Mountains. The Qinhuai and Jinchuan Rivers, historic moats, Xuanwu Lake, Mochou Lake, and other water bodies shall also be protected. Mountains shall not be excavated and trees felled without authorization, and water bodies shall not be filled in or covered without authorization.
Land within protected natural landscape areas shall be used primarily for green spaces. A necessary new public-service facility shall be compatible with its natural and cultural setting in height, bulk, style, and colors. Buildings, structures, and facilities inconsistent with the protection plan shall be renovated or demolished in accordance with the law.
Chapter IV — Protection of Historic Buildings
articles.27: Article 27 The facade, floor plan, courtyard, gateways, trees, and other features of a historic building shall not be damaged. An approved reconstruction or extension shall be compatible with the original building in height, bulk, style, materials, colors, and other respects.
articles.28:
Article 28 A historic building shall be protected at its original site. If protection at the original site is impossible because of public-interest needs and demolition or relocation is necessary, expert review shall be conducted in advance, followed by review by the municipal or county urban and rural planning department together with the cultural relics department at the same level and approval by the relevant provincial administrative department in accordance with the law.
Where a historic building is demolished, it shall be reconstructed elsewhere where feasible or a monument shall be placed at the original site to preserve and convey its historical information.
articles.29: Article 29 Where a qualified appraisal institution identifies a historic building as dangerous and reconstruction is necessary, a construction plan shall be prepared to preserve its original location, height, and exterior appearance. Any use of underground space shall be compatible with the building's historic character. The owner, user, or manager shall submit a written application to the municipal or county urban and rural planning department. That department shall organize expert review and decide whether to approve the application within 20 days after acceptance.
articles.30:
Article 30 The owner of a historic building shall use, maintain, and repair it in accordance with protection requirements. Where the owner, user, and manager have agreed otherwise on maintenance and repair duties, their agreement shall apply. When transferring or leasing a historic building, the transferor or lessor shall notify the transferee or lessee of protection requirements.
A proposal for external repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or alteration of the structure or use of a historic building shall be reviewed by the municipal or county urban and rural planning department together with the cultural relics and real estate departments at the same level, after which relevant procedures shall be completed in accordance with the law.
articles.31:
Article 31 The owner of a historic building shall bear the costs of its maintenance and repair, unless the owner, user, and manager have agreed otherwise.
If the costs genuinely cannot be borne, the owner, user, or manager may apply for a subsidy to the district or county real estate department, which shall submit the application to the municipal real estate department for approval. Subsidies shall be paid from protection funds.
The municipal real estate department shall repair historic buildings whose ownership is unknown or that are managed by the government.
articles.32: Article 32 Where an approved demolition, relocation, or repair of a historic building is necessary and the original records are incomplete or missing, the developer shall commission a qualified entity to survey and document the building. The survey materials shall be transferred to the municipal or county real estate department for preservation.
articles.33: Article 33 Outdoor advertisements are prohibited on historic buildings. Shop signs, markers, and other facilities shall comply with the protection plan, shall not damage the building itself, and shall be compatible with the surrounding environment and landscape.
articles.34:
Article 34 The municipal and county real estate departments shall establish archives and place uniform protection plaques on historic buildings that do not yet have them. They shall regularly inspect their use and protection. The owners, users, and managers shall cooperate with inspections and receive written notice of the results.
No entity or individual may install, move, alter, or damage a protection plaque without authorization.
articles.35:
Article 35 A building or structure with some protection value that has not been included in the protection list may be announced by the municipal or county urban and rural planning department as a building subject to planning control. It shall not be demolished without authorization. Where demolition is necessary, a plan shall be prepared and reviewed by the expert committee and approved by the municipal urban and rural planning department.
Chapter V — Protection of Other Matters
articles.36: Article 36 Famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, and ancient towns and villages shall receive holistic protection. Their traditional layout, historic character, and spatial scale and the natural landscape and environment connected with them shall be preserved.
articles.37: Article 37 Protective renewal and renovation of famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, and ancient towns and villages shall be carried out in an orderly manner under an approved construction design. Where residents must relocate for such renewal, relocation and compensation shall follow relevant laws and regulations.
articles.38: Article 38 No new construction or expansion is permitted within a core protected area of a historic and cultural district, except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. Such necessary facilities shall comply with construction controls in the protection plan.
articles.39:
Article 39 Historic environmental features and the traditional layout, alignment, and names of historic streets and lanes shall be strictly protected. Their existing frontages, spatial scale, traditional character, and environmental features shall be preserved.
Where a historic street or lane is widened, straightened, or rerouted, the names of its original segments shall be marked.
articles.40: Article 40 Before State-owned land-use rights are granted or allocated in the 15 key underground archaeological protection areas, including Tangshan, Xuecheng, Shitoucheng, Changganli, and Yuecheng, the land department shall commission the cultural relics department to conduct archaeological investigation and exploration of the land. If important remains or sites are found, the cultural relics department shall issue a written opinion and notify the land department.
articles.41: Article 41 The owner, user, or manager of an industrial enterprise or industrial heritage shall strengthen its protection and use and cooperate with surveys, assessments, designation, and archival work. During conversion of production, restructuring, auction, exchange, or other asset transactions, its historic features, including form and structure, shall be protected.
articles.42:
Article 42 For intangible cultural heritage projects on the World, national, provincial, or municipal lists—including Nanjing brocade, Nanjing paper-cutting, Nanjing gold foil, Jinling sutra-printing, and the Qinhuai Lantern Festival—the Municipal, District, and County People's Governments shall designate responsible protection entities, assign protection duties, and allocate dedicated funds for surveys, collection, emergency safeguarding, research, transmission, publicity, and education.
The responsible entity shall perform its protection duties under applicable rules on intangible cultural heritage.
articles.43:
Article 43 The Municipal, District, and County People's Governments shall encourage and support representative transmitters of local intangible cultural heritage by providing necessary premises, funding, and other support for transmission activities.
Representative transmitters shall explore, collect, and organize valuable intangible cultural heritage materials, train successors, and actively organize or participate in related displays and performances.
Chapter VI — Legal Liability
articles.44: Article 44 Where a State organ or its staff commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations, the Municipal, District, or County People's Government or relevant competent department shall order correction and impose administrative sanctions in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel: (1) failing to prepare or amend a protection plan or designate or adjust the protection list under statutory procedures; (2) failing to perform approval duties under statutory procedures or the protection plan; (3) failing to supervise the state of protected matters or inadequately supervise approved renovation or use; (4) failing to accept reports or complaints or investigate violations in accordance with the law; (5) abusing official powers, neglecting duties, or engaging in favoritism or malpractice; or (6) other violations prescribed by laws and regulations.
articles.45: Article 45 Where a person damages the layout of a historic street or lane or unlawfully widens it during urban construction or real-estate development in violation of these Regulations, the municipal or county urban and rural planning department shall order restoration of the original condition or other remedial measures within a specified period. If the person fails to comply by the deadline, the department may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, it shall impose a fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual. The violator shall compensate for any losses.
articles.46: Article 46 Where a person installs, moves, alters, or damages a protection plaque for a historic building without authorization, the municipal or county real estate department shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 200 to RMB 2,000.
articles.47:
Article 47 Where a person installs an outdoor advertisement on a historic building or installs a shop sign, marker, or other external facility that does not comply with the protection plan, the urban administration law-enforcement department shall order correction or restoration of the original condition within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 5,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 200 to RMB 2,000 on an individual.
Chapter VII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.48:
Article 48 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 December 2010.
