FBMCLI.10.1421008.title: Regulations of Suzhou Municipality on the Protection of the National Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to protect Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city and preserve and carry forward fine traditional culture, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Law of the People's Republic of China on Intangible Cultural Heritage, the State Council Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to planning, protection, administration, and use of Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city.
The primary focus of protection is the historic urban area, comprising the ancient city within the moat (the ‘one city’), the Shantang and Shangtang lines (the ‘two lines’), and the Huqiu, Xiyuan-Liuyuan, and Hanshan Temple areas (the ‘three areas’) as defined in the protection plan.
Protected matters include the overall layout and character of the historic urban area; historic and cultural districts and areas; waterways; protected cultural relics; underground archaeological zones; Suzhou gardens; ancient architecture and city walls; traditional residences; ancient or notable trees; Wu-culture place names; industrial heritage and traditional industries; intangible cultural heritage; and other matters protected by laws and regulations.
Where laws or regulations separately provide for protection of cultural relics, Suzhou gardens, ancient architecture and city walls, ancient or notable trees, Wu-culture place names, or intangible cultural heritage, those provisions shall prevail.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of protection first, science-based planning, appropriate use, and coordinated development. It shall properly balance economic and social development with historic and cultural protection, preserve and continue the traditional layout and historic character, protect the natural and cultural landscapes connected with them, preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage, and build a historic and cultural city that continues traditional culture while meeting modern urban functions and contemporary living needs.
articles.4:
Article 4 The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protection of Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city and incorporate it into the Municipality's economic and social development plan.
The People's Government of Gusu District shall organize specific protection work in the historic urban area.
The people's governments of the other districts shall organize protection work in other areas within their respective jurisdictions.
articles.5:
Article 5 The Municipal People's Government shall establish a coordination body for protection of Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city to coordinate, guide, and supervise protection work and: (1) study major policies and measures for protection, administration, and use; (2) review relevant protection plans; (3) oversee allocation and use of dedicated protection funds; (4) review the protection list and proposed adjustments; (5) study major construction projects and review solutions to major protection issues; (6) guide and coordinate responses to major emergencies; (7) guide, coordinate, and oversee protection work by member entities; and (8) perform other duties assigned by the Municipal People's Government.
The coordination body shall comprise responsible officials of the Municipal People's Government and relevant departments and of Gusu and other relevant district people's governments. The Municipal People's Government shall determine its establishment, term, and rules of procedure.
articles.6: Article 6 The coordination body's office shall be located in the People's Government of Gusu District and shall: (1) organize preparation of the protection list and proposed adjustments; (2) publicize and implement laws and regulations on protection; (3) organize or assist relevant departments in surveys and research and in collecting and organizing information; (4) organize protection education and training, academic research, and external exchanges; and (5) perform other duties assigned by the coordination body.
articles.7:
Article 7 The municipal urban and rural planning department shall prepare relevant protection plans and supervise and administer their implementation.
The municipal culture and cultural relics department shall supervise and administer protection of cultural relics, ancient architecture and city walls, and intangible cultural heritage.
The departments responsible for landscaping and greening, water affairs, civil affairs, housing and urban-rural development, municipal administration, public security, transport, and other matters shall perform related protection duties according to their respective responsibilities.
articles.8:
Article 8 Under the principles of area-based responsibility and coordination across administrative sectors, the Municipal People's Government shall formulate specific measures reasonably defining protection duties of the Municipality, Gusu District, and their departments and shifting administrative responsibilities and resources to lower levels.
The People's Government of Gusu District shall assign its protection duties to its departments and subdistrict offices and carry out comprehensive administrative law enforcement in accordance with the law.
articles.9:
Article 9 The Municipal People's Government shall establish an expert advisory committee for protection of Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city. The committee shall advise on and assess major matters, including protection plans, protection lists, and construction administration, and provide recommendations.
The Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Gusu District shall establish and improve a hearing system for major protection matters. Experts and members of the public shall be invited to hearings on protection plans and designation of historic areas and traditional residences. Hearing results shall be an important reference for decisions.
articles.10:
Article 10 The Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Gusu District shall include the costs of planning, construction, operation, maintenance, and administration of infrastructure and dedicated protection funds in their respective budgets.
The Municipal People's Government shall establish an industrial transformation and upgrading fund to advance industrial restructuring.
The Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Gusu District shall guide and encourage social capital to participate in protection.
articles.11:
Article 11 The Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Gusu District shall strengthen public education and awareness and encourage public participation through public-benefit organizations, volunteer services, and other means.
The Municipal People's Government may propose establishing a commemorative day for protection of Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city and submit the proposal to the Standing Committee of the Municipal People's Congress for decision under the prescribed procedure.
articles.12:
Article 12 All entities and individuals have a duty to protect Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city and may dissuade, report, or lodge complaints against violations damaging its protection.
The Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Gusu District shall commend and reward outstanding contributors.
Chapter II — Protection Planning
articles.13:
Article 13 The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of the protection plan for the historic and cultural city and submit it to the provincial people's government for approval and to the State Council departments responsible for urban and rural planning and cultural relics for filing.
Based on that plan, the Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation and approval of protection plans for historic and cultural districts in accordance with the rules.
Based on the protection plan for the historic and cultural city and detailed regulatory plans, the People's Government of Gusu District shall organize preparation of protection plans for historic areas and submit them to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
articles.14: Article 14 The authority organizing preparation shall publish drafts of protection plans for the historic and cultural city, historic and cultural districts, and historic areas on the government website or in major local news media and solicit opinions from experts and the public through review meetings, hearings, or other means. Drafts shall be published for no fewer than 30 days.
articles.15: Article 15 Before a protection plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic and cultural district is submitted for approval as required, it shall be deliberated by the Standing Committee of the Suzhou Municipal People's Congress. The Municipal People's Government shall study and address the deliberation opinions.
articles.16: Article 16 Within 30 days after approval, protection plans for the historic and cultural city, historic and cultural districts, and historic areas shall be published on the government website or in major local news media.
articles.17: Article 17 An approved protection plan for the historic and cultural city, historic and cultural district, or historic area shall not be amended without authorization. Any necessary amendment shall follow the original procedure.
articles.18:
Article 18 Based on the protection plan, the municipal urban and rural planning department shall prepare urban designs for the historic urban area and other key areas and submit them to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
The urban design for a key area shall be incorporated into the detailed regulatory plan and reflected in its relevant indicators. If a detailed regulatory plan does not reflect the urban design's content and requirements, it shall be amended promptly.
Chapter III — Protected Matters and Requirements
articles.19: Article 19 The historic urban area shall holistically preserve the traditional checkerboard layout of waterways and streets running parallel and adjacent to one another and its distinctive character of small bridges, flowing water, white walls, dark tiles, historic sites, and famous gardens. Protection shall focus on: (1) graded height controls throughout the area and protected view corridors to Yunyan Temple Pagoda (Huqiu Pagoda), Ruiguang Pagoda, Baosi Temple Pagoda (Beisi Pagoda), the Twin Pagodas, and other ancient pagodas, with building height and bulk controlled within those corridors; and (2) protection of the area's fabric and distinctive traditional streets and lanes, including their spatial form and scale. Their frontages shall preserve historic continuity and present traditional character, and building form, layout, bulk, materials, and colors shall be compatible with the surroundings.
articles.20: Article 20 Construction in the historic urban area shall comply with the protection plan and: (1) shall not add land for industrial or storage use; (2) shall control the eave height of new riverside buildings along waterways and not damage the traditional character of riverside buildings; (3) shall not install new overhead utility lines, and utility lines of the same kind that can be combined underground shall be combined and buried; (4) new construction projects shall separate stormwater and sewage and connect sewage pipes to the urban sewage collection system. If street-space limitations make separation impossible, combined wastewater shall be discharged into that system and not into a river; (5) building colors shall primarily be black, white, or gray, reflecting the city's understated and elegant character; (6) plazas, sidewalks, and traditional streets and lanes shall use paving materials and forms reflecting traditional character; and (7) buildings and structures shall not be newly constructed, reconstructed, or extended in violation of the plan. Existing unlawful buildings, structures, and facilities shall be demolished in accordance with the law. Lawful ones that do not comply with the plan shall be renovated or demolished gradually.
articles.21: Article 21 A historic and cultural district shall delineate core protected and construction control areas and: (1) control the surrounding landscape environment, preserve the original spatial layout and scale, and not alter the street and lane fabric; (2) permit no new construction or expansion of buildings or structures in the core protected area except for necessary infrastructure and public services or reconstruction of a dangerous building at its original site with its original area, height, and design; (3) require new, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures in the construction control area to meet the district's character and visual-landscape requirements and be compatible in height, form, bulk, colors, and style; and (4) relocate gradually factories and warehouses that do not comply with the protection plan or impair the traditional character.
articles.22: Article 22 The overall character of a historic area shall receive focused protection and its historic continuity shall be preserved. Protection shall be combined with appropriate use to strengthen the area's economic and social vitality. Construction within the protected area shall not alter the traditional layout or character.
articles.23:
Article 23 Internal waterways shall be connected with one another and with external water systems. The historic urban area's principal water system of ‘three vertical lines, three horizontal lines, and one ring’ shall be protected, important historic waterways restored as appropriate, and existing waterways shall not be filled in or blocked.
The Grand Canal (Suzhou section), a World Cultural Heritage site, and the ancient city moat and its character-protection buffers on both sides shall be protected.
Waterways shall be cleaned routinely and dredged regularly to maintain flowing water and improve water quality.
articles.24:
Article 24 Repairs to traditional embankments, landing stages, and bridges in the historic urban area shall use traditional techniques and materials and continue the traditional character. Any necessary new embankment, landing stage, wharf, or bridge shall reflect traditional features and provide supporting functions for water transport, sightseeing, and safety and rescue.
Ancient wells shall be protected, maintained, and used appropriately. Important damaged wells shall be repaired in conjunction with street, lane, or courtyard spaces and their functions restored gradually.
articles.25:
Article 25 Planning and construction of the historic urban area and surrounding areas shall be coordinated to continue the traditional character and highlight the features of a water town. Areas outside the historic urban area shall support optimization and upgrading of industry, transport, the environment, and other aspects within it.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.26:
Article 26 The Municipal People's Government shall maintain a classified protection list for Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city. Protected matters approved and announced by the State, provincial, or Municipal People's Government shall be included directly.
The People's Government of Gusu District shall regularly survey protected matters together with relevant municipal departments. The first survey shall be completed within one year after these Regulations take effect.
The People's Government of Gusu District shall prepare and revise the protection list together with relevant municipal departments. After expert review and public notice, the list shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval and publication.
Any entity or individual may recommend inclusion in the protection list to the People's Government of Gusu District.
articles.27:
Article 27 The People's Government of Gusu District shall place protection signs on protected matters. Signs shall comply with relevant laws and regulations and standards of relevant international organizations and be compatible with Suzhou's traditional character.
The People's Government of Gusu District shall maintain archives for the protection list.
articles.28:
Article 28 Where laws or regulations prescribe responsible persons and protection duties for a category of protected matter, those provisions shall apply.
The owner of a traditional residence shall be responsible for its protection. If the owner cannot be located or title is unclear, the actual user or manager shall be responsible. The owner may agree with the actual user or manager on protection duties, but the agreement shall not exempt any party from its own duties.
The actual user shall use the traditional residence lawfully and safely and cooperate with the owner in safety inspections and repairs.
articles.29:
Article 29 A public-housing tenant in a protected cultural relic, ancient building, or traditional residence in the historic urban area shall perform protection duties under the lease and shall not: (1) damage or destroy the property; (2) reconstruct or extend it without authorization; (3) refuse to cooperate with the owner in repairs; (4) sublet it without authorization; (5) change its use without authorization; or (6) use it for unlawful activities.
The housing and urban-rural development and culture and cultural relics departments shall supervise owners and tenants of public housing in such properties and ensure that they perform their lease obligations and protection duties.
articles.30:
Article 30 Within two years after these Regulations take effect, the municipal departments responsible for public security, housing and urban-rural development, urban and rural planning, municipal administration, transport, water affairs, culture and cultural relics, education, landscaping and greening, and other matters shall assist the People's Government of Gusu District in formulating special technical specifications for urban safety and the construction, administration, and safeguards of infrastructure suited to protection of the historic urban area. The specifications shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval and publication.
Before those specifications take effect, where municipal infrastructure, fire-safety facilities or access routes, or repairs, relocation, or reconstruction of ancient buildings and traditional residences cannot meet current technical codes, the Municipal People's Government shall organize the relevant municipal departments, the People's Government of Gusu District, and industry experts to assess the matter and determine construction, administration, and safeguard measures suited to protection.
articles.31:
Article 31 The municipal urban and rural planning department shall formulate design guidelines and pattern books for traditional residences together with the municipal housing and urban-rural development and culture and cultural relics departments and the People's Government of Gusu District. They shall specify height, bulk, exterior appearance, colors, materials, details, construction techniques, and other requirements.
A person responsible for protection who maintains, repairs, reconstructs, renovates, or extends a traditional residence shall follow the guidelines and pattern books and preserve its traditional height, bulk, exterior appearance, colors, and other features.
No entity or individual may damage or destroy a traditional residence. If it is at risk of damage, the responsible person shall promptly maintain and repair it. If that person lacks the capacity to do so, the People's Government of Gusu District shall take protective measures.
The Municipal People's Government shall adopt support policies encouraging domestic and foreign organizations and individuals to purchase or lease traditional residences. A purchaser or lessee shall perform protection duties under these Regulations.
articles.32:
Article 32 The Municipal People's Government shall establish a compensation system for protection of the historic urban area and provide appropriate compensation through subsidies or other policy measures for losses suffered by entities and individuals as a result of government protection measures.
The People's Government of Gusu District shall provide subsidies where a person responsible for a traditional residence repairs or renovates it in accordance with the protection plan and technical standards, or where a housing owner and public-housing user actively cooperate with government expropriation or relocation by agreement.
Compensation and subsidies under the preceding paragraphs shall be covered through the special protection fund for Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city.
articles.33:
Article 33 The Municipal People's Government and the People's Government of Gusu District shall promote appropriate use of protected matters through policy guidance, financial assistance, and other means.
Social organizations and other parties are encouraged to use historic resources appropriately to develop industries consistent with the protection plan and conduct business consistent with industry-layout plans.
Use of idle buildings such as old factories and warehouses for culture, tourism, elder care, and other activities is encouraged. The Municipal People's Government shall formulate detailed measures separately.
articles.34:
Article 34 The following activities are prohibited in Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city: (1) occupying gardens, green spaces, waterways and lanes, traditional streets and lanes, road facilities, or other matters without authorization; (2) carving or defacing ancient buildings, ancient or notable trees, or other protected matters; (3) installing outdoor advertisements without authorization; (4) installing, moving, altering, or damaging a protection sign without authorization; (5) demolishing an immovable cultural relic without authorization; or (6) other activities likely to damage protected matters.
Outdoor food barbecues are prohibited in the historic urban area.
articles.35:
Article 35 The Municipal People's Government shall adopt support policies for protection and transmission of intangible cultural heritage and encourage investigation, collection, organization, and research on traditional culture, arts, folk customs, and arts and crafts through subsidies from the special protection fund and free training.
Use of traditional residences to display Suzhou's traditional way of life and folk customs to the public is encouraged.
Establishment of bases for intangible cultural heritage research and transmission, film and television production, cultural and creative industries, local cultural research, and other activities is encouraged.
The Municipal People's Government shall adopt support policies for promoting the Suzhou dialect. Primary and secondary schools and kindergartens are encouraged to teach it; residents' and villagers' committees are encouraged to organize learning activities; and news media are encouraged to provide Suzhou-dialect programming.
articles.36:
Article 36 The mix of activities in the historic urban area shall comply with the protection plan.
The People's Government of Gusu District shall formulate lawful catalogues of industries to guide, control, or prohibit and support technology and creative industries, cultural tourism, specialty commerce, headquarters-based economic activity, and other modern services, improving cultural transmission, tourism and leisure, traditional industries, and Suzhou-style living.
Education, science, culture, health, sports, and other public services shall be retained reasonably and improved to meet residents' needs.
articles.37:
Article 37 Road connections between the historic urban area and surrounding areas shall be improved and the road network laid out rationally.
Slow traffic shall be encouraged in the historic urban area, with right of way protected and pedestrian and cycling areas and routes increased as appropriate. Streets and lanes shall be adapted for cyclists and pedestrians. Non-motorized transport and walking shall be the principal modes in historic and cultural districts.
Parking and transport interchange facilities shall be expanded outside the historic urban area to reduce motor vehicles entering or passing through it. Parking facilities meeting residents' needs shall be planned and constructed in moderation inside the historic urban area, and measures such as staggered parking, sharing public parking resources, and tiered time-based parking charges shall be used to ease parking difficulties.
articles.38:
Article 38 The historic urban area shall apply total traffic-volume controls and zoned traffic administration, reasonably increase road-use costs for motor-vehicle drivers, and gradually expand areas where motor vehicles are prohibited, restricted, or subject to one-way traffic.
Priority shall be given to public transport, with motorized travel organized primarily around public transit. Rail transit shall be expanded and built more quickly. Bus-only lanes, transit-priority signals, interchange hubs, bus bays, optimized routes, neighborhood shuttle loops, and an integrated transit system shall be developed scientifically.
Water transport shall be laid out rationally and developed in moderation, including distinctive sightseeing routes.
Environmentally friendly public buses and sightseeing boats shall be used in the historic urban area and their use promoted.
articles.39: Article 39 The People's Government of Gusu District shall recruit and train professionals in planning, repair of ancient buildings, Suzhou crafts, restoration of ancient or notable trees, and other fields related to protection of Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city; establish or attract specialized research institutions; and increase investment in training and use of professionals.
articles.40: Article 40 In accordance with the protection plan, population density in the historic urban area shall be controlled and the population structure optimized through administration of the points-based system for the floating population, housing leases, industry adjustment, and other measures.
articles.41:
Article 41 The People's Government of Gusu District shall establish an information management system covering geographic, historic and cultural, planning, place-name, and other information to improve intelligent administration of protection work.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.42: Article 42 Where laws or regulations prescribe penalties for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.43:
Article 43 Where a person responsible for protection violates Article 31(2) by repairing, reconstructing, renovating, or extending a traditional residence in a manner inconsistent with the design guidelines and pattern books and damages its traditional height, bulk, exterior appearance, colors, or other features, the relevant administrative law-enforcement department of Gusu District shall order restoration of the original condition or other remedial measures within a specified period. If serious consequences result, it shall impose a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual. The person shall bear civil liability for property losses caused to others.
Where a person intentionally damages a traditional residence, or a responsible person with the capacity to maintain and repair it fails to perform protection duties and causes damage or collapse, the relevant department shall order restoration or other remedial measures within a specified period. If serious consequences result, it shall impose a fine of RMB 200,000 to RMB 500,000 on an entity or RMB 100,000 to RMB 200,000 on an individual. The person shall bear civil liability for property losses caused to others.
articles.44:
Article 44 Where a person violates Article 34(1)(4) by installing, moving, altering, or damaging a protection sign without authorization, the relevant administrative law-enforcement department of Gusu District shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 1,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual.
Where a person violates Article 34(2) by conducting outdoor food barbecues in the historic urban area, the relevant administrative law-enforcement department of Gusu District shall order correction, confiscate the barbecue equipment and unlawful income, and impose a fine of RMB 500 to RMB 5,000. If circumstances are serious, the fine shall be RMB 5,000 to RMB 20,000.
articles.45: Article 45 Information concerning any entity or individual penalized for a violation under these Regulations shall be included in the public credit information system and subject to joint sanctions as prescribed.
articles.46:
Article 46 A staff member of the Municipal or Gusu District People's Government or a relevant competent department who neglects duties, abuses official powers, or engages in favoritism or malpractice in violation of these Regulations shall be sanctioned in accordance with the law. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.47: Article 47 For purposes of these Regulations: ‘historic and cultural district’ means a district in the historic urban area with exceptionally rich cultural relics and a concentration of ancient buildings and traditional residences that substantially and authentically reflects the traditional layout and historic character and is of a certain scale; ‘historic area’ means an area in the historic urban area containing numerous cultural relics or a concentration of traditional residences that substantially and authentically reflects Suzhou's traditional street and lane character and is of a certain scale; and ‘traditional residence’ means a civil building constructed during any historical period in the historic urban area that reflects Suzhou's traditional character and construction techniques, social ethics, aesthetic views, or other cultural elements, excluding a protected cultural relic, an immovable cultural relic not yet designated as a protected cultural relic, or an ancient building.
articles.48: Article 48 A district people's government outside the historic urban area shall, under the principle of territorial administration and by reference to the specific protection duties assigned to the People's Government of Gusu District under these Regulations, protect Suzhou as a national historic and cultural city within its administrative area.
articles.49:
Article 49 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 March 2018.

Regulations cited in this document
Central regulations
Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics (2017 Revision)
Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages (2017 Revision)
Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China (2015 Revision)
Law of the People's Republic of China on Intangible Cultural Heritage

FBMCLI.10.7321447.title: Regulations of Zunyi Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2023 Amendment)

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to protect Zunyi as a historic and cultural city, carry forward the legacy of the Red Army, tell Zunyi's story, promote the spirit of the Zunyi Conference, continue outstanding traditional culture, and practice core socialist values, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Guizhou Province on the Long March National Cultural Park, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to planning, protection, administration, and use of Zunyi as a historic and cultural city.
Protected matters center on Red Army Long March culture and include the overall layout and character of historic urban areas, historic and cultural districts, famous towns and villages with distinctive northern Guizhou regional culture, and related cultural relics, historic buildings, buildings of traditional character, ancient or notable trees, traditional place names, traditional villages, and intangible cultural heritage.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, protection first, and appropriate use. It shall properly balance economic and social development with historic and cultural protection, preserve and continue the traditional layout and historic character, and preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage.
articles.4:
Article 4 The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protection of the historic and cultural city.
The County People's Governments shall protect protected matters within their respective jurisdictions.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall perform protection duties under these Regulations.
articles.5:
Article 5 The municipal and county-level housing and urban-rural development departments shall review, submit for approval, implement, supervise, and administer protection plans.
The municipal and county-level cultural relics departments shall protect and administer cultural relics within protected areas.
The departments and institutions responsible for Party history, archives, finance, education, forestry, tourism, local chronicles, emergency management, natural resources, comprehensive administrative law enforcement, and other matters shall perform relevant protection and administration duties within their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
Article 6 The Municipal People's Government shall establish a protection committee for the historic and cultural city to coordinate protection work and study major protection matters. Its day-to-day work shall be handled by the municipal housing and urban-rural development department.
The committee shall establish an expert advisory group with experts in planning, culture, cultural relics, architecture, religion, tourism, folk customs, law, and other fields to review and assess protection lists, plans, technical specifications, and standards.
articles.7:
Article 7 The Municipal and County People's Governments shall incorporate protection of the historic and cultural city into economic and social development plans and include necessary funds in the budgets at the same level.
They shall adopt policies to guide and encourage social capital to participate lawfully through donations, funding, investment, and other means.
articles.8: Article 8 The Municipal and County People's Governments shall supervise and inspect implementation of protection plans by relevant administrative departments and regularly report on protection work to the Standing Committee of the people's congress at the same level.
articles.9: Article 9 Where protection of the historic and cultural city causes property loss to a citizen, legal person, or other organization, the relevant people's government shall provide compensation in accordance with the law.
articles.10:
Article 10 The Municipal People's Government shall commend or reward entities and individuals that make significant contributions to protection, in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions.
Chapter II — Protected Matters
articles.11:
Article 11 A protection-list system shall apply. The Municipal People's Government shall establish classified protection lists stating each protected matter's name, location, ownership, date of construction, historic value, and other particulars.
Within one year after these Regulations take effect, the Municipal People's Government shall formulate procedures for nomination, designation, approval, removal, and publication of protected matters and protection lists.
articles.12:
Article 12 A protection sign shall be placed on each matter included in the protection list. Within six months after publication of the list, the County People's Government shall organize installation of the signs.
A sign shall state the protected matter's name, number, location, date of construction, cultural information, and other particulars and may be translated into a foreign language as needed.
No entity or individual may install, move, cover, alter, or damage a protection sign without authorization.
articles.13:
Article 13 Every five years, the County People's Government shall survey or collect information on historic and cultural resources in its administrative area. It shall promptly verify leads on protected resources submitted by entities or individuals and designate any matter with protection value for interim protection.
Within 10 days after such designation, the township or town people's government or subdistrict office where the matter is located shall notify the owner, user, or entrusted manager in writing and specify protection duties.
articles.14: Article 14 The focus of protection shall be revolutionary heritage, Tusi heritage, and regional cultural heritage, including: (1) the system of revolutionary memorial sites associated with the Zunyi Conference, including battle sites, residences of notable figures, important conference venues, and Long March routes of the Red Army; (2) Bozhou Tusi heritage represented by Hailongtun, a World Cultural Heritage site, the tombs of Yang Can and Yang Hui, and the Yangmacheng archaeological site; and (3) other regional heritage, including liquor, tea, Yin Zhen, Shatan, resistance-war, westward relocation of Zhejiang University, Third Front construction, ethnic, and folk cultures.
articles.15: Article 15 The protected boundaries of the historic urban area extend east to the Inner Ring Road, south to the ridgeline of Laoya Mountain, west to the ridgeline of Fuhou Mountain, and north to the ridgeline of Fenghuang Mountain. Protection shall focus on: (1) the overall layout of the old and new urban areas encircled by Fenghuang, Fuhou, and Laoya Mountains and traversed by the Xiang River; (2) the traditional layout of Ziyin Road, Minzhu Road, Yangliu Street, Laosha Lane, and other streets and lanes; (3) view corridors from Fuhou Mountain through Memorial Square, the Zunyi Conference site, and Zunyi Memorial Park to Fenghuang Mountain, and from Huilong Temple through Xiangshan Temple to Taoyuan Mountain; (4) the revolutionary memorial network of the Zunyi Conference site, Chairman Mao's residence, the former site of the General Political Department of the Red Army, the Red Army battle site on Laoya Mountain, the Deng Ping Tomb, and other locations; (5) religious and cultural sites such as Xiangshan and Huilong Temples; and (6) other matters specified in the protection plan.
articles.16:
Article 16 The old-city historic and cultural district is within the historic urban area and shall be protected by reference to the provisions concerning protected matters in that area.
The Gaoqiao Historic and Cultural District shall protect the overall spatial layout, fabric, and character of the Changzheng No. 12 industrial complex.
Famous historic and cultural towns include Tucheng in Xishui County, Datong in Chishui, Yongxing in Meitan County, Anchang in Zheng'an County, and Luolong in Daozhen Gelao and Miao Autonomous County, as well as other nationally or provincially designated towns. Famous villages include Bing'an in Chishui, Longtan in Daping Town of Wuchuan Gelao Autonomous County, Shatan in Xinzhou Town of Honghuagang District, and Manao in Suiyang Town of Fenggang County, as well as other nationally or provincially designated villages.
Chapter III — Protection Measures
articles.17:
Article 17 The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of protection plans for the historic and cultural city and historic and cultural districts. The County People's Governments shall organize preparation of protection plans for famous towns and villages.
A plan for a newly designated historic and cultural town, village, or district shall be completed within one year after its designation and announcement.
articles.18: Article 18 Before submission for approval, a protection plan for the historic and cultural city or a historic and cultural district shall be deliberated by the Standing Committee of the Municipal People's Congress. Before submission for approval, a protection plan for a famous town or village shall be reviewed and approved by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.19: Article 19 Based on the protection plans, the Municipal and County People's Governments shall prepare annual implementation plans specifying work tasks, protection responsibilities, and concrete measures to ensure effective implementation.
articles.20: Article 20 The overall protection plan and special protection plans for the historic and cultural city shall be incorporated into territorial spatial planning.
articles.21: Article 21 The person responsible for protection of a historic and cultural district, famous town, or famous village shall be the subdistrict office or township or town people's government where it is located. The responsible person shall: (1) preserve the integrity of the traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale, and historic environmental features of buildings and structures in the protected area; (2) conduct routine inspections, promptly stop conduct damaging historic and cultural heritage, and notify the relevant administrative department; (3) keep the area clean and orderly; (4) ensure proper operation of fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and access routes and promptly take measures to eliminate hazards; and (5) perform other duties under laws and regulations.
articles.22: Article 22 The owner of a historic building or building of traditional character shall be responsible for its protection. If the owner cannot be located or ownership is unclear, the user or entrusted manager shall be responsible; if none can be identified, the township or town people's government or subdistrict office where it is located shall be responsible. The responsible person shall: (1) preserve the building's original height, bulk, exterior appearance, and colors; (2) repair it in accordance with technical repair specifications; (3) ensure structural safety and proper operation of fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and routes, promptly take measures to eliminate hazards, and notify the competent department; and (4) perform other duties under laws and regulations.
articles.23: Article 23 Protection and use of the historic urban area shall comply with the protection plan and: (1) preserve its overall layout and protect the Xiang River, its embankments, and the ecological environment of Fenghuang, Fuhou, and Laoya Mountains; (2) control the scale and bulk of traditional streets and lanes and preserve their urban fabric and distinctive trees, wells, walls, paving, streets, and other features; (3) keep view corridors unobstructed and control landscape character and building height along them; (4) use traditional materials and forms for paving plazas, sidewalks, streets, and lanes; (5) prohibit new overhead utility lines and combine lines of the same kind underground where feasible; (6) prohibit additional land for industrial or storage use; (7) prohibit construction, reconstruction, or expansion of buildings or structures in violation of the plan; and (8) meet other requirements under laws and regulations.
articles.24: Article 24 Protection of historic and cultural districts, famous towns, and famous villages shall comply with the protection plan and: (1) control the surrounding landscape environment, preserve the original spatial layout and scale, and not alter the street and lane fabric; (2) preserve the original height, bulk, style, and colors of buildings and structures within the protected area; (3) permit no new construction or expansion in a core protected area except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities; (4) require new, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures in a construction control area to meet requirements for preserving the district's, town's, or village's character and visual landscape and to be compatible in height, form, bulk, colors, and style; (5) keep roads in historic and cultural districts accessible, encourage slow traffic, establish pedestrian routes, and strictly restrict motor vehicles from core protected areas; and (6) meet other requirements under laws and regulations.
articles.25: Article 25 Buildings and structures in the protected areas of the historic urban area, historic and cultural districts, famous towns, and famous villages, other than protected cultural relics, shall receive classified protection: (1) a historic building may be repaired or improved, and adaptive use suited to its characteristics is encouraged; (2) a building of traditional character may be repaired and maintained and its interior facilities improved to meet everyday needs, provided its exterior character is not changed; and (3) another building or structure compatible with the historic character shall be retained, repaired, and improved; one that conflicts with the historic character shall be reconstructed or demolished in accordance with the law.
articles.26: Article 26 The following conduct damaging a historic building or building of traditional character is prohibited: (1) producing, storing, or selling flammable, explosive, or corrosive substances; (2) changing its exterior form or style; (3) constructing buildings or structures on its roof or terrace or using its exterior wall for that purpose; (4) damaging its principal load-bearing structure or otherwise endangering its safety; (5) adding doors or windows without authorization or occupying streets, lanes, exterior wall areas, or shared courtyard space when renovating a street-facing facade; (6) hanging, installing, or placing advertisements, signs, equipment, or facilities that impair its spatial setting or landscape character; or (7) other conduct prohibited by laws and regulations.
articles.27:
Article 27 New or reconstructed buildings and structures around a historic building shall comply with the protection plan. Their height, bulk, use, color scheme, and architectural style shall be compatible with the historic building and the original spatial landscape. Buildings that conflict with the historic character or impair the historic building's setting shall be reconstructed or gradually demolished in accordance with the protection plan and the law.
No new enterprise that obstructs protection of a historic building may be established nearby. An existing obstructive enterprise shall be relocated gradually as required by the protection plan.
articles.28:
Article 28 The person responsible for protection of a historic building or building of traditional character shall repair it in accordance with technical repair specifications.
Where the responsible person for a non-State-owned historic building or building of traditional character lacks the capacity to bear repair costs, the County People's Government where it is located may provide a subsidy or exchange or acquire the building.
Within one year after these Regulations take effect, the Municipal People's Government shall formulate and publish technical repair specifications and subsidy measures.
articles.29: Article 29 A system of protection officers shall be established for protected cultural relics and historic buildings. Where travel difficulties or other circumstances make routine inspection and care difficult, township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices may hire protection officers through service procurement or other means.
articles.30:
Article 30 In accordance with the protection plan, the Municipal and County People's Governments shall give priority to construction and improvement of roads, water supply and drainage, electricity, fire-safety, and other infrastructure in the historic urban area and protected areas of historic and cultural districts, famous towns, and famous villages.
If protection needs make it impossible to install infrastructure under current technical standards and codes, the relevant departments responsible for fire safety, housing and urban-rural development, transport, water affairs, and other matters shall formulate safeguards suited to those needs.
articles.31: Article 31 Where environmental improvement in a protected area of the historic urban area, historic and cultural district, famous town, or famous village is required under the protection plan, the County People's Government where it is located shall formulate an improvement plan. After soliciting opinions from relevant departments, experts, interested parties, and the public and obtaining review and approval from the protection committee, the plan shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval and organized for implementation.
articles.32:
Article 32 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall be coordinated with construction and protection of the Long March National Cultural Park.
Based on the overall layout of revolutionary cultural resources and existing protection and use facilities, the Municipal and County People's Governments shall develop a Long March cultural park centered on the Zunyi Conference site, focused on the Central Red Army's Long March routes while in Zunyi, and featuring important sites associated with classic Red Army routes.
They shall accelerate planning and construction and implement protection and development requirements for the park's control and protection areas, themed display areas, culture-tourism integration areas, and traditional-use areas.
articles.33:
Article 33 Where historic and cultural resources of the historic and cultural city are seriously damaged, the municipal housing and urban-rural development department, together with the cultural relics department, shall petition the Municipal People's Government to order the County People's Government where the resources are located to take remedial measures within a specified period to prevent further damage.
Chapter IV — Transmission and Use
articles.34: Article 34 Subject to the protection plan, reasonable use of historic and cultural sites is encouraged and supported, as is the development of cultural tourism, provided that local natural landscapes, cultural landscapes, and historic and cultural resources are not damaged.
articles.35:
Article 35 The Municipal and County People's Governments shall organize public education, including special reports, lectures by notable figures, and public experiences, to disseminate knowledge about protection of the historic and cultural city.
Volunteer service teams for protection are encouraged to guide public participation in protection and publicity.
articles.36: Article 36 The Municipal and County People's Governments shall promote use of digital technology to collect information, establish archives, restore and preserve authenticity, and present key cultural relics.
articles.37: Article 37 The Municipal and County People's Governments shall adjust and optimize the mix of activities in the historic urban area, historic and cultural districts, famous towns, and famous villages and specify proportions for different categories. Locally distinctive businesses involving traditional handicrafts, specialty products, and transmission and use of intangible cultural heritage are encouraged.
articles.38:
Article 38 Investigation, collection, organization, research, and use of historic and cultural resources relating to the city's history, local products, traditional place names, environmental character, folk customs, and other matters are encouraged.
Educational and research institutions are encouraged and supported to train professionals in heritage protection and representative transmitters of intangible cultural heritage to teach apprentices and transmit their skills.
articles.39: Article 39 Based on the region's cultural resources, the Municipal and County People's Governments shall encourage and support social capital to invest in literary, film and television, theatrical, musical, and other artistic works relating to protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.40: Article 40 The culture and tourism department shall integrate revolutionary, Tusi, ethnic and folk, ecological tourism, and other cultural and natural resources according to their characteristics and guide and support tourism enterprises in expanding interpretation, improving routes and services, and offering distinctive products.
articles.41: Article 41 Entities and individuals are encouraged and supported to participate in protection and use by: (1) establishing private museums, exhibition halls, or memorial halls; (2) conducting research on local traditional culture and folk-art performances; (3) displaying or selling traditional handicrafts; (4) establishing intangible cultural heritage studios or training centers; (5) opening cultural inns; (6) developing cultural and creative products and brands; and (7) other forms of protective use.
articles.42:
Article 42 Revolutionary heritage sites that can be opened shall be open to the public.
Counties, county-level cities, and districts rich in revolutionary cultural resources are encouraged to use such sites for displays and exhibitions and to conduct varied activities and services in revolutionary-tradition education.
articles.43: Article 43 Relevant municipal and county entities shall continuously improve training programs for officials in revolutionary culture, research their content, design courses scientifically, and promote orderly development of the training industry.
articles.44: Article 44 State organs, enterprises, public institutions, and social organizations at all levels in this Municipality shall use revolutionary heritage sites for patriotic and revolutionary-tradition education and conduct activities supporting the armed forces and assisting their families. They shall respect and care for service members and their families and promote a positive social culture of supporting the armed forces and giving preferential treatment to their families.
articles.45: Article 45 Schools shall strengthen education on the spirit of the Long March and revolutionary traditions and regularly organize students to learn and conduct practical activities at revolutionary heritage sites. They shall encourage young people to remember revolutionary history, honor heroes and martyrs, and carry forward fine traditions, help them develop sound worldviews, outlooks on life, and values, and ensure that the revolutionary legacy is passed from generation to generation.
articles.46: Article 46 Transmission of the revolutionary legacy and promotion of the spirit of the Long March shall respect historical facts. It is prohibited to distort, fabricate, ridicule, desecrate, or deny the deeds of heroes and martyrs, revolutionary predecessors, or exemplary figures.
articles.47:
Article 47 Entities responsible for protecting memorial facilities for revolutionary martyrs and exemplary heroes shall improve service and management rules and preserve a solemn, respectful, and peaceful environment and atmosphere.
No organization or individual may conduct activities that impair the environment or atmosphere of a memorial facility or damage or deface it.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.48: Article 48 Where a person violates Article 12(3), the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 100 to RMB 200.
articles.49: Article 49 Where a person violates Article 26(1) or (4), the relevant competent department shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period. If the person refuses to stop, compulsory measures shall be taken to prevent continuation. If the person fails to restore the original condition or take remedial measures by the deadline, a capable entity may be designated to do so at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual.
articles.50: Article 50 Where a State organ or staff member commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations and the conduct does not constitute a crime, the Municipal or County People's Government or relevant competent department shall order correction and impose sanctions in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel: (1) failing to organize preparation, submission for approval, amendment, or publication of a protection plan, or failing to follow statutory procedures; (2) failing to perform approval duties under statutory procedures; (3) failing to prepare safeguards or an improvement plan under Articles 30 and 31; (4) failing to conduct routine inspection and protection of a historic and cultural district, famous town, or famous village, or failing to supervise safety and fire safety of historic buildings and buildings of traditional character; or (5) failing to perform other duties, or performing them improperly, thereby seriously impairing protection work or damaging the historic, artistic, or cultural value of a protected matter.
articles.51:
Article 51 Where laws or regulations prescribe penalties for other conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.52: Article 52 For purposes of these Regulations, ‘building of traditional character’ means a building or structure, other than a protected cultural relic or historic building, that has existed for a certain period and has value or significance to the overall character of a historic urban area, historic and cultural district, famous town, or famous village.
articles.53:
Article 53 These Regulations shall take effect on 10 January 2022.

Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages (2017 Revision)

FBMCLI.10.8049106.title: Regulations of Changchun Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to strengthen protection and administration of the historic and cultural city, preserve and carry forward outstanding history and culture, and promote coordinated urban and rural development and social and cultural development, in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
articles.2: Article 2 These Regulations apply to protection, administration, and related activities concerning the historic and cultural city within this Municipality's administrative area.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, differentiated administration, strict protection, appropriate use, joint governance and shared benefits, and transmission and development.
articles.4: Article 4 This Municipality shall establish and improve a protection mechanism for the historic and cultural city under Party leadership, with government coordination, interdepartmental collaboration, participation by multiple parties, and public oversight.
articles.5:
Article 5 The Municipal and County (City) District People's Governments shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration within their respective jurisdictions.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall perform specific protection duties within their jurisdictions according to their division of responsibilities.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist them with protection work.
An administration body for a development zone shall be responsible for protection, supervision, and administration within its jurisdiction to the extent authorized.
articles.6: Article 6 Relying on the Municipal Territorial Spatial Planning Committee, this Municipality shall establish a special working mechanism for protection of the historic and cultural city to coordinate protection work, study major protection matters, and advise the Municipal People's Government. The municipal departments responsible for planning and natural resources and for culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism shall handle its day-to-day work together.
articles.7:
Article 7 The municipal planning and natural resources department shall administer planning for protection of the historic and cultural city.
The municipal culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism department shall protect and administer immovable cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, and related matters.
The municipal departments responsible for urban and rural development, urban administration, housing security and real estate administration, transport, forestry and landscaping, industry and information technology, agriculture and rural affairs, water affairs, civil affairs, finance, human resources and social security, emergency management, and other matters shall perform related duties within their respective responsibilities.
Relevant departments of County (City) District People's Governments shall also perform protection duties within their respective responsibilities.
articles.8: Article 8 The Municipal and County (City) District People's Governments shall incorporate protection of the historic and cultural city into their economic and social development plans, ensure necessary funding, and include it in their respective budgets.
articles.9: Article 9 Publicity on protection of the historic and cultural city is encouraged through public classes, special reports, expert lectures, immersive experiences, and other means to raise public awareness. Schools are supported in conducting practical educational activities related to such protection.
articles.10:
Article 10 Protection of the historic and cultural city is a shared responsibility of society. All entities and individuals have a duty to protect it and may submit opinions and suggestions on preparation and implementation of protection plans.
Entities and individuals are encouraged to participate lawfully through donations, funding, volunteer services, and other means.
Outstanding contributors shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions.
Chapter II — Protected Matters
articles.11: Article 11 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall be coordinated with establishment of a system for protecting and transmitting historic and cultural heritage in urban and rural areas.
articles.12: Article 12 Protected matters include: (1) famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages, historic and cultural districts, historic areas, immovable cultural relics, historic buildings, industrial heritage, agricultural heritage, ancient or notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, place-name heritage, and other matters protected by laws and regulations; and (2) matters included in approved special historic and cultural protection plans and other matters designated by the State, province, or Municipality.
articles.13: Article 13 The Municipal and County (City) District People's Governments shall organize surveys of protected matters, including famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages, historic and cultural districts, historic areas, and historic buildings. Relevant entities and individuals shall cooperate.
articles.14: Article 14 Nomination and approval of protected matters shall follow relevant provisions.
articles.15: Article 15 A protected matter designated in accordance with the law shall not be adjusted or revoked without authorization. Where a change in protection level or loss of protection value requires adjustment, approval shall be obtained from the original approving and announcing authority in accordance with the law.
articles.16:
Article 16 The competent department for a protected matter shall establish and promptly publish its protection list, conduct surveys and create archives, administer records digitally, and maintain and update them dynamically.
The list shall be filed with the Standing Committee of the people's congress at the same level.
articles.17:
Article 17 Where a matter not yet listed is preliminarily determined by a Municipal or County (City) District People's Government to have protection value, it shall be designated for interim protection. Within 10 working days after designation, the owner and user shall receive an interim-protection notice in writing specifying required protection measures.
The competent department shall carry out the designation process under the applicable rules within six months after the notice is issued. If the matter is not designated as protected within six months, interim protection shall expire. If interim protection causes loss to an entity's or individual's lawful rights or interests, the Municipal or County (City) District People's Government shall provide compensation.
Chapter III — Protection Planning
articles.18:
Article 18 The people's government of the city where the historic and cultural city is located shall organize preparation of its protection plan.
The County (City) District People's Government where a famous historic and cultural town or village is located shall organize preparation of its protection plan.
The township or town people's government where a traditional village is located shall organize preparation of its protection plan.
The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of protection plans for historic and cultural districts in the municipal districts; the county-level city people's government shall organize preparation of plans for such districts within its jurisdiction.
Protection plans for a historic and cultural city, famous town or village, traditional village, or historic and cultural district shall be completed within one year after its designation and announcement.
articles.19:
Article 19 The contents of protection plans for the historic and cultural city, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages, and historic and cultural districts shall comply with relevant State and provincial laws and regulations.
A protection plan shall delineate protected boundaries. Boundaries for a famous town or village, traditional village, or historic and cultural district shall include a core protected area and a construction control area.
articles.20:
Article 20 Before submitting a protection plan for approval, the authority organizing its preparation shall broadly solicit opinions from relevant departments, experts, and the public and may hold a hearing where necessary.
The materials submitted for approval shall include an account of the opinions adopted and the reasons for not adopting others. Where a hearing was held, the hearing record shall also be included.
articles.21:
Article 21 After completion, a protection plan for the historic and cultural city, a famous historic and cultural town or village, or a historic and cultural district shall be submitted by the authority organizing its preparation to the provincial people's government for approval.
A protection plan for a traditional village shall be submitted to the County (City) District People's Government where it is located.
The authority organizing preparation shall promptly publish a protection plan approved in accordance with the law.
articles.22: Article 22 An approved protection plan for the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, traditional villages, or historic and cultural districts shall not be amended without authorization. Where amendment is necessary, the authority organizing preparation shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and may prepare an amendment only after consent. The amended plan shall be submitted for approval under the original procedure.
articles.23:
Article 23 Relevant contents of protection plans for the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, traditional villages, and historic and cultural districts shall be incorporated into territorial spatial plans at the corresponding levels. The protection-plan period shall be consistent with the planning period prescribed by the State and province.
Chapter IV — Protection Measures
articles.24:
Article 24 The person responsible for protection of a protected matter shall be determined as follows: (1) for a famous historic and cultural town or village or a traditional village, the township or town people's government or subdistrict office where it is located; (2) for a historic and cultural district or historic area, the County (City) District People's Government where it is located; (3) for a historic building, its owner, or, if the owner cannot be located or ownership is unclear, its user; and (4) where a separate protection and administration entity has been established for a protected matter, that entity.
For a matter spanning jurisdictions, the next higher-level people's government shall designate the responsible person. If no responsible person can otherwise be determined, the Municipal or County (City) District People's Government shall designate one.
After publishing the protection list, the County (City) District People's Government shall notify the responsible person of the protection duties.
articles.25: Article 25 A person responsible for protection of a famous historic and cultural town or village, traditional village, historic and cultural district, historic area, or historic site shall: (1) preserve the integrity of the traditional layout, historic character, and spatial scale of buildings and structures within the protected area and not alter the natural landscape or environment connected with them; (2) conduct routine inspections, promptly stop conduct endangering a protected matter, and investigate it or notify the relevant department; (3) assist relevant departments in ensuring proper operation of public fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; and (4) meet other requirements under laws and regulations.
articles.26: Article 26 A person responsible for protection of a historic building shall: (1) preserve the integrity of its traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale, and historic environmental features, with particular protection for exterior features, structure, components, and other elements embodying its core value; (2) ensure structural safety, promptly take measures to eliminate hazards, and report them to the local township or town people's government, subdistrict office, or competent department; (3) strengthen preventive protection, routine maintenance, and conservation repairs and carry out maintenance, repairs, and use as required; (4) prevent water ingress, damp, and insect damage; (5) ensure proper operation of fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; (6) keep it clean and orderly; and (7) meet other requirements under laws and regulations.
articles.27: Article 27 The following activities are prohibited in a protected area of the historic and cultural city or a famous historic and cultural town or village: (1) hill cutting, quarrying, mining, or other activities damaging the traditional layout or historic character; (2) occupying gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, roads, or other areas designated for preservation in a protection plan; (3) constructing factories, warehouses, or similar facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances; or (4) carving or defacing a historic building.
articles.28: Article 28 Construction in a protected area of the historic and cultural city or a famous historic and cultural town or village shall comply with the protection plan, preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage, and not damage the traditional layout or historic character.
articles.29:
Article 29 Within a core protected area of a famous town or village, traditional village, or historic and cultural district, no new construction or expansion is permitted except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. Planning permission shall be obtained for such necessary construction. Before granting permission, the planning and natural resources department shall consult the culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism department at the same level.
Demolition of a building, structure, or other facility other than a historic building within such a core protected area shall be approved by the planning and natural resources department together with the culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism department at the same level.
articles.30: Article 30 Construction of necessary infrastructure and public service facilities within a core protected area of a famous town or village, traditional village, or historic and cultural district shall: (1) not add facilities that pollute the environment; (2) use effective protective measures for roads, underground works, and other municipal facilities and not damage protected matters; and (3) install new or reconstructed utility lines underground. If conditions make underground installation impossible or require wall-mounted lines, they shall be concealed or technically treated to meet protection requirements.
articles.31: Article 31 New, reconstructed, or extended construction in a construction control area of a famous town or village, traditional village, or historic and cultural district shall comply with the construction controls in the protection plan.
articles.32: Article 32 Outdoor advertisements, plaques, air-conditioning units, neon signs, floodlights, and other external facilities on historic buildings shall be strictly controlled. Such facilities shall be compatible with the building's exterior facade.
articles.33:
Article 33 External repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or alteration of the structure or use of a historic building shall be approved by the planning and natural resources department together with the culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism department at the same level, and related procedures under laws and regulations shall be completed.
The responsible person shall repair the historic building in accordance with the approved protection design and construction drawings. The Municipal or County (City) District People's Government may provide a subsidy.
Residents carrying out maintenance or repairs on buildings and structures other than historic buildings within the protected areas of famous towns or villages, traditional villages, historic and cultural districts, or historic areas shall follow the protection plan and technical repair standards. The Municipal or County (City) District People's Government may provide a subsidy.
articles.34:
Article 34 No entity or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization.
A construction project shall be sited away from a historic building. If special circumstances make this impossible, protection at the original site shall be implemented to the greatest extent possible. The developer shall determine protection measures in advance and obtain approval from the planning and natural resources department together with the culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism department at the same level.
If construction in the public interest makes protection at the original site impossible and relocation or demolition is necessary, the developer shall submit a feasibility report, information on the proposed relocation site, and other materials. After expert review, the planning and natural resources department and the culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism department at the same level shall submit the matter to the provincial housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments for approval.
The developer shall include costs for protection at the original site, relocation, or demolition in the construction project budget.
articles.35:
Article 35 For a historic building lawfully approved for relocation or demolition, the planning and natural resources department, together with the culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism department and the responsible person, shall carry out surveys, assessments, information recording, and archival preservation and promptly transfer the records to the relevant archives in accordance with applicable rules.
The developer shall number, organize, and safely preserve components removed from the building. Original components of a relocated building shall be used in its reassembly and restoration. Components of a demolished building shall be inventoried and transferred to the County (City) District People's Government where it is located for preservation and use in reconstruction, new construction, or renovation within historic and cultural districts and historic-building protected areas.
articles.36:
Article 36 If construction may damage a building or structure in a core protected area of a famous town or village, traditional village, or historic and cultural district, or within the protected area of a historic building, the contractor or developer shall take safety measures.
If construction causes damage, the contractor or developer shall be responsible for repairs and shall solicit opinions from relevant departments on the repair plan.
The county or district housing and urban-rural development department shall inspect repair work on historic buildings requiring a construction permit. If the work does not comply with technical specifications, quality standards, or the repair plan, the department shall direct correction.
articles.37:
Article 37 The County (City) District department responsible for housing safety shall supervise the safety of buildings and structures within core protected areas of famous towns and villages, traditional villages, and historic and cultural districts and within protected areas of historic buildings. During housing safety surveys, it shall mark the safety condition of immovable cultural relics and historic buildings and update the information dynamically.
If the department discovers that a building or structure described above is at risk of damage, it shall promptly notify the responsible person to perform maintenance and repair duties under the relevant rules. The responsible person shall promptly remedy the risk. If the responsible person fails to act or lacks the capacity to do so, the County (City) District People's Government where it is located shall arrange maintenance and repairs as appropriate. The responsible person and user shall cooperate and shall not obstruct the work.
articles.38:
