Article 38 The Municipal and County (City) District People's Governments shall place protection signs at main entrances and other prominent locations for protected matters at the corresponding protection level.
No entity or individual may install, move, remove, damage, alter, or cover a protection sign without authorization.
articles.39: Article 39 In protecting the historic and cultural city, the competent departments for protected matters and other relevant departments shall use digital and other new technologies and methods to collect and analyze information, aggregate and share data efficiently, and facilitate public access to historic and cultural information.
articles.40:
Article 40 The competent departments for protected matters shall monitor them using video surveillance, remote sensing, and other means and promptly discover, stop, and handle unlawful conduct damaging protected matters or involving unauthorized installation, movement, alteration, or damage of protection signs.
The County (City) District People's Governments shall establish and improve routine inspection mechanisms and incorporate inspections into community grid-based administration and other systems.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall conduct routine inspections and investigate violations or notify the relevant department.
articles.41:
Article 41 The Municipal People's Government shall establish a special assessment system for protection of the historic and cultural city. The municipal planning and natural resources department shall conduct assessments together with the culture, broadcasting, television, and tourism department and report the results to the Municipal People's Government. The Municipal People's Government shall require the relevant County (City) District People's Government and departments to promptly address problems identified.
Chapter V — Use and Transmission
articles.42: Article 42 The Municipal and County (City) District People's Governments shall coordinate protection with urban renewal, land transfers, rural revitalization, and other work. They shall improve roads, river and lake systems, and the ecological environment in famous towns and villages, traditional villages, historic and cultural districts, and historic areas; improve infrastructure, public services, and overall character; increase publicly accessible open spaces; and strengthen disaster prevention, mitigation, and response.
articles.43: Article 43 Financial institutions and local financial organizations are encouraged to participate in protection and use projects, innovate financial products and services, streamline service procedures, and broaden financing channels.
articles.44: Article 44 The Municipal and County (City) District People's Governments shall adopt industry-guidance policies for historic and cultural heritage and support time-honored brands, representative intangible cultural heritage projects, businesses and industries embodying historic and cultural value, cultural tourism, cultural and creative industries, and other distinctive sectors.
articles.45:
Article 45 County (City) District People's Governments are supported in making appropriate use of State-owned historic buildings, provided that the use complies with protection requirements and does not impair historic and cultural value.
Protective use through museums, specialty bookstores, intangible cultural heritage workshops, and other facilities that strengthen cultural and public-service functions is encouraged.
articles.46: Article 46 Residents of famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages are supported in producing and selling local handicrafts and engaging in related activities that continue the original form and way of life of those places.
articles.47:
Article 47 Protection and use of time-honored brands, old objects, traditional techniques, historic plays, and other matters with historic value shall be strengthened to build classic Changchun cultural brands. Spaces for transmission of intangible cultural heritage shall be laid out appropriately to support its survival, dissemination, and development. Research and transmission concerning traditional festivals, distinctive folk customs, techniques, and folk literature shall be strengthened.
Training traditional craftspeople, transmitting traditional crafts, and producing traditional materials related to protection are supported. Competent departments for urban and rural development, agriculture, and other industries shall provide professional training and support eligible participants in skills-level certification.
Higher education institutions, secondary vocational schools, and social organizations are encouraged and supported to offer relevant courses and train professional and technical personnel.
Chapter VI — Legal Liability
articles.48: Article 48 Where a person engages without authorization in construction within a core protected area of a famous historic and cultural town or village, traditional village, or historic and cultural district, the following penalties shall apply: (1) where construction is carried out without a construction project planning permit or contrary to its terms, the municipal or County (City) District planning and natural resources department shall order it to stop. If the effect on implementation of planning can be eliminated through correction, correction shall be ordered within a specified period and a fine of 5% to 10% of the construction cost imposed. If the effect cannot be eliminated, demolition shall be ordered within a specified period; if demolition is impossible, the physical property or unlawful income shall be confiscated and a fine of up to 10% of the construction cost may also be imposed; (2) where construction in a township or village planning area is carried out without a rural construction planning permit or contrary to its terms, the township or town people's government shall order it to stop and correct within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, the construction may be demolished.
articles.49: Article 49 Where a person violates these Regulations by failing to construct in accordance with engineering design drawings or technical construction standards, the housing and urban-rural development department shall penalize the contractor in accordance with relevant provisions.
articles.50:
Article 50 Where a staff member of the Municipal or County (City) District People's Government, a relevant department, or a township or town people's government abuses official powers, neglects duties, engages in favoritism or malpractice, or otherwise fails to perform duties lawfully in protecting or administering the historic and cultural city, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the law.
Chapter VII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.51: Article 51 Protection and administration of immovable cultural relics, industrial heritage, agricultural heritage, ancient or notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, place-name heritage, and other matters shall follow relevant laws and regulations.
articles.52: Article 52 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 December 2024. The Regulations of Changchun Municipality on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Districts and Historic Buildings are repealed at the same time.

FBMCLI.10.6844556.title: Regulations of Taiyuan Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to protect Taiyuan as a historic and cultural city, continue the city's historical continuity, and coordinate protection and use of historic and cultural heritage with urban and rural development, in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Shanxi Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2: Article 2 These Regulations apply to protection, administration, and related activities concerning the historic and cultural city within this Municipality's administrative area.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, differentiated administration, strict protection, appropriate use, joint governance and shared benefits, regional coordination, and transmission and development. It shall properly balance protection with economic and social development.
articles.4: Article 4 This Municipality shall establish a protection mechanism for the historic and cultural city featuring government coordination, interdepartmental collaboration, public participation, and social oversight.
articles.5:
Article 5 The Municipal People's Government shall be responsible for protection of the historic and cultural city throughout the Municipality.
The People's Governments of counties, county-level cities, and districts shall protect, administer, and supervise the use of protected matters within their respective administrative areas.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall assist the County (City) District People's Governments in carrying out specific protection and administration work.
Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices with related protection work.
articles.6:
Article 6 The municipal housing and urban-rural development department, together with the municipal cultural relics department, shall protect, supervise, and administer the historic and cultural city throughout the Municipality and organize nominations, preliminary reviews, and other related work.
The municipal departments responsible for planning and natural resources, urban administration, and administrative approval services shall perform related duties concerning protection planning, law enforcement, project approval, and other matters.
The departments and agencies responsible for development and reform, industry and information technology, civil affairs, water affairs, agriculture and rural affairs, culture and tourism, veterans affairs, emergency management, auditing, landscaping, and fire and rescue shall perform related protection duties according to their respective responsibilities.
articles.7:
Article 7 The Municipal and County (City) District People's Governments shall incorporate protection of the historic and cultural city into their economic and social development plans and include necessary funding in their budgets.
This Municipality shall establish mechanisms to raise protection funds from multiple sources and broadly mobilize social funds for related protection work.
articles.8: Article 8 The Municipal People's Government shall establish an expert advisory mechanism to provide review, assessment, and advice on major protection matters.
articles.9: Article 9 Enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individuals are encouraged to participate lawfully in protection through donations, funding, investment, technical services, volunteer services, and other means.
articles.10:
Article 10 Publicity on protection of the historic and cultural city is encouraged through expert lectures, special reports, public classes, immersive experiences, and other means to disseminate knowledge.
Newspapers, radio, television, the Internet, and other media are supported in publicizing and guiding protection and raising public awareness.
Schools are supported in conducting teaching, research, and practical activities relating to protection of historic and cultural heritage.
articles.11:
Article 11 This Municipality shall strengthen cooperation with other cities in the central Shanxi urban cluster and surrounding areas and jointly advance development of a protection system for historic and cultural cities.
Chapter II — Protection System
articles.12: Article 12 The protection area covers all protected matters within this Municipality's administrative area. Priority shall be given to the Fen River cultural heritage corridor; the Xishan and Dongshan historic and cultural belts; the cultural cores of Taiyuan Prefecture City and Jinyang Ancient City; and heritage-concentration areas designated in the protection plan.
articles.13: Article 13 Protected matters include: (1) immovable cultural relics and underground archaeological protection areas; (2) historic buildings, industrial heritage, and revolutionary heritage sites; (3) historic and cultural districts, historic character areas, and historic urban areas; (4) famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages; (5) mountain-and-water patterns and ancient urban-site layouts; (6) historic streets and lanes, traditional place names, and former residences of notable persons; (7) rivers and lakes, scenic areas, protected natural areas, and ancient or notable trees; (8) intangible cultural heritage; and (9) other matters with historic value.
articles.14: Article 14 Protected matters shall receive holistic protection through connected corridors and contiguous areas. Building height and form, viewsheds, ecological landscapes, and other relevant features of protected matters and surrounding traditional character and spatial environment shall comply with construction controls.
articles.15:
Article 15 The municipal housing and urban-rural development department shall organize surveys of famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages, historic and cultural districts, historic buildings, cultural relics, and other historic and cultural resources together with the municipal cultural relics department.
The County (City) District People's Governments shall carry out related surveys as required.
articles.16:
Article 16 A protection-list system shall apply. Matters approved or designated and announced by the State Council or provincial people's government shall be included directly.
For another matter proposed for designation by the Municipal People's Government, the municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments shall prepare a preliminary opinion based on survey results, solicit opinions from relevant departments, organize expert review, apply relevant designation criteria, and prepare a preliminary protection list for public notice of no fewer than 30 days. A hearing may be held where necessary.
After the notice period, the departments shall submit the preliminary list, comments received, expert opinions, and notice results to the Municipal People's Government for approval and publication under the prescribed procedure.
Any entity or individual may recommend a protected matter to the County (City) District People's Government where it is located.
articles.17: Article 17 If a protected matter is damaged or lost due to force majeure or its protection level or category changes, the municipal housing and urban-rural development department and cultural relics department shall propose an adjustment to the protection list and submit it for approval under the original procedure.
articles.18:
Article 18 Where a matter not yet listed is preliminarily determined by the Municipal or County (City) District People's Government to have protection value, it shall be designated for interim protection. Within 10 working days after designation, the owner and user shall receive a written interim-protection notice specifying required measures.
Interim protection shall last six months from the date the notice is issued. During this period, no entity or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish the matter without authorization. The municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments shall organize expert review and public notice and recommend its inclusion in the protection list.
If the matter is not included in the list by the end of the interim-protection period, interim protection shall expire.
Protection of revolutionary heritage sites and industrial heritage shall follow relevant State and provincial provisions.
articles.19: Article 19 The municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments shall establish archives for the protection list, including: (1) basic information on each matter, surveying materials, historic and cultural features, historical development and events, and technical materials; (2) changes in title, current use, and construction approvals within the protected area; (3) approved protection plans and designs; (4) records, drawings, photographs, and video materials produced during repairs, maintenance, relocation, or demolition; and (5) other materials requiring preservation.
articles.20:
Article 20 After the Municipal People's Government approves and publishes the protection list, the municipal planning and natural resources department shall incorporate protected matters and construction controls into territorial spatial plans at the corresponding levels.
Chapter III — Protection Planning
articles.21: Article 21 The protection-planning system includes plans for the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, traditional villages, historic and cultural districts, and historic buildings.
articles.22:
Article 22 A protection plan shall be completed within one year after designation and announcement of the historic and cultural city, famous town or village, historic and cultural district, or historic building. A protection and development plan for a traditional village shall be completed within one year after its designation and announcement.
Plans shall be prepared as follows: (1) the Municipal People's Government shall prepare the protection plan for the historic and cultural city; (2) the municipal housing and urban-rural development department and the County (City) District People's Government where a historic and cultural district is located shall jointly prepare its plan; (3) the County (City) District People's Government shall prepare protection plans for famous historic and cultural towns and villages and protection and development plans for traditional villages; and (4) the municipal housing and urban-rural development department and relevant departments shall prepare protection plans for historic buildings in the municipal districts, while the county-level city people's government shall prepare plans for historic buildings in its jurisdiction.
articles.23:
Article 23 Before submitting a protection plan for approval, the authority organizing its preparation shall lawfully publish the draft and broadly solicit opinions from relevant departments, experts, and the public for no fewer than 30 days; it may hold a hearing where necessary.
Preparation of a plan for a famous town or village or a traditional village shall also solicit opinions from the township or town people's government or subdistrict office where it is located. Preparation of a plan for a famous village or traditional village shall also solicit opinions from the villagers' or residents' committee concerned.
Protection plans for the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, and historic and cultural districts and protection and development plans for traditional villages shall be approved and filed in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions. A historic-building protection plan shall be approved by the Municipal People's Government and filed under the prescribed procedure.
An approved plan shall not be amended without authorization. Any necessary amendment shall follow relevant State and provincial provisions.
articles.24:
Article 24 Relevant contents of protection plans for the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, and protection and development plans for traditional villages shall be incorporated into territorial spatial plans at the corresponding levels. Protection plans for historic and cultural districts and historic buildings shall be incorporated into detailed regulatory plans. The plan period shall be consistent with relevant State and provincial planning periods.
Specialized plans for municipal services, transport, green space, village layouts, and other matters shall be coordinated with protection plans. Before submitting a specialized plan for approval, the authority preparing it shall solicit opinions from the municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments.
Territorial spatial plans at the relevant levels shall be coordinated with protection plans. Before submission for approval, the authority preparing a territorial spatial plan shall solicit opinions from the municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments.
Chapter IV — Protection and Use
articles.25:
Article 25 A system of persons responsible for protection shall apply. The responsible person shall be determined as follows: (1) for a key protected area, a protection body designated by the Municipal People's Government or the County (City) District People's Government where it is located; (2) for a famous historic and cultural town or village, traditional village, historic and cultural district, or historic character area, the County (City) District People's Government where it is located; (3) for a historic building, its owner, or, if the owner cannot be located or ownership is unclear, its user; (4) where a separate protection and administration body has been established, that body; and (5) for a matter spanning jurisdictions, a responsible person designated by the common higher-level people's government.
If no responsible person can otherwise be determined, the Municipal People's Government shall designate one.
After publication of the protection list, the municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments shall notify the responsible person in writing of protection duties.
articles.26: Article 26 The person responsible for protection of a key protected area shall: (1) protect the natural landforms and landscapes of the Fen River basin as a whole, including ancient villages and towns, waterworks and other heritage, intangible cultural heritage, and historic urban landscapes along the Fen River and its tributaries; (2) protect historic and cultural heritage in Xishan and Dongshan, coordinate management of mountains, water, forests, fields, lakes, and grasslands, continue ecological restoration, improve supporting services, highlight cultural features, and enhance quality and vitality; (3) strengthen cultural relics archaeology and advance development of the Jinyang Ancient City archaeological park; protect the traditional layout, street and lane fabric, and historic character of Taiyuan Prefecture City's historic urban area; make adaptive use of heritage; formulate policies to improve the area's functions; and improve infrastructure, public services, and living conditions; (4) protect and use heritage in concentration areas contiguously, improve surrounding environments, support cultural tourism, and improve living conditions to achieve both protection and development; and (5) perform other duties under laws and regulations.
articles.27: Article 27 The person responsible for protection of a famous historic and cultural town or village, traditional village, historic and cultural district, or historic character area shall: (1) preserve the integrity and authenticity of the traditional layout, street and lane fabric, historic character, spatial scale, and historic environmental features; (2) strengthen protection and repair of historic and cultural heritage, prepare annual repair plans, and carry them out; (3) improve supporting services and the quality of the spatial environment; (4) conduct routine inspections, promptly address conduct endangering protected matters, and report to the relevant department; (5) ensure fire safety, flood control and drainage, sunlight and ventilation, corrosion prevention, pest control, and other safeguards; and (6) perform other duties under laws and regulations.
articles.28:
Article 28 The person responsible for protection of a historic building shall: (1) maintain and repair it and preserve its original exterior form and character; (2) ensure its safety and proper operation of fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment, promptly take measures to eliminate hazards, and report them to the County (City) District People's Government where it is located; (3) notify a transferee, lessee, or user in writing of protection duties when transferring, leasing, or lending the building; and (4) perform other duties under laws and regulations.
If the responsible person is a natural person, the County (City) District People's Government shall bear the duties of maintenance, repairs, and hazard elimination, while the natural person shall promptly report risks.
articles.29: Article 29 Renewal and protection of the historic urban area shall strictly control development intensity, give priority to the public interest, and: (1) optimize land-use functions; (2) control building density, capacity, and height and protect and improve residents' living conditions; (3) preserve the spatial scale of historic streets and lanes, which shall not be widened to address traffic issues; (4) improve public services, municipal infrastructure, and transport facilities; (5) give priority to public transport and establish a transport system centered on it; and (6) comply with other requirements in the protection plan.
articles.30: Article 30 Within a core protected area designated in a protection plan for a famous town or village, protection and development plan for a traditional village, or protection plan for a historic and cultural district, no new construction or expansion is permitted. Where construction or expansion of necessary infrastructure or public service facilities is genuinely necessary, or a collapsed or structurally unsound traditional courtyard must be renovated, reconstructed, or rebuilt, the following requirements apply: (1) necessary infrastructure and public service facilities shall comply with construction controls in the protection plan; (2) a dangerous courtyard may be renovated, reconstructed, or rebuilt at its original location, preserving its original layout, form, and character; and (3) a construction project planning permit or rural construction planning permit shall be obtained. Before issuing the permit, the issuing authority shall solicit opinions from the housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments at the same level, organize expert review, and solicit public opinions.
articles.31: Article 31 Demolition of a building, structure, or other facility, other than a cultural relic or historic building, within a core protected area designated in a protection plan for a famous town or village, protection and development plan for a traditional village, or protection plan for a historic and cultural district shall be approved by the competent department designated by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.32: Article 32 New, reconstructed, or extended buildings and structures in a construction control area designated in a plan for a famous town or village, protection and development plan for a traditional village, or protection plan for a historic and cultural district, or within a protected area of a historic character area, shall be compatible with the historic character in height, bulk, and colors and comply with construction controls in the protection plan.
articles.33:
Article 33 No entity or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization.
External repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or alteration of the structure or use of a historic building shall be approved by the competent department designated by the Municipal or County People's Government. Before approval, opinions shall be solicited from the public, experts, and interested parties, and related procedures under laws and regulations shall be completed.
A construction project shall, where possible, be sited away from historic buildings. If special circumstances make this impossible, the developer shall protect the building at its original site to the greatest extent possible, determine protection measures in advance, and obtain approval from the competent department designated by the Municipal or County People's Government.
If public-interest construction or natural causes such as geological disasters make protection at the original site impossible and assessment confirms relocation or demolition is necessary, approval shall be obtained in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions. Where demolition is approved, the developer shall mark and document the building; where it is reconstructed, original components and materials shall be used as far as possible.
If a historic building at risk cannot be maintained or repaired, the responsible person may apply to the competent department designated by the Municipal People's Government for reconstruction at the original site. That department shall organize expert review and examination together with the municipal cultural relics department and submit the matter to the Municipal People's Government for handling under relevant State and provincial provisions.
articles.34: Article 34 If construction reveals a building or structure with protection value, the contractor shall immediately stop demolition or construction, take interim protective measures, and report to the developer. The developer shall promptly report to the local housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments.
articles.35:
Article 35 Within six months after the Municipal People's Government publishes the protection list, the County (City) District People's Government shall place a protection sign at the main entrance to a protected matter or on the protected building itself.
Signs shall be compatible with the traditional character. The Municipal People's Government shall establish uniform installation standards and maintenance requirements.
No entity or individual may install, move, remove, damage, alter, or cover a protection sign without authorization.
articles.36:
Article 36 Reasonable use and orderly public access to protected matters, including famous towns and villages, traditional villages, historic and cultural districts, historic character areas, and historic buildings, are encouraged and supported to display Taiyuan's cultural features.
In accordance with protection plans, diverse distinctive industries may be developed in famous towns and villages, traditional villages, and historic and cultural districts. Activities compatible with traditional culture, including processing and production of traditional crafts, intangible cultural heritage, specialty tourism, cultural and creative activities, calligraphy and painting, and folk performances, are encouraged.
articles.37: Article 37 The Municipal and County (City) District People's Governments shall establish a project pool for protection and development and coordinate development and use of the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, and other historic and cultural resources.
articles.38:
Article 38 Entities and individuals are encouraged and supported to make protective use of historic buildings through museums, exhibition halls, research on traditional culture, and other activities, provided that structural and fire-safety requirements under State codes and the protection plan are met.
Libraries, museums, art galleries, specialty bookstores, intangible cultural heritage workshops, cultural display centers, and other cultural or service functions suited to a building and its surrounding area are encouraged.
articles.39: Article 39 Training traditional craftspeople, transmitting traditional crafts, and producing traditional materials related to protection are supported. The municipal housing and urban-rural development department shall, together with the human resources and social security, agriculture and rural affairs, cultural relics, and other departments, organize professional training and skills certification and establish a grading system for traditional craftspeople.
articles.40: Article 40 Protection and use of old commercial brands, old objects, traditional techniques, historic plays, and other matters with historic value shall be strengthened to build classic Taiyuan cultural brands. Spaces for transmission of intangible cultural heritage shall be laid out appropriately, including in historic and cultural districts, to support its survival, dissemination, and development. Research and transmission concerning traditional festivals, distinctive folk customs, and traditional crafts shall be strengthened.
articles.41: Article 41 Residents of famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages are supported in producing and selling local handicrafts and engaging in related activities that continue the original form and way of life of those places.
articles.42:
Article 42 The municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments shall jointly establish an information platform for protection and transmission of urban and rural historic and cultural heritage, integrate existing management platforms, and improve their functions to support evidence-based decisions, information management, dynamic monitoring, and public services and enable detailed administration at multiple levels.
Chapter V — Supervision and Inspection
articles.43:
Article 43 The Municipal People's Government shall establish mechanisms for assessment, accountability, supervision, and inspection of protection.
The municipal housing and urban-rural development department and cultural relics department shall inspect or assess protection and implementation concerning the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, traditional villages, historic and cultural districts, historic character areas, and historic buildings throughout the Municipality and report results to the Municipal People's Government and the County (City) District People's Government concerned.
Where construction violates a protection plan or protection is inadequate, the Municipal People's Government shall require the relevant entity or local government to make corrections. The municipal housing and urban-rural development department and cultural relics department shall supervise and inspect the corrections.
The County (City) District People's Governments shall incorporate routine inspections of heritage into comprehensive urban administration law enforcement, community grid-based administration, and other systems as appropriate. Under guidance from the municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments and professionals, they shall order correction of problems and promptly take remedial measures.
articles.44: Article 44 Audit authorities shall audit, in accordance with the law, the performance of economic responsibilities by persons in charge of historic and cultural cities and towns during their terms of office.
articles.45:
Article 45 Any entity or individual may dissuade or report to a people's government at any level or a relevant competent department conduct damaging or destroying a famous historic and cultural city or town, famous village, traditional village, historic and cultural district, or historic building.
The relevant department shall handle the report in accordance with the law and provide a response.
Chapter VI — Legal Liability
articles.46: Article 46 Where laws, administrative regulations, or local regulations adopted by the Shanxi Provincial People's Congress or its Standing Committee prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.47: Article 47 Where a people's government at a lower level violates Article 22 or 23, the people's government at the next higher level shall order correction and impose sanctions in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel.
articles.48: Article 48 Where a person damages, relocates, or demolishes a historic building without authorization, in violation of Article 33, the law-enforcement authority shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if serious consequences result, impose a fine of RMB 200,000 to RMB 500,000 on an entity or RMB 100,000 to RMB 200,000 on an individual. The person shall compensate for any losses.
articles.49:
Article 49 A staff member who neglects duties, abuses official powers, or engages in favoritism or malpractice in protecting the historic and cultural city shall be sanctioned by the competent authority or employing entity. If the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.
Chapter VII — Supplementary Provisions
articles.50: Article 50 For purposes of these Regulations: (1) ‘famous historic and cultural town or village’ means a town or village designated by a relevant State department or provincial people's government that has exceptionally rich cultural relics and historic buildings, major historic or revolutionary commemorative significance, and substantially reflects the traditional character and local or ethnic features of a historical period; (2) ‘traditional village’ means a village designated by a relevant State department or provincial people's government that possesses tangible and intangible cultural heritage and has high historic, cultural, scientific, artistic, social, or economic value; (3) ‘historic and cultural district’ means an area designated by a relevant State department or provincial people's government that has exceptionally rich cultural relics and a concentration of historic buildings, substantially and authentically reflects the traditional layout and historic character, and is of a certain scale; (4) ‘historic character area’ means an area with a concentration of historic buildings or buildings of traditional character that has retained a distinctive cultural meaning or urban character during historical stages of the city's development; (5) ‘historic building’ means a building or structure announced by the Municipal or County People's Government that has protection value and reflects historic character and local features but has not been announced as a protected cultural relic or registered as an immovable cultural relic; (6) ‘historic urban area’ means an area within a town or city that reflects its historical development or the character of a particular period, generally including areas commonly called an old town or old urban area; (7) ‘revolutionary heritage site’ means a site, former site, or memorial facility with historic, educational, or commemorative value that reflects the Communist Party of China's leadership of the people of all ethnic groups in the New Democratic Revolution, including sites of important organizations, meetings, events, campaigns, and battles; residences, activity sites, or graves of important figures and influential martyrs; martyrs' cemeteries, memorial halls, monuments, pavilions, sculptures, towers, and shrines; and other sites and facilities relating to the New Democratic Revolution; and (8) ‘industrial heritage’ means buildings, structures, equipment, products, production techniques, and other items formed during long-term industrial development that have high historic, cultural, scientific, artistic, social, or economic value.
articles.51: Article 51 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 May 2023.

FBMCLI.10.1666467.title: Regulations of Dalian Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated, in light of the actual circumstances of this Municipality, to strengthen protection and administration of the historic and cultural city and preserve and carry forward outstanding history and culture, in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2:
Article 2 These Regulations apply to protection, use, and administration of the historic and cultural city within this Municipality's administrative area.
Protection includes the historic urban area, historic areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts and areas with historic character, and historic buildings.
Where protection concerns protected cultural relics, immovable cultural relics not yet designated as protected cultural relics, movable cultural relics, intangible cultural heritage, industrial heritage, historic environmental features, or other matters, relevant laws, regulations, and provisions shall apply.
articles.3: Article 3 Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of science-based planning, strict protection, graded and differentiated administration, appropriate use, public participation, and transmission of cultural continuity. It shall preserve and continue the traditional layout and historic character, preserve the authenticity and integrity of historic and cultural heritage, and coordinate economic and social development with protection.
articles.4:
Article 4 The Municipal and District (County-level City) People's Governments shall be responsible for protection, use, and administration of the historic and cultural city within their respective administrative areas and include necessary protection funding in their budgets.
Township and town people's governments and subdistrict offices shall assist higher-level people's governments and relevant departments with protection, use, and administration in their jurisdictions.
A dispatched agency of the Municipal People's Government with administrative functions shall, to the extent authorized, protect, use, and administer the historic and cultural city within its area.
articles.5:
Article 5 The municipal and county-level city natural resources departments, together with cultural relics departments at the same level, shall implement and supervise protection plans within their respective administrative areas.
The departments of the Municipal and District (County-level City) People's Governments responsible for development and reform, education, industry and information technology, ethnic and religious affairs, public security, civil affairs, finance, housing and urban-rural development, water affairs, emergency management, civil air defense, urban administration, and other matters shall perform related protection and supervision duties according to their respective responsibilities.
articles.6:
Article 6 This Municipality shall establish a protection committee for the historic and cultural city to review, coordinate, and address major protection matters.
The Municipal People's Government shall separately determine the committee's organizational structure and rules of procedure.
articles.7:
Article 7 Entities and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and use through investment, donations, establishment of funds, and other means.
Participation through public-benefit organizations, volunteer services, protection leads, and other means is encouraged.
Scientific research, technological innovation, and professional training relating to protection are encouraged.
articles.8:
Article 8 The Municipal and District (County-level City) People's Governments and relevant departments shall organize public education on protection and raise public awareness. Under relevant State provisions, they shall commend and reward outstanding contributors to protection and use.
Chapter II — Nomination, Approval, and Protection List
articles.9: Article 9 Nomination of famous historic and cultural cities, towns, and villages and historic and cultural districts shall follow relevant State and provincial provisions.
articles.10: Article 10 An area not designated as a historic and cultural district may be nominated as an area with historic character if it meets either of the following criteria: (1) traditional-character buildings are concentrated in a contiguous area, or traditional streets and lanes are relatively well preserved; or (2) its spatial layout, landscape form, and architectural styles substantially reflect the regional cultural features of a particular historical period.
articles.11:
Article 11 The People's Government of the District (County-level City) where a proposed area with historic character is located shall submit the application. The municipal natural resources and planning department and cultural relics department shall organize expert review. After deliberation by the protection committee, the matter shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
If an area meets the criteria but has not been nominated, the protection committee may recommend nomination to the local District (County-level City) People's Government. If it still fails to nominate the area, the committee may directly recommend to the Municipal People's Government that the area be designated as an area with historic character.
articles.12:
Article 12 A building or structure that has existed for at least 50 years, has not been designated as an immovable cultural relic, and meets any of the following criteria may be nominated as a historic building: (1) it reflects Dalian's history, culture, or folk traditions and has characteristics of a particular period and locality; (2) it is associated with an important political, economic, cultural, or military event or famous historical figure; (3) its architectural style, structure, materials, construction methods, or engineering techniques reflect regional architecture or historic, cultural, or artistic characteristics or have scientific research value; (4) it is a representative, landmark, or commemorative building or structure or a representative work of a renowned architect; (5) it is an important former residence of a notable person; or (6) it has other historic or cultural significance.
A building or structure that has existed for fewer than 50 years may also be nominated if it distinctly reflects historic character, local features, or a particular period or has special commemorative significance.
articles.13:
Article 13 For a historic building in a municipal district, the municipal natural resources department shall propose an opinion together with relevant departments and submit it to the protection committee for deliberation and then to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
For a historic building in a county-level city, the local natural resources department shall propose an opinion together with relevant departments and submit it to the people's government at the same level for approval. The approval shall be reported to the protection committee.
articles.14:
Article 14 This Municipality shall maintain a protection list for the historic and cultural city and make it public.
The list shall include the historic urban area, historic areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, historic buildings, and other protected matters.
articles.15: Article 15 If a protected matter on the list is lost or damaged due to force majeure, or its protection level or category changes, the District (County-level City) People's Government where it is located shall organize expert review and propose an adjustment. After deliberation by the protection committee, the adjustment shall be approved under the original procedure and made public.
articles.16:
Article 16 Archives shall be maintained for the protection list. The District (County-level City) People's Government shall collect and organize historical information, including the name, location, and historic value of protected matters. Relevant departments shall compile it and the municipal natural resources department shall enter it into the protection-list archives.
Entities and individuals may access and use information in the archives in accordance with the law.
articles.17:
Article 17 This Municipality shall maintain a system of interim protection. A matter may be placed under interim protection if: (1) it meets the criteria under laws, regulations, and these Regulations but has not yet been designated; or (2) it is discovered through resource surveys, urban development or construction, or a lead submitted by an entity or individual, has some protection value as assessed by experts, and is approved by the protection committee.
Protected boundaries shall be delineated for an interim-protection matter. Interim protection shall last no longer than one year.
Chapter III — Protection Planning
articles.18: Article 18 Protection plans shall be prepared for the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, and historic buildings and shall be completed within one year after designation and announcement.
articles.19:
Article 19 Protection plans for a historic and cultural city or famous town or village shall be incorporated into territorial spatial master plans at the corresponding levels.
A protection plan for a historic and cultural district may serve as a detailed plan. Plans for an area with historic character or a historic building shall be coordinated with the corresponding detailed plan.
Specialized plans for urban transport, municipal services, green space, fire safety, civil air defense, and other matters shall be coordinated with protection plans.
articles.20: Article 20 The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of the Dalian protection plan for the historic and cultural city. After deliberation by the protection committee, it shall be submitted to the provincial people's government for approval.
articles.21: Article 21 The People's Government of a county-level city shall organize preparation of a protection plan for the historic and cultural city within its administrative area and submit it to the provincial people's government for approval. An approved plan shall be filed with the protection committee.
articles.22:
Article 22 The People's Government of a municipal district shall organize preparation of protection plans for famous historic and cultural towns and villages within its administrative area. After deliberation by the protection committee, they shall be submitted to the provincial people's government for approval.
The People's Government of a county-level city shall organize preparation of such plans within its jurisdiction and submit them to the provincial people's government for approval. Approved plans shall be filed with the protection committee.
articles.23:
Article 23 The People's Government of a municipal district shall organize preparation of protection plans for historic and cultural districts within its administrative area. After deliberation by the protection committee and review by the provincial housing and urban-rural development department, they shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
The county-level city natural resources department shall prepare protection plans for historic and cultural districts within its jurisdiction and submit them for review by the provincial housing and urban-rural development department and approval by the people's government at the same level. Approved plans shall be filed with the protection committee.
articles.24:
Article 24 The People's Government of a municipal district shall organize preparation of protection plans for areas with historic character and historic buildings within its administrative area. After deliberation by the protection committee, the plans shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for approval.
The county-level city natural resources department shall prepare such plans within its jurisdiction and submit them to the people's government at the same level for approval. Approved plans shall be filed with the protection committee.
articles.25: Article 25 A protection plan shall specify the protection principles, boundaries, protected matters, and major controls, including: (1) phased implementation requirements for the protection plan for the historic and cultural city; (2) important traditional layouts, street and lane fabric, and historic environmental features in plans for famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, and areas with historic character; (3) core protection elements, use functions, and protection guidelines in plans for historic buildings; and (4) other matters required by laws and regulations.
articles.26:
Article 26 Based on the protection plan, protected boundaries shall be delineated for matters on the protection list as follows: (1) an environmental coordination area may be delineated around a historic urban area as needed; (2) a protected area for a famous historic and cultural town or village or historic and cultural district shall include a core protected area and construction control area; and (3) the protected area of a historic building in a historic and cultural district shall comprise the building itself, while the protected area of a historic building outside such a district shall include the building itself and any necessary construction control area.
Protected boundaries for an interim-protection matter shall be delineated by reference to the preceding provisions.
articles.27:
Article 27 Before submitting a protection plan for approval, the authority organizing its preparation shall publish the draft and solicit opinions from relevant departments, experts, and the public for no fewer than 30 days. A hearing shall be held where expropriation of houses or land is involved.
A protection plan shall be made public within 15 days after approval.
articles.28:
Article 28 An approved protection plan shall not be amended without authorization. Any necessary amendment shall be prepared and submitted for approval under the procedures prescribed by laws and regulations.
Chapter IV — Protection and Use
articles.29:
Article 29 A system of persons responsible for protection shall apply. The Municipal and District (County-level City) People's Governments shall be responsible for protection of historic urban areas, historic areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, and areas with historic character.
The responsible person for a historic building shall be determined as follows: (1) for a State-owned building, its entrusted manager, or, if there is none, its user; (2) for a non-State-owned building, its owner, or, if the owner cannot be located or contacted or title is unclear, its entrusted manager.
If the owner, user, or manager cannot be identified, the District (County-level City) People's Government where it is located, or an entity or individual designated by that government, shall be responsible.
articles.30: Article 30 The District (County-level City) People's Government shall issue a notice to the person responsible for protection of a historic building specifying that person's duties: (1) maintain and repair it in accordance with the protection plan and guidelines and preserve its original exterior form and character; (2) ensure structural safety and proper operation of fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment and promptly take measures to eliminate hazards; (3) notify a transferee, lessee, or user of protection duties when transferring, leasing, or lending the building; and (4) perform other duties under laws and regulations.
articles.31:
Article 31 No entity or individual may damage or demolish an interim-protection matter.
Before construction is carried out within its protected area, the District (County-level City) People's Government where it is located shall solicit opinions from the municipal natural resources department and the cultural relics department at the same level.
The responsible person and protection duties for an interim-protection matter shall be determined by reference to Articles 29 and 30 of these Regulations.
articles.32: Article 32 The following activities are prohibited within the protected areas of historic urban areas, historic areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, and historic buildings: (1) hill cutting, quarrying, mining, or other activities damaging the traditional layout or historic character; (2) occupying gardens, green spaces, river and lake systems, traditional streets and lanes, roads, or other matters designated for preservation in a protection plan; (3) constructing factories, warehouses, or similar facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic, or corrosive substances; (4) constructing buildings, structures, or other facilities that damage the traditional character; (5) damaging buildings, structures, or facilities designated for protection in a protection plan; (6) repairing or decorating such buildings in a manner that changes their original character; (7) carving or defacing a historic building; or (8) other conduct prohibited by laws and regulations.
articles.33: Article 33 The Municipal and District (County-level City) People's Governments shall, in accordance with the protection plan, preserve the traditional layout, historic character, and spatial scale of historic urban areas and historic areas; strictly control total development, population, and the height, bulk, colors, and style of buildings; and protect historic plazas, parks, streets and lanes, wharves, and other features.
articles.34:
Article 34 Within a core protected area of a famous town or village or historic and cultural district, no new construction or expansion is permitted except for necessary infrastructure and public service facilities. Such facilities shall be compatible with the historic character and traditional layout, preserve the original width and alignment of streets and lanes and traditional courtyard spaces, and not be accompanied by unauthorized construction damaging courtyard character.
New buildings in a construction control area shall be compatible with the historic character in height, bulk, and colors. Existing buildings incompatible with the character shall, where feasible, be renovated gradually to restore the traditional layout and historic character.
articles.35: Article 35 Construction within a protected area of an area with historic character shall be controlled and shall not damage the traditional layout. New, reconstructed, or extended buildings shall be compatible with the area's overall character in height, bulk, colors, and other respects.
articles.36:
Article 36 A planning application for any of the following activities shall include a dedicated section on historic protection: (1) lawful construction or expansion of necessary infrastructure or public service facilities within a core protected area of a famous town or village or historic and cultural district; or (2) lawful construction, reconstruction, or expansion within a construction control area of a famous town or village or historic and cultural district or within a protected area of an area with historic character or historic building.
Before issuing planning permission, the municipal or county-level city natural resources department shall solicit opinions from the cultural relics department at the same level.
articles.37: Article 37 Demolition of a building, structure, or other facility, other than a historic building, within a core protected area of a famous town or village or historic and cultural district shall be approved by the municipal or county-level city natural resources department together with the cultural relics department at the same level.
articles.38: Article 38 Before approving a construction activity under Articles 36 or 37, the approving authority shall organize expert review, publicly announce the proposed approval, and solicit public opinions for no fewer than 20 days.
articles.39:
Article 39 The District (County-level City) People's Government shall prepare an annual repair plan for historic buildings and ensure that relevant departments or individuals carry out the work.
The Municipal and District (County-level City) People's Governments may subsidize persons responsible for repairs in accordance with the protection plan from historic and cultural city protection funds.
articles.40: Article 40 External repairs or decoration, addition of facilities, or alteration of the structure or use of a historic building shall comply with its protection plan, protection guidelines, technical specifications, and quality standards and be approved in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
articles.41:
Article 41 If a historic building is identified as dangerous, the relevant department of the District (County-level City) People's Government shall require the responsible person to remedy the danger, and that person shall do so immediately.
If a historic building is at risk of damage, the relevant department shall promptly notify the responsible person to perform required maintenance and repair. If the responsible person lacks the capacity to do so, after confirmation by the department, the local people's government shall take protective measures.
In an emergency, or if the responsible person fails to remedy the danger by the deadline, the District (County-level City) People's Government shall carry out emergency hazard elimination. The responsible person shall cooperate and shall not obstruct the work.
articles.42:
Article 42 A construction project shall, where possible, be sited away from historic buildings. If special circumstances make this impossible, protection at the original site shall be implemented to the greatest extent possible.
Before protecting a historic building at its original site, the developer shall determine protection measures and obtain approval from the municipal or county-level city natural resources department together with the cultural relics department at the same level.
articles.43: Article 43 No entity or individual may damage, relocate, or demolish a historic building without authorization. Relocation or demolition for the public interest shall be approved in accordance with the law and carried out under relevant technical standards and administrative provisions.
articles.44: Article 44 The District (County-level City) People's Government shall establish and administer archives for historic buildings. Archives shall state the name, number, location, and date of construction and include: (1) architectural and historic features, historical information, and rarity; (2) protection guidelines and technical materials; (3) current use and changes in ownership; (4) written records, drawings, photographs, and video materials produced during repair or decoration; and (5) survey records and related materials.
articles.45: Article 45 Where protection of the historic and cultural city requires a competent department to lawfully amend or revoke an effective administrative permit, compensation shall be provided in accordance with the law for losses to the permit holder's lawful rights and interests.
articles.46:
Article 46 Protection, transmission, and appropriate use of famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, and other protected matters are encouraged and supported, provided that local natural landscapes, cultural landscapes, and historic and cultural resources are not damaged.
The District (County-level City) People's Governments shall develop business-use plans, guide commercial development reasonably, and encourage traditional handicrafts, specialty products, and other distinctive local businesses.
articles.47:
Article 47 The Municipal and District (County-level City) People's Governments shall promote appropriate use of historic buildings through policy guidance, financial support, simplified procedures, and other means.
The person responsible for protection may use a historic building as a memorial venue, exhibition hall, museum, tourist attraction, leisure space, or venue for cultural and creative activities or local cultural research, in light of its characteristics.
Use shall comply with the protection plan and fire-safety and other professional requirements and be compatible with the building's historic value and internal structure. State-owned historic buildings may be used appropriately through lawful leasing and other means.
articles.48: Article 48 Protection signs shall be placed on famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, and historic buildings. The Municipal People's Government shall establish a uniform sign design and the District (County-level City) People's Government shall arrange installation. A sign shall state relevant information about the protected matter. No entity or individual may install, move, cover, alter, or damage a sign without authorization.
articles.49:
Article 49 In accordance with the protection plan, the District (County-level City) People's Government shall give priority to construction and improvement of fire-safety, road, water supply and drainage, electricity, sanitation, and other infrastructure for famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, areas with historic character, and historic buildings. Construction shall use effective protective measures and shall not damage protected matters or impair the environmental character.
If protection needs make it impossible to build under current technical standards and codes, the relevant departments shall assess the matter, propose a solution suited to actual conditions, and submit it to the protection committee for review.
articles.50: Article 50 Large outdoor advertisements, signs, plaques, direction signs, and other outdoor advertising facilities within a protected area of a famous town or village, historic and cultural district, area with historic character, or historic building shall comply with the protection plan, shall not damage the building itself, and shall be compatible with the environment and landscape. Before approval under the law, relevant departments shall solicit opinions from the natural resources and cultural relics departments.
articles.51:
Article 51 The Municipal People's Government shall supervise and inspect protection work by the District (County-level City) People's Governments, regularly assess the work, make assessment results public, and promptly correct or address problems identified.
The municipal or county-level city natural resources department and cultural relics department shall inspect the condition of protected matters on the protection list and the preparation and implementation of plans and promptly propose correction where problems are found.
articles.52:
Article 52 Any entity or individual may dissuade or report to a people's government at any level or a relevant competent department conduct damaging or destroying the historic and cultural city, famous towns and villages, historic and cultural districts, or historic buildings.
The Municipal and District (County-level City) People's Governments and relevant departments shall publish complaint and reporting channels and promptly verify, handle, and respond to reports.
Chapter V — Legal Liability
articles.53: Article 53 Where a State organ or its staff commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations, the Municipal or District (County-level City) People's Government or relevant competent department shall order correction and impose sanctions in accordance with the law on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible personnel: (1) failing to organize preparation of a protection plan or failing to follow statutory procedures; (2) amending an approved plan without authorization or failing to publish it; (3) failing to perform approval duties under statutory procedures or the protection plan; (4) inadequate protection causing an officially designated historic and cultural city, town, or village to be placed on an endangered list; or (5) abusing official powers, neglecting duties, or engaging in favoritism or malpractice.
articles.54:
Article 54 Where any of the following conduct violates these Regulations, the law-enforcement authority shall order the person to stop and restore the original condition or take other remedial measures within a specified period, confiscate unlawful income, and, if the person fails to comply by the deadline, may designate a capable entity to carry out the work at the violator's expense. The violator shall compensate for any losses: (1) damaging an interim-protection matter; (2) violating Article 32(1), (2), or (3); (3) externally repairing or decorating, adding facilities to, or changing the structure or use of a historic building without approval, or carrying out an approved activity in a manner that damages the traditional layout, historic character, or historic building; or (4) damaging, relocating, or demolishing a historic building without authorization.
If serious consequences result, for conduct under paragraph (1) or (3), a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 100,000 shall be imposed on an entity or RMB 20,000 to RMB 50,000 on an individual; for conduct under paragraph (2), a fine of RMB 600,000 to RMB 1,000,000 on an entity or RMB 60,000 to RMB 100,000 on an individual; and for conduct under paragraph (4), a fine of RMB 300,000 to RMB 500,000 on an entity or RMB 100,000 to RMB 200,000 on an individual.
articles.55: Article 55 Where a person violates Article 48 by installing, moving, altering, or damaging a protection sign without authorization, the law-enforcement authority shall order correction within a specified period. If correction is not made by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of RMB 20,000 to RMB 50,000 on an entity or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 on an individual.
articles.56:
Article 56 Where laws or regulations prescribe penalties for other conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
Chapter VI — Supplementary Provisions
articles.57: Article 57 For purposes of these Regulations: (1) ‘historic urban area’ means an area with clearly defined historic boundaries, a relatively well-preserved layout and character, and a need for protection; (2) ‘historic area’ means an area with a long history and surviving historic layout and cultural relics that does not qualify as an urban historic district; (3) ‘area with historic character’ means an area with a concentration of historic buildings or buildings of traditional character whose architectural styles, spatial layout, and streetscape substantially reflect regional cultural features of a particular historical period but which does not qualify as a historic and cultural district; and (4) ‘historic environmental features’ means ancient wells, walls, stone steps, paving, embankments, ancient or notable trees, and other features reflecting historic character.
articles.58: Article 58 These Regulations shall take effect on 1 January 2021.

FBMCLI.10.7308159.title: Regulations of Guangzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2023 Revision)

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Guangzhou's circumstances and under the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Regulations on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages and other laws and regulations, to strengthen the protection and management of the city's historic and cultural city, carry forward its outstanding history and culture, and promote coordinated development of urban and rural construction and social culture.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to planning, protection, use, management and related activities concerning the historic and cultural city within Guangzhou's administrative area.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall follow the principles of scientific planning, categorized management, strict conservation, appropriate use, shared governance and regional coordination.
articles.4: Article 4. The municipal and district people's governments shall protect and supervise historic and cultural heritage in their respective areas, improve institutional and policy safeguards, incorporate the work into their economic and social development plans, and provide the necessary funding in their budgets. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall perform their assigned duties, conduct routine inspections and outreach, and encourage public participation. Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist them.
articles.5: Article 5. Historic and Cultural City Protection Committees established by municipal and district governments shall coordinate, guide and supervise protection and review major matters, including protection lists and plans. Each committee shall comprise officials from the government and relevant departments at the same level, with its rules of procedure prescribed by that government. It shall establish expert consultation and public-participation mechanisms; experts shall participate in reviews of major matters, and NPC deputies, CPPCC members and the public shall be consulted through appropriate means.
articles.6: Article 6. The planning and natural resources department shall administer protection planning, promote public awareness and implement this Regulation. The culture, radio, television and tourism department shall protect and supervise cultural relics and intangible cultural heritage. The housing and urban-rural development department shall supervise building-use and structural safety and repair of buildings and structures, historic buildings and traditional-character buildings in protected core areas of historic towns, villages, districts, character areas and traditional villages. The industry and information technology, agriculture and rural affairs, forestry and landscaping, civil affairs, water affairs, commerce, urban management enforcement and other departments shall perform their respective protection duties.
articles.7: Article 7. Municipal and district governments shall, in accordance with national and provincial rules, encourage lawful participation by organizations and individuals through certificates of honor, commendations, awards and other means, including donations, grants, investment, public-interest organizations, technical assistance and volunteer services.
articles.8: Article 8. The municipal government shall use heritage to build connections and cooperation with other cities in China and abroad, jointly protect and use significant cross-regional heritage, study and promote heritage such as the Ancient Post Roads of Southern Guangdong, and advance protection of the Maritime Silk Road and joint applications for World Heritage status.
articles.9: Article 9. Protected subjects include: (1) historic towns, villages, districts and character areas; traditional villages, historic gardens and distinctive tree-lined streets; cultural relics, historic and traditional-character buildings, revolutionary sites, ancient and notable trees and their successor resources, intangible cultural heritage, traditional place names and other subjects protected by law; (2) historic urban areas, industrial, agricultural and water-management heritage, historic waterways, remains of modern railways, the Ancient Post Roads of Southern Guangdong and traditional streets and lanes; and (3) other subjects identified in approved heritage-protection plans or territorial spatial plans, or designated by the State, province or city.
articles.10: Article 10. Identification and adjustment of protected subjects shall follow applicable national, provincial and municipal rules. Where none exist, the competent authority shall formulate identification and adjustment standards and procedures, obtain municipal government approval, and publish and implement them. Proposals shall be developed after consulting experts, relevant departments, owners and other interested parties through hearings, meetings, written comments or other means, and shall be publicly announced. A lawfully identified subject may not be adjusted arbitrarily; an adjustment required by a change in protection level or loss of heritage value shall follow the foregoing procedure.
articles.11: Article 11. The competent authority shall prepare and update the protection list based on identified subjects, stating each subject's name, location, period of origin and historic and cultural value, and promptly publish the list.
articles.12: Article 12. The municipal government shall organize a citywide heritage survey. A district government shall designate resources found in the survey and considered valuable by experts as provisionally protected subjects. Any organization or individual may submit a lead or proposal, including through the government service hotline. The district government shall verify it or arrange expert review within 15 days and designate a resource of protection value provisionally. Within five days of designation, it shall notify the owner, user or custodian, post a public notice at the local villagers' or residents' committee, and arrange routine on-site inspections and protection through the town government or subdistrict office. During provisional protection, the rules applicable to the proposed category apply. The competent authority shall complete formal identification within one year after notice. If it does not, provisional protection expires automatically. The district government shall compensate losses to lawful interests caused by provisional protection.
articles.13: Article 13. The competent authority shall maintain a dynamic, digital archive for each protected subject, including survey and identification materials; cultural, artistic and historic characteristics, historical development, events, notable persons and technical information; current use and ownership changes; protection plans; design and survey materials; records, drawings, photographs and video created during repair, maintenance, relocation or demolition; and other materials requiring preservation. Any organization or individual may inspect archive information as permitted by law.
articles.14: Article 14. Protection plans shall delineate protected core areas, construction-control zones, environmental-coordination zones and other heritage-protection boundaries, and prescribe conservation, spatial-control and other measures. They shall protect heritage holistically and systematically, manage the overall spatial form and architectural character of heritage and its surroundings, coordinate utilities and infrastructure, and improve living conditions. In protected cores of historic towns, villages, districts, character areas and traditional villages, population density and commercial real-estate development shall be reasonably controlled; population and functions in the core, control zone and surrounding areas shall be coordinated, and public services and municipal infrastructure improved. Land-use rights in a protected core may not be transferred as a whole for commercial real-estate development.
