Plans for such areas and for historic buildings may serve as detailed territorial spatial plans. Plans for the historic and cultural city, historic towns and villages, districts, character areas and historic buildings shall be completed within one year after designation and publication.
articles.15: Article 15. Protection plans shall be prepared and submitted for approval as follows: (1) the municipal government prepares the city plan, which is reviewed by the Standing Committee of the Municipal People's Congress and submitted to the provincial government for approval; (2) the municipal government prepares district plans and submits them for approval under applicable rules; (3) district governments prepare plans for historic towns and villages in their jurisdictions, which, after municipal review, are submitted to the provincial government; (4) the municipal planning and natural resources department prepares plans for historic buildings and character areas for municipal approval; (5) district governments prepare protection and development plans for traditional villages and submit them under applicable rules; and (6) other plans follow applicable laws, regulations and competent-authority rules. Draft plans shall be published for at least 30 days, with comments solicited from departments, experts and the public through meetings, hearings or other means, and then reviewed by the Protection Committee. Approved plans shall be published on government websites and in major news media within 30 days.
articles.16: Article 16. The city protection plan shall identify as key subjects: (1) mountains including Baiyun, Maofeng and Jiulian, and river and waterway systems centered on the Pearl River, Liuxi River and Zengjiang River; (2) the ancient axis from Beijing Road to Tianzi Wharf and the modern axis from Zhenhai Tower on Yuexiu Mountain via the Sun Yat-sen Monument and Memorial Hall, People's Park, Guangzhou Uprising Road and Haizhu Square to Haizhu Bridge; remains of the old city walls, the Pearl River ecological and cultural corridor, historic waterways and heritage along them; (3) the mountain-and-river view corridors from Baiyun Mountain to Sun Yat-sen University's north gate and from Baiyun Mountain via Yuexiu Mountain to the Pearl River; (4) heritage reflecting Guangzhou's significance as a center of Lingnan culture, birthplace of the Maritime Silk Road, cradle of China's democratic revolution, pioneer of reform and opening-up and center of overseas Chinese culture, including historic settlements, streets, arcades, immovable cultural relics, revolutionary sites and historic or traditional-character buildings; (5) industrial, agricultural and water-management heritage showing local production and industrial development; (6) intangible heritage reflecting Lingnan culture, including traditional arts, customs and crafts; and (7) other priorities designated by the municipal government.
articles.17: Article 17. District governments shall prepare implementation plans based on approved protection plans, specifying tasks, responsible implementers and measures. These plans shall address character management, uses, fire safety, municipal services and transport, design requirements for construction, and implementation schedules.
articles.18: Article 18. An approved protection plan may not be changed arbitrarily. Where a change is necessary, the original preparer shall submit a reasoned report; after approval by the original approving authority, the plan shall be amended, submitted, approved and filed through the original procedures.
articles.19: Article 19. The competent authority shall publish at service counters and on government websites approved survey results, protection lists, plans and implementation programs. District governments shall publish information on provisionally protected subjects on their websites.
articles.20: Article 20. Municipal and district governments shall designate and publish responsible protection entities for historic towns, villages, districts and character areas and traditional villages: (1) the subdistrict office for a historic district or character area; (2) the town government or subdistrict office for a historic town; (3) the villagers' or residents' committee for a historic village or traditional village; and (4) a protection-management organization established by a municipal or district government, where applicable. For a subject spanning villages, the relevant town government or subdistrict office shall designate the responsible entity; for one spanning subdistricts or towns, the district government shall do so; and for one spanning districts, the municipal government shall do so.
articles.21: Article 21. The responsible entity for a historic town, village, district or character area, or traditional village, shall follow the protection plan and: (1) preserve the integrity of the traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale and historic environmental features of buildings and structures in the protected area; (2) conduct routine inspections and promptly stop harmful conduct, handle it lawfully or notify the competent department; (3) keep the area clean and orderly; (4) assist departments in keeping fire-safety, disaster-prevention and other public facilities operational; and (5) meet other requirements prescribed by this Regulation or municipal or district governments.
articles.22: Article 22. The responsible entity for a historic building shall be determined as follows: (1) for a state-owned building, its managing entity; (2) for a non-state-owned building, its owner; if the owner is missing, cannot be contacted or title is unclear, its custodian; if there is no custodian, its user; and (3) if none of these is identifiable, the responsible sectoral authority, or, if none is identifiable, the housing and urban-rural development department. After designation, the district government shall identify the responsible entity, notify it in writing and explain its duties. If an organization or individual objects, the district government shall decide whether to change the designation based on the evidence. District governments shall periodically verify title, custody and use and promptly update the designation when responsibility changes.
articles.23: Article 23. The responsible entity for a historic building shall: (1) preserve its traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration and historic environmental features; (2) ensure structural safety, take immediate risk-mitigation measures and report hazards to the local town government, subdistrict office or competent department; (3) maintain, repair and use it in accordance with this Regulation and the protection plan; (4) prevent water ingress, damp and insect damage; (5) keep fire-safety, disaster-prevention and other facilities operational; (6) keep it clean and orderly; and (7) meet other statutory requirements. A transfer or lease contract shall specify protection and repair duties, and the transferor or lessor shall notify the transferee or lessee of those requirements.
articles.24: Article 24. The competent departments for industrial and information technology, agriculture and rural affairs, and water affairs shall formulate protection and management measures for industrial, agricultural and water-management heritage and other relevant subjects, submit them for municipal approval, and publish them for implementation.
articles.25: Article 25. Before house expropriation or land banking, the responsible departments shall survey and assess historic and cultural heritage; expropriation or land banking may not begin before completion. Construction projects shall include a dedicated heritage survey, assessment and protection section in project initiation materials, proposed detailed territorial spatial plan amendments, design plans and preliminary designs. Urban-renewal area strategies and design plans shall include such a section as well.
articles.26: Article 26. A protection marker shall be installed in a prominent place within six months after designation. It shall state the subject's name, number, location, period of origin, designation date, historic and cultural information and responsible entities, and shall be translated into relevant foreign languages where needed. Digital tools shall enable public access to related information. The municipal government shall set a standard design and district governments shall arrange installation. No organization or individual may install, move, obscure, alter or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.27: Article 27. The planning and natural resources department shall state protection requirements in the drawings and attachments to a construction-land planning permit or planning conditions, and enter them in the real-property register upon an application for registration, where: (1) a building or structure is within a protected core or construction-control zone of a protected historic town, village, district, character area, traditional village, immovable cultural relic or historic building; or (2) the building or structure has itself been designated as a protected subject.
articles.28: Article 28. The planning and natural resources, culture, radio, television and tourism, housing and urban-rural development, industry and information technology, urban management enforcement, civil affairs, agriculture and rural affairs, forestry and landscaping, water affairs, market regulation and other departments shall collect, enter, manage and update protection information according to their duties and share it through the Historic and Cultural City Protection Information System.
articles.29: Article 29. Construction in a protected core area of a historic town, village, district or character area, traditional village or historic building shall comply with the protection plan and preserve the traditional layout and historic character. In the core of a historic town, village or district, new construction or expansion is prohibited except for necessary infrastructure and public-service facilities. No new pollution-generating facility may be built; existing polluting facilities and enterprises shall effectively control pollution. Roads, underground works and municipal utilities shall be built with safeguards against harm to protected subjects. Outdoor advertisements, signs, awnings, air conditioners, connecting corridors, sculptures, sanitation facilities and other external facilities or decoration shall be compatible with historic character. New or rebuilt urban utility lines shall be underground; where this is impracticable or wall-mounted lines are necessary, they shall be concealed or technically treated to meet protection requirements. Renovation in a protected core and new construction, expansion or renovation in a construction-control zone shall comply with applicable construction controls, including compatible height, bulk and color, and shall not damage the traditional layout or historic character.
articles.30: Article 30. Within a historic urban area or the protected area of a historic town, village, district or character area, traditional village or historic building, it is prohibited to: (1) quarry, mine or undertake similar activities that damage traditional layout or historic character; (2) occupy landscaped green space, rivers or lakes, traditional streets or roads; (3) build factories or warehouses for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; or (4) undertake other activities likely to cause destructive effects on protected subjects.
articles.31: Article 31. In the protected core of a historic building, it is prohibited to: (1) carve or deface the building; (2) store flammable, explosive or corrosive substances inside; (3) build structures on the roof or terrace or against an exterior wall; (4) unlawfully occupy land to build structures; (5) alter courtyard walls or change the interior or exterior structure, form or style without authorization; (6) damage load-bearing components or otherwise endanger structural safety; or (7) engage in other conduct affecting the building's protection.
articles.32: Article 32. An entity or individual undertaking new construction, expansion, or work changing an exterior facade or structure in a protected core or construction-control zone of a historic town, village, district or character area, traditional village or historic building shall include specific heritage-protection measures in the design submitted for planning permission. Where conservation needs make current technical standards impossible to meet, work may proceed while retaining the original building footprint, boundaries and distances from neighboring buildings, subject to planning permission and other required procedures. Before granting permission, the municipal planning and natural resources department shall seek written views from the culture, radio, television and tourism, housing and urban-rural development or other competent departments as appropriate, obtain expert review and seek public comments. Before construction, the developer shall obtain a construction permit, unless the project is a small project below the permit threshold, in which case applicable municipal rules govern.
articles.33: Article 33. The housing and urban-rural development department, together with the planning and natural resources department, shall prepare repair guidelines for buildings and structures in protected cores of historic towns, villages, districts and character areas, traditional villages and historic buildings, specifying repair requirements. Repairs shall preserve traditional layouts and historic character and highlight Lingnan architectural features. The municipal government shall prescribe and publish specific repair-supervision measures.
articles.34: Article 34. The housing and urban-rural development department shall supervise the safety of buildings and structures in the specified protected cores, mark and dynamically update safety information on immovable cultural relics, historic buildings and traditional-character buildings during building-safety surveys, and share information with the planning and natural resources and culture departments. If a building is at risk of damage, it shall promptly notify the responsible entity to repair it. If it is certified as dangerous, the district department shall require remediation, which the responsible entity shall undertake immediately. If danger is urgent or the entity fails to act by the deadline, the district department shall carry out emergency risk mitigation; the entity shall cooperate and may not obstruct it.
articles.35: Article 35. To demolish a building, structure or other facility, other than a historic building, in a protected core of a historic town, village, district or character area, traditional village or historic building, the applicant shall apply to the planning and natural resources department. Within 20 days, that department shall decide jointly with the culture department. Where demolition is part of a new-construction or expansion project, the review may be combined with the construction-planning-permit review. Demolition shall comply with construction-project management rules.
articles.36: Article 36. If construction creates a risk that a building or structure in one of the protected cores specified in this Regulation will be damaged, the construction administration department shall order the contractor to stop work immediately. The contractor or developer shall repair damage caused by construction, and the repair plan shall be reviewed by the planning and natural resources and housing and urban-rural development departments.
articles.37: Article 37. Municipal and district housing and urban-rural development departments shall conduct annual structural-safety reviews of historic buildings and, after hearing the responsible entity, prepare annual repair plans. The district department shall notify responsible entities to repair buildings under the plan, and they shall comply. If a building is certified as dangerous and at risk of damage, and the district civil-affairs department determines that the responsible entity cannot afford repairs, the district government may, with its approval, designate a department to carry out repairs. The responsible entity, town government and subdistrict office shall cooperate and support the work; public funds shall cover the cost.
articles.38: Article 38. Repairs to historic buildings shall comply with technical specifications, quality standards and repair guidelines. Before repair, the responsible entity may request free technical advice from local housing and urban-rural development, planning and natural resources or other departments. The housing department shall provide free technical services for repair drawings and construction plans; the planning department shall provide free design services for additions, alterations or expansions. Departments may procure services from qualified entities for consultation and guidance as needed.
articles.39: Article 39. Except for routine maintenance and minor repairs that do not affect character-defining features, materials, construction or decoration, the responsible entity shall, before repair, prepare preliminary and construction drawings and a work plan in accordance with district housing-department guidance and submit them for review. If a repair changes an exterior facade or structure, the entity shall obtain a construction or rural construction planning permit as required; the permitting authority shall seek the culture department's views as appropriate. During repairs, the contractor shall display information about the building's heritage value and illustrations of the planned result. The district housing department shall inspect repair work and guide corrections if it does not meet technical specifications, quality standards or repair guidelines.
articles.40: Article 40. The responsible entity for a non-state-owned historic building may apply to municipal or district departments for a repair subsidy if repairs comply with technical specifications, quality standards, repair guidelines and the approved design and work plan. If it still cannot afford the repairs after receiving the subsidy, it may apply for hardship assistance. The municipal government shall prescribe and publish detailed subsidy measures.
articles.41: Article 41. Historic buildings shall be preserved in situ. No organization or individual may damage, relocate or demolish one without authorization. If relocation or demolition is essential for a major public interest, such as national-defense facilities or a key national or provincial project, the planning and natural resources department, together with the culture and housing departments, shall review the relocation plan and mitigation measures, publish them and hold a hearing. The municipal government shall decide based on the review and hearing and seek approval as required. For a non-state-owned building, the responsible entity shall be consulted. If relocation or demolition is approved, the developer shall carry it out under construction-management rules and the construction administration department shall supervise it.
articles.42: Article 42. Competent protection authorities and urban-management enforcement departments shall monitor protected subjects using video surveillance, remote sensing and other means, and promptly detect, stop and address damage to protected subjects and unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or destruction of markers. District governments shall establish routine inspection mechanisms and include inspections in community-grid management. In routine inspections, town governments and subdistrict offices shall assist with safety and disaster prevention, handle violations as authorized or refer them to the competent department, and promptly report major incidents to the district government.
articles.43: Article 43. Municipal and district governments shall establish a project pool for protection and use and coordinate heritage work with urban renewal, land transfers and rural revitalization. In coordinated urban-renewal projects, floor-area incentives may be granted under applicable rules where protected subjects are conserved and appropriately used; floor area used for public-benefit, non-profit purposes may be excluded from floor-area calculations. For projects coordinated with land banking and transfer, the competent authority or district government shall propose implementation needs, which, after municipal approval, shall be included in the land-transfer conditions. In rural-revitalization projects, construction-land quotas shall be arranged efficiently. Rural collective economic organizations may revitalize heritage through lawful exchange of new and old homestead sites, equity investment, leasing and operation, or collective acquisition of ownerless property.
articles.44: Article 44. Financial institutions and local financial organizations are encouraged to support heritage protection and use projects, develop financial products and services, improve service processes and broaden financing. Municipal and district governments may include projects in urban-renewal funds. Enterprises, other organizations and individuals are encouraged to support public-interest protection through funds or donations; donors may receive tax benefits under applicable law.
articles.45: Article 45. The administrative authority responsible for a state-owned protected subject shall arrange for its appropriate use, together with the state-assets supervision and culture departments, in light of its characteristics.
articles.46: Article 46. During urban renewal or development of new urban areas, if the owner of a non-state-owned immovable cultural relic, historic building, traditional-character building or industrial heritage agrees to expropriation or redevelopment, the expropriating authority or redevelopment entity shall incorporate protection requirements in the compensation or redevelopment plan, assess value under the applicable house-expropriation assessment rules, and compensate the owner at no less than 120% of the market price of comparable premises in the expropriation block on the date the expropriation decision is announced. The same compensation rule applies when a non-state-owned historic building is demolished under Article 41(2).
articles.47: Article 47. Municipal and district governments shall support third-party operators in acquiring buildings and structures within protected areas through title transfer, exchange, entrusted management, lease termination and other vacating arrangements, and converting them into public-service facilities, innovation and entrepreneurship spaces, or publicly accessible green spaces, squares and pocket parks, in order to restore historic character and traditional layouts and improve living conditions.
articles.48: Article 48. For areas with concentrated heritage, district governments shall adopt industry-guidance policies consistent with heritage value, traditional layout and historic character to optimize resource allocation. Measures may support time-honored brands, representative intangible heritage and culturally significant businesses; cultivate industry clusters and attract universities, research bodies, cultural institutions, innovative enterprises, master artisans and notable-person studios; introduce small incubators, start-up services and shared offices; and promote other uses encouraged by municipal or district governments.
articles.49: Article 49. In accordance with protection plans, municipal and district governments shall prioritize roads, water supply and drainage, electricity, gas, sanitation, fire-safety and other infrastructure around protected subjects. Where current technical standards cannot be followed, departments shall set construction and management requirements and safeguards suited to conservation needs. The municipal government shall arrange standards for service connections and installation of outdoor equipment such as air conditioners to preserve residents' convenience.
articles.50: Article 50. The municipal government shall adopt measures to promote appropriate use of historic buildings through policy guidance, funding, simplified procedures, reduced or waived rent for state-owned buildings and longer lease terms. Municipal and district governments shall support varied uses suited to each building, including memorials, exhibitions, museums, tourism, recreation, cultural and creative work, local-culture research, intangible-heritage and Lingnan-craft transmission, time-honored businesses, technology incubation, start-ups, offices, distinctive food businesses and homestays. While retaining the original exterior and characteristic components, additions, alterations, expansions and facilities may be made to meet modern needs. Governments may acquire or exchange title to protect and use non-state-owned historic buildings, and may acquire on equal terms a subsidized building offered for sale. State-owned historic buildings may be leased for up to 20 years; rent relief may be granted under applicable rules. Subject to structural, fire-safety and protection-plan requirements, responsible entities may put a historic building to varied uses. A difference between actual use and registered use does not require planning approval. Planning approval is also unnecessary for work that does not increase floor area or height, expand the footprint, change boundaries, alter the facade or affect the structure.
articles.51: Article 51. Municipal and district governments shall connect heritage of different types and levels through routes, corridors and networks integrated into everyday life, presenting Guangzhou's history comprehensively. Relevant departments shall research and explain red culture, Lingnan culture, Maritime Silk Road culture, innovation, overseas-Chinese culture, local customs, traditional crafts, Cantonese, historic stories and Cantonese cuisine; hold traditional festivals, markets and cultural activities; connect heritage sites through visitor routes; encourage public access; and encourage schools to conduct related activities. Housing, culture and other departments shall organize training in traditional crafts. Education and human-resources departments shall support vocational and technical schools in offering heritage-conservation courses and training traditional-craft workers.
articles.52: Article 52. Guangzhou shall establish a condition-review and assessment system. The municipal government shall review protection and use conditions annually and comprehensively assess implementation and results of protection plans every five years.
articles.53: Article 53. If a district government or its personnel fails to perform duties, the municipal government shall order correction and issue a notice of criticism. Serious cases shall result in disciplinary action against directly responsible officials and other personnel by the competent authority; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable. This applies to failure to prepare or amend plans for historic towns, villages or traditional villages according to required procedures, deadlines or standards; failure to take provisional-protection measures under Article 12, prepare implementation plans under Article 17, designate responsible entities for cross-jurisdiction subjects under Article 20, or complete heritage assessments before expropriation or land banking under Article 25; and dereliction of duty, abuse of authority or favoritism.
articles.54: Article 54. If a department or its personnel fails to perform duties, the people's government at the same level or a superior department shall, according to its authority, order correction and issue a notice of criticism. Serious cases shall result in disciplinary action by the competent authority; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable. Violations include failure to adopt lawful identification and adjustment procedures; prepare historic-building or character-area plans properly or on time; prepare or update protection lists under Article 11 or publish information under Article 19; discharge protection duties under Articles 23 and 37; issue management measures under Article 24; assess heritage before expropriation or land banking under Article 25; record protection requirements under Article 27; comply with Articles 32 and 39 in granting planning or construction permits; prepare repair guidelines and supervise repairs under Article 33; supervise building safety under Article 34; lawfully approve demolition under Article 35; prepare and implement annual repairs under Article 37; comply with Article 41 on relocation or demolition; appropriately use state-owned protected subjects under Article 45; or issue infrastructure and installation standards under Article 49. Dereliction, abuse of authority and favoritism are also covered.
articles.55: Article 55. If a subdistrict office, town government or its personnel fails to inspect or protect subjects as required by Articles 12 and 42, the district government shall order correction. Serious cases shall result in disciplinary action by the competent authority; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable.
articles.56: Article 56. If a district government, subdistrict office, town government, villagers' or residents' committee, protection-management organization or its personnel fails to perform the duties in Article 21, the competent authority shall order correction and issue a notice of criticism. Serious cases shall result in disciplinary action; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable.
articles.57: Article 57. If a historic-building responsible entity breaches Article 23(1) or (4), causing destructive effects, urban-management enforcement shall order it to perform its duties by a deadline. If it fails, the department may arrange performance by another party at the entity's expense. In serious cases, the entity shall be fined RMB 50,000–100,000 if an organization, or RMB 10,000–50,000 if an individual. The housing department shall apply the same penalties if failure to ensure structural safety or mitigate a known hazard under Article 23(2) causes destructive effects.
articles.58: Article 58. If construction in breach of Article 29(1)(1) or (3), or Article 29(2), violates the protection plan and damages the traditional layout or historic character, urban-management enforcement or the town government shall order work to stop and the unlawful part to be removed or corrected by a deadline, and may impose a fine of up to 10% of the construction cost.
articles.59: Article 59. Repairing a historic building without the construction-planning or rural-construction-planning permit required by Article 39(1) shall be handled by urban-management enforcement or the town government under rules for unlawful construction.
articles.60: Article 60. If a new polluting facility is built in a protected core or construction-control zone, or an existing polluting facility or enterprise fails to take required pollution-control measures, in violation of Article 29(1)(2), the ecology and environment department shall impose penalties under environmental-protection laws and regulations.
articles.61: Article 61. If outdoor advertising, signs, awnings, air conditioners, connecting corridors, sculptures, sanitation facilities or other external facilities or decoration are incompatible with historic character, in violation of Article 29(1)(4), urban-management enforcement shall order correction or restoration by a deadline. In serious cases, the fine shall be RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual.
articles.62: Article 62. Violations of Articles 30 and 31 shall be handled as follows: (1) harmful quarrying, mining or similar activity: urban-management enforcement or the town government under applicable law; (2) occupation of landscaped green space: forestry and landscaping department; (3) occupation of rivers or lakes: water-affairs department; (4) occupation of roads: transport or urban-management department; (5) defacement of a historic building: urban-management department; (6) storage of flammable, explosive or corrosive substances in a historic building: public-security department; (7) unlawful construction or occupation of land for construction: urban-management enforcement or town government; (8) unauthorized alteration of courtyard walls or a building's interior or exterior structure, form or style: urban-management enforcement or town government; (9) damage to load-bearing components or other threats to building safety: housing department; and (10) other activities destructively affecting protected subjects: urban-management enforcement or town government. Applicable laws and regulations govern penalties.
articles.63: Article 63. If failure to repair as required by Article 23(1)(3), Article 37(2) or Article 39 has destructive effects on a historic building, urban-management enforcement shall order correction and restoration or other remedial measures by a deadline. If the violator fails to comply, the department may appoint a capable entity to act at the violator's expense. In serious cases, the fine shall be RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual.
articles.64: Article 64. Unauthorized demolition, contrary to Article 35, of a building, structure or other facility other than a historic building within a protected core shall be penalized by urban-management enforcement under the Regulations on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages.
articles.65: Article 65. If a historic building is damaged, relocated or demolished without authorization in violation of Article 41, urban-management enforcement shall order the conduct to stop and require restoration or other remedial measures by a deadline. If the violator fails, the department may appoint a capable entity to act at the violator's expense. In serious cases, the fine shall be RMB 200,000–500,000 for an organization or RMB 100,000–200,000 for an individual. The department may seek written advice from the planning and natural resources department on whether restoration should be ordered; that department shall reply within 30 days. Restoration shall be completed within the deadline in the decision and approved reconstruction plan, and verified jointly by the relevant urban-management, planning, culture and housing departments.
articles.66: Article 66. Unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or damage of a protection marker in violation of Article 26 shall result in an order to correct by a deadline. If not corrected, the fine shall be RMB 10,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 1,000–10,000 for an individual.
articles.67: Article 67. This Regulation takes effect on 1 January 2024.

FBMCLI.10.7807668.title: Regulations of Weifang Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Weifang's circumstances and under the Urban and Rural Planning Law, the Cultural Relics Protection Law, the national Regulations on the Protection of Historic and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Shandong provincial regulations and other laws, to strengthen protection, carry forward outstanding culture, uphold socialist core values, and promote coordinated urban development and social culture.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to protection, use and management of the historic and cultural city within Weifang's administrative area.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall be based on scientific planning, strict conservation and appropriate use; maintain and continue traditional layouts and historic character; preserve the authenticity and integrity of heritage and ensure sustainable protection and use; and properly balance socioeconomic development with heritage conservation.
articles.4: Article 4. Municipal and county-level (city/district) governments shall protect and supervise heritage in their areas, incorporate protection into economic and social development and territorial spatial plans, and budget for it consistently with the allocation of governmental powers and fiscal responsibilities. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall perform their assigned duties and conduct routine inspections and public outreach. Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist with protection.
articles.5: Article 5. Municipal and county-level governments shall establish Historic and Cultural City Protection Committees to coordinate, guide and supervise protection and review major matters, including protection lists and plans. The government at the same level shall prescribe committee procedures. Committees shall establish expert consultation and public-participation mechanisms, invite experts to review major matters and solicit views from NPC deputies, CPPCC members and the public through appropriate means.
articles.6: Article 6. The natural resources and planning department, together with the housing and urban-rural development and cultural-relics departments (collectively, the protection authorities), shall exercise unified supervision over citywide protection. Natural resources and planning departments shall supervise historic urban areas, districts, areas, historic buildings and traditional-character buildings; housing and urban-rural development departments shall supervise historic towns, villages and traditional villages; and cultural-relics departments shall supervise related cultural relics. Development and reform, education, industry and information technology, civil affairs, finance, urban management, transport, water administration, agriculture and rural affairs, administrative-approval services, national-defense mobilization, fire and rescue, and other bodies shall assist according to their duties.
articles.7: Article 7. Governments at all levels shall provide public education on heritage protection, disseminate relevant knowledge and raise public awareness. Radio, television, newspapers, the internet and other media shall conduct public-interest outreach.
articles.8: Article 8. Social actors are encouraged to participate lawfully through donations, grants, investment, technical or volunteer services and other means. Municipal and county-level governments shall commend or reward outstanding contributions under national rules. Everyone has a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and may stop, complain about or report damage. Departments receiving a complaint or report shall promptly accept and investigate it and take appropriate action.
articles.9: Article 9. Protected subjects include the historic urban area, historic districts, historic towns and villages, traditional villages, historic areas, historic buildings, traditional-character buildings, place-name heritage and other protected subjects. Immovable cultural relics, ancient and notable trees, intangible cultural heritage, industrial and agricultural heritage, irrigation works and other such subjects are protected, used and managed under applicable laws and regulations.
articles.10: Article 10. Identification and nomination of protected subjects shall follow applicable laws and regulations. A historic area or traditional-character building shall be reviewed by experts organized by the county-level natural resources and planning department together with the cultural-relics department, and then designated and published by the government at that level. The standard names of designated historic and cultural cities, towns and villages shall remain relatively stable.
articles.11: Article 11. The municipal government shall establish a historic-city protection list. The municipal natural resources and planning department shall formulate detailed measures. Subjects approved, designated or published by the State Council or a provincial or municipal or county-level government shall be entered on the list.
articles.12: Article 12. Municipal and county-level civil-affairs departments, together with relevant departments, shall survey place names of significant historic and cultural value that reflect Weifang's historical development, and collect, record and compile relevant information. Such place names shall be placed on the protection list and made public.
articles.13: Article 13. County-level natural resources and planning departments, together with housing and cultural-relics departments, shall prepare historic-building protection guidelines to guide conservation. The guidelines shall state the name, location and construction date; core heritage values; protection category, requirements and use recommendations; protected area, construction controls and prohibited uses; and other information required by law. The department shall provide the guidelines and instructions free of charge to owners, users, custodians and property-service providers.
articles.14: Article 14. If force majeure causes a protected subject to be seriously damaged or destroyed, or its protection level or category changes, the competent authority shall promptly propose an amendment to the protection list and submit it for approval through the procedure used by the authority that published the subject.
articles.15: Article 15. Any organization or individual who discovers a possible protected subject under Article 9 shall submit a lead or proposal, including through the government service hotline. Within 15 days after receipt, the county-level government shall verify and inspect the matter with relevant departments and decide how to proceed. If it may qualify, immediate site-protection measures shall be taken. If expert review confirms protection value, it shall be added to the list and the owner, user or manager notified in writing. A county-level government shall appropriately recognize or reward a person or organization whose report, delivery, application or proposal results in timely protection.
articles.16: Article 16. Protection plans shall delineate protected cores, construction-control zones and environmental-coordination zones and set spatial controls, requirements and measures for holistic, systematic and comprehensive conservation. Urban design shall manage the overall spatial form and architectural character of heritage and its surroundings; utilities and infrastructure shall be coordinated; and living conditions improved. Plans or guidelines for the historic city, districts, towns, villages, traditional villages, historic areas and buildings shall be completed within one year of designation. After historic and traditional-character buildings are designated, the county-level government shall establish their protection files.
articles.17: Article 17. Protection plans for the historic city and historic towns shall be incorporated into the overall territorial spatial plans for the city or county and town. Plans for historic districts and areas shall be incorporated into detailed plans. Plans for historic villages and traditional villages shall be incorporated into village plans; a protection plan prepared to village-plan detail may serve as that village's plan. Special plans for roads and transport, municipal utilities, landscaping, sanitation, fire protection, civil defense and underground development affecting protected places shall be coordinated with protection plans. Before submission for approval, the department preparing a special plan shall seek comments from natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, and cultural-relics departments.
articles.18: Article 18. Place names on the protection list shall be protected and used by: (1) strictly limiting renaming; (2) publicizing and protecting their heritage through plaques, steles and similar means; (3) reasonably deriving names from them when naming or renaming nearby geographic features; (4) restoring a discontinued name when the geographic feature is rebuilt at or relocated from its original site, as appropriate; and (5) adopting other protection and use measures.
articles.19: Article 19. Municipal and county-level governments shall designate and publish responsible entities for historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic areas: (1) the county-level government for a historic urban area; (2) the town government or subdistrict office for a historic district or area; (3) the town government or subdistrict office for a historic town, village or traditional village; and (4) a protection-management organization established by a municipal or county-level government. Where a subject spans towns or subdistricts, all relevant governments or offices are responsible and the county-level protection authority coordinates. Where it spans counties or districts, all relevant county-level governments are responsible and the municipal protection authority coordinates.
articles.20: Article 20. Responsible entities for historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic areas shall comply with protection plans and: (1) preserve the integrity of traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale and historic environmental features; (2) inspect routinely and promptly stop harmful conduct, handle it lawfully or notify the competent department; (3) keep protected areas clean and orderly; (4) assign personnel to maintain fire-safety, disaster-prevention and other public facilities and keep them operational; and (5) meet other legal requirements.
articles.21: Article 21. The responsible entity for a historic or traditional-character building shall be: (1) for a state-owned building, its managing entity; (2) for a non-state-owned building, its owner, or, if the owner is missing, cannot be contacted or title is unclear, its custodian, or, if none, its user; or (3) if none is identifiable, the town government or subdistrict office where it is located. After designation, the county-level government shall identify the responsible entity. If an organization or individual objects, it shall decide whether to change the designation based on the evidence. It shall periodically verify ownership, custody and use and promptly update the designation when these change.
articles.22: Article 22. The responsible entity for a historic or traditional-character building shall: (1) preserve traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration and historic environmental features; (2) ensure safety, promptly mitigate hazards and report them to the local town government, subdistrict office or competent department; (3) provide and maintain fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities; (4) use, maintain and repair the building lawfully and appropriately in accordance with protection guidelines; and (5) meet other legal requirements. To discharge the duty in item (4), it may obtain information, financial assistance and technical guidance from natural resources and planning, housing and cultural-relics departments. Transfer or lease contracts shall specify protection and repair duties, and transferors and lessors shall inform transferees and lessees of them.
articles.23: Article 23. Before house expropriation or land banking, the responsible department shall survey and assess heritage; expropriation or land banking may not begin before completion. The results shall be submitted to the municipal natural resources and planning department and filed with the provincial housing and urban-rural development department as required.
articles.24: Article 24. Within protected areas of historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic areas, it is prohibited to: (1) quarry, mine or conduct similar activities that damage traditional layout or historic character; (2) occupy landscaped green areas, rivers, lakes, traditional streets or roads designated for preservation in a protection plan; (3) build factories or warehouses for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; or (4) conduct other activities likely to cause destructive effects on protected subjects.
articles.25: Article 25. Construction in historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic areas shall comply with these requirements: (1) no new construction or expansion is allowed in a protected core; where necessary for infrastructure or public services, the developer shall submit a plan consistent with the protection plan and obtain required approvals; (2) demolition in a protected core of buildings, structures or facilities other than historic buildings requires a compliant demolition plan approved by the local protection authority together with the cultural-relics department; (3) renovation in a protected core of other buildings, structures or facilities requires a compliant renovation plan and approvals; (4) new construction or expansion in a construction-control zone shall meet the protection plan's controls; and (5) construction in an environmental-coordination zone shall meet the plan and be compatible in height, bulk and color with the historic character.
articles.26: Article 26. Within a historic or traditional-character building's protected area, it is prohibited to: (1) carve or deface the building; (2) store flammable, explosive or corrosive substances in a manner endangering its safety; (3) relocate or demolish it without authorization; (4) alter the structure of a traditional-character building or damage its original form or character without authorization; (5) install advertisements, signs or posters that damage or impair its character; or (6) otherwise damage the building or violate its protection guidelines.
articles.27: Article 27. Where construction within a historic or traditional-character building's protected area is necessary for the public interest: (1) if a historic building cannot be preserved in situ and must be relocated or demolished, required procedures under applicable laws and regulations shall be followed; and (2) reconstruction, alteration or demolition of a traditional-character building shall comply with the protection plan for its historic district, town, village or historic area.
articles.28: Article 28. Firefighting facilities and access routes in protected cores of the specified historic places shall comply with fire-safety technical standards and identify a person responsible for fire safety. If conservation needs make compliance impossible, the municipal or county-level fire and rescue agency, together with the protection authority at the same level, shall prepare a fire-safety assurance plan.
articles.29: Article 29. Municipal and county-level governments shall install markers in prominent places in protected areas within three months after approval of the protection plan. Markers for historic and traditional-character buildings shall be installed within six months after listing. Markers shall state the subject's name, location, construction date, historic value and responsible entity, and may be translated into foreign languages as needed. Digital tools shall enable public access to information. No one may falsely claim the title of historic and cultural city, town, village or district, or install, move, alter or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.30: Article 30. When the owner of a building or structure applies for real-property registration, the natural resources and planning department shall note in the register and certificate if: (1) it is within a protected core or construction-control zone of a historic district, town or village, traditional village or historic area; or (2) it has been designated as a protected subject.
articles.31: Article 31. The municipal natural resources and planning department shall establish a unified information platform and database for listed subjects, recording history, ownership, survey data, use and research. Protection files and related data shall, as permitted by law, be made available online to facilitate public access, research sharing and protection and use.
articles.32: Article 32. County-level governments shall establish routine inspection mechanisms and incorporate inspections into community-grid management. Protection authorities and urban-management enforcement shall monitor subjects through video surveillance, remote sensing and other means, and promptly detect and address damage to subjects and unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or destruction of markers. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall assist with safety and disaster prevention, handle violations as authorized or refer them to competent departments, and report major incidents to the county-level government.
articles.33: Article 33. Transmission and use of the historic and cultural city shall promote conservation through appropriate use and activate heritage for continued transmission.
articles.34: Article 34. Municipal and county-level governments shall support third-party operators in acquiring buildings and structures within protected areas through title transfer, exchange, entrusted management, lease termination and other vacating arrangements, and converting them into public-service facilities, innovation and entrepreneurship spaces, or publicly accessible green spaces, squares and pocket parks, restoring historic character and traditional layouts and improving living conditions.
articles.35: Article 35. Governments shall connect heritage of different types and levels through routes, corridors and networks integrated into everyday life, presenting Weifang's history comprehensively. In areas with concentrated heritage, and consistently with heritage value and historic character, they may guide industries and optimize resources by supporting time-honored brands, representative intangible heritage and culturally significant businesses; cultivating clusters and attracting universities, research bodies, cultural institutions, innovative enterprises, master artisans and notable-person studios; introducing incubators, start-up services and shared offices; and promoting other uses they encourage.
articles.36: Article 36. Municipal and county-level governments may support appropriate use of historic and traditional-character buildings as memorials, exhibition halls, museums, tourism and recreation venues, cultural and creative businesses, local-culture research, intangible-heritage and traditional-craft transmission, time-honored businesses, technology incubators, start-ups, offices, distinctive restaurants and homestays. While retaining the original exterior and characteristic components, additions, alterations, expansions and facilities may be made for modern needs. Leasing state-owned buildings for appropriate use shall qualify for support under applicable national, provincial and local rules.
articles.37: Article 37. Subject to structural, fire-safety and protection-plan requirements, where a responsible entity puts a historic or traditional-character building to multiple uses under Article 34(1): (1) a use differing from the registered property use requires approval by the county-level natural resources and planning department together with the cultural-relics department, and completion of other legal procedures; (2) planning approval is not required if the work does not increase floor area or height, expand the footprint, change boundaries, alter the exterior or affect the structure.
articles.38: Article 38. Training traditional craftspeople, transmitting traditional crafts and producing traditional materials related to protection are supported. Housing and culture departments shall provide craft training. Relevant sectoral authorities shall organize vocational-skill certification and establish a grading system for traditional craftspeople. Education and human-resources departments shall support vocational and technical schools in offering heritage-conservation courses and training traditional-craft workers.
articles.39: Article 39. Protection and use of historic places and buildings shall safeguard the lawful rights of original residents and encourage their participation. Original residents are encouraged to operate local industries, improve their living and working conditions, and continue local forms and ways of life. They may participate in protection and use through property, capital contributions or other means.
articles.40: Article 40. The municipal and county-level governments shall use digital technologies, including artificial intelligence and the metaverse, to diversify presentation of heritage and showcase the influence, cohesion and appeal of Weifang's civilization. Modern technologies are encouraged in the presentation and management of protected subjects.
articles.41: Article 41. If another law or regulation prescribes liability for conduct violating this Regulation, that provision applies; otherwise, this Regulation governs.
articles.42: Article 42. If a local government, competent department or its personnel commits any of the following, directly responsible officials and personnel shall be disciplined; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable: (1) failure to protect or supervise, leading to a historic city, district, town or village being placed under warning or stripped of its designation; (2) failure to prepare or lawfully amend the protection list or establish files for historic or traditional-character buildings; (3) failure to prepare or amend protection plans or building guidelines as required; (4) failure to publish the main content of an approved plan; (5) failure to follow the protection plan or statutory approval procedures; (6) failure to provide fire facilities, access routes or a fire-safety plan under applicable standards and procedures; (7) failure to protect listed place names; (8) failure to discharge responsible-entity duties, causing serious consequences; or (9) dereliction, abuse of authority or favoritism. If a town government or subdistrict office fails to conduct routine inspections or protection, the county-level government shall order correction; serious cases shall result in discipline, and criminal liability where applicable.
articles.43: Article 43. For prohibited activity within a protected area, the municipal or county-level protection authority or urban-management enforcement department shall order it to stop and require restoration or other remedial measures by a deadline; unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the violator fails to comply, a capable entity may be appointed to act at the violator's expense. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 500,000–1,000,000 for an organization or RMB 50,000–100,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.44: Article 44. A person falsely claiming the title of historic and cultural city, district, town, village, traditional village or historic area shall be ordered to correct the conduct by a deadline by the municipal or county-level protection authority or urban-management enforcement department. Failure to do so shall result in a fine of RMB 50,000–100,000.
articles.45: Article 45. If, without approval, a person demolishes or renovates a building, structure or facility other than a historic building in a protected core of a historic city, town, village or district, the county-level natural resources and planning and housing departments shall order the conduct to stop and require restoration or other remedies by a deadline. Unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the violator fails, the departments may appoint a capable entity to act at the violator's expense. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.46: Article 46. A person storing flammable, explosive or corrosive substances in a protected area of a historic or traditional-character building in a manner endangering safety shall be ordered to correct the conduct and fined RMB 2,000–20,000 by the county-level natural resources and planning or urban-management enforcement department. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.47: Article 47. A person damaging, relocating or demolishing a historic or traditional-character building without authorization shall be ordered to stop and restore it or take other remedial measures by a deadline. Unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the violator fails to comply, a capable entity may be appointed to act at the violator's expense. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 200,000–500,000 for an organization or RMB 100,000–200,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.48: Article 48. A person installing an advertisement, sign or poster that damages or impairs the character of a historic or traditional-character building shall be ordered to correct it or restore the prior condition by a deadline. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 5,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 1,000–5,000 for an individual.
articles.49: Article 49. Unauthorized installation, movement, obstruction, alteration or damage of a marker for a historic city, district, town, village, traditional village or historic area shall be corrected by a deadline; failure to do so carries a fine of RMB 10,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 1,000–10,000 for an individual. The same conduct concerning a marker for a historic or traditional-character building shall be corrected by a deadline; failure to do so carries a fine of RMB 2,000–20,000 for an organization or RMB 500–5,000 for an individual.
articles.50: Article 50. For purposes of this Regulation: (1) ‘historic urban area’ means an area with concentrated heritage in a historic city, generally within the built-up area, that reflects the city's development or character of a particular period; (2) ‘historic and cultural district’ means an area designated by the provincial government with abundant cultural relics and a concentration of historic buildings that substantially and authentically preserves traditional layout and character over a certain scale; (3) ‘historic town’ or ‘historic village’ means a town or village designated by the provincial government with abundant relics and major historic or commemorative value, substantially reflecting traditional character and local or ethnic features of one or more historical periods; (4) ‘traditional village’ means an early-formed village published by national or provincial housing authorities with rich, substantially intact traditional cultural resources and significant historic, cultural, scientific, artistic, social or economic value; (5) ‘historic area’ means an area designated by a county-level government that authentically reflects traditional character and ethnic or local features of a historical period; (6) ‘historic building’ means a building or structure designated by a municipal or county-level government for its protection value and reflection of historic character or local features, but not designated as a protected cultural relic or registered as an immovable cultural relic; and (7) ‘traditional-character building’ means a building or structure identified by a county-level natural resources and planning department, other than a protected cultural relic or historic building, whose history and character contribute to the overall character of a historic city, district or area.
articles.51: Article 51. This Regulation takes effect on 1 November 2024.

FBMCLI.10.6946695.title: Regulations of Zigong Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Zigong's circumstances and under applicable laws including the Urban and Rural Planning Law, Cultural Relics Protection Law, national historic-city protection regulations and Sichuan traditional-village rules, to protect and administer Zigong, carry forward its historical continuity, integrate heritage protection with urban and rural construction, and promote creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to planning, protection, use and supervision of Zigong as a historic and cultural city. Its protected subjects, centered on the history of well salt, include the historic urban area, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, cultural relics, paleontological fossil sites, historic buildings, industrial and rural production/life heritage, revolutionary resources, intangible heritage, place-name heritage, time-honored businesses, ancient and notable trees and others. Where laws or regulations provide otherwise, they apply.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall follow scientific planning, conservation priority, appropriate use, transmission and development; properly balance socioeconomic development and protection; establish categorized and tiered systems; preserve the authenticity and integrity of heritage; and maintain traditional layouts and historic character.
articles.4: Article 4. The municipal government shall protect and supervise the historic and cultural city, include protection in economic and social plans, improve institutions and policy safeguards, coordinate departments and regions, and advance World Heritage nominations and conservation and development. County-level governments shall protect heritage in their areas. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall conduct routine inspections and public outreach. Residents' and villagers' committees shall assist them.
articles.5: Article 5. The housing and urban-rural development authority shall administer protection and management. Development and reform, natural resources, culture, radio, television and tourism, education and sports, public security, industry and information technology, civil affairs, finance, agriculture and rural affairs, commerce, emergency management, urban management and enforcement, ethnic and religious affairs, and other departments shall perform related duties under law.
articles.6: Article 6. The municipal government shall establish a Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee to coordinate planning and protection. It shall establish an expert committee to provide review, assessment and advice on major matters. The municipal government shall prescribe the committee's procedures.
articles.7: Article 7. Municipal and county-level governments shall provide protection funds in their budgets in line with local socioeconomic development. They shall fully fund lawful measures to protect subjects at imminent risk of loss.
articles.8: Article 8. Municipal and county-level governments shall strengthen inspection of protection work, improve audit oversight of officials' performance of economic responsibilities related to protection, and report on protection to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level.
articles.9: Article 9. Everyone has a duty to protect the historic and cultural city and may comment on protection plans and their implementation and supervise or report damage. Municipal and county-level governments shall commend or reward outstanding contributions under applicable rules.
articles.10: Article 10. Zigong shall maintain a protection list. It shall include: (1) the Ziliujing-Daan historic urban area centered on Ziliujing Old Street, the Xiqin Guild Hall–Zhonghua Road area and Daan Old Street, and the Gongjing historic urban area centered on Gongjing Old Street and riverside street; (2) historic districts such as Gongjing Aiye Cross Street and Fushun Confucian Temple–West Lake; (3) historic towns such as Xianshi and Zhaohua; (4) traditional villages such as Sanduo Zhai and Lüxian; (5) historic buildings such as the former Republican-era government compound at Anquan Lane and Shanhou Bridge; (6) protected cultural relics such as Shenhai Well, the Rong County Giant Buddha grotto and Zhang Boqing Residence, and other immovable relics; (7) fossil sites such as the Dashanpu dinosaur fossils and Lianggaoshan Changshanling petrified wood; (8) industrial heritage such as Dongyuan Well and the former Daan Salt Works; (9) rural production and life heritage such as Gong fan-making and Fushun tofu pudding; (10) revolutionary resources such as the former homes of Jiang Jie and Wu Yuzhang; (11) intangible heritage such as Zigong deep-well salt extraction, the Lantern Festival and tie-dyeing; (12) place-name heritage such as Lubianjing, Daanzhai and Sanba Road; (13) time-honored brands such as Tianche spicy sauce and Taiyuanjing sun-dried vinegar; (14) ancient and notable trees, including specimens planted by Wu Yuzhang in Caijiayan and a Ming-dynasty podocarpus in Daan; and (15) other subjects prescribed by law.
articles.11: Article 11. The municipal housing and urban-rural development authority, together with relevant departments, shall prepare the protection list. It shall consult experts and interested parties, prepare a preliminary list under applicable identification standards, and publish it for at least 30 days. Afterward it shall submit the list, expert opinions and public comments to the Protection Committee for review and to the municipal government for approval and publication. The list shall be filed with the Standing Committee of the Municipal People's Congress and state each subject's name, location, history, value, protection level and protected area. Subjects approved and published by the State Council or provincial government shall be listed directly.
articles.12: Article 12. The municipal government shall periodically organize county-level heritage surveys. Relevant departments shall propose adding valuable discoveries to the list, and any organization or individual may submit an application or proposal to the municipal housing and urban-rural development authority. A subject damaged or lost due to force majeure, or whose protection level or category changes, shall be addressed by prompt list adjustment under Article 11.
articles.13: Article 13. A subject not yet listed but preliminarily found valuable by the municipal housing authority together with natural resources, culture and other departments shall be designated for provisional protection by the county-level government where it is located. That government shall take necessary measures and notify the responsible entity. Within 30 days it shall start the listing procedure. If the subject is not listed within six months after provisional designation, that decision expires automatically. No one may damage, relocate or demolish a provisionally protected subject without authorization. During the period, the local town government or subdistrict office shall inspect it. Governments shall compensate lawful losses caused by provisional protection.
articles.14: Article 14. The municipal housing authority and relevant departments shall maintain a unified information platform and public database of protection files for listed subjects, except for information that must remain confidential by law.
articles.15: Article 15. Protection plans shall be prepared under law for the historic city, districts, towns and villages, and traditional villages, concurrently with territorial spatial plans. The municipal government organizes the city plan, prepared by the municipal housing authority with natural-resources and culture departments. County-level governments organize district plans, prepared by their housing authority with relevant departments. County-level governments organize plans for historic towns and villages and traditional villages, with town governments and subdistrict offices doing the detailed work. Plans shall be completed within one year after designation and publication.
articles.16: Article 16. Protection plans shall coordinate with territorial spatial plans and incorporate spatial controls for the natural environment, traditional layouts and historic character. Special plans for transport, municipal services, landscaping, fire safety and underground development shall be coordinated with protection plans.
articles.17: Article 17. The city protection plan shall delineate the historic urban area and, where needed, an environmental-coordination zone. Plans for districts, towns, villages and traditional villages shall delineate protected areas, including core areas and construction-control zones, and incorporate them in heritage-protection boundaries. For a historic building within a historic district, its protected area is the building itself; outside a district, it includes the building and any necessary construction-control zone.
articles.18: Article 18. Protection plans shall be submitted for approval and filing as required by law. Before submission, the preparer shall publish the draft and solicit expert and public comments through meetings, hearings or other means for at least 30 days. After expert-committee review and Protection Committee examination, the plan shall be submitted for approval. Approved plans shall be published on government websites and in major news media.
articles.19: Article 19. An approved protection plan may not be amended without authorization. If amendment is necessary, the preparing authority shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and may prepare an amendment only after consent. The amendment shall follow the original approval procedure.
articles.20: Article 20. Municipal and county-level governments shall periodically organize departments and experts to inspect and assess implementation of protection plans and promptly correct or address identified problems.
articles.21: Article 21. Zigong shall apply a responsible-entity system. The municipal government is responsible for the historic urban area; the county-level government for historic districts, towns and villages and traditional villages; the owner for a historic building or industrial heritage, or, if the owner is missing or title unclear, the user, or, if neither is identifiable, the manager, or, if none is identifiable, the county-level government; the county-level place-name authority for place-name heritage; and for other subjects, the entity designated by law or, absent one, by the county-level government. Within 10 working days after publication of the list, the county housing authority shall notify the responsible entity for historic buildings and industrial heritage in writing. An objection may be filed with the county-level government within 30 days after notice; it shall decide within 30 days whether to adjust the designation and notify the applicant in writing.
articles.22: Article 22. Responsible entities for historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages and traditional villages shall: (1) preserve traditional layout, spatial scale, historic character and the integrity of related natural landscapes and environments; (2) improve infrastructure, public services and living conditions; (3) research and present historic and landscape value; (4) ensure fire safety, security, disaster prevention and mitigation; and (5) perform other legal duties.
articles.23: Article 23. A historic-building responsible entity shall: (1) maintain and repair the building and preserve its appearance, form and character; (2) ensure structural safety, keep fire and disaster facilities operational, detect hazards and address them promptly; (3) document the parties' protection duties in writing when transferring, leasing or lending the building; and (4) perform other legal duties.
articles.24: Article 24. An industrial-heritage responsible entity shall conduct routine protection, reinforcement, repair, safety measures and management, promptly repair damage to core items, monitor protection through a designated department or person, and perform other legal duties.
articles.25: Article 25. The responsible entity for place-name heritage shall survey significant place names reflecting Zigong's history, collect and record information, and supervise naming, renaming, use and cultural protection.
articles.26: Article 26. County-level governments shall install markers for historic districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, historic buildings, industrial heritage, revolutionary resources and ancient and notable trees in their areas. The municipal government shall set installation and maintenance standards. No one may install, move, remove, alter, obscure or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.27: Article 27. Construction in protected areas of historic districts, towns and villages shall follow the minimum-intervention principle and comply with detailed territorial spatial and protection plans. It may proceed only after review by the municipal or county housing authority together with natural resources, culture and other departments at the same level and after lawful approval. Major construction shall undergo expert review before approval.
articles.28: Article 28. New construction and expansion are prohibited in protected cores of historic districts, towns and villages except for necessary infrastructure and public-service facilities. Necessary works and character-restoration construction under applicable plans shall balance conservation and improved livelihoods, encourage traditional craftspeople and traditional methods and materials, and preserve traditional layouts, street patterns and historic character.
articles.29: Article 29. New construction and expansion in construction-control zones of historic districts, towns and villages shall comply with detailed territorial spatial and protection plans, strictly control building height, bulk and color, and remain compatible with the traditional layout and historic character of the protected core.
articles.30: Article 30. Construction in an environmental-coordination zone shall protect the natural landscape and cultural environment on which the historic city depends, preserve view corridors, and ensure new or renovated buildings are compatible in form, style and color with their surroundings.
articles.31: Article 31. Traditional villages shall be conserved as a whole, retaining their traditional layouts and historic character and the natural environment and landscape on which they depend. Reconstruction, alteration, repair, expansion and exterior decoration shall comply with village and protection plans and remain compatible with the village's overall architectural form, bulk, style, color, construction and decoration.
articles.32: Article 32. Historic buildings shall receive special, key or general protection according to historic, scientific and artistic value and condition. For special protection, the exterior form, finish materials and colors, interior main structure, floor plan and significant decoration may not be changed. For key protection, the exterior form, finish materials and colors and significant interior structure and decoration may not be changed. For general protection, the exterior form, color and significant finish components may not be changed. The municipal housing authority shall prescribe detailed categories and measures.
articles.33: Article 33. Construction sites shall, where possible, avoid historic buildings; if avoidance is impossible, in-situ preservation shall be used wherever possible. No one may damage, relocate or demolish a historic building without authorization. If public interest makes in-situ preservation impossible, expert and public views shall be solicited through meetings, hearings or other means.
