The municipal or county housing authority, together with natural resources and culture departments, shall review the matter; after municipal consent and required approvals, relocation or demolition shall follow applicable technical standards and management rules.
articles.34: Article 34. Historic buildings shall be repaired under protection plans and technical repair standards. Municipal and county-level housing authorities shall provide technical advice and services. Repair affecting exterior form or character, main structure, or mandatory provisions of a detailed territorial spatial or protection plan requires approval from the housing authority together with natural resources and culture departments, and shall follow the approved scope. If a building is at risk and its responsible entity cannot maintain or repair it, the county-level government shall take protective measures.
articles.35: Article 35. A non-state-owned historic-building responsible entity that repairs the building in accordance with applicable plans, technical standards and approved designs and work plans and passes inspection may receive a government subsidy. The municipal government shall prescribe subsidy measures.
articles.36: Article 36. In protected areas of the historic urban area, historic districts, towns, villages, traditional villages and historic buildings, it is prohibited to: (1) quarry, mine or conduct similar activities damaging traditional layout or character; (2) occupy green spaces, waterways, towers, bridges, pavilions, dikes, culverts, roads or other natural and historic features designated for preservation; (3) build structures for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; (4) carve or deface historic buildings; or (5) engage in other conduct likely to damage protected subjects.
articles.37: Article 37. Municipal and county-level governments shall guide and assist industrial-heritage protection and support applications for national or provincial recognition. Responsible entities shall protect industrial heritage and cooperate with surveys, assessments, identification and archiving. During conversion, restructuring, auction or asset exchange, they shall preserve its layout, structure, form and character and prevent damage to core items.
articles.38: Article 38. Place names of significant historic and cultural value reflecting Zigong's history generally may not be changed. If administrative-boundary changes, urban or rural construction, natural changes or other reasons make renaming necessary, the county-level government shall prepare protection measures in advance and follow statutory procedures.
articles.39: Article 39. If a listed subject is seriously damaged, the municipal housing authority and relevant departments shall ask the municipal government to order the county-level government where it is located to take remedial measures by a deadline and prevent further harm.
articles.40: Article 40. Municipal and county-level governments shall promote appropriate use by: (1) adopting positive or negative lists of uses; (2) optimizing land-use patterns and supporting compatible cultural tourism, creative industries, traditional crafts, local products and intangible-heritage transmission; (3) encouraging social and individual investment through policy guidance, grants and fee reductions; (4) promoting appropriate use of historic buildings through public acquisition, title exchange, rent reductions and longer leases; (5) supporting research, innovation, cultural outreach, education and school-based practical learning; (6) investing in specialists in planning, historic-building repair and traditional crafts; (7) using big data, the Internet of Things and other technology for presentation and management; and (8) adopting other conservation-oriented uses.
articles.41: Article 41. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and use by establishing museums, exhibition halls, science-education bases and intangible-heritage demonstration or practice venues; researching local culture and presenting traditional opera and folk arts; establishing creative-industry bases and developing products, brands, film, television and art; producing and selling Zigong specialties and souvenirs, operating cultural inns or themed hotels, and developing tourism themed around the Fuxi River, West Lake, the Giant Buddha and local food; creating public-interest organizations and volunteering; or undertaking other conservation-oriented activities.
articles.42: Article 42. Use of historic districts, towns, villages, traditional villages and historic buildings shall protect original residents' lawful interests and continue traditional customs. Original residents are encouraged to remain in their homes in accordance with protection plans and participate in conservation and development through property, capital or other contributions, with a reasonable share of returns.
articles.43: Article 43. Research and documentation of Zigong intangible heritage, including distinctive customs, traditional crafts, opera, acrobatics and dialect, are encouraged to build cultural brands. Governments shall support representative inheritors with necessary venues and funding and assist organizations and individuals appropriately using representative heritage projects. Inheritors shall discover, collect and organize valuable materials, train successors, transmit heritage and participate in public education.
articles.44: Article 44. Municipal and county-level governments shall plan development of red-culture brands, integrate revolutionary resources with other protected subjects into public cultural services, and build influential red-culture brands and tourism destinations. They shall establish patriotism and Party-education bases and conduct themed education and commemorations to carry forward patriotism and revolutionary traditions.
articles.45: Article 45. Governments shall appropriately use Zigong's distinctive cultural resources and support integration of heritage transmission with characteristic industries, including experiential, educational and leisure tourism based on well salt, lanterns, dinosaur geological heritage and salt-gang cuisine.
articles.46: Article 46. Where another law or regulation prescribes liability for a violation of this Regulation, that provision applies.
articles.47: Article 47. If a state organ or its personnel commits any of the following, the competent body shall order correction and issue a notice of criticism; directly responsible officials and personnel shall be dealt with under applicable rules, and criminal liability pursued where applicable: (1) inadequate protection causing a designated city, town, village or other subject to be listed as endangered; (2) failure to lawfully prepare, publish, manage or adjust the protection list; (3) failure to prepare, submit or publish protection plans as required; (4) unauthorized amendment of detailed territorial spatial or protection plans; (5) failure to install protection markers; (6) failure to perform responsible-entity duties; (7) failure to take provisional-protection measures; or (8) abuse of authority, dereliction or favoritism.
articles.48: Article 48. Unauthorized installation, movement, removal, alteration, obstruction or damage of a historic-building or industrial-heritage marker, contrary to Article 26(2), shall be corrected and the prior condition restored by a deadline by the housing or industry and information technology authority. A fine of RMB 200–1,000 may also be imposed.
articles.49: Article 49. For new construction or expansion in a protected core contrary to Article 28(1), or construction in a construction-control zone violating height, bulk or color controls under Article 29, the natural-resources authority shall order work to stop. If corrective measures can eliminate the planning impact, it shall order correction by a deadline and impose a fine of 5%–10% of construction cost. If the impact cannot be corrected, it shall order demolition by a deadline; if demolition is impossible, the structure or unlawful income shall be confiscated, and a fine of up to 10% of construction cost may also be imposed.
articles.50: Article 50. If a person damages, relocates or demolishes a historic building contrary to Article 33(1), the housing authority shall order the conduct to stop and require restoration or other remedial measures by a deadline; unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the person fails, the authority may appoint a capable entity to act at the violator's expense. For serious consequences, the fine is RMB 200,000–500,000 for an organization or RMB 100,000–200,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.51: Article 51. If a historic-building responsible entity repairs without approval or contrary to approved plans, in violation of Article 34(3), the housing authority shall order work to stop and restoration or other remedial measures by a deadline; unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the entity fails, the authority may appoint a capable entity to act at its expense. For serious consequences, the fine is RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.52: Article 52. Administrative penalties under this Regulation assigned to comprehensive urban-management enforcement shall be imposed by the municipal or county-level urban-management authority.
articles.53: Article 53. For purposes of this Regulation: (1) a ‘historic and cultural district’ is an area designated by a provincial government or national ministry with abundant relics and a concentrated group of historic buildings that substantially and authentically preserves traditional layout and character; (2) a ‘historic town’ or ‘historic village’ is a town or village designated by a provincial government or national ministry with abundant relics, major historic or commemorative value, and an intact reflection of traditional layout, character and local or ethnic features; (3) a ‘traditional village’ is a long-established settlement designated by a provincial government or national ministry, with tangible and intangible heritage, substantial historic, cultural, scientific, artistic, social or economic value, and an intact traditional or ethnic or regional character, and listed as such; it includes natural and administrative villages; (4) a ‘historic building’ is a building or structure designated by a municipal or county government for protection value and its reflection of historic character or local features, but not designated or registered as an immovable cultural relic; (5) ‘industrial heritage’ means industrial remains recognized and published by a competent national, provincial or municipal industry authority for significant historic, technological, social or artistic value formed through long-term industrial development; and (6) ‘rural production and life heritage’ means traditional production techniques and related products recognized by the provincial agriculture authority for historic continuity or ethnic or regional character, close connection with everyday life and principal reliance on manual labor.
articles.54: Article 54. This Regulation takes effect on 1 October 2023.

FBMCLI.10.7706125.title: Regulations of Haikou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2024 Amendment)

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Haikou's circumstances and under the Urban and Rural Planning Law, Cultural Relics Protection Law, national historic-city protection regulations and other laws, to protect Haikou's historic and cultural city and carry forward its outstanding culture.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to protection, management and use of historic districts, historic buildings, immovable cultural relics and intangible cultural heritage in Haikou's administrative area. Other subjects, including ancient and notable trees, geoparks, nature reserves and movable cultural relics, are governed by applicable laws and regulations.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall be based on scientific planning, categorized management, strict conservation and appropriate use; preserve heritage authenticity and integrity; and properly balance transmission, protection and use of heritage with coordinated urban and rural construction and socioeconomic development.
articles.4: Article 4. Municipal and district governments shall protect, manage and use the historic and cultural city in their areas. The municipal government shall establish a protection and management committee to coordinate and guide protection. The municipal housing and urban-rural development and tourism and culture authorities shall administer protection and supervision; the natural resources and planning authority shall administer protection planning. Development and reform, finance, public security, commerce, education, comprehensive law enforcement, fire and rescue and other bodies shall assist according to their duties.
articles.5: Article 5. Municipal and district governments shall include protection and management in economic and social development plans, budget protection funding and increase public investment. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate through donations, grants, technical services and proposals. Investors are encouraged to undertake lawful conservation-oriented use of heritage resources and develop tourism and related industries.
articles.6: Article 6. Municipal and district governments shall periodically inspect or assess protection and report to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level. Those standing committees shall strengthen oversight.
articles.7: Article 7. Governments at all levels shall conduct public education and raise awareness of protection. 13 March each year is Haikou Historic and Cultural City Protection Awareness Day.
articles.8: Article 8. Heritage protection is a responsibility shared by society. Any organization or individual may discourage or report damaging conduct. Municipal and district governments shall commend or reward outstanding contributions.
articles.9: Article 9. The municipal government shall organize preparation of the Haikou Historic and Cultural City Protection Plan, submit it to the provincial government for approval, promptly publish it and incorporate it into Haikou's overall territorial spatial plan. It shall file the plan with the national housing and urban-rural development and cultural-relics authorities.
articles.10: Article 10. The protection plan shall state: (1) principles, subjects and areas of protection; (2) measures, development intensity and construction controls; (3) requirements for traditional layout and historic character; (4) core protected areas and construction-control zones of historic districts; and (5) phased implementation arrangements.
articles.11: Article 11. Protection shall preserve traditional layout, historic character and spatial scale, as well as the natural landscape and environment on which the heritage depends.
articles.12: Article 12. The municipal natural resources and planning authority, together with the housing and urban-rural development and tourism and culture authorities, shall prepare special protection plans for historic districts based on the protection plan, and submit them for municipal approval and publication.
articles.13: Article 13. Natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, tourism and culture, comprehensive law-enforcement and other departments shall strictly implement the plans, review and supervise related construction projects, and investigate unlawful construction.
articles.14: Article 14. Buildings and facilities inconsistent with the protection plan or a historic-district special plan shall be corrected or removed as required by the plan and law by the natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, comprehensive law-enforcement and other departments together with the local government or property owner.
articles.15: Article 15. No one may amend an approved protection plan or historic-district special plan without authorization. If an amendment is necessary, the preparing authority shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and may prepare a revised plan only after consent. It shall broadly solicit public comments and obtain expert review. The revised plan shall be submitted and published through the original approval procedure.
articles.16: Article 16. The provincial government has designated the Haikou Arcade Historic District and Fucheng Traditional Architecture Historic District. The Haikou Arcade district lies south of Changdi Road, east of Longhua Road, west of Heping Road and north of Jiefang West Road and Wenming Middle Road, including mainly Deshengsha, Bo'ai, Zhongshan, Xinhua and Changdi streets. Fucheng is organized around Wen Zhuang and Zhongjie roads east–west and Zhongshan Road north–south, including Beisheng Street, Xiuyifang, Ma'an Street, Dashi Lane, Gulou Street, Zhongjie Road and Fudi Lane.
articles.17: Article 17. A historic district's protected area comprises a core protected area and construction-control zone. The municipal natural resources and planning authority together with housing and tourism and culture authorities shall delineate them in the protection plan and special plan. The municipal government shall place markers at principal entrances to the core. No one may install, move, alter or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.18: Article 18. Construction in a historic district's core shall comply with protection plans, preserve the natural setting and historic character, and protect immovable relics, historic buildings, street patterns and distinctive paving. New buildings and structures in a construction-control zone shall meet the plan's controls.
articles.19: Article 19. Building heights along distinctive lanes in the core shall be strictly controlled. Lawful new construction, expansion or renovation shall not exceed 15 meters overall and shall retain a varied building pattern on both sides of the lane. In the construction-control zone, overall height shall not exceed 20 meters. All heights shall also comply with the plans. The ancient city wall, traditional residential architecture, street pattern, historic place names and traditional market atmosphere of Fucheng shall be protected and, where appropriate, restored.
articles.20: Article 20. The following are prohibited in a historic district's protected area: (1) quarrying, mining or similar conduct that damages traditional layout or historic character; (2) occupying green space, rivers, lakes or roads designated for preservation; (3) building factories or warehouses for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; (4) unlawful demolition or construction; (5) changing land uses prescribed by the protection plan; (6) construction exceeding height or floor-area-ratio limits or violating controls on bulk or color; and (7) other conduct prohibited by law.
articles.21: Article 21. The following activities in a historic district's protected area shall preserve traditional layout, historic character and historic buildings; require a protection plan; and comply with applicable law: (1) changing the natural state of green areas, rivers or lakes; (2) filming or holding large public exhibitions, performances or recreational events in the core; and (3) other activities affecting layout, character or historic buildings.
articles.22: Article 22. A legally owned building in a protected area certified as dangerous may be repaired or renovated under the Urban and Rural Planning Law and other applicable law, while preserving its traditional layout and historic character. The municipal government shall separately prescribe procedures for such work. Governments shall coordinate cultural resources and encourage owners in protected areas to improve living conditions voluntarily through exchanges or similar arrangements.
articles.23: Article 23. Municipal and district governments shall prioritize infrastructure and public services in historic districts in accordance with the plans and improve living conditions. Fire facilities and access routes in the core shall comply with technical standards. If conservation needs prevent compliance, the municipal fire and rescue agency together with the housing authority shall prepare a fire-safety assurance plan.
articles.24: Article 24. Municipal and district governments shall adopt support policies, optimize business uses, encourage distinctive local activities and the concentration of time-honored brands in historic districts, and integrate district protection with culture and tourism.
articles.25: Article 25. A modern building, traditional residence, shop or structure with historic, artistic or scientific value may be designated as a historic building after investigation by the municipal housing authority and tourism and culture authority, consultation with relevant parties, expert review and municipal approval. It shall be published, marked and entered in a protection file.
articles.26: Article 26. The municipal government shall establish and publish a categorized historic-building protection list and standards. For Class I buildings, the original facade, finish material, color, structural system, floor plan and distinctive interior decoration may not be changed. For Class II buildings, the original facade, finish, color and principal floor plan may not be changed. For Class III buildings, the original facade, finish and color may not be changed.
articles.27: Article 27. The municipal government shall dynamically manage and publish updates to the list. If a listed historic building is lost or damaged by force majeure, has lost its protection value, or its category changes, the municipal housing authority and tourism and culture authority shall propose an adjustment after consultation and expert review and submit it for municipal approval. A building designated as a protected cultural relic or registered as an immovable cultural relic shall be removed from the historic-building list from the date of that designation.
articles.28: Article 28. The owner is responsible for protecting a historic building. If the owner is missing, cannot be contacted or title is unclear, the user or manager is responsible; if none is identifiable, the district government shall designate an entity. The responsible entity shall maintain and repair the building under the protection plan and repair standards, which the municipal housing and tourism and culture authorities shall formulate. If the building is at risk and the responsible entity cannot maintain or repair it, governments shall take protective measures. Governments shall encourage owners to sell or donate historic buildings to the State.
articles.29: Article 29. No organization or individual may: (1) damage, relocate or demolish a historic building without authorization; (2) install equipment inside a historic building or its ancillary facilities that shortens its service life; (3) build facilities there for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; (4) carve, post on or deface it; or (5) otherwise endanger it or impair its character.
articles.30: Article 30. Construction sites shall, where possible, avoid historic buildings; if avoidance is impossible, in-situ preservation shall be used wherever possible. The developer shall formulate protection measures and obtain approval from the municipal housing and tourism and culture authorities. If public-interest construction makes in-situ preservation impossible and relocation or demolition necessary, approval shall be obtained from the provincial protection authority and tourism and culture authority under applicable procedures. The developer shall include preservation, relocation or demolition costs in the project budget.
articles.31: Article 31. Exterior repair or decoration, installation of facilities, or changes to the structure or use of a historic building require approval by the municipal housing and tourism and culture authorities and completion of other required procedures.
articles.32: Article 32. For sites of particularly significant political, economic or cultural events, including long-term former sites of important foreign institutions in Haikou, the municipal government shall install commemorative markers and create conditions for restoration. No one may damage such markers.
articles.33: Article 33. Appropriate use of historic buildings is encouraged. Subject to protection requirements, they may house museums, exhibition halls and intangible-heritage venues, or host cultural and creative work, cultural experiences and research, and related exhibitions, to present and transmit history and culture.
articles.34: Article 34. For immovable cultural relics designated at any level, the government with authority under law shall delineate a protected area, install markers, establish records and assign a dedicated institution or person to manage them.
articles.35: Article 35. Key cultural relics reflecting Haikou's character, including the Hai Rui Tomb, former residence and tomb of Qiu Jun, Five Officials Temple, former site of the First Congress of the Qiongya Communist Party and Xiuying Fort, shall be specially protected and appropriately used. The tourism and culture authority shall develop specific measures for each relic, report them to the government at the same level and publish them for implementation.
articles.36: Article 36. Use of an immovable cultural relic shall follow the principles of preserving its original condition and minimum intervention, protect the relic and its associated objects, and not damage, alter, add to or demolish it.
articles.37: Article 37. A citizen or non-cultural-relic entity using a state-owned protected cultural relic or representative memorial building shall sign a protection-and-use responsibility agreement with the tourism and culture authority, manage, maintain and repair it, and accept inspection, supervision and guidance.
articles.38: Article 38. Owners, managers and users of immovable cultural relics shall control fire and electrical hazards and provide necessary firefighting equipment. Automatic alarms, fire suppression, lightning protection, waterproofing and similar facilities shall be installed in key areas as needed, without damaging the relic. If a major hazard threatens safety, they shall promptly mitigate it and report to the tourism and culture authority.
articles.39: Article 39. A cultural-relic site open to visitors shall adopt effective measures to preserve its integrity and safety. Visitors shall comply with cultural-relic laws, regulations and site rules, care for the relic and facilities, and not carve, deface or damage them.
articles.40: Article 40. Intangible-cultural-heritage protection shall prioritize conservation and rescue, promote appropriate use and transmission, and preserve authenticity and integrity.
articles.41: Article 41. Municipal and district governments shall establish lists of representative intangible-heritage projects. The tourism and culture authority shall organize expert review and public notice of municipal and district projects and submit them for approval and publication. National and provincial applications and designations shall follow applicable rules.
articles.42: Article 42. The tourism and culture authority shall survey, collect, organize, archive and research intangible heritage as appropriate, including Hainan coconut carving and Longtang sculpture; Qiong opera and Hainan puppet and vegetarian operas; Hainan bayin music; Hainan rosewood furniture-making, traditional sugar-making and Hainan rice-noodle preparation; Qilin, lion, tiger and Haikou dragon dances; Madam Xian worship and the Fucheng Lantern Festival flower exchange; folk tales, songs and other intangible heritage.
articles.43: Article 43. Municipal and district governments shall delineate and mark protected areas for cultural spaces supporting representative intangible-heritage projects and protect them as a whole. They shall protect related buildings, sites and remains in planning and construction. No one may occupy or damage project materials, physical objects or related buildings, sites or remains.
articles.44: Article 44. Under national and provincial rules, the tourism and culture authority shall designate and publish representative inheritors and groups, comprehensively document their knowledge and skills, and support them through venues and grants, public-interest activities, professional-title applications and talent recognition.
articles.45: Article 45. Representative inheritors and groups shall conduct transmission activities and train successors; preserve relevant objects and records; assist heritage surveys; participate in public education; and meet other national and provincial duties.
articles.46: Article 46. Tourism, culture and commerce authorities shall adopt policies encouraging social actors to research and organize traditional folk arts and crafts, establish specialist private museums and exhibition halls, hold exhibitions and performances, and donate intangible-heritage objects.
articles.47: Article 47. Tourism, culture and education authorities shall support schools and research institutions in training specialists and established artists in teaching successors. Festivals, exhibitions, training, education and mass media are encouraged to disseminate local intangible-heritage knowledge and support transmission and public sharing.
articles.48: Article 48. Artistic creation, product development and tourism using local intangible heritage shall respect its authentic form and cultural meaning and avoid distortion or misuse.
articles.49: Article 49. If a state organ or its personnel responsible for protecting Haikou's historic city commits any of the following, directly responsible personnel shall be disciplined; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable: (1) failure to lawfully prepare or amend the protection or district plans; (2) failure to establish or update a historic-building list; (3) unlawful adjustment of a historic district's protected area; or (4) other failure to perform supervisory duties lawfully.
articles.50: Article 50. Construction in a protected area without a construction-planning permit or contrary to its terms shall be stopped by comprehensive law enforcement. If corrective measures can remove the planning impact, the violator shall correct it by a deadline and be fined 5%–10% of construction cost. If the impact cannot be corrected, demolition shall be ordered; if demolition is impossible, the structure or unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated, and a fine of up to 10% of construction cost may also be imposed.
articles.51: Article 51. A person damaging, relocating or demolishing a historic building without authorization, contrary to Article 29(1), shall be ordered to stop and restore it or take other remedial measures by a deadline; unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the violator fails, comprehensive law enforcement may appoint a capable entity to act at the violator's expense. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 200,000–500,000 for an organization or RMB 100,000–200,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.52: Article 52. If activities in a protected area—including altering natural features, filming or holding large events in the core, or other activities—destructively affect traditional layout, historic character or historic buildings, comprehensive law enforcement shall order cessation and restoration or other remedies by a deadline; unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the violator fails, a capable entity may be appointed at its expense. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.53: Article 53. For equipment installed in a historic building that shortens its service life, contrary to Article 29(2), comprehensive law enforcement shall order removal by a deadline; failure results in a fine of RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 20,000–50,000 for an individual. For unauthorized exterior repairs, facility installation, or structural or use changes contrary to Article 31, it shall order cessation and restoration or other remedies; unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the violator fails, a capable entity may act at its expense. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.54: Article 54. Building a factory, warehouse or similar facility for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances inside a historic building or its ancillary facilities, contrary to Article 29(3), shall be stopped and the prior condition restored or other remedies taken by a deadline. Unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. If the violator fails, a capable entity may act at its expense. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 500,000–1,000,000 for an organization or RMB 50,000–100,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.55: Article 55. Damage or loss of an immovable cultural relic in violation of Article 36 entails legal liability and criminal liability where applicable. Unauthorized relocation or demolition of an immovable relic that is not a crime shall be penalized by comprehensive law enforcement.
articles.56: Article 56. Unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or damage of a marker for a historic district, historic building or intangible-heritage site shall be corrected by a deadline. Failure shall result in a fine of RMB 10,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 2,000–10,000 for an individual.
articles.57: Article 57. A person carving or defacing a historic building shall restore it or take other remedial measures and shall be fined RMB 50.
articles.58: Article 58. Where this Regulation does not prescribe a penalty but another law or regulation does, that provision applies.
articles.59: Article 59. The municipal government is responsible for interpreting specific implementation issues under this Regulation.
articles.60: Article 60. The municipal government may adopt implementing rules under this Regulation.
articles.61: Article 61. This Regulation takes effect on 1 September 2010.

FBMCLI.10.6853863.title: Regulations of Hangzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Hangzhou's circumstances and under the Cultural Relics Protection Law, the State Council regulations on historic and cultural cities, towns and villages, and Zhejiang provincial rules, to protect Hangzhou's historic and cultural city, carry forward its heritage, continue its historical continuity and strengthen its cultural capacity.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to historic-city protection and related activities within Hangzhou's administrative area.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall be based on scientific planning, strict conservation, transmission and development, and appropriate use.
articles.4: Article 4. Municipal and district/county-level governments shall protect and supervise heritage in their areas, include it in economic and social development plans and budget for it. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall manage routine local protection, establish coordination mechanisms and conduct inspections, maintenance, outreach and supervision. Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist them.
articles.5: Article 5. Municipal and district/county-level governments shall establish protection committees to study major matters, including protection lists and plans, organize special assessments, and coordinate and supervise implementation. Members shall include government and department officials, experts and public representatives.
articles.6: Article 6. The municipal historic-city protection authority designated by the municipal government shall supervise protection citywide; district/county-level construction authorities shall supervise it in their areas. Together they are the protection authorities. Development and reform, education, ethnic and religious affairs, public security, civil affairs, finance, planning and natural resources, ecology and environment, construction, housing and property, cultural relics, forestry, water, agriculture and rural affairs, culture and tourism, market regulation, urban management, transport, fire and rescue and other bodies shall assist according to their duties.
articles.7: Article 7. Protection authorities and relevant departments shall use digital and other new technologies to collect and analyze information, efficiently consolidate and share data, and facilitate public access to heritage information.
articles.8: Article 8. Governments and departments shall conduct public education and promote transmission and presentation of outstanding traditional culture. Where appropriate, they may commission qualified enterprises, public institutions or other organizations to conduct research, consultation, outreach or training related to protection.
articles.9: Article 9. Protecting the historic and cultural city is a shared social responsibility. Volunteer groups, public-interest organizations and others are encouraged to participate lawfully through technical services, donations, grants, investment and other means. Anyone may discourage or report damage to protected subjects; protection authorities shall promptly handle reports and provide feedback.
articles.10: Article 10. Protected subjects include: (1) the West Lake Cultural Landscape, the Hangzhou section of the Grand Canal, the Liangzhu Ancient City Ruins and other World Heritage sites; (2) historic urban areas that served as capitals, prefectural seats or county seats in different periods; (3) historic towns; (4) historic villages; (5) historic districts; (6) historic character areas; (7) historic buildings; (8) traditional-character buildings; and (9) other protected subjects. Cultural relics, scenic areas, ancient and notable trees and intangible heritage associated with these subjects, including World Heritage sites, are governed by applicable laws and regulations.
articles.11: Article 11. Applications, approvals and direct designation of historic cities, towns and villages shall follow the national and Zhejiang provincial regulations. Applications and approvals for historic districts shall follow provincial regulations. Before applying for national or provincial designation of a historic city, district, town or village, a county-level government shall consult the municipal protection authority.
articles.12: Article 12. An area not designated as a historic district, town or village may be designated as a historic character area if it contains a substantial concentration of valuable buildings, retains substantially intact historic character and traditional layout, and meets one of these criteria: (1) it played an important role in the formation or development of a town or village; (2) it is closely associated with an important historical figure or event; (3) it has distinctive traditional cultural, regional or period characteristics; or (4) it preserves rich intangible heritage.
articles.13: Article 13. A building or structure not designated as a protected cultural relic or relic site may be designated as a historic building if it: (1) has historic, scientific or artistic value in its style, structure, materials, workmanship or engineering; (2) reflects Hangzhou's history, culture or customs and a distinctive period or regional character; (3) is a representative workshop, shop, factory or warehouse in the history of industry; (4) is a representative building connected with the history of the Communist Party of China, the People's Republic, socialist development or reform and opening-up, or with a historic event, revolutionary movement or notable person; or (5) otherwise has historic or cultural value.
articles.14: Article 14. A building or structure within a protected area of a historic district, town, village or character area, but not designated as a protected cultural relic, relic site or historic building, may be designated as a traditional-character building if it reflects a particular stage of urban development and collective memory, or contributes to the overall character of such a protected area. The protection authority shall survey and review candidates, seek comments from planning and natural resources authorities, the local town government or subdistrict office, and interested parties, and include them in the relevant protection plan under law.
articles.15: Article 15. The municipal protection authority, together with planning and natural resources and construction departments, shall periodically survey heritage citywide. District/county-level authorities shall do so in their areas with cultural-relics, planning and natural resources departments and town governments or subdistrict offices. If a new project requires demolition of existing buildings, the planning authority shall consult the protection authority during site-selection review or preparation of project conditions. Where needed, the relevant authorities shall conduct a heritage survey. Before an urban or village renewal project alters or demolishes a building at least 50 years old, the implementing entity shall conduct a necessary survey and report the results to the local protection authority.
articles.16: Article 16. To establish or amend the city's list of historic character areas and buildings, the municipal protection authority and planning department shall propose a list, consult the district government, interested parties, experts and the public, obtain municipal Protection Committee review, and submit it to the municipal government for approval and publication. A county-level authority shall follow the same process with relevant departments and local entities and submit the list to its government for approval. An approved list may not be altered or revoked without authorization. A historic building designated as a protected cultural relic or relic site is removed from the historic-building list on the date of designation.
articles.17: Article 17. If inadequate protection seriously impairs the value of a published historic character area or building, the municipal or county-level protection authority, after Protection Committee review, may ask its government to publish it on an endangered list and require the local district government, town government or subdistrict office to correct the problem and take remedial measures by a deadline. Afterward, if standards are met, it may be removed from the endangered list. If standards are not met and protection value is lost, it may be removed from the protection list after committee review.
articles.18: Article 18. Plans for historic cities, districts, towns, villages and character areas shall preserve heritage authenticity and integrity, traditional layout, historic character and spatial scale; protect associated cultural and natural landscapes and their setting; and manage building height and form, view corridors and other relevant features. Before planning a super-tall building, its potential adverse effects on the landscape of World Heritage and other protected subjects shall be assessed as required.
articles.19: Article 19. The municipal government shall prepare Hangzhou's historic-city plan and submit it to the provincial government. Municipal and county-level governments shall prepare historic-district plans for provincial approval. District/county-level governments shall prepare plans for historic towns and villages in their areas; after review by municipal planning, natural resources and protection departments, they shall be submitted for provincial approval. Plans for cities, districts, towns and villages shall be reviewed by the relevant Protection Committee and submitted under provincial rules.
articles.20: Article 20. Within one year after publication of a historic character-area list, the municipal or county-level planning and natural resources authority, together with the protection authority, shall prepare its plan and submit it for approval and publication. Before approval, the draft shall be published for at least 30 days and comments sought from departments, experts and the public. Before approving a county-level plan, the county government shall consult the municipal protection, planning and construction departments.
articles.21: Article 21. The municipal protection authority together with planning and natural resources, or the county-level protection authority together with cultural relics and planning departments, shall prepare historic-building protection drawings and submit them for government approval and publication. District/county-level authorities shall prepare use and protection guidance stating each building's protection category, key features, protection requirements and appropriate-use conditions.
articles.22: Article 22. Protected cores and construction-control zones for historic districts, towns, villages, character areas and historic buildings shall be delineated and submitted for approval: (1) the core of a district, town, village or character area shall include areas retaining traditional layout and historic character and concentrated immovable relics and historic or traditional-character buildings; a construction-control zone shall be delineated outside it; (2) a historic-building core shall include the building and necessary safety distance, with a construction-control zone around it; and (3) boundaries shall be clear and readily administered.
articles.23: Article 23. Plans and protection drawings shall specify mandatory content: (1) Hangzhou's city plan shall identify protected areas and subjects, traditional patterns such as ‘mountains on three sides and the city on one,’ the natural environment and key controls; protected areas shall include the historic urban area and other areas needing protection or control; (2) plans for districts, towns, villages and character areas shall identify protected areas, immovable relics, historic and traditional-character buildings, traditional layout, landscape character and controls on height, bulk, style and color; and (3) historic-building drawings shall identify the protected area and key controls.
articles.24: Article 24. Detailed territorial spatial plans shall coordinate with protection plans for historic cities, districts, towns, villages and character areas and comply with protection requirements for historic and traditional-character buildings. Where appropriate, a historic-village plan may be combined with the village plan, and a historic-district or character-area plan with a detailed plan.
articles.25: Article 25. Before area-wide repair, improvement or rehabilitation of a historic district, town, village or character area, the local government shall prepare an implementation plan consistent with the protection plan, specify tasks, responsible implementers and measures, and ensure implementation. It shall consult municipal protection, planning, natural resources and construction departments, revise the plan in light of their comments and file it with the municipal government. Works shall comply with the implementation plan.
articles.26: Article 26. Governments where the following historic urban areas are located shall protect their overall layout, character, city-site remains and natural setting and reasonably control development scale, building height, bulk, color and style: (1) the Western Capital of Wuyue and Yijin City; (2) the Lin'an capital of the Southern Song; (3) Hangzhou Prefectural City; (4) the Prefectural City of Yanzhou; (5) Yuhang County seat; (6) Xiaoshan County seat; (7) Xindeng County seat; and (8) other historic capitals, prefectural seats and county seats.
articles.27: Article 27. In a core protected area of a historic district, town, village or character area, new construction and expansion are prohibited except for necessary infrastructure and public-service facilities. Such facilities in a character-area core shall comply with the plan; before issuing a site-selection opinion or planning conditions, the planning authority shall consult protection and, where applicable, cultural-relics departments. Repair, improvement or rehabilitation in a character-area core shall comply with the plan, and the implementing entity shall file design drawings with the local protection authority. New buildings and structures in construction-control zones shall comply with the plan and remain compatible with the core's traditional layout and character in height, bulk, color and style.
articles.28: Article 28. Municipal and district/county-level governments shall designate and publish responsible management entities: (1) the town government or subdistrict office for a historic district, village or character area; (2) the town government for a historic town; and (3) a protection-management organization established or designated by a government for the relevant protected place. The responsible entity shall conduct daily protection and management under the plan and implementation program, preserve traditional layout, historic character and spatial scale, and ensure building safety.
articles.29: Article 29. The owner is responsible for protecting a historic building. For a state-owned building, the user may be designated by agreement. If the owner of a non-state-owned building is unknown, the local government shall designate a responsible entity. It shall ensure safe use and routine maintenance and repair at its own expense and may obtain information and technical guidance from protection, cultural-relics, planning and natural resources departments. If the building is at risk and the entity lacks capacity to repair it, the government shall take protective measures.
articles.30: Article 30. Historic character areas, historic buildings and traditional-character buildings shall have protection markers of a standard design set by the municipal government and installed by the local district/county-level government. No one may install, move, alter or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.31: Article 31. Historic buildings shall receive categorized protection based on cultural, scientific and artistic value, age and condition. For highly valuable and representative buildings, exterior character, principal floor plan, distinctive structure and components may not be altered. For buildings of significant value and some representative character, exterior character, distinctive structures and components may not be altered. For buildings with a degree of value, principal exterior character and distinctive components may not be altered. Except for conservation needs, no new building or structure may be built in a historic-building core. Construction in such a core for conservation purposes or in a construction-control zone shall comply with protection drawings and use guidance and obtain approvals required by law.
articles.32: Article 32. A person repairing, maintaining or improving a historic building shall prepare an implementation plan under its protection drawings and use guidance and complete procedures required by law. Exterior repairs or decoration, added facilities or structural changes require approval. Other repair and maintenance plans shall be filed with the local protection authority. In the municipal area, the district protection authority shall review plans for exterior work, facilities or structural changes before municipal departments approve them. Traditional craftspeople and techniques are encouraged.
articles.33: Article 33. If public-interest construction cannot preserve a historic building in situ and requires relocation or demolition, the developer shall provide a reasoned necessity and feasibility report, relocation plan and related materials. After review by the county-level Protection Committee and public notice, approval shall be sought under national and provincial rules.
articles.34: Article 34. The responsible management entity shall inspect, maintain and supervise traditional-character buildings in a historic district, town, village or character area. No one may damage their principal exterior character or distinctive components. Reconstruction, alteration or demolition for public-interest construction shall comply with the relevant protection plan.
articles.35: Article 35. If, after review, the protection authority finds that a building or structure recommended or discovered through planning, a special survey, public recommendation, urban construction or other means has protection value, it shall issue a provisional-protection notice to the local town government or subdistrict office. That entity shall promptly install a provisional marker and conduct routine inspections. Within four months, the protection authority shall propose listing and submit it for approval under Article 16. The municipal or county-level government shall decide within two months. If it declines to list, the notice expires automatically; the county-level government shall file its decision with the municipal authority. No one may damage a provisionally protected subject.
articles.36: Article 36. If construction reveals a building or structure of potential protection value, the contractor shall immediately stop demolition or construction, take temporary protective measures and notify the developer. The developer shall promptly report to the local protection authority. Within 10 working days after the report, the authority shall arrange an assessment. If no historic or cultural value is found, it shall notify the parties to resume construction. Departments shall provide necessary assistance where the developer and contractor promptly take and report effective safeguards.
articles.37: Article 37. District/county-level governments shall use modern technology and methods to strengthen disaster prevention, mitigation and response and protect and manage the safety of historic and traditional-character buildings. Dangerous buildings shall be included in emergency plans and urban and rural dangerous-building programs and addressed under law.
articles.38: Article 38. Information about rewards or penalties related to historic-city protection shall be included in the relevant organization's or individual's social-credit file under applicable credit-management rules.
articles.39: Article 39. Municipal and district/county-level governments shall periodically conduct special protection assessments and report results to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level. County-level results shall also be submitted to the municipal government. During assessment or supervision, the municipal government may summon an underperforming county-level government and its principal official to require rectification. County-level governments may establish a similar mechanism and require responsible entities to implement protection measures.
articles.40: Article 40. Governments shall use urban-renewal, rural-revitalization and other policies to improve roads and transport, waterways, ecological conditions, infrastructure, public services and overall character in historic districts, towns, villages and character areas.
articles.41: Article 41. County-level protection authorities, together with planning and natural resources, cultural-relics, fire and rescue bodies, shall prepare fire-safety assurance plans for character-area cores. New or expanded infrastructure and landscaping in protected areas shall meet national and provincial standards. If conservation needs make this impossible, the protection authority and relevant departments shall prepare an assurance plan specifying layout and measures. Where reconstruction in protected areas cannot meet construction standards because it must retain or restore historic layout and character, planning permission may be issued if the original footprint, height and floor area are not exceeded and sunlight to neighboring residences is not reduced.
articles.42: Article 42. Governments may appropriately use state-owned historic and traditional-character buildings through leases or operation by market entities, provided protection requirements are met and heritage value is not harmed. For public interest, governments may expropriate or exchange title to acquire non-state-owned buildings.
articles.43: Article 43. County-level governments shall coordinate construction-land quotas and prioritize rural housing needed to implement protection plans for historic towns and villages and character areas. If an owner of a historic or traditional-character building on a rural homestead voluntarily and lawfully exits the homestead for compensation, or agrees to another homestead, the rural collective may contract with the owner to acquire the building and land while safeguarding housing conditions. Collectives and members may use investment, leases or other lawful means to revitalize the buildings, consistent with conservation requirements and heritage value.
articles.44: Article 44. Governments and departments shall collect, organize, study, present and disseminate distinctive cultural resources; protect and transmit customs, folk arts and traditional crafts; explain related history, cultural value and meaning; integrate heritage and tourism; and use heritage for public education.
articles.45: Article 45. If another law, administrative regulation or Zhejiang local regulation prescribes liability for a violation of this Regulation, that provision applies.
articles.46: Article 46. If a municipal department, district/county-level government or department, town government or subdistrict office: (1) fails to prepare a character-area plan as required; (2) inadequate protection causes a listed character area or historic building to be placed on an endangered list; (3) fails to complete or adequately complete required rectification; (4) fails to install provisional markers or conduct routine inspections; or (5) unlawfully grants administrative permission, the government at the relevant level shall order correction and issue a notice of criticism. The competent authority shall impose administrative discipline on directly responsible officials and personnel.
articles.47: Article 47. If construction in a protected character-area zone fails to comply with the plan and damages traditional layout or historic character, the protection authority shall order cessation and restoration or other remedies by a deadline. If consequences are serious, the fine shall be RMB 500,000–1,000,000 for an organization or RMB 50,000–100,000 for an individual, and unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated.
articles.48: Article 48. If, without proper grounds, a responsible entity refuses to perform its duties under Article 29(2), causing a historic building to be listed as endangered or destructively affected, the protection authority shall order it to perform its duties and restore the building or take other remedial measures by a deadline.
articles.49: Article 49. Unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or damage of a marker for a historic character area, building or traditional-character building, contrary to Article 30(3), shall be corrected by a deadline. Failure results in a fine of RMB 10,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 1,000–10,000 for an individual.
articles.50: Article 50. If an implementation plan is not filed as required by Article 32(1)(2), the county-level protection authority shall order filing by a deadline. Failure results in a fine of RMB 10,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 1,000–10,000 for an individual.
articles.51: Article 51. A person damaging the principal exterior character or distinctive components of a traditional-character building, contrary to Article 34(2), shall be ordered to stop and restore the building or take other remedial measures by a deadline. Failure results in a fine of RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual; unlawful proceeds shall also be confiscated.
articles.52: Article 52. A person damaging a provisionally protected subject and causing destructive effects, contrary to Article 35(4), shall be ordered to stop and restore it or take other remedial measures by a deadline. If serious consequences destroy or eliminate the subject, the fine shall be RMB 100,000–200,000 for an organization or RMB 20,000–100,000 for an individual; unlawful proceeds shall also be confiscated.
articles.53: Article 53. If a contractor fails to take temporary protective measures and report a discovery, or the developer fails to notify the competent department, contrary to Article 36(1), the protection authority shall order work to stop and protective or other remedial measures by a deadline. If serious consequences damage or destroy a building or structure of historic value, a fine of RMB 50,000–500,000 shall be imposed.
articles.54: Article 54. A historic district designated before this Regulation takes effect under the Hangzhou Historic Districts and Historic Buildings Protection Regulation may, if it meets the applicable conditions, be designated and published as a historic character area under this Regulation.
articles.55: Article 55. This Regulation takes effect on 1 May 2023. The Hangzhou Historic Districts and Historic Buildings Protection Regulation is repealed on the same date.

FBMCLI.10.4087861.title: Regulations of Liuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Liuzhou's circumstances and under the Cultural Relics Protection Law, Urban and Rural Planning Law, national historic-city protection regulations and other laws, to protect and administer Liuzhou as a historic and cultural city, carry forward its outstanding heritage and strengthen cultural confidence.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to planning, protection, management and use of the historic and cultural city within Liuzhou's urban area. Protected subjects include historic urban areas, historic districts and areas, historic buildings, cultural relics, intangible heritage, traditional place names, industrial heritage, ancient and notable trees and others. Where laws or regulations separately protect cultural relics, intangible heritage, trees or other subjects, they apply.
articles.3: Article 3. Urban planning and construction shall prioritize heritage conservation. Protection shall follow scientific planning, categorized management, strict conservation and appropriate use; respect local character and improve living conditions; preserve traditional layout, historic character, authenticity and integrity; balance socioeconomic development with heritage protection; and transmit civilization and culture.
articles.4: Article 4. The municipal government shall lead protection and supervision. It shall establish a coordination mechanism for major matters, including: (1) reviewing the protection list and amendments; (2) reviewing citywide and subject-specific protection plans; (3) studying solutions and measures for major protection issues; (4) coordinating major emergencies and implementing significant policies; and (5) other major matters concerning protection.
articles.5: Article 5. District governments shall protect and supervise heritage in their areas and establish a city-district coordination mechanism. Township and town governments and subdistrict offices shall perform related duties under this Regulation.
articles.6: Article 6. The municipal housing and urban-rural development authority together with the cultural-relics authority shall coordinate protection and supervision and implement this Regulation. Other departments shall perform related duties.
articles.7: Article 7. Municipal and district governments shall include protection in their economic and social development plans and budget for it.
articles.8: Article 8. 4 January each year is Liuzhou National Historic and Cultural City Protection Awareness Day. Municipal and district governments shall educate the public, disseminate protection knowledge and promote local heritage, including prehistoric culture, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Sanjie, wartime, industrial, landscape and ornamental-stone culture, to raise Liuzhou's cultural profile.
articles.9: Article 9. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate lawfully through donations, grants, investment, public-interest organizations, technical support and volunteer activities.
articles.10: Article 10. Everyone has a duty to protect heritage and may discourage, report or complain about damage to a protected subject. Municipal and district housing, planning and cultural-relics authorities shall publish reporting channels and promptly verify and handle reports. Governments shall commend or reward outstanding contributions under national rules.
articles.11: Article 11. The municipal government shall establish a protection list including: (1) the historic urban area centered on Liuzhou Prefectural City within the 1379 Ming-dynasty brick wall and extending to Liuhou Park and the old city north of Fei'e Road; (2) historic districts such as Shuguang West Road and Dongmen; (3) historic areas; (4) immovable cultural relics including the Bailian Cave, Liyuzui and Liujiang Man sites, Liuhou Temple inscriptions, Dongmen Tower, Zhang Chong's and his mother's tombs, cliff carvings at Yufeng and Ma'anshan, Ho Chi Minh's former residence, the old airport and defenses, and the former site of the Guilin-South Campaign review meeting; (5) intangible heritage such as Dong songs, Dong timber-building techniques, Liuzhou folk songs and opera, Zhuang shigong dance and handmade river-snail rice noodles; (6) historic buildings such as Liujiang Bridge, the fire brigade watchtower, Liuzhou railway workers' cultural palace and Sun family compound; (7) traditional place names; (8) underground archaeological deposit areas; (9) industrial heritage; (10) ancient and notable trees; and (11) other subjects designated by the municipal government. Subjects approved and published by the State Council, autonomous region or municipal government shall be listed directly; other subjects shall be identified and approved by the municipal government. The list shall state each subject's name, location, period of origin and historic value and be promptly published.
articles.12: Article 12. An area not designated as a historic district may be designated as a historic area if it: (1) substantially preserves the traditional layout and historic character of a landscape city and has a certain scale; (2) distinctly reflects ethnic or local character of a period, such as an industrial city, commercial center of central Guangxi or transport hub; or (3) contains historic and cultural remains and has a certain scale.
articles.13: Article 13. A building or structure not designated or registered as an immovable cultural relic may be designated as a historic building if it: (1) reflects Liuzhou history, culture or customs and a particular period or regional character; (2) is associated with an important political, economic, cultural or military event or notable person; (3) is a representative or landmark work or a notable architect's work; (4) reflects regional architecture, ethnic character or scientific value through its style, structure, materials, workmanship or engineering; (5) is representative of Liuzhou's industrial history; (6) has artistic or historic value in its form, space, details or decoration; or (7) has other major historic significance.
articles.14: Article 14. A geographic, road or street name that authentically reflects the culture, geography, ethnic or local character of a historical period may be designated a traditional place name.
articles.15: Article 15. The municipal cultural-relics authority, together with relevant departments, shall survey heritage and recommend valuable discoveries to the authority responsible for identifying that category of subject. Any organization or individual may report a valuable heritage resource to the municipal cultural-relics authority.
articles.16: Article 16. The municipal housing authority, after consulting interested parties and together with cultural-relics and urban-planning authorities, shall conduct preliminary review of historic areas and buildings, obtain expert review and public notice, and submit them to the municipal government for approval and publication. The municipal place-name authority shall similarly obtain expert review and public notice before submitting traditional place names for approval. Other subjects shall be identified under national and autonomous-region rules.
articles.17: Article 17. The municipal government shall dynamically manage, update and publish the protection list. If a listed subject is seriously damaged or lost, or its protection level or category changes, the municipal housing authority together with the cultural-relics authority shall promptly propose an amendment and submit it for municipal approval.
articles.18: Article 18. The authority identifying a protected subject shall establish its file, and relevant parties shall cooperate. The file shall include: (1) survey materials; (2) cultural, artistic and historic features, development, events, notable-person stories and technical information; (3) current use and ownership changes; (4) protection plans; (5) design and survey data; (6) records, drawings, photographs and video created during repair, maintenance, relocation or demolition; and (7) other materials requiring preservation.
articles.19: Article 19. The identifying authority shall establish and maintain a subject-specific database and collect, organize and enter information within its duties. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall assist. Relevant departments shall share protection data and incorporate it into the municipal territorial-spatial basic information platform.
articles.20: Article 20. The municipal government shall organize the historic-city protection plan. The municipal housing authority together with urban-planning and cultural-relics authorities shall prepare it and submit it for approval. Those departments shall likewise prepare and submit plans for the historic urban area, districts, areas and buildings.
articles.21: Article 21. Plans for historic areas and buildings shall state principles, subjects, requirements, boundaries, core and construction-control zones, measures, development intensity, construction controls and phased implementation. A historic-building plan shall also specify key planning controls and repair guidance. Historic buildings shall receive categorized protection according to historic, cultural, scientific and artistic value, condition and construction quality. City, historic urban-area and district plans shall follow national and autonomous-region requirements.
articles.22: Article 22. The municipal government shall approve plans for historic urban areas, areas and buildings. Before submission, the preparer shall publish the draft and solicit comments from experts and the public through meetings, hearings or other means for at least 30 days. The submission shall explain which comments were adopted and why, and include hearing records where relevant. Within 20 days after approval, the plan shall be published on government websites and in major news media.
articles.23: Article 23. An approved protection plan may not be amended without authorization. If amendment is necessary, the preparer shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and may prepare a revision only after consent. The revision shall follow the original approval procedure. If a subject is removed from the list, the corresponding plan provisions expire automatically.
articles.24: Article 24. Citywide and subject-specific protection plans shall be coordinated with territorial spatial plans and have consistent planning periods. Subject-specific plans shall align with and be incorporated into the city plan. Detailed plans shall comply with protection plans and balance conservation and development. Special plans for infrastructure, public services, housing, environment, transport, green space, tourism, waterways and commerce shall also align with them.
articles.25: Article 25. Based on approved plans, municipal and district governments shall prepare implementation programs that preserve traditional layout and historic character and prioritize infrastructure, public services and living conditions. In residential historic districts and areas, population in the core shall be managed and, in a planned manner, reduced to a reasonable density. Land-use rights in the core may not be transferred as a whole for commercial real-estate development.
articles.26: Article 26. Responsible entities are: the municipal government for the historic urban area; the district government for a historic district or area; for a state-owned historic building, its custodian, or, if none, its user, or, if neither is identifiable, the local housing authority; for a non-state-owned historic building, its owner, or, if the owner is missing, unreachable or title unclear, the user, then a custodian if the user is unknown or none exists, and, if none is identifiable, the local housing authority. The district government shall identify and notify the responsible entity in writing. An objection shall be filed within 30 days after notice; the district government shall decide whether to adjust based on the circumstances.
articles.27: Article 27. The responsible entity for the historic urban area shall: (1) adopt policies for its protection and appropriate use; (2) prepare annual programs and funding and advance protection, management and use in an orderly manner; (3) coordinate improvements to public services and municipal facilities; (4) preserve traditional layout, historic character, spatial scale, principal view corridors and historic environmental features; and (5) perform other statutory duties.
articles.28: Article 28. The responsible entity for a historic district or area shall: (1) implement the protection plan and preserve layout, character, scale, view corridors and historic environmental features; (2) improve infrastructure, public services and living conditions while retaining street scale and character; (3) coordinate management and enhancement of facades, walls, roofs, courtyards and public spaces; (4) conduct routine inspections and promptly discourage harmful conduct and notify competent departments; and (5) perform other duties designated by the municipal government.
articles.29: Article 29. A historic-building responsible entity shall: (1) retain original height, bulk, appearance and color; (2) preserve layout, historic character, distinctive decoration and environmental features; (3) maintain the building and keep it clean; (4) ensure structural safety, mitigate hazards and report them to the local district authority; (5) repair it under this Regulation; (6) keep fire and disaster facilities operational; (7) prevent water, damp and insect damage; (8) use it appropriately under the protection plan; (9) accept housing-authority supervision and guidance; and (10) meet other legal requirements. Transferors and lessors shall inform transferees and lessees of protection and repair requirements.
articles.30: Article 30. Municipal and district housing authorities shall conduct annual structural and quality-safety reviews and maintain files. They shall notify the responsible entity of results in writing, and it shall cooperate. After hearing its views, the authorities shall prepare annual repair plans and notify entities to carry out repairs.
articles.31: Article 31. Repairs shall meet technical specifications, quality standards and repair guidelines. Before work, the responsible entity may request free technical advice from the municipal or district housing authority; it may procure technical services from qualified entities. Except for routine maintenance or minor repairs that do not affect character-defining features, materials, construction or decoration, the entity shall prepare design and work plans under district technical guidance. Exterior repair or decoration, added facilities, structural changes or changes in use require municipal planning and cultural-relics approval and other procedures; other plans shall be filed with the urban-district housing authority. Repairs shall be carried out by a qualified contractor. The responsible entity shall submit the completed repair file to the municipal urban-construction archive.
articles.32: Article 32. The responsible entity shall pay repair costs. If it cannot afford them, it may seek a municipal or district grant or design assistance, or the government may acquire the building through monetary compensation or title exchange for repair and protection. For a building repaired with public funds, the grant terms may provide a government right of first refusal if it is sold, on equal terms and unless law provides otherwise. Governments shall prescribe subsidy measures.
articles.33: Article 33. Historic buildings shall be preserved in situ. No one may damage, relocate or demolish one without authorization. If public interest makes in-situ preservation impossible, approvals under national and autonomous-region rules are required. After approved relocation or demolition, the developer shall create survey and image records and file them with the municipal housing authority.
articles.34: Article 34. The housing authority shall supervise structural safety of buildings and structures in protected cores of historic districts, areas and buildings. If damage is likely, it shall notify the owner, user or custodian to carry out required repairs.
articles.35: Article 35. Outdoor advertisements, signs and similar facilities in a historic urban area, district, area or historic-building protected area shall comply with the protection plan and not damage spatial character or landscape. Existing noncompliant facilities shall be replaced or removed by a deadline under law.
articles.36: Article 36. Place names reflecting Liuzhou's history shall be retained. Renaming for special reasons shall follow applicable laws and national and autonomous-region rules.
articles.37: Article 37. The municipal cultural-relics authority, together with relevant departments, shall survey and publish underground archaeological deposit areas. During land banking, land in such areas or potentially containing relics may not be entered into the reserve until archaeological survey, prospecting or excavation is lawfully completed.
articles.38: Article 38. Municipal and district governments shall support research on industrial-heritage protection and improve its conservation and use. Industrial enterprises and heritage owners, users and managers shall protect and use it and cooperate with surveys, assessments, identification and archiving. During conversion, restructuring, auction or asset exchange, they shall preserve its historic form, structure and other features.
articles.39: Article 39.
