In protected areas of the historic urban area, districts, areas and buildings, it is prohibited to: (1) quarry, mine or conduct similar activities damaging layout or character; (2) occupy green space, waterways or roads designated for preservation; (3) build factories or warehouses for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; (4) store such substances inside buildings; (5) set off fireworks or release sky lanterns or other uncontrolled airborne objects involving open flame; (6) carve or deface historic buildings; (7) unlawfully build structures; (8) change exterior structure or character without authorization; (9) damage load-bearing components or endanger building safety; (10) install protruding safety nets on street-facing buildings; or (11) engage in other conduct likely to damage protected subjects.
articles.40: Article 40. The real-property register and title certificate shall identify a building or structure designated as a historic building. The urban-planning authority shall state protection requirements in the drawings and attachments to its construction-planning permit.
articles.41: Article 41. Planning, cultural-relics, housing and urban-management enforcement authorities may use video surveillance, remote sensing and other methods to monitor buildings and structures in protected areas and promptly detect and stop violations.
articles.42: Article 42. A listed protected subject shall have a marker at its principal entrance within one year after listing. The marker shall state the subject's name, number, location, construction date and cultural information. The municipal government shall set a standard design and urban-district governments shall arrange installation. No one may install, move, obscure, alter or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.43: Article 43. If a resource of protection value has not yet been designated as a historic district, area or building, the municipal housing authority, after preliminary review with cultural-relics and planning authorities and municipal consent, may apply necessary provisional protections under this Regulation. Provisional protection lasts no more than 12 months from notice and expires automatically thereafter.
articles.44: Article 44. The municipal government shall establish a coordinated protection responsibility system. Municipal and district housing, cultural-relics, planning, land, emergency-management and urban-management departments shall coordinate surveys, routine inspections, emergency response and approvals. District governments shall report annually to the municipal government, which shall periodically assess protection and include results in performance reviews of districts and coordinating departments.
articles.45: Article 45. Provided natural and cultural landscapes and heritage are not harmed, appropriate conservation, transmission and use of historic urban areas, districts, areas, buildings, relics, intangible and industrial heritage are encouraged. Urban planning and construction shall incorporate features reflecting Liuzhou's history and integrate cultural transmission with the city's image.
articles.46: Article 46. Municipal and district governments may promote appropriate use by: (1) planning uses for districts and areas and encouraging local crafts, distinctive industries and intangible-heritage transmission; (2) encouraging social and individual investment through policy, grants, fee reductions and awards; (3) establishing operating entities to integrate, research and promote heritage; (4) acquiring non-state-owned historic buildings or exchanging title; (5) commissioning qualified institutions, research bodies, associations and organizations to conduct research and training; (6) encouraging public agencies, enterprises and individuals to open eligible historic places regularly or in part; and (7) leasing or entrusting state-owned historic buildings for appropriate use.
articles.47: Article 47. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to establish museums, exhibition or memorial halls, theme parks and science-education bases; intangible-heritage venues; cultural inns and homestays; traditional workshops and shops; research local culture and present folk arts; or undertake other conservation-oriented activities.
articles.48: Article 48. Governments shall support representative inheritors of local intangible heritage with venues and funding. They may recognize, award or fund those making outstanding contributions or actively transmitting and promoting representative projects. Inheritors shall collect and organize valuable materials, train successors and actively organize or participate in exhibitions and performances.
articles.49: Article 49. Governments shall encourage research and use of heritage resources and develop regional cultural products and service brands based on prehistoric culture, Liu Zongyuan, Liu Sanjie, wartime, industrial, landscape and ornamental-stone traditions, enhancing city quality and character. They shall support high-quality experiential tourism, educational trips and leisure routes based on Liuzhou history and integrate transmission with tourism.
articles.50: Article 50. Where another law or regulation prescribes liability for a violation of this Regulation, that provision applies.
articles.51: Article 51. If a state organ: (1) fails to prepare or amend a plan or designate or update a list through statutory procedures; (2) fails to approve matters lawfully or consistently with a plan; (3) fails to inspect protection or supervise approved alteration and use; (4) fails to accept reports or investigate violations; (5) fails to install markers; or (6) abuses authority, neglects duties or engages in favoritism, the municipal or district government or competent authority shall order correction and discipline directly responsible personnel; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable.
articles.52: Article 52. Releasing sky lanterns or other uncontrolled airborne objects involving open flame in a protected area, contrary to Article 39(5), shall be fined RMB 100 by the urban-management enforcement authority.
articles.53: Article 53. Unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or damage of a marker contrary to Article 42 shall be corrected by a deadline. Failure results in a fine of RMB 10,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 1,000–10,000 for an individual.
articles.54: Article 54. Administrative penalties under this Regulation that fall within a State Council- or autonomous-region-approved centralized enforcement jurisdiction shall be imposed by the designated authority.
articles.55: Article 55. This Regulation may be applied by reference to protection, management and use of historic cities and towns, districts, historic areas and buildings, traditional place names and industrial heritage within counties under the municipal jurisdiction.
articles.56: Article 56. This Regulation takes effect on 1 May 2021.

FBMCLI.10.9903391.title: Regulations of Nanjing Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Nanjing's circumstances and under the Urban and Rural Planning Law, Cultural Relics Protection Law, national historic-city protection regulations and other laws, to protect Nanjing's historic and cultural city, carry forward outstanding Chinese culture, and coordinate heritage protection and use with socioeconomic development.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to planning, protection, use and management of Nanjing's historic and cultural city.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall follow scientific planning, conservation priority, categorized management, appropriate use, shared governance and transmission; preserve Nanjing's traditional layout and character; and protect heritage authenticity and integrity.
articles.4: Article 4. Nanjing shall follow a protection framework led by the Party, guided by government, coordinated across departments, open to diverse participation and subject to public oversight, strengthening holistic and systematic protection. Municipal and district cultural-heritage coordination bodies and the Jiangbei New Area body shall coordinate, guide and review major matters. The Nanjing Historic and Cultural City Protection Expert Committee shall provide review and assessment.
articles.5: Article 5. The municipal government shall protect Nanjing and include this work in development plans, with policy and funding support. District governments and the Jiangbei New Area administrative body shall protect heritage in their areas, arrange funds, establish routine inspections and incorporate them into community-grid management. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall perform local duties, conduct inspections and outreach and encourage participation. Residents' and villagers' committees shall assist.
articles.6: Article 6. The municipal planning and natural resources authority, together with culture and tourism (cultural relics) and urban-construction authorities, shall implement this Regulation. Planning and natural resources shall manage protection plans and support the municipal coordination body. Culture and tourism shall plan, protect, use and supervise World Heritage, immovable relics and intangible heritage and investigate and mark red-culture resources and assign responsible entities. Urban construction shall build municipal infrastructure, administer construction approvals for historic buildings and manage traditional-village applications. Agriculture and rural affairs shall coordinate village infrastructure, living conditions and agricultural heritage. Housing and property shall install and maintain markers, issue historic-building notices and supervise safe use. Industry and information technology, water, civil affairs, landscaping and other departments shall protect industrial, irrigation, place-name, tree and other heritage. Education, sports, commerce, health, ethnic and religious affairs, transport, development and reform, finance, urban management, emergency management, fire and rescue bodies shall assist within their duties.
articles.7: Article 7. Nanjing shall establish multiple funding channels, including municipal, district and Jiangbei budgets and grants; proceeds from appropriate use of state-owned protected buildings; heritage funds established by enterprises, organizations or individuals; donations; and other lawful sources. Funds shall support surveys, identification, markers, measured records, plans, repairs and emergency work, environmental improvement, infrastructure, research, outreach and training. Financial institutions and local financial organizations are encouraged to support projects and broaden financing.
articles.8: Article 8. Governments and departments shall promote new technologies and methods and use the protection information platform to integrate survey, planning, protection and management information and improve effectiveness.
articles.9: Article 9. Everyone has a duty to protect Nanjing's historic and cultural city and may comment on protection work and monitor or report damage. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate through donations, grants or volunteer service; outstanding contributions shall be recognized under national and provincial rules.
articles.10: Article 10. Governments, the Jiangbei New Area administrative body and departments shall conduct public outreach in various forms, disseminate protection knowledge and raise awareness.
articles.11: Article 11. The municipal government shall cooperate with other cities in China and abroad on the protection and use of major cross-regional heritage.
articles.12: Article 12. Nanjing's historic and cultural city covers the entire municipal area. Its defining landscape—Yangtze River, Qinhuai River, Xuanwu Lake and Ningzhen Mountains; capital layouts of the Six Dynasties, Southern Tang, Ming and Republican periods; the ‘river-fronted and lake-bordered’ and ‘dragon coiled, tiger crouched’ historic city-site setting; and historic axes including Zhonghua Road, Yudao Street and Zhongshan North–Zhongshan–Zhongshan East roads—shall be protected as a whole.
articles.13: Article 13. Protected subjects include: (1) the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum and associated Ming-dynasty merit tombs, a World Heritage site; (2) immovable relics such as the Nanjing City Wall and Southern Dynasties tomb carvings; (3) historic towns such as Chunxi, historic villages such as Yangliu, and traditional villages such as Lixiang; (4) ancient towns such as Hushu, Zhuzhen and Longtan and ancient villages such as Dou; (5) the historic urban area; (6) districts such as Confucius Temple and Yihe Road and historic areas along the Inner Qinhuai and at Baizi Pavilion; (7) historic buildings such as the former Geological Society of China site; (8) ancient and notable trees such as the ginkgo at Huiji Temple and wintersweet at Longquan Temple; (9) red-culture, industrial, agricultural, irrigation and place-name heritage; (10) intangible heritage such as Nanjing brocade weaving and Jinling scripture carving and printing; and (11) other subjects designated by the State, province or city. Existing laws and regulations govern protection where applicable.
articles.14: Article 14. Nanjing shall maintain a protection list. Subjects approved and published nationally or provincially, and those identified in the Nanjing protection plan, shall be included directly. Identification and adjustment shall follow applicable national, provincial and municipal rules. Where none exist, the competent authority shall consult departments, owners, users and managers, obtain expert review and public comment, and submit the list for municipal approval and publication. Within one year after publication, it shall create and preserve a file stating each subject's name, location, date of construction or origin and historic value. If archival conditions are unsafe or risk serious damage, the file may be transferred to an archive.
articles.15: Article 15. The municipal government shall organize planning and natural resources, culture and tourism, urban construction, agriculture, industry, water, civil affairs, landscaping, transport and other departments to survey heritage and identify recommended list entries. Before urban renewal or other construction, district governments and the Jiangbei New Area body shall conduct surveys. Any organization or individual may propose a subject for listing. Departments and responsible entities shall cooperate and lawfully provide information and records.
articles.16: Article 16. Nanjing shall provide provisional protection. When a survey identifies a resource warranting protection and it is added to the recommended list, the competent authority shall notify the district government or Jiangbei New Area body. Before public notice of designation, that body shall notify the owner, user or manager and the town government or subdistrict office. For resources discovered in construction or proposed by the public, the district government or New Area body shall arrange preliminary assessment; if protection value is found, it shall promptly issue notice to those parties. Within six months of notice, the competent authority shall complete identification. If it declines to list the subject, it shall lift provisional protection and notify the parties, unless national or provincial rules provide otherwise. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall inspect provisional subjects, stop damage and report serious cases. No one may relocate or demolish a provisional subject without authorization.
articles.17: Article 17. Within one year after a list is published, the competent authority shall install a marker in a prominent location, unless law provides otherwise. Markers shall follow a uniform standard and use digital tools to facilitate public access. No one may install, move, obscure, alter or damage them without authorization.
articles.18: Article 18. An approved list may not be altered without authorization. Changes in protection level or loss of value shall be handled under the original approval procedure. If inadequate protection seriously impairs the value of a listed subject, the competent authority, with municipal consent, shall publish it as endangered and require the local district government or Jiangbei New Area body to rectify the problem by a deadline. If it meets requirements, it shall be removed from the endangered list. If not and protection value is lost, after expert review the local government may apply to remove it from the protection list, subject to municipal approval. Other laws and regulations prevail.
articles.19: Article 19. Nanjing's protection-planning system comprises the city plan, plans for categories of protected subjects and special plans for cultural resources.
articles.20: Article 20. The city protection plan shall be prepared concurrently with the overall territorial spatial plan. After publication of the protection list, plans for historic districts, towns, villages, traditional villages, ancient towns and villages and historic areas, and protection drawings for historic buildings, shall be prepared promptly based on the city plan.
articles.21: Article 21. Protection plans shall comply with national, provincial and municipal technical standards, specifications and guidelines; where none exist, comparable plans may be used as reference. If no protection plan exists, detailed plans shall state heritage-protection requirements. Plans shall cover historical research and current conditions, cultural character and value, protected subjects and boundaries, requirements and measures, presentation, use and transmission, and coordination with related plans.
articles.22: Article 22. Preparation and approval shall follow these rules: (1) the municipal government prepares the city plan and submits and files it lawfully; (2) the district government or Jiangbei New Area body prepares plans for historic towns and villages and submits and files them lawfully; (3) the same bodies prepare district plans and submit and file them lawfully; (4) they prepare plans for traditional villages, ancient towns and villages and historic areas, which after municipal planning review are submitted for municipal approval; plans for nationally recognized traditional villages also require national technical review; (5) the municipal planning and natural resources authority prepares historic-building protection drawings for municipal approval; and (6) competent authorities together with municipal planning prepare special heritage plans for municipal approval. Other plans are encouraged and follow competent-authority procedures. Drafts shall be published and comments sought from departments, experts and the public.
articles.23: Article 23. An approved protection plan may not be amended without authorization. If amendment is necessary, the preparer shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and may prepare a revision only after consent. The revision shall follow the original approval procedure.
articles.24: Article 24. Mandatory city-plan requirements shall be incorporated into territorial spatial plans at all levels. Transport, municipal services, green-space, fire-safety and underground-space plans shall align with the city plan. After a subject plan is approved, its requirements shall be incorporated into detailed plans and may not be changed arbitrarily when those plans are revised.
articles.25: Article 25. Nanjing shall use a responsible-entity system, designated and published by municipal or district governments and the Jiangbei New Area body: (1) the local district government or New Area body for a historic urban area or district; (2) the town government or subdistrict office for a historic town or village, traditional village, ancient town or village, or historic area; (3) the owner for a historic building, or, if unknown, unreachable or title unclear, its user or manager; if they are unknown or disputed, the district government or New Area body shall promptly designate an entity; where the building is transferred with its land parcel, the parcel transferee is responsible; (4) the owner, user or manager for another subject, or, if unknown or disputed, the competent authority shall designate an entity; and (5) the separate protection-management institution, where one has been established for the subject.
articles.26: Article 26. The responsible entity for the historic urban area shall implement holistic, comprehensive and systematic protection by: (1) preserving traditional layout, reasonably controlling development and continuing characteristics from different periods; (2) protecting the urban area and its city-site setting, historic capital layouts, axes, roads, lanes and distinctive tree-lined streets; (3) protecting landmark landscape nodes and view corridors and the distinctive ‘mountain, water, city and forest’ interface; (4) improving infrastructure, public services and living conditions and integrating urban renewal with heritage protection; (5) inspecting subjects and markers to prevent human damage; (6) promoting appropriate use and transmission; and (7) performing other duties prescribed by law or the municipal government.
articles.27: Article 27. Construction in the historic urban area shall strictly comply with building-height controls. Construction in important view corridors or distinctive interfaces shall also undergo visual-impact analysis. Any necessary change shall follow statutory procedures for amending the relevant plan.
articles.28: Article 28. Responsible entities for historic districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, ancient towns and villages and historic areas shall implement protection plans and: (1) preserve and continue traditional layout, street patterns and historic character and protect the supporting terrain, waterways and natural setting; (2) inspect routinely, prevent damage and address or report risks promptly; (3) implement protection measures, appropriate use and improved living conditions; (4) conduct safety and disaster-prevention work; and (5) encourage residents to participate and assist public presentation and education.
articles.29: Article 29. Construction in protected cores and control zones of historic districts, towns and villages, and protected areas of traditional villages, ancient towns and villages and historic areas, shall comply with protection plans. Construction in district, town and village cores and control zones follows applicable laws and rules. Work in other protected areas shall continue traditional layout and character and control height, bulk, style and color. Traditional-character buildings may not be demolished without authorization. Exceptional demolition in the core requires approval by the municipal planning and natural resources authority together with the cultural-relics authority; district governments and the Jiangbei New Area body shall manage such buildings in other areas. Historic streets and lanes may not be altered in width, direction or alignment without authorization.
articles.30: Article 30. Nanjing shall issue historic-building protection notices prepared by the municipal planning and natural resources authority, stating protection requirements. Responsible entities shall comply when protecting, repairing, transferring or leasing a building. They may obtain information and technical guidance from planning, natural resources and urban-construction departments.
articles.31: Article 31. The housing and property authority shall periodically inspect historic-building use and protection and notify the responsible entity in writing to address safety risks through maintenance and repair. The entity shall act promptly. If damage is likely, it shall prepare and implement a maintenance and repair plan; if it lacks capacity, the district government or Jiangbei New Area body shall take protective measures.
articles.32: Article 32. The responsible entity shall pay repair and maintenance costs. If a building is certified as dangerous and requires repair or reinforcement, the entity may apply for a grant from the district government or Jiangbei New Area body under housing-safety rules.
articles.33: Article 33. Construction shall, where possible, avoid historic buildings; if avoidance is impossible, in-situ preservation shall be used wherever possible. If public-interest construction makes this impossible and relocation or demolition necessary, applicable national rules shall be followed. Where feasible, a demolished building shall be reconstructed at another site or a marker erected at the original site to retain and transmit its history.
articles.34: Article 34. Protection and management of industrial, agricultural and irrigation heritage and other subjects identified by competent departments shall follow national and provincial rules. If none exist, the competent authority shall specify protected subjects, requirements and measures.
articles.35: Article 35. A construction design in a protected area of a cultural relic designated at municipal level or above shall be reviewed by the municipal government and submitted under cultural-relic laws. A design in its construction-control zone requires consent from the competent cultural-relics authority under national rules and municipal approval. Major projects in protected cores and control zones of historic districts, towns and villages, and protected areas of historic areas and buildings, require expert review and public notice before municipal approval. The municipal government shall manage existing buildings in the historic urban area and protected areas, avoid arbitrary demolition of valuable structures and require approval through prescribed procedures where demolition is necessary.
articles.36: Article 36. District governments and the Jiangbei New Area body shall establish routine inspection mechanisms, inspect protected subjects, and promptly detect, stop and address damage and unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or destruction of markers.
articles.37: Article 37. Nanjing shall conduct special assessments of historic-city protection. The municipal planning and natural resources authority, together with culture and tourism (cultural relics) and urban-construction departments, shall organize professional teams and experts to assess protection under national requirements and report results to the municipal government. District governments and the New Area body shall promptly prepare corrective measures, set deadlines and complete rectification.
articles.38: Article 38. Nanjing shall develop specialist research institutions and strengthen professional protection capacity. Universities, research teams and social actors are encouraged to participate. Relevant departments shall provide professional training for local administrators and practitioners as needed.
articles.39: Article 39. Nanjing shall establish an overall heritage-protection and transmission framework and mechanisms, encourage appropriate use and orderly public access, use heritage for public education and promote sustainable transmission.
articles.40: Article 40. District governments and the Jiangbei New Area body may adopt and dynamically update positive and negative lists for appropriate use, specifying encouraged, supported, restricted and prohibited activities, and implement them after required approval.
articles.41: Article 41. Municipal and district governments and the Jiangbei New Area body shall select annual heritage-transmission and use projects under relevant plans, include them in annual government investment and urban/rural construction programs, and implement them after required approval.
articles.42: Article 42. If current standards for density, spacing, setbacks, green space, parking or utilities cannot be met in renovating protected subjects, a developer may prepare a design consistent with protection requirements if neighboring property rights are not diminished. The municipal planning and natural resources authority and relevant departments shall arrange expert review and submit it for municipal approval. If conservation needs prevent compliance with current national fire-safety standards, governments and the New Area body shall organize relevant departments to prepare and review a fire-safety assurance plan before implementation; this approach may also apply to ancient towns and villages. Projects meeting urban-renewal or inefficient-land revitalization requirements may receive relevant land, planning and registration policies.
articles.43: Article 43. Municipal and district governments and the Jiangbei New Area body may provide appropriate subsidies for transmission and use projects involving immovable relics, historic districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, ancient towns and villages, historic areas and buildings, and agricultural heritage.
articles.44: Article 44. Use of residential historic districts and areas shall retain their principal residential function and improve livelihoods and historic character in light of local conditions. Governments and the New Area body shall establish resident-centered protection mechanisms and carry out repairs, dangerous-building remediation, unitization and fire-safety upgrades, improve infrastructure and public services and living conditions. With owners' and users' consent, public-housing vacancy, private-property acquisition, lease relocation, self-renewal and factory relocation may support appropriate use. An owner improving living conditions may lawfully add necessary living facilities if neighboring rights are not impaired. Social participation is encouraged; eligible projects may receive tax and credit support under national and provincial rules.
articles.45: Article 45. A historic building may be internally renovated or put to a different use if its original exterior and characteristic components are retained, the work complies with protection plans, positive/negative use lists and structural and fire-safety plans, and its registered real-property use is unchanged.
articles.46: Article 46. Public services shall extend to historic towns and villages, traditional villages and ancient towns and villages. Local history and value shall be researched and presented. Traditional crafts, customs, festivals and arts may support rural tourism, leisure agriculture and creative industries, linking rural revitalization with urban and rural culture.
articles.47: Article 47. Governments and the New Area body shall research heritage and explain the cultural meaning and value of Nanjing's Yangtze and Grand Canal culture, its history as a capital of ten dynasties and its identity as a UNESCO City of Literature, creating distinctive Nanjing cultural symbols.
articles.48: Article 48. Governments and the New Area body shall implement heritage projects and create routes, corridors and networks integrated into daily life, combining online and in-person presentation. They shall: (1) develop cultural routes for the Six Dynasties, Southern Tang, Ming, modern and contemporary periods and for red, landscape, literary, science-and-education, industrial and commercial themes; (2) establish museums, exhibition halls and archaeological parks reflecting Nanjing's heritage; (3) provide venues for intangible heritage; (4) install wayfinding, marker and information signs and use modern technology; and (5) hold traditional festivals and markets, public talks, expert lectures and immersive activities.
articles.49: Article 49. Governments and the New Area body shall develop interdisciplinary heritage specialists. Education and human-resources departments shall encourage schools, vocational-training bodies and social actors to offer relevant courses and train specialists and traditional craftspeople. Urban-construction departments, together with human-resources and agriculture departments, shall provide craft training and skill certification and promote living transmission of traditional skills.
articles.50: Article 50. Where another law or regulation prescribes a penalty for conduct violating this Regulation, it applies. Where administrative penalties are exercised under rules on centralized enforcement or comprehensive administrative enforcement, those rules apply.
articles.51: Article 51. Unauthorized relocation or demolition of a provisional subject, contrary to Article 16(5), shall be stopped by the enforcement body designated by a district government or the Jiangbei New Area body, which shall require restoration or other remedies by a deadline and confiscate unlawful proceeds. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual.
articles.52: Article 52. If inadequate protection causes a listed traditional village, ancient town or village, or historic area to be placed on an endangered list, the municipal or district government or New Area body shall issue a notice of criticism within its authority. If overdue or inadequate correction causes removal from the protection list, the competent authority shall discipline directly responsible officials and personnel.
articles.53: Article 53. If conduct seriously damages or creates a serious risk of damage to a protected subject and harms the public interest, the people's procuratorate or another legally authorized body or organization may bring a public-interest lawsuit.
articles.54: Article 54. If personnel of a municipal or district government, the Jiangbei New Area body or a department abuse authority, neglect duties or engage in favoritism, directly responsible personnel shall be disciplined; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable.
articles.55: Article 55. For purposes of this Regulation: (1) a ‘historic area’ is an area not designated as a historic district and outside a historic town, village or traditional village's protected area, that authentically reflects a period's traditional character, layout and culture and has protection value; (2) an ‘ancient town’ is a town or subdistrict not designated as historic that retains a particular period's traditional character and layout; (3) an ‘ancient village’ is a village not designated as historic or traditional that retains such character and layout; (4) a ‘historic street or lane’ has cultural meaning, distinctive and intact features and an important role in overall character; and (5) a ‘traditional-character building’ is a building or structure within a protected area of a historic district, town or village, traditional village, historic area, ancient town or village, other than an immovable relic or historic building, with sufficient history and value to shape the area's overall character.
articles.56: Article 56. This Regulation takes effect on 1 July 2026. The Nanjing Historic and Cultural City Protection Regulation adopted on 30 June 2010 is repealed on the same date.

FBMCLI.10.7185442.title: Regulations of Baoding Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Baoding's circumstances and under the Urban and Rural Planning Law, Cultural Relics Protection Law, national historic-city protection regulations and other laws, to protect Baoding's historic city, carry forward its heritage, continue its historical continuity and strengthen its cultural capacity.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to planning, protection, management and use of the historic and cultural city within Baoding's administrative area. Where it is silent, applicable laws and regulations govern.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall follow scientific planning, strict conservation, categorized management and appropriate use; preserve traditional layout and historic character and heritage authenticity, integrity and continuity; and retain the public's memories and attachment to Baoding's history.
articles.4: Article 4. The municipal government shall protect, use and supervise the historic city. County-level governments shall carry out these functions in their areas. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall manage routine local protection. Residents' and villagers' committees shall assist. Municipal and county-level governments shall include protection in development plans and budget for it.
articles.5: Article 5. Municipal and county-level governments shall establish protection committees to plan, coordinate, advance and supervise protection. Committees shall provide expert consultation and review, assessment and advice on major matters.
articles.6: Article 6. The protection authority designated by each municipal or county-level government shall supervise protection in its area. Departments and entities shall coordinate within their respective duties and this Regulation.
articles.7: Article 7. Governments and departments shall conduct public education and promote transmission and presentation of outstanding traditional culture. They may commission qualified enterprises, institutions or social organizations to conduct research, consultation, outreach or training.
articles.8: Article 8. Protection is a shared social responsibility. Volunteer groups, public-interest organizations and others are encouraged to participate through technical services, donations, grants or investment. Governments and departments shall recognize outstanding contributions under law. Anyone may discourage or report damage to protected subjects; departments shall promptly handle reports and provide feedback.
articles.9: Article 9. Protected subjects include historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, historic character areas, historic buildings and other subjects. Immovable cultural relics, ancient and notable trees, intangible, industrial, agricultural and irrigation heritage, place-name heritage and other subjects are governed by applicable laws and regulations.
articles.10: Article 10. An area not meeting the criteria for a historic district may be designated as a historic character area if it has a substantial concentration of valuable buildings, retains substantially intact historic character and traditional layout, and: (1) played an important role in a town's formation or development; (2) is closely associated with a notable historical figure or event; (3) has distinctive traditional, regional or period character; or (4) preserves rich intangible heritage.
articles.11: Article 11. A building or structure not designated as a protected cultural relic or relic site may be designated as a historic building if it: (1) has historic, scientific or artistic value in style, structure, materials, workmanship or engineering; (2) reflects Baoding's history, culture or customs and a distinctive period or regional character; (3) is an industrial remnant valuable to the history, technology, culture or social development of Baoding; (4) is a representative building connected with the history of the Communist Party of China, the People's Republic, socialist development or reform and opening-up, or with a historical event, revolution or notable person; or (5) otherwise has historic or cultural value.
articles.12: Article 12. Municipal and county-level governments shall maintain a protection list and include protected subjects. Subjects approved and published by national, provincial or municipal governments shall be listed directly. A county-level designation shall be submitted to the municipal government for approval and inclusion in its list. The list shall state each subject's name, ownership, location, category, protection level, history and value.
articles.13: Article 13. Governments shall periodically survey protected subjects within their duties. Relevant departments shall recommend valuable discoveries for listing. Applications, approval and designation of historic cities, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic buildings shall follow national and provincial rules. A historic character area shall be reviewed by experts and relevant entities organized by the planning authority together with housing and cultural-relics authorities, publicly noticed, and submitted for approval and publication. Anyone may propose a valuable subject to the local government or department.
articles.14: Article 14. A valuable subject not yet listed may, with government consent, be designated for provisional protection. Within seven working days, the competent department shall notify its owner and user of required protective measures. If it is not listed within one year after notice, provisional protection expires automatically. During that period, no one may damage, relocate or demolish it without authorization.
articles.15: Article 15. If a listed subject is seriously damaged or lost, or its level or category changes, the relevant department shall propose an amendment and submit it to the original approving authority under applicable procedures for approval and publication.
articles.16: Article 16. A file shall be established for each listed subject, with cooperation from relevant parties. It shall include: (1) survey materials; (2) cultural, artistic and historic features, development, events, notable-person stories and technical information; (3) current use, ownership changes and approvals for construction in the protected area; (4) protection plans; (5) design and survey data; (6) records, drawings, photographs and video created during repair, relocation or demolition; and (7) other materials requiring preservation.
articles.17: Article 17. New digital and other technologies shall be used to collect and analyze information, efficiently consolidate and share data and facilitate public access to heritage information.
articles.18: Article 18. Within six months after a subject is listed, the municipal or county-level government shall install a marker. Markers shall be placed at principal entrances to protected cores of districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and character areas, and in a prominent exterior location on historic buildings. They shall state the subject's name, number, location, construction date and cultural information. No one may install, move, alter or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.19: Article 19. Municipal and county-level governments shall prepare plans for the historic city and districts. County-level governments shall prepare plans for historic towns and villages and traditional villages. Natural resources and planning authorities shall prepare character-area plans; housing authorities shall prepare historic-building protection drawings. Plans for historic cities, districts, towns, villages and traditional villages and their preparation, approval and amendment shall follow national and provincial rules. Character-area plans and historic-building drawings shall be submitted to the government at the same level. Departments shall provide necessary baseline data.
articles.20: Article 20. Core requirements of city and historic-town plans shall be incorporated into the overall territorial spatial plan. Detailed plans shall implement those requirements, align with plans for districts, villages, traditional villages and character areas, and protect historic buildings. Village plans may be combined with historic-village or traditional-village plans; detailed plans may be combined with historic-district or character-area plans. Special plans for roads, utilities, parks, fire safety and place names shall align with protection plans.
articles.21: Article 21. Governments shall coordinate implementation of protection plans, supervise lower-level authorities and departments and periodically assess implementation. Problems shall be corrected promptly, and assessment information made public.
articles.22: Article 22. An approved protection plan or drawing may not be amended without authorization. If amendment is necessary, the preparer shall submit a reasoned report to the original approving authority and, after consent, submit the revision through the original procedure.
articles.23: Article 23. Protection is administered locally. Governments shall organize protection under plans and drawings. Governments at municipal, county, town and subdistrict levels may establish protection organizations or procure services for routine management.
articles.24: Article 24. Governments shall use urban-renewal, rural-revitalization and other policies to phase out uses incompatible with heritage, optimize functions, and maintain appropriate population and social structure. They shall improve roads, waterways, ecology, infrastructure, public services and overall character in historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and character areas.
articles.25: Article 25. Governments shall designate and publish responsible entities: (1) the county-level government for a historic urban area; (2) the subdistrict office for a historic district; (3) the town government for a historic town or village or traditional village; (4) the town government or subdistrict office for a historic character area; (5) the owner for a historic building, or an agreed user for a state-owned building; if a non-state-owned building's owner is unknown, the county-level government shall designate an entity; (6) a protection-management organization established for a subject; and (7) for a subject crossing jurisdictions, an entity designated by the common higher-level government. If responsibility cannot otherwise be determined, the municipal or county-level government shall designate it. After publishing the list, the county-level government shall notify the responsible entity in writing of its duties.
articles.26: Article 26. Responsible entities for historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and character areas shall comply with plans and: (1) preserve traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale and historic environmental features; (2) inspect routinely, stop harmful conduct and notify competent departments; (3) keep protected areas clean and orderly; (4) assign personnel to maintain fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities; and (5) meet other requirements set by municipal or county-level governments.
articles.27: Article 27. A historic-building responsible entity shall: (1) retain original height, bulk, appearance and color; (2) preserve historic character, distinctive decoration and environmental features; (3) ensure safety, mitigate hazards and report them; (4) keep the building clean; (5) provide and maintain fire and disaster equipment; (6) repair it as required; and (7) meet other legal requirements. No one may damage, relocate or demolish a historic building without authorization. If public-interest construction makes in-situ preservation impossible and requires relocation or demolition, applicable laws and regulations govern.
articles.28: Article 28. Construction in protected areas shall comply with the protection plan. In a historic urban area, no building or structure that harms traditional layout or character may be built, and utility lines for power, communications, water, drainage and gas shall be underground; existing overhead lines shall gradually be moved underground. In cores of historic districts, towns and villages and character areas, new construction or expansion is prohibited except for necessary infrastructure and public services. In traditional-village areas, building height, bulk, form and color shall not conflict with traditional character. In a historic-building protected area, its core heritage values shall remain unchanged.
articles.29: Article 29. The following are prohibited in protected areas: (1) damaging buildings, structures or facilities designated for preservation; (2) unauthorized repairs or decoration that change their original character; (3) advertisements or signs that damage or impair character; (4) indiscriminate dumping or wastewater discharge; (5) damaging objects or sites forming part of intangible heritage; and (6) other conduct prohibited by law or inconsistent with the protection plan.
articles.30: Article 30. Disaster-prevention, mitigation and response shall use structural, personnel and technological measures. Facilities and access routes shall comply with technical standards. If conservation needs make compliance impossible, the competent disaster-prevention authority together with relevant departments shall prepare a safety-assurance plan.
articles.31: Article 31. Training traditional craftspeople, transmitting traditional crafts and producing traditional materials related to heritage protection are supported, and related intellectual property shall be protected under law. Universities, vocational schools and social actors are encouraged to provide relevant courses and train specialists.
articles.32: Article 32. Protection funding shall be raised through multiple channels for surveys, identification, repair, emergency response, environmental improvement, infrastructure, research, planning, education, training, archaeology and appropriate use. Sources include: (1) municipal and county budget allocations; (2) donations; (3) rent from state-owned buildings within the historic city; and (4) other lawful sources.
articles.33: Article 33. The Baoding Ancient City is the historic urban area defined in the Baoding Historic and Cultural City Protection Plan: east to the east bank of the eastern moat, south to the south bank of the Fu River, west to the west bank of the western moat, and north to the north bank of the northern moat.
articles.34: Article 34. The traditional spatial pattern of Baoding's ancient city—‘boot-shaped city, four gates, offset cross streets, towers, Lotus Pond and Zhili Governor's Office’—shall be protected.
articles.35: Article 35. The city walls shall be repaired; green space along the moat, Fu River and Great Wall South Street controlled; and existing parks connected, retaining the city's distinctive boot-shaped outline.
articles.36: Article 36. Historic lanes including East Street, West Street, the southern section of Lianchi South Street and North Street shall be protected. Street-facing buildings and structures shall be repaired and improved in a manner compatible with nearby relics and historic buildings.
articles.37: Article 37. The courses of the moat and Fu River shall be preserved. Filling waterways and discharging wastewater are prohibited. Natural conditions and riverside landscapes shall be improved. The plan form of Lianchi shall be protected; its water shall be dredged and revitalized and its environment improved.
articles.38: Article 38. Core protected areas and construction-control zones shall be delineated for historic districts including Governor's Office–West Street, East Street–North Street and Huai Army Office–Qinghe River Administration Office. Their traditional layout, historic character and related natural landscapes and environment shall be preserved and continued.
articles.39: Article 39. Building height in the ancient city shall be reasonably controlled, preserving the Daci Pavilion as its landmark high point. Building character and landscape around Daci Pavilion, the Zhili Governor's Office, Lianchi Academy, Huai Army Office, Qinghe River Administration Office, city wall and other relics and historic buildings shall be improved.
articles.40: Article 40. New, expanded or renovated buildings in the ancient city shall respect traditional architecture, reflect Baoding's history and regional culture, and guide bulk, color, materials and roof forms to create a coherent traditional character.
articles.41: Article 41. Large commercial complexes, wholesale markets, factories, major sports venues, schools and other uses that impair the ancient city's character and historic atmosphere shall be appropriately relocated. Buildings that harm character shall be lawfully renovated, and unlawful structures removed.
articles.42: Article 42. Positive and negative lists of permitted uses shall be established. Vacated or exchanged spaces shall support cultural, tourism and leisure services; cultural and public green space shall increase; public services and infrastructure shall improve; and living conditions in the ancient city shall be enhanced.
articles.43: Article 43. Public transport is prioritized in the ancient city, with denser bus networks, more stops, wider coverage and improved service. Traditional commercial pedestrian streets may be established in an orderly manner as part of urban renewal.
articles.44: Article 44. A distinctive ancient-city sign system shall be developed, including wayfinding, introductory, display and interpretive signs.
articles.45: Article 45. A themed visitor loop shall connect historic and cultural resources and guide tourism development across the historic urban area.
articles.46: Article 46. Use of heritage shall suit its historic, artistic, scientific, cultural and social values while considering economic benefits and balancing protection, use and transmission. Conservation and appropriate use and development of tourism and culture are encouraged, provided local natural and cultural landscapes and heritage are not damaged. Governments and departments shall collect, research, present and disseminate cultural resources; protect and transmit customs, folk arts and crafts; explain history and values; integrate culture and tourism; and use heritage for public education.
articles.47: Article 47. Governments shall provide online platforms and diverse text, audio, video and digital presentation of Baoding's influence, cohesion and appeal and showcase municipal heritage resources.
articles.48: Article 48. Time-honored brands, old objects, crafts and performances shall be protected and used to create enduring cultural brands, with suitable space for intangible-heritage transmission. Heritage may support product-design bases, creative products and audiovisual works, turning cultural resources into industry strengths. Local crafts, distinctive products and intangible-heritage activities are encouraged in protected areas; unrelated commercial development shall be strictly controlled.
articles.49: Article 49. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to use heritage in protected areas by establishing specialist museums, exhibition halls or memorials; presenting folk arts and filming audiovisual works; hosting inheritor studios and practice venues; opening eligible historic buildings to the public; making and presenting traditional crafts; creating educational experience bases; or conducting other public-benefit conservation activities.
articles.50: Article 50. Research and use of cultural resources, regional cultural brands and locally distinctive cultural products are encouraged, as are cultural or folk inns, distinctive restaurants and cultural or tourism activities in unused buildings. Original residents are encouraged to remain in protected areas, continue traditional ways of life and operate businesses compatible with protection using their own assets.
articles.51: Article 51. Governments may promote appropriate use by: (1) establishing operating organizations to integrate, research, promote and use heritage; (2) selecting qualified entities through public tender or similar means; (3) leasing or entrusting use of non-state-owned immovable relics or state-owned historic buildings; and (4) simplifying procedures and providing grants, fee reductions or development-right incentives.
articles.52: Article 52. Education authorities shall encourage schools to integrate heritage protection, use and transmission into curricula, organize public lectures and student community activities, and use school and community resources. Governments, departments and responsible entities shall support a lasting mechanism for free student visits to museums, exhibition halls, art galleries and similar venues.
articles.53: Article 53. Where another law or regulation prescribes liability for a violation of this Regulation, that provision applies.
articles.54: Article 54. If a municipal or county-level department fails to perform heritage-protection duties, causing serious consequences, the government at the same level, a superior department or supervisory authority shall hold its principal official accountable. Personnel who neglect duties, abuse authority or engage in favoritism shall be disciplined by their entity, superior authority or supervisory body; criminal liability shall be pursued where applicable.
articles.55: Article 55. A person damaging, relocating or demolishing a provisional subject without authorization shall be ordered by the designated county-level department to restore it or take other remedies by a deadline. For serious consequences, the fine shall be RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–30,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.56: Article 56. Unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or damage of markers for historic districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, character areas or historic buildings shall be corrected by a deadline by the municipal or county-level housing authority or designated protection authority. Failure results in a fine of RMB 10,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 1,000–10,000 for an individual.
articles.57: Article 57. Unauthorized construction, alteration or expansion in protected areas shall be stopped by the authority exercising planning penalties or the town government. If corrective measures can remove the planning impact, correction shall be ordered by a deadline and a fine of 5%–10% of construction cost imposed. If the impact cannot be corrected, demolition shall be ordered; if demolition is impossible, the structure or unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated and a fine of up to 10% of construction cost imposed.
articles.58: Article 58. Administrative penalties assigned by comprehensive urban-management enforcement rules to another enforcement body shall be imposed by that body under the applicable rules.
articles.59: Article 59. For purposes of this Regulation: (1) a ‘historic urban area’ is a town area reflecting its historical development or a period's character, commonly called an old city or downtown, with clear historic boundaries, substantially preserved layout and character and a need for protection; (2) a ‘historic district’ is a provincial-designated historic area with abundant relics and concentrated historic buildings that substantially and authentically preserves traditional layout and character; (3) a ‘historic town’ or ‘historic village’ is a town or village designated by the national housing authority or provincial government, with abundant relics, major historic or commemorative value, and an intact reflection of period character and local or ethnic features; (4) a ‘traditional village’ contains tangible and intangible heritage and has significant historic, cultural, scientific, artistic, social or economic value; (5) a ‘historic character area’ is a municipal or county-level designated area with a concentration of valuable buildings and a scale that reflects a period's historic character and ethnic or local features; (6) a ‘historic building’ is a municipal or county-level designated building or structure with protection value that reflects historic or local character but is not designated or registered as an immovable cultural relic; and (7) ‘boot-shaped city, four gates, offset cross streets, towers, Lotus Pond and Zhili Governor's Office’ describes Baoding's distinctive spatial order: the boot-shaped walls; four eastern, western, southern and northern gate districts; street pattern centered on East, West, North and South streets; Daci Pavilion as visual focus and high point; the Lianchi waterways, including the Ancient Lotus Pond, moat, Fu River, Xixi and Zi River; and cultural relics and historic districts represented by the Zhili Governor's Office.
articles.60: Article 60. This Regulation takes effect on 8 December 2023.

FBMCLI.10.8694652.title: Regulations of Xuzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Xuzhou's circumstances and under the Cultural Relics Protection Law, national regulations on historic cities, towns and villages, Jiangsu provincial historic-city and town rules and other laws, to protect Xuzhou's heritage and carry forward its history and outstanding traditional culture.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to planning, protection and use of the historic and cultural city, and related safeguards and supervision, within Xuzhou's administrative area.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall follow scientific planning, conservation priority, categorized management, appropriate use and shared protection; preserve traditional layout and historic character and heritage authenticity and integrity; balance development with conservation; and sustain a historic city that transmits tradition and supports modern life.
articles.4: Article 4. Municipal and county-level governments shall lead and coordinate protection in their areas, include it in development plans, provide policy support and supervision and resolve major issues. Town governments and subdistrict offices shall perform local duties, assign responsibility and conduct inspections, maintenance, outreach and supervision. Villagers' and residents' committees shall assist. Development zones, industrial parks, scenic areas and other administrative bodies shall assist or perform delegated protection duties.
articles.5: Article 5. The housing and urban-rural development department shall survey, document and supervise historic buildings and, with culture and tourism (cultural relics), administer protection. Natural resources and planning shall incorporate plans into territorial spatial plans. Culture and tourism shall protect relics and intangible heritage in protected areas. Urban water affairs shall protect and plan water bodies, famous springs, spring landscapes and spring catchments. Landscaping and forestry shall protect nature reserves, parks and notable trees. Civil affairs shall protect traditional place names. Development and reform, industry, public security, finance, environment, transport, agriculture, education, science, commerce, emergency management, state assets, market regulation, civil defense, administrative approval, ethnic and religious affairs, comprehensive enforcement and other departments shall assist according to their duties.
articles.6: Article 6. The municipal government shall establish expert consultation to provide professional assessment and advice. Municipal and county-level departments shall solicit public comments through hotlines, email and meetings and facilitate access to protection information.
articles.7: Article 7. Governments and departments shall conduct public education and promote outstanding traditional culture. They may commission qualified enterprises, institutions or organizations to conduct related research, consultation, outreach and training. Media shall conduct public-interest outreach.
articles.8: Article 8. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate lawfully through donations, grants, investment, public-interest organizations, technical services and volunteering.
articles.9: Article 9. Everyone has a duty to protect the historic city and may report or discourage violations. Departments shall promptly handle reports. Outstanding contributions shall be rewarded under national and provincial rules.
articles.10: Article 10. Protected subjects include: (1) historic districts such as Hubu Mountain and Zhuangyuan Mansion; (2) historic towns such as Yaowan, historic villages and traditional villages; (3) ‘Pengcheng Seven Li,’ Xuzhou's historical urban continuity; (4) the Xuzhou section of the Grand Canal; (5) underground deposit areas such as the City-under-City Ruins; (6) immovable relics such as the Han-Chu kings' tombs, Huating site and Yunlong Mountain carvings, and historic buildings such as Xuzhou Museum; (7) intangible heritage such as Xuzhou paper-cutting, sachets and qinshu storytelling; (8) red-culture material and intangible resources such as Huaihai Campaign memorial architecture; (9) agricultural heritage such as Pizhou ginkgo cultivation, water heritage such as the Ming-era old Yellow River embankment, place-name heritage such as Pengcheng Road and modern industrial remains; (10) historic environmental features such as waterways, roads, ancient trees, and natural and cultural landscapes and spatial patterns tied to the city's value; and (11) other valuable subjects.
articles.11: Article 11. Governments shall organize surveys of all urban and rural heritage and scientifically assess historic, cultural, artistic, scientific and technological value to identify protected subjects. Identification shall follow national and provincial rules. Where none exist, the competent authority shall formulate and publish identification standards and procedures. An identified subject may not be adjusted without authorization; a change in protection level or loss of value shall be handled under the same procedures.
articles.12: Article 12. A building or structure not designated or registered as an immovable relic may be designated a municipal historic building if it: (1) is associated with a major historical event or figure and has historic, commemorative or educational value; (2) reflects traditional culture, ethnic or regional character or a period's style, or is a local landmark; (3) represents a period's architectural design or has notable architectural-art value; (4) reflects engineering or scientific standards through materials, structure or construction; or (5) otherwise has historic, scientific or artistic value.
articles.13: Article 13. Xuzhou shall maintain a protection list. Municipal and county-level governments shall organize competent departments to prepare categorized lists and maps based on identification and update them dynamically. They shall state each subject's name, category, location and protection level and be published.
articles.14: Article 14. A municipal or county-level government shall designate a valuable resource not yet listed for provisional protection, notify its owner and user in writing within 10 working days and state applicable protection requirements. The local town government or subdistrict office shall conduct routine inspections. Provisional protection lasts six months from notice. If listed, the competent authority shall notify the owner and user; if not listed by expiry, provisional protection ends.
articles.15: Article 15. Historic districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, historic buildings and protected cultural relics shall have markers. Unless national or provincial rules prescribe a design, the municipal government shall set a standard design and county-level governments shall install them. No one may install, move, obscure, alter or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.16: Article 16. Competent authorities shall maintain databases and archives for protected subjects, collect and enter information within their duties, including artistic and historic features, age, rarity, current use, ownership changes, and records from repair and decoration, and technical survey materials.
articles.17: Article 17. Within one year after designation, governments shall organize plans for historic cities, districts, towns, villages and traditional villages and submit them for approval. Plans shall align with territorial spatial plans, preserve authenticity, integrity, traditional layout, character and spatial scale, protect associated natural and cultural environments, manage building height, form and views, and provide holistic and systematic conservation. Drafts shall be published for at least 30 days, with comments sought from departments, experts, interested parties and the public. Submissions shall explain adoption of comments and include hearing records where relevant. Approved plans shall be published under law.
articles.18: Article 18. Protection plans shall state: (1) overall goals, principles, subjects and areas; (2) conservation measures and construction controls; (3) requirements for traditional layout and character; (4) urban and rural heritage-transmission requirements; (5) boundaries of historic urban areas and key protection zones, and core and construction-control zones for districts, towns and villages; (6) phased implementation and safeguards; and (7) other national or provincial requirements.
articles.19: Article 19. An approved protection plan may not be amended or adjusted without authorization. If necessary, the preparer shall submit a reasoned report to the original approving authority and, after consent, submit the revision through the original procedure.
articles.20: Article 20. Governments shall prepare action plans based on the city plan, select annual heritage-transmission projects and include them in annual urban and rural construction plans.
articles.21: Article 21. Housing departments together with planning and cultural-relics authorities shall prepare historic-building protection drawings, obtain expert review and submit them for approval and publication. Drawings shall state the name, location and construction date; core heritage values; protection category, requirements and use recommendations; protected area, construction controls and prohibited uses; and other statutory information. The department shall provide drawings and instructions free of charge to owners, users, managers and property-service providers.
articles.22: Article 22. Governments shall strictly implement protection plans, organize implementation and periodically inspect and assess plan implementation and protection. Problems shall be promptly corrected. The government where the historic area, district, town, village, traditional village or building is located shall implement its protection list and plans.
articles.23: Article 23. Town governments and subdistrict offices responsible for historic towns and villages, districts, character areas and traditional villages shall: (1) receive public complaints and suggestions, stop harmful conduct and report it; (2) help maintain fire and disaster-prevention facilities; and (3) meet other statutory or government requirements.
articles.24: Article 24. The municipal planning and natural resources authority shall establish and maintain an information platform with geospatial, place-name and heritage data. Housing, cultural relics, water, forestry, industry, civil affairs, ethnic and religious affairs, comprehensive enforcement and other authorities shall collect and enter information within their duties, share data and update the platform. It shall publish protection lists, plans and historic-building drawings and support participation by organizations and the public.
articles.25: Article 25. The following are prohibited in protected areas of historic cities, towns, villages and districts: (1) quarrying, mining or similar activities damaging traditional layout or character; (2) occupying forest or green space, rivers, lakes or roads designated for preservation; (3) building factories or warehouses for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; and (4) other conduct prohibited by law.
articles.26: Article 26. Activities in protected areas of historic cities, towns, villages and districts shall preserve traditional layout, historic character and buildings and comply with required procedures, including changes to green space or waterways, major filming or events in a protected core, and other activities affecting character or buildings.
articles.27: Article 27. Where a legally owned building in a protected area is certified as dangerous, its owner may apply for repair or renovation under applicable law while preserving traditional layout and character. The municipal government shall prescribe detailed measures. Governments shall encourage owners to improve living conditions voluntarily through exchanges and similar arrangements.
articles.28: Article 28. Municipal and district governments shall prioritize infrastructure and public services in protected areas in accordance with plans and improve living conditions. Fire facilities and routes in protected cores shall meet technical standards; where conservation needs prevent compliance, the municipal fire and rescue agency together with housing shall prepare a fire-safety assurance plan.
articles.29: Article 29. Governments shall adopt support policies, optimize business uses and encourage local distinctive activities and time-honored brands in historic districts, integrating conservation with culture and tourism.
articles.30: Article 30. Historic buildings may be designated after investigation, consultation, expert review and municipal approval. They shall be published, marked and entered in a protection file.
articles.31: Article 31. The municipal government shall establish a categorized protection list and standards for historic buildings. Class I buildings shall retain their original facade, finish, color, structural system, layout and distinctive interior decoration; Class II shall retain facade, finish, color and principal layout; Class III shall retain facade, finish and color. The list shall be dynamically maintained. A building lost by force majeure or lacking protection value may be removed after consultation, expert review and municipal approval; a building designated as a cultural relic shall be removed from this list.
articles.32: Article 32. The owner is responsible for a historic building; if missing, unreachable or title is unclear, the user or manager is responsible, and if none is identifiable the district government shall designate an entity. The responsible entity shall maintain and repair the building and follow protection plans and standards. Governments shall support a responsible entity lacking capacity. Governments shall encourage owners to sell or donate buildings to the State.
articles.33: Article 33. No one may damage, relocate or demolish a historic building; no one may install equipment that shortens its service life, store hazardous substances, deface it or otherwise harm it. Construction shall avoid such buildings where possible; if unavoidable, preserve in situ where feasible. Necessary relocation or demolition for public interest requires approval under law, and project costs shall be budgeted. Exterior repair, additions, or structural or use changes require approval and other procedures. Appropriate public-facing cultural uses are encouraged.
articles.34: Article 34. Protection and management of the Xuzhou section of the Grand Canal, modern industrial remains, agricultural and water heritage, and place-name heritage shall follow national and provincial rules. If none exist, the competent authority shall formulate measures and submit them for municipal approval and publication.
articles.35: Article 35. Before redevelopment or large-scale land development in old urban areas, governments shall survey immovable cultural relics, identify and register them and take lawful protection measures. Construction may not start before the survey, to prevent destructive construction.
articles.36: Article 36. Before transferring or allocating land in areas that may contain underground relics, governments shall request provincial cultural-relics archaeological survey and prospecting. Any relic found shall be protected under law.
articles.37: Article 37. Governments shall survey underground deposits in protected areas and request designation and publication of concentrated areas requiring holistic protection as underground cultural-relic deposit zones.
articles.38: Article 38. Construction in protected cores or control zones of historic districts, towns and villages shall comply with plans and be compatible in layout, height, bulk, style and color. New construction or expansion in a core is prohibited except for necessary infrastructure, public services and living-condition improvements. New polluting facilities are prohibited; existing ones shall be handled under environmental law. Roads, underground works and utilities shall use effective safeguards. External facilities and decoration shall match historic character. New or renovated utility lines shall be underground; where impossible, they shall be concealed or technically treated.
articles.39: Article 39. In key protection zones of historic cities and towns, it is prohibited to: (1) build structures damaging traditional character; (2) damage protected buildings or facilities; (3) undertake construction or blasting, sand extraction or excavation endangering relics or changing their terrain; (4) occupy or damage protected streets, green space or waterways; (5) alter protected buildings in ways changing their character; (6) install signs or objects that impair character; or (7) engage in other unlawful conduct.
articles.40: Article 40. Conservation and repair shall continue historic continuity and highlight historic depth, regional character, production and living wisdom, and cultural and artistic achievements.
articles.41: Article 41. Governments shall prepare plans to improve living environments in historic districts, towns and villages and traditional villages, investing in facilities, housing and environmental improvements.
articles.42: Article 42. Governments shall protect and use intangible heritage such as traditional crafts and customs, establish lists of representative projects, create venues, support representative projects and inheritors, and encourage transmission and public presentation.
articles.43: Article 43. Appropriate use shall prioritize conservation, use heritage moderately, retain overall character, manage commercial intensity, add public open space and proceed through gradual, small-scale renewal.
articles.44: Article 44. Governments shall research and transmit Xuzhou's Han and Chu, Pengzu, red, landscape, canal, Su Shi and military cultures; collect and present local customs, dialect, crafts, food and history; explain cultural values; integrate heritage and tourism; and use heritage for public education.
articles.45: Article 45. Governments and departments shall integrate conservation with urban renewal and modern life, coordinate new and old urban areas, manage old-city density and intensity, develop ways of expressing heritage compatible with daily life, create visitor routes and networks and make heritage part of public life. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to participate in street renewal under protection plans, with technical support and possible grants.
articles.46: Article 46. The municipal government shall coordinate protection and use of ‘Pengcheng Seven Li,’ research its history, optimize functions, adjust uses, improve public services and environment, establish a transmission system and create a north–south cultural axis through the central city.
articles.47: Article 47. The municipal government shall delineate the protected area for ‘Pengcheng Seven Li’ and prepare a protection and development plan coordinated with the city protection plan. New construction shall comply with it and required approval procedures; existing incompatible buildings shall be gradually modified under the plan.
