articles.48: Article 48. Governments shall develop tourism routes and sites based on heritage, build Xuzhou tourism brands, cooperate regionally and integrate heritage tourism with rural, educational and technology tourism.
articles.49: Article 49. Governments shall guide industries and optimize uses in heritage areas, supporting local businesses and time-honored brands, intangible-heritage projects, cultural institutions, studios, innovation services and shared offices, integrating heritage protection with culture and tourism.
articles.50: Article 50. Use of historic buildings shall preserve overall integrity, safety and continuity, especially core exterior, structure and components. Responsible entities may host creative, leisure-tourism, research, traditional-craft and intangible-heritage activities if protection requirements are met. Governments shall support appropriate use, including reduced rent or longer leases for state-owned buildings.
articles.51: Article 51. If current fire-safety standards cannot be met for conservation reasons during redevelopment of protected subjects, governments shall organize planning, housing, culture, fire and rescue authorities to assess and prepare a fire-safety assurance plan. Special construction projects shall submit special fire-design materials and complete required review. The municipal housing department and fire-rescue authority shall issue technical guidance.
articles.52: Article 52. Governments shall protect and appropriately use ancient tombs and sites, including the Han-Chu kings' tombs, and establish archaeological parks and site museums for conservation, collections, research, education and public visits.
articles.53: Article 53. Organizations and individuals may conduct lawful, moderate, reasonable and sustainable heritage activities, including cultural research, traditional markets and performances; distinctive tourism products and routes; exhibitions and research bases; adaptive use of industrial and cultural remains and river works; support for intangible-heritage documentation and presentation; and other activities that protect and transmit Xuzhou's heritage. Governments and departments shall facilitate such activities.
articles.54: Article 54. Governments shall budget for protection and use and coordinate existing funding at all levels. Social investment is encouraged; governments shall facilitate participation through policies and project information.
articles.55: Article 55. Universities, research institutions and enterprises are encouraged to research and develop protection technologies. Science departments shall support key technology development, demonstration and technical standards.
articles.56: Article 56. Governments and departments shall develop professional capacity and train technicians, local administrators, repair-skill inheritors and craftspeople through multiple channels, including training bases with universities, research bodies and enterprises.
articles.57: Article 57. Governments shall improve roads, water, drainage, power, sanitation and other public services and infrastructure in protected areas. Where conservation prevents use of current standards, relevant departments shall prepare special measures, obtain expert review and implement them. Governments shall coordinate service delivery and provide strong public-service support.
articles.58: Article 58. Governments shall establish a digital information platform for heritage, continuously update all protected-subject information and enable connectivity and data sharing.
articles.59: Article 59. Municipal and county-level governments shall conduct self-assessments under national and provincial rules and periodically assess protection and subject conditions. They shall promptly issue risk alerts and require rectification of significant problems.
articles.60: Article 60. Governments and departments shall conduct routine inspections and may integrate them into urban and rural grid services, comprehensive urban enforcement and community policing.
articles.61: Article 61. If an administrative authority responsible for protection unlawfully exercises or fails to exercise its powers, harming state or public interests, procuratorial authorities may require it to perform its duties. Procuratorial authorities and other eligible organizations may bring public-interest lawsuits for damage to heritage or other harm to state or public interests; governments and departments shall support or cooperate.
articles.62: Article 62. Where another law or regulation prescribes a penalty for conduct violating this Regulation, that provision applies.

FBMCLI.10.1255208.title: Regulations of Changzhou Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Changzhou's circumstances and under the Urban and Rural Planning Law, Cultural Relics Protection Law, national historic-city regulations, Jiangsu historic-city and town rules and other laws, to protect and administer Changzhou's historic and cultural city and transmit its heritage.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to planning, protection, management and use of the historic and cultural city within Changzhou's administrative area. Protection includes historic urban areas, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, historic areas and buildings, protected cultural relics, immovable relics, ancient and notable trees, traditional place names and intangible heritage. Other applicable laws govern those subjects where relevant.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall be government-led and open to participation, prioritize conservation and allow appropriate use, follow scientific planning and lawful management, and preserve heritage authenticity, integrity and continuity.
articles.4: Article 4. The municipal government shall protect and supervise the historic city. County-level (city/district) and town governments shall do so in their areas; subdistrict offices shall perform related duties; villagers' and residents' committees shall assist. Governments shall incorporate protection into development plans and annual programs and provide policy and funding support. The municipal government shall assess protection annually and include performance in reviews of county-level governments and municipal departments.
articles.5: Article 5. The urban-planning authority together with cultural-relics authorities shall implement this Regulation. Development and reform, industry, education, science, public security, civil affairs, finance, land, construction, transport, water, culture, environment, housing, landscaping, urban management, local history, tourism, religious affairs, civil defense and other departments shall assist within their duties.
articles.6: Article 6. Municipal and county-level governments shall establish dedicated protection funds for surveys, measurements, identification, emergency response, plan preparation, repair grants, research and awards.
articles.7: Article 7. Standing committees of municipal and county-level people's congresses shall supervise governments through inspections and review of special reports.
articles.8: Article 8. Changzhou shall maintain a protection list, including: (1) the Changzhou section of the Grand Canal; (2) traditional layout and historic character of the historic urban area; (3) historic districts such as Qingguo Lane, Nanshi River and Qianhou Beian; (4) historic towns such as Menghe; (5) historic villages such as Jiaoxi; (6) traditional villages such as Yangqiao; (7) historic areas such as Tianning Temple–Yizhou Pavilion, Suoqiaowan, Nanheyan and Sanbao Street–Xizhi Street; (8) historic buildings; (9) modern industrial heritage; (10) valuable historic environmental features; (11) protected relics and immovable relics such as the Chinese Shuyu fossil site, Yancheng and Helü City sites, and Qu Qiubai's former residence; (12) underground deposit zones and archaeological sites; (13) place names of historic value, commemorative significance or long standing; (14) intangible heritage such as Jintan paper-cutting, Changzhou comb-making, bamboo carving and random-needle embroidery; and (15) other subjects designated by the municipal government. County-level governments may create their own lists. Lists shall state names, locations, periods of origin and values, and be published. An approved list may not be adjusted without authorization.
articles.9: Article 9. An area not designated as a historic district may be designated as a historic area if it: (1) substantially preserves traditional layout and character at a certain scale; (2) distinctly reflects the ethnic or local character of a historical period; or (3) contains abundant historic and cultural remains at a certain scale.
articles.10: Article 10. A building or structure not designated or registered as a protected cultural relic may be designated a historic building if it: (1) is associated with a major historical event or figure; (2) represents urban development; (3) represents an industry; (4) has commemorative, educational or other historic-cultural significance; (5) reflects a period's architectural style; (6) has distinctive artistic design or detail; (7) reflects regional or ethnic architecture; (8) is a recognized local landmark or symbol; (9) is a notable architect's work; (10) reflects the engineering or scientific standards of its time; (11) had an advanced form or spatial arrangement for its period; or (12) otherwise has distinctive value.
articles.11: Article 11. Subjects approved and published by national, provincial or municipal governments shall be listed directly. Other subjects shall be considered by municipal planning and cultural-relics authorities after consultation with interested parties and the public, expert review and public notice, and submitted for municipal approval.
articles.12: Article 12. The municipal government shall periodically organize county-level heritage surveys. Departments shall recommend valuable discoveries for listing. Any organization or individual may apply or propose a subject to the municipal planning authority, which shall conduct preliminary review, seek comments, obtain expert review and public notice, and submit it for municipal approval. If force majeure destroys or damages a historic area or building, an amendment shall be proposed by planning and cultural-relics authorities and submitted through the same process.
articles.13: Article 13. The municipal planning authority together with the cultural-relics authority shall collect and organize historic records about listed subjects.
articles.14: Article 14. The municipal planning authority shall maintain files for listed subjects, with cooperation from relevant parties. Files shall include: (1) survey materials; (2) cultural, artistic and historic features, development, events, notable-person stories and technical data; (3) current use and ownership changes; (4) protection plans; (5) design and survey data; (6) records, drawings, photographs and video from repair, relocation or demolition; and (7) other materials requiring preservation. Anyone may inspect file information as permitted by law.
articles.15: Article 15. Plans for the historic city, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages, historic areas and buildings shall protect heritage as a whole, preserve layout, character and spatial scale, and protect related buildings, streets, rivers, green areas and environmental features to present history and culture.
articles.16: Article 16. Preparation, approval and amendment of plans for the historic city, districts, towns and villages shall follow national and provincial rules. The municipal or county-level planning authority with cultural-relics authorities shall prepare plans for traditional villages, historic areas and buildings for government approval. Plans shall be completed within one year after designation.
articles.17: Article 17. Before approval, the preparer shall publish a draft for at least 30 days and solicit comments from departments, experts and the public through meetings, hearings or other means. Approved plans shall be published on government websites and in major local news media within 30 working days.
articles.18: Article 18. Plans for the historic city, districts, towns and villages, and traditional villages shall be submitted to the standing committee of the relevant people's congress for review; the government shall consider and address its comments.
articles.19: Article 19. An approved plan may not be amended without authorization. If necessary, the preparer shall submit a reasoned report to the original approving authority and, after consent, submit the revision under the original procedure.
articles.20: Article 20. The city plan shall protect: (1) the integrity of traditional layout and character, relics, buildings, environmental features, traditional residences and intangible heritage; (2) Grand Canal hydraulic heritage, related physical and settlement heritage, intangible heritage, ecology and landscape; (3) gardens, archways, wells, towpaths, docks, bridges, ancient trees and their setting; and (4) landmark structures, using urban design to control surrounding height, bulk, form and color and strengthen their identity.
articles.21: Article 21. The historic urban-area plan shall protect: (1) city-wall forms created by the ancient, Ming and Guan canals and inner and outer cities and later expansions; (2) the Grand Canal, Guan River, Suoqiao River and other waterways, including course, width, banks, facilities and planned riverside building heights and interfaces; (3) traditional street patterns formed by long streets such as Biji Lane, Xiyingli and Qingguo Lane and short lanes such as Tianjing, Zhengsu, Zaokefang and Yangliu; and (4) view corridors to Wenbi Pagoda and between major heritage sites, with planned height and character controls.
articles.22: Article 22. Historic-building plans shall state character and environmental features, the protected area including the building and necessary character-coordination zone, and protection and use requirements.
articles.23: Article 23. The main content of plans for historic districts, towns, villages and traditional villages shall follow applicable rules. Plans for historic areas shall follow the approach for districts. Plans shall delineate core protected areas and construction-control zones.
articles.24: Article 24. In planning for historic districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic areas, buildings and structures other than protected relics and historic buildings shall be classified as traditional-character buildings or other buildings. A traditional-character building has a history and reflects historic character and local features.
articles.25: Article 25. Plans for historic districts and areas shall meet detailed-plan requirements and may serve as detailed plans. Detailed or village plans affecting the historic city, towns, villages, traditional villages or historic buildings shall include a heritage-protection section.
articles.26: Article 26. Governments shall strictly implement the city plan, coordinate implementation, supervise lower-level governments and departments and periodically assess performance.
articles.27: Article 27. The county-level government where a historic urban area, district, town, village, traditional village, historic area or building is located, or a department designated by the municipal government, shall implement protection under the plan and unified management requirements.
articles.28: Article 28. Governments may procure services or establish area-management organizations for routine protection of districts, towns, villages, traditional villages, historic areas and buildings.
articles.29: Article 29. Town governments and subdistrict offices responsible for historic districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic areas shall: (1) preserve the integrity of traditional layout, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale and environmental features; (2) inspect routinely, stop harmful conduct and notify departments; (3) keep the area clean; (4) help maintain fire and disaster-prevention facilities; and (5) meet other government requirements.
articles.30: Article 30. For a state-owned historic or traditional-character building, its custodian is responsible; if none, its user; if neither is identifiable, the housing authority. For a non-state-owned building, the owner is responsible, or, if missing, unreachable or title unclear, its custodian, or, if there is none, its user. If none can be identified, the local housing authority, town government or villagers' committee shall be responsible. The county-level government shall designate and notify the responsible entity. An objection shall be investigated and may result in adjustment.
articles.31: Article 31. The planning authority together with cultural-relics authorities shall specify and notify responsible entities of their rights and duties under protection plans. They shall comply. A lessor shall inform a lessee of protection and repair requirements.
articles.32: Article 32. Governments shall prioritize roads, water, drainage, power, sanitation and fire infrastructure in protected areas. Where conservation prevents compliance with current standards in protected cores of districts, towns, villages, traditional villages or historic areas, fire, construction, transport, water, cultural-relics, environment, planning, housing, urban management, civil defense, earthquake and other departments shall prepare safeguards within their duties.
articles.33: Article 33. Traffic in the historic urban area shall be strictly managed through a scientifically designed road network of arterial and local streets and a transport system centered on public transit and walking and cycling. Motor vehicles shall be strictly limited in historic districts and areas.
articles.34: Article 34. In protected areas of the historic urban area, districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic areas, it is prohibited to: (1) quarry, mine or conduct similar activities damaging layout or character; (2) occupy protected parks, green areas, waterways, traditional lanes or roads; (3) build facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; or (4) engage in other conduct likely to damage protected subjects.
articles.35: Article 35. Construction in protected areas shall comply with plans: (1) no buildings or structures that harm traditional character, elevated roads or major interchanges may be built in the historic urban area; utility lines shall be underground; (2) in cores of historic districts, towns and villages, new construction or expansion is prohibited except for necessary infrastructure and public services; (3) construction in traditional-village and historic-area zones shall not conflict with traditional layout and character in height, bulk, form or color; and (4) no new building may be built in a historic-building protected area except necessary conservation-related facilities.
articles.36: Article 36. New construction in protected areas shall comply with controls in relevant plans and not damage traditional layout, historic character or view corridors. Existing incompatible buildings shall be gradually improved to restore traditional layout and character.
articles.37: Article 37. Demolition in a protected core of a historic district, town, village, traditional village or historic area, other than a protected relic, immovable relic or historic building, requires an application to the municipal or county-level planning authority. It shall review jointly with the cultural-relics authority and decide within 20 working days.
articles.38: Article 38. Governments shall survey underground archaeological deposits and publish deposit zones. Construction there shall undergo archaeological survey, prospecting or excavation under law. Anyone discovering a relic during construction or production shall immediately stop work, protect the site and report to the cultural-relics authority.
articles.39: Article 39. Historic buildings shall receive special, key or general protection based on historic, artistic, scientific, social and cultural value and age, with the category shown on the marker. Specially protected buildings shall retain their structure, facade, plan and distinctive interior decoration; key buildings their structure and facade; and generally protected buildings their structure and principal facade. Interior facilities may be reasonably improved and modern methods used to strengthen seismic, fire, lightning, flood, damp and insect resistance. No one may damage, relocate or demolish a historic building without authorization. Relocation or demolition for public interest requires approval under applicable rules.
articles.40: Article 40. Buildings other than protected relics and historic buildings in protected areas of districts, towns and villages, traditional villages and historic areas shall be classified. Traditional-character buildings may be maintained, repaired or improved and their interiors upgraded without changing their exterior. Other buildings shall be retained, improved or altered according to their effect on historic character.
articles.41: Article 41. If plans require environmental improvement in a protected area, the county-level government shall prepare a plan. After municipal planning review and consultation with cultural-relics authorities, interested parties and the public, it shall be implemented.
articles.42: Article 42. By 31 December each year, the planning authority or designated county-level department shall prepare the next year's repair plan for historic and traditional-character buildings and submit it for government approval. The plan shall be published online and in local media.
articles.43: Article 43. Repair shall organically renew traditional layout and character under approved plans; preserve street patterns, alignment, frontage, scale and landscape and not build or widen lanes except where consistent with traditional character; ensure repaired buildings' height, bulk, color, materials and structure fit the area; and protect environmental features. Residential areas shall retain their residential function, manage density and continue traditional cultural life.
articles.44: Article 44. Planning authorities together with cultural relics, construction and housing departments shall prepare repair drawings for historic buildings and other buildings in protected areas, state repair requirements, obtain expert review and publish them.
articles.45: Article 45. A responsible entity may repair a historic or traditional-character building under the plan if the work does not affect traditional layout or character. Work increasing floor area or height, expanding the footprint, changing boundaries, altering the facade or structure requires permits. Repairs shall be carried out by qualified contractors under repair standards and drawings.
articles.46: Article 46. Municipal and county-level governments shall provide repair grants to responsible entities for non-state-owned historic and traditional-character buildings where repairs follow technical requirements and drawings. The municipal government shall prescribe grant measures.
articles.47: Article 47. The housing authority shall supervise building safety and notify responsible entities to repair buildings at risk. If a building is certified as dangerous, the entity shall promptly address it. In an emergency, the housing authority shall mitigate the danger; the responsible entity shall cooperate and may not obstruct.
articles.48: Article 48. Listed subjects shall receive markers within six months. Markers for important vanished waterways or buildings in the historic urban area shall present historic information at or near their former sites. The municipal government shall set marker designs and county-level governments install them. No one may install, move, obscure, alter or damage a marker without authorization.
articles.49: Article 49. Nanjing shall establish an information system with geospatial, place-name and historic-cultural data to enable sharing. The municipal planning authority shall administer it; departments shall collect and enter data within their duties.
articles.50: Article 50. Enforcement information related to protection shall be entered in the subject's credit file and included in industry oversight and social-credit systems.
articles.51: Article 51. For protection needs, a department may lawfully amend or withdraw an effective administrative permit. If this causes property loss, compensation shall be paid under law. The planning authority together with cultural-relics, development, finance, housing and construction departments shall prepare compensation rules for government approval.
articles.52: Article 52. Use shall suit heritage's historic, artistic, scientific, social and cultural values while considering economic benefits and balancing protection, use and transmission.
articles.53: Article 53. The municipal government shall adopt measures for appropriate use of historic and traditional-character buildings through policy guidance, grants, rent reductions and rent subsidies.
articles.54: Article 54. A historic building on collectively owned land, or a building in a historic town, village or traditional-village protected area, may be transferred while retaining the collective construction-land status, or after the land is lawfully expropriated as state-owned.
articles.55: Article 55. Governments and village collectives may establish market entities to participate in protection and use, subject to conservation priority. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to contribute funding, donations, funds, technical services or leases and equity in buildings. Governments shall facilitate participation by social actors.
articles.56: Article 56. Governments shall encourage research and use of heritage and development of regional brands and distinctive cultural products. Organizations and individuals are encouraged to establish museums, exhibition or memorial halls; research local culture or present folk arts; make and sell traditional crafts; host intangible-heritage studios; operate cultural inns; create school education bases; or conduct other conservation-oriented activities.
articles.57: Article 57. Subject to protection plans and structural and fire-safety requirements, responsible entities may put historic and traditional-character buildings to multiple uses. They shall strictly preserve historic features and intangible values.
articles.58: Article 58. Governments shall conduct public lectures, reports, expert talks and public experiences to disseminate knowledge. Public institutions and enterprises using eligible historic places shall periodically or partially open them to the public. Professional volunteers are encouraged.
articles.59: Article 59. Schools and education authorities shall protect heritage formed through school development, establish participatory decisions and integrate conservation and transmission into curricula and student activities. Governments, departments and responsible entities shall support regular student visits to museums and cultural venues. Entities receiving public funding for heritage use shall provide free access and educational opportunities to primary and secondary students and teachers.
articles.60: Article 60. If a state organ or its personnel: (1) fails to prepare a protection plan; (2) fails to follow statutory procedures in preparing, amending or publishing plans or lists; (3) fails to approve matters lawfully or consistently with plans; (4) fails to prepare necessary safeguards; (5) fails to supervise safety of historic or traditional-character buildings; or (6) otherwise fails in its duties, seriously impairing protection or heritage values, the municipal or county-level government or competent department shall order correction and discipline responsible personnel.
articles.61: Article 61. If a town government, subdistrict office or its personnel fails to inspect or protect as required by Article 29, the county-level government shall order correction and discipline directly responsible personnel.
articles.62: Article 62. If a responsible entity fails its duties and destructively affects the historic, artistic, scientific, social or cultural value of a historic building, the planning authority shall order cessation and restoration or other remedies by a deadline; unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. For serious consequences, the fine is RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law. The same remedies apply to damage to a traditional-character building; for serious consequences the fine is RMB 20,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 3,000–30,000 for an individual.
articles.63: Article 63. For quarrying, mining or similar damage, occupation of protected green space, waterways, lanes or roads, or construction of facilities for producing or storing hazardous substances, the planning authority shall order cessation and restoration or other remedies by a deadline; unlawful proceeds shall be confiscated. For serious consequences, the fine is RMB 500,000–1,000,000 for an organization or RMB 50,000–100,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.64: Article 64. Unauthorized demolition in protected cores of districts, towns and villages of structures other than protected relics or historic buildings shall be penalized by the planning authority under national historic-city rules. Unauthorized demolition in traditional-village or historic-area cores shall be stopped and restoration ordered; for serious consequences, the fine is RMB 50,000–100,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–50,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.65: Article 65. Unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or damage of a marker, contrary to Article 48(4), shall be corrected by a deadline. Failure results in a fine of RMB 10,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 1,000–10,000 for an individual. Losses shall be compensated under law.
articles.66: Article 66. Administrative penalties assigned by comprehensive urban-management enforcement rules to another enforcement body shall be imposed by that body under the applicable rules.
articles.67: Article 67. This Regulation takes effect on 1 June 2017.

FBMCLI.10.1587081.title: Regulations of Harbin Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2020)

articles.1: Article 1. This Regulation is enacted, in light of Harbin's circumstances and under the Urban and Rural Planning Law, Cultural Relics Protection Law and other laws, to protect heritage and preserve the city's traditional layout and historic character.
articles.2: Article 2. This Regulation applies to protection and supervision of Harbin's historic and cultural city within the municipal area. Protected subjects include the historic urban area, districts, character areas, historic courtyards and buildings. Cultural relics are governed by applicable laws, or by this Regulation where those laws are silent.
articles.3: Article 3. Protection shall follow scientific planning, categorized management, strict conservation and sustainable use, and preserve authenticity and integrity.
articles.4: Article 4. The municipal government shall implement this Regulation. District and county-level city governments shall protect and supervise heritage in their areas.
articles.5: Article 5. The natural resources and planning authority shall administer protection. The cultural-relics authority shall manage buildings and structures that are immovable cultural relics. The finance authority shall manage protection funds. Housing and urban-rural development, urban management and other departments shall perform related duties.
articles.6: Article 6. Planning committees established by municipal and county-level governments shall: (1) review the city plan, special historic-urban-area plans, major policies and solutions to major issues; (2) review protection lists and amendments; (3) guide and coordinate protection; (4) coordinate major emergencies; and (5) review other major matters referred by the government.
articles.7: Article 7. Each Planning Committee shall establish an expert committee to assess and review protection plans, lists and related matters. Members shall include experts in planning, architecture, property, landscaping, culture, cultural relics, history, folklore, tourism, religion, society and law.
articles.8: Article 8. The municipal government shall establish a protection information system containing geographic, place-name and historic information. District/county governments and municipal planning, cultural-relics, housing and other departments shall collect, manage and update data within their duties and share information to improve digital protection management.
articles.9: Article 9. Governments shall conduct public lectures, reports, expert talks and public experiences to disseminate knowledge and encourage participation. Outstanding contributions shall be recognized. Governments may commission qualified research bodies, industry associations and organizations to conduct research, training and outreach.
articles.10: Article 10. Everyone has a duty to protect the historic city and may stop or report damage. Departments shall promptly investigate and inform the reporter of results.
articles.11: Article 11. Professional protection-volunteer groups are encouraged, and governments shall facilitate public participation and outreach.
articles.12: Article 12. Municipal and county-level governments shall maintain a protection list and file it with the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level.
articles.13: Article 13. The planning authority shall survey historic urban areas and districts, obtain expert review and Planning Committee approval, and submit them to the provincial government for designation.
articles.14: Article 14. The planning authority, together with the cultural-relics authority, shall survey historic character areas, courtyards and buildings, consult relevant parties, obtain expert review and public notice, and submit them for government approval and publication.
articles.15: Article 15. An area with concentrated historic buildings that substantially and completely reflects a period's regional cultural character and has a certain scale may be designated as a historic character area.
articles.16: Article 16. A courtyard retaining abundant remains that substantially and authentically reflects the traditional character, ethnic or local features of a period may be designated as a historic courtyard.
articles.17: Article 17. Criteria for historic buildings shall follow provincial rules. If a historic building is registered as a cultural relic, the cultural-relics authority shall notify the planning authority in writing within 30 days.
articles.18: Article 18. Subjects published by national, provincial, municipal or county-level governments shall be included in the protection list directly. Within 15 days after designation, the municipal government shall publish the list, stating each subject's name, location, purple-line boundary, period of origin and historic value.
articles.19: Article 19. Within 60 days after publication, governments shall install markers at principal entrances to protected cores of historic districts and character areas and at prominent locations on historic courtyards and buildings. Markers shall state the subject's name, number, location, construction date, historic value and cultural information and may be translated into foreign languages. QR codes or similar tools shall facilitate access. No one may alter, damage, install or move a marker without authorization.
articles.20: Article 20. Every five years, governments shall survey heritage resources. Valuable resources shall be designated and listed through statutory procedures. Anyone may propose a resource to the planning authority, which shall conduct preliminary review and proceed with identification if protection value is found.
articles.21: Article 21. The planning authority shall maintain files for listed subjects, with cooperation from relevant parties. Files shall include: (1) survey materials; (2) cultural, artistic and historic features, development, events, notable-person stories and technical data; (3) current use and ownership changes; (4) protection plans; (5) design and survey data; (6) records, drawings, photographs and video from repair, relocation or demolition; and (7) other materials requiring preservation. Anyone may inspect file information as permitted by law.
articles.22: Article 22. Municipal and county-level governments shall prepare the city protection plan and submit it to the provincial government for approval. It shall be incorporated into the city's overall plan.
articles.23: Article 23. Plans shall preserve heritage holistically, maintain traditional layout, character and spatial scale, protect related buildings, streets and green areas, present history and culture and coordinate protection, use and transmission. Special plans for transport, municipal services, landscaping, fire safety and tourism shall align with protection plans.
articles.24: Article 24. Within one year after designation, the planning authority shall prepare plans for the historic urban area, districts, character areas, courtyards and buildings and submit them for government approval and filing with the standing committee of the people's congress. Plans not completed before this Regulation took effect shall be completed within one year after list publication.
articles.25: Article 25. The historic urban-area plan shall preserve traditional layout and character, control historic lanes and view corridors, and manage building height and development intensity.
articles.26: Article 26. A historic-district plan shall meet detailed-planning requirements and: (1) preserve authentic historic remains and sources of historic information; (2) preserve the completeness of historic character and spatial environment; and (3) maintain social continuity, transmit culture, improve infrastructure and housing, and retain vitality. Character-area plans shall follow the same controls.
articles.27: Article 27. A historic-building plan shall identify: (1) the protected area, including core and construction-control zones; (2) character and related environmental features; and (3) protection and use requirements. Courtyard plans shall follow historic-building controls.
articles.28: Article 28. Plans shall comply with laws and national technical requirements and delineate purple lines for historic districts and buildings. Once lawfully delineated, those lines may not be changed without authorization. Plans shall include text, drawings and attachments.
articles.29: Article 29. Before approval, plans shall receive expert review and Planning Committee approval. Drafts shall be public for at least 30 days and comments sought through meetings, hearings or other means. Submissions shall state which comments were adopted and why and include hearing records where relevant.
articles.30: Article 30. Within 30 days after approval, the preparer shall publish the protection plan on government websites and in major news media.
articles.31: Article 31. An approved protection plan may not be amended without authorization. If necessary, the preparer shall submit a special report to the original approving authority and, after consent, submit the revision through the original procedure.
articles.32: Article 32. The municipal government shall coordinate implementation, inspect lower-level governments and departments and periodically assess performance. Problems shall be corrected promptly.
articles.33: Article 33. Municipal and district/county governments shall budget protection funds for emergency rescue of endangered buildings; acquisition or expropriation of historic courtyards and buildings; repair grants for districts, character areas, courtyards and buildings; surveys; awards; and other protection work.
articles.34: Article 34. The municipal finance authority and planning departments shall formulate fund-management rules for government approval. Fund use and management shall be subject to public oversight.
articles.35: Article 35. The municipal government may establish a historic-building protection fund. Its establishment, fundraising, use and management shall follow fund laws and regulations.
articles.36: Article 36. Renewal of the historic urban area shall follow protection plans, strictly control construction intensity and prioritize the public interest by: (1) reasonably planning land use without increasing land except for green space and other public open space; (2) controlling population and improving residents' living conditions; (3) reducing building density and controlling floor area and height; and (4) improving public services, municipal infrastructure and transport.
articles.37: Article 37. Public transport shall be prioritized, including rail transit, bus lanes and transfer hubs, optimized routes and an integrated transit system.
articles.38: Article 38. New construction and expansion are prohibited in a historic-district core except for necessary infrastructure and public services. Such work shall comply with the plan, and the planning authority shall consult cultural-relics departments before issuing permits. Demolition of other buildings or facilities requires joint planning and cultural-relics approval. Dangerous non-historic buildings may be reconstructed or rebuilt under applicable procedures.
articles.39: Article 39. New, altered or expanded buildings in a construction-control zone shall be compatible in height, bulk and color with historic character and comply with protection plans.
articles.40: Article 40. Historic districts and character areas shall retain spatial scale and street alignment and preserve compatible buildings, squares, green areas, utilities and paving. Exterior finishes, colors, public facilities and sculptures in the core shall fit the overall environment.
articles.41: Article 41. Urban renewal shall connect street networks with surrounding areas, improve road structure and parking-transfer facilities, reduce motor vehicles entering or crossing protected areas and create walkable and cycle-friendly streets.
articles.42: Article 42. In the Central Avenue and Daowai Traditional Market districts: (1) street-facing repairs and decoration shall respect historic setting, form, color, style, scale, proportions and quality standards; (2) signs on protected buildings along Central Avenue and Jingyu Street may cover no more than 5% of the facade, and signs on other buildings no more than 8%, without obscuring characteristic features; (3) new street-facing construction in control zones shall continue the Central Avenue and Jingyu Street frontage; and (4) incompatible structures shall be renovated according to a plan.
articles.43: Article 43. Historic courtyards shall preserve traditional buildings, spatial boundaries and scale, roads and green areas, improve necessary infrastructure and services and enhance environmental quality. Incompatible buildings may be removed as part of urban renewal with lawful compensation.
articles.44: Article 44. Historic buildings shall receive categorized protection: Class I may not change the original facade, materials, color, structural system, layout or distinctive interior decoration; Class II may not change facade, materials, color or principal layout; Class III may not change facade, materials or color. The municipal government shall set categories and municipal or county-level governments shall publish designated buildings and file the list with the standing committee of the people's congress.
articles.45: Article 45. Historic buildings shall be preserved in situ. No one may damage, relocate or demolish one without authorization. If public interest makes relocation or demolition necessary, the developer shall prepare a project plan and obtain approval from the provincial authorities through municipal or county-level planning and cultural-relics departments. Class I and II buildings shall be relocated as a whole unless technical or other reasons make this impossible for Class II. After approval, survey and archival records shall be prepared and filed with the planning authority within 30 days.
articles.46: Article 46. When investigating ownership, use and floor area of homes in an expropriation area, the district/county government shall consult the planning authority about whether historic buildings are affected.
articles.47: Article 47. No one may: (1) carve or deface historic buildings or immovable relics; (2) produce or store hazardous substances in their core areas; (3) install exterior features that seriously impair their appearance; (4) install equipment inside them that shortens their service life; or (5) engage in other conduct prohibited by law or protection plans.
articles.48: Article 48. Before approving signs, lighting or awnings on historic buildings or relics; signs or advertising on other buildings in a district; or temporary occupation of roads in a district core, urban-management departments shall consult planning and cultural-relics authorities. Signs shall comply with special plans and coordinate with facades; a building-safety assessment is required if safety may be affected.
articles.49: Article 49. District/county governments shall designate and publish responsible entities for historic districts and character areas. They shall preserve traditional layout, character, decoration, scale and environmental features; inspect routinely and stop harmful conduct; keep the area clean; and assist in maintaining fire and disaster facilities.
articles.50: Article 50. For a state-owned historic courtyard or building, its manager is responsible, or, if unclear, its user, or, if neither is identifiable, an entity designated by the municipal or county-level government. For a non-state-owned property, its owner is responsible, or, if the owner is missing or title unclear, its user, unless the owner and user agree otherwise. If no responsible entity is identifiable, the government shall designate one.
articles.51: Article 51. The planning authority and housing department shall sign a responsibility agreement with the responsible entity. The entity shall retain original height, bulk, appearance and color; preserve layout, character, decoration and environmental features; ensure safety and prevent water, damp and insect damage; mitigate hazards and report them; and keep fire and disaster facilities operational. Transfer or lease contracts shall specify protection and repair duties, and transferors and lessors shall notify transferees and lessees.
articles.52: Article 52. The planning authority and housing department shall conduct annual structural-safety reviews and, after hearing responsible entities, prepare annual repair plans for historic courtyards and buildings.
articles.53: Article 53. A responsible entity shall use a historic courtyard or building consistently with its approved use and carry out maintenance and repair under plans and annual programs at its own expense.
articles.54: Article 54. If a responsible entity capable of repairs refuses to perform its legal duty, the municipal or district/county government may carry out emergency repairs first. If serious failure to repair continues, the local planning authority and housing department may determine this and request entry in the real-property registration file.
articles.55: Article 55. Repair entities shall have required technical capacity and may not damage the property. During historic-building repairs, contractors shall display its protection value and repair illustrations. The municipal government shall separately prescribe repair-management procedures.
articles.56: Article 56. If authorities confirm a historic courtyard or building is at risk and the responsible entity lacks capacity, governments shall provide a grant or carry out emergency reinforcement. The entity may ask the planning authority to have the district/county government or a designated body acquire it. If no request is made and statutory conditions for expropriation are met, it may be expropriated under law.
articles.57: Article 57. For protection needs, governments may negotiate with tenants of state-owned historic courtyards and buildings to terminate leases and recover use rights after reasonable relocation.
articles.58: Article 58. Tourism and cultural-industry projects using historic districts, character areas, courtyards and buildings are encouraged.
articles.59: Article 59. Governments may attract participation through policy guidance, fee reductions and grants. Donations shall be used exclusively for protection. Organizations and individuals may contribute funds, donations, foundations, technical services or leases and equity in buildings.
articles.60: Article 60. Private investors may obtain certain use and revenue rights in state-owned historic buildings without changing state ownership, with conservation rights and duties specified by contract.
articles.61: Article 61. Subject to structural, fire-safety and protection-plan requirements, organizations and individuals may use historic buildings for museums, exhibitions, traditional-culture research or folk businesses and retain operating income.
articles.62: Article 62. Former embassy, railway, church and industrial heritage buildings may host cultural centers or historic-building routes that present city history, provided their protection values are not damaged and their historic value, structure and condition are respected.
articles.63: Article 63. Harbin's characteristic residential buildings and neighborhood settings shall be protected and municipal services improved. Original residents are encouraged to remain and continue traditional ways of life and community continuity.
articles.64: Article 64. Governments, departments and responsible entities shall support regular student visits to museums, exhibitions, art galleries and historic buildings. Schools shall protect heritage formed through their own development and integrate city protection and transmission into curricula, lectures and student activities. Publicly funded heritage institutions and operators shall provide free access and educational opportunities to primary and secondary students and teachers.
articles.65: Article 65. If government personnel fail to supervise, do not investigate violations or otherwise abuse authority, neglect duties or engage in favoritism, the competent authority shall impose discipline.
articles.66: Article 66. Changing a Class I building's facade, materials, color, structure, layout or distinctive interior decoration; changing a Class II building's facade, materials, color or principal layout; or changing a Class III building's facade, materials or color shall result in an order to correct and a fine of RMB 50,000–200,000 by the planning authority.
articles.67: Article 67. If a repair entity lacks technical capacity and damages a historic courtyard or building during work requiring special techniques, the planning authority shall order restoration by a deadline and impose a fine of RMB 100,000–200,000.
articles.68: Article 68. Installing equipment inside a historic building or its ancillary facilities that shortens its service life shall be removed by a deadline. The fine is RMB 20,000–50,000 for an organization or RMB 10,000–20,000 for an individual.
articles.69: Article 69. For purposes of this Regulation: (1) a ‘historic urban area’ is a provincially designated area reflecting the city's development or a period's character, with clear boundaries, many historic buildings and a need for protection; (2) a ‘historic district’ is a provincially designated area with abundant cultural relics and a concentrated group of historic buildings substantially and authentically preserving traditional layout and character; (3) a ‘historic character area’ is a municipal or county-level designated area with a concentrated group of historic buildings that reflect a period's regional character, where relic and historic-building sites cover less than 60%, so it does not yet qualify as a historic district or has not been designated as one; (4) a ‘historic courtyard’ is a municipal or county-level designated courtyard bounded by historic buildings, with clear spatial limits and quality, reflecting traditional local style or historical events and people; (5) a ‘historic building’ is a designated building or structure with protection value that reflects local character but is not designated or registered as an immovable relic; (6) ‘protection plan’ includes plans for the historic city, urban area, districts, character areas, courtyards and buildings; and (7) a ‘purple line’ is the protected-area boundary for historic districts and buildings.
articles.70: Article 70. Where another law or regulation provides for protection and supervision, it applies.
articles.71: Article 71. This Regulation takes effect on 1 June 2020.

FBMCLI.10.1640823.title: Regulations of Jinan Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City

articles.1: To strengthen the protection of the historic and cultural city, pass on its outstanding cultural heritage, improve the living environment and enhance the city's cultural quality, these Regulations are enacted in light of local circumstances and in accordance with the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Shandong Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and other laws and regulations.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to the protection and supervision and administration of the historic and cultural city within the administrative area of this Municipality.
articles.3: Protection of the historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of giving priority to protection, scientific planning, administration in accordance with law, and rational use; preserve its traditional urban pattern, historic character and cultural continuity; and maintain the authenticity and integrity of its cultural heritage.
articles.4: The Municipal People's Government is responsible for protection and supervision and administration of the historic and cultural city. It shall establish a joint-meeting system and an expert review committee for such protection, and coordinate major matters. The people's governments of counties and districts are responsible for protection and supervision and administration within their respective jurisdictions. Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall assist with that work. Villagers' and residents' committees shall cooperate in related protection work.
articles.5: The municipal housing and urban-rural development department, together with the departments of natural resources and planning and cultural relics, is responsible for the specific protection, supervision and administration of famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages, historic and cultural blocks, and historic buildings. The municipal natural resources and planning department is responsible for planning administration for the protection of the historic and cultural city, historic and cultural blocks, traditional-character areas and historic buildings, and shall guide the preparation of protection plans for famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages. The municipal cultural relics department shall guide protection, supervision and administration of immovable cultural relics and underground cultural relic protection areas within the relevant areas. The municipal water affairs department is responsible for protection, planning, implementation and supervision and administration concerning water bodies, famous springs, spring-related cultural landscapes and spring catchment areas. The municipal landscaping and forestry department is responsible for protection of nature reserves, natural parks and ancient and famous trees. The municipal civil affairs department is responsible for protection and supervision and administration of traditional place names. The departments of development and reform, industry and information technology, public security, finance, ecology and environment, urban administration, transport, agriculture and rural affairs, commerce, culture and tourism, emergency management, state-owned assets supervision, market regulation, civil air defense, administrative examination and approval, ethnic and religious affairs, comprehensive administrative law enforcement and other relevant departments shall, within their respective responsibilities, jointly carry out related protection work.
articles.6: The municipal natural resources and planning department shall organize experts from relevant fields to assess protection plans, protection lists and important protection measures within the historic urban area, and provide professional and technical support for administrative decision-making.
articles.7: The municipal and county/district people's governments shall include protection of the historic and cultural city in their respective national economic and social development plans, and include the necessary funding in their fiscal budgets. Such funds may be used for surveys, mapping, designation, emergency rescue, plan preparation, repair, subsidies, awards and academic research, among other purposes.
articles.8: The municipal and county/district people's governments and their relevant departments shall organize public information and education on protection, disseminate relevant knowledge and raise public awareness. Volunteer groups for protection are encouraged, and public participation in protection and outreach shall be encouraged.
articles.9: Units and individuals making outstanding contributions to protection of the historic and cultural city shall be commended and rewarded by the municipal or county/district people's government in accordance with relevant State provisions.
articles.10: Any unit or individual may complain or report conduct violating laws or regulations on protection of the historic and cultural city. The department receiving a complaint or report shall promptly accept it, investigate and handle it.
articles.11: Protected subjects in Jinan's historic and cultural city include: (1) the natural pattern and traditional character of the historic urban area; (2) the Old City, the Weizihao Protection Area and the Commercial Port Area; (3) historic and cultural blocks and traditional-character areas; (4) famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages; (5) historic buildings; and (6) immovable cultural relics, underground cultural relic protection areas, famous springs, mountains, wetlands, ancient and famous trees, traditional place names, industrial heritage and other subjects prescribed by laws and regulations. Where laws or regulations provide otherwise for protection of these resources, those provisions shall prevail.
articles.12: The Municipal People's Government shall establish a system of lists of protected subjects. A subject approved, designated or announced by the State Council or a people's government at provincial, municipal or county level shall be included directly in the protection list. For other subjects proposed for designation by the municipal or county people's government, the competent departments of natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics and other relevant departments shall organize expert assessment; the subject shall be included after the people's government at the corresponding level designates and announces it.
articles.13: A building or structure that is at least 50 years old and has not been designated as a cultural relic protection unit or registered and announced as an immovable cultural relic may be designated as a municipal historic building if it meets any of these conditions: (1) it is associated with an important historical event or person, or has outstanding historical and cultural value representative of Jinan's urban development or construction history or the history of an industry; (2) it substantially reflects architectural characteristics of Jinan or another region and has architectural artistic value in its style or details, or is locally iconic and recognized by the community; (3) its materials, structure or construction techniques reflect the engineering or scientific and technological level of the time, or its form or spatial layout was advanced for its period, demonstrating scientific value; or (4) it is representative industrial heritage, relates to springs, or has other historical and cultural significance. A building or structure 30 or more but less than 50 years old may also be designated if it meets one of those conditions and has exceptional historical, scientific, artistic or social value.
articles.14: An area may be designated as a municipal traditional-character area if it meets any of the following conditions: (1) although not designated as a historic and cultural block, it retains, in a relatively complete and concentrated contiguous area, its traditional pattern, historic character and local features; (2) its traditional streets and lanes are relatively well preserved and buildings along them substantially display traditional character; or (3) it has a relatively dense distribution of springs and distinctive riverside interfaces, spaces, banks or bridges. The protection and administration of such areas shall follow the provisions applicable to historic and cultural blocks.
articles.15: The Municipality shall establish a system of advance protection for potential resources that may qualify as protected subjects, and regularly survey such resources within its jurisdiction. A county/district people's government shall place a town, village, block, building or structure found through a survey or routine administration and assessed by experts as having protection value on an advance-protection list. It shall provide advance protection and give written notice to the owner, user or manager (custodian). If the subject is not added to a protection list within 12 months after receipt of the notice, the advance-protection decision expires automatically. During advance protection, no unit or individual may damage or demolish the subject. The municipal or county/district people's government shall compensate any lawful rights or interests harmed by advance protection.
articles.16: Where the protection level or category of a subject on a protection list or advance-protection list changes, or the subject is seriously damaged or lost and has genuinely lost its protection value, the relevant competent protection department shall promptly propose an adjustment to the list or removal from it.
articles.17: The municipal or county/district people's government shall complete a protection plan within one year after designation and announcement of a famous historic and cultural city, town or village, historic and cultural block, or traditional-character area, and complete a protection and development plan for a traditional village within two years after its designation and announcement. A protection plan for a famous historic and cultural city shall be prepared separately. Plans for famous historic and cultural towns and villages, historic and cultural blocks and traditional-character areas, and protection and development plans for traditional villages, shall be prepared separately in accordance with the city protection plan. Their principal contents shall comply with relevant State and provincial provisions.
articles.18: The key subjects of the protection plan for Jinan's historic and cultural city are: (1) the overall pattern of one core, five corridors and ten clusters, and the integrated character of mountains, springs, lakes, rivers and the city; (2) the historic pattern in which the Old City and Commercial Port Area sit side by side in the east and west of the historic urban area and are linked by the east-west axes of Jinger Road, Jingsi Road, Puli Street, Gongqingtuan Road, Quancheng Road and Jiefang Road, including traditional streets, roads and buildings along those axes; (3) the Old City's walls encircled by a moat, its four gates, its north-south traditional streets and east-west connections, their names, routes and dimensions, the north-south axis from Lixia Pavilion to the former site of the Shandong Governor's Office during the Qianlong Emperor's southern tour, key buildings including the Prefectural School and Confucian Temple, Dragon God Temple, former Shandong Provincial Administration Commission site (including the former examination compound) and City God Temple, as well as Daming Lake's natural and cultural landscapes; (4) the Commercial Port Area's east-west and north-south grid, the overall pattern centered on Zhongshan Park, the traditional character of one park and twelve wards, traditional street names, routes and dimensions, and its distinctive character formed by modern Chinese and foreign buildings; (5) the outer-wall pattern of the Weizihao Protection Area guarding the Old City, north-south roads suited to the higher southern and lower northern terrain and flood diversion, its interconnected historic street network and predominantly traditional buildings, the dense spring-emergence area and water network formed by more than 100 ancient spring pools and channels in the four major spring groups of Baotu, Heihu, Wulongtan and the Pearl Spring, and its urban gardens and characteristic landscape of springs and willows; (6) the historic character and spatial pattern of historic and cultural blocks, including streets, courtyards, buildings, structures, famous spring pools and channels; (7) mutual-view corridors between Qianfo Mountain and the Old City, four view corridors around Daming Lake, view corridors in important scenic areas such as Baotu Spring and Wulongtan Park, and mountain-view corridors for Huashan and Queshan; and (8) other key subjects prescribed by laws, regulations or rules or designated by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.19: A protection plan shall serve as a basis for planning administration and construction. Its preparation, approval and amendment procedures shall comply with laws and regulations.
articles.20: Protection plans for famous historic and cultural cities and towns shall be incorporated into the territorial spatial master plan of the city, county or town, as applicable. Plans for historic and cultural blocks and traditional-character areas shall be incorporated into the regulatory detailed plan for the area. Plans for famous historic and cultural villages and traditional villages shall be incorporated into village plans; where a protection plan is prepared to the same level of detail as a village plan, it may serve as that village's plan. Special plans for roads and transport facilities, municipal utilities, landscaping, sanitation, fire safety, civil air defense and underground-space development that concern protected areas shall be coordinated with the corresponding national economic and social development and territorial spatial plans, and aligned with the protection plans. Before submitting a special plan for approval, its preparer shall seek the views of the development and reform, natural resources and planning, and housing and urban-rural development departments at the same level.
articles.21: The municipal and county natural resources and planning departments shall, together with the cultural relics and housing and urban-rural development departments at the same level, prepare protection guidelines for historic buildings. After expert assessment, the guidelines shall be submitted to the people's government at the corresponding level for designation and announcement. The guidelines shall guide protection and state: (1) the building's name, location and date of construction; (2) its key value-bearing features; (3) its protection category, requirements and suggested uses; (4) its protection area, controls on construction and prohibited uses; and (5) other matters prescribed by laws and regulations. The departments shall provide the guidelines and instructions free of charge to owners, users, managers (custodians) and property service providers.
articles.22: The municipal and county/district people's governments shall strictly implement protection plans and organize their implementation. They shall periodically arrange for relevant competent departments and experts to supervise, inspect and assess implementation of plans and protection of famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages, historic and cultural blocks, traditional-character areas and villages, and historic buildings within their jurisdictions, and promptly correct and address problems found. The county/district people's governments and relevant departments where the historic urban area, protected areas or historic buildings are located shall carry out protection in accordance with the protection lists and plans.
articles.23: Township people's governments and subdistrict offices where famous historic and cultural towns or villages, historic and cultural blocks, traditional-character areas or traditional villages are located shall perform protection duties in accordance with protection plans and shall: (1) receive residents' complaints and suggestions, stop conduct endangering cultural heritage and promptly report it to the relevant administrative departments; (2) assist relevant departments in ensuring the proper operation of public fire-safety and disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; and (3) perform other duties prescribed by these Regulations or determined by the municipal or county/district people's government.
articles.24: The municipal natural resources and planning department shall establish and maintain an information platform for protection of the historic and cultural city, containing geographic, place-name and historic-cultural information. The housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, water affairs, landscaping and forestry, industry and information technology, civil affairs, ethnic and religious affairs, comprehensive administrative law-enforcement and other departments shall collect and enter relevant information within their respective responsibilities and under these Regulations, and promptly share it on the platform. The platform shall publicly disclose protection lists, protection plans for famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages and historic and cultural blocks and traditional-character areas, guidelines for historic buildings, and other relevant information to support protection and appropriate use by enterprises, public institutions, social organizations and individuals.
articles.25: Within the protected areas of famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages and historic and cultural blocks, the following are prohibited: (1) mountain excavation, quarrying, mining or other activities damaging the traditional pattern or historic character; (2) occupation of forest or green land, rivers or lakes, or roads designated for retention in a protection plan; (3) construction of factories, warehouses or other facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; and (4) other conduct prohibited by laws or regulations.
articles.26: Any activity within the protected areas of famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages and historic and cultural blocks that may affect their traditional pattern, historic character, immovable cultural relics or historic buildings shall preserve those features and subjects. A protection plan shall be prepared and required procedures completed in accordance with relevant laws and regulations for: (1) an activity changing the natural condition of forest or green land, rivers or lakes; (2) filming or holding a large-scale public event in a core protected area; and (3) other activities affecting the traditional pattern, historic character, immovable cultural relics or historic buildings.
articles.27: Construction in protected areas of famous historic and cultural towns or villages, historic and cultural blocks, or traditional-character areas shall comply with these requirements: (1) No new construction or expansion may take place in a core protected area of a famous historic and cultural town or village or a historic and cultural block. Where infrastructure or public-service facilities must be newly built or expanded, the developer shall submit a plan consistent with the protection plan. Before issuing a construction-project planning permit or rural construction planning permit, the municipal or county natural resources and planning department shall seek the views of the cultural relics and housing and urban-rural development departments at the same level; expert review and public consultation shall be organized where necessary. (2) To demolish a building, structure or other facility, other than a historic building, in such a core protected area, the developer shall submit a demolition plan consistent with the protection plan. The municipal or county/district housing and urban-rural development department, together with the natural resources and planning and cultural relics departments at the same level, shall approve it; expert review and public consultation shall be organized where necessary. (3) New construction, expansion or similar activity in a construction-control area of a famous historic and cultural town or village or a historic and cultural block shall satisfy the controls set by the protection plan. (4) Construction in a traditional-character area shall satisfy the plan's controls; its height, scale, colors and other features shall harmonize with the historic character and shall not damage the traditional pattern or historic character.
articles.28: Where the layout, environment or historic character of a famous historic and cultural city, town or village, historic and cultural block or traditional-character area has been seriously damaged because of inadequate protection, corrective measures shall be taken in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions. Existing buildings and structures that affect protected view corridors, the natural mountain-and-water pattern or the ecological environment shall gradually be reduced in height or demolished, with compensation provided in accordance with law.
articles.29: The following measures shall be taken to protect traditional place names, immovable cultural relics and historic buildings in the historic urban area: (1) A traditional place name shall not be changed without special circumstances. If change is necessary, the civil affairs and administrative examination and approval departments shall obtain consent from the natural resources and planning department and follow statutory approval and registration procedures; expert review and public consultation shall be organized where necessary. Where a traditional place name has disappeared but the relevant road, street, bridge, embankment, building or structure remains, the civil affairs and administrative examination and approval departments shall, together with the natural resources and planning and cultural relics departments, organize expert review and public consultation and restore the traditional name through statutory procedures. (2) If the user of a state-owned immovable cultural relic fails to perform a repair duty as required by law, the cultural relics department shall order performance. If the owner of a non-state-owned immovable cultural relic is capable of repair but refuses to perform the duty, the cultural relics department may, with approval of the people's government at the same level, organize emergency repair; the owner shall bear the cost. (3) The housing and urban-rural development department, together with the natural resources and planning department, shall prepare, on the principles of prompt rescue, appropriate repair and scientifically sound restoration, plans for emergency rescue, repair and maintenance of historic buildings; after expert assessment, the relevant district people's government shall implement them.
articles.30: The following measures shall protect wall remains, waterways, important roads, spring pools, public green spaces and trees, and construction projects in the Weizihao Protection Area: (1) Site selection and layout for new construction, expansion or alteration shall avoid wall remains and original wall alignments, waterways, and roads or lanes that divert floodwater during rainy seasons. Building forms and colors shall reflect traditional character, and no person may exceed the building height set by the plan. Residential designs are encouraged to leave at least 20 centimeters beside the entrance doorframe for couplets. (2) The water affairs department shall supervise and provide technical guidance on maintenance and repair of famous spring pools and channels and improvement of their cultural surroundings; improve existing Weizihao waterways and banks; and, together with the natural resources and planning, cultural relics, and housing and urban-rural development departments, organize expert assessment and, after approval by the Municipal People's Government, gradually reconnect the Weizihao water system. (3) The landscaping and forestry department shall plan and improve public green spaces, using existing terrain, landforms, water bodies and historic sites and prioritizing local plant species to reflect traditional garden styles. It shall survey and register ancient and famous trees and other rare, precious, historically valuable, commemorative or mature trees of notable landscape scale. (4) Other measures decided by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.31: Historic buildings shall receive graded protection in accordance with their protection guidelines. The person responsible for protection shall be determined as follows: (1) for a state-owned building, its manager (custodian) is responsible; if there is none, its user is responsible; if neither is clear, the municipal or county people's government shall designate a responsible person; (2) for a non-state-owned building, its owner is responsible; if the owner cannot be located or title is unclear, the actual user or manager (custodian) is responsible. The owner may agree with the actual user or manager (custodian) on allocation of protection duties but neither may thereby avoid their respective duties; and (3) if no owner, user or manager (custodian) can be identified, the municipal or county people's government where the building is located shall designate a responsible person.
articles.32: A system assigning protection responsibility shall apply to historic buildings, specifying protection duties and rights such as eligibility for subsidies. For a state-owned historic building, the municipal or county/district housing and urban-rural development department shall sign a protection-responsibility agreement with the responsible person. For a non-state-owned building, it may do so.
