articles.33: A county/district people's government shall establish an annual structural-safety inspection system for historic buildings, assess repair needs and, after hearing the responsible person's views, prepare an annual repair plan. The county/district housing and urban-rural development department shall notify the responsible person to repair the building according to that plan, and the responsible person shall carry out the repair as required.
articles.34: A responsible person who maintains or repairs a historic building in accordance with its protection guidelines may apply for a subsidy from the municipal or county/district people's government, which may grant one from protection funds. The Municipal People's Government shall separately formulate and publish detailed subsidy measures. The municipal and county/district housing and urban-rural development and natural resources and planning departments shall provide free technical guidance and services for emergency rescue, repair and maintenance needed for protection.
articles.35: No unit or individual may: (1) relocate or demolish a historic building without authorization; (2) store flammable, explosive or corrosive materials in a way that endangers its safety; (3) carve or write on, or deface, a historic building; or (4) otherwise damage a historic building.
articles.36: A construction project shall avoid historic buildings. If special circumstances make avoidance impossible, protection at the original site shall be implemented to the greatest extent possible. Before such protection, the developer shall determine protective measures and submit a plan consistent with the protection plan to the municipal or county natural resources and planning department for approval, together with the cultural relics and housing and urban-rural development departments at the same level.
articles.37: Where construction for the public interest makes protection of a historic building at its original site impossible and relocation for protection elsewhere or demolition necessary, the developer shall submit a relocation or demolition plan consistent with the protection plan. It shall be submitted by the municipal or county/district housing and urban-rural development department, together with the natural resources and planning and cultural relics departments at the same level, to the provincial housing and urban-rural development department for approval together with the provincial cultural relics department. The developer shall include the costs of in-situ protection, relocation or demolition in the construction-project budget.
articles.38: External repair or decoration of a historic building, addition of facilities, or alteration of its structure or use shall be approved by the municipal or county/district housing and urban-rural development department together with the natural resources and planning and cultural relics departments at the same level, and the procedures prescribed by relevant laws and regulations shall be completed.
articles.39: The municipal and county natural resources and planning departments shall establish historic-building archives together with the housing and urban-rural development departments at the same level. Each archive shall include: (1) architectural, historical and construction-period characteristics and rarity; (2) protection guidelines; (3) current use and changes in ownership; (4) written, graphic, photographic and video records produced during repair, decoration, relocation or demolition; (5) survey and mapping records and related materials; and (6) other materials requiring preservation. The responsible person shall cooperate with archival surveys and mapping.
articles.40: As required by protection plans, the municipal and county/district people's governments shall give priority to arranging for relevant departments to build and improve roads, water supply and drainage, electricity, sanitation and fire-safety infrastructure in protected areas of the historic urban area, historic and cultural blocks and traditional-character areas. Where protection needs make it impossible to comply with current technical standards and specifications in a core protected area of a historic and cultural block or traditional-character area, the competent departments for fire safety, housing and urban-rural development, transport, water affairs, cultural relics, ecology and environment, natural resources and planning, urban administration, civil air defense and earthquake administration shall, within their respective responsibilities and with respect for history, formulate corresponding safeguards and implement them after expert review.
articles.41: The municipal and county/district transport departments shall, together with the natural resources and planning and cultural relics departments at the same level, scientifically and appropriately design traffic conditions for existing road networks in the historic urban area, historic and cultural blocks and traditional-character areas, improving circulation and traffic distribution. Their streets and lanes shall be designed to accommodate non-motorized traffic and pedestrians.
articles.42: Within three months after approval of a protection plan, signs for famous historic and cultural towns and villages and historic and cultural blocks shall be installed at principal entrances to their core protected areas. Signs for historic buildings shall be installed within six months after publication of the protection list. A sign shall state the protected subject's name, number, location, period of existence, protection category and historical value, and may be translated into foreign languages as needed. Markers shall also be installed, at the original site or nearby, to display historical information about important ancient waterways, buildings or courtyards, the seven gates and walls of the Old City (inner city), the twelve gates and walls of the Weizihao outer city, and surviving ancient city gates such as Huibo Gate, in accordance with city-protection and heritage-transmission requirements. The Municipal People's Government shall prescribe a uniform design, and county/district people's governments shall arrange installation. No unit or individual may falsely use the designation of a famous historic and cultural city, town or village or historic and cultural block, or unauthorizedly install, move, alter or damage a sign.
articles.43: Outdoor advertisements, plaques and signs, lighting equipment, cables and other external facilities installed within a protected area delineated by a protection plan shall harmonize with the overall character of that area.
articles.44: Use of famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages, historic and cultural blocks, and traditional-character areas shall give priority to protection and allow appropriate use. Spaces shall be used for living or business as appropriate, through gradual improvement and small-scale renewal, with attention to preserving overall character and controlling the intensity of commercial development.
articles.45: Protection and use of famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages, historic and cultural blocks, traditional-character areas and historic buildings shall safeguard the lawful rights and interests of original residents and encourage their participation. Original residents are encouraged to operate local characteristic industries and related activities, improve their living and working conditions, and sustain the original form and way of life of the protected places. They are encouraged to continue living there and to participate in protection, use and development through contributions of housing, funds or other means, and to receive reasonable returns. The municipal and county/district people's governments shall provide corresponding compensation where protection affects original residents' normal lives or production activities.
articles.46: Sustainable and rational use of the cultural resources of famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages, historic and cultural blocks and traditional-character areas is encouraged, as are local traditional handicrafts, distinctive products and activities that pass on and use intangible cultural heritage. Tourism development in these areas shall comply with laws, regulations and the relevant protection plan, and preserve their distinctive historic character.
articles.47: Citizens, legal persons and other organizations are encouraged and supported in exploring, collecting, organizing and researching traditional culture, arts, folk customs and arts and crafts. In accordance with relevant provisions, they may establish venues in protected areas of famous historic and cultural cities, towns and villages and historic and cultural blocks, and in traditional-character areas, to present, promote and pass on representative items of intangible cultural heritage. Development of cultural industries related to intangible cultural heritage is encouraged.
articles.48: Units and individuals are encouraged, supported and guided, subject to relevant protection requirements, to make rational use of historic buildings for displaying cultural heritage; developing cultural tourism and local cultural research; establishing museums, exhibition halls, memorial halls and traditional workshops; and conducting commercial, homestay and other activities. Such use shall be compatible with the building's historical value and interior structure, comply with its protection guidelines and applicable fire-safety standards and specifications, and shall not unauthorizedly alter its main structure, principal floor plan or appearance or endanger the building or its ancillary facilities.
articles.49: The municipal and county/district people's governments may protect and make use of non-state-owned historic buildings through purchase, exchange of property rights and other means. Social investment in protection and use is encouraged through policy guidance, fee reductions, subsidies and other measures. Units and individuals are encouraged to participate by investing or donating funds, establishing funds, providing technical services, or leasing or contributing buildings or structures as equity. Bearers of representative intangible cultural heritage items are supported in passing on and displaying intangible cultural heritage in historic and cultural blocks, immovable cultural relics and historic buildings; funding, simplified procedures, fee reductions and other measures may encourage them to acquire historic buildings.
articles.50: The municipal and county/district people's governments may promote rational use of historic buildings through policy guidance, financial support, simplified procedures and technical guidance, and may also encourage rational use of state-owned historic buildings by reducing rent or granting development-rights incentives.
articles.51: The municipal and county/district people's governments shall organize, encourage and promote comprehensive and multi-level academic research on Jinan's history and culture, and publicize and promote the rich and diverse cultural character of Jinan as a historic and cultural city.
articles.52: Where laws or administrative regulations already prescribe legal liability for conduct violating these Regulations, those provisions shall apply.
articles.53: Where a municipal or county/district people's government, a department responsible for protecting or supervising and administering the historic and cultural city, or its staff commits any of the following acts, the responsible persons shall be disciplined in accordance with law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued: (1) failing to organize preparation of a protection plan or failing to follow the statutory procedure; (2) revising a protection plan without authorization; (3) failing to perform approval duties in accordance with the protection plan or statutory procedures; (4) failing to perform protection, supervision or administration duties as required by law, resulting in a famous historic and cultural city, town, village or historic and cultural block being issued a warning or stripped of its designation; or (5) abusing powers, neglecting duties, engaging in favoritism or committing other misconduct.
articles.54: Where, in a protected area of a famous historic and cultural city, town or village, a person commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations, the municipal or county natural resources and planning department, together with the housing and urban-rural development department and other relevant departments at the same level, shall order the violation to stop and require restoration to the original state or other remedial measures within a prescribed time. Illegal gains, if any, shall be confiscated by the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department. If restoration or other remedies are not completed by the deadline, the natural resources and planning department may appoint a capable entity to carry them out at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 500,000 but not more than RMB 1 million on a unit, or not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000 on an individual. Losses shall be compensated in accordance with law. The prohibited acts are: (1) excavating mountains, quarrying, mining or otherwise damaging the traditional pattern or historic character; (2) occupying forest or green land, rivers or lakes, or roads designated for retention in a protection plan; (3) constructing factories, warehouses or other facilities for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; or (4) other conduct prohibited by laws or regulations.
articles.55: A person who stores flammable, explosive or corrosive materials in a way that endangers a historic building, in violation of these Regulations, shall be ordered to correct the violation by the municipal or county/district housing and urban-rural development department and fined not less than RMB 2,000 but not more than RMB 20,000 by the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department. Losses shall be compensated in accordance with law.
articles.56: A person who damages, unauthorizedly relocates or demolishes a historic building in violation of these Regulations shall be ordered by the municipal or county/district housing and urban-rural development department, together with the natural resources and planning department at the same level, to stop the violation and restore the original state or take other remedial measures within a prescribed time. Illegal gains shall be confiscated by the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department. If the deadline is missed, the housing and urban-rural development department may appoint a capable entity to carry out the restoration or other remedies at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000 on a unit, or not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000 on an individual. Losses shall be compensated in accordance with law.
articles.57: Where, without approval and in violation of these Regulations, a person commits either of the following acts, the municipal or county/district housing and urban-rural development department, together with the natural resources and planning department at the same level, shall order the violation to stop and require restoration to the original state or other remedial measures within a prescribed time. Illegal gains shall be confiscated by the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department. If the deadline is missed, the housing and urban-rural development department may appoint a capable entity to carry out the restoration or other remedies at the violator's expense. If serious consequences result, the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000 on a unit, or not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000 on an individual. Losses shall be compensated in accordance with law: (1) demolishing a building, structure or other facility, other than a historic building, in the core protected area of a famous historic and cultural town or village or a historic and cultural block; or (2) externally repairing or decorating a historic building, adding facilities, or changing its structure or use. A unit or individual undertaking an activity specified in Article 26, or an activity under the first paragraph of this Article with approval, shall be punished under that paragraph if the activity nevertheless causes destructive effects on the traditional pattern, historic character or a historic building.
articles.58: A person who falsely uses the designation of a famous historic and cultural city, town or village, or historic and cultural block, in violation of these Regulations shall be ordered to correct the violation within a prescribed time by the municipal or county natural resources and planning department together with the housing and urban-rural development department at the same level. If the person fails to do so by the deadline, the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000.
articles.59: A person who unauthorizedly installs, moves, alters or damages a sign for a historic and cultural block, famous historic and cultural town or village, in violation of these Regulations, shall be ordered to correct the violation within a prescribed time by the municipal or county natural resources and planning department together with the housing and urban-rural development department at the same level. If the person fails to do so by the deadline, the comprehensive administrative law-enforcement department shall fine a unit not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and an individual not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.60: For purposes of these Regulations, the “one core” means the central urban area centered on the historic urban area and its surroundings. The “five corridors” are cultural-heritage corridors within the Municipality: the Jiaoji Railway, Xiaoqing River, Yufu River, Xiujiang River and Yellow River cultural-heritage corridors. The “ten clusters” are heritage-concentration areas: Hongfanquan Village; Yushan transport town; Fangyu village stockade; Lingyan Temple springs-and-tea heritage; cliff sculptures; ancient architecture at Huashan and Huayang Palace; Yuntai Temple springs and temple views; Sanjianxi and Baimai Springs; the former Zhangqiu City at Xianggongzhuang Town; and Zhujiayu ancient village. The historic urban area's boundaries, as determined in Jinan's historic-city protection plan, are Lishan Road to the east, Jingshi Road to the south, Weishi'er Road to the west and the Jiaoji Railway to the north, covering 18.6 square kilometers. The Old City is the area enclosed by the moat. The Commercial Port Area is bounded by Weiyi Road to the east, Jingsi Road to the south, Weishi'er Road to the west and the Jiaoji Railway to the north. The Weizihao Protection Area is bounded by Lishan Road to the east, a line 50 meters south of Wenhua West Road to the south, Shunhe Street to the west, and Minghu North Road and Minghu East Road to the north. The Furong Street–Baihuazhou Historic and Cultural Block is bounded by the line of Xianxi Lane, Zhenchi Street, Yuanqian Street and Xigengdao Street to the east; Quancheng Road and the south side of Qushuiting Street to the south; Gongyuanqianggen Street to the west; and Daming Lake Road to the north. The Jiangjunmiao Historic and Cultural Block is bounded by Bianzhi Lane to the east, Quancheng Road to the south, Taipingsi Street and Xichenggen Street to the west, and Daming Lake Road to the north. The Shandong University West Campus (former Cheeloo University) Historic and Cultural Block includes the university's Baotuquan Campus and Qilu Hospital: its boundaries are Baotuquan South Road and the west boundary of Shandong University No. 1 Affiliated Primary School to the east; Jingshi Road to the south; Xishuanglong Street and Guangchang West Ditch to the west; and the southern boundary of Jinan Finance School to the north. The One Park and Twelve Wards Traditional-Character Area is bounded by Weisan Road to the east, Jingsi Road to the south, Weiba Road to the west and Tonghui Street to the north. The eight gates of the Old City (inner city) are the east gate (Qichuan Gate), south gate (Lishan Gate), west gate (Luoquan Gate), north gate (Huibo Gate), new east gate (Xunli Gate), new south gate (Kunshun Gate), new west gate (Qianjian Gate) and new north gate (Genji Gate). The twelve gates of the Weizihao outer city are Ji'an, Haiyan, Yongjing, Xun'an, Yonggu, Zhongshan, Dai'an, Xinjian, Yongsui, Linxiang, Puli and Yongzhen Gates.
articles.61: These Regulations shall take effect on 1 October 2020.

FBMCLI.10.1687579.title: Measures of Beijing Municipality for the Protection of the Historical and Cultural Landmark of Beijing (2021)

articles.1: To strengthen protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city, pass on the city's historical continuity, improve the living environment, and coordinate cultural heritage protection and use with urban and rural development, these Regulations are enacted in light of local circumstances and in accordance with relevant laws and administrative regulations.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city and related activities.
articles.3: Protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of scientific planning, classified administration, strict protection, rational use, joint governance and shared benefits, and regional coordination. It shall preserve the authenticity of cultural heritage, integrity of historic character, continuity of social life and diversity of urban functions; sustain historical and cultural depth; promote the integration of outstanding culture with modern life; and preserve the people's memories and feelings associated with Beijing's history and culture.
articles.4: The Municipality shall establish and improve a working mechanism for protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city under the leadership of the Party committee, with government-wide coordination, implementation by relevant entities, public participation and social oversight. Major matters concerning such protection shall be reviewed by the Capital Planning and Construction Commission and reported to the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council as required.
articles.5: The Municipal People's Government is responsible for protection of the historic and cultural city. It shall incorporate such protection into the Municipality's national economic and social development plans and programs, coordinate funding, improve institutions, mechanisms and policy safeguards, and advance World Heritage nominations and protection and development of the historic and cultural city. A district people's government is responsible for protection within its administrative area and shall include it in its own development plans and programs and perform its duties concerning protection, use and improvement of people's livelihoods. Subdistrict offices and township people's governments shall conduct inspections in their areas and mobilize and guide public participation. Residents' and villagers' committees shall assist them with related protection work.
articles.6: The Beijing Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee is responsible for overall planning, coordination, advancement and oversight of protection work and shall be incorporated into the work system of the Capital Planning and Construction Commission. The municipal planning and natural resources department shall handle the Committee's routine work. The Committee shall establish an expert advisory mechanism to provide review, assessment, consultation and other services on major protection matters.
articles.7: The planning and natural resources department is responsible for planning administration for protection of the historic and cultural city, historic and cultural blocks, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages and historic buildings. The housing and urban-rural development department shall provide technical guidance and services for repair of historic buildings and of buildings and structures other than cultural relics within historic and cultural blocks and famous towns. The cultural relics department shall implement World Heritage nominations and guide and supervise protection and administration of revolutionary sites and other protection work prescribed by laws and regulations. The agriculture and rural affairs department shall guide protection and development of famous historic and cultural villages and traditional villages. Other relevant departments shall carry out protection within their respective responsibilities.
articles.8: Protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city is a shared responsibility of all society. Every unit and individual has a duty to protect it and may comment on or make suggestions concerning preparation and implementation of protection plans, and supervise and report conduct damaging it.
articles.9: The Municipality shall establish mechanisms for raising protection funds from multiple sources. Funds shall be used for surveys and designation of protected subjects, protection and repair, emergency rescue, environmental improvement, infrastructure, academic research and planning and design, education and training, archaeology, and protection and use under these Regulations. Sources include: (1) protection funds allocated in the municipal and district fiscal budgets; (2) social donations; (3) proceeds from transfer, mortgage or lease of state-owned buildings associated with the historic and cultural city; and (4) other funds raised lawfully.
articles.10: Units and individuals are encouraged to participate in protection and use, designation of listed subjects, public education, preparation of plans and other protection work through donations, sponsorship, volunteer services and other means. Units and individuals making outstanding contributions may be commended or rewarded by the municipal or district people's government or relevant competent department in accordance with State and municipal provisions.
articles.11: Public education on protection is encouraged through public lectures, special reports, expert talks, immersive experiences and other formats to raise awareness. Schools are supported in providing practical education related to protection of the historic and cultural city.
articles.12: The Municipality shall strengthen cooperation with Tianjin, Hebei Province and surrounding areas and advance development of a Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei system for protecting historic and cultural cities.
articles.13: The area of Beijing's historic and cultural city covers the entire Municipality and primarily includes the Old City, the Three Hills and Five Gardens area, and the Grand Canal, Great Wall, and Xishan-Yongding River cultural belts (collectively, the three cultural belts).
articles.14: Protected subjects of Beijing's historic and cultural city include: (1) World Heritage properties; (2) cultural relics; (3) historic buildings and revolutionary sites; (4) historic and cultural blocks, distinctive areas and underground cultural relic burial areas; (5) famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages; (6) historic rivers, lakes and water-related cultural heritage; (7) mountain-and-water patterns and remains of city sites; (8) traditional hutongs, historic streets and lanes, and traditional place names; (9) scenic areas, historic gardens, and ancient and famous trees; (10) intangible cultural heritage; and (11) other subjects prescribed by laws and regulations. Historic buildings include outstanding modern-era buildings, industrial heritage, courtyards designated for protection, and former residences or homes of notable people. Where laws or administrative regulations set designation criteria for a subject listed above, those criteria shall apply. Otherwise, the Beijing Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee shall organize relevant departments to formulate designation criteria for subjects within their respective responsibilities.
articles.15: Protected subjects shall be protected as a whole through connected routes and contiguous areas. Controls shall also apply to surrounding traditional character and spatial environment, including building heights and forms, view corridors, ecological landscapes and other related elements.
articles.16: Protection of the Old City covers the area inside and including the moat and its remains of Beijing's Ming and Qing period city. The Municipality shall strengthen holistic protection, focusing on the traditional historic character and spatial pattern formed by: (1) the traditional central axis and Chang'an Avenue; (2) the convex-shaped city outline; (3) the Ming and Qing Imperial City; (4) historic rivers, lakes and water-related cultural heritage; (5) traditional hutongs, historic streets and lanes, and traditional place names; (6) the hutong-siheyuan courtyard-house form; (7) a low-rise, open spatial form; (8) view corridors and street vistas; (9) traditional architectural colors and forms; (10) ancient and famous trees and large trees; and (11) altars, temples and other related remains.
articles.17: Protection of the Three Hills and Five Gardens area covers cultural heritage from different historical periods, represented by the Qing imperial gardens in Beijing's northwestern suburbs. Key subjects are: (1) classical gardens; (2) the landscape pattern in which mountains and water complement each other; (3) historic rivers, lakes and water-related cultural heritage; (4) ancient villages, roads and traditional place names; (5) important modern-era sites of education and dissemination; (6) revolutionary sites; (7) paddy-field landscapes; and (8) other related remains.
articles.18: The three cultural belts shall give priority to protecting: (1) the Grand Canal from the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties; (2) the Great Wall from all historical periods; (3) areas of concentrated cultural resources along the Xishan-Yongding River; and (4) ancient villages, roads, mountain-and-water patterns and other protected subjects along the Grand Canal, Great Wall and Xishan-Yongding River.
articles.19: The relevant districts shall strengthen protection institutions for the historic and cultural city, improve mechanisms and staffing, and enhance coordination and implementation of protection in the Old City, the Three Hills and Five Gardens area and other key areas within their jurisdictions.
articles.20: In accordance with the annual work plan of the Beijing Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee, district people's governments shall organize surveys of historic buildings and revolutionary sites; historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages and traditional villages; historic rivers and lakes; traditional hutongs; historic streets and lanes; historic gardens; and other protected subjects.
articles.21: Protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city shall use a system of protection lists. Based on survey results, a district people's government shall organize expert assessment, prepare a preliminary list under relevant designation criteria, and make it public for at least 30 days. After the public-comment period, it shall submit the preliminary list, expert opinions and comment results to the Beijing Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee for review. Any unit or individual may nominate or recommend a protected subject to the district people's government where it is located. If a subject meets designation criteria but is omitted from the preliminary list, the Committee may recommend its inclusion to the district people's government; if it is still omitted, the Committee may directly recommend to the Municipal People's Government that it be included in the protection list.
articles.22: The Beijing Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee shall review materials submitted by district people's governments, prepare the protection list and submit it to the Municipal People's Government for approval and publication.
articles.23: If a protected subject is damaged or lost due to force majeure, or its protection level or category changes, the district people's government where it is located shall propose an adjustment to the protection list and submit it for approval through the original approval procedure.
articles.24: If a subject not yet included in a protection list is preliminarily found by a district people's government to have protection value, the district shall designate it as an advance-protection subject and, within seven working days after designation, notify its owner and user of the protective measures to be taken. No unit or individual may damage, unauthorizedly relocate or demolish an advance-protection subject. Within two months after issuing the notice, the district shall recommend to the Beijing Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee that the subject be included in the protection list. Within two months after receiving the recommendation, the Committee shall submit it to the Municipal People's Government for approval and publication. If the subject is not included by the deadline, the advance-protection notice expires automatically.
articles.25: The protection-planning system for Beijing's historic and cultural city includes a citywide protection plan; protection plans for the Old City, the Three Hills and Five Gardens area, historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages; and protection and development plans for traditional villages. Planning authorities shall prepare such plans in an orderly manner and incorporate them as special plans into the territorial spatial plan at the corresponding level. A traditional-village protection and development plan may be combined with the village plan.
articles.26: The protection plan for Beijing's historic and cultural city shall state the protected area, overall objectives, protection subjects, protection requirements and safeguards, among other matters.
articles.27: Plans for protection of the Old City, the Three Hills and Five Gardens area, historic and cultural blocks and famous towns and villages, and plans for protection and development of traditional villages, shall include: (1) protected areas and protection principles; (2) areas of urban and rural construction land and their designated uses under territorial spatial planning; (3) population capacity; (4) buildings, structures and surrounding historic environmental elements requiring protection; (5) controls on building height, scale, colors and other features of traditional character; (6) classification of buildings for protection and improvement measures; (7) protection and use measures and improvements to the living environment; (8) specific measures to implement the plan; and (9) other required matters. Protected areas of historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages, and traditional villages shall include core protected areas and construction-control areas.
articles.28: Protection plans shall be prepared as follows: (1) the municipal planning and natural resources department shall prepare plans for Beijing's historic and cultural city, the Old City and the Three Hills and Five Gardens area; (2) the district people's government where located shall prepare plans for historic and cultural blocks and famous towns and villages; and (3) the township people's government where located shall prepare protection and development plans for traditional villages. Before submitting a draft for approval, the preparing authority shall publish it for public comment in accordance with law and fully solicit expert and public views for at least 30 days.
articles.29: Protection plans shall be approved and filed as follows: (1) plans for Beijing's historic and cultural city, the Old City and the Three Hills and Five Gardens area shall be reviewed by the Beijing Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee, approved by the Municipal People's Government and filed with the Standing Committee of the Municipal People's Congress; the citywide plan shall also be filed with the relevant State Council department in accordance with law; (2) plans for historic and cultural blocks and famous towns and villages shall be reviewed by the municipal planning and natural resources and cultural relics departments and approved by the Municipal People's Government; and (3) traditional-village protection and development plans shall be reviewed by the municipal planning and natural resources and agriculture and rural affairs departments, approved by the district people's government, and filed with the district people's congress standing committee and the municipal planning and natural resources and agriculture and rural affairs departments. Each plan shall be published to the public through public media within 30 days after approval.
articles.30: A protection plan approved in accordance with law shall not be amended without authorization. If amendment is necessary, the authority that prepared it shall submit a special report to the original approval authority and may prepare an amendment only after consent. The amended plan shall be submitted for approval and filing through the original procedures.
articles.31: Based on protection plans, the municipal planning and natural resources department, together with relevant departments, shall prepare integrated planning and implementation plans for construction projects in historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages, traditional villages, contiguous traditional one-story residential areas and distinctive areas. These plans shall cover design requirements, land title, planning indicators, municipal utilities and transport, implementation schedule, functions and business uses, character controls, investors and project quotas, protection and renewal models, housing arrangements and other matters.
articles.32: The Municipal People's Government shall incorporate health-check and assessment of historic and cultural city protection into the Municipality's territorial spatial planning review and shall promptly correct and address problems found.
articles.33: Protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city shall use a system assigning protection responsibility. Responsible persons are: (1) the district people's government where the Old City, the Three Hills and Five Gardens area or one of the three cultural belts is located; (2) the subdistrict office or township people's government where a historic and cultural block, famous town or village, or traditional village is located; (3) the owner of a historic building, or, if the owner cannot be located or ownership is unclear, its user; (4) a separately established protection-management entity, if any; or (5) a responsible person designated by the common higher-level people's government for a subject crossing administrative boundaries. The municipal or district people's government shall designate a responsible person where none can otherwise be identified. After publication of the protection list, the district people's government shall notify each responsible person of the duties to be performed.
articles.34: The district people's government where the Old City is located shall: (1) prevent damage to all protected subjects and contiguous traditional one-story residential areas and ensure that all eligible subjects receive protection; (2) facilitate relocation of occupants from key cultural relics and historic buildings, strengthen protection of cultural relics and improvement of surrounding areas, and promote appropriate public access and use; (3) protect and organically renew historic and cultural blocks and contiguous traditional one-story residential areas, strictly control construction scale and building height, and preserve traditional character; and (4) adopt policies and measures to optimize the Old City's urban functions and improve infrastructure, public services and the living environment.
articles.35: A district people's government where the Three Hills and Five Gardens area is located shall: (1) protect the natural historic character of the mountain, water and agricultural landscape as a whole; (2) strictly control construction scale and building heights and protect view corridors and spatial patterns; and (3) gradually improve the environment, restore ecosystems and reestablish large areas of green space.
articles.36: A district people's government where one of the three cultural belts is located shall: (1) protect World Heritage properties and cultural relics along the belt; (2) protect and restore its mountain, water, forest, field, lake and grassland ecosystems; (3) research and display its historical, cultural and landscape value; and (4) support related cultural industries and improve the living environment in towns and villages along the belt. The Municipal People's Government shall establish a cross-district coordination mechanism for protection and use of the three cultural belts.
articles.37: Under the leadership of the district people's government, subdistrict offices and township people's governments shall implement protection of historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages and traditional villages in their areas. Their duties are to: (1) preserve the integrity of historic patterns, street and lane layouts, traditional character, spatial scale and historic environmental elements; (2) conduct routine inspections, promptly address conduct endangering protected subjects and report it to competent departments; (3) carry out protection, renewal and living-environment improvements; and (4) assist relevant departments with safety and disaster prevention.
articles.38: Owners and users of historic buildings shall: (1) maintain and repair them routinely, preserving their original historic pattern and traditional character; (2) ensure building safety and normal operation of disaster-prevention facilities and equipment, promptly address safety hazards or emergencies, and report them to competent departments; and (3) when transferring, leasing or lending a historic building, agree in writing with the transferee, lessee or user on each party's protection responsibilities. The real-property registration authority shall promptly notify the district people's government where the building is located of registration information concerning its title.
articles.39: Within protected areas of historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages, and traditional villages, the following activities that may destructively affect protected subjects are prohibited: (1) mountain excavation, quarrying, mining or other activities damaging traditional patterns or historic character; (2) occupying gardens, green spaces, rivers, lakes or roads designated for retention in a protection plan; (3) building factories or warehouses for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; (4) carving or defacing historic buildings; (5) construction exceeding controls on building height or floor-area ratio or violating controls on building scale, colors or other features; (6) unauthorized demolition of existing buildings; and (7) damaging historic patterns, street and lane layouts or traditional character prescribed in a protection plan.
articles.40: In core protected areas of historic and cultural blocks and famous towns and villages, no new construction, alteration or expansion may take place except for necessary municipal infrastructure or public-service facilities or restoration of historic character in accordance with a protection plan. Such necessary works and restoration shall strictly preserve historic patterns, street and lane layouts and traditional character. Use of traditional craftspeople, techniques and materials is encouraged to the greatest extent possible. In core protected areas of traditional villages, new construction, alteration or expansion shall not change historic patterns, street and lane layouts or traditional character; repairs to building exteriors shall use traditional techniques and materials to the greatest extent possible.
articles.41: New construction, alteration or expansion of buildings or structures in construction-control areas of historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages, or traditional villages shall satisfy controls in the protection plan. Building heights, scale, colors, floor-area ratio and other parameters shall be strictly controlled and shall harmonize with the character of the core protected area.
articles.42: Within protected areas of historic and cultural blocks and famous towns, any new construction, alteration, expansion or demolition of an existing building, or change to an existing building's exterior, roof or structure, requires a planning permit from the planning and natural resources department and submission of a protection-design plan. Before issuing the permit, that department shall seek the views of the housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments at the same level. Within protected areas of famous historic and cultural villages and traditional villages, such work shall obtain a planning permit or approval from the planning and natural resources department or township people's government as required; before granting it, that authority shall seek the views of the district agriculture and rural affairs and cultural relics departments.
articles.43: When constructing, altering or expanding buildings or structures in contiguous traditional one-story residential areas or distinctive areas using new materials, technologies or modern design methods as permitted by protection requirements, attention shall be paid to preserving historic patterns, street and lane layouts and traditional character.
articles.44: Improvements to ventilation and natural lighting, energy conservation and insulation, water supply and drainage, sanitation and other living conditions within protected areas of historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages, traditional villages, contiguous traditional one-story residential areas and distinctive areas shall satisfy character controls and public-safety requirements.
articles.45: To address buildings, structures or other facilities that endanger the safety of immovable cultural relics or historic buildings; damage the historic patterns, street and lane layouts, traditional character or spatial environment of the Old City, the Three Hills and Five Gardens area, protected historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages or traditional villages; fail to meet a protection plan's requirements for building height, form or view corridors; or seriously affect residential safety, the district people's government where they are located or the property-owning entity may organize occupant relocation or renovation by lawful means, including voluntary lease-back applications, housing exchange or expropriation. The Municipal People's Government shall formulate detailed measures.
articles.46: The municipal planning and natural resources department shall, together with the municipal housing and urban-rural development, agriculture and rural affairs, cultural relics, and economic and information technology departments, prepare protection guidelines for historic buildings, covering basic information, historical value, character, protection areas and recommendations. Based on those guidelines, the municipal housing and urban-rural development department shall, with relevant departments, prepare technical standards for repair of buildings and structures other than cultural relics within historic-building protection areas and protected areas of historic and cultural blocks and famous towns. The municipal agriculture and rural affairs department shall, with relevant departments, prepare technical standards for repair of historic buildings and buildings and structures other than cultural relics within protected areas of famous historic and cultural villages and traditional villages.
articles.47: To maintain or repair a historic building, its protection-responsible person shall prepare a protection-design plan in accordance with the building's protection guidelines and repair technical standards and obtain approval from the district planning and natural resources department. Based on the approved design plan, the person shall prepare a construction plan and obtain approval from the district housing and urban-rural development department. Routine maintenance and repairs that do not involve features, materials, structures or decoration embodying historic character are exempt. The responsible person shall perform the work in accordance with the approved plans. A district people's government may provide funding or other subsidies for compliant maintenance and repair, and its housing and urban-rural development department shall provide technical guidance.
articles.48: If a historic building that can be maintained or repaired is at risk of damage and its responsible person refuses to perform the maintenance or repair duties, the district housing and urban-rural development department shall take measures to eliminate the danger, and the responsible person shall bear the costs.
articles.49: No unit or individual may damage, unauthorizedly relocate or demolish a historic building. A construction project shall avoid historic buildings; if special circumstances make avoidance impossible, the developer shall protect the building at its original site to the greatest extent possible. If construction for the public interest genuinely makes in-situ protection impossible and relocation for protection elsewhere or demolition necessary, the developer shall submit a feasibility report, information on the proposed relocation site and other materials. The municipal planning and natural resources department shall jointly review and approve the proposal with the municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments; where necessary, it shall submit the matter to the Municipal People's Government for decision. If a historic building that cannot feasibly be maintained or repaired is at risk of damage, its responsible person may apply to the municipal planning and natural resources department for reconstruction at the original site. That department shall organize expert review and jointly approve the application with the municipal housing and urban-rural development, cultural relics, ecology and environment and other departments; where necessary, the matter shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for decision. Before demolition, the developer shall mark the building and preserve related materials; reconstruction shall use original building components and materials to the greatest extent possible.
articles.50: A district people's government where a historic and cultural block, famous town or village or traditional village is located shall coordinate construction-land quotas under the principle of intensive land use and give priority to housing for residents and villagers and public-service facilities required to implement protection plans. If protection of a famous historic and cultural village or traditional village requires a new settlement site, the township people's government shall select a site that does not affect the original village pattern or character. Residents and villagers in protected areas shall maintain and repair buildings other than historic buildings in accordance with protection plans and repair technical standards. A district people's government may provide funding or other subsidies for compliant work, and the district housing and urban-rural development or agriculture and rural affairs department shall provide technical guidance.
articles.51: The municipal finance department, together with the municipal agriculture and rural affairs department and relevant district people's governments, shall establish and improve mechanisms for raising funds for protection of famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages in accordance with municipal provisions, coordinate relevant policies and support their protection and development.
articles.52: Within six months after the Municipal People's Government publishes the protection list, the district people's government shall install a protection marker at a principal entrance or another prominent location for each protected subject. The Municipal People's Government shall uniformly prescribe marker-installation standards and maintenance requirements. No unit or individual may unauthorizedly install, move or remove a marker, or damage, alter or cover it.
articles.53: Protection of historic rivers, lakes and water-related cultural heritage shall document historical information such as function, location, form and materials and satisfy these requirements: (1) the overall course of historic rivers and lakes shall not be changed, and their original channels and traditional banks shall be maintained as far as possible; (2) the intensity of use of water-related cultural heritage shall be reasonably controlled; (3) traditional techniques and materials shall be used as far as possible for repair; and (4) other activities damaging historic rivers, lakes or water-related cultural heritage are prohibited.
articles.54: Public facilities such as transit stops and lighting systems, and urban landscape designs, in historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages, and traditional villages shall harmonize with the historic character of the area. No unit or individual may unauthorizedly change a traditional place name associated with a protected subject.
articles.55: The municipal or district people's government may establish a protection fund to support areas related to protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city. Use of the fund shall be open and transparent and subject to public oversight. Donors and beneficiaries shall enjoy tax preferences in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.
articles.56: The Municipality supports training traditional craftspeople, passing on traditional techniques, and producing traditional materials related to protection of Beijing's historic and cultural city; protecting related intellectual property in accordance with law; and improving market mechanisms for transactions involving repair-technology patents. The municipal housing and urban-rural development department shall, together with the municipal human resources and social security and agriculture and rural affairs departments, organize professional training and vocational-skill certification for traditional craftspeople and establish a grading system. Universities, secondary vocational schools and social organizations are encouraged and supported in offering related courses and training professional and technical personnel.
articles.57: If protection needs make it impossible to design or construct a building or project in accordance with standards or specifications for building spacing, building setbacks, landscaping, fire safety, energy conservation, earthquake resistance or other matters, the municipal planning and natural resources department shall organize expert review with the municipal cultural relics, housing and urban-rural development, urban administration, ecology and environment, water affairs, transport, emergency management, civil air defense, earthquake administration and other relevant departments; formulate appropriate planning indicators or safeguard measures; and submit them to the Beijing Historic and Cultural City Protection Committee for review before publication and implementation.
articles.58: The Municipality encourages and supports appropriate use and orderly public access to historic buildings, historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages, traditional villages and other protected subjects of Beijing's historic and cultural city. In response to heritage-protection needs, the municipal planning and natural resources department shall formulate positive or negative lists for protection and use of historic buildings, historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages and traditional villages, specifying encouraged, supported, restricted or prohibited activities.
articles.59: The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation of relocation plans and implementation programs for protected subjects and coordinate them with plans to relieve Beijing of functions that are not essential to its role as the national capital. Space and premises vacated through such functional relocation may be used to resettle units or individuals relocated from protected subjects.
articles.60: When protecting and using historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages and traditional villages, the protection-responsible person shall first protect and then use them, preserve their overall character, comply with applicable positive or negative lists, reasonably control the scale of commercial development, improve public services and pass on traditional culture.
articles.61: A district people's government may coordinate resources and establish platforms for housing exchange, acquisition and enterprise operation as needed, to guide and encourage owners and users of housing in historic and cultural blocks, contiguous traditional one-story residential areas and distinctive areas to improve living conditions voluntarily through lease-back applications, housing exchange and other means.
articles.62: Public-housing management entities shall, in accordance with character-protection requirements, carry out protective repairs on directly managed public housing entrusted to them or vacated through an application process; gradually restore original courtyard patterns; improve municipal infrastructure; and make appropriate use of vacated space.
articles.63: Protection and use of revolutionary sites shall preserve their physical safety and distinctive historic character. Commemorative events connected with major historical events are encouraged. Historical documents and accounts of martyrs shall be researched, organized, publicized and displayed to promote patriotism and revolutionary traditions. Revolutionary sites may be integrated with other protected subjects to expand routes and content for public presentation; such use shall avoid excessive commercialization or entertainment and shall not be vulgarized.
articles.64: Historic buildings may be transferred, mortgaged or leased in accordance with law. If, subject to planning, positive-list, structural-safety, fire-safety, environmental-protection and other requirements, the actual use of an industrial-heritage or other historic building differs from the land use recorded in its title registration, an application may be made to the planning and natural resources department to change the use. Relevant departments shall complete approval procedures in accordance with the changed use.
articles.65: Historic buildings are encouraged to accommodate cultural and service functions suited to their characteristics and the role of the surrounding area, such as libraries, museums, art galleries, physical bookstores and intangible cultural heritage display centers. Historic gardens are encouraged to open to the public in diverse ways and become part of residents' daily lives.
articles.66: In accordance with protection plans, historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages and traditional villages may develop diverse distinctive industries and appropriately conduct tourism, traditional crafts, production of traditional handicrafts and other businesses compatible with traditional culture.
articles.67: Local residents and villagers are encouraged to participate in protection and use of historic and cultural blocks, famous towns and villages, traditional villages and historic buildings. Residents and villagers in famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages are supported in producing and operating local specialty handicraft industries and related activities, sustaining the original form and way of life of those places.
articles.68: Research into and documentation of traditional festivals, distinctive folk customs, traditional crafts and local dialects shall be strengthened. Protection and appropriate use of historically valuable time-honored brands, old objects, traditional crafts and classic performances shall be strengthened to develop stable and enduring traditional cultural brands. Spaces for transmitting intangible cultural heritage shall be suitably arranged and provided with room to survive, spread and develop. Protection of time-honored brands at their original sites and in their original appearance is encouraged.
articles.69: The municipal planning and natural resources department shall establish a unified information platform and create protection archives and databases for subjects on the protection list, recording their history, ownership, survey data, use and related research. Except for information that must be kept confidential by law, archives and related data shall be made public through the internet and other platforms to display cultural resources and facilitate information access, sharing of research and protection and use by organizations and individuals. Modern science and technology are encouraged for displaying and managing protected subjects.
articles.70: If, in violation of the first paragraph of Article 38 of these Regulations, a person fails to perform protection duties for a historic building, the planning and natural resources department shall order correction. If the person fails to correct by the deadline, it shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 200,000 on a unit, or not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 100,000 on an individual. If the historic building is damaged, the fine shall be not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000 for a unit, or not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000 for an individual; the violator shall also be ordered to restore it within a prescribed time. If restoration is not completed, a capable entity shall be designated to restore it, at the expense of the person responsible for protecting the historic building.
articles.71: For violation of Items (1) through (4) of Article 39, the planning and natural resources department shall impose penalties in accordance with the State Council's Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages. Violation of Item (5) of Article 39 shall be penalized in accordance with the Beijing Urban and Rural Planning Regulations. For violation of Items (6) or (7) of Article 39, the planning and natural resources department shall order restoration to the original state within a prescribed time. If the deadline is missed, it may designate a capable entity to restore the original state at the violator's expense. If adverse consequences result, a unit shall be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and an individual not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000.
articles.72: If, in violation of Article 47, a person fails to submit a protection-design plan for approval or fails to repair a historic building in accordance with the approved design plan, the planning and natural resources department shall fine a unit not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and an individual not less than RMB 5,000 but not more than RMB 10,000. If adverse consequences result, the person shall be ordered to restore the original state within a prescribed time and a unit shall be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, or an individual not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. If restoration is not completed by the deadline, a capable entity shall be designated to restore it at the violator's expense. If construction begins without approval of a construction plan or does not follow the approved plan, in violation of Article 47, the housing and urban-rural development department shall impose the foregoing penalties on the construction entity.
articles.73: If, in violation of the second paragraph of Article 24 or the first paragraph of Article 49, a person damages, unauthorizedly relocates or demolishes a historic building or advance-protection subject, the planning and natural resources department shall order restoration to the original state within a prescribed time and fine a unit not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000, or an individual not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000. If restoration is not completed by the deadline, a capable entity shall be designated to restore it at the violator's expense, and the unit shall additionally be fined not less than RMB 200,000 but not more than RMB 500,000, or the individual not less than RMB 100,000 but not more than RMB 200,000. If restoration is impossible, a fine of three to five times the replacement value of the historic building or advance-protection subject shall be imposed. A person causing loss by damaging, unauthorizedly relocating or demolishing a historic building shall compensate the loss in accordance with law. Where public interests are harmed, a legally authorized authority or relevant organization may bring a civil public-interest lawsuit to seek compensation.
articles.74: If, in violation of the second paragraph of Article 52, a person unauthorizedly installs, moves or removes a protection marker or damages, alters or covers it, the subdistrict office or township people's government where it is located shall order correction within a prescribed time. If the person fails to comply, a unit shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and an individual not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.75: If a violator refuses to pay costs that these Regulations require the violator to bear for substitute maintenance, repair, restoration or similar work, the enforcement authority shall impose late fees in accordance with law. If late fees have accrued for more than 30 days and the violator still fails to comply after a demand, the enforcement authority shall apply to a people's court for compulsory enforcement.
articles.76: For purposes of these Regulations: (1) “Three Hills and Five Gardens” collectively refers to cultural heritage from various periods in Beijing's northwestern suburbs, represented by Qing imperial gardens. The three hills are Fragrant Hill, Jade Spring Hill and Longevity Hill; the five gardens are Jingyi Garden, Jingming Garden, the Summer Palace, the Old Summer Palace and Changchun Garden. (2) “Historic building” means a building or structure of protection value that reflects historic character and local features but has not been announced as a cultural relic protection unit or registered as an immovable cultural relic. (3) “Outstanding modern-era building” means a building, group of buildings, structure, group of structures or historic site constructed between the mid-19th century and the 1970s, substantially preserved in its current state, reflecting the history of Beijing's modern urban development and having significant historical, artistic or scientific value. (4) “Industrial heritage” means buildings, structures, equipment, products and production processes formed in the long development of industry and having significant historical, cultural, scientific, artistic, social or economic value. (5) “Revolutionary site” means important heritage formed since 1840 through the Chinese people's historical efforts to achieve national independence, national liberation, democracy and freedom, and to build a modern socialist China. It includes physical heritage such as revolutionary cultural relics and commemorative facilities, including premises of Party, government, military and mass organizations; sites of revolutionary activities, campaigns and battles; martyrs' cemeteries; memorial halls, rooms and pavilions; monuments and statues; and former residences of Party and revolutionary figures; it also includes intangible heritage such as revolutionary stories and songs. (6) “Historic and cultural block” means an area of a certain size that retains a number of immovable cultural relics, historic buildings, traditional-character buildings and historic environmental features such as traditional hutongs and historic streets and lanes, and that comparatively fully and authentically reflects its historic pattern and traditional character. (7) “Distinctive area” means an area outside a historic and cultural block, of a certain size, representing urban planning and construction exploration in a particular period and comparatively fully and authentically reflecting the urban character and social life of that time. (8) “Famous historic and cultural town or village” means a town or village with especially rich cultural relics, significant historical value or commemorative significance, and a comparatively complete reflection of traditional character and local ethnic features of one or more historical periods. (9) “Traditional village” means a village possessing tangible and intangible cultural heritage and having significant historical, cultural, scientific, artistic, social or economic value. (10) “Historic rivers, lakes and water-related cultural heritage” means rivers, waterways and water areas closely related to the development of Beijing and having historical and cultural value, together with waterworks, structures and remains such as wells, bridges and gates. (11) “Traditional hutong” means a hutong formed during or before the Qing dynasty. (12) “Historic street or lane” means a street or lane formed through comprehensive planning from the early 20th century through the 1970s. (13) “Street-and-lane pattern” means the spatial pattern and structure formed by streets, lanes and hutongs from different historical periods, together with buildings and structures along them, that reflects traditional character. (14) “Traditional place name” means a place name passed down or used in any historical period, primarily the names of streets, lanes and hutongs. (15) “Historic garden” means a garden of outstanding historical and cultural value that embodies traditional garden-making techniques, including gardens built around cultural relics or historic sites. (16) “Contiguous traditional one-story residential area” means a contiguous area of one-story housing exceeding one hectare that embodies Beijing's traditional character and is not included in a historic and cultural block. (17) “Large tree” means a deciduous tree with a trunk diameter at breast height of at least 20 centimeters or an evergreen tree with such a diameter of at least 15 centimeters.
articles.77: These Regulations shall take effect on 1 March 2021. The Regulations of Beijing Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City, adopted at the 19th Meeting of the Standing Committee of the 12th Beijing Municipal People's Congress on 25 March 2005, shall be repealed at the same time.

FBMCLI.10.9483232.title: Regulations of Xi'an Municipality on the Protection of the Historic and Cultural City (2025 Revision)

articles.1: To strengthen protection and use of Xi'an's historic and cultural city, inherit and promote outstanding cultural heritage, and integrate protection and transmission of history and culture with urban and rural development, these Regulations are enacted in light of local circumstances and in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics, the State Council's Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the Regulations of Shaanxi Province on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, and other relevant laws and regulations.
articles.2: These Regulations apply to protection, use and administration of Xi'an's historic and cultural city. Where such protection and use concern cultural relics, scenic areas, ancient and famous trees, place-name cultural heritage, intangible cultural heritage or other subjects for which laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise, those provisions shall apply.
articles.3: Protection of Xi'an's historic and cultural city shall follow the principles of scientific planning, classified administration, strict protection, rational use, joint governance and shared benefits, and integrated development. It shall preserve the traditional pattern, historic character and cultural continuity; maintain the historical authenticity of cultural heritage, integrity of historic character and continuity of culture; and promote integration of history and culture with modern life.
articles.4: Protection of Xi'an's historic and cultural city shall uphold and improve a working framework led by the Party committee, with government responsibility, social coordination and public participation.
articles.5: The Municipal People's Government is responsible for protection, use and administration of Xi'an's historic and cultural city. It shall strengthen overall coordination and policy safeguards, improve institutions and mechanisms, coordinate resolution of major issues and incorporate protection and use into the Municipality's national economic and social development plan. A district or county people's government is responsible for protection, use and administration of protected subjects in its jurisdiction; shall include this work in its development plan; establish and improve routine inspection and administration systems; and incorporate inspections into community grid-based administration. Township people's governments and subdistrict offices shall perform related duties under these Regulations and strengthen routine inspections. Residents' and villagers' committees shall assist them. Inclusion of cultural heritage protection in residents' covenants and village rules is encouraged.
articles.6: The municipal natural resources and planning department is the competent authority for protection of Xi'an's historic and cultural city. Together with the municipal cultural relics administration department, it is responsible for protection, use, supervision and administration and shall implement these Regulations. The natural resources and planning department is responsible for protection and planning administration of the historic urban area, historic and cultural blocks and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, and historic buildings. The cultural relics administration department supervises and administers protection of cultural relics. The departments and authorities responsible for development and reform, finance, housing and urban-rural development, urban administration, culture and tourism, ethnic and religious affairs, industry and information technology, forestry, civil affairs, agriculture and rural affairs, state-owned assets, Qinling protection, water administration, ecology and environment, commerce, transport, human resources and social security, education, emergency management, fire and rescue, archives, local gazetteers and other matters shall jointly perform related protection, use, supervision and administration within their respective responsibilities.
articles.7: The Municipal People's Government shall improve mechanisms for raising funds for protection of Xi'an's historic and cultural city, using budget allocations and other lawful sources. The municipal and district/county people's governments shall allocate necessary funds according to actual needs, include them in their fiscal budgets, supervise their use and improve efficiency. Funds shall mainly support surveys and designation, maintenance and repair, digitization, public outreach, academic research, planning and design, education and training, and related work. Financial institutions and local financial organizations are encouraged to participate in protection and use projects, innovate financial products, improve services and broaden financing channels.
articles.8: The Municipal People's Government shall establish expert-advisory and public-participation mechanisms. Experts shall be invited to assess major protection matters, and public views shall be widely solicited.
articles.9: Protection of Xi'an's historic and cultural city is a shared responsibility of society. Every unit and individual shall help protect it and cooperate in surveys, assessments, designation and documentation of protected subjects. They may comment on designation, plan preparation, maintenance, repair and other protection and use work, and complain or report damage to protected subjects or other conduct violating laws and regulations on protection of historic and cultural cities. Relevant departments shall handle and respond to complaints and reports within the prescribed time.
articles.10: Citizens, legal persons and other organizations are encouraged to participate in protection and use by establishing social funds, investing, donating, adopting protected subjects or providing technical services. Research on protection and use is encouraged, as is promotion of advanced and appropriate techniques and methods to improve its scientific basis. Public-interest organizations and volunteer teams are encouraged to guide public participation; the natural resources and planning department shall guide and support related public-benefit and volunteer activities. Units and individuals making outstanding contributions to protection and cultural transmission shall be rewarded in accordance with relevant State and provincial provisions.
articles.11: The municipal and district/county people's governments and their departments shall organize public education on protection, publicize relevant laws, regulations and knowledge, and raise public awareness. News media shall conduct public-service publicity and public oversight in diverse formats. Museums, memorial halls, exhibition halls, libraries, mass art centers, cultural centers and other relevant institutions shall provide related education in connection with their exhibits. Social organizations, enterprises, public institutions and other social forces are encouraged to hold public lectures, special reports, expert talks and immersive experiences. Schools are supported in providing related education and practical activities.
articles.12: The Municipality shall use cultural heritage as a bridge, strengthen cooperation with other cities within Shaanxi, across China and internationally, jointly protect and use cross-regional heritage, and promote coordinated protection systems and mechanisms. The Municipal People's Government shall research and use the cultural resources of the Guanzhong Plain urban cluster; study and promote the heritage value of the Silk Road, Qinling ancient routes, the Qin imperial road and other routes; and advance nominations of Xi'an's City Wall, Western Han imperial mausoleums and other heritage for World Cultural Heritage status.
