articles.13: The Municipality shall protect the historic urban area, major archaeological sites, other cultural heritage and the natural mountain-and-water pattern forming the setting of Xi'an's historic city as a whole and systematically, linking individual sites and routes into contiguous areas.
articles.14: Protected subjects of Xi'an's historic and cultural city include: (1) World Cultural Heritage; (2) major archaeological sites and other immovable cultural relics; (3) the historic urban area; (4) historic and cultural blocks and historic areas; (5) historic buildings, industrial heritage and revolutionary cultural remains; (6) famous historic and cultural towns and villages and traditional villages; (7) natural mountain-and-water patterns and historic axes; (8) scenic areas, agricultural heritage, irrigation-engineering heritage and historic cultural routes; (9) historic environmental elements such as ancient and famous trees, wells and bridges; (10) place-name cultural heritage and intangible cultural heritage; and (11) other protected subjects prescribed by laws and regulations or specified in cultural-protection plans.
articles.15: Designation and adjustment of protected subjects shall comply with relevant State, provincial and municipal provisions. Where no provisions exist, the municipal natural resources and planning department shall, together with the competent department for the subject, formulate designation and adjustment criteria and procedures, obtain approval from the Municipal People's Government, and publish and implement them. A subject designated in accordance with law shall not be adjusted without authorization. If adjustment is necessary because its protection level or condition has changed, the foregoing procedure shall apply.
articles.16: A district or county people's government shall nominate qualifying towns and villages for designation as famous historic and cultural towns and villages. If a town or village meets statutory conditions but has not been nominated, the municipal natural resources and planning department, together with the municipal cultural relics administration department, may recommend nomination to the district or county people's government and urge it to act promptly.
articles.17: The historic urban area covers the complete area within and including Xi'an's City Wall. Priority shall be given to protecting: (1) the City Wall and gates; the area within 20 meters inside the wall; the area from the outside of the wall to the outer edge of the moat; and the squares and green spaces inside and outside Changle, Anding, Yongning and Anyuan Gates; (2) the checkerboard road network; (3) the historic axes Anyuan Gate–Bell Tower–Yongning Gate, Anding Gate–Bell Tower–Changle Gate, and the Tang Chengtian Gate site–North Guangji Street–South Guangji Street–Zhuque Gate; (4) historic and cultural blocks such as Beiyuanmen, Sanxue Street and Qixianzhuang; (5) historic areas such as Defu Lane, Zhuba Market, Zhengxue Street and Xiamaling; (6) historic roads such as Jiefang, Heping, Jianguo and Shangqin Roads; (7) historic streets and lanes such as Damai Market Street, Dapi Courtyard, Kaitong Lane and Huajue Lane; (8) view corridors from the Bell Tower toward Changle, Anding, Yongning and Anyuan Gate towers; (9) historic environmental features such as ancient and famous trees and wells; and (10) place-name heritage such as Bingjiao Lane, Xiwu Garden, Tianshuijing Street and Yaowang Cave.
articles.18: The Beiyuanmen, Sanxue Street and Qixianzhuang historic and cultural blocks shall protect: (1) in Beiyuanmen, the street-and-lane pattern of long main streets and short lanes, the traditional clustered residential pattern, remains reflecting cultural diversity, and time-honored brands, traditional foods and folk activities passing on traditional market culture; (2) in Sanxue Street, the traditional pattern formed by the Temple of Confucius and the Xi'an Prefectural School, Chang'an County School and Xianing County School; the Temple of Confucius, academies and notable people's former residences embodying Confucian, Guanzhong and other outstanding traditions; and traditional businesses and customs passing on academy culture; and (3) in Qixianzhuang, revolutionary cultural remains represented by the former Eighth Route Army Xi'an Office and Revolutionary Park, and cultural elements passing on red culture and revolutionary spirit.
articles.19: The Fenghao, Epang Palace, Han Chang'an City, and Sui Daxing/Tang Chang'an City sites (including Daming Palace) and other sites or site groups included in the national major archaeological-site protection program shall preserve the authenticity and integrity of remains in accordance with law. Priority shall be given to traditional patterns, city sites, palaces, gardens and other remains created through successive capital-city construction, together with the terrain and landforms on which they depend.
articles.20: The natural mountain-and-water pattern formed by the Qinling Mountains, rivers and lakes, tableland landforms and other historic terrain and geographic features shall protect: (1) natural mountains such as the Qinling range; (2) waterways including the Wei, Jing, Ba, Chan, Feng, Hao, Lao and Jue Rivers; and (3) tablelands such as Leyou, Longshou, Fengqi, Shaoling, Bailu, Tongren, Hongqing, Gaoyang and Xiliu.
articles.21: The municipal natural resources and planning department shall, together with competent departments for protected subjects, prepare a list of protected subjects of Xi'an's historic and cultural city based on designation and adjustment decisions. The list shall state each subject's name, location, date of construction or formation, protection level and historical and cultural value, and shall be dynamically maintained.
articles.22: Based on the list of protected subjects, the municipal natural resources and planning department shall, together with the competent departments, collect and organize files and establish related databases, recording subjects' history, title, survey information, use and related research, and promote information sharing.
articles.23: The Municipal People's Government shall regularly organize surveys of cultural resources. Units and individuals may recommend historically and culturally valuable resources to the municipal natural resources and planning department. For an unlisted block, area, building or structure discovered in a survey or recommended by a person or unit, that department shall, together with the municipal cultural relics administration department, inspect it, arrange expert assessment and solicit views of interested parties within 60 days after discovery or recommendation. If it is considered to have protection value, it shall be designated for interim protection. Within five working days after designation, the department shall publish an interim-protection notice identifying the responsible person and informing them in writing of protective measures to take.
articles.24: No unit or individual may damage or demolish a subject designated for interim protection. During interim protection, the township people's government or subdistrict office where it is located shall conduct routine inspections and protection. The municipal natural resources and planning department, together with the municipal cultural relics administration department, shall arrange expert assessment of its value. If it meets the criteria for a historic and cultural block or historic area, the district or county people's government shall be urged to apply for designation in accordance with law. If it meets the criteria for a historic building, it shall be submitted to the Municipal People's Government for designation and publication in accordance with law. If it fails to meet the criteria or is not designated after an application, the department shall promptly notify the relevant unit or individual in writing that interim-protection measures are lifted. If it is not designated as a historic and cultural block, historic area or historic building within one year after publication of the interim-protection notice, the interim-protection decision expires automatically. Compensation shall be provided for losses to lawful rights or interests caused by interim protection.
articles.25: The Municipal People's Government shall organize preparation, in accordance with law, of protection plans for Xi'an's historic and cultural city, historic and cultural blocks and areas. District or county people's governments shall organize preparation of plans for famous historic and cultural towns and villages. The municipal natural resources and planning department shall, together with relevant departments, organize preparation of protection schemes for historic buildings. Plans for other protected subjects shall be prepared under relevant laws, regulations and State provisions; where none apply, the municipal natural resources and planning department may prepare them as needed.
articles.26: Protection plans for Xi'an's historic and cultural city, historic and cultural blocks and areas, and famous historic and cultural towns and villages shall include: (1) objectives, principles, historical and cultural values and features, protected subjects and areas; (2) protection measures, development intensity, construction controls and safeguards; (3) requirements to protect traditional patterns and historic character; (4) the historic urban area's protected area and the core protected and construction-control areas of blocks, areas, towns and villages; (5) infrastructure, public services and improvements to the living environment; (6) disaster prevention, mitigation, relief and emergency measures; (7) recommendations and measures for transmission and use; and (8) phased implementation. The plan for Xi'an's historic and cultural city shall also address protection of the setting of the city site. A traditional-village protection plan shall follow the requirements for famous historic and cultural villages.
articles.27: A protection scheme for a historic building shall state: (1) its historical development and basic information; (2) its protected area, protected features and key control measures; and (3) requirements for maintenance, repair, use and fire safety.
articles.28: Protection plans shall comply with the territorial spatial master plan and rural revitalization plan and align with special plans such as cultural relic protection plans. The main contents of protection plans for Xi'an's historic and cultural city, historic and cultural blocks and areas, and famous historic and cultural towns and villages shall be incorporated into detailed territorial spatial plans. A protection plan for a famous historic and cultural village or traditional village may be combined with its village plan.
articles.29: Once approved in accordance with law, a protection plan shall not be amended without authorization. If amendment is necessary, the authority that originally prepared it shall submit a special report to the original approval authority and may amend it only after consent. The amended plan shall be submitted for approval and filing through the original procedures.
articles.30: The municipal and district/county people's governments shall arrange for the natural resources and planning, cultural relics and other relevant departments to supervise and inspect implementation of protection plans and schemes. Any violation of law or of a protection plan or scheme shall be promptly corrected and addressed.
articles.31: The Municipal People's Government is the protection-responsible authority for Xi'an's historic and cultural city. Responsible persons for protected subjects shall be determined as follows and shall implement specific protection measures: (1) the district or county people's government where a historic urban area, historic and cultural block or historic area is located; (2) the township people's government or subdistrict office where a famous historic and cultural town or village or traditional village is located; (3) the owner of a state-owned historic building, who may agree that its user will be responsible; (4) the owner of a non-state-owned historic building or, if the owner cannot be located or title is unclear, its manager; if there is no manager, its user; if none can be identified, the district or county people's government shall designate a responsible person; (5) the owner of industrial heritage; (6) a separately established protection-management organization for a protected subject; or (7) where laws or regulations designate a responsible person for another protected subject or special circumstance, that person; otherwise, the municipal or district/county people's government shall designate one. Responsible persons under Items (1), (2) and (6) shall be publicly announced by the Municipal People's Government. Once a responsible person under Items (3), (4) or (5) is identified, the municipal natural resources and planning department shall notify that person of their duties. That department shall periodically verify ownership, management and use of historic buildings and promptly update the responsible person if any such information changes.
articles.32: The responsible person for a historic urban area, historic and cultural block or historic area shall: (1) holistically protect traditional patterns, historic character, street-and-lane layouts, spatial scale and interdependent natural landscapes and surroundings; (2) improve policies and measures, implement protection requirements, conduct routine inspections and promptly address conduct endangering protected subjects; (3) strictly control construction scale, building height, volume, style and colors, and improve buildings, structures and landscape features within the protected area that are inconsistent with historic character; (4) organize emergency repairs for endangered or at-risk protected subjects; (5) improve infrastructure and public services, the living environment and appropriate activation of cultural resources; (6) organize relevant departments to ensure safety and disaster prevention and mitigation; (7) optimize urban functions and integrate urban renewal with transmission of history and culture; and (8) perform other duties prescribed by laws and regulations or determined by the Municipal People's Government.
articles.33: The responsible person for a famous historic and cultural town or village or a traditional village shall: (1) preserve the integrity of traditional patterns, historic character, distinctive decoration, spatial scale and historic environmental elements of buildings and structures in the protected area; (2) promptly stop conduct endangering protected subjects and report it to relevant departments according to administrative authority; (3) keep the protected area clean and presentable; (4) assist relevant departments with safety, disaster prevention and mitigation; (5) implement required improvements to infrastructure, public services and the living environment; and (6) perform other duties prescribed by laws and regulations or determined by the municipal or district/county people's government.
articles.34: The responsible person for a historic building shall: (1) maintain, repair and use it in accordance with its protection scheme and preserve its original height, scale, appearance, colors and other character features; (2) conduct routine administration and prioritize protection of its exterior, structure, components and historic environmental elements embodying its core value; (3) ensure safety, promptly address safety hazards or emergencies and report them to the municipal natural resources and planning department; (4) ensure the normal operation of disaster-prevention facilities and equipment; (5) when transferring, leasing or lending the building, give the transferee, lessee or user written notice of protection requirements; and (6) perform other duties prescribed by laws and regulations.
articles.35: The responsible person for industrial heritage shall: (1) monitor its condition, delineate its protected area and take measures preserving historic features such as its pattern, structure, style and character; (2) establish an archive recording protection of core items, collection of remains, maintenance and repair, development and use, and funding and support; (3) install signs and appropriate exhibition facilities in the heritage area; (4) ensure the safety of core items, promptly address safety hazards or risks of damage, repair damaged core items, and report matters to relevant departments according to administrative authority; and (5) perform other protection duties prescribed by laws, regulations and relevant provisions.
articles.36: The principal functions of the historic urban area shall be culture, commerce and tourism. In light of the carrying capacity of its environmental resources, population capacity shall be managed and the total amount of housing construction for State organs, enterprises, public institutions and urban residents strictly controlled. Enterprises and public institutions incompatible with these functions shall adjust or relocate by a deadline. Compensation shall be provided for resulting losses to lawful rights and interests of relevant units or individuals.
articles.37: Building heights and styles in and around the historic urban area shall meet these requirements: (1) new construction, alteration or expansion within the area shall not exceed 24 meters in height; (2) within 20 meters inside Xi'an's City Wall, the area shall be restored as a patrol path or developed as green space; within 100 meters, buildings shall not exceed 9 meters and shall use traditional forms; beyond 100 meters, buildings shall transition in tiers, with grey-tile pitched roofs in the transition area; (3) within a 100-meter radius from the inner centerline of Changle, Anding, Yongning and Anyuan Gate towers, land shall be used for squares, green spaces and roads, and surrounding buildings and structures shall harmonize with the towers' style and colors; (4) within a 200-meter radius from the outer centerline of those gate towers, land shall be used for squares, green spaces and roads. Beyond that radius and outside the outer red line of the ring road, 60-meter transition zones shall successively increase the permitted building height from below 24 meters to below 36 meters and then below 50 meters; and (5) between the outside of the City Wall and the ring-road greenbelt, only garden-style public-service facilities no higher than 6 meters may be built.
articles.38: View corridors between the Bell Tower and the towers of Changle, Anding, Yongning and Anyuan Gates shall be delineated and building heights controlled as follows: (1) the corridor to Changle Gate shall be 50 meters wide; buildings within it shall not exceed 9 meters, and buildings within 20 meters outside it shall not exceed 12 meters; (2) the corridor to Anding Gate shall be 100 meters wide, and buildings within it shall not exceed 9 meters; (3) the corridor to Yongning Gate shall be 60 meters wide; and (4) the corridor to Anyuan Gate shall be 50 meters wide.
articles.39: Construction in the historic urban area shall comply with the protection plan and: (1) shall not add industrial or warehouse land; (2) shall not add overhead lines; (3) shall not involve construction, alteration or expansion of buildings or structures in violation of the plan; (4) ensure buildings and structures harmonize in style and color with the area's character, and preserve traditional residences and shops by repairing them to their original appearance; and (5) use paving materials and forms reflecting the area's character in squares, sidewalks and historic streets and lanes.
articles.40: Outdoor advertising in the historic urban area shall comply with the advertising plan and harmonize with the area's character. No outdoor advertising may be installed inside or around the Bell Tower traffic circle or inside or around the traffic circles at Changle, Anding, Yongning and Anyuan Gate towers. The advertising plan shall define the precise areas covered by the foregoing restrictions.
articles.41: Public transit routes in the historic urban area shall be optimized, transit stops and transfer hubs appropriately planned, and motor-vehicle entry into and passage through the area reduced. Walking and other slow modes of transport are encouraged; pedestrian and low-speed areas and routes shall be reasonably expanded to provide an environment suitable for bicycles and pedestrians. Non-motorized travel and walking shall be the main modes in historic and cultural blocks.
articles.42: The Municipal People's Government and relevant district people's governments shall strengthen protection and administration of gardens, green spaces and squares in the historic urban area. They shall plan new, expanded or renovated pocket parks, street greenery and recreational squares, add cultural facilities and street trees, and increase vegetation coverage.
articles.43: The Municipal People's Government shall delineate an environmental-coordination zone around the historic urban area and prepare urban design for it, ensuring that building height, scale, style and colors in the zone harmonize with the character of the historic urban area.
articles.44: The municipal natural resources and planning department shall, together with the municipal cultural relics administration department, prepare technical specifications for repair of historic buildings, specifying maintenance and repair measures by category. The responsible person shall maintain and repair a historic building in accordance with its protection scheme and the specifications, and, as needed, improve disaster-prevention facilities and equipment. Modern technology and methods may be used where necessary to improve resistance to damp, theft, insects and other risks. Use of traditional craftspeople, local traditional techniques and materials is encouraged. The responsible person is entitled to obtain information and technical guidance on protection, repair and use from the natural resources and planning department.
articles.45: To externally repair or decorate a historic building, add facilities, or change its structure or use, an implementation plan shall be prepared in accordance with its protection scheme and approved by the natural resources and planning department together with the cultural relics administration department at the same level; other required procedures under laws and regulations shall also be completed. Routine maintenance and minor repair not affecting features, materials, structures or decoration embodying historic character are exempt.
articles.46: The municipal and district/county people's governments shall subsidize maintenance and repair by the responsible person for a non-state-owned historic building performed in accordance with its protection scheme and repair specifications. The municipal natural resources and planning and finance departments shall jointly formulate subsidy standards for implementation after approval by the Municipal People's Government. If a historic building is at risk of damage and its responsible person lacks the financial ability to maintain or repair it, the district or county people's government shall take protective measures and may designate a relevant department to carry out repairs. The responsible person and township people's government or subdistrict office shall cooperate and provide support. Repair costs shall be shared by municipal and district/county fiscal funds.
articles.47: A construction project shall avoid historic buildings; if special circumstances make avoidance impossible, protection at the original site shall be implemented to the greatest extent possible. Before in-situ protection, the developer shall determine protective measures and obtain approval from the natural resources and planning department together with the cultural relics administration department at the same level.
articles.48: Where construction for the public interest makes in-situ protection of a historic building impossible and relocation for protection elsewhere or demolition necessary, the developer shall organize an assessment, widely solicit views from relevant departments, experts and the public, and prepare a relocation or demolition plan. After review by the municipal natural resources and planning department together with the municipal housing and urban-rural development and cultural relics departments, it shall be submitted to the provincial housing and urban-rural development department for approval together with the provincial cultural relics administration department. The responsible person shall be consulted before relocating or demolishing a non-state-owned historic building. Before demolition, the municipal natural resources and planning department shall create a digital model and preserve photographs, survey drawings and other records, and transfer them to the municipal urban construction archives authority in accordance with law. Components removed for relocation shall be used to reassemble and restore the building. Components removed during demolition shall be inventoried, numbered, properly stored and rationally used.
articles.49: No unit or individual may: (1) carve or deface a historic building; (2) produce, store, pile or sell explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances inside it; (3) dismantle, transfer or damage its components; (4) externally repair or decorate it, add facilities, or change its structure or use without authorization; (5) relocate, demolish or rebuild it without authorization; or (6) otherwise damage it.
articles.50: Construction within the protected areas of the historic urban area, historic and cultural blocks and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages or historic buildings shall comply with the applicable protection plan and scheme, shall not impair the authenticity or integrity of cultural heritage, destructively affect its traditional pattern or historic character, or change the natural landscape or environment on which it depends. Buildings, structures and other facilities inconsistent with a protection plan shall be renovated, relocated or demolished in accordance with law. Where they were historically established or lawfully approved, the district or county people's government shall carry out relocation or demolition in phases and provide resettlement and compensation as required. Illegal construction shall be handled in accordance with law.
articles.51: Construction in core protected areas of historic and cultural blocks and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, and traditional villages shall: (1) not involve new construction or expansion, except necessary infrastructure, public-service facilities and projects to improve the living environment; (2) use effective protective measures when building roads, bridges, underground works or other municipal utilities, without damaging protected subjects; (3) ensure outdoor advertisements, signs, awnings, air conditioners, corridors, sculptures, sanitation facilities and other external installations, and exterior decoration, harmonize with historic character; (4) bury new or renovated urban utility lines underground, or, if conditions make that impossible or wall-mounted routing is needed, conceal or technically treat them to meet character-protection requirements; and (5) comply with other requirements of laws and regulations. New buildings and structures in construction-control areas shall comply with the controls in the protection plan and harmonize with the historic character of the core protected area.
articles.52: To demolish a building, structure or other facility, other than a historic building, within the core protected area of a historic and cultural block or a famous historic and cultural town or village, an application shall be submitted to the natural resources and planning department and approved by that department together with the cultural relics administration department at the same level.
articles.53: Before urban renewal in an area, the municipal or district/county people's government shall organize a special survey and assessment of cultural resources in accordance with law, document and assess existing resources, identify those to be retained and protected, and arrange expert review. Urban renewal shall not proceed in an area where no such survey and assessment has been conducted. In accordance with provincial provisions, assessment results shall be reviewed by the municipal natural resources and planning department and submitted to the provincial housing and urban-rural development department as a basis for selecting urban-renewal projects and preparing project implementation plans.
articles.54: Within protected areas of Xi'an's historic and cultural city, historic and cultural blocks and areas, and famous historic and cultural towns and villages, the following are prohibited: (1) mountain excavation, quarrying, mining or other activities damaging traditional patterns or historic character; (2) occupying or damaging gardens, green spaces, rivers, lakes, roads, ancient and famous trees, wells, bridges or other historic environmental features designated for retention in a protection plan; (3) constructing factories or warehouses for producing or storing explosive, flammable, radioactive, toxic or corrosive substances; and (4) other activities destructively affecting Xi'an's historic and cultural city, protected blocks or areas, famous towns or villages, or historic buildings.
articles.55: Fire-safety facilities, fire lanes, flood-control and drainage facilities and similar infrastructure within core protected areas of historic and cultural blocks and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, and traditional villages, and within protected areas of historic buildings and industrial heritage, shall be installed in accordance with applicable technical standards and specifications. If protection needs make compliance impossible, the emergency-management department and fire and rescue agency shall, together with the natural resources and planning department, conduct a safety-risk assessment and expert review and formulate corresponding safeguards and an emergency plan.
articles.56: The municipal and district/county people's governments and relevant departments shall strengthen coordinated protection of major archaeological sites, orderly develop archaeological-site parks, display their scale and significance, and improve their presentation and use. The Municipal People's Government shall coordinate efforts to obtain support from relevant State and provincial departments, accelerate archaeological research on major sites and facilitate that research. Before construction of an archaeological-site park, living-environment improvement or other project at a major archaeological site, the district or county people's government shall prepare a construction plan and submit it to the municipal cultural relics administration department for review together with the municipal natural resources and planning, housing and urban-rural development, agriculture and rural affairs and other relevant departments. Where law requires approval from another authority, the applicable procedures shall be followed.
articles.57: The Municipal People's Government shall establish a coordination mechanism for protection of natural mountain-and-water patterns and historic cultural routes, strengthen interdepartmental coordination and resource integration, and organize municipal departments and district/county people's governments to gradually restore natural environments and cultural landscapes in accordance with protection plans, promoting holistic protection and systematic presentation of cross-regional cultural heritage.
articles.58: The municipal and district/county people's governments shall strengthen protection and administration of place names in Xi'an's historic and cultural city and include qualifying place-name cultural heritage in the scope of intangible cultural heritage protection in accordance with law. Place names of significant historical and cultural value that embody the continuity of Chinese history shall generally not be changed.
articles.59: The municipal and district/county people's governments shall install protection markers at principal entrances to core protected areas of historic and cultural blocks and areas and famous historic and cultural towns and villages, at entrances to traditional-village protected areas, and at prominent locations on historic buildings. Markers shall be installed within six months after a protected subject is approved and published. Their form shall follow relevant State provisions; where none exist, the Municipal People's Government shall adopt a uniform design reflecting Xi'an's history and culture. A marker shall state the subject's name, number, protected area, designation date and relevant historical and cultural information, be translated into other languages as needed, and use digital technology to facilitate public access. No unit or individual may unauthorizedly install, move or alter a marker or damage it. Markers displaying historical information about historic spatial names, sites of historical events and poetic or literary heritage are encouraged.
articles.60: The competent departments for protected subjects shall use video surveillance, remote sensing and other technologies to monitor them and promptly detect, stop and address illegal damage to protected subjects or unauthorized installation, movement, alteration or damage of protection markers.
articles.61: Each year, the Municipal People's Government shall organize a self-assessment of protection work for Xi'an's historic and cultural city, historic and cultural blocks and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages and historic buildings, prepare a report and submit it to the provincial housing and urban-rural development department. Problems found in the assessment shall be promptly corrected. The report shall cover surveys, assessment and designation of cultural resources; performance of protection-management duties; and the results of protection and use.
articles.62: Transmission and use of Xi'an's historic and cultural city shall draw on the educational and practical value of cultural heritage, improve people's livelihoods, use appropriate activity to promote protection and transmission, and integrate cultural protection and transmission with high-quality urban and rural development. Rational use and orderly public access are encouraged and supported for the historic urban area, historic and cultural blocks and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, traditional villages, historic buildings, industrial heritage and other protected subjects. Research and transmission are supported for traditional techniques, customs, medicine, festivals, foods, folk art and literature, dialects, poetry and couplets, and other cultural resources; modern ways of expressing history and culture in contemporary life and production may be explored.
articles.63: In accordance with the Shaanxi Provincial Regulations on the Protection of Famous Historical and Cultural Cities, Towns and Villages, the municipal or county people's government shall arrange for the natural resources and planning department, together with competent departments for protected subjects, to formulate positive and negative lists for protection and use, specifying encouraged, supported, restricted and prohibited activities, and periodically assess and dynamically adjust the lists.
articles.64: The municipal and district/county people's governments shall strengthen research and interpretation of cultural heritage, explore its historical stories, cultural values and spiritual meaning, connect heritage of different levels and categories, and create routes, corridors and networks that present history and culture as part of everyday life, fully displaying Xi'an's history and culture.
articles.65: The Municipal People's Government shall arrange for competent departments to establish a unified digital presentation platform for cultural resources and make the list of protected subjects, protection archives and related data available to the public, facilitating access to information, sharing of research and protection and use by organizations and individuals, except for information that must be kept confidential by law. Modern technologies are encouraged for presenting and using protected subjects.
articles.66: The municipal and district/county people's governments shall use urban-renewal, rural-revitalization and other policy measures to improve infrastructure, public services and living conditions in protected areas of the historic urban area, historic and cultural blocks and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, and traditional villages, including water and electricity supply, communications, roads, fire safety, and household waste and sewage treatment.
articles.67: Activation and use of historic and cultural blocks and areas, famous historic and cultural towns and villages, and traditional villages shall respect the wishes of local residents, protect their lawful rights and interests, encourage their participation in protection and transmission, and shall not forcibly relocate them. Residents are encouraged to participate in transmission and use by contributing housing, funds or other resources as equity and to receive reasonable returns. Production, business and other activities related to local specialty industries are supported in these places to sustain their original form and way of life.
articles.68: The municipal and district/county people's governments and their departments shall formulate policies to guide and support industries, optimize industrial layouts in areas where cultural heritage is concentrated, and strengthen protection and use of protected subjects and other culturally valuable time-honored brands, old objects, traditional crafts, classic performances and historic place names. They shall promote their historical and cultural value and features, develop traditional cultural brands, support cultural and creative products, distinctive historical and cultural experiences and related industries, and turn cultural-resource advantages into industrial strengths. Creation of film and literary works, design and production of traditional clothing, animation and game development, and educational travel and experiential products that promote fine traditional Chinese culture and Xi'an's distinctive history and culture are supported. Protection of time-honored brands at their original sites and in their original appearance is encouraged. Qualifying traditional techniques of time-honored brands are supported for inclusion in the State catalogue for revitalizing traditional crafts and the representative intangible cultural heritage list. Time-honored brands are encouraged to apply for demonstration bases for productive protection of intangible cultural heritage.
articles.69: On the basis of effective protection, the Municipality supports designing tourism routes, developing tourism products, building tourism brands and deepening regional tourism cooperation using the historical and cultural resources of Xi'an's historic and cultural city, and promoting integration of culture and tourism.
articles.70: Historic buildings and industrial heritage may be mortgaged, transferred or leased in accordance with law. Where laws, regulations or State policy provide otherwise, those provisions shall apply. The municipal and district/county people's governments may promote activation and use through policy guidance, financial support, simplified procedures and technical guidance. While preserving original exterior character and representative components and ensuring building safety, additions, alterations and added facilities may be used to improve conditions and meet modern needs. Revenue from activation and use of state-owned historic buildings and industrial heritage shall be used mainly for their maintenance, repair, routine care and improvement of surrounding areas.
articles.71: Historic buildings and industrial heritage may be used for diverse purposes if they comply with protection plans and schemes, applicable positive lists, structural safety, fire safety, environmental protection and other professional requirements. According to their characteristics and the role of the surrounding area, historic buildings are encouraged to accommodate museums, memorial halls, exhibition halls, libraries, venues for displaying and transmitting intangible cultural heritage, time-honored brands, distinctive restaurants and homestays. Suitable industrial heritage is encouraged to be used for distinctive districts, industrial-cultural parks, innovation and entrepreneurship bases, film and television locations, industrial experience centers, cultural and tourism venues, mixed-use complexes and open spaces; industrial tourism, industrial-culture education and practical activities, industrial design, arts and crafts, and industrial creativity are encouraged. Necessary technical-security, physical-security and pollution-control facilities shall be provided for business activities in historic buildings and industrial heritage.
articles.72: Transmission and use of revolutionary cultural remains shall preserve their physical safety, distinctive historic character and surroundings. Commemorative activities connected with major historical events are encouraged; revolutionary historical materials and accounts of martyrs shall be researched, organized, publicized and displayed to promote patriotism and revolutionary culture. Revolutionary remains may be integrated with other protected subjects to expand presentation routes and content. Their presentation and use shall avoid excessive commercialization or entertainment and shall not be vulgarized.
articles.73: The municipal and district/county people's governments shall organize relevant departments to survey, designate, document and archive intangible cultural heritage, and recommend representative items for display at major events and holidays. Units and individuals are encouraged to collect, organize, research, protect and use intangible cultural heritage in accordance with law. Lawful venues for displaying and transmitting it are encouraged and supported. Representative bearers of representative items are supported in presenting and transmitting intangible cultural heritage and shall be provided with space for its preservation, dissemination and development. On the basis of effective protection, the distinctive advantages and resources of intangible cultural heritage may be used rationally, related industries supported and developed, and cultural products and services with local or ethnic characteristics and market potential created.
articles.74: Training traditional craftspeople, passing on and using traditional techniques, and producing traditional materials related to protection of Xi'an's historic and cultural city are supported, and related intellectual property shall be protected in accordance with law. Universities, vocational schools, vocational-training institutions and other social forces are encouraged and supported in offering related courses and training people in traditional skills.
articles.75: Where a municipal or district/county people's government, its department or a township people's government or subdistrict office commits any of the following acts in violation of these Regulations, an authority with jurisdiction shall order correction and issue a notice of criticism. The directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible personnel shall be disciplined in accordance with law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued: (1) failing to perform duties to prepare, amend or publish a protection plan or scheme as required by law; (2) failing to perform supervision and administration duties or failing to investigate an identified violation; (3) inadequate protection resulting in serious damage to Xi'an's historic and cultural city, a historic and cultural block or area, famous historic and cultural town or village, traditional village or historic building, or resulting in its placement on an endangered list or revocation of its designation; (4) failing to include an eligible historic and cultural block or area, famous town or village, traditional village or historic building in a protection list, resulting in serious damage to its historical and cultural value; (5) failing to install protection markers as required by law; (6) unlawfully granting an administrative license; or (7) neglecting duties, abusing powers, engaging in favoritism or committing other misconduct.
articles.76: A person who carves or defaces a historic building in violation of Item (1) of Article 49 shall be ordered by the natural resources and planning department to restore it to its original state or take other remedial measures and fined RMB 50. A person who dismantles, transfers or damages a historic building's components in violation of Item (3) of Article 49 shall be ordered by that department to stop the violation and restore the original state or take other remedial measures within a prescribed time. Illegal gains, if any, shall be confiscated. If serious consequences result, a unit shall be fined not less than RMB 50,000 but not more than RMB 100,000, and an individual not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000. Losses shall be compensated in accordance with law.
articles.77: A person who unauthorizedly installs, moves or alters a protection marker, or damages it, in violation of the third paragraph of Article 59, shall be ordered by the natural resources and planning department to correct the violation within a prescribed time. If the person fails to comply, a unit shall be fined not less than RMB 10,000 but not more than RMB 50,000, and an individual not less than RMB 1,000 but not more than RMB 10,000.
articles.78: If a violation of these Regulations damages a historic urban area, historic and cultural block or area, famous historic and cultural town or village, or historic building and thereby infringes State or public interests, an authority or organization authorized by law may bring a public-interest lawsuit. The municipal and district/county people's governments and their departments shall cooperate and provide support.
articles.79: Where other conduct violates these Regulations and laws or regulations prescribe legal liability, those provisions shall apply.
articles.80: For purposes of these Regulations: (1) “Historic and cultural block” means an area designated and published in accordance with law that contains especially rich cultural relics and a concentration of historic buildings, comparatively fully and authentically reflects a traditional pattern and historic character, and has a certain scale. (2) “Historic area” means an area designated and published in accordance with law that authentically reflects the traditional character and ethnic or local features of a particular historical period in Xi'an. (3) “Historic road (street or lane)” means a road, street or lane within the historic urban area, a historic and cultural block or area, a famous historic and cultural town or village, or a traditional village that is clearly documented historically, retains a clear pattern and layout, has rich cultural resources and displays distinctive cultural continuity. (4) “Famous historic and cultural town or village” means a town or village designated and published in accordance with law that has especially rich cultural relics, significant historical and cultural value or commemorative significance, retains its traditional pattern and historic character, and comparatively fully reflects local features. (5) “Traditional village” means a village formed relatively early that has abundant traditional cultural resources, is comparatively well preserved, and has significant historical, cultural, scientific, artistic, social or economic value. (6) “Historic building” means a building or structure designated and published in accordance with law that has protection value and reflects historic character and local features but has not been announced as a cultural relic protection unit or registered as an ungraded immovable cultural relic. (7) “Historic axis” means the urban-axis system formed through capital-city construction in successive dynasties, including the Feng and Hao capitals axis, Epang Palace axis, central axis of Han Chang'an City, north-south central axis of Sui Daxing and Tang Chang'an City, north-south axis of Tang Daming Palace and Ming-Qing Xi'an central axis. (8) “Historic cultural route” means the physical routes and route remains formed in different historical periods for trade, transport, military, water conservancy or other purposes, including the Silk Road, Qinling ancient routes, Qin imperial road and historic canals. (9) “Industrial heritage” means industrial remains formed through long-term industrial development, designated in accordance with law and relevant regulations, and having significant historical, technological, social or artistic value. (10) “Revolutionary cultural remains” means sites, remains, places and objects formed since 1840 through the Chinese people's historical efforts to achieve national independence, national liberation, democracy and freedom, and build a modern socialist China, with significant commemorative, educational or documentary value. (11) “Agricultural heritage” means an agricultural production system passed down through generations in the long-term coordinated development of people and their environment, with rich agricultural biodiversity, a complete system of traditional knowledge and techniques, and distinctive ecological and cultural landscapes. (12) “Place-name cultural heritage” means place names and related cultural expressions of historical and cultural value that embody the continuity of Chinese history and have been passed down and used to the present.
articles.81: Development-zone administrative committees and the administrative committee of the Han Chang'an City National Major Archaeological Site Protection Special Zone shall, as authorized by the Municipal People's Government, be responsible for protection of Xi'an's historic and cultural city within their respective responsibilities.
articles.82: These Regulations shall take effect on 1 March 2026.
